eligibility: Only British citizens or UK residents may sign; others may browse.

records.title: Hold a UK-wide briefing on climate and nature risks
records.description: The UK faces growing risks from climate and nature breakdown - from extreme weather to economic disruption and national security threats. Yet the public has never been given a clear national briefing on the scale of these risks. Government should hold an emergency briefing from leading experts.
records.further_details:
These risks could have serious consequences across UK society, with threats to health and food supply - which could become irreversible if without urgent action. Many people are unclear how these risks may affect them, and information in the public domain is often misleading.
 
A credible national briefing from independent experts would give people clear, trusted guidance on what these risks mean in practice, and what we can do - both together and individually - to prepare and respond.

records.title: End the mandatory fortification of white flour with folic acid immediately
records.description: We call on the Government to stop the fortification of flour with synthetic folic acid. Folic acid is a medicine not a food. We believe it is unethical to mass medicate the entire population without their knowledge or consent in the hope that a minority group of people might see a benefit.
records.further_details: The NHS website lists sections of the population (including people with cancer, a stent or low vitamin B12 levels) who should avoid folic acid exposure because of possible detrimental health impacts. Even if these people are aware of the issue, it is becoming harder to avoid as wholemeal and gluten free products are voluntarily adding folic acid.

records.title: Reduce the state pension age to 65 for all
records.description: Reduce the state pension age to 65. We believe this could mean people can retire with dignity and avoid hardship. We also think it could free up jobs for younger workers entering the labour market.
records.further_details: Many aged 65–67 face poor health, caring pressures, and limited work options, which we think is unfair.

records.title: Launch a public inquiry into illegal migration in the UK
records.description: We call on the Government to launch a full-scale public inquiry into illegal migration in the UK. The inquiry should investigate the effectiveness of UK border control, the financial cost on taxpayers, and the deportation system.
records.further_details: Thousands of people illegally migrate to the UK each year. We believe this has negatively impacted the UK to a significant extent and resulted in some people feeling unsafe walking the streets. Furthermore, we believe it has brought a great burden onto taxpayers as the Government has had to pay for more support for illegal migrants.

records.title: Make statutory maternity pay 90% of wage for first 12 weeks & minimum wage after
records.description: We believe mothers should never be forced back to work because maternity leave is unaffordable. UK SMP is among Europe’s least generous, falling to around 41% of minimum wage after 6 weeks. The Government should fix this and give mothers 12 weeks of Statutory Maternity Pay at 90% of their salary.
records.further_details:
It is estimated that between 2023-26, SMP rose by just 12.7%, whilst the National Living Wage rose by 22%. We are concerned the gap is widening. It was estimated that the proportion of mothers returning earlier to work for financial reasons rose from 42% in 2022 to 58% in 2023. 
  
Public research links maternity leave under 12 weeks to greater depression, poorer maternal wellbeing & lower sensitivity to a baby’s needs. Low SMP can hit low-income families hardest, forcing mothers back before they’re ready. We feel Statutory Maternity Leave for 12 weeks at 90% of salary, and the National Minimum Wage for the remainder, are the absolute minimum families deserve.

records.title: Make catapult attacks against animals a standalone criminal offence
records.description: Introduce legislation in England to make it a specific, standalone criminal offence to intentionally or recklessly use, discharge or attempt to discharge a catapult or slingshot at or towards any animal.
records.further_details:
Animals including swans, ducks, gulls, pigeons and squirrels have been deliberately targeted with catapults firing stones, ball bearings and other projectiles. Those struck can suffer broken bones, blindness, internal injuries and death.
 
Existing protections are spread across different laws and may depend on the species and circumstances. We believe the law should be clear and consistent: catapults should never be used as weapons against animals.

records.title: Provide lifelong vet care and financial support for retired service animals
records.description: We want the UK Government to create a national support scheme to provide lifelong veterinary care and financial assistance for retired service animals, including police dogs, military dogs, and police horses.
records.further_details:
Service animals protect the public and support the emergency services and armed forces. Many retire with injuries or health conditions linked to their service. Ongoing care costs often fall to former handlers, adopters, or charities. 
We want a national support scheme or pension to help fund lifelong veterinary care and welfare support for retired service animals.

records.title: Permanent driving ban on intoxicated drivers guilty of causing death
records.description: I urge Parliament to take decisive action by implementing a lifetime driving ban on those guilty of driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs and killing innocent people while under influence. Other countries have set precedents by enforcing stringent penalties.
records.further_details:
We feel the current legal framework fails to deter repeat offenders and adequately protect innocent people. endangering more lives and communities.
 
We believe implementing a lifetime driving ban is about ensuring public safety, deterring repeat offenses, and sending a powerful message that our society refuses to tolerate such negligence. For the families affected, this legal change could offer a measure of justice and a chance to prevent others from enduring a similar tragedy.

records.title: Ensure new sewage treatment infrastructure meets higher standards as in the EU
records.description: We urge the government to review the regulations for new sewage treatment infrastructure and introduce new legislation to ensure high international standards are met; to safeguard people’s health, better protect all water bodies and reduce damaging long term impacts.
records.further_details: All new wastewater infrastructure must be built to well-established, higher international standards, in line with the revised EU Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive (UWWTD) standards in force since 1 January 2025, to significantly reduce the pollution load on water bodies. Proposed new schemes built to outdated standards must be stopped as they will continue releasing biological and chemical contaminants, including forever chemicals, harming water bodies, wildlife, and public health. They also risk a dramatic increase in customer water bills to pay for expensive and avoidable upgrades.

records.title: Ban children & their likeness being used to promote pornography or adult-content
records.description: We want the Government to introduce legislation making it illegal to use children or their likeness in advertising, promotional material or social-media content to promote commercial pornography or adult-content businesses, including where the material featuring the child is not sexually explicit.
records.further_details: We believe there is a safeguarding gap where children, or dolls intended to represent children, can appear in otherwise non-explicit social-media content used to promote commercial adult-content businesses. Children cannot consent to such associations. We want clear legal boundaries preventing the use of children, or representations of children, to advertise or generate engagement for commercial pornography or adult content.

records.title: Reduce the retirement age for the NHS pension scheme to 60
records.description: Reduce the retirement age for NHS staff pension scheme to 60. We are concerned NHS staff are facing extreme physical and mental burnout daily. High stress and long shifts can risk employee health and patient safety.
records.further_details:
We want the Government to lower the age NHS staff can draw their full pension to protect staff and patients. NHS roles can be physically exhausting and mentally draining. Long shifts, heavy workloads, and intense stress can cause severe burnout. We believe having staff work until 65+ is dangerous, risks employee health and compromises patient safety.
 
Lowering the retirement age could prevent workforce exhaustion, attract younger professionals into the service, prevent staff turnover & support frontline workers.

records.title: Introduce urgent moratorium on AI Data Centres and BESS outside AI Growth Zones
records.description: Introduce: (1) an immediate moratorium on planning approvals for BESS (Battery Energy Storage Systems) and Data Centres outside designated AI Growth Zones; (2) mandatory Rural Impact Assessments conducted at local level; and (3) mandatory comprehensive investigation into financing of all proposals.
records.further_details: We believe robust evaluation is needed as to: (i) the cost-benefit analysis of each BESS/Data Centre; and (ii) all financing, including non-UK-based funds. Proposals outside AI Growth Zones can be highly problematic, because they may seek to evade regulation and Government scrutiny. Rural areas are especially vulnerable. There are reports of farmers being threatened with compulsory purchase. Loss of farmland could endanger UK food security. Irreparable harm may be caused to heritage, landscapes, ecology, public health and wellbeing.

records.title: Fund £20,000 a year (term time) wage for Teaching Assistants
records.description: Up Teaching Assistants' pay to a minimum of £20,000 a year (term time) to reflect the amount of work they do. It's not just displays and marking. It's challenging behaviour, teaching, marking, first aid, displays, emotional coaching and supporting children with SEN.
records.further_details: We believe that Teaching Assistants' job roles have changed massively over the years. It used to be that we were in to do photocopying, displays and some marking. We feel that now, many TAs must deal with a lot of children with SEN on a daily basis, without reflective pay for that. We mark, we teach, we problem solve, we deal with sick children, we work with small groups of children, we do multiple interventions, we read daily, we coach children on how to manage emotions.

records.title: Fund second stem cell transplants on NHS for relapse within 12 months
records.description: We want the UK Government to provide funding to the NHS so that patients with blood cancer who relapse within one year from their first transplant, and whose clinical team feel they would benefit from a second transplant, are not denied a potentially lifesaving transplant.
records.further_details: For some people whose blood cancer returns after a stem cell transplant, a second transplant can be lifesaving. NHS England’s policy states patients are not eligible for a second stem cell transplant if the cancer returns within 12 months of their first transplant. Anthony Nolan, DKMS and Leukaemia UK are calling on the UK Government to fund and enable NHS England to change its policy, so that no patient is denied a potentially lifesaving stem cell transplant just because they can’t afford it.

records.title: Require asylum seekers & foreign criminals to be detained on remote UK islands
records.description: Require the offshore detention of asylum seekers and criminals who are foreign nationals on remote UK islands away from the general population whilst providing them with humanitarian aid and shelter. This could keep the UK population safe and reduce the taxpayer burden.
records.further_details:
We believe asylum seekers should be housed on remote UK islands whilst their claims are processed and receive basic humanitarian support rather than being placed in local communities at the taxpayers’ expense. 
 
We believe the Government’s first duty is to protect British citizens and secure the borders. If the ECHR prevents deportations, they should remain there until they can be returned.

records.title: Require public bodies to achieve unqualified audit opinion before raising taxes
records.description: Require public bodies whose accounts cannot be certified with an unqualified opinion by auditors to be banned from increasing taxes or receiving a larger budget the following year.
records.further_details:
If this happens for two consecutive years, all elected representatives for that authority should be unable to stand for re-election.

The UK Government's accounts have not been certified with an unqualified opinion by auditors for three consecutive years. The DWP, HMRC and Ministry of Defence have repeatedly failed to achieve entirely unqualified audits, while hundreds of councils each year cannot get their accounts signed off. The National Audit Office estimates up to £81 billion is lost annually to fraud and error. Yet politicians continue raising our taxes while claiming they need more money. We believe it's time to restore financial accountability.

records.title: Minimum State Pension should equal the National Minimum Wage for under 18s.
records.description: The National Living Wage age for 21+ is now £23,132 (35 hour week; 52 week year). Even the National Minimum Wage for under 18's is £14,560 (same basis). My full New State Pension is only £12,564 after working for a lifetime.
records.further_details:
I believe for 65+ a minimum UK standard of living is £14,500 and the State Pension should match this.

The full New State Pension lags well behind those in Europe (UK only 13th of 28). Even an apprentice, or under 18 worker, is now legislated to earn a salary of at least £14,560. For 18 to 20 year old workers this National Minimum Wage equates to £19,747 per annum. For those who have worked and paid NI and taxes all their lives, we believe a full State Pension of £12,564 is just not fair and equitable and the State Pension should be at least the £14,500 necessary for a minimum standard of living for retirees.

records.title: Disapprove the draft Equality Act 2010 guidance laid on 21 May 2026
records.description: I want the House of Commons to disapprove the Equality Act 2010: Draft Code of Practice for services, public functions and associations, 2026 laid on 21 May 2026.
records.further_details: We are concerned that the guidance published on 21 May 2016 could lead to women being excluded from women's spaces based on their appearance. We think that the guidance will make it harder for trans people to participate in sport as either gender, and that it can limit trans people from accessing toilets and other facilities that match their acquired gender. I therefore think the House of Commons should disapprove this draft guidance.

records.title: Stop plans to use MoD sites for asylum seekers without full local consultation
records.description: Calling on the new Prime Minster and his Government to immediately withdraw plans to use MoD sites for asylum seeker accommodation without full, open and transparent consultation with the local communities and local representatives whose lives will be impacted most.

records.title: Make carbon monoxide alarms mandatory in all holiday accommodation
records.description: We ask the UK Government to introduce legislation requiring all holiday accommodation, including short-term lets and rentals, to install and maintain working carbon monoxide alarms, with mandatory regular safety checks and proper enforcement.
records.further_details: This petition is written by a mother whose heart has been broken forever. My daughter and her boyfriend died from carbon monoxide poisoning whilst on holiday in Bridlington. Carbon monoxide is a silent, preventable killer. No family should go away and not come home. Stronger laws are needed to ensure all holiday accommodation has working carbon monoxide alarms to prevent further devastating loss.

records.title: Ban on sale of disposable BBQs
records.description: We want the Government to introduce a nationwide ban on the sale of single-use disposable barbecues. Disposable BBQs are increasingly linked to preventable wildfires, which  poses a serious risk to public safety, wildlife, and emergency services. Also, disposable BBQs contribute to unnecessary waste
records.further_details:
With increasing pressure on waste management systems and growing climate-related fire risk, we believe action is needed to reduce avoidable harm caused by these products. We are therefore asking the Government to:
 
1. Introduce a UK-wide ban on the sale of disposable BBQs
2. Encourage safer, reusable alternatives through public guidance
3. Work with retailers to support the transition away from single-use outdoor cooking products

records.title: Ensure fair and transparent faith security funding for all faith communities
records.description: Publish clear data on how faith security funding is allocated and ensure all communities can access it fairly. We think this should be done alongside improving transparency, outreach, and support so underrepresented groups, including Hindu community, can apply and receive appropriate protection.
records.further_details: Recent announcements show £73.4m funding, with £40m and £28.4m allocated to specific groups, while others share £5m. Greater transparency is needed to ensure all communities feel equally supported, protected, and fairly treated.

records.title: Introduce a national strategy to tackle the cat overpopulation and rescue crisis
records.description: This strategy should seek to expand affordable neutering, support overwhelmed rescue centres, strengthen responsible pet ownership education, and review measures to reduce irresponsible breeding and cat abandonment.
records.further_details: Animal rescues across the country are overwhelmed, with many unable to take in more cats and kittens. We believe the Government should introduce a national strategy to reduce cat overpopulation by expanding access to affordable neutering, supporting rescue organisations, improving public education on responsible pet ownership, and reviewing measures to reduce irresponsible breeding and abandonment, helping to improve cat welfare nationwide.

records.title: Raise Human Rights Issues in Azad Kashmir with the Government of Pakistan
records.description: We urge the UK Government to raise human rights concerns and communication restrictions in Azad Kashmir with the Government of Pakistan.
records.further_details: Reports state that residents of Azad Kashmir have faced restrictions affecting communication services, impacting contact with families, including overseas Kashmiris. Access to communication and information is important for education, livelihoods, community engagement and the ability to raise concerns peacefully. We call on the UK Government to raise these concerns with the Government of Pakistan and advocate for the protection of human rights, freedom of expression and access to communication services.

records.title: Launch a public inquiry into the regulation of animal experimentation
records.description: We call on the Government to launch an independent public inquiry into the regulation of animal experimentation under the Animals (Scientific Procedures) Act 1986 (ASPA).
records.further_details:
We believe the system regulating animal research is failing. Reports find serious weaknesses in licensing oversight, including procedures approved without regulators verifying substances or protocols, undermining the duty to weigh harm against benefit. Oversight heavily relies on self-reporting, which we feel lacks transparency. There have also been no fines or prosecutions from cases of non-compliance under the Animals (Scientific Procedures) Act 1986 in the last ten years.
 
We believe an inquiry is needed to expose failure, ensure accountability, and advance human relevant non-animal methods.

records.title: General election now – and always call one if a PM is replaced
records.description: In July 2024, Sir Keir Starmer was elected as Prime Minister. His Government introduced measures that weren't in the Labour Party's manifesto and he has resigned. We want an election now. If any PM resigns, their successor should have a mandate from the people and call an immediate General Election.
records.further_details:
We believe many people have lost confidence in the current Government, that we were misled, and we cannot go on like this for a further 3 years. It is time for action. 

We believe the Government has failed to defend our borders from the small boats, and illegal immigration is out of control. We have no confidence in the way this Government has acted. In our view, pensioners and farmers have been betrayed by policies that were not included in Labour's manifesto.

We also feel that rape gang survivors have been badly let down. Justice delayed is Justice denied. Dissolve Parliament. General Election now!

records.title: Ban the sale and consumption of alcohol in House of Commons venues
records.description: I would like the House of Commons to ban the sale and consumption of alcohol within House of Commons venues on the Parliamentary estate.
records.further_details: I believe drinking is incompatible in the modern workplace. MPs have a crucial role in passing laws which impacts the lives of the citizens of the UK. I believe that the consumption of alcohol, whilst making important decisions that can have far reaching consequences, is clearly not in the national interest.

records.title: Mandate standardised cancer training for all GPs in England
records.description: We ask the Government to mandate cancer training for all GPs in England, requiring all GPs to complete mandatory, standardised training on cancer red-flag symptoms, with formal assessment, regular revalidation, NHS England regulation, and GMC linkage to improve early diagnosis.
records.further_details: Early cancer diagnosis saves lives, yet delays in primary care remain. There is no mandatory, standardised training for GPs on cancer red-flag symptoms or reassessment. We call for nationally mandated, assessed, and regularly updated training to improve recognition, reduce delays, and improve patient outcomes, especially for children and young people.

records.title: Lower the State Pension age to free up jobs for young adults
records.description: Lower the State Pension age for workers so young adults that don't currently work have more chance of getting a job.
records.further_details: The longer people are having to work the fewer jobs there are out there for young adults. If the Government lowered the State Pension age we believe it could encourage retirement so that employers might take on a young adult to fill the space – that would help young people get jobs and also help the older generation that have done their bit for society and get to enjoy the last few years of their life.

records.title: Amend standards for PIP to clearly include type 1 diabetics
records.description: Type 1 diabetics do not usually qualify for PIP despite dealing with a dangerous condition 24 hours a day. We believe there is a general lack of understanding and education of Type 1 Diabetes which may affect PIP assessments.
records.further_details: Managing Type 1 Diabetes is a relentless, 24-hour responsibility that requires frequent blood glucose monitoring, insulin adjustments, and careful planning around food, activity, and stress. When combined with the pressures of full-time employment, this can lead to significant physical exhaustion and mental burnout. We believe allowing more types 1 diabetics to receive PIP would provide financial support for helpful technology not provided by the NHS and support individuals to reduce working hours due to the demands of managing the condition.

records.title: Ban balloon releases
records.description: I would like the Government to ban balloon releases due to the devastating impact, misery and suffering they can cause to marine life and other animals, including swallowing balloons, getting tangled in balloons, and dying a painful death as a result of this.
records.further_details: Releasing balloons into the sky can cause mass devastation to wildlife and can endanger the environment. I feel very passionate about banning this practice completely. I believe that if people could see first hand and educate themselves about cruelty and suffering caused by releasing balloons, they would support banning balloon releases completely.

records.title: Hold a referendum on abolishing the Scottish Parliament & Government
records.description: We call on the UK Government to legislate on holding a referendum in Scotland to decide whether the Scottish Parliament & Government should be abolished.
records.further_details:
We believe it has become clear that the Scottish Parliament is not representative of the views of the Scottish electorate, even more so in the recent election, which saw the SNP and Greens receive 57% of the seats but only 41% of the votes cast.
 
We feel the over-representation of nationalist parties in Holyrood has been to the detriment of public services and the wellbeing of the population. We believe there is a growing voice for the dismantling of devolution in Scotland and the return of local, more accountable democracy.

records.title: Reinstate mandatory warning before seizing a vehicle for anti-social driving
records.description: Amend Section 59 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026 to reinstate the mandatory warning before seizing a vehicle for anti-social driving. The Government should instead introduce strict statutory guidelines and body-worn video requirements for officers before immediate seizure to protect due process.
records.further_details:
We believe the 2026 removal of mandatory warnings allow police to immediately seize vehicles based on subjective judgment. We feel this change will result in a lack of due process, creates inconsistent enforcement, and imposes severe financial penalties on motorists without prior notification or an independent tribunal appeal. 
 
Reverting to a 'two-strike' system or mandating strict body-cam evidence could ensure transparency, protect innocent drivers from unfair seizures, and balance anti-social behaviour enforcement with basic legal rights.

records.title: Remove the grey belt planning rules
records.description: The grey belt was introduced as a measure to enable building on poor quality Green Belt such as old car parks, abandoned petrol stations and scrub. We are concerned the planning rules are framed in such a way that high quality Green Belt can be lost to development.
records.further_details:
We think the grey belt policy needs to be revoked.

We are concerned high quality Green Belt is being lost to development and that the grey belt policy is causing great harm.

records.title: Deport all foreign-born criminals & individuals on the terror watchlist
records.description: Deport all foreign-born criminals and individuals currently on the terror watchlist to their countries of origin with effect immediately.
records.further_details: We believe the British people do not need to pay for this, and in an ever-changing World, should not be subjected to having these people as neighbours.

records.title: Require meat to be labelled if religiously slaughtered & stunned or not stunned
records.description: We want the Government to require all meat products to be clearly labelled to show whether the animal was religiously slaughtered (RS or NRS) and if the animal was stunned before slaughter or not-stunned before slaughter (SS or NSS).
records.further_details:
Current labelling rules do not provide enough transparency. In some cases, animals may undergo a recoverable stun and regain consciousness during the slaughter process. We believe this raises important animal welfare concerns that the public should be fully informed about. 

We are also concerned that meat from religious slaughter may enter the wider food chain without consumers being aware of the method used. We believe transparency and informed choice are essential.

records.title: Stop a single Minister having the final say on national infrastructure projects
records.description: Amend the Planning Act 2008 to end the system where one Minister makes final decisions on Nationally Significant Infrastructure Projects (NSIPs). We want this power transferred to an independent panel of experts or decided by a vote in Parliament ensuring transparent and collective decision-making.
records.further_details: One politician can currently approve huge projects like pylons, solar farms or motorways, even if an independent inquiry recommends refusal. We believe this creates a risk of political bias and undermines public trust. These projects affect the environment and communities for generations; they are too significant for one person to decide alone. We feel that moving to a panel or Parliamentary vote ensures decisions are expert-led and carry a stronger democratic mandate for the nation’s future infrastructure.

records.title: Do not extend the BBC licence fee to streaming services
records.description: There are widespread reports that the Government is considering extending the BBC licence fee to include subscribers of streaming services that are not owned or run by the BBC. We believe this is a wholly unacceptable proposal.
records.further_details: Amid a cost-of-living crisis, we believe the Government should be finding ways to save the public money, not expanding their means of taxation. We feel the BBC already has a tarnished reputation, and this move could further diminish the reputation of the BBC.

records.title: Add fish-eating birds to Schedule 2.1 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981
records.description: Amend Schedule 2.1 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 to list cormorants, goosanders and red-breasted mergansers that they may be managed, enabling proportionate control to protect inland fisheries and migratory fish populations where serious damage is evidenced.
records.further_details:
Evidence points to Atlantic salmon being at crisis point — around 90% of principal salmon rivers in England are now classified as at risk, and declared catches are at their lowest since records began. Millions invested in river restoration are being undermined by predation. Course fisheries are also under threat.
 
We believe Natural England licensing is too slow for fisheries managers to respond effectively. Adding these species to Schedule 2.1 will in our view enable targeted, evidence-based management to protect inland fish stocks.

records.title: Coeliac disease awareness training to be mandatory for all catering industries
records.description: Government must require all staff working in a catering service to be provided with basic coeliac disease awareness training, to ensure a set standard of understanding & awareness around the importance of meal preparation & food serving to a person with Coeliac disease including cross-contamination.
records.further_details: Coeliac disease is a chronic autoimmune disorder where the ingestion of gluten - a protein found in wheat, barley and rye, triggers an immune response that can significantly damage the small intestines. I have come across many food industries, who offer gluten free options however, are unaware the importance to prepare this separately to avoid cross-contamination. Coeliac is not an allergy but is chronic disorder and should be taken as seriously as any allergy.

records.title: Reform regulation through the GMC to put patient safety and fairness first
records.description: On 24th March, the Government published intended reforms to the doctors’ regulator, the General Medical Council (GMC). We believe the proposals fail to deliver necessary changes to a system of regulation that is failing doctors and their patients. Instead, we urge the Government to fix the system.
records.further_details: Specifically, reform should ensure that the GMC: legally protects the working titles of doctors, becomes a single-profession regulator for doctors only, has a legal duty of care to the doctors it investigates, applies the criminal standard of proof, cannot appeal medical tribunal determinations, is subject to investigation when complaints are made against it, and returns to a governing body with a majority of members elected by doctors.

records.title: Review discharge of mental health patients
records.description: Why do we allow people struggling with mental health to be discharged alone. We think this is a huge safeguarding issue and not protecting the vulnerable. A review should consider requiring that patients are discharged into the care of someone. We think this could prevent the loss of lives.

records.title: Start negotiations now to Rejoin the EU
records.description: 10 years after the Brexit referendum and 6 years after leaving the EU, it is clear to us that Brexit isn't working. We believe any benefits have been dwarfed by loss of influence, extra costs and the inefficiencies it has created.
records.further_details:
We think it is time for the Government to Apply to Rejoin the European Union.

While we might not get the same deal as before we nonetheless believe that it would reduce the damage caused by Brexit and help restore our influence by becoming a full member of the EU again. The UK is a large country but is still small in world terms. We feel that improving cooperation with our neighbours will help increase economic stability and strengthen international influence, since relying on distant partners alone is not sufficient. We firmly believe that our future is best secured as part of a strong, united and democratic Europe.

records.title: Review and reform laws on keeping wild animals as pets
records.description: Wild animals are inherently unsuited to life as pets, yet millions are kept in UK homes in conditions that fail to meet their complex welfare needs, with a growing trade and weak oversight. We call for urgent review and reform of laws on the keeping and trade of wild animals as pets.
records.further_details: The current legal framework is fragmented and outdated, failing to protect animal welfare, biodiversity and public health. Online trade and weak regulation are driving growth in the wild pet trade. We call on the Government to review and reform laws in England and Wales, introducing evidence-based measures to prevent harm, close loopholes, strengthen enforcement and meet UK commitments to animal welfare, biosecurity, conservation and public health.

records.title: Protect creators' rights: require AI firms to disclose training data
records.description: We ask the Government to introduce a statutory duty requiring AI developers to disclose the copyrighted works used to train generative AI in enough detail for creators to identify use of their work, enforce their rights, negotiate licences and be fairly paid.
records.further_details: Creators need clear rules and regulations that ensure their work is used with consent, proper licensing and fair remuneration. They need transparency about how their work is being used in AI training, accountability from AI companies, and legal protections that respect creative rights. This isn't about rejecting technology, but about establishing a framework that makes AI development fair and sustainable for the creative industries.

records.title: Review & amend immigration rules for Hongkongers with political convictions
records.description: We want the Government to review and amend immigration rules that include but are not limited to SUI 5.1(a) and BN(O) suitability provisions, regarding Hongkongers with politically motivated criminal convictions.
records.further_details:
This is to ensure the sentence does not become an unreasonable barrier to enter and stay in the UK, and that political context is properly considered. An offence name or sentence alone may not reflect the conduct, political context or fair-trial concerns. This can leave Hongkongers affected by political prosecutions without a viable route to protection.

We believe the BN(O) route should remain true to its purpose: providing a viable pathway for Hongkongers facing political persecution, including those imprisoned or facing imprisonment in political cases. We believe politically related convictions should not become a barrier to BN(O) protection.

records.title: Review and refund overcharged UK Student and Child Student visa fees
records.description: International students who paid UK Student visa fees from Autumn 2023 onwards were overcharged £127-£161, confirmed by a House of Lords Committee. The Home Office's own refunds policy allows claims within 5 years but affected students have never been officially notified.
records.further_details: We are calling on the Government to review which students were affected, notify them all and make the refund process clear and accessible. Due to a drafting error in law, international students who paid UK Student visa fees from Autumn 2023 onwards were overcharged - by £127 or £161. This was confirmed by the House of Lords Secondary Legislation Scrutiny Committee. The Home Office's own refunds policy allows claims within 5 years, yet affected students have never been officially notified.

records.title: Review the law on unfit to plead & reform it to protect victims & public safety
records.description: Government to review and reform the law on unfitness to plead, including the judicial powers following a "trial of facts" with the aim to ensuring that victims' rights and public protection are central to outcomes. This review should consider mandatory public safety measures (such as driving bans).
records.further_details: In our view, current laws on defendants "unfit to plead" are outdated and fail to protect the public or deliver justice. Even when a jury finds someone caused serious harm or death, courts have limited powers and may impose no meaningful sanction. We believe that this legal gap denies justice to victims, restricts judges, and risks public safety. Reform is urgently needed.

records.title: Review access to NHS treatment for Retrograde Cricopharyngeal Dysfunction
records.description: We want the Government to review the adequacy of recognition of, and NHS treatment access for, people with Retrograde Cricopharyngeal Dysfunction (R-CPD).
records.further_details:
We believe too many sufferers are dismissed or misdiagnosed before paying privately for treatment - patients deserve better awareness and NHS access to care.

We want the Government to work towards improving recognition and NHS treatment access for Retrograde Cricopharyngeal Dysfunction (R-CPD), a condition that prevents sufferers from being able to burp. R-CPD can cause severe bloating, pain and major impacts on daily life. We believe patients deserve better awareness, referral pathways and NHS access to treatment.

records.title: Dedicated funding for Epidermolysis Bullosa and rare skin conditions research
records.description: Increase dedicated, ring-fenced Government funding for research into rare skin conditions, including all forms of Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB), to accelerate the development of effective treatments and support UK clinical trials.
records.further_details: We call on the Government to provide dedicated, ring-fenced funding for research into EB and other rare skin conditions. Children with conditions such as EB experience severe, painful blistering from birth. Promising gene and cell therapies offer real hope, yet research remains significantly underfunded. We urge the Government to ring-fence funding, support clinical trials, and prioritise these conditions within the UK Rare Diseases Framework.

records.title: Make seizure training mandatory in all child and vulnerable adult work settings
records.description: Our family have been through a lot due to epilepsy. We want the government to change the law so that anyone working in a child or vulnerable adult care setting goes through seizure training as part of their training, before starting the job.
records.further_details: Currently there is no requirement for all staff to receive seizure‑specific training and many settings provide little or no training. We are concerned that this puts children and adults who suffer from seizures at risk. Seizures can be extremely dangerous. Simple training at the start of a new job could save lives. We are asking for this to be mandatory for all nursery, school and care setting staff.

records.title: Mandatory 15-year minimum sentence for all child sexual offences
records.description: We urge the government to amend the Sexual Offences Act 2003 to introduce a mandatory minimum 15 year custodial sentence for all sexual offences against children including grooming, exploitation and rape. Current sentencing does not reflect the lifelong trauma caused to victims.
records.further_details: Child sexual abuse is one of the most serious crimes, yet many offenders receive sentences below 15 years. Mandatory minimums would ensure justice for victims, act as a stronger deterrent, and protect the public by keeping predators off the streets longer.

records.title: Make it illegal to walk dogs during extreme heat to prevent suffering and death.
records.description: Introduce legislation to make it an offence to walk or exercise dogs during dangerously high temperatures (i.e. 25°C and above), to protect them from heatstroke and burned paws.
records.further_details:
Every year in the UK, dogs suffer and die from preventable heat-related illnesses. Many owners are unaware that dogs cannot regulate their body temperature effectively and can overheat within minutes.
 
Hot pavements can also cause severe burns to dogs’ paws. When air temperatures reach 25°C, pavement temperatures can be significantly higher and dangerous.
 
Animal welfare organisations warn against walking dogs in hot weather.
 
We believe this legislation would help prevent unnecessary suffering, raise awareness, and hold owners accountable for avoidable harm.

records.title: Protect raced greyhounds from exports by introducing spay/neuter laws
records.description: Make it law to spay and neuter all raced greyhounds once they finish racing on licensed race tracks to protect them from being shipped around the world to breeding/racing kennels.
records.further_details:
There is strong evidence that raced greyhounds can be sold in the guise of pets to countries where there are little to no welfare laws. British raced greyhounds are found in China at breeding/racing kennels. Some rescued and returned to Britain have been found to be emaciated and bred from up until very old age, over 11yrs old. Many are confined to cages for their whole lives. 
 
I am concerned that the public are led to believe that almost all greyhounds are safely retired into loving homes. Shipping data exists showing the ongoing shipment of greyhounds to breeding facilities in Pakistan where we are concerned that there are outdated welfare laws.

records.title: Detain undocumented asylum seekers and review and strengthen background checks
records.description: Detain undocumented asylum seekers as their claims are processed. No ID then they should not be allowed to wander our communities. Also, review and improve criminal, background and health checks. This could be known as Rhiannon's Law.
records.further_details: Some of the people who are coming into our country are committing crimes, the most heinous crimes. My daughter died at the hands of someone who entered this country illegally and this needs to stop for the safety of other women and children.

records.title: Fund permanent, 24-hour police patrols in Jewish communities
records.description: In the face of a significant rise of antisemitism across the UK, we ask the Government to fund permanent 24-hour police patrols in Jewish communities.
records.further_details: Following the antisemitic attacks, including on voluntary run ambulances that serve the Golders Green Community, we ask that the Government do more than offer what we feel are empty words of solidarity and shock. We believe our community needs a visible and permanent police presence that is on patrol 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. We feel closing police stations and reducing police patrols by foot and car play their part in creating a breeding ground where antisemitic attacks are more likely to take place.

records.title: Ban supermarkets from throwing away food and drink that is safe to consume
records.description: We want the Government to introduce legislation requiring supermarkets to prevent edible food & drink from being discarded as waste. Unsold items that are safe to consume should be discounted, redistributed or donated, with disposal permitted only where they are unsafe or otherwise unfit for use.
records.further_details: Perfectly edible food and drink should feed people, not become waste. France has introduced laws preventing retailers from deliberately making unsold edible food unfit for use and requiring certain retailers to offer donation agreements to charities. We want a similar system, requiring supermarkets to prevent surplus, reduce prices and redistribute or donate safe unsold items. The law should include penalties, while protecting food safety and allowing disposal when products are unsafe.

records.title: Fund culturally appropriate retirement support for Polish veterans and families
records.description: We call on the Government to fund the continued operation of culturally appropriate retirement provision to Polish veterans and their families. Such homes provide culturally specific care for elderly residents. The last home of its kind, Ilford Park Polish Home, is due to be closed.
records.further_details: We call on the Government to provide funding to ensure there is culturally appropriate retirement provision for Polish veterans, such as the Ilford Park Polish Home.

records.title: Extend the NHS Graduate Guarantee to newly qualified paramedics
records.description: We want the Government to extend the NHS Graduate Guarantee to newly qualified paramedics, providing a supported route into employment after completing their degree and gaining HCPC registration, amid concerns about limited vacancies for newly qualified paramedics.
records.further_details: Student paramedics undertake years of demanding academic study and extensive clinical placements to qualify for a vital healthcare profession. Yet many are approaching graduation facing limited vacancies and uncertainty about employment. We believe workforce planning should better align training places with available roles, and newly qualified paramedics should receive the same opportunity for a supported transition into NHS employment as other healthcare graduates.

records.title: Require tracking of companion animal euthanasia to prevent unnecessary deaths
records.description:
Every day healthy and treatable companion animals are put to sleep not because they are old or because they are beyond help but because there are limited places for them to go

Their lives end quietly in pounds, commercial kennels, veterinary practices and rescues, often unseen and unrecorded.
records.further_details:
Stray dogs can be PTS after 7 days

Stray cats rely on charities not councils

Healthy/treatable animals are euthanised with no record, no transparency, no opportunity for reform 

We call on Government to:

* Record when healthy/treatable animals are euthanised
* Publish annual data
* Introduce a nationwide system to protect stray cats
* Scan microchips for Rescue Back Up and registered keeper

Without this data preventable deaths will continue

Every animal deserves the chance to live

Tuks Law

records.title: Require safety assessments and support for children at risk of elopement/ danger
records.description: Require NHS services to provide a safeguarding pathway for children identified as being at risk of elopement, wandering or having limited awareness of danger, including safety assessments and appropriate preventative equipment and support for families.
records.further_details: Some children, including some autistic children and children with learning disabilities, may elope or have limited awareness of dangers such as roads, water and heights. Families can report these risks to health professionals but may not receive practical preventative support. We want identified risks to trigger a safety assessment and appropriate support, such as door/window alarms, window safety measures, identification aids and suitable location technology.

records.title: Automatic extension for Non- Molestation order when it is breached
records.description: The Government should change the law so that Non-Molestation Orders must be automatically extended where an abuser has breached the order and been convicted. Victims should not be forced to relive trauma through further statements and court hearings to prove an already established danger.
records.further_details: Victims seeking to extend a Non-Molestation Order can be forced to relive trauma, submit new statements, and attend hearings, even when an abuser has already breached the order and been convicted. This causes unnecessary stress on the victim and added pressure on the courts. Where a breach has led to conviction and for offences such as stalking and/or harassment or violence, Non-Molestation Orders should be automatically extended without victims having to repeatedly prove the danger they face.

records.title: Introduce an immediate ban on the sale and promotion of smart glasses
records.description: The government should immediately ban the sale and promotion of glasses that contain recording capability. The government should explore using existing laws, such as RIPA, GDPR, DPA to take immediate action, whilst beginning the process of new legislation.
records.further_details:
Smart glasses allow the recording of others without their knowledge or consent and the uploading of this content to the internet. We believe this violates GDPR law and the DPA 2018. There are already reported cases, including unsuspecting women being livestreamed to the internet.

AI capabilities allow people to 'dox' others, in real time, to create an inhospitable environment in our towns and spaces, fostering a climate of fear and menace, especially for vulnerable groups, including children.

records.title: Ban the construction of new AI data centres
records.description: We call on the Government to implement an immediate ban on the construction of any new AI data centres, including approved ones, to protect our people, wildlife, water resources, and environment from the significant and growing impacts of these centres.
records.further_details: We believe their vast demand for water and electricity, contribution to greenhouse gas emissions and continuous industrial noise place an unacceptable burden on communities, wildlife and finite natural resources. We are concerned that expanding this infrastructure risks undermining the UK’s legally binding net zero commitments. The Government should act in the public’s interest by implementing this ban and preventing any avoidable environmental harm before it occurs.

records.title: Urgently review & adjust steel import quota & tariff changes - effective 01/07
records.description:
Either, the timeline for these changes needs extending
The 60% quota reduction needs reducing
The 50% tariff applied after quarterly quota exhaustion needs significant reduction
The impacted commodity codes needs review & reduction
Or a combination of some/all of the above
records.further_details:
UK steel manufacture & infrastructure, is not immediately capable of satisfying the additional demand which the quota & tariff changes are intended to effect
Current changes will have a profound impact on all UK industry, where they have any exposure to the commodity codes affected
Thousands of UK jobs directly jeopardised by current legislation

records.title: New legislation for ponds to have safety measures to prevent access by children
records.description:
Introduce legislation requiring all domestic garden ponds to have at least one appropriate safety measure in place to prevent accidental access by young children.
 - This could include:
- Secure fencing or barriers
- Rigid pond covers or metal grids
- Raised or otherwise secured pond designs
records.further_details:
This petition is inspired by the loss of our 18 month old son, Harry. Since this happened, I have become increasingly aware of incidents involving children drowning in the UK.
 
Children are losing their lives in preventable pond accidents. While parents and carers do everything they can, it is common for toddlers to wander. Risks must be minimised.
 
Other countries have introduced safety laws for private water hazards.
 
We believe England should take steps to help prevent further tragedies.

records.title: Review legal rights to wheelchair spaces on buses and coaches
records.description: Review legislation giving wheelchair users an enforceable right to designated spaces on buses and coaches, regardless of boarding order.
records.further_details:
Passengers without a competing disability-related or extenuating need should be required to follow directions to move, share or fold belongings, with penalties for refusal

Right now, wheelchair users can be denied travel if another passenger refuses to make the wheelchair space available.

Access should not depend on goodwill. The law should require passengers without a competing disability-related need to move, reposition luggage or fold a buggy, and require drivers to take steps to enforce this. Genuine disability-related conflicts should be protected.

records.title: Fully fund Specialist Palliative Care provided by hospices
records.description: Hospices provide vital care yet are dependent on fundraising. Palliative care costs are lower in a hospice than hospital. UK hospices are in financial crisis, having to drastically reduce specialist services for patients and their families or face closure. Hospices urgently need appropriate funding.
records.further_details: On average just 1/3 of funding for hospices comes from government, forcing over-reliance on charitable giving which is no longer sufficient. Over 50% of hospices were in financial deficit last year and nearly 60% of hospices have made or are considering cuts to vital services. Palliative care needs are projected to increase 25% by 2048. Loss of hospices further increases pressure on hospitals and NHS services, is more costly to the NHS, and results in non-specialist care for palliative patients.

records.title: Introduce weekend access to death certification for burials
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce a weekend service for families to obtain death certification promptly after a death, including from Friday evening through to Sunday night and into Monday morning, so that burial can take place without avoidable delay in accordance with religious requirements.
records.further_details: At present, many families are unable to obtain a death certificate outside normal weekday hours because this service is not usually provided at weekends. This means that when a death occurs on a Friday evening or during the weekend, burial may be delayed. For many religious communities, this delay creates serious hardship, as prompt burial is a deeply held religious obligation.

records.title: Require sex specific language in government, NHS, education, and public bodies
records.description: Require Government departments, NHS, education and publicly funded bodies to use the words women, girls, mothers and pregnant women as the primary and default wording in policies, guidance and public messages. These words must not be replaced, removed, diluted or overshadowed by alternative wording.
records.further_details:
We believe clear, sex-specific language is essential to safeguarding and safe healthcare for women, men and children, ensuring that biological differences, risks and needs are properly recognised and understood.
 
We hold that women should not have to see the words woman, girl, mother, and pregnant woman disappear or become secondary. I raised concerns with House of Lords members about language obscuring women’s reality, issues which remain unresolved. The Government accepts sex matters but appears to defend additive wording. We assert you cannot safeguard girls and women if language is deleted or diluted. We believe this recognises the importance of motherhood highlighted by the UN Special Rapporteur.

records.title: Strengthen copyright laws on our voices
records.description: Our voice is a key part of our identity and right now we feel it is inadequately protected by UK law! We are demanding every person in the UK have a clearer, more enforceable copyright ownership over their own voice.
records.further_details:
With advancements in AI technology the ability to replicate voices is becoming alarmingly simple.
In Denmark, there are legislative proposals to counteract this growing problem. There are similar state-level laws in the USA. However we think the UK government is not doing enough on the issue. This lack of enforceable protection by law not only could destroy careers of voice artists but also expose UK citizens identity security which could put us all at risk! 
The Government needs to act.

records.title: Suspend Climate Change Act targets & undertake a full national impact assessment
records.description: We call on the Government to temporarily suspend the legal duties to meet the UK's statutory carbon budgets and 2050 Net Zero target under the Climate Change Act 2008 until Parliament has considered an independent national assessment of their full costs and impacts.
records.further_details: The Climate Change Act targets affect policy on energy, transport, heating, industry and land use. The assessment should quantify public and private costs; impacts on bills, fuel poverty, industry, food and energy security; and land and infrastructure required for solar, wind, networks, sub-stations and storage. It should assess peatland, landscapes and rising electricity demand from data centres. The findings should inform Parliament's decision on whether the targets should continue unchanged.

records.title: Negotiate visa-free stays over 90 days for Britons in Spain
records.description: The UK Government should negotiate a bilateral agreement with Spain allowing UK citizens to stay in Spain for longer than 90 days without requiring residency or complex visa applications. Since Brexit, UK citizens are restricted by the Schengen 90/180-day rule, which has negatively affected many.
records.further_details: Since Brexit, UK citizens are restricted by the Schengen 90/180-day rule, which has negatively affected retirees, second-home owners, remote workers, long-stay tourists and families with ties to Spain. Spain is one of the most popular destinations for British citizens, and many contribute significantly to local economies through tourism, property ownership and spending.We believe the UK Government should seek a reciprocal agreement with Spain similar to arrangements some countries have.

records.title: Create a legally enforceable maximum working temperature
records.description: Introduce a legally binding maximum working temperature of 25°C for all workplaces, covering both indoor and outdoor jobs. Currently, there is an advisory minimum temperature in statutory guidance but no upper limit. We want the Government to change this by introducing a strict 25°C maximum cap.
records.further_details: Currently, there is statutory guidance on a minimum working temperature but there is no legal maximum cap, leaving staff vulnerable to extreme heat We want the Government to set a strict limit of 25°C for both indoor and outdoor work. When temperatures hit 25°C, employers must legally provide cooling measures or pause work. The law must also enforce lower thresholds for more physical roles. Under the Health and Safety at Work Act, we believe 'reasonable comfort' is not  clear enough, & enforceable limits are needed to protect everyone.

records.title: Make admissions to children's indoor play centres zero-rated for VAT
records.description: We want the Government to permanently zero rate VAT from admissions to children's indoor play centres to make active play more affordable, improve access for families and support children's health, well-being and development.
records.further_details: The Government has already recognised the value of children's indoor play through a temporary VAT reduction. Making this permanent could help families access safe, active play all year round. Indoor play supports children's physical health, mental well-being, learning and social development. A permanent zero rate of VAT could improve affordability for families, support community businesses and help encourage healthier lifestyles.

records.title: The North Of England A1 Safety Guarantee: Action Immediate Protection.
records.description: Commit to continuous dualling of the A1 through the north of England to the Scottish Border. Implement immediate, interim safety upgrades —including junction visibility & hazard warnings—to prevent fatal collisions & stop dangerous traffic displacement through local rural villages.
records.further_details: The single-carriageway sections of the A1 in the north of England are an active public safety crisis. Sudden bottlenecks and dangerous flat junctions cause frequent fatal collisions and serious injuries. When crashes gridlock the A1, heavy freight and tourist traffic flood inadequate local village roads, gridlocking rural communities. We need a permanent safety guarantee: a commitment to continuous dualling and immediate, interim safety upgrades to protect lives and the economy.

records.title: Referendum to reinstate death penalty for most serious crimes against children
records.description: We want a referendum on reinstating capital punishment for adults convicted of rape of a child, assault by penetration, both 15 and under, & most serious violent offences (murder/GBH causing permanent harm/death) against children 15 & under where guilt is proven with conclusive evidence.
records.further_details: Hold a national referendum on reinstating capital punishment for adults (18+) convicted of rape of a child or assault of a child under 15 by penetration under the Sexual Offences Act 2003, and the most serious violent offences (murder, attempted murder, or causing grievous bodily harm with intent resulting in permanent injury, maiming, torture or death) against children aged 15 and under where guilt is proven beyond reasonable doubt with conclusive evidence.

records.title: Make performing a Nazi salute a criminal offence in the UK
records.description: We want the Government to introduce legislation making it a criminal offence to intentionally perform a Nazi salute in public (including online) or at public events, except where it is clearly used for legitimate educational, historical, artistic, journalistic or law-enforcement purposes.
records.further_details: The Nazi salute is widely recognised as a symbol of Nazi ideology and the atrocities of the 2nd World War. Its intentional use in public can reasonably be understood as intimidation or endorsement of extremist ideology. It falls outside existing hate speech protections unless targeted at specific groups. We believe a clear criminal offence is needed to address deliberate public use, provide legal clarity and deter its use, while protecting legitimate use, where the intent is not extremist.

records.title: Revoke the BBC Royal Charter, abolish the TV Licence Fee & privatise the BBC
records.description: Abolish the mandatory TV licence fee and revoke the BBC’s Royal Charter. Legislate to transition the BBC into a private corporation, as they did with BBC Studio's. We believe the BBC should compete independently in the media market without state funding & Royal Charter rights, akin to BBC Studios.
records.further_details: We believe the BBC is no longer the trusted ‘backbone’ of Britain it once was, having been linked to multiple scandals and alleged cover-ups. This has driven boycotts and reduced willingness to pay the TV Licence amongst many, alongside the rise of cheaper, better streaming alternatives. In a digital, data-driven era, we feel government control of the airwaves to curb disinformation is outdated. Moreover, we believe it seems unjust that a licence is required for all live broadcasts when only the BBC is funded by the fee.

records.title: Require Dating Apps to Verify Users and Prevent Abuse
records.description: Require all dating apps operating in the UK to verify users using government-issued photo ID and implement measures to prevent individuals convicted of serious sexual, domestic abuse, stalking and coercive control offences from creating or maintaining accounts.
records.further_details: Millions of people use dating apps to form relationships, yet users can often create accounts with little meaningful verification. We believe mandatory photo ID checks would improve accountability and reduce fake profiles. We also believe dating platforms should be required to take reasonable steps to prevent individuals convicted of serious sexual, domestic abuse, stalking and coercive control offences from accessing these services and potentially targeting new victims.

records.title: Criminalise unauthorised development & ban retrospective permission
records.description: We call on the UK Government to amend the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 making it a criminal offence to develop any large-scale space without first securing the correct planning permission.
records.further_details: We are calling on the UK Government to reform planning and enforcement laws, to stop anyone from placing in any green space hard standing or fencing, and from residing/ living there, without full planning permission already in place. We also want  the Government to disallow retrospective permission in these instances thus putting a stop to any lengthy delays before remediation. We want to strengthen powers available to councils and police to deal with unlawful occupation of land where planning permission has not already been granted.

records.title: Ban trades unions from donating money to political parties
records.description: Introduce legislation to prohibit trades unions from donating funds to political parties, directly or indirectly. Unions represent members with a wide range of political views, yet their collective funds are often used to support a single political party.
records.further_details: We believe trades unions funding political parties creates an imbalance in political financing and risks giving disproportionate influence to organisations that are not politically neutral. We feel that preventing unions from funding political parties would help ensure fairer, more transparent and more balanced political competition, strengthen public confidence in the independence of both unions and the democratic process.

records.title: Fund routine screening for bacterial vaginosis (BV) during pregnancy.
records.description: BV has been associated with increased risks of pregnancy complications, including preterm birth. earlier identification and treatment of BV may help reduce avoidable pregnancy loss and improve outcomes for mothers and babies.
records.further_details: Bacterial vaginosis (BV) is a common condition that can occur during pregnancy and has been associated with an increased risk of pregnancy complications, including infection and preterm birth. Current NHS guidance does not recommend routine screening for all pregnant women. We want the Government to fund routine BV screening during pregnancy, to help identify and treat infections earlier and improve outcomes for mothers and babies.

records.title: Review support for ARFID and fund national treatment pathways
records.description: ARFID (Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder) affects thousands across the UK, yet support remains inconsistent - creating a postcode lottery that must end. Around 1.25 million people have an eating disorder, 5% ARFID, yet many cannot access appropriate care.
records.further_details: This is urgent. Without proper support, ARFID can be - and has been - fatal. It does not end in childhood; it can continue into adulthood, where people are often overlooked and left without suitable pathways. We need action now: improved clinician training, more ARFID specialists, and dedicated pathways supporting both children and adults nationwide. No one’s health should depend on their postcode. We need more ARFID clinics and specialists in every city, not just a few.

records.title: Require all schools to teach ADHD & neurodiversity education
records.description: We want the Government to require schools to provide age-appropriate education in every school about ADHD and neurodiversity, to help reduce stigma, improve inclusion and ensure all children, staff and parents are educated about these conditions.
records.further_details: Through my lived experience, campaigns and the free education initiative I provide whilst touring schools with, I have seen the importance of the Government introducing mandatory, age-appropriate education on ADHD and neurodiversity in schools to reduce stigma and improving understanding and inclusion.

records.title: Make it a criminal offence if tenants don't pay rent
records.description: Tenants who refuse to pay rent should be made to face criminal charges similar to theft.
records.further_details:
Some tenants deliberately stop paying rent, costing landlords thousands of pounds and this has to stop.

The Renters Rights Act has given so much more power to tenants and, and we believe landlords have very little recourse nowadays.

We believe landlords need some sort of balance.

records.title: Reform UK Bail Law: Require Passport Surrender for Serious Criminal Charges
records.description: Make passport surrender an automatic bail condition to protect victims’ families, uphold justice and restore confidence in the courts. Prevent criminals absconding while on bail for serious crimes. Currently making this a bail condition is at the discretion of the judge.
records.further_details: Jack Ryan was killed by a speeding driver in 2021, and that driver has never served his sentence. Not requiring the surrender of a passport as a condition within the Bail Act means some defendants charged with serious offences can leave the UK before trial or sentencing, denying justice to victims and their families. The Justice For Jack Ryan campaign calls for passport surrender to become an automatic bail condition in serious criminal cases to help prevent offenders from absconding and restore confidence in the justice system.

records.title: Legislate to protect ILR applicants from retrospective changes
records.description: Keep the 5-year ILR route for people already in the UK and do not apply new settlement rules retrospectively. Future changes should apply only to new arrivals. We support waiting up to 10 years for access to public funds if the 5-year ILR pathway is protected.
records.further_details:
Don’t move the goalposts for those already here.
 
People already lawfully living in the UK should remain eligible for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) after 5 years under the rules in place when they arrived. New settlement rules should apply only to future arrivals, not retrospectively. If the Government extends access to public funds, we support waiting up to 10 years, as proposed by the Justice and Home Affairs Committee, while retaining the existing 5-year ILR route.

records.title: Abolish early release for sex offenders and murderers
records.description: I am a survivor of serious sexual abuse as a child and was raped as an adult. I would like the Government to change the law where anyone sentenced for rape or murder should not be eligible for early release on licence.
records.further_details: I live with my trauma every day, so I do not believe that serious offenders should be allowed to leave prison early.

records.title: Launch a public inquiry into the UK's role in Israeli operations in Gaza
records.description: We want the UK Government to launch an inquiry into any British involvement in Israeli operations in Gaza, including the sale, supply or use of weapons, surveillance aircraft and Royal Air Force bases. We believe the UK has played a vital role in Israeli military operations in Gaza.
records.further_details: We call on the UK Government to launch a fully independent inquiry into the UK’s involvement since October 2023, which would have the power to question government ministers and officials involved in decision-making processes, particularly relating to: what arms have been supplied to Israel, what RAF bases have been used and why; what intelligence was collected during RAF flights; and what legal advice has the UK Government sought in assessing whether a genocide has taken place in Gaza.

records.title: Require local authorities to provide 90 minutes of free parking in town centres
records.description: Introduce a law which requires all local authorities in England to provide a minimum of 90 minutes of free parking in town and city centres to help support economic growth and high street businesses.
records.further_details: We believe Britain's independent retailers are the heart of our high streets, supporting jobs, communities and local economies. Yet many town and city centres face declining footfall. Providing 90 minutes of free parking could make it easier for people to visit local shops, encourage local spending, support small businesses and help revitalise high streets across England.

records.title: Fund & mandate early intervention plans for minors who deliberately harm animals
records.description: I ask for the Government to fund and mandate early intervention plans, which include assessments and education, for minors who deliberately harm animals in order to recognise cruelty as behaviour that requires action, support and prevention.
records.further_details:
As a wildlife rescuer, I have witnessed first hand the devastating injuries and suffering caused by deliberate animal cruelty. These incidents can affect animals, rescuers and entire communities.
 
I believe deliberate animal cruelty constitutes concerning behaviour that should not be ignored. We should have mandatory early intervention plans to understand and address these behaviours early, protect animals and support safer, more compassionate communities.

records.title: Introduce the Right to Breastfeed and Express at Work
records.description: We call on the UK Government to align UK employment law with Article 10 of ILO Convention No. 183 by introducing a statutory right to paid breastfeeding and expressing breaks, together with suitable workplace facilities.
records.further_details: Breastfeeding parents in the UK have no statutory right to paid breastfeeding or expressing breaks at work. This forces many to choose between feeding their baby and participating fully in work. We call on the Government to align UK employment law with Article 10 of ILO Convention No. 183 by introducing paid breastfeeding and expressing breaks, together with suitable private facilities, to support maternal and child health, equality and workforce participation.

records.title: Create a National Disability Hate Strategy for the UK
records.description: Develop and fund a National Disability Hate Strategy, co-produced with Disabled People’s Organisations, to tackle disability hate crime, online abuse, discrimination, public stigma and improve awareness of visible and hidden disabilities.
records.further_details:
Disability hate is rising online and in public. 

Disabled people are abused, questioned and targeted simply for existing. 

Government must develop a National Disability Hate Strategy with Disabled People’s Organisations to prevent hate and better protect victims.

records.title: Hold a national referendum on introducing Digital ID
records.description: We believe Government plans for Digital ID represent the most radical change in our governance since universal suffrage. We want the  Government to put this plan to the people via a referendum before proceeding with what we feel is a monumental shift in how we are governed.
records.further_details: If a new Digital ID system is implemented without full disclosure of what this will involve, we believe there will be no democratic mandate from the governed. We are anxious that this plan might lead to: mandatory digital identification, whether paper or phone-based; surveillance of citizens and recording data on behaviour, location, spending, social media etc; alongside a credit scoring system which could lead to exclusion or denied permissions to participate fully in normal society.

records.title: Establish an independent Veterinary Ombudsman for pet owners
records.description: To establish an independent Veterinary Ombudsman to provide a fair, impartial system for handling complaints about veterinary care. The service should be able to investigate cases, make binding decisions, and ensure accountability across all vet practices.
records.further_details: Many pet owners feel there is no fully independent and effective way to raise concerns about veterinary care. Complaints are often handled by the same practice or limited mediation processes, and the regulator does not provide binding decisions or resolve individual disputes. This can leave owners feeling unheard and without confidence in the outcome. An independent Veterinary Ombudsman would provide impartial investigation, fair decisions, and greater transparency and accountability.

records.title: Reform Carer’s Allowance rules so carers can earn more without losing support
records.description: Many unpaid carers balance demanding caring responsibilities with the need to remain financially secure. We believe the current limit allowable for carers to earn is set way too low. It makes it difficult for carers to work, take on a second job, or rent out property to supplement their income.
records.further_details: Reforming the rules by increasing the earnings limit and reviewing how different types of income (including modest rental income) are assessed would, we believe, allow carers to maintain stability, stay connected to the workforce and support themselves while continuing their essential caring work. Updating these rules would help prevent carers from falling into poverty, improve their financial resilience and recognise the vital contribution that carers make to society.

records.title: Stop DWP additional spouse payments in overseas-registered polygamous marriages
records.description: From April 2026, the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) permits people in the UK in specific, legally recognized, overseas-registered polygamous marriages to receive additional benefit payments, with rates for "additional spouses" increasing to £125.25 per week.
