records.further_details: We believe this should not be UK tax-payer funded.

records.title: End the ban of care workers bringing dependants to the UK
records.description: End the ban on care workers being able to bring their dependants to the UK. Allow them to sponsor spouses, children, or other dependants, even if their sponsorship is issued after 11 March 2024.
records.further_details:
We ask the UK Government to allow care workers already living and working in the UK to be able to sponsor their dependants, including those who are already in the UK.
 
We believe the Government should allow them because if they agree to support and contribute to care services, it could help NHS and Care sector. We request an end to this ban to prevent family separation, as well as ensure fairness and stability for care workers who support the UK care sector.

records.title: Write off Armed Forces Pension overpayments.
records.description:
Veterans are being told that they have to pay thousands back to the MoD after a disastrous pension error occurred, estimated to be around £5.1 million. 
I’m calling for the MoD to have the pension overpayments written off, as the Veterans were not at fault for the incorrect calculations.
records.further_details: Pensions were overpaid for years due to the error, and in some cases Veterans owe back more than £100,000. The problem was first identified by the MoD two years ago, but Veterans have only received letters this year detailing the money they owe. The Forces Pension Society said that there are 398 cases linked to incorrect National Insurance modification rules. The issue has been described as a “failure of leadership, oversight, process and quality assurance”

records.title: Mandatory Prison for Drivers Who Conceal Accidents or Obstruct Investigations
records.description: We are seeking a minimum sentence of a jail term for drivers who are proven to have purposely looked to avoid justice after killing someone in a road traffic collision.
records.further_details: Impose a mandatory prison sentence in cases where the driver of a vehicle knowingly avoids reporting any accident immediately, regardless of whether they believe that have hit an animal, in order to allow drug or alcohol levels in their bloodstream to fall below the legal limits or obstruct discovery of a victim and at the same time has knowingly perverted the cause of justice or not cooperated with the investigation which as a consequence causes significant hurt and distress to the victims’ family.

records.title: Repeal the Hong Kong Economic Trade Office Act 1996
records.description: Pass legislation to close the Hong Kong Economic Trade Office in light of the lack of autonomy Hong Kong now has from Beijing, by introducing legislation to repeal the Hong Kong Economic Trade Office Act 1996 through, for example, a Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office (Revocation) Act 2026.
records.further_details:
Hong Kong’s Economic and Trade Office was granted diplomatic privileges and immunities by the Act in 1996 ahead of the city's handover from Britain to China, recognising promised autonomy under “one country, two systems.” Since the 2020 National Security Law, that autonomy has ended.

The UK Government says China has undermined the “one country, two systems” and the Sino-British Joint Declaration, a legally binding treaty, while Beijing insists Hong Kong is fully part of China. We believe the basis for the office no longer exists, so it should be closed.

records.title: Scrap the planned 2029–2039 Asylum Support and Accommodation programme
records.description: Cancel the Home Office Asylum Support and Accommodation Programme procurement (2029-2039). Shift focus from long-term housing to rapid enforcement. We want to protect taxpayers from multi-billion corporate contracts, ease pressure on local public services & enforce strict contractor accountability.
records.further_details: The 2029–2039 Asylum procurement locks the UK into a massive long-term framework which we believe directly contradicts urgent immigration reform: first, it commits billions of taxpayer funds to unaccountable private corporate contractors under failed models; second, it avoids shifting policy completely from housing to rapid enforcement and deterrence; and third, these vast arrangements in our view place an unsustainable, unfair burden on local public services. We want the Government to scrap this exercise and focus entirely on enforcement.

records.title: Mandate monthly welfare updates and photos for owners of all seized dogs
records.description: I am campaigning to mandate monthly welfare reports and photos for seized dogs I think this is essential to ensure accountability, uphold humane standards of care, and enable timely intervention to prevent suffering.
records.further_details:
Many seized dogs are held in kennels for extended periods. I'm worried that these dogs may return home in poor physical and mental condition.
 
Mandating monthly welfare reports and photographs could help ensure accountability, maintain higher standards of care, and allow for necessary intervention before a dog's health reaches a breaking point.

records.title: Introduce Full Statutory Regulation of the Funeral Industry by Spring 2027
records.description: Legislation needs to be introduced urgently to ensure the prevention of any Funeral Director malpractice including the hoarding of the deceased, degrading storage of the deceased including ashes and preventing the lawful burial of the deceased.
records.further_details:
We need: 
A Statutory Regulatory regime. 
An Independent Governance to oversee the entire sector.
Mandatory Standards and licencing, ensuring consistent care through licensed and Professional standards.
Independent inspections, regular unscheduled checks of premises.
Oversight and accountability, new roles to oversee the care of the deceased, namely a Commissioner for the Dignity of the Deceased and a Chief Inspector.
All of this as per the Fuller Inquiry Phase 2 Final Report and Recommendations.

records.title: Ban access to legal aid funds for illegal migrant appeals
records.description: This petition calls on the Government to prohibit access to legal aid funding for asylum appeals following a rejected claim, which would help ensure that individuals whose claims have been fully assessed and refused are removed from the UK without delay.
records.further_details: We believe the UK asylum appeals system is financially unsustainable. Over 100,000 people are awaiting appeal outcomes, with cases taking 63 weeks on average. Many rejected applicants stay in hotels costing on average £118.87 per night, totalling over £52,000 per person and more than £5.25bn overall. This petition calls for ending legal aid for failed claims and ensuring immediate removal after refusal to reduce costs and improve system efficiency.

records.title: Introduce new penalties for repeated breaches of SEND law
records.description: We call on the UK Government to introduce enforceable penalties where local authorities, schools, academy trusts and responsible bodies repeatedly breach their legal duties to children and young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND).
records.further_details: Current systems, including the SEND Tribunal, mainly resolve individual disputes and do not hold public bodies accountable for repeated or systemic unlawful practice. Children and young people with SEND deserve a statutory accountability framework, including mandatory corrective action, financial penalties and Government intervention powers for continued breaches of SEND law.

records.title: We call for harsher sentencing for causing death by careless driving.
records.description:
• We want the maximum sentence raised from 5 to 20 years.
• We want driving licences to be suspended pending investigation outcome, and only reinstated if there are no charges brought.
• We want consecutive sentences where there are multiple fatalities.
• We want a review of judicial guidelines.

records.title: Mandate anti-racism training for all staff in nurseries & primary schools
records.description: Mandate all nursery and primary school staff in England to complete accredited anti-racism training, including how to recognise, address, and prevent racism in early years and primary school settings.
records.further_details:
Children encounter racial bias from a very young age. Nurseries and primary schools are where attitudes and identities form, yet no mandatory anti-racism training exists for staff. 
 
We believe this leaves many ill-equipped to respond, and children, particularly from ethnic minority backgrounds, without adequate support. Making this training compulsory could equip educators with the tools to build fairer, safer, more inclusive schools from the start.

records.title: legislation for accountability within NHS, Police, CPS and findings of Inquiries
records.description:
We ask the UK government to introduce legislation requiring enforceable measures for the NHS, police and CPS where serious failings or neglibence are identified.
This should include a statutory duty for organisations and individuals to act transparently and honestly during investigations
records.further_details:
Senior leaders within the NHS, Police & CPS must be held responsibile when failures of duty happen.
Following serious incidents in our country that lead to Inquiries, lessons are not learnt, mistakes are not acknowledged and so trust in public services erodes.
Lessons from Inquiries that are expensive to hold, in the first place, must be embedded by law. An example is the Clunis Inquiry where lessons were not learnt or unlearnt because they was no statutory power to embed them in systems.

records.title: Require NHS to offer base line X-rays for children born with a limb difference
records.description: Limb different children have unusual anatomy. Without a baseline X-ray on NHS records, some A&E doctors can’t tell what is an injury & what is the norm for that child. We want every limb different child to have a baseline X-ray at diagnosis, stored and easily accessible
records.further_details: When a limb different child attends A&E following an injury, some doctors cannot tell what is normal anatomy for that child and what is a new injury. Without a baseline X-ray on NHS records, there is risk of misdiagnosis, missed fractures and incorrect treatment. families are left having to answer medical questions in moments of crisis. One single baseline X-ray taken at diagnosis, stored and accessible to any emergency team nationwide, changes everything.

records.title: Allow Charities to continue to re-home adult dogs with historic injuries
records.description: We ask Parliament to include an exemption in the Animal Welfare (Import of Dogs, Cats and Ferrets) Act 2025 allowing registered charities and responsible rescue organisations to continue to rehome adult, healthy dogs with historic injuries or mutilations to the UK.
records.further_details:
Without this exemption, we will be unable to rescue dogs that have lost eyes, tails, or limbs due to abuse, trauma, or past working lives—not cosmetic practices.
We support the Act’s aims, but urge a targeted exemption that protects animal welfare, prevents unintended harm, and allows responsible rescue work to continue, without creating loopholes.

records.title: Outlaw fireworks for the general public
records.description: Outlaw the sale and/or possession of Fireworks for all but accreditted/professional pyrotechnicians.
records.further_details: Fireworks have no place in modern society. They are at best a nuisance to people, pets and wildlife. At worse they are a dangerous projectile which can cause serious bodily harm or property damage. Fireworks should only be possessed by professional pyrotechnicians as they are the only people who should be able to be trusted to use these responsibly.

records.title: Act on UN Commission findings of Genocide of Palestinian Children
records.description: The UN Commission of Inquiry found Israel is committing genocide against Palestinian children. We urge the UK Government to formally recognise these findings and act on its legal obligations under international law.
records.further_details:
The UK Government should adjust foreign policy in accordance with the Genocide Convention and cease arms sales, reconsider its diplomatic positioning on Israel, and hold Israel to account in multilateral forums. 

The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel published a report on 18 June 2026. The report explicitly finds that Israel’s actions constitute genocide and other atrocity crimes against Palestinian children, with evidence of continued violations despite the October 2025 ceasefire. We call on the UK Government to review this report, reflect its findings in UK foreign and domestic policy, and fulfil its legal obligations to act against the genocide of children under international law.

records.title: Extend Statutory Maternity Pay and Leave for Twins, Triplets and Multiple Births
records.description: Extend Statutory Maternity Leave and Statutory Maternity Pay for mothers of twins, triplets and other multiple births. We believe maternity entitlements should reflect the additional care, financial costs and practical demands associated with raising multiples.
records.further_details: Current maternity entitlements are based on the number of pregnancies, not the number of children born. A mother who has two singleton children may receive maternity leave and pay twice, while a mother who gives birth to twins receives only one period despite having two children. We believe maternity leave and pay should better reflect the number of children born and the additional financial and caregiving demands faced by families of multiples.

records.title: Create a legal right to ADHD or Autism assessment within 3 months
records.description: NICE says Autism assessments should start within 3 months. Recent data shows c294,792 people in England are waiting, 86.8% of whom have done so for longer than 13 weeks. For ADHD there is no standard time period at all. We want the Government to make 3 months a legal right for both.
records.further_details: The Government's own review into mental health, ADHD and autism says the system is not working well. NICE says an autism assessment should start within 3 months of referral. In June 2026, c294,792 people in England were waiting, 86.8% of them already past 13 weeks. For ADHD there is no NICE waiting-time standard at all, and up to 959,662 referrals are open. Since 2010 there has been a legal right to start treatment within 18 weeks. Assessment has no similar legal status. Make 3 months a legal right for both.

records.title: Ban the sale of helium balloons
records.description: I'm calling for the sales on helium balloons to be banned. April 2024 we tragically lost our son Joshua on his 8th birthday, due to him unintentionally inhaling helium from his birthday balloon.
records.further_details:
These balloons are not required to come with warnings and can be a silent killer. I believe changing the law could save lives.

I believe had there been regulations and awareness raised on the dangers of these balloons my son's death may have possibly been prevented. I ask for a ban after my son’s death, to prevent another child losing their life due to a tragedy that could be prevented with a ban on sales. I call for Parliament to take immediate action and prevent further deaths happening. One life taken is one too many.

records.title: Require every primary school to have a published plan for outdoor free play
records.description: We call on the Government to require every primary school in England to publish a plan for outdoor free play at breaktimes and lunchtime, and for the Department for Education to produce statutory guidance defining what quality provision looks like, with Ofsted required to inspect against it.
records.further_details: This was a key recommendation of the 2025 Play Commission report. Breaktimes make up 20% of the school day, yet, despite it being essential for wellbeing, no school is required to plan for outdoor free play. They must have carbon reduction plans, but not one for play. With screen time rising and play outside school declining, for many children, school playtime is their only active outdoor play. Play is never inspected. Why does the DfE not care about the quality of 20% of what schools do?

records.title: Fund free GCSE exams for all home-educated children
records.description: We want the Government to fund free GCSE exams for all home-educated children. We believe that they should be free as parents already pay tax, and that decisions to not enrol in mainstream schools, as it can often be too much for many children, should not mean they are denied access to GCSE exams.
records.further_details: Many children thrive from being educated at home, as they feel safe and listened to – things which cannot always be achieved in mainstream schools. Despite this, access to GCSEs is not free of charge for home-educated children, unlike students in mainstream schools.

records.title: Establish a single, powerful, independent statutory regulator for all news media
records.description: The Government must create a single, independent statutory regulator covering print, broadcast, and digital news media. This regulator should have the legal power to enforce truth and factual reporting via a mandatory code of conduct for journalists and prohibit the reporting of opinion as fact.
records.further_details: Currently, UK media is split between statutory regulation for broadcast (Ofcom) and voluntary self-regulation for the press (IPSO/Impress). We believe that this inconsistency allows misinformation to spread across platforms, with varying levels of accountability. A single regulator would ensure a 'level playing field' with unified standards for accuracy and a clear legal distinction between editorial opinion and factual reporting, backed by meaningful sanctions for non-compliance.

records.title: Increase funding and review children’s mental health system
records.description:
Many families with children suffering from mental health difficulties feel as though there is not enough support in place from services such as CYPMHS and CAMHS.
Increase funding and review the children’s mental health system.
records.further_details:
We are looking to see a change in children’s mental health services as there are many families in crisis. We think there should be a complete review of all children’s mental health services.
 
We are seeking for more funding for children’s mental health support. This proposal could better our children’s overall quality of life and give them the support they need in transition to adult life.

records.title: Apologise for the Balfour Declaration and fund the teaching of its legacy
records.description: We ask the Government to issue a formal apology for the Balfour Declaration and Britain’s actions in Mandate-era Palestine, and to commit to funding educational initiatives that acknowledge this history. This should include public resources and curriculum support reflecting Britain’s role.
records.further_details: We believe Britain’s policies from 1917-1948 shaped events that led to the displacement of Palestinians and left a legacy still felt today. Many MPs, legal experts and historians have argued that Britain failed to uphold the rights of the Palestinian population. A formal apology could offer symbolic justice, while investment in education - both in the UK and internationally- could ensure this history is accurately taught, understood, and not forgotten by future generations.

records.title: Seek agreement with the EU to accept pet passports for UK-EU travel
records.description: Seek to negotiate an agreement with the EU to allow UK residents who hold valid EU Pet Passports to use them for travel without needing an Animal Health Certificate (AHC). This would allow UK residents to travel with pets to the EU without repeated high fees and complex admin.
records.further_details: Recent changes prevent UK residents from using EU pet passports, forcing them to obtain costly Animal Health Certificates for each trip. This incurs costs for every journey and creates unnecessary stress and complexity. Dual nationals and frequent travellers are disproportionately affected. A year ago, the Government explored reintroducing a pet passport scheme but has since moved backwards. We believe this risks pet welfare and unfairly penalises responsible pet owners especially dual citizens.

records.title: Repeal all religious exemptions
records.description: Repeal all religious exemptions in law. Ensure laws relating to public safety, animal welfare, and other legal obligations apply equally to all individuals and organisations, regardless of religion or belief.
records.further_details: I feel current religious exemptions allow practices that would otherwise be restricted, such as exemptions relating to religious slaughter and the carrying of certain ceremonial blades. I believe there should be one set of laws that applies equally to everyone, regardless of religion or belief, and that any existing religious exemptions should be repealed.

records.title: Pause military support for Ukraine and hold a referendum
records.description: The government has spent billions supporting Ukraine in the conflict. We believe this has no strategic or economic interest to the UK and that it’s adversely affected the cost of energy and of living. There should be a pause in the policy until there is a national debate and referendum on the issue.
records.further_details: We believe the UK should have remained neutral in the conflict in 2022. There have been many casualties since then on both sides. The UK has officially given Ukraine £16bn in military support and we think now the government is risking British security by its support for Ukraine. Some of the sanctions and policies against Russia have also contributed to the major rise in energy and cost of living costs since the conflict began.

records.title: Add specific content on men’s mental health to RSE & health guidance for schools
records.description: Statutory guidance for secondary schools on mental health should be expanded to include more specific content about men. This should include the importance of men opening up and breaking traditional stereotypes that young men are being forced into by presences online.
records.further_details: I’ve seen the impact first hand that people not opening up can have and the effect it can have on so many communities. So many times in school have I seen men’s mental health month get completely bypassed and unnoticed and how it would give young men a boost to feel seen and heard causing a positive impact on society.

records.title: Expand home university fee eligibility to UK residents without settled status
records.description: This petition is to make UK residents regardless of immigration status or timeline eligible for home university fees. All immigrants living in the UK should have the right to a fair education at higher level in England.
records.further_details: Knowing well that many immigrants are from low income families, we are asked to pay at least 3 times the home fees in tuition alone. Many with no support or help. We work hard, contribute but are held back simply because of a passport colour. We believe this is unfair. We feel that a lot of immigrant children work twice as hard ie work, school, family contributions, just to be on the same level as other kids and are still held back and put on hold by situations they can't control.

records.title: Make it a criminal offence for MPs to deliberately mislead the public
records.description: We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation—similar to the Senedd Cymru Wales (Member Accountability and Elections) Bill—to create a criminal offence for all election candidates who knowingly make false or misleading statements during campaigns, and for MPs while in office.
records.further_details: Electoral campaigns should be fought on the basis of truth and accuracy.  For MPs in office, the current standards regime relies on conventions and self-regulation, which have proven insufficient in maintaining trust. While the Ministerial Code and the MP Code of Conduct exist, they lack the legal power to hold individuals accountable for deliberate deception of the electorate. The Senedd has already taken steps to introduce accountability measures for misleading statements during elections. We believe Parliament should follow this precedent and  ensure political integrity is protected by law.

records.title: Make child maintenance evasion a criminal offence
records.description: It would be child neglect if a parent providing full time care failed to provide a child with food, clothing or shelter. Yet, when a parent deliberately avoids child maintenance, depriving their child of those same essentials, it is not treated the same. It should be made a criminal offence.
records.further_details: We call on the Government to legally recognise the deliberate and persistent evasion of child maintenance obligations as a form of statutory child neglect. Where there is clear evidence that a parent has intentionally avoided providing financial support for their child, the Government should introduce criminal sanctions. Children should be protected from financial neglect just as they are protected from other forms of neglect.

records.title: Define "Significant NHS Experience" as 2-3 years for Training Prioritisation
records.description: Define significant NHS service for medical training prioritisation as two years’ NHS service for entry to core specialty training and three years’ NHS service for entry to higher specialty training. We believe this will uphold fairness and protect the NHS workforce.
records.further_details: In our view, doctors who have dedicated years of NHS service should have that contribution recognised in specialty training prioritisation. The Royal College of Physicians supports defining significant NHS experience as 2–3 years and basing prioritisation on NHS service rather than immigration status. We ask the government to define this as 2 years for entry to core specialty training and 3 years for higher specialty training.

records.title: Launch an inquiry into the psychiatric care and diagnoses of child abuse victims
records.description: In light of the official apology from the Royal College of Psychiatry, we request that the Government launch an inquiry to explore the treatment of victims of child abuse, sexual abuse and domestic abuse who may have been incorrectly pathologised, framed as mentally ill, and wrongly diagnosed.
records.further_details: In August 2026, The Royal College of Psychiatrists published an official apology to victims of abuse, admitting that UK psychiatrists had diagnosed victims, medicated them, and admitting that there is no significant evidence base for "false memory syndrome". Thousands of UK victims of abuse have had their credibility and disclosures harmed by these false diagnoses, including in criminal court, family court, mental health services, and NHS records. We now need an inquiry to establish the scale of this issue and impact.

records.title: Ban service charges on inherited retirement properties while vacant
records.description: The Government should ban retirement-housing operators from charging service charges after a leaseholder's death. Estates must not be billed while a flat is empty, in probate, or stuck on the slow resale market common in this sector. We believe this unfair financial burden should end.
records.further_details: Many families inherit retirement flats that are hard to sell, facing service charges of £5k-14k a year from the day the leaseholder dies. Estates can be billed for years while flats sit empty, unsold, or restricted from renting. It affects anyone with parents in retirement housing and can wipe out inheritances entirely. When the estate's money runs out, payments come from the family's own finances including pensions to stop arrears growing. If they die, the financial burden lands on their heirs again.

records.title: Do not require tech manufacturers to detect nudity content on devices
records.description: Do not require tech manufacturers to scan content taken or viewed by users for 'nudity'. The government announced in June that if companies don’t take steps within 3 months to prevent children seeing nude content online, it will bring forward legislation to force them to activate the technology.
records.further_details: The software does not know which photo contains nudity unless it has already scanned it. We believe the privacy implications of this are enormous and having age verification to disable it is even worse for privacy. The responsibility for stopping children seeing nudity online should be with platforms that host content instead.

records.title: Increase penalties for motorbike and e-bike theft & enable self-defence
records.description: We want the Government to introduce harsher penalties for vehicle theft—especially when filmed for social media—and reform self-defence laws so victims are not unfairly prosecuted for protecting their property from thieves.
records.further_details: Motorcycle and e-bike theft is at epidemic levels in some regions, often driven by thieves stealing vehicles to brag about on social media. We believe current laws are failing as a deterrent, and due to a lack of police action, owners feel forced to protect their property. Shockingly, victims defending their livelihoods can often face harsher legal consequences than the thieves. We call for tougher sentences—especially if crimes are shared online—and reformed self-defence laws so owners aren't criminalized for protecting their vehicles.

records.title: Review slaughterhouse regulation and welfare protections
records.description:
We want the government to review slaughterhouse oversight.
 
- More accountability for facilities & individuals found in breach of animal welfare laws
- Increased transparency of inspections & enforcement actions
- Review the role, structure & accountability of the Food Standards Agency
records.further_details:
Recent undercover investigations have raised questions about whether current monitoring systems are effective. Video evidence showed animals suffering severe welfare violations in facilities where official inspectors and veterinary personnel were present. This raises fundamental concerns about transparency, accountability, and the effectiveness of existing enforcement mechanisms.
 
The UK claims it’s a nation of animal lovers. We must do better!

records.title: No 'Pay per Mile' on EVs and Hybrids in 2028 - just £200 VED
records.description: Scrap the 3p pay per mile tax on EVs and 1.5p per mile on Hybrids entirely, & charge every driver the flat rate of £200 in VED instead.
records.further_details: EV owners already pay a flat rate of £200 per year in VED, so it seems to us the Government wants essentially to tax people twice for using the road. We think It should be one of the other, as pay per mile is a tax on people's freedom, a tax on going on a holiday, a tax to drive abroad, a tax to go to work & a tax to visit the shop. We feel this will just put people off switching to an EV, putting it at odds with the country's net zero targets, and will also put those who own EVs off travelling for leisure, affecting businesses outside of cities.

records.title: End the use of the term child prostitution in official documents and UK Laws
records.description: We call on the Government to remove all references to child prostitution or any other variation of the term prostitution in relation to children. The language used matters and impacts victims for life.
records.further_details: The Government has already recognised this term is inappropriate by legislating to expunge references to it from victims’ records. However, the same language continues to exist in some official documents and legal documentation. We believe this creates a damaging double standard. A child cannot consent to prostitution. Any sexual activity involving the exploitation of a child is abuse. We feel this needs to also be reflected in all official documents and Laws.

records.title: Fund a national pro-building stimulus package to get Britain building again
records.description: Fund support package to encourage house building, including simpler, faster, cheaper rules-based planning consent process powered by AI, and financial incentives for people to buy/improve their homes, incentivise careers in building & construction, accelerate training and talent attraction.
records.further_details: We believe that building & construction, the backbone of Britain’s economy, is in crisis; due to high financing costs, planning gridlock, skilled labour shortages, rising compliance burdens, no financial stimulus for homebuyers. In our view builders & tradespeople are leaving in droves because the economics no longer stack up. Research suggests that 225,000 additional tradespeople needed by 2027 to build 565,000 new homes needed annually to close 6.5 million housing gap. We think if action like that suggested in this petition is taken, construction output could improve. One forecast suggests it would surge by 10% (2026) & 11% (2027) if barriers removed.

records.title: Adopt the "citizen advance": 28-40s may take £12,500 advance & delay retirement
records.description: We call on the government to adopt the Social Market Foundation proposal allowing 28-to-40-year-olds to take a £12,500 advance in exchange for delaying retirement by one full year.
records.further_details: The current cost-of-living and housing crises make it incredibly difficult for young adults to secure home deposits, clear high-interest debt, or invest in career training.A recent report by the Social Market Foundation think tank proposed a "Citizens' Advance." This policy would allow working adults aged 28–40 with at least 10 years of National Insurance contributions to access a tax-free lump sum of roughly £12,500 today. We urge the government to formally consider and debate this policy.

records.title: Create a government-owned, free software for Making Tax Digital (MTD)
records.description: With the roll-out of Making Tax Digital going ahead, HMRC must provide an in-house, government-developed, fully-functional software that allows easy and confident compliance with MTD. Self-employed people should not be obliged to hand data to private companies.
records.further_details:
The relationship to HMRC should be secure and simple with no obligatory commercial intermediaries.

On commercial platforms we can be beholden to: price increases; reduced functionality in free or non-premium versions; software becoming unavailable through company failure. Yes, free software is available, but it is basic and carries the same risks. 

HMRC must develop a government-owned, free software that cannot fail or be subject to the vicissitudes of the market.

records.title: Protect sports bodies from coercive legal actions over inclusive trans policies
records.description:
1 Legislate to give protection to British sports bodies and charities from legal actions that are intended to intimidate them in abuse of the British legal system
2 Until legislation is in place provide funding to all charities and sport bodies who receive such legal actions to help resist them
records.further_details: Several sports bodies have been threatened with legal action because of their policies relating to trans people. We need laws to prevent this and protect charities that are key to healthy lifestyles.

records.title: Appoint independent body to bar elected officials with discriminatory views
records.description: If information comes to light indicating that a candidate/elected official may hold views that could harm people with protected characteristics, as defined by the Equality Act, an independent adjudicator should be empowered to investigate & if appropriate, remove them from the ballot paper or office
records.further_details: Our system needs to be updated in line with the evolution of our nation into a free and fair society. Equal rights are now at the core of our national identity, and our public officials must lead the way. In the modern age it has become problematic on occasions when information has come to light which reveals that due to prejudicial views, a candidate may be unsuited to a role which requires them to represent everyone with fairness and respect. Our system must protect our communities

records.title: Make helmets legal requirement while riding a bicycle or scooter on public roads
records.description: My brother Riley died following a fatal collision in 2021. I believe my brother would still be with us today if he was wearing a helmet. Make it a legal requirement to wear a helmet when you are on a bicycle or scooter.
records.further_details: Wearing a helmet can save lives and reduce head injuries in the event of an accident. This could be called Riley's Law.

records.title: Raise income tax threshold to £18,000
records.description: Before he became Prime Minister, the PM has previously hinted at increasing the tax thresholds which have been frozen since 2021.
records.further_details:
These are currently due to continue to be frozen for the next 5 years. We want the Government to raise the thresholds to £18,000 as we believe millions of people are hurting financially.

The Prime Minister previously hinted at raising the allowances, we believe he is now apparently back tracking.
 
Had thresholds not been frozen in 2021 they today could be around £16,400 a year. Governments are expecting people to take what we feel is a 10 year pay freeze, which I believe is not acceptable.

records.title: Legally require absent parents to undertake medical testing if child is unwell
records.description: We call on the Government to make it a legal requirement for absent parents to present themselves if requested by a medical professional, for medical history or a blood sample if it can benefit the living child in determining why the child is so unwell.
records.further_details: For some children who are unwell genetic testing is required to help medical professional establish the issue. I do not think it is right for absent parents to not present themselves for such testing or to disclose medical history when it can benefit the child’s health. This should therefore be made a legal requirement with appropriate penalties if the absent parent does not co-operate.

records.title: Fund access to tumour treating fields devices for glioblastoma patients
records.description: Fund access to tumour treating fields (TTF) devices like Optune for Glioblastoma patients. Other countries have and we think it's a disgrace that UK citizens are not able to access it on the NHS. Huge amounts are paid for other cancer medicines, so this type of treatment should be funded too.
records.further_details: TTF cancer therapy can extend the life expectancy of Glioblastoma patient by years. Some people in other countries have been wearing the device in excess of 10 years, without reoccurring tumours, yet it's not funded on the NHS. Private health insurance in the UK often funds it for their patients, and in our view, insurers would not fund it if there wasn't significant evidence of life extension! We think UK citizens are being abandoned by their government.

records.title: Ban solar panels in countryside fields or farmland
records.description: The countryside gives us food. We're currently unable to feed ourselves as a nation. Insects pollinate, their habitat is being destroyed by construction. Solar panels add to this massively. Thousands of acres being handed over to them.
records.further_details: I want the government to pass a bill that prevents green fields being used for solar energy. We can use the rooftops of existing building in cities to get solar energy. If we treasure the planet, we can't keep destroying it to create energy from the sun, it has a grave cost. These solar panels that could leak minerals, permanently polluting the land, need to be restricted to cities.

records.title: Retain the 5-Year ILR Route & Fund Faster Decisions on Syrian Asylum cases
records.description: We call on the UK Government to retain the current five-year route to Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) for recognised refugees and to fund quicker processing and decisions of Syrian asylum claims.
records.further_details: We believe that replacing the five-year settlement route with repeated grants of temporary leave could prolong uncertainty, hinder integration and increase costs for both refugees and the Home Office. In our view the slow processing of decisions on Syrian asylum decisions has also left many applicants waiting indefinitely. We urge the Government to maintain a fair, efficient asylum system by preserving the five-year ILR route and fund quicker processing and decisions on Syrian claims. We also call on the Government to ensure that any assessment of whether a Syrian applicant can safely return is made on an individual basis, taking account of their personal circumstances and protection needs, and is not determined solely by reference to the general situation in Syria.

records.title: Require all owned cats to be neutered by six months of age unless exempted
records.description: Require all owned cats to be neutered by six months of age, with exemptions for cats being kept for breeding by a legally recognised and licensed breeder, or medical grounds by veterinary surgeons. Their neutered or exemption status should be recorded on the cat’s microchip database record.
records.further_details:
Female cats can become sexually mature as early as four months old and become pregnant whilst still a kitten. Unplanned breeding can result in unwanted cats, growing feral populations and increased pressure on already overstretched rescue organisations.

We believe mandatory neutering, with appropriate exemptions and status recording through the existing microchip system, could reduce preventable litters, improve cat welfare and help tackle the growing number of unwanted cats.

records.title: Legalise cannabis for adults, take action on past convictions, fund compensation
records.description: Legalise cannabis for adult use, require that criminal records for non-violent cannabis offences be expunged, require a review of past convictions and driving disqualifications, and establish and fund compensation for people who have been harmed by prohibition.
records.further_details: We believe cannabis prohibition has harmed patients, families and communities while helping to fuel organised crime. We want the Government to legalise and regulate cannabis for adult use, require that criminal records for non-violent cannabis offences be expunged, require a review of past convictions and driving disqualifications which we think were affected by outdated cannabis laws, and establish and fund a fair process to compensate those who have been harmed by prohibition.

records.title: Abolish the BBC TV Licence and Introduce a Subscription-Only BBC
records.description: We want the Government to abolish the BBC TV licence fee and make BBC services subscription-based. We believe people should be able to choose whether they pay for BBC content, rather than being required to pay for a TV licence to watch live television or use BBC services.
records.further_details: The current system requires people to pay for a TV licence to watch live television or use BBC iPlayer. We believe the BBC should move to a subscription-based model, allowing people to choose whether they want to pay for BBC services. This would give households greater choice over which services they pay for, while allowing the BBC to continue providing content to those who subscribe.

records.title: Grant Protected Status to UK Trig Points
records.description: Grant UK trig points protected heritage status, recognise them as nationally significant, create a national register, and ensure their preservation through listing, monitoring, and maintenance by bodies like Historic England and Ordnance Survey.
records.further_details: Built between 1936–1962, over 6,500 trig points formed the backbone of Britain’s mapping system. They are historic, cultural, and landscape icons for walkers and communities. Many are now damaged or lost, with no consistent protection. Without action, we risk losing these unique markers of scientific achievement and national heritage forever.

records.title: Amend Public Order Act 1986 to include protections on the grounds of disability
records.description: As it currently stands, the Public Order Act 1986 protects against inciting hatred on the grounds of race, religion and sexual orientation but not of disability. I want the Government to amend that legislation to extend the protections under that Act to disability.
records.further_details: The Public Order Act 1986 protects against publishing content that incites hatred based on race, religion and sexual orientation. Under this legislation, disability is not currently protected in this way and it may be legal to publish content, regardless of how harmful the rhetoric might be to the disabled community. We believe this legislation should be updated and ensure that disabled people are protected against content created to incite negativity and hate.

records.title: Set a firm launch date for Alternative Student Finance (ASF) and the LLE
records.description: We call on the Government to publish a dated timeline for the launch of Alternative Student Finance (ASF), confirm exactly how it will work alongside the Lifelong Learning Entitlement (LLE), and guarantee that students who take out standard loans for 2026 can transition onto ASF without penalty.
records.further_details: The Government first committed to introducing Alternative Student Finance in 2014. More than ten years later, there is still no launch date. The current position is only that ASF will be introduced "as soon as possible" after the Lifelong Learning Entitlement, with no firm date attached to that promise. This is not a request for special treatment. It is a request for a firm date and clear information on a scheme the Government has already promised to deliver.

records.title: Clarify Grey Belt policy for land adjoining nationally protected nature sites.
records.description: Clarify how Grey Belt policy should apply to land adjoining Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSIs), ancient woodland and other nationally protected nature sites to ensure consistent application.
records.further_details: The Government said Grey Belt policy would prioritise poor-quality Green Belt land while protecting genuine nature sites. We are concerned it is being applied inconsistently, with undeveloped countryside adjoining Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSIs), ancient woodland and other nationally protected habitats being classified as Grey Belt despite the National Planning Policy Framework. The Government should clarify the policy and issue guidance to ensure consistent application.

records.title: Fund free lifelong NHS prescriptions for organ transplant recipients
records.description: Update the medical exemption criteria to make all post-transplant maintenance medications free on the NHS in England, ending the geographical inequality with the rest of the UK and preventing costly graft failures.
records.further_details: Transplants are lifesaving, not a cure. Many recipients face a heavy lifelong medication routine, sometimes starting at 30+ daily tablets. Prescriptions are free in Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland, but not in England. Prepayment Certificates don't stop the financial strain, which may risk missed doses and graft failure. With dialysis costing up to £35k/year vs. cheaper maintenance, we believe charging patients is a dangerous false economy.

records.title: Stop the introduction of driverless cars
records.description: Stop the introduction of the commercial use of driverless taxis and other driverless passenger transport services, and protect the livelihoods of over 400,000 licensed private hire and Hackney carriage drivers by preventing their replacement with autonomous vehicles.
records.further_details: Driverless cars could threaten the livelihoods of hundreds of thousands of licensed private hire and Hackney carriage drivers. We believe the Government should prioritise protecting jobs and ensuring public safety before allowing commercial autonomous taxi services. We want the Government to prohibit the commercial operation of fully driverless passenger transport services and prevent operator licences being issued for these services.

records.title: Make parents legally responsible for their children's crimes against wildlife
records.description: There have been multiple reports of children torturing and killing wild animals. Change the law and prosecute the parents for their children's crimes.
records.further_details: I believe if this is left unchecked then these children will grow up believing that it's acceptable to harm or kill wild animals. It could become a natural part of their behaviour. We believe we need stricter laws to stamp out animal cruelty, especially with children.

records.title: Fund improved aftercare, support & advice for mothers after caesarean sections
records.description: We call on the UK Government to fund improved post-caesarean aftercare across the NHS including standardised scar-care, abdominal rehabilitation, pelvic health & mental-health support. With caesareans accounting for around 45% of births (& increasing) mothers require consistent, specialist aftercare
records.further_details: In our view, post-caesarean aftercare urgently needs improvement. We call for standardised scar care, abdominal rehabilitation, pelvic health and mental-health support. We believe this should be basic care following major abdominal surgery. With caesareans accounting for around 45% of UK births and increasing, we call on aftercare to evolve. “Rest and don’t lift anything heavy” is not enough now. Mothers deserve consistent, evidence-based support and properly trained professionals to improve recovery and outcomes.

records.title: Require independent investigations of police officers accused of sexual offences
records.description: Legislate to require every allegation of a sexual offence against a serving or former police officer, and every allegation of abusing a policing role for a sexual or intimate relationship, to be investigated by an independent body established by law. This could be called Harriet’s Law.
records.further_details: Police officers hold unique powers and positions of public trust. Allegations of sexual offences or abuse of a policing role for a sexual or intimate relationship should always be investigated by a statutory independent investigative body. Harriet's Law would safeguard victims, strengthen public confidence in policing, ensure accountability, improve transparency, reinforce the integrity of the criminal justice system, and encourage victims to come forward without fear of institutional bias.

records.title: Make species-specific training, advice and care mandatory for pet shop staff.
records.description: Pet shops in the UK may give outdated or harmful advice, leading to poor care and preventable illness. There is no legal requirement for species-specific knowledge. We call on the Government to make these training and care standards mandatory.
records.further_details: Pet shops are often the first source of advice for new owners, yet there is no requirement for staff to have species-specific knowledge. This can result in incorrect guidance on diet, lighting, and housing, leading to preventable illness and suffering. Mandatory training could improve welfare and ensure owners receive accurate, responsible advice.

records.title: Fund access to GLP-1 medications on the NHS for women with PCOS/PMOS
records.description: Fund NHS access to GLP-1 medication for women with PCOS/PMOS, especially those with obesity and insulin resistance.  We believe this could help treat debilitating symptoms, support weight loss, improve metabolic health and fertility, & reduce physical and mental health impact of the condition.
records.further_details: PCOS/PMOS can cause severe weight gain, insulin resistance, chronic pain, irregular periods, poor mental health and infertility, yet, in our view, treatment options on the NHS remain limited. For many women, obesity linked to PCOS worsens symptoms and long-term health risks. Some studies suggest GLP-1 medications can support weight loss, improve insulin resistance and help manage symptoms. We believe women with PCOS/PMOS should be able to access these treatments on the NHS where clinically appropriate.

records.title: Require a £22 per hour minimum wage and overtime play for HGV drivers
records.description: Introduce a specific minimum £22/hour wage for UK HGV drivers and mandate overtime pay. Driving heavy vehicles carries high legal risks, long hours, and severe exhaustion. We believe pay must match HGV driver daily responsibilities to reflect hazards and liability. Overtime must be legally paid.
records.further_details: HGV driving demands professional qualifications, medical fitness, and strict adherence to regulations. Drivers face extreme fatigue, high accident risks, and strict personal legal liability on UK roads. Despite this, we feel wages have stagnated, overtime pay has been removed, and many drivers may earn less than unskilled, low-risk jobs. We are concerned that this drives experienced logistics staff out of the sector. The UK Government must legislate to protect HGV drivers' earnings.

records.title: Immediately pause the early release scheme and establish a review
records.description: In July 2024, the Government announced that sentences for serious violent offences of four years or more, as well as sex offences, would be automatically excluded from the new early release scheme. What we were promised has now changed and some of the most violent offenders are set to be released.
records.further_details:
We call for an immediate pause to this scheme and a full review. We believe those convicted of serious violent offences, including domestic abuse offences such as controlling or coercive behaviour, non-fatal strangulation and stalking, should be excluded from early release.

We were promised that those convicted of the most serious crimes and sentenced to 4 years+ would be excluded. We believe the Government has U-turned and begun including these individuals for early release. This leaves many victims feeling as though justice has not been delivered. We believe it is an insult to survivors across the nation and risks the public losing confidence in reporting crimes, when that is already such a significant issue.

records.title: Suspend licences after fatal or serious road collisions
records.description: Introduce a law requiring immediate suspension of a driver’s licence after a road traffic collision causing death or serious injury, pending a full investigation, with a right to appeal.
records.further_details: Drivers involved in fatal or serious collisions may continue driving while investigations are ongoing. This can be distressing for families and may put others at risk. A temporary suspension would not assume guilt but would reflect the seriousness of the situation while investigations take place, helping improve safety and public confidence.

records.title: Allow clinical and biomedical scientists to use patient group directions.
records.description: Patient Group Directions are already used safely by nurses, pharmacists and allied health professionals. We want the Government to extend this framework to trained and statutory regulated clinical scientists and biomedical scientists, with suitable governance, training and competency frameworks.
records.further_details: The Commission on Human Medicines (CHM) has already considered this issue. In 2023 it supported PGD use by clinical and biomedical scientists for diagnostic PGD's with appropriate training and oversight. Expanding this to therapeutic PGD's, could provide timely access to treatment, reduce delays and referrals, remove repeat visits, ease workforce pressures and improve patient outcomes. We therefore urge the Government to build on CHM’s findings and update the legal framework.

records.title: Establish a Pathway to Permanent Settlement for Ukrainians in the UK
records.description: Provide a pathway to permanent settlement (Indefinite Leave to Remain) for Ukrainians under humanitarian schemes who are already contributing to the UK economy but are forced to live in uncertainty for almost 5 years many with no place to return due to destroyed homes or hostile territory occupation
records.further_details: Over 200,000 Ukrainians live in the UK, many of whom are employed, and with children who often are deeply rooted in local schools and colleges. While we understand the Government’s respect for the Ukrainian government's repatriation desire, we think displaced people should be treated with dignity and choice, not as resources to be automatically returned. In our view this uncertainty inflicts severe distress. Aligning with European nations offering residency paths, we respectfully urge the Government to provide a structured route to settlement.

records.title: Make all manufactured gluten-free foods VAT-free & help reduce their cost
records.description: Manufactured gluten-free foods are essential for people with coeliac disease and intolerance, yet they are often very expensive. We call on the Government to remove VAT and seek to reduce production costs to ensure fair pricing and access to necessary dietary products.
records.further_details: The cost of living for coeliacs feels extortionate. People who have coeliac disease rely on a strict gluten-free diet to stay healthy. However, gluten-free foods are significantly more expensive than standard products, placing a constant financial strain on families. What should be a medical necessity is treated as a premium lifestyle choice, limiting options and accessibility. No family should have to pay more simply to keep their child well, and this inequality needs to be addressed.

records.title: Animal cruelty & Neglect cases at Court  should be charged per animal.
records.description: We believe that each animal's suffering from Abuse/Cruelty or Neglect, should be charged to reflect this. One charge per animal. We also request that  sentencing guidelines  reflect single charge per single animal. Every animal deserves justice and stronger sentences will act as a deterrent.
records.further_details: Currently animal cruelty laws and sentencing is not harsh enough. We still continue to see mass harm coming to multiple animals. Each animal should be treated as a separate case and charged accordingly. It cannot continue whereby harming one animal or 50 animals incurs the same sentence. Each animal deserves justice and we call upon Parliament to make the changes for all animals and to stop mass cruelty of animals to go unnoticed again.

records.title: Ban meat and dairy advertising
records.description: We think billions of animals suffer in factory farms while meat and dairy ads hide the cruelty. Ban meat and dairy ads to support humane, sustainable, plant-based choices. The less people see these advertisements, kinder choices can be made. Help to save animals lives by stopping advertisements.
records.further_details: We believe meat and dairy ads hide the cruelty of factory farming behind misleading images of happy animals. Billions suffer each year in inhumane conditions while consumers are encouraged to support these industries. In our view banning these ads would promote compassion, encourage sustainable plant-based choices, and align advertising with ethical values. End the promotion of animal cruelty and support a kinder, healthier, and more honest future for animals, people, and the planet.

records.title: Enact military, diplomatic & economic sanctions on Israel for attacks on Lebanon
records.description: The UK Government should enact military, diplomatic and economic sanctions against Israel unless they stop their attacks on Lebanon, end their invasion, and withdraw from Lebanese territory. We believe Israel should also pay compensation for the destruction of civilian infrastructure.
records.further_details: We believe the Lebanon should not suffer indiscriminate attacks because of Hezbollah or Israel. The widespread destruction of civilian infrastructure means major rebuilding is vital. Over 1 million people have been displaced so far, and this could lead to more refugees seeking a better life in the U.K. and other countries. We are concerned that inaction on this could encourage the Israeli Government to feel they are untouchable. Thus, we believe the UK Government must take firm action to help reverse this situation.

records.title: Increase the personal tax allowance threshold to £20,000
records.description: The personal allowance has been frozen while living costs have risen, meaning workers pay more tax in real terms. Increasing it to £20,000 would put more money into millions of workers’ pockets, helping with rising bills and supporting low and middle earners.
records.further_details: The personal allowance has been frozen since 2021 while living costs have risen sharply, meaning workers are paying more tax in real terms. As wages increase slightly to keep up with inflation, more people are pulled into paying tax or higher rates. Increasing the threshold to £20,000 would put more money into millions of workers’ pockets, ease financial pressure, and support low and middle earners during a cost of living crisis.

records.title: Reduce maximum weekly working hours to 32 & introduce statutory overtime pay
records.description: Amend the Working Time Regulations to reduce the legal maximum baseline working week to 32 hours from 48 hours, maintaining current pay levels (100:80:100 model). Make it a legal requirement that any hours worked beyond 32 hours a week be paid statutory overtime across all sectors.
records.further_details: A 40-hour work week can cause extreme burnout. UK trials by Cambridge/Salford universities proved that a four-day week model is an economic success: businesses saw a 35% revenue increase compared to a similar period from previous years, a 65% drop in sick days, and a 57% drop in turnover. Crucially, reducing the legal hour limit could ensure that 24/7 sector staff (like nurses) receive a vital pay rise through overtime for hours worked beyond 32. We need time back, not compressed hours. The data proves we can work smarter, not longer.

records.title: Make directly threatening action based on a constituency’s voting record illegal
records.description: We believe that voters should feel free to vote for whatever candidate they prefer, and not be guided by threats of Government action in the constituency based on the voting record of that constituency, and that therefore making such threats as a part of political campaigning should be illegal.
records.further_details: A recent political campaign stated that detention centres would be placed in constituencies which were not voting for a specific party, and we believe that this can be perceived as a threat by many. In our view political campaign standards need to become more robust to ensure this type of threat is not acceptable.

records.title: Cease and ban all UK trade with Israel due to its occupation of Palestine
records.description: We urge the UK Government to cease all trade with the State of Israel concerning the Occupied Palestinian Territories (oPt) and ban UK businesses from trading with Israel in this regard. We believe Palestinian-led businesses in the oPt should have direct UK trade without Israeli involvement.
records.further_details:
We believe the UK is under a legal obligation not to recognise, aid, or assist in the maintenance of Israel’s unlawful presence in the Occupied Palestinian Territories, including all illegal settlements (see ICJ Advisory Opinion July 2024, paras 274-279 and UNGA res 77126 and 32/161).

We believe that UK trade with Israel is currently in breach of international law. According to UN General Assembly Resolution 2625 of 1970, the UK has a duty to promote the self-determination of the Palestinian people, and we believe the UK Government must amend its policies and practices to fulfil this duty.

records.title: Fund a public health campaign to reduce the stigma of suicide
records.description: Fund a multi-year campaign which should include mass media, social media, workplace toolkits, promotion in schools and universities, media collaboration and clear support signposting. Over five years, this should include development, pilots, evaluation and targeted campaigns for high risk groups.
records.further_details:
Suicide is the biggest killer of young people, and is on the rise across the UK. Between 2012-2022, 73% of people who died by suicide were not mental health service patients, and we believe that stigma often stops people seeking help. A public health campaign could engage with suicide prevention charities and:
• Normalise conversations about suicide
• Increase public confidence in talking about suicidal thoughts
• Encourage early help-seeking
• Reduce shame and fear associated with suicidal feelings

records.title: Commission review of NICE guidelines on optimal TSH target & thyroid shared care
records.description: Review NICE Guideline NG145. For symptomatic patients, mandate targeting lower optimal thyroid levels. NHS England to standardize lab ranges, allow GP-led Free T3/Antibody tests, stop generic brand-switching, mandate standardized patient education & create a specialist digital shared care pathway.
records.further_details: We believe UK thyroid care relies on an out-dated "one-size-fits-all" model that leaves patients facing many secondary health issues. Varied UK lab limits can cause symptoms to be dismissed, while pharmacy brand-switching can cause filler side effects. We feel that this crisis strains the NHS with costly secondary care referrals for unmanaged complications, while driving major workplace absenteeism. We want standardised education and testing, a wider range of treatments, and shared expert care where symptoms persist.

records.title: Create an applied pathway within GCSE English and Maths,  like Functional Skills
records.description: Create an applied assessment pathway within GCSE English and Maths based on existing Functional Skills assessment methods. Students would still achieve a GCSE qualification, but could demonstrate the same literacy and numeracy skills through an applied, criterion-referenced assessment pathway.
records.further_details: Over 200,000 young people each year leave school without a Grade 4 pass in GCSE English and maths. Many later pass Functional Skills qualifications, showing they have the required skills but struggle with the assessment format. We want GCSE English and maths to include an applied assessment pathway, based on existing Functional Skills methods, so students can demonstrate the same skills and still achieve a GCSE qualification.

records.title: Review FCDO procedures for supporting investigations into British deaths abroad
records.description: We believe the UK government should take a more active role in ensuring that deaths of British nationals abroad are properly examined.
records.further_details:
There is clear public concern given the number who travel each year. families report difficulty accessing information, evidence, & transparent investigations. After my brother, Regan, died in Thailand, we urge the UK government & FCDO to urgently review procedures, improve transparency and ensure access to information.
 
We would like an independent review process that families can access to assess the processes, support and actions taken by UK authorities, including the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office when handling the deaths of British nationals overseas.

records.title: Introduce ban on keeping wolves in captivity
records.description: We call on the Government to enact a legislative ban on keeping wolves in captivity including all zoos and wildlife parks.
records.further_details: We believe the "Wildwood Five" tragedy proves the Zoo Licensing Act 1981 is failing social apex predators, and that wolves' natural instincts for dispersal and hierarchy are incompatible with the physical constraints of UK parks. We feel we need to phase out the public exhibition of wolves, and instead prioritise specialist, non-public sanctuaries. The Government should act to end "management" culling and modernise laws that we feel are no longer fit for purpose.

records.title: Add Endometriosis to NHS Medical Exemption List for Free Prescriptions
records.description: We want the Government to add endometriosis to the list of qualifying long-term medical conditions that entitle patients in England to Medical Exemption for free NHS prescriptions. Endometriosis is a recognised incurable chronic inflammatory condition that requires lifelong medical treatment.
records.further_details:
Women and people with endometriosis often require lifelong or long-term prescription medication to manage an incurable chronic disease, including hormone suppression, pain relief, bladder medication, bowel medication and treatment for related complications.
Despite this, endometriosis is not currently recognised as a qualifying condition for an NHS Medical Exemption Certificate, meaning many sufferers must pay prescription charges indefinitely simply to manage a disease that cannot be cured.

records.title: Mandate parental CCTV access in childcare settings after safeguarding incidents
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce a legal right for parents to have clear, timely CCTV access in all childcare settings and nurseries within a set timeframe, following a safeguarding incident involving their child.
records.further_details: This should include prompt viewing or provision of relevant footage, subject to safeguards protecting other individuals. We are concerned that current processes can leave parents waiting weeks, navigating SARs and receiving transcripts instead of seeing what happened. CCTV can be crucial to understanding incidents, challenging inaccuracies and ensuring accountability. We are calling for a standard timeframe and clear, mandated access, with measures to protect other children’s privacy.

records.title: Mandate diabetes awareness training for all childcare professionals & educators
records.description: Recently, my world was turned upside down when a family member was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes. One thing that struck me deeply was the realisation that so many childcare professionals and educators lack adequate training to recognise the symptoms of type 1 diabetes.
records.further_details: Type 1 diabetes is a life-threatening condition that affects approximately 1 in 500 children in the UK alone (Diabetes UK). We believe immediate recognition of its symptoms—such as excessive thirst, tiredness, frequent urination, and unexplained weight loss—is crucial for early intervention to prevent DKA (diabetic ketoacidosis) which is fatal if left untreated. Unfortunately, many children continue to attend educational settings where professionals are not equipped to identify these signs.

records.title: More funding for Lipoedema and Lymphoedema care on the NHS
records.description: Currently there is no treatment for Lipoedema or Lymphoedema available within the NHS. We believe we need more funding for training and for more specialists in all parts of the country, along with the treatments such as liposuction to be funded on the NHS
records.further_details: Lipoedema is a chronic, progressive condition that is often misdiagnosed as obesity, leading to delayed care and worsening symptoms. Access to Lymphoedema clinics currently depends on location, forcing many patients to self-fund essential treatment such as liposuction as this is not available on the NHS. We believe enhanced funding for early diagnosis and appropriate NHS care would improve quality of life and reduce long-term costs.

records.title: Amend microchip rules to prevent stolen pets being re-registered without consent
records.description: We call on Defra to amend The Microchipping of Cats and Dogs (England) Regulations 2023. Databases must not transfer keeper registration for a lost or stolen pet if the original keeper is contactable and has not given consent. This could stop thieves or finders re-registering pets in their name.
records.further_details: Microchipping is meant to reunite lost and stolen pets. Databases claim the current regulations force them to record the new “keeper” (where the animal lives) and transfer details even when the original owner is known. We believe that re-registration of reported lost or stolen pets must not override the rights of the original keeper. We feel that this loophole undermines the Pet Abduction Act 2024 and defeats the purpose of microchipping. Defra must close it to protect owners, deter theft and improve trust in the system.

records.title: Review Local Government Reorganisation decisions
records.description: This petition asks the government to review recent Ministerial decisions on Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) particularly in relation to the size and practicality of councils in rural areas.
records.further_details: The Government has recently announced government plans for LGR. In our view, this announcement ignored all 6 of the criteria originally outlined by Government. We think that the proposals pay no attention to community cohesion, local context or residents’ views and do not support devolution. We think the rural parts of shire counties such as Devon, Lincs, Leics, Notts and Rutland will become unitary councils far too large in geographical area and numbers of elected members, yet the proposals put people further away from decision-making.

records.title: Lift the ban on new UK oil & gas exploration licences to improve energy security
records.description: With ongoing wars pushing up global energy prices and increasing reliance on volatile imports, we call on the Government to immediately lift the ban on new oil and gas exploration licences, approve viable projects and support domestic drilling to secure affordable energy for families and businesses.
records.further_details: We believe this will strengthen energy security, protect jobs, generate tax revenue for public services and reduce exposure to international crises while we transition to renewables and scale up nuclear. Recent maps show we have significant untapped potential that we feel should be responsibly developed now. In an unstable world, energy security is national security.

records.title: Reintroduce capital punishment for child murder, rape and abuse offences
records.description: We want the Government to pass a law to reintroduce capital punishment for the most serious crimes against children, including child murder, rape, and extreme abuse.
records.further_details: We believe that crimes such as the murder, rape, and severe abuse of children are among the most serious offences that can be committed. Recent cases have caused significant public concern and many people feel that current punishments do not adequately reflect the severity of these crimes. We want the Government to change the law to allow the strongest possible penalty for those convicted of the most heinous crimes against children.

records.title: Provide more funding and aid for children's education in Gaza
records.description: We ask the Government to provide funding and support for teachers and educators in Gaza to help children access education, ensuring they have the chance of a future once the war has ended. They need new schools that are safe, and teachers to teach them, who aren't worried about being hurt or killed.
records.further_details: In Gaza, education has been completely disrupted since October 2023 for over 625,000 children and 22,000 teachers. Some reports indicate that over 21,000 children and more than 1,000 teachers and school staff may have been killed, and that around 90% or more of schools have been damaged or destroyed. We are shocked and want this to stop. Article 28 of the UN Rights of A Child says that all children have the right to education.

records.title: Fund awareness, care and treatment of Stiff Person Syndrome
records.description: Provide funds to improve awareness of Stiff Person Syndrome (SPS), recognise the value of patient lived experience, increase access to specialist care, remove unnecessary barriers to clinically appropriate medications, including treatments not routinely available in the UK.
records.further_details: SPS is a rare, brutal, catastrophic progressive condition, causing excruciating muscle spasms, rigidity & falls. Due to the triggers of the disease, patients often end up housebound unable to leave their homes. Most GP's have never met patients diagnosed with this condition so have little understanding of how truly debilitating it is. Gaining access to appropriate medications alongside dealing with the brutality of the disease is exhausting. We desperately need access to diazepam nasal spray.

records.title: Fund access to lipreading classes, and classify as Health and Wellbeing course
records.description: Lipreading courses can be essential rehabilitation for anyone who has lost some or all of their hearing. Therefore the Government should fund access to them and ensure they are classified as health and wellbeing courses rather than leisure activities, to recognise their importance.
records.further_details: They can teach communication skills, coping in noise, problem solving, understanding hearing aids and the ear, and managing tinnitus.

records.title: Require independent adjudication for private toll penalties
records.description: We call on the UK Government to require that all penalty charges issued by privately operated toll roads with statutory enforcement powers are subject to independent adjudication by an approved tribunal.
records.further_details:
Some privately operated toll roads in England have enforcement powers similar to local authorities, but motorists may not have access to a fully independent appeals process.

We believe motorists should have the same right to independent adjudication as for local authority penalties.

The Government should require these operators to join an approved tribunal scheme, such as the Traffic Penalty Tribunal, to ensure fairness and consistency.

records.title: Introduce a Bereaved Parent Support Framework following the death of a child
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce a national Bereaved Parent Support Framework, including improved transitional financial support and proactive bereavement care in the form of GP contact within 14 days of a child's death and dedicated bereavement support for surviving siblings.
records.further_details: When a child dies, parents are often left without structured support at the most devastating time of their lives.
