Financial support can end after a few weeks, mental health support is rarely offered proactively, and surviving siblings often receive little help. We call on the Government to introduce a Bereaved Parent Support Framework, including improved transitional financial support, and proactive bereavement care in the form of GP contact within 14 days and dedicated bereavement support for siblings.

records.title: Extend NHS Learning Support Fund Eligibility to fully include MPharm Students
records.description: We ask the Government to fully include MPharm students in the NHS Learning Support Fund. We believe pharmacists are essential to NHS services, including Pharmacy First, yet many pharmacy students receive less support than other healthcare students despite completing clinical placements.
records.further_details: Despite completing clinical placements and training for a frontline healthcare profession, MPharm students do not receive the same financial support as many other healthcare students. Fully including pharmacy students in the NHS Learning Support Fund could promote fairness, reduce financial hardship, support recruitment into the profession, and help ensure the NHS has the pharmacy workforce needed to deliver its future healthcare ambitions.

records.title: Introduce stronger welfare regulations for pet care services
records.description: We want the Government to introduce a Pet Care Regulations Bill to mandate licensing for all commercial pet care services, including pet sitters and dog walkers, groomers & trainers, and require welfare training, enhanced DBS checks, public liability insurance and an animal cruelty public register.
records.further_details:
We believe unregulated pet care puts animals and owners at risk. Anyone can offer pet care or dog walking without stringent checks, training or insurance, which can leave animals at risk and homeowners exposed. Unregulated platforms and no ID checks can allow unsafe, even underage, operators. 
 
We are calling on the Government to introduce mandatory licensing for commercial pet sitters and dog walkers, requiring welfare training, enhanced DBS checks, public liability insurance and a central public register, similar to the sex offenders register, for anyone convicted of animal cruelty, to protect pets and reassure owners.

records.title: Increase support and awareness to help IPF sufferers
records.description: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) is life limiting. There is no cure, it's caused by scarring on the lungs which gets worse, breathing reduces, you end up reliant on oxygen & death is inevitable. Once diagnosed we experienced in our case no real support at all.
records.further_details: I want the Government to improve the level of support for IPF & to make more people aware of this life limiting disease. There are 36,000 diagnosed IPF sufferers in GB. We want them to have the same support as those who are diagnosed with cancer and not just to be left on their own to find answers. We need more support groups, and trained designated nurses who can support them through this harrowing time as well as more awareness of this disease with adverts etc. IPF is a killer just like cancer so give us a voice too.

records.title: Fund free transport for all Serving Armed Forces Personnel
records.description: Fund free transport, rail and bus services for Serving Armed Forces Personnel 365 days a year to ensure families see their loved ones and alleviate high costs and pressures on service members.
records.further_details: We believe serving Armed Forces personnel should receive free, year-round transport. Assignment orders routinely place service members far from their families and children. Over key leave periods like Christmas, some remain isolated in Single Living Accommodation because travel costs are unaffordable-even with a Forces Railcard. This isolation can severely impact mental health.

records.title: Fund NHS access to Lecanemab & Donanemab to slow dementia/Alzheimer's symptoms
records.description: We call on the Government to fund NHS access to Lecanemab & Donanemab on prescription for those with early-onset dementia, Familial Alzheimer's Disease and those who are asymptomatic, but carry a genetic mutation that will result in early onset Dementia.
records.further_details:
Lecanemab & Donanemab are drugs licensed by the UK’s MHRA, for the treatment of mild Alzheimer's symptoms. It is clinically proven to slow the progression of Alzheimer's disease. Clinical trials showed they slowed the onset of people with early Alzheimer’s Disease.
 
Nearly 1 million people live with Dementia in the UK, costing the economy an estimated £42 million per year.
 
Familial Alzheimer’s disease accounts for less than 1% of all Dementia cases. People who carry that genetic mutation will develop Alzheimer’s Disease symptoms before the age of 65.

records.title: Make it mandatory for the NHS to offer scans at 9-10 weeks
records.description: Introduce early mandatory scanning at 9-10 weeks to help reduce miscarriages going undetected. 1 in 4 women suffer a miscarriage. 1-5% of these are known as a "missed miscarriage", which averagely happens between 6-9 weeks and are only detected at the 12 week scan.
records.further_details: We believe earlier scanning needs to be introduced to help early detection which will contribute towards ensuring that woman do not suffer medically and do not suffer any long term health issues due to the unguided/ unaided end of a pregnancy. We feel this will also ensure that women get the correct after-support when processing what has happened. In a lot of cases, a missed miscarriage goes unnoticed for 5-6 weeks which can be medically dangerous and pose health problems to females.

records.title: Financially redress 3.8m taxpayers excluded from Covid-19 financial support
records.description: We want the Government to establish a fair financial redress scheme for the 3.8 million taxpayers excluded from Covid-19 financial support, reflecting the support received by comparable taxpayers and businesses.
records.further_details: Around 3.8 million UK taxpayers were excluded from meaningful Covid-19 financial support, including newly self-employed people, company directors, freelancers and new starters. Many lost income, businesses, homes and financial security, while comparable taxpayers received substantial government support. Years later, the consequences continue. We believe fairness requires proportionate financial redress for those excluded.

records.title: Launch a rural proofing review & suspend the use of the grey-belt test
records.description: Launch a rural proofing review into the grey-belt test and completely suspend the use of the grey-belt test for villages for all planning applications pending the outcome.
records.further_details:
We want the Government’s review to look into updating planning policy by recognising the primacy of Green Belt purpose, village settlement boundaries & made Neighbourhood Plans when deciding on planning applications.

The 2026 NPPF uses purposes (a), (b) and (d) to identify grey belt. Those tests address the sprawl of large built-up areas, the merging of towns and the setting of historic towns — they do not directly assess the equivalent functions of land around villages. We feel this creates a serious risk that genuinely rural greenbelt land between villages is being judged by tests that do not reflect its function. We believe villages are not spaces between towns; countryside encroachment should be a decisive test.

records.title: Require Children’s Faces to Be Hidden in Monetised and Publicly Shared Content
records.description: We want the UK Government to introduce legislation requiring content creators to hide or obscure the faces of children in publicly shared or monetised online content, protecting children’s privacy and preventing them from having a permanent digital identity created without their informed consent.
records.further_details: A child cannot consent to having their face permanently placed online. Once shared, images can be copied, redistributed and manipulated by strangers, including being used to create abusive AI images. Most images found in abusive contexts are reported to originate from social media. We believe children should have a legal right to privacy, with creators required to hide children’s faces in publicly shared or monetised content. Children are not content.

records.title: Commit to Protect Rights to EOTAS/EOTISC for Children & Young People with SEND
records.description: In any SEND reforms, maintain the legal right to education other than in school for children & young people whose needs mean no school or college placement is appropriate. Retain the SEND Tribunal’s power to order EOTISC and specify the provision required for a child’s individually assessed needs.
records.further_details:
EOTISC (Education Otherwise Than In School or College) allows children and young people with SEND to receive education when a school or college setting is not suitable. It is intended to enable tailored provision based on professional assessment of each child’s needs.
 
Without this safeguard, some children with SEND who cannot safely or effectively attend formal settings may struggle to access education.
 
We ask the government to commit to protecting EOTISC to help ensure vulnerable children are not left without appropriate educational support.

records.title: Ban All Knives including ceremonial knives in Schools
records.description: Introduce a clear policy banning knives of any kind in schools, including religious or ceremonial blades. Schools should remain completely weapon-free environments so pupils and staff can learn and work safely.
records.further_details: We think allowing any type of blade on school grounds can create unnecessary risk, even if ceremonial. Knife crime remains a serious issue in England and Wales, with tens of thousands of offences involving knives recorded each year. There has also been an incident in which a student in Australia was stabbed during an altercation involving a ceremonial knife. We think a single clear rule banning knives in schools would protect pupils and remove confusion over exceptions.

records.title: Referendum on the TV Licence
records.description: Hold a simple yes or no referendum on whether the TV Licence should be abolished.
records.further_details: We keep being told by many politicians that the BBC is a national institution and should be protected by the continuing of the TV licence. This petition calls on the government to give the people a voice and to hold a yes/no referendum to see how the population truly feels.

records.title: Fully fund specialist glasses for visually impaired children
records.description: We call on the Government to fully fund clinically necessary specialist glasses and tinted lenses for all visually impaired children through the NHS.
records.further_details:
We call on the Government to require the NHS to fully fund specialist glasses, tinted lenses, and visual aids for visually impaired children, including those without a standard prescription.
Current NHS vouchers often fail to cover the true cost, forcing families to pay for essential medical aids. This creates a postcode lottery where children’s access to vital visual support depends on where they live and what their family can afford.

records.title: Cap income used to calculate Child Maintenance to Minimum Wage over a 40hr week
records.description: We call on the UK Government to introduce a fair and sustainable cap on the income figure used to calculate CMS payments. We propose that the maximum weekly income considered for CMS assessments be limited to the equivalent of the National Minimum Wage multiplied by a 40-hour working week.
records.further_details:
We believe this cap would ensure that maintenance obligations are calculated based on a reasonable and widely understood benchmark of full-time work. Those who attempt to improve their situation by working additional hours or taking on extra employment may find themselves penalised in subsequent assessments, as increased earnings can lead directly to higher maintenance payments.
 
By capping the income used in calculations in line with minimum wage and a standard working week, we believe the system would become fairer and more predictable.

records.title: Mandate working a/c and heating systems on all new public transport vehicles
records.description: Heatwaves are becoming increasingly more frequent, so let's get working air conditioning and heating systems made a legal requirement before a new public service vehicle can go in to service.

records.title: Restore the Age-Related Personal Tax Allowance for Pensioners
records.description: We call on the Government to reintroduce the age-related personal income tax allowance for people of State Pension age, setting it at 110% of the full annual new State Pension and increasing it automatically each year in line with the Triple Lock State Pension.
records.further_details:
Pensioners are more likely to spend additional income in their locally. That spending supports high streets, small businesses and jobs and generating additional VAT and other tax revenues. 

The Government should restore the age-related personal allowance for everyone of State Pension age, set it at 110% of the full annual new State Pension, and uprate it annually in line with the State Pension, which should retain the triple lock.

records.title: Make it law to have working parking air conditioners in all HGVs
records.description: Pass a law to make it mandatory for all Heavy Goods Vehicles to have a fully working Parking Air Conditioning unit installed. HGV drivers’ lives can be at risk when parked up due to record breaking temperatures and we believe existing laws are not sufficient to prevent this.
records.further_details: Year on year we are seeing record temperatures all over the UK. We are calling for a law to be passed to make it mandatory for fully functioning parking air conditioning to be installed in all HGVs, reducing the risk of sleep deprivation as well as heat exhaustion or life-threatening heatstroke. It will also save fuel and stop illegal engine idling. In turn reducing the number of RTCs, keeping roads safer for all users as HGV drivers will be well rested and in good health.

records.title: Funding for specialist police to tackle antisocial behaviour on illegal e-bikes
records.description: Funding to be made available to police forces to tackle illegal off road electric motorbikes and anti social behaviour. This funding could be used for specialist motorbike drone units designed to catch and prosecute those involved in the behaviours outlined above and make our communities safer.
records.further_details: Most of us will have seen young people, wearing balaclavas to hide their identity, riding these bikes on our roads with total disregard for the law or our safety. However, specialist motorbike drone units will be able to track and follow the bikes, arrest the riders and, destroy their bikes. We believe this will be a strong deterrent.

records.title: Motability to maintain higher mileage options for disabled people
records.description: Require Motability to maintain higher mileage options for disabled people who need to travel more than 30,000 miles in three years and not to proceed with the changes planned for 1 July.  We believe these changes will risk restricting access to work, healthcare and essential independence.
records.further_details: We believe the reduced mileage allowance and increased excess charges mean many disabled people with essential high mileage needs may no longer be able to use the Motability scheme. In our view this risks limiting access to work, healthcare and independent living: a fair higher mileage option would ensure the scheme meets the real needs of disabled people.

records.title: Introduce new legal protections for access to purchased video games
records.description: Introduce new legal protections requiring video games sold in the UK to remain accessible to consumers who have purchased them. This could involve a requirement to provide physical versions or equivalent permanent ownership options for software.
records.further_details:
The Government should strengthen UK consumer law so people who buy digital games retain fair long term access if a store closes, a licence changes, or content is removed.
 
Companies should be required to give clear notice before access changes and provide a permanent download, offline option, physical release, refund, or fair alternative where possible.

records.title: Lower bowel cancer screening from 50 to 40—save more lives, detect cancer early.
records.description: We are calling for bowel cancer screening to start at 40 instead of 50. Bowel cancer can affect younger people, and early detection saves lives. Lowering the screening age could help find cancer sooner, improve treatment outcomes and give more families precious extra years together.
records.further_details: We are calling on the Government and NHS to lower the age for routine bowel cancer screening in England from 50 to 40. Bowel cancer can affect people in their 40s, and finding it early can save lives. Starting screening at 40 would help detect cancer and warning signs sooner, give people faster access to treatment, and improve survival. We believe everyone should have the opportunity to protect their health before symptoms appear. Lower the screening age to 40 and help save lives

records.title: Teach severe autism, non-verbal needs and sensory crises in PSHE⁠
records.description: We want the UK Government to mandate teaching about severe autism, non-verbal communication, sensory overload, and dysregulated behavior in the national PSHE curriculum.
records.further_details: Current school education often focuses on mild autism, leaving the public ignorant about severe, non-verbal autism and dysregulated behavior. This lack of awareness leads to judgment, misunderstanding, and distress when families use necessary protective holds during sensory crises in public. Educating students on severe autism, meltdown triggers, and non-verbal needs will build real understanding, end public stigma, and protect SEN families from hostility.

records.title: Reverse the DfE rules that restrict agency social workers’ pay and movement
records.description: Reverse new DfE rules that cap agency social worker pay, restrict movement, and impose conditions that push workers into permanent local authority roles.
records.further_details: Sector bodies have raised concerns about limited consultation, the lack of a full, published impact assessment, and potential procedural issues in the development of the reforms. Community Care reports widespread worry among social workers, and BASW has noted concerns that the changes may worsen recruitment, retention and service stability. The reforms also target only social workers.

records.title: Fund Long Covid compensation scheme
records.description: Fund a long covid compensation scheme (like the covid vaccine compensation) for people who have caught covid and are now living with long covid, some with debilitating effects.

records.title: Fund a medical cannabis reimbursement scheme for veterans ​
records.description: We want the UK Government to set up a reimbursement scheme for armed forces veterans who are prescribed medical cannabis by a specialist doctor.​
records.further_details:
Medical cannabis can be legally prescribed in the UK but is not readily available on the NHS. This means veterans who are prescribed medical cannabis for chronic pain, PTSD and other conditions must pay privately for their medication. ​

We believe eligible veterans who pay for medical cannabis should be able to access a government-funded reimbursement scheme. ​Veterans Affairs Canada reimburses veterans for the cost of medical cannabis.  We believe UK veterans deserve similar support.

records.title: Make it mandatory for food services to provide detailed carbohydrate information
records.description: In educational and professional environments where food is served people with T1 Diabetes need to be able to manage their insulin intake with confidence. Carbohydrate information needs to be available in restaurants and in school. It seems discriminatory to not provide this.
records.further_details: It needs to be the law. Policies around educational provision are not strong enough for those with this life long condition. Until there is a cure these people/children need to eat unhindered by the fact it's not mandatory to supply them with the necessary information in order for them to eat safely. This information needs to be given without a choice of whether to or not.

records.title: Regulate Social Media Platforms as News Publishers to Prevent Misinformation
records.description: Review and amend the Communications Act 2003 and the Online Safety Act 2023 to hold social media platforms to the same standards of "Due Accuracy" and "Due Impartiality" as mainstream news broadcasters.
records.further_details: Mainstream news must follow Ofcom’s rules on "due accuracy" and "impartiality." Social media platforms are not defined as publishers which can create a loophole used to spread misinformation. Amend the Communications Act 2003 and Online Safety Act to hold platforms liable when their algorithms promote unverified, biased, or harmful "news" content.

records.title: Cap Child Maintenance: 10% of a paying parent’s basic salary excluding overtime
records.description: We want the Government to cap child maintenance payments at 10% of a paying parent's basic salary, excluding overtime. We also propose a minimum payment of £210 per month for parents in full-time employment – which is roughly 10% of the minimum wage based off a 40hr week, minus any deductions.

records.title: Make Drama a mandatory subject in the National Curriculum for Key Stage 3
records.description: We ask the Government to make Drama a mandatory subject within the National Curriculum for all pupils in Key Stage 3 in England, and provide appropriate curriculum time, guidance, and support for its delivery.
records.further_details:
We believe Drama develops essential life skills including communication, confidence, creativity, empathy, critical thinking and collaboration. These skills can support success across education, employment and everyday life.
 
We feel access to Drama is currently inconsistent across schools, limiting opportunities for many students, particularly those from lower-income backgrounds.

records.title: Establish dedicated independent statutory SEND regulator for Local Authorities
records.description: Establish an independent statutory dedicated SEND regulator with powers to monitor, investigate and enforce Local Authorities’ compliance with their legal duties towards children and young people with SEND.
records.further_details: In our view too many children with SEND only receive the education and support they are legally entitled to after their families pursue complaints, mediation or Tribunal appeals. We think children should not have to rely on whether their parents have the time, money, confidence or legal knowledge to secure the education and support they are already legally entitled to. We therefore believe that an independent dedicated SEND regulator could better oversee Local Authorities’ compliance with SEND law and address systemic failures.

records.title: Free School Meals for Children in Kinship Care-Regardless of Household Income
records.description: Make free school meals automatic for all children in kinship care, including those under Special Guardianship Orders and Child Arrangements Orders, regardless of household income. Kinship carers save the state money and should not be financially penalised for stepping up.
records.further_details: Kinship carers step in during trauma, neglect, bereavement or family crisis, often preventing children from entering the care system and saving the Government thousands each year. Many of these children are recognised as vulnerable and qualify for Pupil Premium Plus, yet kinship carers are expected to pay for school meals if they do not claim benefits. This unfairly penalises families who step up to keep children safe.

records.title: Create secure safeguarding children’s risk register
records.description: Create a safeguarding register to which police, education, health, councils and other agencies can input information they collect about people who may pose a risk to children. Parents should be able to request information from this register, with independent oversight.
records.further_details: In our view, agencies often fail to act in cases where children are at risk due to not having the full context of a situation. For example, where a child discloses abuse but withdraws due to trauma or coercion, we think the system frequently fails to act due to not having the full history or context. We would like this to be called “Eva’s law”.

records.title: Launch a public inquiry into the SEND system in England
records.description: We call on the Government to launch a statutory public inquiry, under the Inquiries Act 2005, into the provision of SEND services in England following whistleblower allegations, which have led to wider concerns from many about the existence of systemic failures within SEND services.
records.further_details: Children and young people with SEND are legally entitled to appropriate support, yet many families report long delays, unmet needs and difficulties accessing the provision set out in Education, Health and Care Plans. Following recent allegations, we believe only a statutory public inquiry, with the power to compel evidence and hear testimonies from families and professionals can establish the full extent of the problem, identify causes, demand accountability and transparency and make recommendations for reform.

records.title: Make organ donation consent made prior to someone’s death binding
records.description: We call on the Government to legislate so that a person’s registered decision to donate is legally binding and cannot be overridden by family members after the person’s death.
records.further_details: Under the current system, families are still consulted and can effectively prevent donation, even when a person has clearly stated their wishes. We think this undermines personal autonomy and can result in fewer lifesaving transplants.

records.title: Allow artistic swimming as a GCSE and A-level option for PE coursework.
records.description:
Current coursework options for GCSE and A-Level PE include many options, but do not recognise Artistic Swimming as one, even though it is a skilled Olympic sport.

Not having it as an option prevents artistic swimmers from being able to count their specialist sport as part of their skills.
records.further_details:
Artistic (formerly synchronised) swimming has elements of dance, cheerleading, gymnastics, & swimming - all in PE curriculums. 
Athletes possess precision, endurance, flexibility & coordination, all while performing intricate routines in water. 
We are as passionate about artistic swimming as many are about football, netball, or athletics.
Recognising artistic swimming validates hard work & promotes inclusivity & diversification within sport curriculums.
Sign to help make it an option for PE.

records.title: Reduce state pension age to 60 to create jobs for young people
records.description: Reduce the state pension age to 60 years old. We think this change could create jobs for young people, reduce sickness and healthcare costs for older adults in the workforce, and reduce workforce strain due to sickness amongst older workers.
records.further_details: We believe this could also free up grandparents to contribute part time, if they wish, to childcare, thereby reducing government costs. It could also enable skilled pensioners to volunteer to support new apprentices in the workforce, reduce NHS costs, and open up jobs for young people.

records.title: Cap Child Maintenance payments at £200 per child
records.description: We want Child Maintenance payments to be capped to a maximum of £200 per child – rather than to be based on pre-tax income – and to be reduced according to the proportion of days’ care given by the paying parent.
records.further_details: Doing this will, we believe, help reduce the stress and financial difficulties that many face when it comes to having to pay Child Maintenance and will make it more equal and fair to both parties when each has a share of the care of each child. Currently, we feel it is an unjustified system which only benefits the receiving party.

records.title: Raise the age for invites to regular mammograms beyond the age of 71
records.description: Women are entitled to have mammograms for their whole lives, yet they stop receiving regular invites after 71 and then have to arrange screenings themselves. Many women don’t realise this and assume they no longer need a mammogram, which means they miss vital screening.
records.further_details: We want the Government to increase the age for invites to routine mammograms beyond 71 so regular invites continue. I'm a nurse and advise women that they are entitled to have mammograms for their whole lives. However, women over 71 no longer receive a letter regularly inviting them to a screening - they have to arrange it themselves. Most women in this age group aren't aware of this and assume that screening ends at 71. Breast cancer risk increases with age, and breast cancer is more common in women over 70.

records.title: Referendum on English Independence
records.description: We call for a referendum on full English independence from the UK due to what we believe is the enormous financial burden which the nations of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland place on tax-payers in England.
records.further_details: We believe England should finally separate and prove it can prosper entirely on its own without also supporting the rest of the Union. Many politicians, commentators, and media outlets regularly claim Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland are a financial burden on taxes raised in England. We therefore believe England should have the opportunity to become fully independent and demonstrate it can thrive without supporting the other nations of the UK. We believe that such a referendum would allow England to take full responsibility for its own economy, resources, public services, and international position while ending constant constitutional disputes within the Union.

records.title: Seek to negotiate a freedom of movement arrangement with the EU
records.description: We call on the UK Government to seek to negotiate and secure UK participation in the EU freedom of movement framework or equivalent reciprocal arrangements. This would allow eligible UK residents and European nationals to live, work, study and travel freely between regions.
records.further_details: Restoring freedom of movement could bring meaningful benefits: supporting family reunions, creating work and study opportunities, boosting cross-border business and tourism, and strengthening cultural ties. Currently, many face barriers to moving between the UK and Europe, while industries report skills shortages and operational challenges. We also recognise differing perspectives, such as concerns about regulation and border controls.

records.title: Introduce a 6-month time limit for police misconduct investigations
records.description:
We ask the Government to legislate for a statutory 6-month time limit for completing police misconduct investigations.

Where cases cannot reasonably be concluded within 6 months, extensions should require approval from an independent authority, with clear justification and regular review.
records.further_details:
The law should also require:

* A formal review at 3 months
* Welfare and occupational health support for officers under investigation
* Publication of anonymised data on investigation times and outcomes

Prolonged investigations can undermine fairness, efficiency, and workforce wellbeing. Clear time limits with independent oversight would support timely, proportionate decision-making while maintaining public confidence in police accountability.

records.title: Legalise Regulated Non-Lethal Self-Defence Tools
records.description: Rising knife crime and violent attacks can leave citizens vulnerable when police cannot arrive instantly. While some self-defence can be legal, the public lacks practical tools. Legalise self defence tools such as pepper spray to help save lives of men, women and children.
records.further_details: Legalise regulated non-lethal self-defence tools for law-abiding residents. Ordinary people, including men, women and older children, have limited means to protect themselves from violent attacks. We feel incidents such as the recent Belfast attack show that police cannot always arrive in time. We propose legalising tools such as pepper spray under strict licensing and training. We believe this would help save lives, prevent serious injury, and improve public safety.

records.title: Make those convicted for domestic abuse ineligible for early release
records.description: I want the Government to change the law so that people convicted of serious domestic abuse offences must serve their full prison sentence instead of being released early.
records.further_details: I am a survivor of horrific domestic abuse. I am worried that domestic abusers may end up only serving a fraction of their sentences. Victims should be allowed the time to heal before their abuser is released.

records.title: Fund the inclusion of music therapy in community mental health support
records.description: We believe government plans to expand community mental healthcare support are vital to improving access, outcomes and quality of life for service users. The Government should fund the provision of music therapy services, offering an evidence-based route to support that transcends words and language.
records.further_details:
If there is to be a new community model for mental healthcare, we believe it is vital that service users have access to the full range of evidence-based psychological support that meets their needs, meaning music therapy should be included in these developments from the outset.
 
We feel failing to provide music therapy would be a significant missed opportunity to make care more accessible, responsive, and inclusive, particularly for those who may find predominantly verbal approaches inaccessible.

records.title: Mandate GPS location, time details and photo for all parcel delivery companies
records.description: Mandate that all parcel delivery companies provide recipients with GPS location recorded at delivery, time, estimated GPS accuracy & a map showing the delivery location alongside the proof-of-delivery photo. This should only be available to the intended recipient and comply with UK data protection.
records.further_details:
Every day, thousands of consumers experience parcels being delivered to the wrong address. Courier companies often provide a photograph as proof of delivery, but this frequently fails to identify where the parcel has been left. We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation requiring :
• The GPS location at point of delivery
• The time of delivery
• The estimated accuracy of the recorded location
• A map showing the recorded delivery location alongside the delivery photograph

records.title: Criminalise pretending to be a member of the armed forces or a veteran
records.description: I want the Government to make it a specific criminal offence for any person to pretend to be serving or to have served in His Majesty’s Armed Forces.
records.further_details: Any person gaining any financial or any type of help by pretending to have served in the Armed Forces past or present should be made a specific criminal offence under charges similar to fraud. This includes turning up to parades wearing medals.

records.title: Introduce a New Homicide Offence for Abuse Related Suicide
records.description: We call on the UK Government to introduce a new, bespoke criminal offence recognising cases where controlling or coercive behaviour and other serious forms of domestic abuse contribute to a victim’s death by suicide.
records.further_details: We believe the law must recognise when domestic abuse contributes to suicide and hold perpetrators accountable. The NPCC recorded 150 suspected suicides following domestic abuse in the year to March 2025. Evidence shows that this is not a marginal issue; it is a serious and growing area of domestic abuse deaths that requires a clear legal response, greater accountability and a route to justice for bereaved families. We believe families deserve a law that recognises the abuse behind these devastating deaths.

records.title: Apply to rejoin EASA and obtain a reciprocal agreement on licensing
records.description: Apply to rejoin the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) and obtain reciprocal licensing agreements to allow the airline industry to grow and undo the lasting effects from having left the agency.
records.further_details:
Leaving EASA resulted in much confusion as to what the new standards would be, with people unsure as to what license to study for, the ramifications of which included stress, loss of relationships, severe debt and less co-operation with an agency responsible for regulating other aircraft and pilots still flying in British sovereign airspace.
 
We believe an agreement would allow British pilots who are stuck with an EASA licence to obtain a UK one, thus growing the economy and industry.

records.title: Categorise all air rifles as firearms and require owners to be licenced
records.description: Currently some air rifles can be purchased by anyone over the age of 18. Every year wild animals and pets die or are permanently injured by air rifle bullets. All air rifles should be treated as firearms and subject to the same rules as owning a gun. They are not toys.
records.further_details: I volunteer at a wildlife rescue. Yesterday a beautiful fox was brought in, from an urban area, having been shot 4 times by an air rifle. She was paralysed. I have heard of numerous cases of cats, squirrels, foxes, waterfowl and hedgehogs being injured by air rifle bullets …I refuse to call them pellets. They are not for idiots who think shooting an animal is a laugh.

records.title: Include Martial arts as an individual sport in the Examinable PE GCSE
records.description: Broaden the GCSE PE practical criteria to include martial arts. These disciplines require immense technical skill, physical fitness, and mental discipline. Including them ensures that dedicated student-athletes in these fields are not disadvantaged compared to those in traditional sports.
records.further_details:
As a 1st Dan black belt in Taekwondo, I'm looking to take Examinable PE. I'm in my GCSE years and I would like to be able to take Taekwondo as an individual sport option as I've worked hard and long hours to become good at it. 

Martial Arts require immense technical skill, physical fitness and mental discipline. Including them ensures that dedicated student-athletes in these fields are not disadvantaged compared to those in traditional sports. Many martial arts are recognised Olympic sports.

records.title: Make Ketamine a Class A drug and fund better support, awareness and research
records.description: I urge the UK Government to reclassify ketamine from a Class B to a Class A controlled drug under the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 due to the increasing harm it is causing to individuals, families and communities.
records.further_details: I also call for stronger penalties for supply, increased funding for addiction treatment, nationwide education and awareness campaigns, and more research into ketamine-related deaths and long-term health harms. These measures could help protect lives and tackle the growing impact of ketamine misuse across the UK. I believe ketamine should be a Class A drug because of the long lasting effects this causes as well as the amount of deaths that are rising.

records.title: Ban the sale and use of high-frequency and ultrasonic animal deterrents
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce legislation to ban the sale, supply and use of all ultrasonic and high-frequency sound devices marketed or used as animal deterrents. These products should be removed from sale and existing units withdrawn from use entirely.
records.further_details:
Sold as humane and safe, but we think this is misleading.
They can cause pain & harm to birds, bees, bats, cats, squirrels, rabbits, hedgehogs & wildlife, many protected or vital to nature. Noise travels through walls, often run non-stop at full power.
We believe these can disrupt survival, causes suffering, ruins habitats, disturbs homes & health. In our view no safe ultrasonic method exists - total ban is the only solution to stop the high-pitch horrible sound that disturbs the peace and makes everyday life unbearable for everyone nearby.

records.title: Review how to better weave nature and wellbeing into the curriculum
records.description: Review how to make nature and wellbeing core parts of the curriculum — not optional. We think this, a "living curriculum", would transform outcomes for children, especially those with SEND and mental health needs. With a new curriculum in 2028, the evidence, and workforce we have, we should act now.
records.further_details: In our view, a nature-based curriculum should mean weaving nature, movement, play, and relationships through every subject — with a focus on science in gardens, maths through building things, literacy through storytelling. We are concerned that we are raising the first generation more connected to screens than to the natural world, but that children learn best through meaningful, hands-on experience. As a signatory to the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, the UK is committed to developing every child's fullest potential. We believe the expertise exists. Let’s do this.

records.title: Require processed meat products to have a carcinogenic warning label
records.description: We call on the UK Government to introduce mandatory, front-of-pack cancer warning labels on processed meat products sold to inform consumers that regular consumption can increase the risk of bowel cancer.
records.further_details: The WHO’s IARC classifies processed meat as a Group 1 carcinogen (like tobacco) and confirms it causes bowel cancer. According to the WHO, eating 50g daily increases bowel cancer risk by 18%, and Cancer Research UK estimates 13% of UK bowel cancers are caused by processed meat. Bowel cancer is the UK’s 4th most common cancer, with 48,200 cases yearly. Cases among 25–49-year-olds have risen around 22% since the early 1990s. We believe consumers have a right to know the health risks of processed meat.

records.title: Replace 'hysterectomy' with 'uterectomy' in NHS patient materials
records.description: Direct NHS England to adopt 'uterectomy' as the primary term in all patient-facing materials, consent forms and clinical guidelines, replacing 'hysterectomy' - a term we believe is rooted in misogyny, not anatomy.
records.further_details: For many people hysterectomy is associated with hysteria - a diagnosis used to pathologise women, removed as an official diagnosis only in 1980. The International Federation of Associations of Anatomists has recommended removing eponyms like this. Research shows one in five people don't know hysterectomy means uterus removal, compromising informed consent for women. In our view, this is medical misogyny in language. Women deserve clarity about what is happening to their bodies and terminology that respects them.

records.title: Appoint a Cabinet Minister for Disability & Equalities
records.description: Appoint a Minister for Disability & Equalities, with responsibility for overseeing disability rights, equality policy, fair treatment of all disabled people as disability affects all the protected characteristics.
records.further_details: Hold all government departments accountable for the impact of their policies on disabled people. At present, disability and equality responsibilities are often combined with wider ministerial roles and placed under broader departmental portfolios. We feel that this does not provide the focused leadership or accountability needed to address the challenges faced by disabled people. Address issues relating to discrimination, negative stereotyping, media representation and barriers to participation in society. Act as a central point of contact and advocacy for disabled people and their organisations.

records.title: Introduce new rules and protections from development in rural green heartlands
records.description: We believe that the South West — Devon, Somerset, Dorset, and Cornwall — stands at a breaking point. We are concerned that our cherished green fields, productive farmland, and close-knit rural communities are being swallowed by unchecked urban expansion.
records.further_details:
Strengthen the National Planning Policy Framework with these rules for rural areas:
1. Require developers to evidence a genuine local connection (e.g. headquarters or major operations within the county) before reserved matters approval.
2. Mandate full upfront infrastructure funding via Section 106 or Community Infrastructure Levy — no new homes without the services to support them.
3. Review policy and make any necessary changes to ensure best agricultural land (Grades 1–3a) and wider countryside is excluded from the grey belt unless every realistic brownfield alternative is exhausted.

records.title: Scrap Mandatory Advice and Guidance for Primary Care Referrals
records.description: On the 1st April 2026, NHS England introduced mandatory advice and guidance for GPs and primary care professionals. This means clinicians must get advice and guidance from secondary care colleagues before referring patients, which we think removes their ability to make direct referrals.
records.further_details: We demand that the Department of Health and Social Care U-turn on this section of the new GP contract for 2026/27 and restore advice and guidance as a voluntary service. In our view, mandating advice and guidance in primary care makes it even harder for patients and their GPs to advocate on their behalf.  We believe this is nothing more than a PR stunt by the government to create the illusion of reducing waitlists by stealth. We think it will only push patients out of sight, stuck between the inboxes of consultants and GPs.

records.title: Fund NHS dyslexia assessments
records.description: Dyslexia affects many people yet NHS assessments are unavailable. This leaves access limited to those who can pay or navigate complex systems. The government must ensure free, early assessments for all to support education, wellbeing, and equal opportunity.
records.further_details: Many people with dyslexia go undiagnosed or receive a late diagnosis often due to cost and limited access, leading to avoidable struggles in education, work, and daily life. Early identification is vital for understanding needs and accessing support. We are concerned that without NHS provision, inequality persists. Government action is needed to ensure fair, timely access to assessments for all, regardless of financial circumstances.

records.title: Review regulation of animal boarding and licensing conditions
records.description: A review should consider introducing a new framework for paid pet care including minimum standards, more efficient checking of licences and enforcement of online platforms. There should be more alignment between devolved governments. These changes could be known as Molly's Law.
records.further_details: These changes could protect pets and owners by making it easier to check who is licensed/insured before booking, and lead to better enforcement relating to unregulated carers. They should also support responsible providers who invest in training, hygiene, safe premises, supervision and emergency planning. The UK Government should work with devolved nations to deliver consistent rules, clear penalties, and properly resourced enforcement so animal welfare isn’t a postcode lottery.

records.title: Introduce new safeguards when police return devices containing intimate images
records.description: Introduce legislation requiring police to follow a safeguarding process before returning a seized device containing intimate images or recordings of a complainant, including informing them and allowing them to request that the material is removed or put beyond the device owner’s use.
records.further_details: Intimate images or recordings may be discovered on a seized device during a sexual offence investigation. If the investigation does not result in a conviction, there should still be safeguards before that device is returned. Police may need to preserve a forensic copy as evidence, but this should not automatically mean returning access to the original intimate material. Complainants should have clear rights to information, privacy and safeguarding regardless of the outcome of the investigation.

records.title: Do not bring in the new Ecodesign Regulations on tumble dryers in the UK
records.description: Don't make heat pump tumble dryers effectively the only new models legally permitted for sale. The proposed ban undermines the purpose of the UK Right to Repair Regulations. Set up an independent taskforce of experienced appliance engineers to assess the cost/benefit ratio of the ban on UK consumers
records.further_details: Heat pump tumble dryers require an ambient temperature between 5°C and 35°C to operate efficiently. The optimal room temperature to prevent extended drying times is between 19°C and 24°C. During winter a machine in an unheated garage or outbuilding can multiply drying cycle times or stop it from functioning. These dryers can also be far more expensive to repair than standard condensers, if the heat exchanger becomes clogged or compressor fails. We believe this ban will only benefit manufacturers & not the British people.

records.title: Make it mandatory to offer late 3rd trimester pregnancy scan
records.description: We call on the Government to make it mandatory for all NHS trust to offer late 3rd trimester scans for ALL pregnant mothers including "low risk" pregnancies.
records.further_details: We believe this scan could help to check the health of baby, their weight, blood flow, growth etc. This could provide an opportunity for healthcare professionals to act on an early delivery if necessary, which could reduce the number of stillborns

records.title: Review bereavement policies for pupils sitting GCSE and A-level exams
records.description: I want the government to review the grading and expectations set by the Joint Council for Qualifications, for pupils that have lost a close relative immediately before starting their GCSE or A-level exams.
records.further_details: Mitigations are in place for pupils who have recently lost a close relative. For example, if they have recently lost a parent, they may be expected to sit 15% of each subject and will be marked up by 5%. We believe it would be fairer to allocate marks based on their predicted grades as happened during Covid. No child should be expected to attend school so soon after saying goodbye to a parent or sibling.

records.title: Mandate offer of Group B Streptococcus screening for all pregnant women
records.description: Mandate offer of Group B Strep (GBS) screening for all pregnant women at 35–37 weeks, provide funding for NHS-wide access to testing and antibiotics during labour to those who test positive to help prevent serious newborn infections.
records.further_details: Group B Strep can cause life-threatening infections in newborns, yet most pregnant women in the UK are not routinely tested. Many families only learn about GBS after their baby becomes seriously ill. These infections are often preventable with simple screening and antibiotics in labour. We believe Mandatory offering of testing could save babies’ lives, spare families trauma, and help ensure no parent has to face a preventable loss.

records.title: Require trauma informed specialist advocate for victims reporting domestic abuse
records.description: Require that victims are given a trauma-informed specialist advocate, separate from an IDVA or appropriate adult, who will support them in person when: reporting abuse; getting help from mental health services and; navigating the system ensuring their abuse, risk, trauma and safety are understood.
records.further_details: We are concerned that there is a dangerous gap between reporting abuse and receiving effective protection. Trauma responses and mental health can be used against victims. This new specialist advocate could close this gap via trauma-informed specialist advocacy, mandatory review of original allegations after counter allegations are made & joined up mental health and safeguarding responses.

records.title: Create new route to appeal CPS decisions to drop rape or child abuse cases
records.description: We want the Government to create a new and more affordable route for victims and families to appeal a Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) decision to drop rape and child abuse cases. This should apply to both current and past cases.
records.further_details: In our view, victims currently have no affordable way to challenge decisions by the Crown Prosecution Service to drop rape or child sexual abuse prosecutions, other than Judicial Review or bringing a private prosecution. We think this places a heavy financial and emotional burden on families and can leave serious cases without independent scrutiny. We believe victims and families should have a clear route to appeal these decisions, including where prosecutions were previously discontinued, to improve accountability and confidence in justice.

records.title: HMRC: extend MTD ITSA quarterly update deadline from 5 weeks to 3 months
records.description: HMRC should extend the Quarterly Update deadline under Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 5 weeks to 3 months after each quarter, giving taxpayers and agents more time to prepare accurate submissions and better align with existing reporting cycles.
records.further_details: The current 5week deadline creates significant pressure on taxpayers and agents, increasing reliance on estimates and raising the risk of errors and incomplete records. Extending the deadline to 3 months would improve data quality, reduce last-minute submissions and spread workloads more evenly. HMRC has already demonstrated flexibility by extending CGT UK property reporting deadlines from 30 to 60 days showing that pragmatic changes can reduce administrative burden while maintaining compliance.

records.title: Ban the use of piercing guns / hand pressure piercing devices
records.description: We believe piercing guns are incredibly dangerous and should be prohibited to prevent the ongoing danger to the public. We believe piercing guns are a severe infection hazard as they can’t be fully sterilised, increasing the risk of cross contamination and the spread of life-threatening diseases.
records.further_details: Piercing guns are often just ‘cleaned’ with alcohol wipes which cannot kill all pathogens. Piercing guns can cause blunt force trauma and cartilage shattering. The jewellery used in piercing guns is often low quality metal, and either has an arrow head or butterfly back, which we think is hazardous for multiple reasons and not suitable for fresh piercings. People are piercing babies with guns…enough is enough! In our view, any reputable, safe piercer would perform piercings with single use, sterile, disposable needles.

records.title: Abolish quarterly Making Tax Digital submissions for self-assessment
records.description: We want the Government to abolish the requirement for quarterly tax submissions under Making Tax Digital, introduced this April by HMRC.  We believe it is difficult enough doing annual submissions and now to be forced to submit tax calculations 4 times a year is more than many of us can bear.
records.further_details: We feel that annual submissions are more than appropriate for the amount of time and effort it takes to do self-assessment tax submissions and that changing it to having to submit every 3 months is unnecessary, too much to ask and not possible for many individuals.

records.title: Ban generative AI music software in the UK
records.description: The UK music industry has generated £8 billion in yearly revenue to the UK economy. We are concerned AI-generated music is threating the livelihoods of professionals in Britain’s music sector, we call on the Government to ban generative AI music software to protect British jobs.
records.further_details: An estimated 2.4 million people work in Britain’s thriving creative sector. We are concerned that new technologies threaten to entirely wipe out British recording studios, British songwriters, British session musicians, British recording engineers, British artists and British record companies. We believe this disruptive technology should not be allowed to infiltrate our industries and threaten livelihoods. We call on the Government to ban generative AI music software to protect British jobs.

records.title: Start mining British coal again for the environment and heritage sector
records.description: We call on the Government to start mining coal again. A small anthracite mine, which we think could bring the cost of fuel down enormously for heritage sites and be considerably greener, as it wouldn't need to shipped from the other side of the world.
records.further_details: Currently, museums and railways are having to pay huge premiums to import coal from abroad. We believe that not only is the quality poor, it has to be shipped across the ocean. Somehow this called 'clean coal' when we believe that it is actually the opposite. In our view our own supplies are far cleaner burning, there would be less transport cost and emissions doing this. I hope the government can open their minds to what is happening here, as I believe net zero is destroying the industry while generating more pollution than a domestic solution.

records.title: Review the Regulation of Pet Insurance Premium Increases and Consumer Choice
records.description: We believe that many pet owners face huge & unsustainable rises in their monthly pet insurance on renewal far above inflation & income growth with limited transparency or ability to switch providers due to even minor pre-existing conditions leaving many effectively locked into their current insurer.
records.further_details: We call for a review to investigate price increases and pricing structure, to ensure there is clearer transparency on how renewal prices are set, review rules on pre-existing conditions (such as simple conversations at your vet) and their impact on switching, ensure long-term customers are not unfairly penalised compared to new customers, enable safer switching between providers without losing cover for investigated but undiagnosed conditions and assess the wider impact these prices have on pet welfare and pressure on rescues.

records.title: Criminalise failing to report hitting cats with a vehicle & taking them to a vet
records.description: Make it a criminal offence to hit a cat with a vehicle and drive away and legally require reporting collisions and taking them to the vet immediately. Social media posts show the cruelty of leaving cats to suffer horrific injuries or die alone in pain.
records.further_details: Beyond the severe harm it can cause to cats, collisions can devastate loving owners, who are left heartbroken without closure or medical help for their pets, and can traumatise witnesses and heavily impact their mental health. We believe cats deserve strong legal protection, and that drivers should be held accountable and act responsibly.

records.title: Lower the bowel cancer screening age to 25
records.description: Lower the bowel cancer screening age from 50 to 25. There is a huge increase in younger people being diagnosed with bowel cancer with one in every 20 cases being in someone under 50.
records.further_details: Some people are only finding out they have bowel cancer when it has reached the later stages such as stage 3 and above. There are people with young families having to deal with the tough process of chemotherapy and other treatments. There is also an increased risk of secondary cancer if bowel cancer is not diagnosed fast enough.

records.title: Amend the Ancient Monuments Act 1979 to ban building on all scheduled sites.
records.description: Parliament must amend the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Areas Act 1979 to mandate a total ban on Scheduled Monument Consent for any permanent above-ground construction. This should apply to all list entries where archaeological deposits exist, removing discretionary executive powers.
records.further_details: Current law allows the Government to grant consent for commercial building on ancient sites via unscrutinised executive orders. This fails to protect our heritage from irreversible damage. For example, at Castle Hill (List 1009846), development is planned despite significant archaeological remains and public outcry. We need a mandatory statutory ban on construction to ensure the 1979 Act serves its primary purpose: the absolute preservation of monuments for future generations.

records.title: Remove VAT from all children’s swimming lessons
records.description: We want the Government to remove VAT from all children’s swimming lessons to keep them affordable and accessible. We believe swimming is a vital life-saving skill, not a luxury, and high costs can prevent many children from learning to swim safely.
records.further_details: We believe swimming is a life-saving skill, not a luxury. Adding VAT to children’s swimming lessons makes them less affordable and we feel risks excluding children from learning to swim safely. when there are fewer school swimming lessons available, private swim schools become more  essential. Thousands of children leave primary school unable to swim confidently. Increasing lesson costs will, we think, only make this worse. We urge the Government to remove VAT from all children’s swimming lessons and keep swimming accessible for all children.

records.title: Allow disputed landlord service charges be paid to courts for better justice
records.description: Make it possible for tenant/leaseholders to pay disputed service charges to a court. The funds will then only pass to landlords if they can prove the charge's legitimacy within a specified timeframe. Otherwise, the money returns to the tenant/leaseholder.
records.further_details: According to housing campaign group SHAC overcharging for services is common across private, council, and housing association landlords. We believe that the current legal framework disadvantages tenants and residents by requiring them to pay up then seek refunds. This proposal seeks to balance the power between landlord and tenant/leaseholder, allowing for fast, objective, independent adjudication. We think it could end the current flawed system in which landlords, having received payment, have no incentive to engage with those who believe they have been overcharged.

records.title: Ban all face coverings at all protests and demonstrations
records.description: Face coverings at protests allow individuals to hide their identity, making it harder to prevent and investigate crime, disorder, and intimidation. We call for a clear, universal ban on face coverings at protests to ensure accountability and public safety.
records.further_details: Peaceful protest is a fundamental right, but it must be exercised responsibly. When people conceal their identity, we believe it undermines trust, enables anti-social behaviour, and limits effective policing. A consistent, no-exceptions rule would provide clarity, deter disorder, and protect both the public and those taking part in lawful demonstrations.

records.title: Fund a national diagnostic DLD pathway & better services for people with DLD
records.description: Fund a national diagnostic Developmental Language Disorder (DLD) pathway and improved services for those with DLD. This pathway should raise awareness, understanding and inclusion of DLD, provide early intervention and DLD training for professionals in the public & education sectors.
records.further_details: We want the Government and the NHS to listen to the lived experiences of those of DLD, to learn how DLD impact on our daily lives, and what it is like living with a lifelong condition that many people are not aware of. We feel current services and support for children and adults with DLD are limited. Those with DLD need continuous support throughout our lives, and at different stages.

records.title: Make keeping horses tethered with no shade, food or drink a specific offence
records.description: Many horses are left with no shade, very little water or food tethered in open fields. Some hardly have any grazing and when in severe weather conditions all they do is walk in circles all day. Keeping horses tethered outside with no access to shade, food or drink, should be made a specific offence.
records.further_details: I'm fed up with sitting at home worrying about horses tethered in fields in all weathers and no grazing or access to water. We are having a heatwave at the moment and these poor horses have no shade. If you own a horse, then it should have access to water, shade and food. I'm surprised this is still going on and I think it's cruelty at its worst and I want something done about it.

records.title: Fund free bus travel for school pupils, college students and apprentices
records.description: We believe the Government should fund free bus travel for school pupils, college students and apprentices. The cost of travelling to education or training can be a barrier for young people and families. Free travel could improve access to learning, training and employment opportunities.
records.further_details: Bus fares can stop some young people getting to school, college and apprenticeships. We believe no young person should face barriers to going out, meeting friends and taking part in their community. The Government could introduce a travel pass issued by schools, colleges and apprenticeship providers to give eligible students free travel for education.

records.title: Give BSL, Cornish, Irish, Scots, Gaelic & Welsh UK-wide language protections
records.description: We call on the UK Government to give Cornish, Irish, Scots, Scottish Gaelic, Welsh and BSL the same official language protections that exist in the constituent nations of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
records.further_details:
These languages have devolved protections, but not UK-wide; we want these languages to have the same protections nationally.

We are concerned that Amendment NC107 to the Representation of the People Bill could criminalise election leaflets in Cornish, Irish, Gaelic, Scots and BSL, affecting bilingual constituencies like Na h-Eileanan an Iar, Irish-speaking areas of NI, and BSL users nationwide. It could even outlaw party names written in these languages. Devolved governments have granted these languages protections, but we feel problems remain for general elections.

records.title: Review UK policy treatment of bio-based chemicals and materials
records.description: Reducing reliance on fossil resources is seen as vital for national security and resilience. We call on the UK Government to conduct an urgent review of how bio-based chemicals and materials are treated across UK policies, regulations and taxation including how their biogenic carbon is accounted for
records.further_details: We believe current policies effectively lock the UK into continued reliance on oil and fossil fuels, increasing exposure to global price shocks, supply disruption, and geopolitical instability. At the same time, the current framework works to limit the deployment of bio-based solutions that could replace many of the everyday products underpinning modern society. We feel this is a critical issue as engineering biology, a key UK growth sector, depends on clear, consistent policy signals to scale.

records.title: Hold a public referendum on whether to hold an early general election
records.description: Call an immediate referendum to allow the public to decide whether there should be an early general election.
records.further_details: We believe adaptability is the reasons humans thrive while our democratic systems still seem prehistoric, being designed for a pre-digital era which treats delay as a solution. We believe the NHS, Parliament, and regulatory bodies are choking on backlogs they created. The Fixed Term Parliaments Act has now been repealed  — there is no legal barrier to an early election, only political convenience.

records.title: Make Perimenopause Training Mandatory for All UK Doctors
records.description: Perimenopause affects millions of UK women, yet many are dismissed or misdiagnosed. We call for mandatory training for all doctors and at least one trained specialist in every GP practice to ensure women are properly recognised, supported and treated.
records.further_details: Too many women are told their symptoms are “just stress” or prescribed antidepressants instead of receiving appropriate hormonal support. This can lead to worsening physical and mental health, impacting work, relationships and quality of life. Perimenopause is a natural stage of life, not a niche issue. Proper medical training could improve diagnosis, treatment and outcomes for millions of women across the UK.

records.title: Mandate maximum 12 week dental waiting time for SEN children & increase funding
records.description: Mandate a maximum 12-week wait for SEN children requiring urgent dental care under sedation or general anaesthetic. Provide emergency funding to increase surgical capacity and ensure Integrated Care Boards are held accountable for delays that leave vulnerable children in prolonged pain.
records.further_details: When a non-verbal child has to wait months for urgent care such as for a dental abscess, the pain can be an invisible torture that can restrict an already limited diet and cause extreme distress. We believe it is a failure of care that SEN children are left in agony due to systemic delays. These children cannot wait over a year for basic relief. As parents we are our children’s voice, and we are demanding that no child be forced to endure months of preventable, unbearable pain.

records.title: Require venues to accept government evidence of disability or caring needs
records.description: Require venues and event organisers to accept existing government evidence (PIP, DLA, Carer's Allowance letters) for disability or caring needs, instead of forcing people to purchase a third-party card or repeatedly share private medical data for reasonable adjustments.
records.further_details: Many disabled people and carers already have government evidence (PIP, DLA, Carer's Allowance letters), yet many venues only accept a paid for third-party card or require repeatedly submitting private medical data to third-party systems. This petition asks the Government to require venues and event organisers to accept existing government-issued evidence of disability or caring responsibilities, rather than requiring a paid card or repeated submission of private medical data to third-party systems.

records.title: Make water companies statutory consultees in housing development planning
records.description: We call on the UK Government to make water companies statutory consultees in all housing development planning applications. This would ensure that no development can proceed unless the relevant water company confirms that adequate water supply, wastewater, and drainage infrastructure is in place.
records.further_details: New housing developments can place significant pressure on existing water and wastewater systems. Without early input from water companies, developments risk causing water shortages, sewage overflows, and environmental harm. Making water companies statutory consultees would help protect public health, safeguard the environment, and ensure sustainable growth.

records.title: Review DVLA’s performance & processes, increase funding & create governing body
records.description: We want the government to conduct a review of the DVLA's performance and processes to make sure everyone is treated fairly & equally.
records.further_details:
- Ensure all forms are available to download or complete online & all payments can be submitted online. 
- Ensure enquiries & complaints are resolved in no more than 14 days.
- Review the information given by staff and the computer and phone systems.
- Set new standards for the medical exams of High Risk Offenders & all applicants so all medical professionals carry out the same exam.
- Create a new Governing Body specifically to oversee the DVLA 
- Increase funding to the DVLA

records.title: Reduce child maintenance, exclude overtime & introduce no contact, no payment
records.description: We want the government to review and reduce child maintenance rates, stop including overtime in calculations, and halt payments when contact is denied or contact does not exist, especially if there is a new parental figure.
records.further_details: We feel that these policies are unfair, often leaving non-custodial parents financially unstable. We think they fail to consider full circumstances, such as overtime or lack of contact. For many, it is a source of deep humiliation and alienation when a new parental figure is in place and contact is denied. A fairer system is needed to ensure both children’s well-being and the financial and emotional stability of non-custodial parents who are making a real effort.

records.title: Criminalise Repeated Non-Consensual Photography and Recording in Gyms
records.description: We want the Government to create a specific criminal offence for repeated non-consensual photography and filming in gyms and leisure facilities, giving police clear powers to investigate and prosecute those who repeatedly target individuals without their consent.
records.further_details: There is current no law that specifically addresses repeated photography or filming of people in gyms and leisure facilities without their consent. This behaviour can cause distress, humiliation and fear, especially when someone is targeted over a long period. We want the Government to create a specific criminal offence for repeated non-consensual recording in these settings and give police clear powers to investigate and take action.

records.title: Formally recognise the killings of Bengali people in 1971 as genocide.
records.description: We call on the UK Government to formally recognise the killings of the Bengali people of East Pakistan in 1971 as genocide - so that nearly 1 million British Bangladeshis, and the generations carrying this history, are no longer left without an answer.
records.further_details:
There are already established institutions that have recognised these events as genocide. Genocide Watch, the Lemkin Institute, and the International Commission of Jurists have all recognised these events as genocide. The US House introduced recognition resolutions in 2022 and 2026. The UK has not.
 
Many British Bangladeshis carry this history without their country ever acknowledging it. Research has shown genocide trauma passes across generations. Silence makes it worse.
 
We are asking for the truth to be named, to enable the start of healing.

records.title: Review The Number Of Asbestos-Linked Lung Cancers
records.description: The HSE states that the ratio of mesothelioma deaths to other asbestos-related deaths is 1 to 1. Some research suggests that deaths from asbestos linked lung cancer are much greater than deaths from mesothelioma. We believe this may hide the scale of UK asbestos deaths and current asbestos risks.
records.further_details: By reviewing and reporting the true scale of the problem, it is hoped that asbestos management policy may be overhauled.

records.title: Bring down driving test wait times
records.description: The wait time for learner drivers to get a driving test is unacceptable, we need more examiners, reward them accordingly and incentivise them to do more tests.
records.further_details: Some learner drivers are waiting 5 months for a driving test, this is leading to mainly young people not being able to get their licenses which can lead to them missing opportunities, delaying employment and causing unnecessary pressure and stress for a driving test if they’re able to get one. As a government I would want you to address this and the core problem is there isn’t enough examiners to conduct tests due to low wages and poor incentives to do more tests.

records.title: Ban the sale of glue traps
records.description: The sale of glue traps should be banned in line with the current ban on their use under the Glue Traps (Offences) Bill 2022 in order to protect animals and wildlife and limit their suffering caused by such traps.
records.further_details: To protect wildlife and other animals from these inhumane traps and the prolonged suffering they cause, a ban on the sale of glue traps should be introduced. The RSPCA and numerous wildlife organisations continue to report illegal use of glue traps by businesses and members of the public, despite existing restrictions. We believe prohibiting their sale except to glue-trap license holder would help prevent unnecessary animal suffering and improve animal welfare protections.

records.title: Review employment law awareness and enforcement in private Early Years
records.description: There are concerns that employment rights are not being enforced in the private early years sector, both by level 2 and 3 qualified staff, and managers and leaders. We therefore call for a review of employment law awareness and enforcement of the law in the Early Years sector.
records.further_details: We also think that employment practices should be better incorporated into Ofsted's Leadership and Management inspection judgement. In our view the sector includes many staff and managers with limited knowledge of employment law, and there are repeated examples of poor practice, including excessive hours for young workers, lack of contracts, no breaks and unpaid training. We believe that workforce shortages exacerbate these issues, and that whilst safeguarding and recruitment are closely monitored, there is insufficient focus on employment law.

records.title: Fund NHS preceptorships for unemployed Physician Associates
records.description: Fund a national NHS preceptorship programme for unemployed qualified Physician Associates, providing paid supervised NHS employment and a clear pathway into permanent NHS roles while maintaining patient safety and clinical competence.
records.further_details: Thousands of qualified Physician Associates remain unemployed despite completing postgraduate medical training, passing the national qualifying examination and registering with the GMC. Many are becoming deskilled while the NHS continues to face workforce shortages. A funded NHS preceptorship programme would provide supervised employment and a clear pathway into NHS roles.
