We did what was asked of us. We are qualified. We are ready to work.

records.title: Ban removing Rescue Back Up details from pet microchips & make them permanent
records.description: Rescue Back Up details registered on microchips can be removed by authorised external users like alternate rescuers, without informing the original rescue organisation.
records.further_details:
We call on the Government to amend Microchipping Of Cats and Dogs Regulations to ban the removal of Rescue Back Up details and other important welfare information registered on microchips, create a permanent audit trail, and automatically notify registered rescue organisations of any attempts to remove these details.

When a rescue or breeder register their RBU details on the microchip of a pet they rehomed, they may do so on the basis that it will remain there so they can be contacted if the pet is vulnerable. Authorised users with access to microchip databases, can remove original registration or rescue back up details without telling the original rescue, breeder, owner, keeper or rehoming centre, which can leave them unable to trace their dog or offer lifetime protection.

records.title: Change the law to allow public to carry and use pepper spray for self-defence
records.description: Legalise carrying and using pepper spray for self-defence from age 16 or 18, with approved types only used against immediate threats. The Secretary of State should regulate standards, sales, and storage, and set penalties for misuse. This could ensure safety while protecting personal security.
records.further_details: I urge the government to legalise pepper spray for personal self-defence. Citizens over sixteen or eighteen should be allowed to carry approved pepper spray to protect themselves against imminent threats. Proper regulation by the Secretary of State could ensure safety and responsible use, with clear rules for possession and penalties for misuse. This law could empower individuals to guard their safety while maintaining public order and oversight.

records.title: Legalise assisted dying for terminally ill adults
records.description: Introduce legislation to legalise assisted dying for mentally competent adults suffering from terminal illnesses or incurable, painful medical conditions. Current UK law denies individuals the right to a peaceful death. We believe citizens deserve dignity to a peaceful & insufferable end of life.
records.further_details:
We urge the Government to introduce legislation to legalise assisted dying for mentally competent adults who have a terminal diagnosis or an incurable, irreversible physical condition causing suffering that cannot be relieved. This legislation should include rigorous, multi-layered safeguards.
 
Under this legislation, eligibility should be verified through independent assessments by medical specialists, a mandatory reflection period, proof of mental capacity and robust protection against external coercion.

records.title: Regulate podcast platforms to prevent the spread of misogyny and harmful content
records.description: Strengthen regulation of podcast and social media platforms to meet minimum editorial standards, strengthen oversight & prevent algorithmic promotion of harmful content, in order to delegitimise misinformation and dangerous ideologies which endanger not just women and protected groups, but everyone.
records.further_details:
With growing concern around under-16’s access to social media we should be equally concerned about content they have unlimited access to via podcasts
With such influence and access to individuals there must be equal responsibility and accountability for podcasters.

A recent YouGov study found misogyny in schools is a big problem and teachers report it's worsening.

With Ofcom now holding powers to regulate global streaming services we question why this has not been extended to podcasting platforms.

records.title: End mileage tax on EVs & plug-in hybrid cars and reduce VAT on public charging
records.description: Remove the planned mileage tax on electric and plug-in hybrid cars.
records.further_details:
We oppose the proposed 3p/mile EV tax starting 2028, which will be 1.5p/mile for plug-in hybrid vehicles. We believe it’s short-sighted and contradicts UK investment in EV manufacturing and Net Zero goals by suppressing consumer demand. 
 
EV owners already pay VAT on electricity (20% at public chargers, 5% at home) and PHEV owners also pay tax on petrol too. We feel this tax is double taxation and unfairly penalises drivers. We call in the Government to withdraw the tax and reduce VAT on public charging to 5%.

records.title: Require freeholders to allow fixed AC with external units in leasehold flats
records.description: Require freeholders to allow leaseholders to install safe, compliant fixed split air conditioning with external condenser units unless they can justify reason to refuse it. Freeholders and managing agents should not refuse by default and must give evidence-based reasons for refusal.
records.further_details: Many leaseholders in modern flats in buildings that are not listed or protected are blocked from installing fixed air conditioning with external condenser units because freeholders control walls, roofs, balconies and facades. Portable, internal-only and water-cooled systems are often inadequate as heatwaves make flats unsafe. This is not about uncontrolled facade changes: freeholders could set locations, noise limits and screening. We believe refusal should be based on genuine evidence, not a default policy.

records.title: Ban animal testing, require use of alternative testing and invest more in this
records.description: The government should ban animal testing, and require and invest more in the use of cruelty-free alternatives like AI and human cell research. We believe we need stronger laws to protect animals from painful experiments, forcing companies to use safer, modern scientific methods and not harm animals.
records.further_details: We believe animal experimentation should be banned in the UK because it causes unnecessary suffering to animals that cannot defend themselves. Millions of animals are used in painful tests every year despite modern alternatives such as computer models, AI, and human cell research being available. These methods can often be more accurate and humane. The government should invest more in cruelty-free science and create stronger laws to ban animals being harmed for testing and experiments.

records.title: Exempt Student HMO’s from Renters Rights Act 2025
records.description: We believe Student HMO’s should be exempt from the Renter’s Rights Act 2025 as these properties are run on a totally different business/rental model compared to professional and private rentals.
records.further_details: In our view Student HMO’s are a totally different entity to professional HMO’s. For example, if a professional leaves a HMO, you will re-rent the room easily. However, if a student leaves mid year we think the landlord is very unlikely to find a replacement student tenant as students plan their accommodation ahead of time, and often choose a house with their friendship group for the academic year. We think the changes brought in by the Act will make life for student landlords like myself extremely unpredictable and financially unstable and in turn, leaves student accommodation in an extremely vulnerable position

records.title: Respond fully to The Law Commission's recommendations on Surrogacy
records.description: The Law Commission of England & Wales published its joint report with the Scottish Law Commission in March 2023, with recommendations for a robust new system to govern surrogacy. The Government gave an interim response on 8 Nov 2023. We want the government to publish a final response.
records.further_details:
Current surrogacy law is out of date, yet surrogacy is becoming more common. The report outlines a new regulatory regime that offers clarity, safeguards and support for the children, surrogates and intended parents. The recommendations are accompanied by draft legislation. 
 
The Government's response to the report is overdue.

The delay leaves families navigating uncertainty and contributes to unnecessary risk. A full response and a timetable for bringing the Bill before parliament would help.

records.title: Create an Independent Cruise Passenger Regulator and Strengthen Consumer Rights
records.description: We want the Government to establish an independent statutory regulator to protect UK cruise passengers, with powers to set and enforce minimum consumer standards covering cancellations, significant disruption, compensation, complaints, denied boarding and unfair treatment.
records.further_details: Around two million Britons cruise each year, yet passengers lack the dedicated regulatory protection available to airline passengers through the CAA. When cruises are cancelled or significantly disrupted, passengers can face substantial losses and be directed to travel insurers. With no dedicated regulator to independently hold cruise lines to account, we believe this significant gap in UK consumer protection must be addressed urgently.

records.title: Ban carrying religious, cultural & ceremonial bladed & pointed items in public
records.description: I believe that the carrying of religious, cultural and ceremonial bladed & pointed items in public should be treated the same as the carrying of all other bladed & pointed items.
records.further_details: I believe that a knife is a knife, and that religious and cultural traditions should not be put above public safety.

records.title: Include 'Indo-Caribbean' as an ethnic group on Government documents
records.description: We ask the UK Government to include “Indo-Caribbean” as an ethnic group option on Government documents, alongside existing categories, so people of Indian-Caribbean heritage can accurately identify their ethnicity and be better represented in UK equality data.
records.further_details: Indo-Caribbean identity has a direct connection to British history. Under British indentureship, approximately half a million Indians were brought to the Caribbean. During the Windrush era, descendants of these indentured labourers migrated to the UK, contributing to the growth and diversity of Britain’s Caribbean community. Yet ethnicity monitoring forms provide no clear space for Indo-Caribbean people. We think recognition would reflect this distinct heritage, improve representation and data accuracy, and help public bodies better understand the communities they serve.

records.title: Recognise reputational abuse as a distinct form of abuse in the law
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce legislation recognising reputational abuse, including reputational sexualisation, as a distinct form of abuse in law.
records.further_details: This should include creating a specific criminal offence for deliberately creating or sharing false, manipulated or fabricated content intended to damage the reputation of an innocent person, together with statutory guidance for police, prosecutors, courts and victim support services.

records.title: Review access to, and funding for, NHS powered wheelchairs
records.description: Too many ambulatory wheelchair users are denied NHS-powered wheelchairs because they can walk short distances. We want eligibility to be soundly based on clinical need, safety and independence, not just on walking or standing ability.
records.further_details: Too many ambulatory wheelchair users are refused NHS-powered wheelchairs because they can walk short distances, even when walking might be unsafe or worsen their condition. We call on the Government to review NHS eligibility and provider relevant funding so decisions are based on clinical need, functional ability and safety rather than just walking ability. We believe this would help people with conditions such as ME/CFS, POTS, MS, EDS and other disabilities improve quality of life, remain independent, and access work, education and family life.

records.title: Review the RE curriculum to ensure equal depth in teaching all major religions
records.description: Review the Religious Education curriculum in all schools to ensure all major religions are taught with equal depth and respect. I believe Christianity should still be taught, but religions like Sikhism, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism and Buddhism should receive more meaningful and balanced coverage.
records.further_details: I feel many students only learn surface-level information about religions outside Christianity, which can lead to stereotypes and misunderstanding. As a Sikh, I feel the teaching of other religions in schools are often reduced to festivals or basics instead of their history, beliefs and contributions.

records.title: Regulate Foot Health Practitioners to require supervision by HCPC podiatrists.
records.description: We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation to regulate Foot Health Practitioners (FHPs), requiring that they do not practise independently and may only provide foot care services under the clinical supervision or governance of an HCPC-registered podiatrist.
records.further_details:
The title “Foot Health Practitioner” is not statutorily regulated in the UK. This can lead to confusion for patients, including vulnerable groups such as people with diabetes and vascular disease who may not be able to distinguish between regulated podiatrists and un-regulated practitioners.

We believe that introducing a clear supervisory requirement would improve patient safety, ensure appropriate clinical oversight and provide clarity for the public about levels of training.

records.title: Restrict transport of asylum seekers from MoD sites to local towns
records.description: We want the Government to end what we see as unnecessary taxpayer-funded transport from MoD asylum sites to local towns & cities. Transport contracts already operate from Wethersfield & Crowborough. Future MoD sites should provide minimal offsite travel & provide services onsite wherever practical.
records.further_details: We believe routine transport from MoD asylum sites to local towns should be limited to essential journeys only. There have been reports of arrests involving some asylum seekers linked to sites such as Wethersfield. We believe daily transport, including early evening collections 365 days a year, is unnecessary, increases costs to taxpayers and raises concerns within local communities.

records.title: Review and remove judicial immunity for judges & magistrates
records.description: Launch a review into all laws, rules and conventions that grant judges and magistrates judicial immunity and legislate to remove judicial immunity for judges and magistrates.
records.further_details: We feel current judicial immunity rules mean there is no proper way to challenge wrongdoing, corruption or gross failures by those in public office. We believe that those working for the public must be answerable to the law in the exact same as any other citizen.

records.title: Extra funding for SEND holiday clubs
records.description: Provide funding to allow more holidays clubs for SEND children, so parents can go to work!
records.further_details: Due to the lack of support during school holidays for parents with SEND children, is making it difficult for parents to go to work or even have a break. By providing funding and extra support during the school holidays will not only benefit SEND children but also benefit the parents. It will improve both health and wellbeing for both.

records.title: Mandate emergency hydrocortisone IM injection training in schools
records.description: Mandate emergency hydrocortisone IM injection training in schools for pupils with Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH). Parents can't leave hospital without this training, yet schools can opt out of it. Change DfE guidance to mandate similar training to that for the use of EpiPens.
records.further_details: Parents can't leave hospital with CAH newborns until trained in life-saving hydrocortisone injections. Yet, DfE guidance leaves school training purely voluntary. This loophole lets schools refuse training, which can lock children out of education. If a child has a crisis at school, delay risks brain damage or death; and ambulance services explicitly warn against people always relying on their early arrival times. Change the guidance to mandate emergency injection training for staff, just like EpiPens.

records.title: Stop taxing UK citizens on the state pension
records.description: British citizens who have, though out their working life, paid National Insurance & tax, should not then be taxed on the state pension regardless of other earning/pensions.
records.further_details: They have worked throughout their lives & paid tax on their earnings, to then be taxed again is abhorrent.

records.title: Hold a public inquiry into the use of defence-linked AI in the UK public sector
records.description: We feel public concern is rising about AI companies deploying automated targeting in military, intelligence & policing. We believe their contracts and influence have been secured without adequate public scrutiny or democratic control. A public inquiry could investigate & address these concerns.
records.further_details: We believe there is growing concern about the role of private defence-linked AI companies in UK public services, including the NHS, where sensitive data is used. These systems are also deployed in military operations abroad, which we feel raises questions about accountability, civilian harm and risks to civil liberties. The public should have confidence that such systems are transparent, lawful and accountable, and not exposing citizens to misuse of data or technologies developed for surveillance and warfare.

records.title: Introduce stricter regulation for pet cremation
records.description: I want stricter rules such as requiring those who carry out pet cremation to have license, compulsory inspections, mandatory identity tags on pets, storage standards, staff training and respectful handling. We also think there should be CCTV requirements covering all key areas of the crematoria.
records.further_details:
My dog Teddy’s ashes went missing, after doing some investigating I uncovered an awful situation I’ll never unsee but I’ve also learnt how unregulated pet cremation is.
This has caused me trauma, but if any good can come out of it maybe it’ll help heal me and many other owners who are going through the same thing. In Teddy’s honour I’d like to try get pets remains treated with more respect to prevent heart ache or loss of ashes!

records.title: Establish a national alert system for missing autistic & vulnerable people
records.description: The Government should introduce a national alert system which alerts every phone in a county when an autistic or vulnerable person goes missing.
records.further_details: We have seen many vulnerable people, autistic children and other young people go missing. We believe a national alert system could help to drastically reduce the time it takes to find a child or young person. We hope this can lead to a safe and happy ending where the missing person is found.

records.title: Seek to introduce a UK-led humanitarian aid corridor to Oleshky in Ukraine
records.description: We call on the UK Government to call for the establishment of and lead a humanitarian corridor to provide aid and relief to Oleshky and neighbouring communities in the Kherson region in Ukraine.
records.further_details:
“Human safari” FPV drone attacks that target civilians in the Kherson region violate international humanitarian law, and attacks have left around 2,000 inhabitants trapped in occupied Oleshky, which is essentially besieged. 
 
Systematic “human safari” hunting of civilians sets a terrifying precedent. The UK should use the available diplomatic channels to push for immediate humanitarian relief of Oleshky and surrounding areas. We urge the UK Government to provide assistance to victims in Oleshky and its neighbouring communities in Kherson.

records.title: Fund research on the symptoms of Gilbert’s Syndrome
records.description: Gilbert’s Syndrome is classified as a harmless condition, however we are concerned that some patients are experiencing debilitating symptoms that are dismissed. We want the government to fund more research into this condition and its symptoms, which could inform clinical guidelines.
records.further_details: Gilbert’s Syndrome is a genetic liver condition causing high bilirubin levels. Whilst current NHS guidelines claim it requires no treatment or monitoring, some patients report symptoms such as fatigue, brain fog, nausea, abdominal pain and poor appetite. New UK research studying 1.8 million patients found that abdominal pain and fatigue were more common in people with Gilbert’s syndrome compared to control patients up to five years before diagnosis.

records.title: Raise the maximum charge for an MOT to £87.17 for cars & £47.12 for motorcycles
records.description: The maximum charge for an MOT test has not increased since 2010, despite a rise in business costs. Independent garages can be forced to close due to not earning a living wage. In line with inflation since 2010 the maximum fee for a car MOT should be raised to £87.17, and for a motorcycle to £47.12.
records.further_details:
The DVSA charge MOT stations to take tests every year, buy MOT slots, and require them to have certain test equipment. Business rates rise, as well as cost of electricity and telecoms. Independent garages can be forced to close due to not earning a living wage.
 
In line with inflation the cost of a car MOT should rise to £87.17, and a motorcycle MOT to £47.12. Many garages lose money by continuing to provide this vital service.

records.title: Fund a pancreatic cancer screening programme
records.description: There is currently no routine screening programme on the NHS for pancreatic cancer, which is detected in far too many cases when it is too late to be cured. This affects thousands of families. It is one of the deadliest cancers, yet there is no nationwide, routine screening programme.
records.further_details: The Government should fund routine tests or scans to detect pancreatic cancer earlier which would make it easier to treat.

records.title: Strengthen laws on ending the use of Listed assets
records.description: I ask Parliament to strengthen Planning Laws and require any organisation wanting to end use of a Listed asset to provide valid Planning reasons to the Planning Authority if they wish to end the function of a Listed asset.
records.further_details: This would help ensure that private companies cannot close heritage listed assets such as the Scenic Railway in Margate unless the local planning authority also supports this action. What is happening in Margate is, we feel, an example of why we need better Planning protections for Listed structures.

records.title: Halt copper landline switch-off in all areas
records.description: We believe the reliability, simplicity of use & clarity of sound of the copper landline makes it far superior to other telephony systems and is therefore essential for the elderly, vulnerable & unwell. In addition, equipment & back-up for digital systems is too complex and error-prone for many.
records.further_details: We feel that the need for mobile back-up for VOIP during outages can be problematic for those requiring a low-EMF environment and that VOIP routers with Wifi & DECT signals can be problematic for the considerable numbers of people with electromagnetic hypersensitivity (EHS) as well as those with metallic & medicinal implants. The latter are not covered by UK EMF safety exposure limits as confirmed by Thomas v. Cheltenham Borough Council [2024] EWHC 1035. There is also scientific controversy about how protective the exposure limits are for everyone. We believe relying on mobile back-up for emergencies in outages is dangerous as EHS people need to live far from masts and as weather events such as thunderstorms can disrupt mobile signals.

records.title: Mandate suspension of police officers under investigation for serious injuries
records.description: Change the Police Conduct Regulations 2020 to make suspension mandatory for any officer under investigation for incidents causing serious injury. This should apply automatically where an independent review finds evidence of a cover-up or the withholding of material evidence.
records.further_details: Current laws allow officers to stay on duty even when suspected of serious misconduct. We believe public trust is destroyed when officers keep their job and powers while being investigated for near-fatal injuries or acts of misconduct. We believe we need mandatory suspension now.

records.title: Fund specialist chronic illness flare-up centres in every county
records.description: Fund dedicated, county-level chronic illness flare-up centres to manage acute flares for conditions like PoTS, Crohn’s, and Colitis. Hubs could offer rapid access to IV fluids, anti-nausea medication, pain management, and direct-to-ward admissions to reduce A&E wait times and infection risks.
records.further_details: GPs and specialists cannot provide immediate, same-day intervention, forcing vulnerable patients into emergency departments. A&E doctors often lack specialized training in complex chronic illnesses, leading to suboptimal care and dangerous exposure to infectious viruses.These centers could safely assess clinical risk, treat and discharge stable patients, or provide direct inpatient admissions. This targeted expert care could improve outcomes and save spaces in general emergency departments.

records.title: Independent environmental impact assessment for data centres & make AI opt-in
records.description: Require independent environmental impact assessments before any data centres are approved end the designation of data centres as "critical national infrastructure". We also call for AI to be opt-in, not built into everyday online services by default, so the public is not forced to fuel this boom.
records.further_details: In our view data centres for AI use vast amounts of water, yet communities get little say. In Morgan County, Georgia (USA), residents beside a major data centre report discoloured, undrinkable water and many now rely on shipped-in supplies, prompting calls for a federal investigation. Now, in North Devon, an 850-acre data campus, is proposed on protected farmland in a region currently facing hosepipe bans. In our view, the public never chose this boom but will pay for it in water, land and higher bills.

records.title: Give Early Parole or Deportation for Certain Life Prisoners in the UK
records.description: The UK stands for justice and human rights, yet many life-sentence prisoners remain in custody for excessive periods despite clear evidence of rehabilitation and reform. We ask the Ministry of Justice to introduce a structured review process allowing tariff reductions, early parole or deportation.
records.further_details:
We urge Government to prioritise reviews for life prisoners who meet one or more of the criteria, after serving half of their tariff :
1. Were convicted below the age of 21 without previous criminal records.
2. Are foreign nationals serving life sentences in the UK.
3. Convicted under the Joint Enterprise law.
4. Demonstrated consistent good behaviour and genuine rehabilitation.

This reform would support rehabilitation, reduce overcrowding, and reflect a more humane and balanced justice system.

records.title: Require NHS settings to address fragrance exposure as a patient safety risk
records.description: Require NHS organisations to introduce fragrance awareness measures, including signage, staff guidance, and consideration of low to zero fragrance areas to reduce preventable reactions in sensitive patients.
records.further_details: Fragrance exposure can trigger serious reactions in patients with conditions such as MCAS, asthma, COPD, migraines and chemical sensitivities. Symptoms can include breathing difficulty, cognitive impairment and systemic reactions. These risks are largely avoidable but remain unmanaged in NHS settings. Simple measures such as awareness and signage would reduce harm and improve accessibility for vulnerable patients.

records.title: Change waste classification laws so pet ashes can be buried with owners
records.description: We want the Government to change the law to permit pet ashes in human graves by ending their classification as waste so that families can be buried with their beloved pets.
records.further_details: I am petitioning the Government to amend the law so cremated pet remains can be interred with their owner when families choose. Many people see pets as family, and being buried together can bring comfort and reflect that bond. Current rules can block this or treat pet ashes as waste. We believe a clear legal change, subject to cemetery consent and health and safety rules, would respect personal wishes, support bereaved families, and allow dignified, lawful burial.

records.title: Require green rooves and solar panel shelters in all car parks
records.description: Require all car park operators to build green roof and solar panel parking shelters which could reduce the need to use farmland for solar farms and support biodiversity.
records.further_details:
Trees have been up-rooted to make way for housing, and fields are being used for solar farms. This doesn't just impact wildlife but also has an impact on us too.
We think need to do something now.
 
Green roofing can give wildlife a chance to thrive by building small gardens on top of a conventional shelter, transforming unused roof space into an eco-friendly infrastructure. These could also hold small sections of solar panels, reducing the need to build on unused land.

records.title: Hold a rejoin EU referendum now
records.description: We call for a referendum on whether the United Kingdom should rejoin the European Union after the Brexit referendum, giving the public a fresh, informed choice based on current realities and future needs.
records.further_details: We support this because circumstances have changed since the Brexit referendum. A new vote would allow people in the United Kingdom to weigh economic impacts, trade barriers, and lost opportunities such as free movement. It would strengthen democracy by letting voters decide with real-world evidence, while setting a clearer long-term direction for the country's economy, global role, and future generations.

records.title: Issue a statement committing to no new drilling licenses for oil or gas
records.description: We ask the Government to abide by the 2024 Labour manifesto and commit to no new drilling licenses for North Sea oil or gas. This summer has been another warning of extreme weather ahead. We believe the science is clear; to ensure climate security any remaining reserves must stay in the ground.
records.further_details:
Extreme, record-breaking heat. Drought. Smoke blanketing cities. To mitigate the environmental and public health impacts of the climate crisis that we are already suffering, fossil fuels need to be kept in the ground.

We are concerned that one of the first policies which the Prime Minister may announce could be for plans for more drilling in the North Sea. We think this is caving to the fossil fuel lobby, the very industry to blame for our current crisis. We believe this would be climate vandalism and must not happen.

records.title: Ban face coverings in all public spaces to tackle anti-social behaviour
records.description: Ban face coverings in all public spaces to tackle intimidating anti-social behaviour and harassment. Those in breach of this ban should pay a fixed penalty notice of £5000 or serve 6 months in prison. People wearing face coverings for genuine religious or health reasons should be exempted.
records.further_details: We want to ban face coverings in public spaces to tackle intimidating, anti-social behaviour and harassment caused particularly by young people on electric bicycles. We believe a ban could restore public safety, transparency and decrease crime.

records.title: Ban synthetic fragrance chemicals from public spaces and enforce full labelling
records.description: We want the Government to ban the use of synthetic fragrance chemicals and ambient scenting in public spaces, and introduce mandatory full-ingredient labelling including health risks on all fragranced consumer products.
records.further_details: We are concerned that the Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) and phthalates in synthetic fragrances could cause harm. Members of the public might face exposure to them in public restrooms, waiting rooms, clinics & supermarket laundry aisles.

records.title: Make non-fatal strangulation an offence punishable in line with attempted murder
records.description: Amend section 75A of the Serious Crime Act 2015 so that non-fatal strangulation is treated as seriously as attempted murder, reflecting the intent and potential lethality of the act and ensuring perpetrators face appropriate sentencing of up to life in prison.
records.further_details: Evidence indicates that non-fatal strangulation is one of the strongest predictors of homicide and can cause life-altering injuries days or weeks later. We believe survivors are often left without justice as the severity and intent of the act is minimised. Treating this offence as equivalent in seriousness to attempted murder would, we feel, better reflect the reality of the violence, improve victim protection, and act as a stronger deterrent.

records.title: Require venues to have full, up to date accessibility info on their websites.
records.description: To improve disability rights, there should be a legal requirement for all venues, businesses and shops to publish easy to find accessibility information on their websites and/ or social media, even if it means stating they are not accessible.
records.further_details: Navigating the world as a disabled person is difficult enough without venues not showing vital information that could make things so much easier. Too many places either have no information about accessibility at all, or it’s very difficult to find. Emails are often ignored, and answers not easy to get - in some cases because places might not want to admit they aren’t accessible. I believe this kind of legal requirement would make planning easier and would stop companies avoiding the subject.

records.title: Require airlines to amend stored API data between outbound and inbound flights
records.description: Following the UK's full implementation of ETA on 25/02/2026 and the EU's full implementation of ETIAS in 2027, please require all airlines operating flights to the UK to allow dual nationals to amend advance passenger information (API) data between outbound and inbound flights.
records.further_details: A dual British/EU national will not be able to check in for a flight from the UK to the EU using their British passport, because the carrier would receive a "NOT OK" response from the EU. A dual British/EU national will not be able to check in for a flight from the EU to the UK using their EU identity card or passport, because the carrier would receive a "0B" response from the Home Office. Therefore it is essential that airlines are required to allow API data to be amended mid-itinerary.

records.title: Require licensed venues to offer free anti-spiking drink covers to patrons
records.description: Amend the Licensing Act 2003 to make anti-spiking drink covers a mandatory licence condition for all venues serving open drinks in England and Wales. Covers should be available free of charge, on request, to any patron.
records.further_details: Almost 1 million UK adults were spiked last year with over 90% of incidents inside licensed venues or at festivals. Most victims never report it. Drink spiking often only takes seconds to carry out and is virtually undetectable, yet no requirement exists for venues to take preventative action. Public safety is already a statutory licensing objective under the Licensing Act 2003. Drink covers are low-cost, simple and widely available. The Government must make drink covers a licence condition.

records.title: Establish an official annual Women’s Health Awareness Week in England
records.description: Women's health campaigns across England are fragmented, with no national platform to unite them. We call on the UK Government to establish an official annual Women's Health Awareness Week, delivering on its own Women's Health Strategy and matching other countries like the US, NZ and Australia.
records.further_details: England already has many valuable women's health campaigns, covering individual conditions, life stages and areas of health, but they remain fragmented with no single national week to unite them. The Government's own Women's Health Strategy recognises the need for better information, education and awareness. An official Awareness Week would connect these campaigns, working with the NHS, workplaces and charities to promote evidence-based information and boost public engagement and knowledge.

records.title: Review NHS PTSD diagnosis and treatment pathways
records.description: The Government should conduct a review to look at introducing national PTSD diagnosis and treatment standards, including: assessment within 8 weeks, improved GP trauma awareness training, recognised PTSD referral pathways, faster access to appropriate specialist treatment and support.
records.further_details: Too many people experiencing trauma spend years misdiagnosed or untreated before reaching crisis point without support. Earlier recognition and intervention could improve recovery outcomes, reduce suicide risk and lower long-term NHS costs. PTSD can affect anyone, and delayed diagnosis can have severe consequences for individuals, families and communities. We believe national standards and earlier access to specialist care would improve outcomes and help prevent avoidable crises.

records.title: Require NHS autism diagnoses to include assessment of level of support needed
records.description: Autism varies greatly. Some autistic people live independently, while others are non-verbal, unsafe without supervision, self-harm, or need lifelong care. We want NHS autism diagnoses to include a clear, nationally standardised assessment of support-need levels.
records.further_details: Families caring for autistic children with profound or high support needs often face very different daily realities from families whose children may eventually live independently. Some autistic children are non-verbal, wear nappies beyond early childhood, self-harm, have no awareness of danger, and require 24-hour supervision for their safety. Others may communicate verbally, attend mainstream education, develop independence skills, and eventually live independently as adults.

records.title: Create community right to buy for empty pubs that are Assets of Community Value
records.description: We call on the Government to pass a law where pubs designated as an Asset of Community Value that are empty for 6 months or more, and where the owner refuses to sell or rent out the asset at an independently assessed fair market value, automatically trigger a community right to buy at market value.
records.further_details: Across England, hundreds of valued pubs are protected as Assets of Community Value, yet owners can leave them closed for years and refuse fair offers to reopen them, with no duty to act in good faith. Communities risk losing their last shared space and watch listed buildings rot. We ask the Government to give communities a real right to save their pub.

records.title: Introduce national heatwave resilience strategy & legal protections
records.description:
Create a national heat resilience strategy with legal protections for excessive indoor temperature in workplaces and homes.

Britain increasingly faces dangerous summer heat, but there is no legal maximum workplace temperature in the UK, and many buildings are ill-equipped for heatwaves.
records.further_details: Introduce a national heat resilience strategy & legal protection for excessive temperature in workplaces and homes. The Government should consult on: Maximum safe indoor working temperatures; mandatory heat risk assessments during heatwaves; minimum cooling and ventilation standards for new-build housing; funding to retrofit existing homes and buildings; issuing public guidance; the implications for public transport such as bus, tram, and rail; during heatwave events.

records.title: More regulation for home-based childcare: nannies, maternity nurses & tutors
records.description: We believe that this sector needs more regulation. Anyone can call themselves a nanny, maternity nurse, or tutor without qualifications, training, or background checks. This can put children at risk.
records.further_details:
We call on the UK Government to introduce more regulation for all home-based childcare professionals, including nannies, maternity nurses, and tutors.
 
This could include:
 
A compulsory national register
Mandatory enhanced DBS checks
Minimum training standards (including safe sleep and safeguarding)
Protected job titles
A clear system for reporting concerns and enforcing standards
This could improve safety, transparency, and accountability for families.

records.title: End Section 24 taxation against private individual landlords
records.description: We ask the Government to abolish Section 24 finance cost restrictions for private individual landlords and apply the same tax treatment and mortgage interest deductibility rules that currently apply to limited companies and corporate landlords.
records.further_details: Following substantial interest rate rises, many private individual landlords are effectively being taxed on their gross rental income rather than genuine profit, despite often owning only one or two rental properties. We further believe that this unequal taxation regime is contributing to smaller landlords leaving the market, reducing housing supply and increasing rents within the private rented sector.

records.title: Parents/guardian legal right to prevent use of their deceased child’s image
records.description: I want parents or guardians to have the legal right to stop people using a dead child's name or picture to make money, mock them, provoke others or glorify violence and to be able to get that content removed when the family has not agreed to it.
records.further_details: I am aware of many troubling examples of deceased children’s images after their death in ways which the families does not agree with, and which in some cases have caused families’ distress. Grief should never be turned into content, profit or something that fuels retaliation.

records.title: Introduce Stamp Duty relief for domestic abuse survivors forced to relocate
records.description: Require the Government to introduce Stamp Duty Land Tax relief for people who are forced to leave their main home because of domestic abuse and purchase a replacement home for their safety.
records.further_details: Domestic abuse can force survivors to leave their homes suddenly, often with significant financial costs. Stamp Duty can further reduce the money available to secure safe, suitable housing and rebuild their lives. The law should recognise that relocating because of abuse is not an ordinary choice to move home, but a necessary step towards safety and stability. Survivors should not be financially penalised for escaping abuse. This relief would help families secure safety, stability and new start.

records.title: Review digital exclusion in NHS GP practices and produce national guidelines
records.description: We call on the Government to review NHS GP services to ensure elderly and vulnerable patients can access health services without being disadvantaged by digital-first systems.
records.further_details:
Many older people struggle to book appointments because of long phone queues, limited appointment availability, online-only booking systems, and communication barriers. Access to healthcare should not depend on technology skills.

We urge the Government to review current processes and introduce national standards for GP access to improve telephone and face-to-face booking options, strengthen interpreter services, and require transparent reporting of access performance so all patients can obtain timely care.

records.title: Fund accommodation for mothers and fathers that have their baby in the NICU
records.description: Provide funding to ensure that parents, carers and foster carers of babies receiving care in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) have access to dedicated, separate accommodation within or alongside the hospital, rather than being expected to stay on general hospital wards or at home.
records.further_details:
This would help allow families to remain close to their critically ill baby, providing essential emotional and practical support throughout their child’s neonatal journey.
 
They can go home if they wish but have the option to stay close by.

records.title: Make mental health screening mandatory after military deployments
records.description: Require all Armed Forces personnel to have a mental health screening with a qualified clinician before post-deployment leave. This could help identify hidden struggles, provide early support, and reduce suicide risk among service members.
records.further_details: Too many service personnel struggle in silence after deployment. In 2021, 253 UK veterans died by suicide, with rates significantly higher among those under 25. Studies show around 1 in 5 UK Armed Forces personnel experience mental health issues such as PTSD, depression or anxiety. Mandatory screening before leave could identify hidden struggles early, provide support, and help prevent avoidable deaths.

records.title: Review accountability & evidence standards in children’s social care
records.description: Launch a review into children’s social care services in England which includes looking into strengthening evidence standards for decisions affecting families, improved independent review rights and correction processes for inaccurate records.
records.further_details:
Social services make life-changing decisions for children & families. We feel stronger safeguards are needed to ensure professional opinion & working hypotheses are not treated as established fact without appropriate evidence, transparency & opportunities for fair review.
 
We call for clearer recording standards, stronger evidence requirements, independent review rights, improved processes to challenge and correct inaccurate records, formal written accountability for significant decisions and records, and greater accountability while maintaining effective safeguarding.

records.title: Reform deportation Law for serious violent and sexual offenders
records.description: We call on the Government to amend immigration and deportation law so that long-term residence protections cannot prevent deportation where a non-British citizen has been convicted of serious offences including child sexual exploitation, rape, trafficking, murder, or serious violence.
records.further_details: The law should ensure that public safety and victims’ rights are given proper weight in cases involving grave criminal offending.

records.title: Reverse application of 20% VAT to independent schools
records.description: With the recent policy decision to apply 20% VAT on independent schools, we believe this additional burden on tax paying parents has had significant impact on the education system & caused the closure of schools with great history, legacy & value.
records.further_details:
As a parent, I want the Government to reverse this immediately.

One of the great schools being hit hard by this recent policy decision is St Joseph's College, Reading. Please help to save our school by removing VAT on all independent schools.

records.title: Increase the Motability mileage allowance from 10,000 to 15,000 miles per year
records.description: Increase the Motability mileage allowance above 10,000 miles. Mobility is about more than medical appointments and school runs. People need to visit family, including those 200+ miles away, and travel for mental wellbeing, breathing space, independence and quality of life.
records.further_details: Increase the Motability mileage allowance above 10,000 miles a year. Mobility is about more than hospital appointments, work and school runs. Customers need to visit family, including those living 200+ miles away, maintain relationships, access support and protect their mental and physical wellbeing. People should also be able to drive outside their town for fresh air, a change of scenery or breathing space without constantly worrying about running out of miles.

records.title: Anti-social behaviour in social housing: Review police response and enforcement
records.description: I call on the Government to review police response to anti-social behaviour in social housing & enforcement when tenants engage (but not limited to) threats, intimidation & repeated harmful behaviour. I believe there should be clearer limits on out-of-court disposals & faster action from the police
records.further_details:
No one should have to feel unsafe in their own home after reporting threats, intimidation or repeated anti-social behaviour. I believe that too often, victims face ongoing fear and disruption while authorities take time to act. Serious incidents may not result in formal prosecution despite strong supporting evidence, and housing action can be slow. In my view this leaves victims exposed to further incidents.
I want stronger, more consistent action so victims are better protected and can feel safe in their homes again.

records.title: Legislate a statutory maximum temperature for classrooms and fund school cooling
records.description: We want the government to establish a statutory maximum classroom temperature and provide ring-fenced grants to fund air conditioning in schools that breach this limit. We are concerned that schools cannot afford this vital safety equipment without central funding.
records.further_details: We believe classrooms are dangerously hot. Combined with warm nights at home causing sleep loss, children cannot concentrate - just as crucial exams occur in peak summer. Schools cannot fix this; their budgets cannot cover capital costs like AC. Many MPs and office workers enjoy climate-controlled environments, yet children are left baking. The Government must legislate a strict maximum heat cap and provide central funding to enforce it.

records.title: Make it an offence to post accident or crime scene photos on social media
records.description: Introduce legislation to prohibit the publication of photos of crime scenes and accidents - particularly those involving serious injuries and fatalities - to prevent people from profiting from the suffering and misfortune of victims’ families. This should exclude regulated news organisations.
records.further_details: In 2024, I lost my brother in a tragic accident. Within 24 hours, a social media account with thousands of followers had posted footage of the scene, including the ambulance carrying his body. Instead of being able to grieve with my family, I spent hours trying to get the video removed. The road was already clear, so there was no public interest in sharing it. The same has since happened to other grieving families. No one should profit from another family’s loss.

records.title: Increase Universal Credit savings limits in line with inflation
records.description: We ask the Government to increase the £6,000 and £16,000 capital thresholds to the value these had in real-terms when they were set in 2006; introduce automatic annual uprating to maintain their value; and set proportionately higher capital thresholds for joint claims than for single claimants.
records.further_details:
Universal Credit reduces support when savings exceed £6,000, and closes claims when savings exceed £16,000.  These limits were set in 2006 and apply to single and joint claims.

Restoring the limits' original real-terms value could allow claimants to build financial resilience.   Joint claims should have higher limits to reflect that partners may not have access to each others' savings, and reduce barriers for those experiencing financial abuse.

records.title: Tighten Election Spending Rules to Prevent Mass Letter Campaigns
records.description: We call on the Government to ensure that all mass letters sent by political parties count towards legal election spending limits. These limits exist to keep elections fair and free from undue influence. We believe the current loophole lets wealthy donors, not voters, shape election outcomes.
records.further_details: Current rules let parties send letters to every voter during an election without it counting towards their legal spending limits, as long as they avoid naming the candidate or the election. Spending limits exist to keep elections fair, competitive and free from undue influence. We believe this loophole lets wealth shape outcomes rather than voters, as some reports have indicated in recent by-elections and council elections.

records.title: Introduce 25% commission rate cap for private hire (ride hailing companies)
records.description: We ask the Government to introduce regulations capping ride-hailing platform commission at 25% per trip and require transparency in fare and commission structures. Drivers are told lower fares improve rider affordability, yet high rates of commission impact fair earnings and transparency.
records.further_details: Drivers cover vehicles, fuel, insurance, maintenance, and self-employed tax. Yet commissions may hit 40-50%, slashing driver pay and pushing rider fares up. We call for a fair commission cap of 25% and transparency on fare splits. Lower commissions help provide a stable income for drivers and fairer, more predictable prices for riders.

records.title: Review Equality Act 2010 to protect Transgender, Non-binary & Intersex people
records.description: Launch a review into updating the Equality Act 2010 to explicitly improve protections for transgender children and to include intersex and non-binary adults and children.
records.further_details:
We believe the law should reflect current medical understanding, lived experience and international human rights standards.
We are concerned that presently people’s rights are being pushed back, due to what we feel is a lack of clarity by the Equality and Human Rights Commission and Parliament in the protection of the LGBTQIA+ population.
We feel our government has a duty to keep The Equality Act 2010 up to date.
There were 262,0000 trans people and around 30,000 non-binary people identified in the UK Census 2021. It is also reported that there are around 358,105 people with intersex variations in the UK.

records.title: Do not ban mobile phones in schools for students over KS3
records.description: The government is moving toward a legal ban on mobile phones in schools. We think that while this is agreeable for perhaps Key Stage 3 and below, it is simply ridiculous at a certain age. People who are able to vote in general elections by the end of this year, are treated like children.
records.further_details: Schools often let older students out into the local community at lunch. If a student were to be attacked somewhere away from others, there would be no way to call for help. We believe that if the government keeps treating us like infants, we will not make good adults. Teenagers are the future of this country, and we should have a say in decisions that affect us.

records.title: Fund new reservoirs to increase future water supplies
records.description: England faces growing pressure on its water supplies due to factors like population growth, climate change and rising demand. The Government estimates 5 billion litres more water per day will be needed by 2050. Substantial additional water storage capacity will be needed to meet this challenge.
records.further_details:
We ask the Government to commit to a long-term programme of funding new reservoirs to increase water storage capacity and secure future water supplies.
 
We believe building new reservoirs will help provide reliable water supplies during periods of drought, reduce pressure on rivers and groundwater, support farming and allow England to accommodate future population and economic growth while protecting the environment.

records.title: Issue a formal UK Government apology to the victims of the Tinker Experiment
records.description: We call upon the UK Government to apologise for its role in the Tinker Experiment. We also want the Government to recognise the intergenerational trauma caused to families within the indigenous highland traveller community.
records.further_details: The Tinker Experiment was a range of policies that targeted Traveller groups in Scotland. Such policies included assimilation into sub-standard accommodation and the unlawful removal of Traveller children from their families. This was done in an attempt to disintegrate Traveller life, liberty and ethnicity. This has been cited by independent human rights assessments as the cause of  severe cultural harm. While the Scottish Government has apologised, the UK Government has yet to apologise for its role.

records.title: Fund direct discounts on repair bills for clothing & footwear
records.description: We call the UK Government to introduce a British Repair Bonus: a practical, people-first discount that makes repairs more affordable for everyone. Modelled after France’s repair bonus, we want a government-backed discount applied, which is directly deducted from the repair invoice.
records.further_details:
We want the British Repair Bonus applied to clothing and footwear. We feel that too often, repairing clothing and footwear costs more than replacing them, which can drive up waste and put pressure on household budgets whilst skilled tailors and cobblers struggle to survive.
We call on the Government to make repairs more affordable by funding a discount, and to include textiles within the UK's Right to Repair framework, in order to reduce textile waste, and support consumers & local businesses.

records.title: Increase the Council Tax Single Person Discount from 25% to 50%
records.description: Amend Council Tax legislation to increase the Single Person Discount to 50% for all single-adult households. We believe this will ensure fair taxation for people living alone.
records.further_details: Single occupants currently receive only a 25% discount, forcing them to pay 75% of the total bill. We believe this penalises single people, who must already cover 100% of rent, mortgages, and fixed utility standing charges on a single income. Single-person households will almost always use fewer local services than multi-adult homes. In our view, the current system acts as an unfair penalty on those living alone due to choice, divorce, bereavement, or circumstance. We want the discount to be raised to 50% to reflect true fairness.

records.title: Fund a 30-35 Railcard
records.description: We call on the Government to fund a railcard for adults aged 30-35.
records.further_details: We think the 26–30 Railcard leaves a gap for individuals aged 30 to 35 who may be navigating rising living costs, rent increases, and commuting expenses. Those in their early 30s must pay full price despite often being at critical early stages in their careers or starting families.

records.title: Suspend MCA plans to remove Coastguard Rescue Officer remuneration
records.description: Require the Maritime and Coastguard Agency to suspend its plans to remove remuneration for Coastguard Rescue Officers and move to an expenses-only model, pending an urgent legal, equality and operational review.
records.further_details: Following Groom v MCA, we believe the MCA’s plan to remove CRO remuneration and move to expenses only undermines the judgment and strips recognised workers of rights - In effect, making around 3,500 remunerated CRO roles effectively redundant and asking the same people to continue the same skilled emergency work unpaid. We believe this risks resignations, reduced availability, inequality and a weaker emergency response. Government must suspend the plan pending a legal, equality and operational review.

records.title: Exempt Lifelong Warfarin Users from NHS prescription charge
records.description: We want lifelong warfarin users to be exempt from NHS prescription charges. Patients with mechanical heart valves must take warfarin for life and have no choice but to remain on this medication.
records.further_details:
People born with congenital heart disease who require a mechanical heart valve must take warfarin every day for life to prevent blood clots, stroke and valve failure.

Unlike people with some other lifelong conditions, those who depend on warfarin after mechanical valve replacement are not exempt from prescription charges. We think this is unfair. We call on the Government to fund an NHS prescription charge exemption for a lifelong warfarin users.

records.title: Publish framework to remove VAT on donations of medicines
records.description: Patients with rare cancers face limited treatment options. VAT should not create another barrier to accessing possibly life-extending medicines offered free of charge. We ask the Government to publish their plans on removing VAT on medicines donated via compassionate-use and early-access schemes.
records.further_details: The Government has already recognised this problem and committed to a new approach. We ask the Government to act urgently and publish its plans and the new framework on removing VAT on medicines donated through compassionate-use and early-access schemes, and ensuring no patient loses access to treatment simply because a free medicine creates a tax charge.

records.title: Stop charging VAT on fuel duty
records.description: Remove VAT from the fuel-duty element of petrol and diesel prices. We believe a tax should not itself be taxed. Require announcements of fuel-duty changes to clearly state the full VAT-inclusive impact, rather than just the change in duty.
records.further_details: VAT is charged on fuel duty: a tax on a tax. At current rates, removing this would cut the tax on petrol and diesel by 10.59p per litre, allowing the same reduction at the pump if passed on in full. Higher pump prices also mean more VAT per litre. We want relief for households and businesses, not the abolition of all fuel taxes. We believe the Government should exclude fuel duty from VAT and ensure the saving reaches consumers.

records.title: Review how rape and sexual offence information is recorded
records.description: A review should examine how rape and sexual offences are recorded across police, prosecution and courts, and seek to establish consistent reporting of cases, charges, prosecutions, convictions and other outcomes.
records.further_details: The public needs a clear and transparent picture of rape and sexual offending. Different official sources can measure different things, including police-recorded offences and estimated victimisation. We want the Government to identify gaps and inconsistencies and explain clearly what happens to cases from reporting through investigation, prosecution and final outcome.

records.title: Fund breast cancer referrals for all patients regardless of age & family history
records.description: Fund urgent breast cancer referrals for any patient presenting breast cancer symptoms to a GP and ensure they are automatically put on the urgent referral pathway, regardless of their age or family history.
records.further_details:
Current GP guidelines restrict fast-track breast cancer referrals by age, which can leave younger patients struggling for urgent care. Yet, it is reported that around 2,500 UK women aged 40 & under are diagnosed annually, along with 400 men. 
 
Around 85% of patients have no family history, and it is the leading cause of death in women under 50. We believe we must remove these restrictive barriers so everyone presenting with potential breast cancer symptoms gets immediate, life-saving care.

records.title: Hold a review into alcohol home delivery and safeguarding of vulnerable adults
records.description: Commission a review into safeguarding gaps in the home delivery of alcohol. It should examine enforcement of the Licensing Act 2003 for delivered alcohol, doorstep intoxication checks, and the regulatory accountability of online delivery platforms.
records.further_details: Alcohol home delivery has expanded rapidly through supermarkets and delivery apps, with little corresponding scrutiny of safeguarding. Doorstep intoxication checks are inconsistent. Round-the-clock availability removes friction at moments of relapse or crisis. Regulatory accountability is unclear where third-party platforms fulfil sales. A review is needed to assess the harms to vulnerable adults and recommend reform.

records.title: Protect UK citizens’ living in the EU right to home fee status & loan access
records.description: We call on the Government to scrap plans to remove university home fee status and student loan access from British citizens living in the EU from 2028. This could financially discourage EU-based UK citizens from studying in the UK. Often, one or both parents have paid into the UK tax system.
records.further_details:
I am one of many bi-national families living in Europe and I am thinking about our childrens' futures. I feel it is unfair that UK citizens living in the EU shouldn’t have the same opportunity to send their children to UK universities, as those living in the UK. 
 
Often, families are in the EU because one, or both parents are on temporary relocation (3-5 years or more). Potential students who are British nationals and are living in the EU are often bilingual and could be excellent additions to the UK universities.

records.title: Introduce local authority run permit system for homeless outreach services
records.description: Introduce permit system for organisations delivering homeless outreach services. We think a permit system overseen by local authorities could ensure a better regulated provision and ensure service standards, preventing the delivery of such services being banned due to poor practice of some services.
records.further_details: We believe without a permit system, some local authorities may instead move to restrict the access to homeless outreach services which we believe risks removing vital support. We recognise concerns around safety and disruption caused by poor practices of some services, but we think banning services will only displace the issue. A permit system could enable better regulation, coordination, and accountability of services, while ensuring vulnerable people can still access essential support.

records.title: Strengthen sentences for death & injuries caused by criminal use of vehicles
records.description: We ask the UK Government to review the law and introduce stronger offences and sentencing where people are seriously injured or killed by offenders using stolen or illegally ridden vehicles.
records.further_details: Current laws do not always reflect the devastating consequences for victims and their families. We believe that where offenders knowingly ride stolen vehicles, drive dangerously, flee the scene, or show reckless disregard for human life, sentences must be tougher. We want this new law to be called Sienna’s Law.

records.title: Ensure provision of emergency stoma kits in supermarkets and shopping centres
records.description: We want the Government to help people who are in a situation with their stoma bags not feel embarrassed by mandating that emergency kits are available in supermarkets & shopping centres, like sanitary products. There are more people with them now. Maybe a card to ensure they are entitled to them.
records.further_details: My husband, who has now sadly passed away, was once in a situation where his bag has split. The glue wasn’t sticking on his spare and we had no alternative. It is difficult for people to imagine how that feels. I went into multiple pharmacies to be told I needed a prescription. In an emergency, I think it’s a little bit demoralising to have to worry about the risk when it could be easily solved. It the world we live in today I think that these should be made readily available.

records.title: Require clear front-of-pack religious certification labelling on food & drink
records.description: We want the Government to require front-of-pack labelling for all food and drink products that have a religious certification, including halal, non-halal, kosher, and non-kosher. Clear labelling could help everyone make informed choices, including those with religious dietary needs.
records.further_details: We want recognised religious certification symbols clearly displayed on the front of all food and drink products, so consumers can easily see when an item meets these standards. We also want a simple red line through the symbol to show when a product does not hold a religious certification. Clear, universal front of pack symbols could give everyone straightforward, transparent information when choosing food.

records.title: Introduce a total ban on any fox killing and mandate non-lethal management
records.description: Ban all fox killing/injuring in the UK, including for "control." Amend the law to mandate humane, non-lethal deterrents (fencing, tech, guardian animals) for farmers and ban any lethal control or culling. We must transition from what we see as extermination to coexistence. Protect our wildlife now.
records.further_details: We want Parliament to amend the Hunting Act 2004 and Wild Mammals (Protection) Act 1996 to outlaw all intentional killing or injuring of foxes, ensuring that no foxes can be killed for "pest control" or any other purposes. Parliament must mandate the use of humane, non-lethal deterrents such as fox-proof fencing and motion-tech and the provision of government subsidies to help farmers transition. We demand an end to what we see as the culling cycle, shifting UK policy toward a model of coexistence that protects our wildlife from all harm.

records.title: Fund heart ultrasounds as part of NHS health check for those aged 45+
records.description: We call on the Government to fund heart ultrasounds to check cardiovascular health, as part of the NHS health check for over 45s. A British Heart Foundation study has shown an increase of an 18% spike in cardiovascular disease related deaths among working-age adults.
records.further_details: Early intervention can be critical and could significantly reduce heart attack/death. A someone who suddenly lost someone due to a heart attack, it pains me to think how this could have been intervened and potentially saved their life. I then thought about how many adults have their life cut short due to a cardiovascular issue that most people probably didn't know they had. The aim of this petition is for heart ultrasounds to be included as part of the NHS health check, potentially saving lives.

records.title: Review evidence underpinning recent tax reforms affecting independent schooling
records.description: Commission an independent review of the evidence underpinning tax reforms implemented in 2025 affecting independent schooling: VAT on fees & removal of charitable business-rates relief, including their cumulative effects, assumptions & forecasts, assessed against evidence since reforms took effect.
records.further_details: A parent-led organisation, the Association for Families of Independent Schooling (AFIS), has analysed the published evidence underpinning the Government’s pre-implementation assessment of tax reforms affecting independent schooling and identified questions about assumptions, data, methodology and forecasts, including family and school responses, pupil movement, state education and public finances. We believe many questions still cannot be resolved from published information. Evidence of outcomes is now emerging, allowing the original forecasts to be tested

records.title: Reform Child Maintenance: Introduce a set weekly rate per child
records.description: Replace current income-based percentage system with a standardized set weekly rate per child. We think this would ensure all children receive a fair & consistent amount of support, regardless of their parent’s employment status or career success, while preventing excessive charges on working parents
records.further_details: In our view, the current system is unfair as non-workers or those on benefits often pay a flat rate of just £7 per week, while working parents can be charged extreme amounts—sometimes over £350 per week for the same number of children. We believe that a child’s basic needs do not fluctuate this wildly based on a parent’s salary. We call for a fixed rate that reflects the true cost of raising a child. This could remove the "work penalty," simplify the system, and ensure equal financial value for every child.

records.title: Review KCSIE to protect trans and intersex students' rights
records.description: We think the Keeping Children Safe in Education 2026 guidance is unsafe for trans youth and should be reviewed. For example, mandating active parental involvement in most cases, setting a binary criteria & requiring provision of single-sex toilet facilities unless self-contained individual toilets.
records.further_details: We believe that the KCSIE guidance does not adequately protect transgender and intersex students, and is violating their rights, and abusing their vulnerability. We urge the DfE and UK government to revise it to respect students’ gender identities, support use of chosen names and pronouns, provide safe and appropriate access to facilities, and explicitly prevent non-consensual “outing” of trans students, including parents, who may not be supportive. We think this would protect privacy, dignity and equality for every pupil.

records.title: Require airlines provide spaces for passengers to stay in their wheelchairs
records.description: Require airlines to provide safe, secure spaces on planes where wheelchair users can remain in their own wheelchairs during short-haul and long-haul flights.
records.further_details:
I have quadriplegic cerebral palsy and use a wheelchair. When I fly, I need two people to support me. I have to be lifted into my aircraft seat because I cannot use an aisle chair. I can also slip or slide in the aircraft seat.
 
I believe wheelchair users should be able to remain in their own wheelchairs during flights where it is safe and possible. This should apply to both short-haul and long-haul flights.

Wheelchair users deserve to travel safely and with dignity.

records.title: Review motorcycle access to bus lanes
records.description: Launch a review into motorcycle access to bus lanes, which looks into requiring councils to publish safety data and justifications for restrictions, and introducing consistent national guidance that improves safety, reduces conflict and supports predictable road layouts for all riders.
records.further_details: We believe allowing motorcycles in bus lanes supports aims within the UK’s new Active Travel Strategy (CWIS3) of achieving predictable layouts, conflict reduction and efficient use of road space, and has been shown to improve safety in several UK cities. However, we feel many areas still ban motorcycles without presenting clear evidence. A nationwide review could protect vulnerable riders, reduce risk and create consistent, evidence based national guidance.

records.title: Require large hotel chains to provide properly equipped accessible rooms
records.description: We want the Government to change the law so large hotel chains must offer a minimum number of properly equipped accessible rooms for 1 or 2 guests at fair prices.
records.further_details:
Disabled people are too often told the only suitable room is a larger and more expensive, can't accommodate families or that they must travel much further to find a hotel with the equipment they need. Wide doors, and level floors alone do not provide real access.

The law should require large hotel chains to provide proper accessible rooms, clear accessibility information, and equipment such as hoists or hoist-ready rooms, electric profiling beds and tilt-in-space shower chairs where needed.

records.title: Review and fund alternative tests for Lyme disease
records.description: We are concerned that the two-tier Lyme test can give some false negatives, including early on or in immunosuppressed people. We urge a review of broader, potentially more accurate tests to detect all strains. We think this will help prepare for future Lyme vaccines and ensure more timely treatment.
records.further_details: Lyme symptoms can vary in the body, ranging from person to person. Some research has suggested that neurological symptoms are associated like anxiety, ocd, psychosis, Parkinson’s, dementia. Joint issues which may appear to be rheumatoid arthritis can be Lyme arthritis needing different treatment. Heart issues like Lyme carditis, or other co-infections of Lyme like Babesia & bartonella, may also be missed in testing. We ask for a review of alternatives which can cover multiple strains with a higher accuracy.

records.title: Amend the Highway Code to incorporate Horse Riders'/handlers' hand signals
records.description: Add a photographic page of horse riders' hand signals used while on the road to clarify urgently for safety reasons what is referred to in 2 sections of the Highway Code, namely section 215 & the one on Signals to other Road users, so that they align with what is taught to horse riders.
records.further_details: Horse Riders are taught an extended arm moving up and down as a request for vehicle drivers to slow down. Section 215 of the Highway Code clearly states 'Look out for horse riders’ and horse drivers’ signals and heed a request to slow down or stop'. Yet the Highway code does not show what this signal is, and to confuse matters has explained elsewhere, in a photograph of a motorcyclist, that it means the horse rider is slowing down. Consistency is needed in the Highway Code and we believe the current advice could cause dangerous confusion.

records.title: Require all pet microchip databases to update contact details free of charge
records.description: Require all pet microchip databases to let owners/keepers update contact details free of charge. Keeping microchip records accurate is a legal duty. We think no one should have to pay to comply with it. Free, clearly-advertised updates mean more lost pets reunited with their owners.
records.further_details:
Owners/keepers are legally required to keep microchip details current, or risk a £500 fine - yet the 24 pet microchip databases charge inconsistent fees, from free to up to £30 one-off payments to tiered subscriptions. I am concerned this confuses owners and discourages updates. If it’s a legal duty, why should people pay to comply with it? Making updates free could remove a real barrier, ensuring the system works as intended for animal welfare and public safety. 

Make Chips Count - Pet Theft Reform

records.title: Mandatory 3-year custodial sentence for carrying a bladed article
