records.description: A mandatory three-year custodial sentence for anyone caught carrying a knife or other bladed article in public, without lawful reason. The law aims to deter knife carrying, strengthen consequences and prevent our children’s lives being taken. This could be known as Archie’s Law.
records.further_details:
No family should endure losing a loved one to knife crime. My son was just 19 when his life was tragically taken after a night out in Kingston in 2020. I lost my only child.

We need stronger measures to deter knife carrying and keep our children safe. Please sign and share this petition supporting serious consequences for carrying a knife or bladed article in public.

In my son Archie's memory—and for every family affected—let’s prevent another life being taken.

records.title: Require all end parking spaces to be for disabled parking
records.description: Require every end space in all car parks, including supermarkets, retail parks and council car parks, to be reserved for disabled parking where safe and practical. This provides vital side access for wheelchair users and carers to open doors and transfer people safely.
records.further_details: Disabled parking is about more than being close to a building. Many wheelchair users need extra space beside their vehicle to open doors, position a wheelchair and safely transfer with help from a carer. Ordinary bays are often too narrow. End spaces provide natural side access. We want every suitable end space in car parks to be a disabled bay, making everyday life more accessible and reducing barriers for wheelchair users and carers.  Access Is a Necessity, Not a Luxury.

records.title: Review the NPPF to strengthen protections for Green Belt and National Landscapes
records.description: Review and amend the National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) to introduce clear national standards for protecting Green Belt, Grey Belt and National Landscapes. Require brownfield land, urban densification, infrastructure and Green Infrastructure to be assessed before protected land is allocated.
records.further_details: We support the Government's ambition to build needed homes and believe the NPPF should set clear national standards before Green Belt, Grey Belt or National Landscapes are considered for development. Planning decisions should be transparent and evidence-based. Brownfield land, regeneration, densification, infrastructure and Green Infrastructure should be assessed before protected land is released. This would improve public confidence, support sustainable housing and protect England's landscapes.

records.title: Explicitly name Selective Mutism in national SEND training for schools
records.description: Selective Mutism is not named in SEND training published 24/09/26. It affects 1 in 140 children. We feel that more must be done to ensure it is supported in schools — where it happens.
records.further_details:
We ask Government to name it explicitly in the guidance, to work with expert organisations and include it in 2027 updates of the guidance.

In our view, when unnamed and excluded from this guidance, selective mutism can be misunderstood and negatively impact the student who may risk school avoidance and becoming NEET (not in education, employment or training). We believe support and safeguarding must be in place and is important when children cannot speak up and say “no”, “stop” or “I am hurt”. Support can be environmental adaptations, which may benefit every child. We call on the Government to involve experts and organisations specialised in selective mutism when reviewing this guidance.

records.title: Review policies for seized dogs to ensure their welfare
records.description: Review policies for seized dogs to ensure their welfare. Police should need clear evidence, written reasons, urgent welfare reviews and court/independent oversight before keeping non-banned family dogs with no history in kennels for weeks or months.
records.further_details: Dogs seized in investigations can be held in kennels for weeks or months while police and CPS decisions are awaited. Owners may have no visit rights, no guaranteed updates, no clear timescale and no written reason why the dog cannot return home under conditions. Dogs are living animals, not evidence in storage. The law should require urgent welfare reviews for continued detention.

records.title: Immediately close all asylum hotels & deport all illegal migrants living there
records.description: The Government pledged to close down asylum hotels in its manifesto for the 2024 General Election.
records.further_details: It has transpired that these hotels may stay open until 2029. We want these hotels shut down immediately, and to immediately deport any migrants or asylum seekers who are being housed there and came to the UK illegally.

records.title: Review shared care arrangements for ADHD between NHS and private specialists
records.description: Review shared care arrangements for ADHD where a patient has been diagnosed and stabilised by a qualified specialist, including appropriately qualified private specialists and via the Right to Choose pathway, to ensure consistent access to medication and continuity of care by the NHS.
records.further_details: We believe that many ADHD patients who seek private diagnosis to avoid long NHS waits, or access care via the Right to Choose pathway, are later refused shared care by their GP. This may force patients to pay privately or stop medication abruptly, which NHS guidance advises against. In our view this creates inequality, financial hardship, and risks patient safety, and a consistent national policy is needed to ensure fair access to treatment.

records.title: Public inquiry into illegal immigration
records.description: We call on the Government to launch a full-scale public inquiry into illegal immigration into the UK. The inquiry should investigate the effectiveness of UK border control, the financial cost on taxpayers, and the deportation system.
records.further_details: The issue of illegal migration is one of the most significant, complex, and debated challenges facing the UK today. There is widespread public concern about the scale, cost, and fairness of the current system — yet key facts remain unclear, data is inconsistent, and public trust has been eroded. We believe an independent public inquiry is the only way to establish the full truth, examine root causes, and recommend effective, fair solutions.

records.title: Allow tax-free salary sacrifice for fertility treatment and egg/sperm freezing
records.description: Government to allow individuals to pay for private fertility treatments, including IVF, egg/sperm freezing, and testing via tax-exempt Salary Sacrifice. The Treasury should classify reproductive care as an exempt workplace benefit, removing what can be a massive financial barrier.
records.further_details: Fertility challenges affect 1 in 7 UK couples, alongside same-sex couples and single individuals. Funding via the NHS can be limited, and private IVF or egg/sperm freezing can cost £5,000–£10,000+. We believe that if this was tax-free, more people could use bonuses for private care, significantly relieving NHS pressure. Currently, the only way to divert bonuses pre-tax is into pensions. We call on the government to allow pre-tax salary sacrifice for fertility treatments and testing to remove financial barriers and give everyone a fair chance to build a family.

records.title: Scrap Making Tax Digital (MTD) for Income Tax and remove £200 fine
records.description: The Government should scrap the new Making Tax Digital (MTD) scheme for Income Tax and revert to the previous system where Self Employed People handed in accounts once a Year. We also call on the Government to drop the £200 fines for late submissions and requirement to upload information online.
records.further_details: We think that the concept of putting personal information and confidential business information online is wrong, and that this information should be confidential. We simply call for Making Tax Digital (MTD) for Income Tax to be dropped and for a return to the Self Employment Tax system that we think has worked well for many years.

records.title: Ringfence NHS funding & review clinical training for women’s health conditions
records.description: Ringfence NHS funding and review clinical training for all women’s health conditions. This should comprehensively cover severe menstrual health, pregnancy, menopause, and all chronic pain, fatigue, or autoimmune ailments that disproportionately affect women.
records.further_details:
Historically, many have used the male body as the medical default. It is reported that women are more likely to die in car crashes as most dummies used in crash tests are male. Research shows that women are nearly twice as likely to experience adverse side effects from prescription drugs due to male-dominated clinical trials. 
 
Furthermore, around only 2.4% of research funding goes to gynaecological health. We ask for equity for our families, sisters and daughters.

records.title: Ban under 16s from being featured in social media content
records.description: Ban the publication and sharing of images and videos on social media featuring children under 16 years old. We believe children should not be used as content.
records.further_details:
We feel the ban on social media for under 16s misses one thing: parents can freely share their children online, even without the child's consent, sometimes to make money from them.
 
This can create a digital footprint for the child, long before they have access at 16 years old. Many children featured in social media content are bullied online (by adults) and face embarrassment as they grow up, being denied privacy for sensitive moments. We believe there are many safety & safeguarding concerns too.

records.title: Make bodycams and improved restraining training compulsory for SIA staff
records.description: We call on the Government to make it compulsory for all SIA staff to wear bodycams and for improved restraining training to be introduced for all SIA staff, in order to prevent death or serious injury to members of the public.
records.further_details: We believe that the use of bodycams and improved restraining training can ensure that members of the public restrained by SIA staff, such as door staff at a venue, are safer. We are concerned that the current standards of training mean that excessive force is sometimes used, which in some cases have led to deaths.

records.title: Require monitoring & response within 72 hrs to children at risk due to bullying
records.description: Require schools, local councils, CAMHS and safeguarding services to monitor & share information when a child is at risk due to severe bullying. We believe this must be treated as a safeguarding issue, and parents must be informed. This should be known as Ollie’s law.
records.further_details: We believe self-harm, suicide risk, school refusal, SEND vulnerabilities and mental health decline linked to bullying are all a safeguarding emergency which should require a response from support services within 72 hours. Children in this situation should be given a same-day risk assessment and safety plans, and be provided with support from a named continuity lead. We therefore want the Government to require monitoring and sharing of information when a child is at risk due to bullying, and for timely support to be provided.

records.title: Fund private healthcare for gynaecology wait list to clear the NHS backlog
records.description: Reduce suffering by providing targeted funding for the use of private facilities and surgeons to reduce the surgery wait list time for those with chronic gynaecological conditions such as endometriosis, adenomyosis and PCOS.
records.further_details: Around 1 in 10 women have endometriosis. Average diagnosis is 7-8 years that’s before treatment to relieve symptoms. There is no cure only management. It can affect fertility. It’s an invasive condition that returns. It can affect multiple organs including the bladder, bowel and even the lungs. Surgery waitlists are between 12-24 months once you get on them which takes years in itself. The pain doesn’t wait, this fast spreading condition just pushes on.

records.title: Regulate veterinary care costs to improve affordability & accessibility
records.description: We believe veterinary costs have risen significantly in recent years, placing financial pressure on pet owners and risking animal welfare when treatment becomes unaffordable.
records.further_details:
Regulate veterinary care costs, such as requiring transparent pricing, capping medicine markups and creating a Veterinary Ombudsman.
 
We feel veterinary costs have risen sharply, making essential care unaffordable for many pet owners and risking animal welfare. In some cases, routine procedures and emergency treatment for pets can cost more than equivalent surgeries for humans. We believe many practices also lack clear pricing, while medicine markups and prescription fees increase costs further. Following concerns raised by the Competition and Markets Authority, we believe stronger regulation is needed.

records.title: Immediately pause Pathfinder Courts roll-out to hold independent public inquiry
records.description: Pause the national rollout of Pathfinder/Child Focused Courts and launch an independent public inquiry into the family justice system, including CAFCASS, social services, judges, legal professionals, safeguarding failures, human rights breaches, and compliance with UK law.
records.further_details: The 2020 Report on Harm in Family Courts identified serious failings {in family courts}, including minimisation of domestic abuse, safeguarding failures, and children’s voices not being properly heard. Many families continue reporting mirroring concerns 6 years later. We believe expanding Pathfinder before these issues are investigated and addressed risks fast-tracking trauma for children and protective parents, increasing reliance on untested professional opinion, and undermining public confidence in the family justice system.

records.title: Create new national knife crime prevention strategy to save young lives
records.description: We want the Government to introduce a national knife crime prevention strategy, including harsher sentences, education in schools & prisons, youth services & early intervention, a confidential support helpline, & safe guidance for people who want to surrender knives before they are used.
records.further_details: No parent should have to watch their child face a future devastated by a knife attack. I am asking Parliament to act before another family gets that phone call: educate young people about knife crime, invest in youth support and early intervention, strengthen rehabilitation, and give people a safe way to ask for help and walk away from violence.

records.title: Introduce an offence to the Highways Act for failure to maintain public roads
records.description: Drivers and owners of vehicles used on the public highway can commit an offence if their vehicle is not maintained in a roadworthy condition. Introduce a similar legal offence to the Highways Act to prosecute responsible Authorities for failure to maintain the roads they are responsible for.
records.further_details: We believe that despite adequate tax revenue the public roads infrastructure has been poorly maintained and often poses a risk of damage to vehicles and to the safety of road users. The Highways Act 1980 places a duty of care on Authorities but without any sanction for failure to do so. We are concerned that Authorities have developed defensive procedures to deter and limit private claims whilst continuing to avoid their obligations under the Act. To correct this, we want sanctions for 'failure to maintain' to be set within the Act.

records.title: Preserve digital terrestrial television distribution to save Freeview
records.description: The Government’s White Paper on the future of TV distribution in the UK sets out its proposals to switch to internet-only TV in future. This is likely to have an impact on anyone living in a poor Internet location as it will end the current Freeview service.
records.further_details: The Government's White Paper makes clear that they intend to switch to internet-only TV in the future, which will be a problem for anyone in an internet blackspot. Many elderly people rely on TV as their only company on a daily basis. Once Freeview has gone, we believe it's a small step to charge per view for all TV, taking it away from the poorest in our society. Please help us save this precious service.

records.title: Review Landlords' Rights and Fair Balance in the Private Rental Sector
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce a faster, more efficient possession process where landlords have legitimate grounds for repossession, strengthen protections against late rent payments, rent arrears, and property damage, and ensure the courts resolve housing disputes promptly and fairly.
records.further_details:
We call on the UK Government to review the impact of the Renters' Rights Act 2025 and ensure tenancy laws remain fair for landlords. Recent legal changes created concerns about the ability of landlords to regain possession of their properties and manage financial risk.
We ask the Government for a faster, more effective possession process, quicker court claims, and timely recovery of properties where tenants repeatedly make late payments or fall into rent arrears.

records.title: Fund guaranteed paid community work shifts via Jobcentres
records.description: Fund a voluntary Community Works Guarantee allowing Jobcentres to offer paid shifts tackling community needs such as cleaning and maintenance.
records.further_details: We think that such shifts should not require qualifications or experience, letting unemployed people just turn up and work. They would be paid the National Living Wage and would get the chance to build a CV and boost wellbeing. We also think it would help councils, while protecting benefits for those unable to work.

records.title: Hold a consultation & publish a national strategy for foreign language teaching
records.description:
We call on Government to consult with language teachers across all educational levels & use this evidence to develop a modern national strategy for foreign language teaching.

This strategy should address curriculum content, assessment methods, & the level of difficulty in language qualifications.
records.further_details:
Foreign language learning in the UK is in long-term decline, with falling GCSE and A-level uptake and a shortage of teachers.

This has consequences for the UK’s global competitiveness, cultural understanding, and ability to engage internationally.

We call on the Government to publish a national strategy for foreign language education, including:
	•	measures to improve teacher recruitment & retention
	•	support for schools to expand language provision
	•	steps to increase student participation

records.title: Remove false accusations involving children services from parents’ records
records.description: We want the Government to legislate to automatically remove any accusations proven to be false as a result of previous investigations from parents' children’s services records, so that parents do not have to declare an involvement in the past with social services on future hospital, etc visits.
records.further_details: Claims that are proven false should be removed from these records if parents have done nothing wrong, and they should not be made to feel any shame that they feel whenever they visit a hospital.

records.title: Publish rationale and need for UK asylum law guidance, and risk mitigations
records.description: The Government has issued guidance to asylum seekers explaining UK laws and expectations, including on sexual consent, rape and sexual assault. We believe the public has a right to understand why this guidance was considered necessary and what evidence or risk assessment informed its introduction.
records.further_details: We are asking for the Government to be transparent about why it was necessary to issue asylum seekers with this guidance which includes rape, sexual consent and sexual assault. We call on the Government to publish the evidence and any risk assessments behind this decision and explain what screening, safeguarding and protective measures are in place to protect women, children and the wider public as a result. This is to ensure that any potential risks are properly assessed and managed and that the public is given clear info about how their safety is being protected.

records.title: Exempt all persons convicted of any sexual/violent offences from early release
records.description: We call on the UK Government to amend the Sentencing Act so that all individuals convicted of any sexual or violent offence are ineligible for any form of early automatic release scheme or brought-forward release dates.
records.further_details: Releasing convicted sexual offenders can cause severe trauma and psychological harm to victims. Many victims spend years in therapy preparing for a specific release date, only for sudden policy changes to destroy their mental health and sense of safety. We believe public safety and victim welfare must be prioritised over prison capacity, and offenders must serve their full, court-mandated sentences. We call on the government to protect the public by removing all violent and sexual offenders from early release entirely.

records.title: Launch a review into resourcing & behaviour policies in Multi-Academy Trusts
records.description: We call on the Government to launch a review into Multi Academy Trusts (MATs) to investigate pupil wellbeing & behaviour policies. We are deeply concerned by what we feel is a lack of accountability, with many trusts operating with little transparency and a non-functioning complaints procedure.
records.further_details: We want the Government to review behaviour policies and their impact on pupil wellbeing. The review should provide recommendations about ways to create a single, dedicated system that audits trust finances and recruitment to ensure funding prioritises qualified teachers over executive pay. Finally, we believe the Government should create a monitoring system to increase transparency and give parents, carers, and local authorities more involvement in key decisions to ensure inclusive education, especially in rural single-school areas.

records.title: Statutory right for domestic abuse victims to separate from joint mortgages
records.description: Create a statutory right for domestic abuse victims to unilaterally separate from joint mortgages, with specific protections against arrears, damaged credit and their abuser refusing to pay, sell or cooperate; ensuring a joint mortgage cannot be used as a tool of post-separation economic abuse.
records.further_details:
Despite physically escaping abuse, the mortgage system can leave victims financially tied and exposed to the consequences of their abusers’ actions. We want a statutory right where domestic abuse victims can unilaterally end their personal liability under a joint mortgage without their abuser’s consent.
 
I feel the experiences of domestic abuse victims show a wider gap in protection: survivors should not remain vulnerable to post-separation economic abuse through a joint mortgage. Leaving an abuser should mean freedom including financial freedom.

records.title: Fund mandatory dementia training for all health and social care professionals
records.description: We want the UK Government to fund mandatory dementia training for all health and social care professionals, incorporating lived experience and person-centred care.
records.further_details: I want to educate and empower others. People living with dementia should receive the dignity, compassion and person-centred care that everybody deserves.

records.title: Legalise spray, tasers & airguns for self-defence & require businesses hold them
records.description: We should be allowed to prepare to defend ourselves and those around us, I want to legalise the use and carry of pepper spray and tasers and also allow the use of less lethal airguns in your home. We feel that we can prepare for every worst scenario except for defending ourselves.
records.further_details: Legalise pepper spray and tasers allowing anyone to carry them. Make all business have them and complete a mandatory course and be inspected once a year like fire extinguishers so we know people are safe everywhere. We think that not only would it guarantee to save lives, it could generate billions for the economy and create lots of jobs. We believe there is literally no downside to this and that even the thought of people carrying items to defend themselves with is enough to put off potential attackers.

records.title: Appoint a Minister of State for Water Safety
records.description: We want the Government to appoint a Minister of State for Water Safety. The Minister should ensure water safety standards are adhered to, warnings are put out all year-round, so landowners take responsibility for their land/bodies of water, and adequate signage & safety equipment are in place.
records.further_details: We believe that local authorities should be responsible for their own areas; they need a point of contact. We want an official Minister who will support families and people affected by drownings regardless of the constituency they’re in.  We believe this Minister should be in charge of any safety standards relating to bodies of open water, as well as safety equipment, signage, maintenance, and fencing by open waters.

records.title: End the religious slaughter exemption and require irreversible stunning
records.description: Remove the religious slaughter exemption and require all animals to be irreversibly stunned before slaughter. End non-stun and recoverable stunning for religious slaughter, in recognition of animals as sentient beings under the Animal Welfare (Sentience) Act 2022
records.further_details: Current law permits religious slaughter exemptions for halal and kosher production, allowing animals to be slaughtered without prior stunning. Recoverable stunning is also used in halal slaughter, where animals may regain consciousness if the neck cut is delayed or ineffective. We believe all animals are sentient and should receive the same welfare protection at slaughter, regardless of the intended market. The exemption should end and irrecoverable stunning should be required for all animals.

records.title: Fund a dedicated family support team for all missing children cases
records.description: As the mother of Ben Needham, I know the pain of no answers. Families face unequal support. We call on the UK Government to fund a centralised team to ensure fair, equal help for all missing children cases. so no family fights alone.
records.further_details:
Families of missing children in the UK face an unfair and inconsistent system, where support, funding, and resources vary widely between cases. No family should have to struggle alone or feel their child matters less because of circumstance or attention.
 
This petition calls on the UK Government to establish a fully funded, centralised team to ensure equal support, resources, and long-term assistance for all families of missing children—so that no one is left to fight for answers on their own.

records.title: A nationwide referendum on reinstating the death penalty for child sexual abuse
records.description: We want the British public to have a say on whether the most serious child sexual abuse offences should be punishable by death or be tax-funded with life imprisonment.
records.further_details: We ask the Government to allow the British people to vote in a national referendum to reinstate the death penalty for child sexual abuse that leads to death or life-changing harm.

records.title: Seek agreement to protect refugees and restore humanitarian access in Libya
records.description: We call on the UK Government to work with international partners to strengthen protection for refugees, asylum seekers, and migrants in Libya and to seek to ensure humanitarian organisations have safe and sustained access to provide assistance.
records.further_details: There are reports from the UN and humanitarian organisations alleging serious human rights abuses against refugees, asylum seekers, and migrants in Libya. We are also concerned that humanitarian organisations may face growing restrictions, limiting access to safety and assistance for vulnerable people. The UK should support international efforts to improve protection, humanitarian access, and safe pathways for those at risk.

records.title: End routine PIP reassessments for people with lifelong & progressive conditions
records.description: We want the Government to end routine Personal Independence Payment (PIP) reassessments for people with lifelong, progressive or irreversible conditions where there is no realistic prospect of significant improvement. Most chronic illness' worsen over time / remain unchanged from initial assessment.
records.further_details: People with lifelong and progressive conditions are often required to undergo repeated reassessments despite medical evidence showing their condition is unlikely to improve. We believe these reassessments cause unnecessary stress, worsen health, consume NHS and DWP resources, and provide little benefit. We believe longer-term or ongoing awards should be the default for claimants with permanent conditions.

records.title: Make covert placement of a tracking device an offence without repeated tracking
records.description: I call on the Government to make it a criminal offence to intentionally and covertly place a tracking device on another person’s vehicle, belongings or property to monitor or locate them without consent. The offence should apply from the initial placement, without requiring repeated tracking.
records.further_details: Covert tracking can be used in stalking, domestic abuse and coercive control, exposing someone’s home, workplace or place of safety. The law should recognise the danger from the moment a device is deliberately placed with intent to track or locate someone. Victims should not have to prove repeated monitoring or a course of conduct before action can be taken. Once is enough.

records.title: Change family law proceedings burden of proof to “beyond a reasonable doubt”
records.description: In family law proceedings judges make decisions based on a standard of proof based on a balance of probabilities that something is more likely than not to have happened, and we think this should be changed in line with criminal law so that it must be proven “beyond a reasonable doubt”.
records.further_details: We think the current process is causing false allegations being upheld and can prevent parent and child contact, and that a parent can lie in family court in order to alienate the opposing parent. We believe this is happening purely because the balance of probabilities does not require the burden of proof to suggest that it is true beyond a reasonable doubt.

records.title: Cancel the consultation on “In-use emissions of road vehicles”
records.description: We believe the consultation for the "In-use emissions of road vehicles: regulating environmental impacts" is a pretext for taking many internal combustion engine cars off the road and pushing car ownership outside the financial reach of millions of taxpayers. We want the consultation cancelled.
records.further_details:
We feel the consultation is unclear over the aims to take older cars off the road, referencing badly maintained and modified vehicles, which we are concerned is open to scope creep. Many perfectly roadworthy cars currently on the road may be prematurely scrapped, we believe makes no environmental sense.
 
At a time of financial hardship, we feel possible amendments to existing legislation could punish citizens who are already being squeezed by high inflation and low private sector annual pay increases.

records.title: Ban MPs who resign with open standards investigations from standing as an MP
records.description: MPs that resign and therefore escape open parliamentary standards investigations should be banned from standing as an MP, unless the investigations are resumed and completed whilst they are not in office.

records.title: Mandate a stand-alone VAWG policy in all secondary schools & colleges in England
records.description: Require all secondary schools and colleges in England to have a mandatory Violence Against Women and Girls policy by September 2027 as a legal requirement, including staff training, incident recording, published data and reporting routes.
records.further_details: We believe girls are being failed. Schools aren’t legally required to have a VAWG policy, record incidents separately, or train staff on misogyny and we feel victims are facing injustice and disadvantage to no fault of their own, in an environment they’re required and entitled to be in. Most schools are not required to track abuse incidents. The Government published a VAWG strategy in December 2025 but set no legal deadline for an explicit policy in schools. Girls deserve enforceable protection, not vague promises.

records.title: Ban the sale of vapes within a 1km radius of schools
records.description: We call on the Government to ban the sale of vapes, and ban new vape shops opening, within 1km of schools. This could reduce youth exposure to nicotine products, support public health, strengthen safeguarding, and help prevent underage vaping and addiction among children and teenagers.
records.further_details: Youth vaping has increased significantly across the UK, with many students regularly exposed to vape shops, advertising, and disposable vape products near schools. We believe the concentration of vape retailers close to educational settings normalises nicotine use and increases the risk of addiction among young people. We are calling on the Government to introduce a 1km protection zone around schools, in order to support healthier school environments for future generations.

records.title: Replace the VAWG strategy with a VAP - Violence Against People strategy
records.description: We call on the Government to replace the Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG) strategy with Violence Against People (VAP) strategy to ensure Government policy, funding and support protect all victims of violence, abuse and coercive control equally, regardless of sex, based on evidence and need.
records.further_details: In our view, the VAWG strategy treats violence as a sex-based issue rather than a behaviour based one. We think this overlooks male victims and risks unequal treatment. We therefore call on the Government to replace it with VAP (Violence Against People) so all victims receive equal recognition, protection and support regardless of sex. Policy should be evidence-led, based on individual circumstances, and should not presume victimhood before the facts are established.

records.title: Create and fund a support system for dog attack victims
records.description: Those attacked by dogs can be left with fear, nightmares and lasting trauma. Families can face huge gaps in care following dog attacks. We need a national trauma support service so victims aren’t left alone.
records.further_details: The Government should create and fund a national support system offering guidance, therapy and recovery so no child, adult or family is left to cope alone.

records.title: Require bereavement support in all private pregnancy scan clinics
records.description: We are calling for a legal requirement that at least one fully trained member of staff in bereavement and pregnancy loss support is present at all times in private scan clinics, with the knowledge to guide families through their next steps.
records.further_details: On April 1st 26, we attended a private clinic filled with excitement, expecting to see our baby at 9 weeks and 4 days pregnant. Instead, we were told that our baby’s heartbeat had stopped at 7 weeks and 3 days - a miscarriage with no symptoms. We were placed alone in a small side room. There was no trained professional to support us, no one to guide us through what had just happened, and no one who could answer the many questions we were left with.

records.title: Fund NHS BSL interpreters and deaf awareness training
records.description: Deaf BSL users can face barriers in A&E and NHS appointments. Some patients can't hear their names being called or access a BSL interpreter when needed. The government should ensure all hospitals provide timely BSL interpreters and deaf awareness training for staff.
records.further_details: Patients may not hear their names being called in A&E, clinics or appointments and can face delays in accessing qualified BSL interpreters. We are concerned that this can affect communication, informed consent, patient safety and dignity, particularly before operations and during emergencies. NHS hospitals should provide timely BSL interpreters and deaf awareness training for staff.

records.title: Fund a national lymphoma awareness and early diagnosis campaign
records.description: Fund a national lymphoma awareness campaign with the aim of increasing public awareness of the signs and symptoms of lymphoma so that people are better able to recognise unexplained or persistent symptoms and seek medical advice.
records.further_details: Lymphoma is one of the UK’s most common cancers, yet public awareness remains dangerously low. Early symptoms like a single swollen gland are easily mistaken for minor infections, causing severe diagnostic delays. Many patients, including myself, present with a single symptom. We must encourage early detection to catch this cancer early and save lives.

records.title: Mandate registration with a recognised regulatory body for all personal trainers
records.description: The Government must act to introduce a protected title of Registered Personal Trainer, require registration with a professional body, enforce qualifications, and create a national safeguarding register. We believe this will improve safety, accountability, and trust across the fitness industry.
records.further_details: Currently, anyone in the UK can call themselves a personal trainer without qualifications, registration, or oversight. While CIMSPA offers standards, its membership is voluntary. We believe this creates safeguarding risks, allowing banned individuals to operate freely. We call for a protected title, mandatory registration, minimum qualifications, and a national safeguarding system to protect the public and ensure accountability.

records.title: Government to mandate brownfield development targets for local councils
records.description: We believe that in order to meet government housing targets and protect greenfield land, the government should legislate to ensure that local councils are bound by law to develop housing on brownfield sites.
records.further_details: In our view, green spaces are under threat from unscrupulous developers while at the same time brownfield sites are abandoned and undeveloped. We therefore think local councils must be legally bound to develop such sites for housing. Brownfield sites are often a blight on the surrounding community, developing them could have multiple benefits including protecting green spaces.

records.title: Mandate standardised Trans HRT pescribing training for all NHS GPs
records.description: Many NHS GPs will not offer shared care for hormone pescribing for Trans patients who are under the care of a NHS GIC (Gender Identity clinic). In many cases, many of them cite not having training, or adequate training to do so.
records.further_details:
We feel this underserves the TNBI (Trans, Non Binary and Intersex) community. Ideally a letter from a NHS GIC or NHS Gender Service to pescribe and what dosages should be sufficient.

We are asking that the Government mandate TNBI pescribing training to all NHS GPs on a national level to so a TNBI person can access HRT pescribing at any NHS GP, anywhere within the whole of the country, without all the uncertainty.

records.title: Fund all NHS hospital parking through general taxation and abolish visitor fees
records.description: We believe hospital parking charges hit the poor, sick & and NHS staff unfairly. The Government should fund the costs of this from general taxation so NHS car parks are free at use. To prevent non-patient abuse, in-clinic digital validation kiosks could bill the Department of Health directly.
records.further_details: We believe that hospital parking fees are an unfair flat-rate tax that devastates the unhealthy-poor. The Government must fund NHS parking via general taxation. In our view, parking fraud by non-hospital commuters can be completely eliminated by moving all validation terminals inside specific hospital wards and clinics. Only genuine patients and visitors inside the building could then log their registration when leaving, billing the cost to the Department of Health who are funded through a fairer general taxation.

records.title: All video games must be available to purchase as a physical, complete version
records.description: Game developers when releasing a new game must provide a physical copy either disc or USB key. This media must be transferable and saleable.
records.further_details:
A physical copy of a game allows you to have ownership of the game.
It allows you to share the game with friends and family.
Having a physical game allows you to sell it and supports business that sell 2nd hand games.
2nd hand games can help those on low incomes to purchase games.

records.title: Mandate publishing annual statistics on data centre water & electricity usage
records.description: Parts of the UK have experienced a drought, and residents have been asked to conserve water. We are concerned that the concerted efforts to build new data centres could place a huge strain on our water supply.
records.further_details:
We feel our water supply has been pushed to breaking point. By allowing developers to opt into the NSIP regime, planning permission can be granted by Ministers and not local councils. 
 
We feel this denies residents meaningful control over stopping these developments from being built in their area, and that designating data centres as Critical National Infrastructure deserves special scrutiny as it gives data centres access to resources during shortages.
 
Data centres also use a huge amount of electricity, which could result in increases in wholesale electricity costs for everyone at a time when many are already financially struggling. We believe people deserve to know the impact data centres are having.

records.title: Conduct a review into women's confidence in Judicial handling of Rape
records.description: Recent high profile cases have been met with shock, anger and dismay. We are calling on the Government to review women's confidence in judicial handling of rape and particularly look at the Judicial Discipline guidance issued in July 2024.
records.further_details:
Currently, the conviction rate for all reported rape cases is 2% (Victims' Commissioner 2022). Many women withdraw because the process is stressful and the trial is retraumatising.

We believe that recent high profile cases will have produced a further serious loss of confidence in the judiciary's ability to administer justice in cases of violence against women and girls, which as well as being emotionally damaging to these victims, could deter other victims from pursuing cases.

records.title: Conduct review into NHS recognition, diagnosis & treatment of cluster headaches
records.description: Cluster headaches are among the most severe pain conditions but are often misdiagnosed and under-treated in the NHS. We feel the name fails to reflect their extreme, disabling nature, reducing urgency. Patients can face delays, poor access to oxygen therapy, and limited specialist care.
records.further_details: We call on the UK Government to review training and awareness among NHS staff, ensure faster and consistent referrals to neurology specialists, and expand access to effective treatments including oxygen therapy. We think greater public and workplace awareness is needed, alongside increased research funding and better NHS data collection. We also urge review of how cluster headaches are classified and described to better reflect their severity and impact.

records.title: Issue guidance encouraging compassionate leave for companion animal bereavement
records.description: We ask the Government to recognise companion animal bereavement by introducing guidance encouraging employers to allow compassionate leave when an employee experiences the death of a pet. This would help ensure employees are treated with understanding during a difficult time.
records.further_details: For many people, companion animals are beloved members of the family. Their loss can cause genuine grief and emotional distress. However, there is currently little recognition of pet bereavement in workplaces and people often feel their grief is dismissed with comments such as “it’s just a cat” or “it’s just a dog”. Recognising companion animal bereavement would help promote compassion and understanding for people experiencing this loss.

records.title: Ban all gambling advertisements
records.description: Ban all adverts that promote gambling on tv and in media.
records.further_details: Gambling is a serious addiction for many people that should not be advertised in an easy going manner.

records.title: Provide a 'Home Care Allowance' as an alternative to funded childcare
records.description: Introduce a Government-funded 'Home Care Allowance', equivalent to the value of funded childcare, for parents who are entitled to but choose not to claim funded childcare hours or Tax-Free Childcare so they can care for their child at home.
records.further_details: We believe parents who are entitled to funded childcare or Tax-Free Childcare should be able to choose an equivalent Home Care Allowance instead if they wish to care for their child at home. Current support mainly benefits families using formal childcare. We believe parents should have genuine choice, with equal Government support whether they choose nursery care or provide care themselves. Parents could not claim both.

records.title: Government to fund shortfall for Science and Technology Facilities Council
records.description: We want the Government to ensure sufficient funding beyond 31 March 2028 for the Science & Technology Facilities Council through the UKRI so that it no longer requires funding cuts which imperil key scientific research projects & establishments, such as Jodrell Bank Observatory & e-MERLIN project.
records.further_details: Ending scientific operations through the withdrawal of funding would affect thousands of scientists, risk many jobs, and, we believe, weaken international partnerships and remove nationally important training just as other countries are investing in areas such as radio astronomy and the Square Kilometre Array. We feel that losing this unique scientific and research capabilities, in the case of Jodrell Bank and the e-MERLIN project for the sake of just £2.8 million a year, would be a false economy.

records.title: Require stop signs at junctions from minor roads to A & B roads
records.description: The leading human factor in road casualty collisions is ineffective observation e.g. failing to look properly or misjudging the speed of approaching priority traffic. If Give Way signs at junctions from minor roads to A & B roads were changed to Stop, we think drivers would use better observation.
records.further_details:
Reported road casualty statistics for Great Britain in 2025 show that around half of all casualties resulted from collisions occurring at or within 20 metres of a junction. We are particularly concerned about T-Junctions and Staggered Junctions.
 
Drivers having to stop would allow more time for better observation. We believe this would reduce collisions and injury rates.
 
Roundabouts and Give Way junctions on minor roads would remain as currently signed.

records.title: Make it illegal for drivers to idle engines outside schools.
records.description: We call on the UK Government to make it illegal for drivers to keep car engines running while stationary outside schools, and to introduce penalties or mandatory environmental awareness courses for those who do.
records.further_details: Children are especially vulnerable to air pollution because their lungs are still developing, and many schools are near busy roads. Even one minute of engine idling releases unnecessary pollution, increasing the risk of asthma and breathing problems and contributing to climate change. Banning idling outside schools, with fines or environmental awareness courses, would reduce emissions and help keep children healthy and safe.

records.title: Make it mandatory for all food outlets/restaurants to offer gluten free options
records.description:
We call for:
1. At least three clearly labelled gluten-free option on every menu.
2. Staff training on gluten-free preparation and cross-contamination prevention.
3. Transparent ingredient labelling for all menu items.
4. Commitment to inclusivity for people with dietary restrictions.
records.further_details: For individuals living with coeliac disease, gluten intolerance, or other health conditions requiring a gluten-free diet, access to safe food is not a lifestyle preference—it is a medical necessity. Even small amounts of gluten can cause serious health consequences, making it essential that suitable alternatives are widely available.

records.title: Review compensation schemes for businesses affected by HS2 construction
records.description: We ask the Government to launch a review of compensation schemes for businesses  along the HS2 route that are suffering serious financial harm due to ongoing construction. Road closures, reduced access, noise, and disruption are driving away customers and putting many livelihoods at risk.
records.further_details: We request the Government to launch a review in order to ensure fair, timely compensation to businesses materially impacted by construction. This review should include looking at creating a new compensation scheme for HS2-affected businesses.

records.title: Review protections for England’s National Parks from industrial infrastructure
records.description: Review protections for England’s National Parks from industrialisation caused by large infrastructure projects. Stop private companies from damaging the environment, through projects not in keeping with local areas, even where biodiversity net gain might be demonstrated.
records.further_details: We believe our National Parks, such as the Peak District National Park, deserve better protection from large-scale industrial infrastructure projects. They are the jewel in the crown of our land, a vital natural haven for wildlife, and an escape for the public from the trials of modern life. They contribute to our economy via tourism, and help improve the mental health of the population.

records.title: Act to improve patient safety, staffing & accountability in NHS hospitals
records.description: We want Government to ensure the introduction and enforcement of  minimum safe staffing levels in NHS hospitals, strengthen accountability for poor patient care and set up a review of discharge practices.
records.further_details: We also want the Government to require the use of monitored safeguarding measures on wards caring for vulnerable patients. We hear of many patients, particularly elderly & vulnerable people, who experience unacceptable standards of care in NHS hospitals; patients left without basic dignity due to staff shortages; important medical notes not read or followed; & patients handled in ways that risk further injury; as well as concerns about patients being discharged too early due to pressure on hospital beds. We believe these systemic problems require Government action.

records.title: Require park home site owners to allow individual water meters
records.description: Require park home site owners to allow individual water meters, read such meters and provide bills for each homes usage.
records.further_details: Many park home sites have water supplied through one or two main meters. The subsequent bills are then divided by all residents regardless of how many occupiers there are in each home, so a single occupant pays the same as two or three. We believe residents should only pay for what they personally consume. With individual meters the owner will be encouraged to fix or replace old leaking pipework. Individual meters would provide fairness, improve accountability and encourage water conservation.

records.title: Increase the minimum sentence for those found guilty of rape to 15 years
records.description: Currently the minimum sentence for people convicted of rape is typically 4 years. I would like that to be upped to a minimum of 15 years.
records.further_details: We believe 4 years minimum in prison is not justice for those who have been raped, and that a minimum of 15 years would help give survivors greater justice and also more peace of mind that their attacker didn't simply get what some see as a slap on the wrist.

records.title: Reform statutory time limits for all offences involving child victims under 16
records.description: Review and reform statutory prosecution time limits for all offences involving victims under 16. A review could consider extending or removing time limits where delayed disclosure, safeguarding investigations, or multi-agency child protection processes may prevent prosecutions.
records.further_details: Current law means some common assault prosecutions become time-barred after six months. Children may delay disclosure due to fear, trauma, coercion or family pressures, while safeguarding investigations can take months to complete. Although Parliament has extended prosecution time limits in certain domestic abuse cases, victims under 16 may not benefit from equivalent protections. We call on the Government to review and reform the statutory time limits which can affect child victims.

records.title: Ban the sale and release of exotic and native waterbirds
records.description: Ban all breeding, sale and release of exotic and native water birds. We think birds may be mis-sold by breeders, which could lead to charities having to step in and rescue birds that are put in danger when released in insecure locations with unsuitable conditions by inexperienced owners.
records.further_details: I am a volunteer swan rescuer and I have seen many examples of irresponsible handling of birds and think we need to stop the sale and release of exotic and native waterbirds.

records.title: Fund affordable unilateral bras on the NHS
records.description: Fund affordable unilateral bras on the NHS. While some retailers offer post surgery bras designed to hold prostheses, bras for women with a single mastectomy who choose to remain flat on one side are much harder to find and often cost more.
records.further_details: For many of us, this is a valid, personal choice, yet access remains limited. We want the government’s help because we believe this is a structural access and fairness issue, not just a personal shopping problem. Post mastectomy needs are part of healthcare. Clothing that supports comfort, mobility, and wellbeing after surgery directly affects quality of life. Dignity, recovery, and equal access after cancer treatment should not depend on private retail choices or personal finances.

records.title: Cap Out-Of-Hours Veterinary Fees to Prevent Pet Abandonment
records.description: Introduce regulations to cap charges for essential veterinary emergency treatments carried out outside normal working hours, ensuring fees are fair, transparent, and proportionate, by scrapping excessive mark-up prices.
records.further_details: Pet owners are being charged disproportionately high fees for basic veterinary treatments outside normal hours. While higher costs for emergency care are expected, many practices charge 200–300% more for routine procedures such as blood tests and IV fluids. These costs place owners under severe financial pressure, sometimes forcing them to surrender or euthanise pets. With many dogs/cats having to be given up or just abandoned on the streets.

records.title: Allow trained HCPC podiatrists emergency access to hyaluronidase
records.description: Allow appropriately trained HCPC-registered podiatrists to obtain, store and administer hyaluronidase for the emergency management of suspected vascular compromise following the administration of hyaluronic acid gel for medical purposes in the lower limb.
records.further_details: This petition concerns medical hyaluronidase use in the lower limb by trained, insured, HCPC-registered podiatrists, not cosmetic practice. Vascular compromise is rare but serious and may require urgent hyaluronidase. As with emergency adrenaline, we believe trained podiatrists should be able to obtain, store and administer hyaluronidase for this specific emergency, under appropriate training and governance. In our view this is about timely emergency care, protecting patients and preventing avoidable harm.

records.title: Do not apply retrospective ILR rule changes to spouses on family visas
records.description: We call on the UK Government to ensure that spouses who have entered or applied to come to the UK via family visas are not unfairly affected by retrospective changes to rules relating to Indefinite Leave to Remain.
records.further_details:
Families make life-changing decisions based on the immigration rules in place when they apply. We believe it is unfair for new rules to be applied retrospectively to those, including spouses, who have already entered via the legal visa route.
 
We call on the Government to protect existing spouse visa holders and applicants from retrospective changes to ILR eligibility requirements and to recognise the emotional, financial, and mental health impact that changing rules have on families.
 
We feel that those who have followed the legal process should be able to rely on the rules that were in place when they applied.

records.title: Ban adoption & the removal of children from their birth parents
records.description: We call for a complete ban on adoption and any legal activities that aim to take children away from the care of their birth parents. The Government should provide services to support families and end any discrimination or human rights abuses.
records.further_details:
We believe the laws need to change surrounding laws regarding children, to end and ban adoption. We support this proposal because we believe children deserve positive relationships with their biological parents, and that children services’ assessments are discriminatory and are destroying families. 
 
We believe adoption should be illegal, that the foster care sector should be entirely closed down, and that it should be illegal to remove children from the care of their biological parents.

records.title: Ban breeding & use of doves & pigeons at weddings, funerals & sex reveal events
records.description: Legislate to prevent breeding of doves and pigeons intended for release at weddings/funerals and make it illegal to pay to release birds at such events. Many of these birds are unable to navigate their way back home and as they are domesticated, they may not survive in the wild after being released.
records.further_details: Release of white doves and pigeons at family events has become a fashionable yet, in our view, cruel spectacle and an industry is growing to accommodate this. We believe that a majority of the birds are released to die slowly from starvation as they have been reared in aviaries and fed daily with no opportunity to develop navigational or foraging skills or ability to find appropriate shelter. We think this industry needs to be stopped forthwith and not facilitated by churches or wedding organisers.

records.title: Launch a public inquiry into the costs of imposing VAT on private school fees
records.description: We would like the Government to launch a public inquiry into the costs involved in imposing VAT on private school fees, including the costs of school closures, redundancies, fiscal costs due to the decline in overseas pupils, and the subsequent harm to surrounding areas and local economies.
records.further_details:
We feel the imposition of VAT on private school fees is an attack on perceived privilege, with the main victims being pupils with parents and grandparents who are making sacrifices to send their children to private schools. The imposition of VAT is an extra cost and has made private schooling untenable for many.
 
We feel the rich are not really affected. We believe the other victims of cost-cutting and redundancies are working-class ground staff, cleaners and security. We would like the inquiry to investigate whether the costs outweigh the extra revenue, and the amount of revenue that placing VAT on private schools has actually raised

records.title: Ban AI advertisements
records.description: The government should create legislation to prevent businesses using generative AI for advertisements, including medical advertisements.
records.further_details:
We believe Generative AI ads can be dangerous - especially to those who struggle to tell if something’s real or not.
 
Real photos, videos and testimonials of products should be used instead.

records.title: Review NHS guidance on iron deficiency for women
records.description: Iron deficiency is one of the leading contributors to the global burden of disease, disproportionately impacting reproductive age women. We think iron deficiency is often overlooked because blood counts or ferritin is in “normal range” and NHS guidance should be reviewed to support women's health.
records.further_details: Some research suggests that laboratory ferritin reference intervals result in under-diagnosis and under-treatment of iron deficiency, especially in women. Current evidence suggests that a serum ferritin concentration of less than 30 μg/L has a high specificity and sensitivity for diagnosing iron deficiency in adults. The NHS guidance is different across regions, and some only flag low levels for women when under 15 μg/L. We believe this results in underreporting of a widespread health issue.

records.title: Require an apology to SEND families for local authority failures
records.description: We are calling on the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, to issue a formal apology to families of children with SEND for years of failures within local authority SEND services. Families have faced delays, poor communication and purposeful barriers to support, causing significant stress and harm.
records.further_details: For years, families across England have been left exhausted and distressed, fighting battles they should never have had to face simply to secure support for their children. They repeatedly describe local authorities putting systems and processes in place designed to delay progress, create barriers and wear them down rather than help. Behind every delay is a child waiting for support and a family living with heartbreak. Current reforms will be meaningless if local authorities do not change.

records.title: Publish a timetable and approval pathway for supervised self-driving systems.
records.description: Publish a timetable and approval pathway for supervised self-driving systems in GB.
records.further_details:
The Government has published plans for self-driving vehicle pilots and is implementing the Automated Vehicles Act 2024. However, there remains uncertainty around the assessment and approval of supervised self-driving systems that require an attentive human driver.

We believe the Government should publish a clear timetable, safety requirements and approval pathway for these systems so that manufacturers, consumers and road users understand how they will be evaluated for use on roads in Great Britain.

records.title: Make it an offence to publish suspect details before they are charged
records.description: We want publishing details of a suspect before they have been charged with a crime to be an offence to protect innocent people being destroyed by false allegations. Public naming before charge can cause irreversible harm to innocent people. Some people lose their jobs reputations & mental wellbeing.
records.further_details: Some people’s lives are being torn apart by public accusations before any charge is made. Jobs are lost, families suffer and mental health collapses under judgement for allegations that may never lead to a charge. We therefore call for naming a suspect before they are charged with a crime to be an offence, so people are not destroyed by premature exposure and can keep their dignity while the justice process runs its course.

records.title: Fund free hospital parking for NHS staff and students on placement
records.description: We want the Government to fund free hospital parking for staff and medical & dental students working in NHS hospitals on placement during working hours and ensure they are protected from parking penalties at all times, including when they are required to work beyond their scheduled hours.
records.further_details: NHS staff can face significant parking costs simply for attending work, with some hospitals charging around £10 to £12 per day. Medical and dental students can also pay substantial amounts while completing compulsory NHS placements. We believe the Government should fund free parking for staff and students working in NHS hospitals, and ensure staff are not penalised, including when clinical duties unavoidably require them to work beyond their scheduled hours.

records.title: Require Rapeseed Oil to be listed as an allergen on food packaging
records.description: We want  the Government to ensure that Rapeseed Oil is listed as an allergen on food packaging. Many brands have switched to Rapeseed without labelling it as a recipe change & this is causing a health issue as many people find they are unable to consume the same foods without stomach upset.
records.further_details: Many people are finding it difficult to navigate shopping as many foods sold in supermarkets have switched to using this cheaper oil which is causing people to have reactions to foods that should otherwise have no issue. Rapeseed Oil is now found in many products such as Greek yoghurt, bread and dried fruits despite not needing oil to make. This petition is to make it so that Rapeseed Oil is listed in bold as an allergen to make it easier for people with IBS and allergic reactions to avoid said foods.

records.title: Strengthen the Serious Violence Duty to Help Keep Young People Safe
records.description: We call on the UK Government to strengthen the statutory Serious Violence Duty by introducing minimum national standards for youth violence prevention, including access to safe youth spaces, early intervention, mentoring and community-based prevention programmes.
records.further_details:
The Government must strengthen the Serious Violence Duty by ensuring:
 
• Safe youth spaces in every community.
• Early intervention for young people at risk.
• Long-term funding for prevention.
• Transparency on local prevention efforts and outcomes.
• A meaningful voice for affected young people and families.
 
We cannot wait until a child is injured, exploited or killed before acting.  Prevention must come before tragedy. We've had enough children dying. Enough families bereaved. Enough funerals. This should be done in memory of Jamal.

records.title: Put all proposals for closer ties to the EU to a referendum
records.description: Hold a referendum on proposals for closer ties to the European Union, and commit to holding a referendum on any future proposals for closer ties, including if the government decided it wanted the UK to become a full EU member state.
records.further_details: Because the current Government are making decisions to have closer ties to the EU without asking the electorate via a referendum.

records.title: Regulate “Counsellor” and “Psychotherapist” as protected statutory titles
records.description: Introduce statutory regulation for counselling and psychotherapy, with protected titles for “Counsellor” and “Psychotherapist”. Anyone using these titles must meet statutory standards, register with an independent statutory regulator, and be subject to complaints and fitness-to-practise processes.
records.further_details: Faster access to therapy must develop alongside safety. People seeking counselling or psychotherapy may be distressed, isolated or in crisis. They shouldn't have to navigate unclear titles, voluntary registers and complex complaints routes alone. Protected titles would not prevent all malpractice, but could create clearer standards, support ethical practitioners and strengthen accountability when therapy causes harm. This matters as harm can be hard to report due to stigma, shame or disbelief.

records.title: Review DWP guidelines for DLA Higher Rate Mobility component
records.description: Review DWP guidelines for the DLA Higher Rate Mobility component, to ensure the assessment explicitly recognises that autistic children who lack spatial and danger awareness, and risk bolting or self-harm MAY meet the criteria for "virtually unable to walk" due to severe safety risks.
records.further_details: Many families of autistic children face immense hurdles proving eligibility for Higher Rate Mobility. We feel DWP decisions heavily favour physical disabilities, ignoring that an autistic child in distress or experiencing sensory overload cannot process danger. Many bolt into traffic, refuse to walk, or have severe meltdowns. This can make journeys impossible without constant physical restraint. We call for a review to ensure DWP assesses "virtual inability to walk" with realism and a scientific understanding of autism.

records.title: Migrate UK civil service to open-source software for data sovereignty & security
records.description: I want the government to develop a plan to migrate all civil service IT systems from proprietary software to secure open-source alternatives. This should setting clear targets, budgets and training to ensure full data sovereignty, enhanced cybersecurity and support for UK innovation.
records.further_details: We believe foreign private companies cannot guarantee UK data sovereignty, with sensitive data regularly transferred outside the UK, risking breaches of the Data Protection Act and exposure to foreign laws like the US Cloud Act. We believe relying on proprietary software undermines national security, creates vendor lock-in, and stifles innovation. Open-source solutions offer transparency, stronger cybersecurity and the ability to keep data under UK jurisdiction. This could support domestic firms and make public services more resilient.

records.title: Exempt childminders with domestic premises from the new EYFS sleep rules
records.description: We urge the Government to exempt domestic childminding settings from the new EYFS sleep rules. We believe childminders should be allowed to use their own professional judgement on a safe place for children to sleep. We are home-from-home settings and often work alone in one room with limited space.
records.further_details: We believe a one size fits all approach ignores children’s individual sleep needs and can result in children being unable to sleep because they won’t settle – which is neither practical nor in children’s best interests. We believe childminders must be trusted to use professional judgement and provide a safe, suitable place for each child to sleep, including a pram, pushchair or sofa where appropriate.

records.title: Mandate Oliver McGowan training on learning disabilities & autism in education
records.description: Make Oliver McGowan Mandatory Training compulsory for all staff members in all education settings, ensuring staff are equipped to support autistic pupils and reduce trauma, misunderstanding and exclusion.
records.further_details: Thousands of DWP health care professionals completed the training and we believe education staff should be required to complete the same training. As a Tier 2 Co-Trainer, I have seen how lived-experience training transforms professionals. It could reduce trauma, improve inclusion and secure Oliver’s legacy.

records.title: Government to issue public solar and wind power forecasts
records.description: The Government should issue 3-day solar & wind power forecasts to help ease the energy crisis. We believe these will help the public maximize their domestic power instead of wasting it. By timing usage with these peaks, they can reduce the energy crisis's impact & lower national costs for everyone.
records.further_details: We believe maximizing our homegrown energy infrastructure that already exists is the fastest way to ease the energy crisis. Currently, the public has no clear way to know when our wind and solar are at their peak and so is frequently wasting energy. A public 3-day forecast would we believe allow us to align our demand when generation is highest, empower households to lower their costs, reduce reliance on expensive imports, and ensure that we make the most of every energy unit available.

records.title: Resentence IPP prisoners; end indefinite licence and limit recall
records.description: We call on the Government to make arrangements for a resentencing all on IPP sentences, to fixed-term sentences with clear release dates. It must end indefinite licence periods for all, and reform the threshold for recall so only those who have reoffended or who present a serious risk are recalled.
records.further_details: IPP was abolished in 2012, yet many remain imprisoned years beyond tariff with no release date. As an ex prison officer, I have seen this harm first hand. The European Court of Human Rights found aspects unlawful. Indefinite detention, lifelong licence and repeated recall without new offending or serious risk posed can cause severe psychological harm, destroy stability, and create a continuing injustice for individuals and families.

records.title: Fund the addition of Krabbe disease in the newborn blood spot programme
records.description: We ask the UK Government to assess Krabbe disease for inclusion in the NHS newborn blood spot screening programme, so babies at risk can be identified before symptoms develop and families can access early treatment and specialist care where appropriate.
records.further_details: Krabbe disease is a rare inherited neurological disorder that can cause devastating illness in babies who may initially appear healthy. We believe there is an urgent need for earlier diagnosis. We believe Krabbe disease should be formally assessed for inclusion in newborn blood spot screening, so the UK can determine whether babies could benefit from earlier identification and treatment.

records.title: Fund access for all women to a genetic blood test for breast cancer risk genes
records.description: Fund a national NHS screening programme offering all women the opportunity to be tested for BRCA1 and BRCA2 gene mutations. This could be offered alongside routine cervical screening appointments, such as at a woman’s first smear test or at her next scheduled appointment.
records.further_details: At present, testing is often only offered when someone meets certain criteria. My sister was diagnosed with breast cancer in November 2025 and was only offered genetic testing because of her age. We feel that this highlights how limited access to testing can be. Why should women have to wait until illness to be offered the chance to know their risk? A national programme could move us towards prevention rather than relying mainly on treatment after diagnosis.

records.title: Mandate hip scan offer for newborns with a family history of hip problems (DDH)
records.description: Require the NHS to automatically offer a hip ultrasound scan for all newborn babies if there is a known family history of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) or related hip conditions on either parent’s side.
records.further_details: DDH is a condition that can be present at birth but may not always be detected through physical examination alone. Early diagnosis is critical, as treatment in infancy is far simpler, less invasive, and more successful than treatment later in childhood. Currently, not all babies with a family history of hip problems are consistently referred for early ultrasound screening. This can lead to delayed diagnosis, resulting in avoidable pain, complex surgeries, and long-term mobility issues.

records.title: Mandate specialist input for neurological NHS continuing care assessment panels
records.description: Mandate clinical specialists such as neurologists on assessment panels for complex neurological conditions. We believe many with complex neurological conditions (Posterior cortical atrophy, Parkinson's, MND, atypical dementias) can face systemic refusal of NHS Continuing Healthcare (CHC) funding.
records.further_details: We are concerned that integrated Care Boards (ICBs) can reclassify severe visual, spatial, behavioural and cognitive needs as "social care," shifting 24/7 care costs onto families. We believe generic panels lack neurological expertise, undervaluing complex symptoms. We feel that ICBs routinely breach the Coughlan precedent by stripping funding once skilled care stabilises patients.

records.title: Abolish seasonal clock changes & keep the UK on a fixed time all year-round
records.description: Pass a law to end the practice of seasonal clock changes and commit to a stable, consistent time that does not changes with the seasons. The Government should adopt a permanent, fixed time year-round, either GMT or BST, and scrap the twice-yearly seasonal clock change.
records.further_details: We believe the clock change causes real harm to public health. Research links the spring transition to increased rates of heart attacks, strokes, and sleep disruption. The original justification for Daylight Saving Time was to reduce energy consumption for industrial purposes, which we feel is no longer relevant to modern life. We believe flexible working, modern lighting, and 24-hour industry have made it obsolete. Many countries have already abolished the clock change. We feel it is time the UK did the same.

records.title: Require all police forces to review serious cold cases within 5–10 years
records.description:
Require all police forces in England and Wales to review serious cold cases within 5–10 years. This should be called 'Stacey’s Law’.

End the postcode lottery, protect vital evidence, give families a fair, timely chance at justice.
records.further_details:
Support ‘Stacey’s Law’ so no victim is forgotten and no other family waits 33 years for justice

Families can wait decades for justice while evidence degrades and witnesses are lost. With no national rule, we’re concerned that reviews depend on funding and location, creating a postcode lottery.
Police and Crime Commissioners who currently decide will soon leave post due to government changes, we believe now is the time to act.
‘Stacey’s Law’ would ensure timely, fair reviews and protect every victim’s chance of justice.”
