records.title: Require businesses to offer interviews to care leavers meeting minimum criteria
records.description: We ask Government to introduce a national policy so medium and large employers offer care leavers a guaranteed interview for any role where they meet the essential criteria, ensuring fair access to work and consistent opportunity.
records.further_details: Care leavers face significant barriers to employment, despite having the skills and motivation to work. A guaranteed interview would help level the playing field, reduce long‑term unemployment, and support better life outcomes. This small, practical step would create fairer access to work and long‑term savings for the public sector

records.title: Require bars, pubs and clubs to have CCTV covering all areas surrounding toilets
records.description: I believe it should be a legal requirement for CCTV to cover all areas of the venue. This includes stairwells/corridors leading up to toilet facilities to monitor the safety of customers. This could help prevent spiking and other forms of assault or support in the prosecution of the attacker.
records.further_details: In September 2025, I was spiked with a needle whilst coming down the stairs from the toilets. However, my case was dropped due to lack of CCTV along the stairwell it happened. I have been left with anxiety and feelings of injustice following this event and I want to make a change to support others. CCTV is so important in monitoring the safety of customers in an establishment and unfortunately, corridors and stairwells leading to toilets are hotspots for these sorts of attacks.

records.title: All schools to have staff to administer glucagon to pupils with Type 1 diabetes
records.description: Require all schools to have trained staff available to administer prescribed emergency glucagon to pupils with Type 1 diabetes experiencing severe hypoglycaemia.
records.further_details: Children with Type 1 diabetes can become unconscious within minutes if severe hypoglycaemia is not treated. Although many pupils have prescribed emergency glucagon in school, staff are not legally required to administer it. A child’s chance of receiving life-saving treatment should not depend on whether a member of staff is willing to help. Every school should have trained staff with a legal duty to administer prescribed emergency glucagon.

records.title: Establish welfare body to end horse deaths in racing now
records.description: Create an independent welfare-focused body empowered to implement measures that eliminate deaths of horses in racing immediately.
records.further_details: Every year, around 150-200 horses die on British race tracks from racing injuries, exhaustion, or whip use, as reported in welfare analyses. The British Horseracing Authority (BHA) regulates the industry but has not eliminated these preventable deaths. The Government should act on animal welfare grounds to create a new independent authority with powers to enforce strict safety measures that essentially remove fatal risks to horses and jockeys.

records.title: Hold a review into the effects of parental alienation on families
records.description: We are calling on the UK Government to launch a review into parental alienation, examining its scale, how courts and services respond, and the impact on children. The review must deliver clear reforms to protect parent-child relationships and ensure fair, evidence-based decisions.
records.further_details: The Government currently refers to parental alienation as a “concept”, but for many families it is a reality with serious consequences. Across the UK, some parents are being cut off from their children without justification, leading to emotional distress. In some tragic cases, this has contributed to parents taking their own lives. This is why a review is needed, to examine the evidence, understand the scale of harm, and ensure the system responds with accountability and reform.

records.title: Require criminal trial juries to provide reasons using a verdict questionnaire
records.description: Introduce legislation requiring criminal juries to complete a structured verdict questionnaire detailing the factual reasons for their decisions, learning from international models to ensure a transparent, appeal-resilient justice system.
records.further_details: English and Welsh juries deliver unreasoned verdicts, which can leave victims and defendants unable to see if the law was applied correctly. We think this lacks transparency and hinders fair appeals. Since 1995, Spain has successfully used a structured "verdict questionnaire" where juries answer specific factual questions to justify their decisions. We propose a system utilising legally vetted, standardised question templates and a judicial "pre-check" phase.

records.title: Introduce new guest safety and security standards for all hotels
records.description: We want the Government to introduce mandatory national hotel safety and security standards, considering women and vulnerable guests, with secure room access, emergency contact, safeguarding, and clear risk-assessment.
records.further_details: A locked hotel room should mean you are safe. But recent cases have raised serious questions about hotel security, especially for women travelling alone and vulnerable guests. Guidance and individual hotel policies are not enough. We need clear national standards for room access, emergency help, safeguarding, risk checks, and reporting and accountability when things go wrong.

records.title: Require coconut be labelled as an allergen on food packaging
records.description: Require coconut be labelled as a mandatory allergen on all food packaging. Any product containing coconut must clearly list it. Other countries, including the US and Canada, already require this. Clear labelling could protect children and adults at risk of life-threatening reactions and death.
records.further_details: Coconut allergy can be life-threatening. My child has severe reactions, including eye swelling, digestive issues and risk of anaphylaxis. In the UK, coconut isn’t mandatory to label, putting families at daily risk. Mandatory labelling could prevent serious allergic reactions, hospitalisations, and save lives, align the UK with safer international standards, and give families confidence their food is safe.

records.title: Maintain direct-to-schools PE & sports premium funding
records.description: We want the Government to maintain the current system of direct-to-schools PE & sports premium funding.
records.further_details: We believe the Government’s plans to end the direct-to-schools PE & sports premium’ will damage the wrap around provision schools provide for children and deprive them of expert and professionally run PE lessons in school. We want the Government to prioritise children and their time away from screens by protecting this valuable social opportunity, which the direct premium provides for them, at a time when it is needed most.

records.title: Conduct review of sudden alopecia cases, diagnosis and patient support
records.description: We call on the UK Government to review diagnosis of, and care for rapid-onset alopecia areata, including severe forms resulting in total hair loss.
records.further_details: We think this review should consider reported cases of rapid or severe alopecia in relation to immune system activation. It should also consider how to ensure better NHS pathways for patients experiencing severe or sudden autoimmune hair loss, including those who do not wish to use immunosuppressive treatments, and how to improve access to psychological & emotional support.

records.title: Ban food delivery account holders from substituting deliveries to other people
records.description: Close loopholes for food delivery platforms that allow delivery account holders to substitute and pass on their delivery job to another worker.
records.further_details:
We believe delivery drivers using rented or shared accounts put the public at serious risk. We are concerned by cases were delivery drivers using someone else’s account have committed crimes whilst making deliveries.
 
We feel customers have no reliable way of knowing who is actually delivering. We call on the Government to close substitution loopholes and require delivery platforms to take legal responsibility for the actions of anyone operating under their company.

records.title: Legal restrictions on heading in football training to protect players’ brains
records.description: Create clear, legal restrictions to limit repetitive heading in football training to protect children, young people & all players from repeated head impacts. Some data suggests more than 5m children & 10m adults in England play football. We're concerned that they're in danger.
records.further_details: Repetitive heading can cause brain disease including CTE (Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy) which affects memory, mental health & behaviour. It’s been found in teenage brains & has developed into adult dementia. We believe that’s why we need to introduce and clarify legal limits on repetitive heading in training & protect all players. The FA acknowledges the need for protection, phasing out heading for U11s, but limits in training at later ages remain only guidance. We want consistent legal limits so every player, no matter how young/old, is protected. We hold that prevention is the only cure. Think head safe: reduce heading in training

records.title: Fund NHS pathways & mandated training for Pelvic Congestion Syndrome (PCS)
records.description: We call on the Government to fund a clear NHS clinical pathway for PCS that bridges the gap between Gynaecology and Interventional Radiology. Funding should also support mandated training for healthcare staff, improved testing and timely referrals to meet the 18-week treatment standard.
records.further_details:
It is reported that PCS affects around 1.5 million women in the UK, causing chronic pelvic pain, yet it can fall through the cracks between medical specialities. We believe many patients face years of medical gaslighting and misdiagnosis. We demand:
• Integrated MDT pathways between Gynaecology and Interventional Radiology.
• Mandated training for GPs and Gynaecologists to recognise Pelvic Venous Disorders.
• Standardised access to Transvaginal Duplex Ultrasound.
• Dedicated funding to end the "postcode lottery" for treatment.

records.title: Review & reform the per pupil funding formula to support rural & coastal schools
records.description: Schools in coastal and rural areas often receive less funding because they have fewer pupils. They may be forced to become academies or even close because the funding formula doesn’t cover costs. Therefore, we ask the government to use a different funding method that allows them to function well.
records.further_details: Over 300 secondary schools have less than 500 pupils and are often in coastal and rural areas. The funding formula is designed for secondary schools that have at least a 600 capacity for 11-16 year olds. Therefore, they are at a huge disadvantage. These areas are often disadvantaged areas. All children deserve to attend a school that is properly funded. These schools are often forced to close meaning peer groups then get dispersed to other schools and travel times become unacceptable.

records.title: To legally ensure that allergen-friendly food is always available in airports
records.description:
Airports should have at least one facility which holds food that can safely
cater to people who have medical dietary requirements related to the 14 main allergens.Travelling can be long and exhausting,it’s worse when you have to worry about whether you can safely eat, meaning some can’t eat at all.
records.further_details: When you are in an airport, you will find that there are a variety of food options. However, having a food related medical condition often means you cannot consider any of these options. There are still risks with cross contamination which is still enough for someone to become incredibly ill. By ensuring there is one station which holds allergen friendly food, it ensures that more people are able to eat properly and aren’t left with the option to make themselves poorly, or to not eat at all.

records.title: Review the NHS breast screening age
records.description: Review NHS breast screening and ensure women with possible breast cancer symptoms, including those mistaken for menopause, receive timely investigation regardless of age.
records.further_details: Women under 50 can develop breast cancer, yet symptoms may be dismissed because of age or mistaken for menopause. Earlier diagnosis could save lives.

records.title: Deploy the Royal Navy to turn illegal small boats back to France
records.description: We believe no boats containing illegal migrants should be allowed to land on our shores, including illegal migrants rescued at sea. We want the UK Government to deploy Royal Navy vessels to turn back all small boats that are attempting to illegally cross the Channel into the UK back to France.

records.title: Ban horse racing in the UK and fund transition to lifelong horse welfare safely.
records.description: Pass legislation to prohibit horse racing in the UK, end the commercial use of horses for racing, and create a funded transition plan for horses bred for or leaving racing, including retraining, rehoming, sanctuary placement, retirement care, and enforceable welfare protections during the phase-out.
records.further_details: We believe horse racing causes avoidable suffering through overbreeding and wastage, early weaning, the racing and training of physically immature horses, restrictive husbandry, a high prevalence of gastric ulcer disease, and a well-recognised risk of serious and fatal musculoskeletal injury. We believe these harms conflict with modern animal welfare principles, including the Five Domains framework, which requires good nutrition, environment, health, behaviour and mental state in this industry.

records.title: Legalise and fund medical cannabis cafés for medical patients
records.description: Some medical cannabis patients may be isolated and fearful despite having legal prescriptions. We want the Government to legalise and fund safe, regulated cafés where patients can use their medication, access support, and feel part of a community without stigma.
records.further_details: Medical cannabis has been legal in the UK since 2018 under the Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2001, yet patients remain isolated and unsupported. We feel there are no safe, recognised spaces to use prescribed medication, which can create fear and stigma. Regulated cafés could reduce isolation, provide education and community, and ensure patients can access their treatment with dignity and support.

records.title: Fund Improved Access to NHS Orthodontics for Children with Airway Problems
records.description: We want the Government to fund improved access to NHS orthodontic assessments for children with airway or breathing problems, including sleep apnoea, who also have narrow jaws or a narrow palate. Where early treatment is clinically needed, it should be available through the NHS.
records.further_details: Children with significant breathing and sleep problems may need early dental assessment. Children with airway problems and narrow jaws or palates should have access to early NHS orthodontic assessment and treatment where clinically needed. We therefore call for improved access to NHS Orthodontics for Children with Airway Problems so that treatment can be provided earlier.

records.title: Mandate neurodiversity training for all school staff
records.description: Introduce mandatory training for all staff in schools, including teachers, to be more aware of neurodiverse children. We believe by doing so we can ensure neurodiverse children get their needs met, so they feel more accepted in school.

records.title: Require all Government Ministers to be Elected Members of Parliament
records.description: We call on the UK Government to change the law so that only people elected in a general election or by-election to the House of Commons may serve as government ministers. No person should be able to become a minister solely through appointment to the House of Lords.
records.further_details:
Ministers should be directly accountable to voters through election.
Government ministers exercise significant executive power and make decisions affecting the public. Those who hold ministerial office should therefore have a direct democratic mandate from the electorate rather than serving by virtue of appointment to the House of Lords

records.title: Legislate to ensure public inquiry recommendations lead to action
records.description: The Government must establish a statutory duty on public bodies covered in the findings or recommendations from public inquiries to report progress regularly on their implementation or set out reasons for such recommendations not being implemented, with other means suggested for remedying failings.
records.further_details: These reports should be public so that people affected by the subject of the inquiry can see demonstrable progress towards remedying the failings in question. There should also be a mechanism for implementation to be independently verified to ensure recommendations have been effectively carried out, and for reasons given for non-implementation to be transparent, independently scrutinised and assessed. This proposed law will be called the Matthew Leahy Law in memory of my son, Matthew Leahy, whose death inspired my campaign for greater accountability and lasting change.

records.title: Increase the VAT taxable turnover threshold to £150,000 for small businesses
records.description: We believe small businesses are struggling to grow with the current threshold and many businesses are worse off when registering for VAT as you need to make significantly more than the current £90,000 to see the benefits.
records.further_details: In our view, increasing the taxable turnover threshold to £150,000 would grow business with the chance to explore more avenues of their trade.

records.title: Require Enhanced DBS Checks & Transparency for All Councillors and Politicians
records.description: We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation requiring all elected councillors and politicians, at both local and national level, to undergo an Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check before taking office and at regular intervals throughout their term.
records.further_details:
Those elected to represent the public are entrusted with significant responsibility. They make decisions affecting children, vulnerable adults, public finances, education, social care, housing, policing and many other essential services.
People working in schools, healthcare, social care, emergency services and countless other professions are often required to undergo DBS checks because of the trust placed in them. The public should have confidence that those making decisions.

records.title: Reduce salary for MPs who miss over 30% of their votes
records.description: We call on Parliament to introduce financial sanctions in the form of proportional salary reductions for any who participates in fewer than 70% of Parliamentary divisions, with fair exemptions for the Speaker, illness, parental leave, and official duties.
records.further_details: MPs are elected to vote on our behalf. We call on Parliament to introduce proportional salary reductions for MPs missing more than 30% of Parliamentary divisions per session, with exemptions for the Speaker, illness, parental leave, and official duties. MPs are paid over £91,000 a year — we believe taxpayers deserve representatives who show up.

records.title: Review single sex spaces guidance requiring use on the basis of biological sex
records.description: Review and revoke approval of the statutory code of practice requiring single-sex spaces in England, Scotland, and Wales to be designated and used on the basis of biological sex.
records.further_details:
In August 2026, an official statutory code of practice from the Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) came into force and stated that single-sex spaces can legally restrict access based on a person’s biological sex rather than their gender identity. However, we believe this guidance could do more harm than good.
 
We are concerned that rates of hate crime may increase. Transgender and gender non-conforming individuals are already subjected to discrimination daily and we believe continued implementation of the guidance would only increase hostility to individuals.

records.title: No new capped safe and legal routes for refugees to come to the UK
records.description: We want the Government to abandon its plans for "capped safe and legal" routes for refugees to come to the UK, including the new sponsorship scheme announced by the Home Secretary on 26 June
records.further_details: As a country we believe we simply cannot support any more refugees /asylum seekers – we are unable to cope with those who are already arriving and cannot document or vet them correctly.

records.title: Government must immediately move to increase defence spending as promised
records.description: We believe the Government’s plan to increase national security expenditure to 5% and defence expenditure to 3.5% is a laudable aim. We do however believe there is far too little urgency about this planned increase.
records.further_details: With increasing instability in the world and doubts about NATO, we feel the Government should urgently prioritise defence spending above other commitments. An article in The Times on 14/04/26 highlighted this lack of urgency on the Government’s stated defence commitments. Defence spending during the Cold War was 4-7% of GDP. Preventing a problem is always less expensive than fixing it. Defence expenditure during WW1 and WW2 peaked at 47% and 80% of GDP respectively. By spending 5% or more of GDP now we may deter any aggressor and avoid the high financial and human cost of a hot war.

records.title: Exempt those involved in the killing of emergency workers from early release.
records.description: Any person involved, in any way, directly or indirectly, in the killing of an emergency worker should be exempt from early release from prison and should complete the sentence as passed by a court of law.
records.further_details: Persons who are sentenced to a term of imprisonment, by a Court of Law, for any part played in the killing of an on duty emergency worker should complete the whole sentence, as passed, and not be eligible for early release.

records.title: Legislate to allow additional vehicle lighting for Community First Responders
records.description: Legislate to allow volunteer ambulance community responders in trust approved & marked vehicles to use additional lighting ONLY to make progress to category 1 (highest priority) emergency calls. They are volunteers who support their local community by attending medical emergencies.
records.further_details: Currently even though we are able to drive in marked vehicles and use the NHS crest and logo's we are not able to utilize any form of additional lighting. We are not asking for blue lights and a siren, but the opportunity to make quicker progress to the most serious incidents such as cardiac arrest by better indicating to others on the road that it is an emergency. Seconds can mean the difference between life and death.

records.title: Require shops to sell knives in lockable cabinet/behind a counter and ban offers
records.description: At present there is "Sale of knives: voluntary agreement by retailers" 2016 (updated in 2024). Many do not follow this agreement so legislation needs to be brought in to force retailers to restrict access to knives to help stop them being stolen and also getting into the hands of children.
records.further_details:
We ask for legislation, which could be called Tracy’s Law, to require:
 
- All knives sold to be kept in a lockable cabinet or behind the counter
 
- Age restrictions to be clearly advertised
 
- Knife display/cabinets to be out of view of children
 
- Shops to report bulk buyers to authorities
 
- No special offers on knives
 
There are restrictions to buying knives online however the access to knives in shops is still too open. Knives have been stolen from shops or easily bought and used for the wrong reasons. This needs to stop.

records.title: Withdraw from the ECHR and replace with domestic human rights legislation
records.description: We believe withdrawing from the ECHR is necessary to ensure national security and protect British citizens from harm. The ECHR has repeatedly limited the government's flexibility to enforce robust immigration policies to deport illegal immigrants and criminal foreign nationals swiftly.
records.further_details:
In our view, the Government has no effective deterrent to stop illegal immigration. An additional 3,003 crossed the channel in the first 3 weeks of the Prime Minister’s time in office.
 
The UK should leave the ECHR and establish an independent framework of human rights that balances individual freedoms with public safety and national interests. The ECHR to be replaced and managed under an independent, domestic British Bill of Rights tailored to national values.

records.title: Remove permitted development rights for telegraph poles & require full planning
records.description: Remove permitted development rights for telegraph poles and require planning permission and resident consultation for all new installations.
records.further_details:
Telecommunications operators can currently install telegraph poles for fibre broadband without applying for planning permission under existing permitted development rights.

This means Local Planning Authorities do not have to consult residents and operators are not required to consider alternatives such as underground cabling. Many residents only discover new poles when they appear in their street.

records.title: enquiry into OPG Power of Attorney laws/rules & police responses to POA abuse
records.description: Commission an independent enquiry into the gap between OPG rules on the use and misuse of Power of Attorney and the inconsistent responses of police forces when POA‑related financial abuse is reported. Create clear national standards for investigating POA misuse.
records.further_details: OPG rules set clear safeguards for how attorneys must act, how revocation must be respected, and how concerns about misuse should be handled. Families across the UK report that police responses vary widely, with POA misuse often treated as a civil matter. This inconsistency leaves vulnerable adults at risk. National standards are needed

records.title: Ban betting on sports involving animals, including horses and dogs
records.description: We believe animals are not here for our entertainment and betting on them can lead to cases of abuse. They deserve better protection.
records.further_details: Both dogs and horses are used as products and not beings. We consider the exploitation of animals for betting to be immoral and unnecessary and could destroy the lives of innocent animals - let them live in peace.

records.title: Statutory mental health early intervention framework for children & young people
records.description: Introduce a statutory early intervention framework for children and young people to include: clear national thresholds for early intervention; mandatory multi-agency escalation pathways; and time-bound response requirements for assessment and support. These changes could be known as Mia's Law.
records.further_details:
We are concerned that current responses for child mental health and safeguarding often require children and young people to reach crisis point before receiving meaningful support. Services can be delayed, inconsistent, and fragmented between education, health, and local authority systems.
 
A statutory framework would aim to create a consistent national approach to early identification and response, ensuring that support is provided at the earliest point of need rather than at crisis stage.

records.title: Review CMS Payments To Ensure Fairness For Paying Parents and Children
records.description: Government should review the Child Maintenance Service (CMS) to ensure it is fair and sustainable for both parents while supporting children appropriately.  It should protect paying parents from financial hardship and take blended families and additional dependent children into account fairly.
records.further_details: We believe all children within a household deserve equal financial consideration. CMS payments should not increase solely based on income where this causes financial hardship, impacts housing and living costs, affects mental health, or limits a parent’s ability to support their household and maintain child contact. We are concerned that the current system often favours the receiving parent and does not fully consider the financial pressures faced by paying parents after separation, including housing, court costs, and supporting new or blended families.

records.title: Legalise small scale Cannabis cultivation for medical patients
records.description: Allow the cultivation of no more than three (3) Cannabis SP. plants for personal use if the patient has a Medical Cannabis prescription.
records.further_details:
I am writing to the members of Parliament in order to change the legislation surrounding Medical Cannabis.

Currently, patients with a Medical Cannabis (hereafter referred to as MC) prescription can only receive their medication through private clinics.

My proposal would be to allow patients, with a prescription, to cultivate and process Cannabis plants (C. sativa, indica, ruderalis) at home.

This medicine allows people to return to their normal lives, and prices can be prohibitively high.

records.title: Ban surface dressing as a method of road repair
records.description: In our view, our roads are in an appalling state of repair but we do not believe that the practice of Surface Dressing is the solution. We think it’s a dangerous solution for all road users, especially motorcyclists and cyclists. I call on the government to ban this method of road repair.
records.further_details: As a motorcyclist myself, I believe that Surface Dressing is not conducive to a safe method of passage for motorcyclists or cyclists, even at 20mph. In my experience roads which have been surface dressed are akin to sheet ice.

records.title: Rename Teaching Assistants to Assistant Teachers to fully reflect their roles
records.description: The government needs to change the perception of the contribution that Teaching Assistants actually provide to the education system, and better educate parents on the role they play.
records.further_details:
We think the simplest way to do this is rename them to Assistant Teachers to better reflect the role they play in class.

My partner often comes home feeling undervalued after a hard day's work at school, only to hear hurtful comments like, "you're just an assistant, you don't teach." This is not only misleading but sorely underestimates the vital role that teaching assistants play in the educational system. We feel we must change the perception of the pivotal role they play in our children's education.
 
A study has found that the presence of teaching assistants can improve pupil progress.

records.title: Significantly increase dedicated funding for endometriosis
records.description:
- Increase ring-fenced funding for endometriosis research through UK research bodies.
- Support the development of faster, non-invasive diagnostic methods.
- Invest in better treatment options and long-term care strategies.
- Improve education and training for healthcare professionals.
records.further_details:
Despite its prevalence, endometriosis remains significantly under-researched and poorly understood. On average, it takes around 7–10 years to receive a diagnosis in the UK. During this time, many individuals experience severe pain, fatigue, infertility, and a reduced quality of life, often impacting education, employment, and mental health.

Current treatment options are limited and there is no known cure. Many patients undergo repeated surgeries or rely on hormonal treatments which do not work.

records.title: Create a specific foster carer status within the Universal Credit system
records.description: We want the Government to create a specific foster carer status in the Universal Credit system which provides them with unique work requirements, housing entitlements and clear rules. We believe foster carers should not have to repeatedly prove caring responsibilities.
records.further_details:
Foster carers provide care to vulnerable children, yet we feel Universal Credit does not adequately recognise their role. Carers can be classed as unemployed, called to work-related appointments and repeatedly asked to prove their circumstances.
 
We believe the system also fails to reflect when both carers must be available full-time, or correctly account for foster and birth children and bedroom needs. We believe foster families need a clear, consistent process that recognises how fostering actually works.

records.title: Increase safeguarding & human oversight regulation of Artificial Intelligence
records.description: Increase AI regulation to ensure it supports rather than replaces human contribution. This should include ethical standards with AI developers, mandatory social impact assessments and more human oversight in care & education for transparency and to safeguard against harmful or manipulative AI use.
records.further_details: AI offers major benefits but, without safeguards, it could risk undermining jobs, creativity, dignity and meaningful human roles. Work and contribution support identity, community and wellbeing. Unregulated AI could also enable manipulation, exploitation and concentration of power. We believe Government action is needed to protect human creativity, care, empathy and social connection, ensure ethical use of AI, and guarantee technology strengthens society while preserving dignity and opportunity.

records.title: Review and fund more support for care leavers
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce a national suicide prevention and wellbeing standard, ensuring care leavers have continuous support through the transition to adulthood.
records.further_details:
A new review shows that young adults who have left care have a death rate around four times higher than the general population. Just over a third of the care leavers were thought to have died by suicide.
 
We want the Government to fund a national care leaver mental health and suicide-prevention programme, informed by the 2026 review and care leaver death rates. This should provide local support groups, a dedicated mental health worker alongside each care leaver’s PA, and access to specialist support. Care leavers need a clear, funded pathway to help. Government should also fund consistent national reporting of care-leaver deaths and suspected suicides.

records.title: Abolish the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
records.description: We call on the Government to abolish the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero since it, in our view, is palpably unfit for purpose and hugely costly for businesses and households across the country.
records.further_details: We believe that energy security and Net Zero are mutually opposed, and that the UK needs to exploit its existing energy supplies rather than, as we see it, hand billions of pounds to other countries such as China to supply economically inferior alternatives. We think that Net Zero is an unproven and unscientific objective.

records.title: Require online platforms to identify and remove monetised ‘rage bait’ content
records.description: This petition calls on the UK Government to introduce legislation requiring social media platforms to take effective action against creators who use rage bait or exploit controversy for profit. We believe stronger accountability is needed to help protect users.
records.further_details: We have witnessed harmful content across social media. Despite repeatedly reporting it through the appropriate channels, little or no meaningful action has been taken. We believe the UK Government should introduce stronger legislation to hold online creators and social media platforms accountable when harmful content is repeatedly used for profit. We believe creators who use rage bait to generate views, engagement, and financial gain encourage harassment and misinformation.

records.title: Enact a multi-millionaire wealth tax to fund research for ultra-rare diseases
records.description: Enact a wealth tax on multimillionaires and use the revenue to create a ring-fenced NHS and UKRI fund that would finance research, clinical trials and treatments for ultra-rare diseases.
records.further_details:
Many families of children with terminal conditions like Sanfilippo syndrome and BPAN have to fundraise millions themselves to finance research trials or foreign care. We believe a child’s survival shouldn’t depend on private fundraising.
 
The Government should create a ring-fenced fund administered by the NHS and UKRI to finance research and development, clinical trials and compassionate treatment access for ultra-rare diseases, which would be sustainably funded through a tax on UK-based individuals with net assets exceeding £10 million.

records.title: Fund the UK Youth Parliament beyond 2027
records.description: We ask the Government to secure and restore proper funding for the UK Youth Parliament beyond 2027, so it can continue from 2027 onwards and give young people across the UK a meaningful voice in democracy. All we ask is for funding so the UK Youth Parliament can continue for future years to come!

records.title: Relax EU meat and dairy personal import rules for travellers
records.description: We ask for a review of the current blanket ban on personal imports of meat and dairy from the EU, to allow products that we think are low risk such as sealed, pasteurised or fully cooked items.
records.further_details: Current rules treat all meat and dairy products the same, regardless of processing or packaging. However, we think that products such as pasteurised dairy, cooked meat and industrially sealed goods carry very low risk. In our opinion, this would not be a reduction in biosecurity protections, but would make them proportionate and evidence-based, in line with modern food safety standards and existing commercial trade controls.

records.title: Fund specialised regional task forces to tackle bike & motorcycle theft
records.description: We believe motorcycle owners across the country are targeted and endangered everyday by organised gangs of thieves. We call on the Government to fund dedicated regional task forces to manage a coordinated approach in tackling bike & motorcycle thieves and keeping all road users safe.
records.further_details: We feel there needs to be a coordinated approach to tackling thefts and bike jackings. Thieves can not only cost bikers millions in damage and loss every year; they can also put them at risk of injury and death. Despite convictions of bike and motorcycle thieves, thefts and bike jackings continue on a daily basis. We call on the Government to fund the establishment of specialised and dedicated regional task forces to tackle this.

records.title: Require NHS patients to have the right to human contact instead of AI at triage
records.description: Patients contacting NHS primary care must always have the option to speak to a person, and AI must not be the sole mechanism for assessing symptoms or urgency or deciding whether a patient can access care. The government must urgently review the deployment of AI systems in NHS call handling.
records.further_details:
Some patients have been required to speak to an AI call-handling service when contacting their GP surgery. We think AI systems can ask unnecessary questions and make incorrect suggestions. We are concerned that this can make it hard to access the right support, and that medication and treatment could be delayed.
 
AI has the potential to support our NHS, but it cannot become a barrier between patients & the healthcare they need. Patients must retain the right to speak to a human.

records.title: Introduce a higher, sector-specific Minimum Wage for PCAs and veterinary nurses
records.description: Require veterinary employers to increase wages to £14 per hour for patient care assistants and £15.50 for vet nurses/vet techs. We feel the industry is extremely taxing on mental and physical health and has extremely high standards set in place.
records.further_details: This should not be considered a minimum wage job especially in the medical field. We are concerned that most of these individuals live pay cheque to pay cheque and are barely be able to make rent, while enduring harsh work environments under an immense amount of stress and pressure.

records.title: Fund "Universal" Breakfast Clubs to include all SEND Children
records.description: While the Equality Act 2010 requires 'reasonable adjustments’ in our view the current funding model for breakfast clubs makes 1-1 support for children who need it financially impossible for schools. We are calling for the government to provide SEND funding for this.
records.further_details: Provide ring-fenced funding to ensure that all children with SEND can safely access the new national breakfast clubs. The current £1-per-child model fails to cover the 1-1 support some require for safety and communication. While the government promotes these clubs to help parents return to work, we think many SEND parents are being excluded because "universal" provision is currently inaccessible for our children. No child should be turned away because of their disability.

records.title: Reform prisoner recalls and require independent review of repeated recalls
records.description: Require an independent review before someone is repeatedly recalled to prison for licence breaches, particularly where there has been no new offence.
records.further_details: People released from prison on licence can be recalled for breaching licence conditions. We believe repeated recalls need stronger safeguards, particularly where there is no new offence. We are not asking for public protection to be weakened. We want independent review of repeated recalls to ensure they are necessary and proportionate, while considering support and community measures that could safely prevent repeated imprisonment and support rehabilitation.

records.title: Launch a public inquiry into the failures of HS2
records.description: Launch a public inquiry with statutory responsibility to hold to account anyone responsible for the costs on UK taxpayers due to HS2. The inquiry should look at ways to hold accountable those responsible for what we believe has been one of the greatest failures in public spending.
records.further_details:
We believe politicians and officials responsible must be held accountable for failures relating to HS2. The original cost was around £30 billion; HS2 is now expected to cost over £100 billion with possible delays and worse service. 
 
We believe UK citizens have the right to demand that those responsible for these failures are held accountable. The inquiry should look into putting a provision in place so that decision-making mechanisms in future projects ensure accountability from the outset.

records.title: Fund barriers and cameras to make bridges and motorways safer
records.description: Sadly, there are around 50 suicides per year on roads in the UK. We feel that there should be more funding put towards making bridges and motorways safer, to prevent people losing a family member/friend.
records.further_details: The Government should fund higher barriers on bridges & cameras on access points that might alert emergency services when they see someone on a motorway bridge. Such bridges might have pedestrian gating access ways with a code that only emergency services have. Every day thousands of people experience a crisis so I believe that extra funding may help people a bit more. My family and I lost my sister to suicide and we don't want others to feel the grief we do.

records.title: Require & fund healthcare services prior to building housing developments
records.description: We believe combined cumulative impacts of housing developments on healthcare services are not being adequately assessed despite requirements under the NPPF. We believe infrastructure improvements must precede new housing developments, and developers should be mandated to pay.
records.further_details: Many GP surgeries are unable to expand their premises to meet demand, whilst new housing is being developed without always allocating space for additional facilities. This needs to be mandated.

records.title: Grant home fee status to UK & EU nationals who live in the EU
records.description: The Government should grant British citizens living in the EU and EU nationals the right to qualify for home fee status at English universities, even if they have not spent the 3 years before the start of their university term living in the UK.
records.further_details: From 1st January 2028, UK citizens living in EU will no longer qualify for home fee status.

records.title: Review transparency and standardised labelling for pet food
records.description: Review transparency of pet food labelling rules so consumers can make informed choices. Manufacturers should disclose individual ingredients, the proportion and origin of key ingredients, standardised nutritional information, and notify customers when recipes materially change.
records.further_details:
We ask the Government to strengthen pet food labelling by requiring manufacturers to disclose individual ingredients, their proportions and origins, standard nutrition and processing information, and notification of recipe changes.
 
Labels should list ingredients by weight, state main ingredient percentages and origins, and use consistent standards for nutritional, health and processing claims. Government should also review an independent nutritional assessment framework for complete pet foods.

records.title: Seek to negotiate a UK-EU youth mobility deal for under-30s
records.description: We call the government to seek to negotiate a reciprocal youth mobility scheme with the EU, letting UK and EU citizens aged 18-30 study and work freely across borders without the current visa and work permit bureaucracy.
records.further_details: Since Brexit, it has become far harder for young people to study or work across the UK-EU border. Many who were too young to vote in 2016 are now stuck living with the consequences. Several EU member states and the European Commission have already floated youth mobility schemes. We think a reciprocal deal for under 30s could restore that lost opportunity, without reopening the question of free movement itself. In our view, this generation deserves a government that acts to address its consequences.

records.title: Legalise and regulate e-scooters & e-bikes exceeding current limits for road use
records.description: Introduce a regulated framework allowing privately owned e-scooters and higher-speed e-bikes on roads, with a two-tier system: low-speed devices with basic registration, and higher-speed devices requiring a simple licence, ID and annual fee, with clear safety and enforcement rules.
records.further_details: Rising fuel costs and the cost-of-living crisis limit access to transport, especially for low-income households. Legalisation would provide a low-cost alternative, reduce fuel dependency, and support the electric transport market. A clear, tiered system with registration and licensing could reduce police time spent enforcing current restrictions and improve compliance. It would support jobs, make use of existing infrastructure, and provide a fair, affordable alternative to car ownership.

records.title: Cancel the British Council’s Covid Debt Now
records.description: The British Council, seen as a cornerstone of UK global influence, is reported to be under threat from an unsustainable Covid-era debt which is driving cuts, instability, and loss of assets. We call on the UK Government to cancel this debt and protect its future.
records.further_details: The British Council supports education through teaching and exams, cultural exchange, and UK partnerships in over 100 countries. We believe a  £197m Covid-era government loan is forcing cuts, job insecurity, the closing of some country operations and the sale of key assets. Covid was an extraordinary crisis, not mismanagement. We feel that cancelling the debt would protect jobs, safeguard vital services, and preserve a key UK global asset in an uncertain world.

records.title: National scheme for QR code driver identification for all Hackney Carriage cabs
records.description: Introduce a mandatory national QR code identification system displayed in the rear passenger area of all Hackney Carriages. When scanned, this QR code could include the driver’s full name, photograph, badge/licence number, the vehicle registration and current licensing status.
records.further_details:
A mandatory QR code system could:
- Allow discreet verification of driver identity  
- Improve passenger safety and confidence  
- Support rapid reporting of inappropriate behaviour  
- Increase accountability and professionalism  
- Help prevent misconduct and impersonation  
- Support safeguarding obligations
The purpose of this petition is to allow lone people to feel safe when travelling in these Hackney Carriages (Black Cabs). There have been reports of misconduct, especially with young women.

records.title: Fund childcare for working parents immediately after maternity leave ends
records.description: We want the Government to change the Funded Childcare for Working Parents scheme in England so eligible parents can access their childcare hours immediately after maternity, paternity, adoption or shared parental leave ends, rather than waiting until the next school term.
records.further_details:
Eligible working parents can receive up to 30 hours of funded childcare per week for children aged from 9 months old, but support only starts from the next school term. 
 
This means parents returning to work after a cut-off pay full nursery fees for months despite already being eligible. A parent returning in May will not receive funded childcare until September.
 
Parents do not plan maternity leave around school terms. HMRC should be able to process support from the date parental leave ends

records.title: Create a SEND access fund within the Every Child Can enrichment programme
records.description: We call on the Government to create a dedicated SEND access support fund within Every Child Can & related enrichment programmes. This fund should be available to eligible community organisations & children’s activity providers when a child with SEND needs additional adult support to participate.
records.further_details:
This petition is about funding the 1:1/1:2 additional adult support and reasonable adjustments many SEND children need to access activities they love all year-round (not just in holidays).
If a child needs 1:1 support Activity Providers are often faced with a hard choice:
They absorb costs,
Ask parents to stay,
Or turn a child away.
We believe that Every Child Can should mean every child actually can.

records.title: Require disabled toilets on all commercial flights
records.description: We believe that having a disabled toilets on commercial flights would massively benefit many people.
records.further_details: This is a problem for many people and can put them off travelling. Why should disabled people not be able to travel for something so simple? They shouldn’t be singled out and should be able to access the same facilities as others. This is a huge thing for me and my family as we are big travellers and have family living abroad.

records.title: Create a legal right for families to request copies of CCTV of homicide victims
records.description: We want to create a statutory right for families of homicide victims to obtain physical/digital copies of CCTV footage featuring their deceased loved one. This should be known as James’s Law,  so Police aren’t stopped from providing copies to families by citing third-party ownership/data protection.
records.further_details: Families of homicide victims are sometimes permitted to view CCTV of their loved ones, but police can refuse to provide copies for families to keep, claiming the footage belongs to a third party. Our strong view it that viewing footage in a controlled police room is not enough. Families can feel trapped by red tape and denied the right to retain these final records. We demand a legal framework compelling police to provide families with copies of this CCTV, bypassing third-party ownership and copyright reasons.

records.title: Review maternity guidance for women pregnant after a previous stillbirth
records.description: Review maternity guidance for women with a previous stillbirth who attend hospital with reduced fetal movements, to ensure their previous loss is recognised and they receive appropriate assessment, personalised care and support in subsequent pregnancies.
records.further_details: Women who have experienced a previous stillbirth face unique medical and emotional challenges in future pregnancies. I am asking the Government to review maternity guidance so women with a previous stillbirth who present with reduced fetal movements receive care that recognises their history, provides appropriate assessment, and supports personalised decision-making. The aim is to improve care and outcomes for future families.

records.title: Make public EV charging subject to the same VAT rate as home charging
records.description: We want the Government to reduce VAT on public electric vehicle (EV) charging from 20% to the same rate applied to home charging. EV drivers who cannot charge at home should not be penalised through higher costs simply because of their housing circumstances.
records.further_details: This petition is about creating a fairer VAT system for electric vehicle charging. Currently, electricity used for public EV charging is subject to 20% VAT, while those able to charge at home benefit from a lower rate and, from October 2026, VAT-free charging. Many drivers cannot install home chargers due to their housing situation and have no choice but to use public chargers. EV drivers should be treated equally regardless of where they charge.

records.title: Make it a legal requirement to report cat collisions and cover vet fees
records.description: I propose that the government enforce a new law that requires all drivers involved in a cat collision to report it to the police and also be legally required to cover all veterinary expenses caused by the collision. Cats are loved pets too. Cats’ lives matter just as much as any other animals.
records.further_details: On 07/08/26 my beloved cat Tiger was involved in a cat collision. A collision where the driver did not stop, report nor seek help for her. Thankfully Tiger was helped by locals but sadly the injuries she sustained were so severe the kindest thing we could do for her was to end her pain. It is unfair that it currently is not a legal requirement to report a cat collision but it is a dog. Cats are equally loved pets and deserve the same law. Drivers should be held responsible for their actions.

records.title: Require employers to give annual leave equal to at least 20-25% of hours worked
records.description: We are calling for an increase in minimum level of annual leave, to be calculated as 20-25% of total hours worked, not a fixed allocation of days. This could also help people to take mental health days and encourage healthier workloads. Burnout, stress, and poor recovery are rising
records.further_details:
Please support policy change to help protect wellbeing, retention, and public health.
 
Across workplaces professionals are witnessing the psychological impact of insufficient rest. Rising burnout, stress, anxiety, and depression demand urgent action. We call for increased annual leave, protected mental health days, and healthier workloads across the NHS, public, and private sectors to improve wellbeing, reduce burnout, and create a sustainable workforce.
 
Act to:
1. Increase UK annual leave
2 Add mental health days
3. Reduce stigma
4. Align workloads with capacity.

records.title: Make controlled burning mandatory for landowners
records.description: We want the UK Government to make prescribed burning mandatory for Landowners in order to mitigate the impact of Wildfires on Moorland, Heathland and in Woodland.
records.further_details: In our view, by intentionally burning away accumulated dead brush, leaves, and small trees (known as ‘fuel loads’), the risk of catastrophic, uncontrolled wildfires is significantly reduced. It can also create firebreaks that can slow the spread of accidental fires. Many ecosystems are naturally fire-dependent. We believe that by clearing out choking undergrowth, fire encourages the growth of native plants and wildflowers, and that burning dead vegetation quickly returns nutrients to the soil.

records.title: Convene relevant parties to seek agreement on international regulation of AI
records.description: We believe there has been too much talk about regulation of AI and not enough action. The Government should host a meeting of fellow Governmental officials, relevant NGOs and Senior Executives from the top AI labs to discuss and propose a set of international AI regulation principles.
records.further_details: I am an avid supporter and user of AI. I can see the benefits it is already delivering, and the potential it has. But I am also hugely concerned that something that has the power to irrevocably change (and potentially threaten) human existence currently has little to no regulation. There are a growing number of reports of AI hacking into systems without authorisation or trying to trick humans with malicious code.

records.title: Introduce a Publicly Accessible Sex Offenders Register
records.description: Introduce a public Sex Offenders Register. We believe "Sarah’s Law" is too reactive, and that communities deserve a proactive "right to know". In our view, transparency must outrank offender privacy and we demand an official, searchable database to empower parents and enhance safety.
records.further_details: We urge the Government to legislate for a publicly accessible Sex Offenders Register as I believe the current "Sarah’s Law" is reactive and insufficient; it requires parents to suspect a threat before acting. We believe that we need a proactive, searchable database that grants communities a "right to know" who lives among them, and that public safety and child protection must take priority over the privacy of convicted offenders. We think such a register could empower our neighbourhoods with transparency to prevent harm and enhance local safeguarding.

records.title: Government must abolish Ofsted
records.description: I want the Government to abolish Ofsted.  I believe the existence of Ofsted is the single most limiting factor in progressing education within this nation. Removing what I believe is its toxic influence would allow schools to thrive.
records.further_details: I have been in education since 1997; a class teacher, local authority education consultant, assistant head, deputy headteacher & headteacher. I can safely say the most disruptive & toxic part of working in education has always been the over-influence of Ofsted. I believe removing this organisation will demonstrate to the sector how the current Government wishes a more inclusive educational mainstream sector and will show who is actually in charge of education.

records.title: Government must regulate veterinary business practices
records.description: The UK has no statutory regulation for vet practices. The Vet Surgeons Act 1966 regulates individual vet surgeons but does not regulate the businesses they work for. Most practices are owned by large corporate groups. Pet owners often face rising fees, reduced out of hours care, and up-front costs.
records.further_details: With most practices now owned by large corporate groups, pet owners face rapidly rising fees, reduced access to local out-of-hours care and significant upfront costs. We call on the Government to proceed with plans to introduce regulation of veterinary businesses, ensuring it includes pricing, standards and access to emergency care.

records.title: Mandate collection & publication of criminals’ immigration status & nationality
records.description: We call on the Government to mandate the collection and publication of all crime statistics broken down by immigration status and nationality for the past 5 years, including data on illegal immigrants and asylum seekers, in the interest of transparency and public accountability.
records.further_details: We call for full transparency: the mandatory collection and publication of all crime statistics broken down by nationality and immigration status including asylum seekers and illegal immigrants for the past five years, so the public can hold all political institutions, politicians, and external organisations to account.

records.title: Seek to work with the EU to develop European alternatives to key US products
records.description: Seek to cooperate with the EU to examine areas where we rely upon American products and services and work to remove those dependencies.
records.further_details:
We believe it would be hugely negligent to not be looking into this and the government should immediately open talks with the EU about this as a matter of urgent national security.
 
We should move critical payment and software systems to European companies. Areas such as cloud computing, semiconductors, vaccines, LNG, armaments, soya beans and more need either European production or alternative suppliers.

records.title: End the tax threshold freeze to stop potentially pushing families into poverty
records.description:
1. Legislate that, from April 2031, all income tax thresholds will rise automatically each year in line with CPI inflation or average wages (whichever is higher).
 
2. Apply a one-off sharp upward correction in 2031 to restore the real value lost over the decade — not a token increase.
records.further_details:
The Government has frozen core income tax thresholds (personal allowance £12,570, higher rate £50,270) at 2021/22 levels until April 2031. Nearly a decade of unprecedented fiscal drag.
 
This stealth tax erodes the real value of allowances and will pull millions more people into poverty by 2031, even if wages rise with inflation. If thresholds had been indexed to inflation, the personal allowance would be around £4,920 higher and the higher rate threshold £20,120 higher.

records.title: Extend legal regulation of the teaching profession to teaching assistants
records.description: Extend Teaching Regulation Agency powers to Teaching Assistants so they are subject to the same professional misconduct regulations as qualified teachers, allowing the Teaching Regulation Authority (TRA) to investigate serious safeguarding concerns involving all teaching assistants.

records.title: Require convicted domestic abuse offenders to be placed on a national register
records.description: Create a national register for people convicted of domestic abuse offences, with appropriate safeguards, to help protect future partners and improve public safety. Domestic abuse often involves repeat offending.
records.further_details:
We believe a register could support risk management, improve information sharing, and help prevent further abuse.

As someone who has experienced domestic abuse in both my childhood and adulthood, and who knows many other women who have experienced it too, I feel strongly that there should be a register to help protect potential future partners from repeat offenders. I believe greater transparency and appropriate information sharing could help prevent further abuse and improve public safety.

records.title: Making Veteran Status a Protected Characteristic
records.description: Make veteran status a protected characteristic under UK equality law. Veterans should be protected from discrimination in employment, housing, healthcare and public services because of their veteran status. Recognise and protect those who served.
records.further_details: Veterans have made a significant commitment to our country, yet some face disadvantage or discrimination after leaving the Armed Forces. Veteran status is not currently a protected characteristic under the Equality Act 2010. This petition calls on the Government to recognise veteran status in law, protecting veterans from discrimination in employment, housing, healthcare and public services. This is not about preferential treatment, but fairness and recognition.

records.title: End mandatory online age verification & mandate parental controls instead
records.description: We call on the Government to stop mandating age verification for online content and instead require software companies to provide a fully functional, free and simple to use parental control system so parents can control what their kids can access if they wish.
records.further_details: We believe education should also be provided to parents who are unsure what to do rather than forcing everyone to age verify. We feel that an even better option would be one tool that supports all operating systems, phones, laptops, games consoles, etc, that is free to use so parents have full control to safeguard their own children as their duty as parents to do so. We believe it should be an opt-in system.

records.title: Polluter levy on companies whose products make up most litter
records.description: Introduce an annual independent nationwide litter audit to identify the brands and products most commonly found littering the UK’s streets, parks, countryside and waterways and introduce a polluter levy on the 100 companies whose branded products are found most frequently.
records.further_details:
The audit should be commissioned by DEFRA using standardised counting methods with local authorities and environmental organisations. It should include packaging, cigarette butts, disposable vapes and other branded disposable waste.
The Government should introduce a polluter levy on the 100 companies whose branded products are found most frequently. Funds raised should be ringfenced for street cleaning, litter enforcement, recycling infrastructure and community environmental projects.

records.title: Require news organisations to give equal coverage for inaccurate reporting
records.description: We want the Government to legislate to require news organisations to give equal coverage to correcting materially inaccurate reporting to the original publication or broadcast on their media platform.
records.further_details:
Corrections to inaccurate reporting should be presented in a way that gives viewers an equal opportunity to see or hear it. We believe truth in news is vital to a healthy democracy. Inaccurate reporting can reach millions, while corrections may receive far less prominence.
 
Press freedom should be protected, but we feel that with freedom should come accountability for factual accuracy.
 
When reporting is found to be materially inaccurate, its correction should be reported and presented to viewers in the same way. Requiring equal coverage for corrections could improve accountability while protecting the freedom of expression.

records.title: Amend the Pet Abduction Act 2024 to remove exemptions for having lived together
records.description: We want the government to amend Sections 1 and 2 of the Pet Abduction Act 2024 to remove the exemptions from committing an offence which rest on the fact of having lived together
records.further_details: We want subsections 1(2) and 2(2) removed so that even if people lived together in the same household the offence of pet abduction is still committed if taken by one of those people. At present if the above happens it is a civil matter not criminal. Not everybody has money for civil action & it can be a lengthy process. We believe abusive partners/family are using this to their advantage.

records.title: Ban the use of carbon dioxide gas to slaughter pigs
records.description: Set a firm deadline to ban high-concentration CO₂ gas stunning of pigs in England. The Government has already committed to consult on a ban. We want legislation and a clear, short timetable to replace CO₂ with higher-welfare stunning methods.
records.further_details: Most UK pigs are stunned using high concentrations of carbon dioxide (CO₂). This method can cause pain, fear and respiratory distress before pigs lose consciousness. The Government and industry are already considering alternative stunning methods. We believe this work should be accelerated, with a clear timetable to phase out high-concentration CO₂ stunning and replace it with more humane alternatives.

records.title: Review the use of digital technology in schools
records.description: Following the example of Sweden, we want the UK Government to review how digital technology is used in UK schools and restore a better balance between screens and traditional learning, include more use of printed books, handwritten work, and focused reading time, especially in early education.
records.further_details:
Many parents and teachers are concerned that too much screen use could be affecting children’s focus, reading ability, and depth of understanding, as well as health.
Research has found that reading printed books and writing by hand supports better learning and memory than screen-based work. There is limited evidence that increasing classroom technology improves overall scores.

records.title: Make lying or spreading disinformation in public office a criminal offence
records.description: We want the Government to make it a criminal offence if a person or persons in public office has/have knowingly lied and/or spread disinformation and/or suppressed factual information.
records.further_details: We believe this new criminal offence is required in order to restore ethical standards and integrity given the widespread lying we feel is especially evident in politics, and other public office sectors. Without accountability for such damaging behaviours, prospects seem bleak for democracy, effective government and public trust in national and local government and other public sector actions. We fear that without robust legal accountability, damaging non-adherence to ethical standards will continue to be normalized behaviour in this country.

records.title: Require the use of renewable energy only to power the national grid
records.description: Require the sole use of renewable energy sources to power the national electricity grid so that 100% of electricity generated in the national grid is from renewable energy sources.
records.further_details: We could dramatically change our country by ensuring that the electricity coming into our homes, workplaces, and everywhere else in our country only comes from renewable energy, rather than a mix that includes fossil fuels. This change could significantly impact climate change in the UK as by not using fossil fuels to generate electricity, we could significantly reduce carbon emissions and slow down climate change, which we believe is absolutely vital.

records.title: Review communication of diagnostic results in cases of suspected cancer
records.description: Review the communication of diagnostic test results that indicate suspected cancer, and ensure NHS providers are making urgent suspected cancer referrals where national referral criteria are met.
records.further_details: This petition is inspired by my own experience after being diagnosed with stage 4 ovarian cancer. I believe patients should be informed promptly when tests suggest cancer and receive urgent referrals where national guidance indicates this is appropriate. We call for NHS providers to urgently review the communication of suspected cancer results to help reduce avoidable delays and improve patient safety.

records.title: Raise the age of consent to 18 with peer exception for 16-17 year olds
records.description: Set the legal age of consent at 18. Allow a “close-in-age” or “peer” exception: 16–17 year olds can consent only with other 16–17 year olds. Make it illegal for any adult (18+) to engage in sexual activity with someone under 18, unless they had an existing sexual relationship from age 16/17.
records.further_details: This proposal is about safeguarding, not restriction. Teenagers form peer relationships, but there is a clear difference between these and those involving adults. We believe that raising the age of consent to 18, with a close-in-age/peer exception, would better protect young people from exploitation while respecting development. We believe that at 16 individuals are still maturing and should not be considered able to consent to sex with adults, not only those in positions of trust.

records.title: Fund wildlife vet care and give rehabilitators access to medicines.
records.description: We want the Government to amend the Veterinary Medicines Regulations to allow qualified wildlife rehabilitators regulated access to essential medicines, and to work with the RCVS to establish a funded framework requiring vets to cooperate with recognized rescues on long-term treatment.
records.further_details: Vets only have to give emergency aid to wildlife, absorbing costs themselves. Due to this and rigid prescription laws, treatable wild animals are often euthanised, even when qualified wildlife rehabilitators are willing to do the care. Strict laws also stop carers accessing basic medications without a vet physically seeing every animal, causing fatal delays. We need government-funded wildlife vet reimbursement, a medication safe-list for carers, and updated RCVS guidance.

records.title: Allow for shorter visa extensions & HIS refunds for migrants nearing ILR
records.description: We want the Government to allow migrants and dependents who are close to qualifying for Indefinite Leave to Remain to be able to apply for shorter visa extensions and receive a refund of Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) payments that is proportionate to their time left before receiving ILR.
records.further_details: Many people must pay for more years of IHS even when they may only need a short period before becoming eligible for settlement, which can create an unnecessary financial burden on individuals and families. We believe it’s not fair and there is no explanation about it.

records.title: Ban greyhound racing in England
records.description: We believe greyhounds deserve protection, not exploitation for profit. Greyhound racing causes injuries and deaths to dogs every year. Wales has committed to banning the sport and Scotland is ending it.
records.further_details:
We believe England should follow their lead and put animal welfare first by introducing a ban on greyhound racing.

Greyhound racing continues to cause injuries and deaths to dogs in England each year. Although welfare measures have been introduced, serious concerns remain about the treatment of racing greyhounds and their quality of life. Wales has announced plans to ban greyhound racing, and Scotland is moving towards ending the sport. We believe England should follow suit by introducing legislation to ban greyhound racing and prioritise animal welfare over commercial interests.

records.title: Require all airlines to ban nuts and nut products on UK flights
records.description: Require all airlines operating flights from the UK to ban the sale and consumption of peanuts, tree nuts and nut-containing products onboard, to reduce the risk of potentially life-threatening allergic reactions and provide consistent protection for passengers.
records.further_details: For people with a severe peanut allergy, flying can be extremely frightening because of the risk of exposure to nuts. Airline policies can vary, leaving passengers unsure what protection they will have. I am asking the UK Government to introduce consistent rules banning nuts and nut products on UK flights.

records.title: Reduce the UK Census closure period from 100 years to 80 years
records.description: We request the Government to reduce the UK Census record closure from 100 to 80 years, retaining safeguards for sensitive information, enabling families, genealogists and researchers to access vital historical records earlier while balancing privacy with the legitimate public interest.
records.further_details: UK Census is a vital historical record. 100-year closure denies access. We propose reducing it to 80 years, benefiting genealogists, historians, researchers, schools and the public. Records connect generations and reveal unique details. Earlier access lets families research ancestors while relatives remain alive.  Privacy: anyone under 94 when the records open, the information recorded about them would largely describe their childhood circumstances. We believe an extra 20 years privacy is disproportionate.

records.title: Mandate CMPA training & fund specialised referral pathways in primary care
records.description: Mandate standardised CMPA (Cow's Milk Protein Allergy) for all primary care staff and fund guaranteed, fast-tracked paediatric dietetic referral pathways. We want to end diagnostic delays, trial-and-error formula restrictions, and poor early intervention for infants with Cow’s Milk Protein Allergy.
records.further_details: Many families face months of delay, misdiagnosis, and dismissive care when seeking help for infants with Cow’s Milk Protein Allergy (CMPA). Non-IgE (delayed) symptoms like severe reflux, blood in stool, skin flare-ups, and extreme distress can be written off as "just colic". Many parents experience lengthy trial-and-error formula changes without specialist support. We believe primary care teams need standardised training to recognise CMPA early and specialised pathways to refer infants to dietitians without delay.

records.title: Create a £5,000 tax-free allowance for online marketplace income
records.description: We want the UK Government to create a £5,000 annual tax-free allowance for income earned through online marketplaces and side hustles, including eBay, Vinted, Depop and similar platforms.
records.further_details: We want the UK Government to introduce a £5,000 annual tax-free allowance for income earned through online marketplaces. Many people use platforms such as eBay, Vinted, Depop and Etsy to supplement their income during a period of high living costs. We believe a £5,000 tax-free allowance would encourage entrepreneurship, help households manage rising costs and reduce administrative burdens for people earning modest additional income.

records.title: Require elected public office holders to identify their role on social media
records.description: Require elected public office holders, including MPs, councillors and mayors, to clearly state their official role in their social media profile name.
records.further_details:
We believe people should be able to identify when they are interacting with an elected representative rather than a private individual.
