Elected officials can influence public debate, particularly on local and national issues. Without clear identification, their comments may be mistaken for those of ordinary members of the public.
We think greater transparency would support openness, accountability and public trust. 

We believe this could be achieved through guidance or a code of conduct.

records.title: Mandate Social, Emotional, and Mental Health informed school behaviour policies
records.description: Set out guidelines and legally mandate SEMH-informed school behaviour policies. This should include replacing punitive discipline with early intervention, stopping exclusions which we see as punishing mental health struggles, enforcing trauma training for staff, funding better mental health support.
records.further_details:
We believe SEMH has to be more clearly recognised and treated as an educational need, and not a behavioural failure, to protect children's futures.
 
We are concerned that a large number of SEMH students may be out of education in part because rigid discipline can punish mental health struggles and neurodiversity as bad behaviour. Having experienced this first-hand, I know the pain of being treated as a problem to be managed rather than a student to be helped. We demand the Government set out guidelines for and legally mandate SEMH-safe behaviour policies, in the way we've proposed, to help protect our futures.

records.title: Include British Citizens Studying Medicine Abroad in NHS Training Prioritisation
records.description: The Government should work to ensure the inclusion of British citizens who studied medicine abroad in internationally recognised institutions, in the NHS foundation and specialty training prioritisation, so they are not treated the same as overseas applicants without UK ties.
records.further_details: Some families have funded medical education abroad, expecting their children to return and serve in the NHS. UK citizenship should be recognised as part of the priority to ensure fairness, while strengthening the NHS with graduates whose training cost the UK nothing.

records.title: Review and improve safeguarding for children before and after adoption
records.description: Review and strengthen safeguarding for children before and after adoption by improving multi-agency working, recognising professional judgement alongside evidence, and considering routine and unannounced welfare visits before Adoption Orders.
records.further_details:
As a foster carer and adopter, I believe children placed for adoption are among the most vulnerable in society, often having experienced abuse, neglect or trauma. Most adoptive families provide loving homes, but vulnerability does not end when a child is placed. I believe safeguarding should be reviewed to ensure professional judgement, information sharing and appropriate welfare visits help identify concerns before harm occurs.

A child does not stop being vulnerable when they become adopted.

records.title: Fund IVF & PGT-SR for all families with genetic conditions
records.description: We ask the Government to fund NHS-provided access to IVF & PGT-SR for all families with diagnosed genetic conditions, such as hereditary chromosome abnormalities.
records.further_details:
We want treatment to be based on medical need & genetic risk, not income, and for factors like having a child & your postcode to be excluded.
 
Many couples are denied NHS-funded IVF and PGT-SR simply because they already have one child, despite facing a high risk of miscarriage, failed IVF cycles, infertility, or passing on serious genetic abnormalities.
 
We believe this creates an unfair system based on postcode and financial circumstances rather than medical need. Families may be forced to pay £10,000+ privately per cycle for treatment that is not elective, but medically necessary to give them the best chance of a healthy pregnancy.

records.title: Review Investigative and Prosecutorial Standards in Sexual Offence Cases
records.description: We call for a review into the investigative and prosecutorial practices in sexual offence cases to ensure fair evidence standards, proper disclosure, and accountability, protecting the integrity of the justice system for all.
records.further_details: We call for a review of the handling of sexual offence cases, including the practices of the CPS and police to ensure fair investigations. In our view stronger oversight, fair procedures, and strict adherence to evidence-based standards are essential to prevent wrongful accusations and lives being damaged and to protect justice and the presumption of innocence.

records.title: Amend UK trade agreements with the Faroes to protest dolphin hunting & killing
records.description: We call on the UK Government to review and amend trade agreements with the Faroe Islands. The Grindadráp involves driving dolphins and whales into shallow waters where they are horrifically killed. The practice goes against all marine mammal protection law in the UK.
records.further_details: We call on the UK Government to review and amend trade agreements with the Faroe Islands to ensure they do not inadvertently support the killing of dolphins. We want all imported fish products from the Faroes to be clearly marked as being from the Faroes and stating that it is not a dolphin-friendly product. Dolphins are protected in UK waters, yet this practice continues abroad in a country which is a UK trading partner. We believe UK trade policy should reflect strong animal welfare standards morals and public concern.

records.title: Commission an inquiry into wrongful convictions & the current appeals process
records.description: The current appeals system provides for errors in law and/or evidence that was not available at trial. We are concerned that many people have been found wrongly convicted after years of imprisonment.
records.further_details:
We call on the Government to commission an inquiry into the current appeals system and making changes to reduce wrongful convictions. Many wrongly convicted will never admit guilt to a crime they did not commit and therefore may be ineligible for release on licence. We believe the law must change to help those wrongly convicted. In some cases, there has been lack of evidence, in others a lack of adequate defence. 
 
We want the inquiry to look into ways to ensure those wrongfully convicted can access quick resolutions to their convictions, have sufficient defence teams, and ensuring uniformity in sentencing.

records.title: End Funding For Military Interventions Overseas and Spend Taxes In The UK.
records.description: We demand the government end the use of taxpayers’ money to fund military interventions, or providing military support for conflicts abroad. We believe that our taxes should be spent on improving public services, supporting communities and addressing urgent domestic issues rather than war.
records.further_details:
We think the British public deserves to know, that their hard-earned money, is being spent responsibly and ethically, prioritising peace, stability and prosperity at home. We seek a foreign policy grounded in diplomacy and peace-building, rather than what can be costly and divisive military actions, that may have limited long-term success.

The financial burden of war is significant. The UK’s involvement in wars and military operations over the last two decades has cost billions of pounds.

records.title: Fund recovery wards in hospitals for mothers that have newborns in NICU
records.description: Fund separate wards for mothers who have babies in the NICU where they don’t have to watch other mothers bonding with their babies. It could be a space for women in the same position to seek comfort and reassurance from each other.
records.further_details: My son was born at 34 weeks via emergency C section he was sent to the NICU straight away. I was sent up to the ward with 3 other women who had their babies with them. I watched them hold, cuddle and feed their babies. It wasn’t until the next day that it really affected me emotionally, especially because we had to keep all the curtains open because of the babies being jaundiced. It’s hard enough being separated from your baby but to watch other women holding theirs is really difficult.

records.title: Establish a new Independent Complaints Process for Serving Police Officers
records.description: Amend the Police Reform Act 2002 to create an independent complaints process for police officers which would allow them, whether victims, suspects, or whistleblowers, to raise concerns about their force without those matters being referred back internally.
records.further_details: Officers often feel they cannot raise concerns independently, as complaints via the IOPC are often returned to the same force. This discourages reporting of misconduct, discrimination, or unlawful behaviour. Officers, whether victims or suspects must have fair access to independent review. Listening early to officers’ concerns can prevent harm, rather than reacting only after serious incidents or deaths. We believe mistreatment and lack of support has caused significant harm to officers and shows urgent need for change.

records.title: Do not bring forward the rise in state pension age to 68
records.description: The Government must halt any plans for an earlier State Pension age rise to 68.  Data suggests that healthy lifespans are falling. We believe it is unfair to force millions who started work at 16 to work longer despite declining health & Ministers must protect workers, and keep the timeline.
records.further_details: Reports suggest that the Government is considering bringing forward state pension age rises so that millions more people, who started work at 16, will have to continue to work until 68. Since 2019, healthy life expectancy has fallen. Those affected will have worked longer and may have shorter retirements than their parents - a retrograde step. Many people cannot get jobs at this age because they are simply considered too old to keep working.

records.title: Change the rule on admissibility of recorded evidence in domestic abuse cases
records.description: We want the Government to create a presumption of admissibility for recordings submitted as evidence by victims to the police relating to domestic violence in order to help protect victims from further abuse.
records.further_details: As it stands, covert recordings are only admissible  in court at the judge’s discretion even if they are recordings of the abuse either taking place or the abuser talking about the abuse they have caused. Victims often struggle to have sufficient evidence for the CPS to prosecute the abuser. If you record the abuse without the abuser knowing the evidence usually cannot be used in a court of law as you did not gain consent from the abuser to record them.

records.title: Provide funding to increase capacity for employment tribunal hearings
records.description: Employment Tribunals are severely under-resourced, leaving claimants and respondents waiting up to 5 years for hearings. We call on the Government to invest sufficient funding to increase judicial resource into the ET system, and publish a clear, time-bound plan to reduce waiting times.
records.further_details: Employment rights only matter if they can be enforced in reasonable time. Many Employment Tribunal claimants wait years for hearings on unfair dismissal, discrimination, whistleblowing and unpaid wages claims. These delays bring financial hardship, stress and uncertainty, and make it harder for people to move on with their careers and lives. Timely access to justice is a cornerstone of a fair legal system. Delays weaken the value of any remedy and erode public trust in the tribunal system.

records.title: Fund research into improving maternal health outcomes for black women in the UK
records.description: We are calling for the Government to increase funding into research focused on maternal health outcomes for black women, including improved data collection and transparency around maternal outcomes.
records.further_details: We must ensure all women receive equal, safe, and respectful care during pregnancy and childbirth. Black women in the UK are more likely to experience serious complications during pregnancy and childbirth, as well as being at higher risk of death, as reported by MBRRACE-UK IN 2024. Reasons include delayed diagnosis, untreated conditions, and poorer care. We believe more research and funding are needed to understand these disparities, improve outcomes, and ensure all women receive safe, equal and timely maternity care.

records.title: Create a tax-free overtime allowance for overtime worked above 40 hours per week
records.description: We want the Government to introduce a change to Income Tax so that genuine overtime worked above 40 hours per week is tax free, up to a set cap. This should apply only to hours worked above a person’s normal contracted hours. The policy should also comply with existing working time law.
records.further_details: We believe people who work beyond a full working week should keep more of what they earn from those extra hours. A tax-free overtime allowance could improve take-home pay, make extra shifts more worthwhile, help employers fill hard-to-cover shifts and support the wider economy. Limiting it to genuine overtime above contracted hours, with a cap and payroll recording, would help reduce abuse and make the policy more practical and affordable.

records.title: Require employers to notify all interviewees of their hiring outcome
records.description: The law does not legally require employers to inform interviewees if they are unsuccessful. This "ghosting" can cause stress for job seekers. We call on the Government to require employers to notify all job candidates of their application’s outcome after an interview, even if it is automated.
records.further_details:
There is currently no legal requirement for employers to inform interviewees if they have been unsuccessful. This common practice of "ghosting" can leave candidates in limbo, cause unnecessary anxiety and damage morale during an already stressful job search.
 
Requiring a simple, automated notification could ensure closure and transparency for all job seekers.

records.title: Ban local authorities from approving driven piling near existing homes
records.description: We ask the government to change planning legislation and national planning policy so that local planning authorities cannot approve the use of driven piling near existing residential properties as part of the planning process.
records.further_details:
Driven piling causes constant, prolonged significant noise and low/high constant infiltrating vibration leading to loss of peace and enjoyment in residents’ homes. Mental wellbeing is greatly affected and very quickly.
We are concerned that LPAs currently have discretion to approve devs. that include driven piling even where lower-impact methods are available.
We believe the govt. should remove this discretion and introduce prohibitive national rules to stop driven piling close to homes.

records.title: Add Long Covid as a qualifying condition to access nirmatrelvir with ritonavir
records.description: Long Covid patients are ineligible for accessing nirmatrelvir with ritonavir on the NHS when reinfected with Covid-19. There is no NHS treatment pathway to cure Long Covid. Nirmatrelvir with ritonavir can’t even be bought privately over the counter in the UK, so ineligible patients cannot access it.
records.further_details:
We ask the Government to add Long Covid to the health conditions that make patients eligible to accessing nirmatrelvir with ritonavir on the NHS, as Long Covid patients are currently ineligible for the antiviral medication on the NHS when reinfected with Covid-19.
 
Reinfection can worsen symptoms or trigger relapse.  We ask the UK Government to add Long Covid to the qualifying health conditions to access nirmatrelvir with ritonavir on the NHS, so patients already living with the long-term effects of Covid-19 are protected from reinfection.

records.title: Require schools to ringfence SPP and report how it helps service children.
records.description: Introduce rules so SPP (Service Pupil Premium) is used specifically for service children, tracked clearly, overseen by a designated lead in each school, and used to provide targeted support that helps them thrive during parental deployment and improve their wellbeing and learning outcomes.
records.further_details: SPP is intended to support children of armed forces families, particularly during parental deployments and postings. Without ringfencing, the funding can be absorbed into general Pupil Premium, meaning children may not receive the targeted support they need. Clear rules on spending, tracking, and oversight would ensure that SPP actually improves the wellbeing, attendance, and learning outcomes of service children, giving families confidence that the funding is used as intended.

records.title: Government must abolish IPSA
records.description: We believe MPs should be stopped from claiming tax-payer-funded & none-means-tested perks & allowances which we feel contrasts hugely with the means-tested and limited support available to the public.
records.further_details:
While many single people & families struggle to tighten their belts, MPs continue to receive substantial salaries, and can claim expense allowances, and perks, that most of their constituents could never dream of. We believe this disparity, what we see as the lack of transparency, and the growing frustration among taxpayers who have little say in how their money is spent, has to stop.
 
We believe this should also go some way to ending the career politician, as we need elected MP's who can relate to their constituents.

records.title: Conduct a review into the treatment of white people by the police
records.description: We call on the government to conduct a review into whether there are internal or external factors that are impacting police services and how they respond to white people, particularly if the police are discriminatory towards white people.
records.further_details: We believe some recent high profile cases are raising concerns that the policing response to white people is below adequate. The government needs to review this to see whether this is happening and if so, why it is happening.

records.title: Fund research into the causes, treatment & medical training for Fibromyalgia
records.description: I would like the Government to invest in research into the causes of Fibromyalgia, and fund better training for all health professionals who may encounter sufferers and a better care pathway that is more effective and accessible to Fibromyalgia patients.
records.further_details:
Fibromyalgia is a chronic pain condition that has no cure. It is treated with medication that we feel is not effective long term as the cause is not clearly understood.
 
For this reason, we believe care and the treatment of Fibromyalgia patients needs improvement. We feel better research, education and treatment is needed to improve the quality of life of those living with this condition. We therefore call for the Government to provide funding on research and education of Fibromyalgia.

records.title: Legislate to release the 1951 census in 2032 instead of 2052
records.description: Legislate to allow the release of the 1951 census details in 2032 instead of 2052 due to there being no censuses available in 1931 and 1941. This would mean that many families could find answers to genealogical questions that currently have no answers and no means of finding the answers elsewhere.
records.further_details:
The next census that should be available is the 1931 census but has been destroyed. In 1941 there was no census due to war. There is a precedent for releasing personal information early and that is the 1939 register where data is redacted if the named individual is not known to be dead.
 
Twenty six years is a long wait for family historians to wait for new data on their ancestors to be revealed and many now searching will unfortunately not be alive themselves when the census is published.

records.title: Fully fund tuition fees for all healthcare-related degree programs
records.description: Fund healthcare tuition fees and reintroduce living grants. The NHS spends £2bn+ on agency staff while students work thousands of clinical hours for free. We think we must remove debt barriers & placement poverty to stop dropouts, end the staffing crisis, and ensure the NHS is staffed for the future
records.further_details: In our view, current student debt levels create an elitist barrier, preventing the NHS from reflecting the diverse communities it serves. We believe removing these hurdles is essential for social mobility, ensuring the most talented candidates, not just the wealthiest, enter the profession. We think funding degrees is a strategic national investment that ensures safe staffing ratios, reduces trainee burnout, and guarantees a resilient, world-class health service for the next generation. It is time to treat healthcare training as a public good

records.title: Launch a national awareness campaign on sepsis & emergency responses
records.description: We are calling for greater awareness, earlier recognition and faster treatment of sepsis – a life-threatening condition, by launching a national awareness campaign. We hope it will prevent loss and heartbreak. We believe sepsis should be treated as an emergency.
records.further_details:
Sepsis can develop rapidly and requires urgent action. We believe the Government should launch a national awareness campaign for health authorities and hospitals, so they can strengthen training, improve early response protocols, and help increase public awareness so suspected sepsis is treated with the urgency it deserves.
 
Our hope is to spare other families the pain of losing a loved one from sepsis.

records.title: Require insurers to verify animal boarding licences before providing insurance
records.description: Legislate to require insurers to verify animal boarding licences before issuing or renewing insurance cover for animal boarding businesses. Insurers should be responsible for checking licences are valid, current and relevant to the activity being insured.
records.further_details: Many businesses, including animal boarding providers, are legally required to hold certain licences to operate. However, insurers can issue or renew policies without verifying that the licence exists, is current or covers the activity being insured. We believe insurers should be required to verify legally required animal boarding licences before issuing or renewing insurance cover, to help protect consumers, animals and the public from unlicensed operators.

records.title: Fund free rail travel for Armed Forces veterans and a nominated companion
records.description: We ask the Government to fund free rail travel for everyone eligible for a Veterans Railcard, replacing the one-third discount. We also ask that a veteran's nominated companion, such as a spouse or partner, be entitled to free rail travel when travelling with the veteran.
records.further_details:
Those who served in our Armed Forces accepted demands and sacrifices far beyond an ordinary career, and some never return home. Their families also endured deployments, separation and uncertainty, making them an integral part of that service. Free rail travel would be a practical, lasting way for the country to recognise veterans and those who supported them, while helping them stay connected to work, healthcare, family and their communities.
 
A small national thank-you for a lifetime of service.

records.title: Ban suspended sentences for sexual and violent offences against children
records.description: Change the law so custodial sentences for sexual and serious violent offences against children cannot be suspended. When a court decides an offence against a child is serious enough for custody, we believe that sentence should be served in custody.
records.further_details: Children are particularly vulnerable victims of sexual and violent crime. We believe that when a court decides an offence against a person under 18 is serious enough to warrant a custodial sentence, that sentence should not be suspended. Courts would still determine the appropriate length of sentence based on each case. We want legislation to ensure custodial sentences for sexual and serious violent offences against children are served in custody.

records.title: Ban financial lobbying from groups linked to states facing active ICJ cases
records.description: Legislate to ban groups with financial links to states facing active litigation at the ICJ from lobbying MPs and All-Party Parliamentary Groups. This includes a ban on MPs and APPGs accepting funded hospitality, travel or other gifts from these lobby groups.
records.further_details:
Current legislation and rules regulate direct foreign funding, but third-party political lobby groups can bypass these restrictions. Many MPs have accepted gifts and sponsored travel from certain lobby groups linked to states accused of severe international law violations.
 
We believe Parliament should submit legislation to freeze the financial influence of these lobby groups. This could ensure the conduct of UK diplomatic relations and parties strictly align with international humanitarian standards and the rule of law.

records.title: Ban the sale and hiring of e-scooters across the country by 2028
records.description: We would like the Government to ban the purchase & hiring of e-scooters throughout the country. We believe e-scooters are dangerous for both the riders & road users. Hireable e-scooters are a problem, as they can be used and then discarded in roadways, pathways & sometimes on people's properties.
records.further_details: Data suggests that e-scooters are dangerous to the riders and road users. In 2025, there were 1484 collisions recorded involving electric scooters - a 6.4% increase from the previous year - and at least 20-25% of these accidents involve those under the age of 18. A percentage of these accidents end fatally or result in severe injury, including broken bones and head trauma. These accidents can severely impact those involved, the rider, other riders and pedestrians, their families and bystanders. We believe that by signing this you could save a loved one.

records.title: Reinstate Ofsted nannies for the Student Finance Childcare Grant
records.description: We ask the Government to reverse the decision to exclude Ofsted-registered nannies from the Student Finance England Childcare Grant and reinstate them as eligible childcare providers, including protection for existing student families affected by the August 2026 rule change.
records.further_details: From August 2026, student parents can no longer generally use the Childcare Grant for Ofsted-registered nannies. This affects parents, including student nurses and midwives, who need childcare for night, weekend and irregular placements when nurseries or childminders may be unavailable. Older children may also need suitable home-based care. Registered nannies have invested in Ofsted requirements, training, DBS checks, first aid and insurance, yet now risk losing their livelihoods.

records.title: Cut Fuel Duty by 20p per Litre to Reduce the Cost of Living.
records.description: We call on the UK Government to cut fuel duty by 20p per litre to ease the cost of living. Lower fuel prices would reduce everyday costs, support workers who rely on driving, and help bring down prices across the wider economy while still earning estimated £20bn in tax revenue.
records.further_details: Fuel costs impact the price of almost everything in the UK, from food and deliveries to public transport. High fuel duty increases costs for businesses and is passed on to consumers, worsening the cost of living. A 20p reduction could ease pressure across the economy, lower prices, and support growth, while the government could still receive over £20bn annually in fuel tax revenue.

records.title: Apologise and hold inquiry into ESN schools in the 1950s to 1980s
records.description: From the 1950s through to the 1980s, thousands of children were labelled “educationally subnormal” and removed from mainstream education. Many of these children were misclassified due to flawed testing, cultural bias, racism, poverty, and low expectations within the education system.
records.further_details: Once placed in ESN schools, children were often given little or no meaningful education. Many were left unable to read, write, or access basic qualifications. For many, consequences have lasted a lifetime —affecting employment, income, mental health, and self-worth. Despite the scale and impact of this injustice, there has been no full public inquiry, no formal government apology and no comprehensive support or compensation for survivors.

records.title: Make vehicle odometer tampering ('clocking') a criminal offence in the UK
records.description:
We call on the Government to update the law to:
Make altering a vehicle's odometer illegal in all circumstances (for both electrified and internal combustion engine (ICE) cars).
records.further_details:
Under current UK law, selling a clocked car without disclosure is illegal, but the actual act of rolling back an odometer is not. Mileage correction kits can easily be bought online for a few hundred pounds, artificially inflating vehicle values and exposing buyers to hidden safety risks. 

The government has acknowledged the necessity of banning clocking as part of the Pay-Per-Mile EV tax (set for 2028), but the discussion hasn’t extended to banning clocking for all vehicles, including ICE.

records.title: Make British Summer Time (BST) permanent year-round - No more Clock Changes
records.description: We call on the UK Government and Parliament to keep the UK on British Summer Time (BST) permanently—by ending the bi-annual clock changes and remaining one hour ahead of GMT year-round.
records.further_details:
1. Lighter evenings may improve safety, health and encourage active lifestyles.
2. Permanent BST helps avoid dark winter afternoons, which may make communities safer and more welcoming.
3. Ending clock changes may prevent disruption to sleep, work, travel and digital systems — potentially boosting productivity.
4. More daylight reduces energy use, helping households with bills and supporting climate goals.
5. Other nations have shown permanent daylight saving works, the UK should lead with a modern, consistent approach.

records.title: Make Makaton Training Mandatory In Care, Education & Extracurricular Settings
records.description: Make Makaton Level 1 training compulsory for people working in care, education and extracurricular activities.
records.further_details: Many people with communication difficulties rely on Makaton to express needs, feelings and participate safely. Basic training would improve inclusion, safeguarding, accessibility and equal opportunities for children and adults across the country. Too often, staff in schools, care and extracurricular settings cannot understand basic signs.

records.title: Abolish vehicle excise duty on battery electric vehicles
records.description: We want the Government to abolish vehicle excise duty on electric vehicles. My car emits 0 co2 and weighs 1345kg. My VED is £200 pa. My friend's petrol car emits 128 g/km co2 and weighs 2080kg. Her VED is £170. I do not know how this can be considered fair.
records.further_details: I believed the Government was trying to incentivise people to help industry and buyers. EVs are more expensive to buy, depreciation is much higher than ICE cars, and the public charging network is still not good enough, and in some cases more expensive than fossil fuel. We feel this needs to be addressed in the interests of fairness – it shouldn’t just be about gaining revenue.

records.title: Review and strengthen child car seat law
records.description: We want the Government to review current child car seat law to strengthen it. We believe the current law is derived from outdated research. Recent research has suggested that the law should be updated, better protecting children on every journey.
records.further_details:
A review should include:
1.	improving standardised safety grading
2.	making extended rear-facing compulsory until a seat is genuinely outgrown
3.	When extended rear-facing car seat is outgrown, a high-back booster to be used until they are at least 150cm tall
4.	School and commercial trips to use high-back boosters.

Extended rear-facing car seats can offer better protection in a crash. High Back Boosters provide a better seat belt fit and more protection from side impact. We feel there is a lack of understanding of these benefits among the general public, including parents and care givers.

records.title: Family parking space badges for children up to 12 and fines for illegitimate use
records.description: Create a badge system similar to the blue badge that will allow families with children up to 12 years old or pregnant mothers to be the only ones allowed to use parent parking. Introduce fines for individuals who break the rules and park there without a child or who aren't pregnant.

records.title: Make abdominal aortic aneurysm screening available for women 65+
records.description: Make aneurysm screening available for women from the ages of 65 onwards as  it is now for men. As an employee of the NHS on our ward alone there has been 5 women in the last 9 months with such aneurysms, only picked up by scans and checks for other medical reasons. We believe this needs to change.
records.further_details: Aneurysms are a silent killer and as I said in my previous statement 5 women in the last 9 months on our ward that we work on have be found to have aneurysms from a scan/check from another medical reason. Women's lives are just as important as men's and we all should be treated equally.

records.title: Require fines instead of points for drivers exceeding speed limits by up to 5mp
records.description: Drivers should be fined instead of given points for exceeding any speed limit by up to 5mph, with the amount being similar to charges for parking violations.
records.further_details:
Most road users understand speed limits. But we feel getting points which can lead to the loss of a driving licence is outdated and inappropriate given the multiplicity of modern road hazards.
 
Speed limits often change and we consider signage to be inconsistent and inadequate in towns and on motorways especially. Many drivers constantly avoid modern hazards, especially cyclists, potholes and worn-out white lines. We feel modern technology is ruthlessly good, so its use should be ruthlessly fair too.

records.title: Increase penalties for motor vehicles that exceed legal noise pollution levels
records.description: We ask the UK Government to introduce stricter penalties for excessive vehicle noise, including modified loud exhaust systems and unnecessary use of car horns during night hours. Excessive noise from vehicles is a growing problem in many communities across the UK.
records.further_details:
Modified exhaust systems and anti-social driving behaviour often produce noise levels that disturb residents, disrupt sleep, and negatively impact mental wellbeing. Similarly, the misuse of vehicle horns late at night adds to unnecessary noise pollution.

We feel current enforcement measures and fines are not sufficient to deter repeat offenders. Many individuals continue to modify vehicles or engage in disruptive behaviour without facing meaningful consequences.

records.title: Remove requirement to be 10-year seizure & medication free for HGV & PSV license
records.description: Remove requirement for people diagnosed with epilepsy to be seizure and medications for seizures free for 10 years to hold a licence for group 2 drivers (HGV & PSV). We believe that the individual case should be assessed to see by their medical teams to hold such a licence.
records.further_details: In my view the road traffic act of 1988 is out of date, unfair and unjustified. We want the Government to question why other medical conditions for example those who have had heart attacks and strokes are considered as having high risk conditions which are also medicated, but they are still allowed to drive group 2 vehicles.

records.title: Give legal gender recognition to non-binary+ people
records.description:
What I want the Government/Parliament to do:
 - For nonbinary+ people to have Legal Gender Recognition (for people to be able to put N/A or none of the above or X etc on legal documents)
- Marriage/Civil Partnership labels to be other than bride or groom
- Legal gender-neutral titles (such as Mx)
records.further_details: I myself as a nonbinary individual who is on the spectrum understand the difficulties that nonbinary+ and neurodivergent people face. It has angered me that we do not have these rights, and I think that it is time to change. It would help countless people, and you can help by signing this petition.

records.title: Amend the Nursery Milk Scheme to fund alternatives for children with allergies
records.description: Allergic toddlers often sit with nothing to drink while peers have free milk unless parents pay a c£307/yr "allergy tax" for safe cartons which can create a large financial penalty or can leave vulnerable toddlers with a nutritional deficit. The scientific consensus now shows plant milks are safe.
records.further_details: Children should not be excluded from the benefits of the Nursery Milk Scheme due to medical need! Allergic toddlers are left out at snack time while peers get free state milk. Because this Scheme cannot reimburse dairy and soya-free alternatives, families can face an unfair c£307 yearly "allergy tax" per child to provide safe, fortified cartons if they can. For low-income families, this can create a major nutritional deficit or force children to feel excluded. Government reviews have confirmed that fortified plant milks are safe. It's time to stop medically discriminating against children.

records.title: Give Coroners Discretion to Restrict Press Access
records.description: Give coroners discretionary powers to restrict press access when they judge an inquest as sensitive, and where reporting may cause unnecessary harm or distress to bereaved families. This should not prevent transparency of proceedings and an open justice process.
records.further_details: Bereaved families attending inquests often have no control over press attendance or how their loved one’s death is reported. In sensitive cases, reporting can cause further trauma, stigma and harmful public speculation. We want coroners to have clear discretionary powers to limit press access in circumstances where this is necessary to protect families and the dignity of the deceased.

records.title: Classify beverages at or below 0.5% ABV as alcohol free
records.description: Change the law so any drink at 0.5% ABV or below can be labelled “alcohol-free”. At 0.05%, the UK’s limit is the strictest in the world. The Government has consulted twice and committed to it. Stop consulting and act.
records.further_details: For context: a ripe banana or a bread roll can hold as much alcohol as a 0.5% beer, yet the beer can’t call itself alcohol-free. We are concerned that the world’s strictest 0.05% limit is easy for big brands with big budgets to hit and market, but a costly barrier for small independent brewers. It also fuels the myth that a 0.5% beer is much like a real pint, when the amount is negligible. We think that aligning with the 0.5% international standard would mean honest, consistent labelling people can actually trust.

records.title: Add Pet Heat Safety Warnings to UK Met Office Extreme Heat Alerts
records.description: We call on the Government to work with the Met Office to include pet heat safety advice in all official extreme heat warnings. This should include guidance on avoiding dog walks in dangerous temperatures, hot pavements, preventing heatstroke and when to seek urgent veterinary care.
records.further_details: Every year, dogs across the UK suffer and die from preventable heatstroke during periods of extreme heat. Many owners seem unaware of the dangers of hot pavements, high temperatures and overexertion. We believe the Government should work with the Met Office to include clear pet safety advice in all official heat warnings, helping owners recognise the risks, protect their animals and reduce avoidable suffering, injury and veterinary emergencies.

records.title: Introduce a maximum NHS waiting time for risk-reducing mastectomy
records.description: Introduce a maximum NHS waiting time of 12 months for people who have been approved for risk-reducing mastectomy because they are at very high risk of developing breast cancer.
records.further_details: People at very high genetic risk of breast cancer can choose risk-reducing mastectomy, yet may face long waits for surgery. I have a BRCA1 mutation and waited 16 months for mine. Breast cancer was unexpectedly found in the tissue removed during my operation. I believe people undergoing surgery specifically to reduce their cancer risk should not face prolonged waits during which that risk remains. A 12-month maximum would provide a clear national standard and greater certainty for patients.

records.title: Raise higher rate tax threshold to £60k, and raise yearly in line with inflation
records.description: This petition asks the Government to increase the higher rate income tax threshold from £50,270 to £60,000 now and going forwards introduce automatic annual increases to the threshold in line with inflation.
records.further_details: Frozen thresholds are pushing many workers, such as some NHS staff in London, into the 40% tax band. High Cost Area supplements increase taxable pay but often may only cover travel and living costs, not real income. As a result, pay rises don’t necessarily improve take-home pay.

records.title: Create national "Low Demand School Hubs" for students with EBSA, ODD, and PDA
records.description: The Government should provide funding and a national framework for "Low-Demand School Hubs" specifically designed for students with Emotional Based School Avoidance (EBSA), Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD), and Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA).
records.further_details: Current "inclusion bases" within mainstream schools are often insufficient—acting like a band-aid on a broken leg. Students with these profiles require an environment built on autonomy, collaborative communication, and sensory regulation, rather than the high-pressure, rigid structures of traditional education.

records.title: Review how the Home Office deals with False Domestic Abuse Claims to get ILR
records.description: A BBC investigation raised concerns that the UK Home Office have granted settled status to migrants based on insufficient evidence when applicants claimed they had experienced domestic abuse.
records.further_details:
The government should review past cases to ensure they were processed fairly and if evidence from both sides were properly considered.
 
It has been reported that some migrants are marrying British citizens and then claiming false domestic abuse to obtain a fast track route to Indefinite Leave to Remain. A BBC Investigation found that the number of people using the domestic violence route rose by more than 50% in just three years. This has caused trauma and ruined British citizens lives.

records.title: Increase national single-carriageway, dual-carriageway & motorway speed limits
records.description: Increase respective speed limits on appropriately-engineered single carriageway, dual carriageway & motorway class roads to 70mph, 80mph & 90mph respectively.
records.further_details: Vehicle technology (brakes, suspension, tyres & associated driver assistance systems) have improved out of all recognition since the existing limits were imposed. Many accidents are caused by poor observation, poor hazard perception & hence poor hazard response; so accompanying road user training; focussed on enhancing road user attention on the driving task, could help negate the issue of higher vehicle speeds.

records.title: Require asylum claims to meet the same evidential standard as other routes
records.description: We ask the Government to require asylum claims to be assessed against the same standards of verified identity, evidence and background checks as other legal immigration routes, ensuring fixed decision timeframes, enforced removal after failed appeals, and a review of accommodation costs and impact.
records.further_details: We are concerned that asylum seekers can currently remain in the UK for years with less identity verification than someone applying for a work or family visa. We are calling for asylum claims to be checked against the same range and standard of proof, documentation and background checks as every other immigration route. We want requirements for fixed timeframes for decisions, verified identity and origin, enforced removal once appeals are exhausted, and an independent review of the cost and community impact of hotel accommodation.

records.title: Cut FLR(FP) waiting times for people with British children or British partners
records.description: Reduce delays in Further Leave to Remain (Family and Private life) applications for parents of British children and partners. Some families have waited over 12 months despite paying £5,000+ including for the Immigration Health Surcharge and usually having no access to public funds.
records.further_details: Delays can harm jobs, businesses, mental health and children’s welfare. We want the Government to set an 8-week maximum decision time with automatic priority processing for family cases. With no access to public funds, delays can affect work, businesses, housing, mental health and children’s wellbeing. We believe British children should not suffer because a parent’s application is delayed.

records.title: Amend Health and Safety at Work Act to include the provision of defibrillators
records.description: This petition calls on the UK Government to review and update the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 to explicitly include the provision and consideration of automated external defibrillators (AEDs) within workplace and public health and safety requirements.
records.further_details:
When this legislation was originally enacted, defibrillators were not widely available within communities, nor were they considered a standard component of emergency response. Advances in medical technology and increased public access to AEDs have since demonstrated their critical role in saving lives during sudden cardiac arrest, where immediate intervention can significantly improve survival rates.

Despite this progress, there remains no clear statutory requirement or guidance within the Act.

records.title: Mandate wheelchair-accessible emergency safety zones in motorway barriers
records.description: We ask the Government to require National Highways to install wheelchair‑accessible emergency gates, ramps or lowered alcoves along motorway barriers, especially where no hard shoulder exists. The Department for Transport should update the DMRB to ensure disabled drivers can also reach safety.
records.further_details: Current motorway guidance (“Go Left, Get Safe”) instructs drivers to exit their vehicles and wait behind the barrier, but standard steel and concrete barriers are impossible for paraplegic and wheelchair‑using drivers to cross. On motorways without a hard shoulder, this leaves disabled motorists trapped in live lanes or narrow refuge areas. Installing accessible rear‑opening gates or roll‑through alcoves at intervals would provide a safe, equal escape route for all.

records.title: Legally require ministers to seek expert advice from the UN Human Rights Office
records.description: Legally require ministers to seek and consider advice from relevant human rights experts at the UN Human Rights Office before introducing significant counter-terrorism measures, expanding counter-terrorism powers, or proscribing organisations under UK law.
records.further_details: We believe counter-terrorism powers should protect the public from real threats while respecting human rights, peaceful protest and freedom of expression. We call for stronger safeguards, published human rights assessments, and a legal requirement for ministers to seek and consider UN human rights expert advice before major counter-terrorism decisions are made.

records.title: Reinstate the death penalty for child murderers
records.description: There is no room in society for child murderers. We call on the Government to introduce legislation to reintroduce the death penalty for those convicted of the deliberate murder of a child.

records.title: Write off all Plan 1 student loans after 25 years, not when someone turns 65
records.description: We think that the Plan 1 student loan rules are deeply unfair. If someone started university after Sep 2006, and debt is wiped after 25 years. Start just weeks earlier, and you're trapped paying until age 65. We call on the government to standardise the rules: wipe all Plan 1 loans after 25 years.
records.further_details: We call for equal Treatment for student loan borrowers. In our view, the UK student loan system uses an arbitrary date 1 September 2006 to penalise older Plan 1 graduates. Those starting university after this date have debt wiped 25 years after graduation. Those starting just weeks earlier are trapped paying until age 65, some carrying debt for 40+ years. We therefore call on the Government to standardise the rules: write off all remaining debt 25 years after graduation. Stop punishing older graduates with a lifetime financial penalty based on the calendar

records.title: Provide funding for public outdoor 10m diving platforms
records.description: Provide funding to build outdoor high-diving platforms to provide safe legal sites for diving, reduce trespass, and promote outdoor sport. Inspired by Europe, these facilities could support recreation, training, events, and community wellbeing.

records.title: Ban LGBTQIA+ conversion therapy
records.description: Ban the use of conversion therapy intended to change the sexual orientation or gender identity of members of the LGBTQIA+ community. We believe all forms of “conversion therapy” disrespect the equal moral value of LGBTQIA+ people and violate specific protected areas of liberty and equality.
records.further_details: We believe it has been proven to be ineffective, as citied on gov.uk: “There is no robust evidence that conversion therapy can achieve its stated therapeutic aim of changing sexual orientation or gender identity.” The American Psychological Association also declared that conversion therapy is “not evidence-based therapy.”

records.title: Mandate alcohol breathalyser and drug swab tests in House of Commons
records.description: MPs should be banned from taking part in proceedings if they are found to be under the influence of drugs or alcohol whilst at work. Mandatory drug and alcohol testing is common in many professions. This is important for MPs as they are making decisions that shape the future of the nation.
records.further_details:
Take for example the department of transport, would you expect a bus driver to be under the influence of alcohol or drugs, would you expect an electrician responsible for electrical safety in your home, to be impaired by substances or alcohol?

Why should MPs be permitted to be an exception, when they can make decisions that may send your sons and daughters to war, or change your retirement age, increase your bills and decrease your standards of living. They should be absolutely sober at work.

records.title: Double Government UK civil space spending from its current level by 2030
records.description: Support the UK to join other developed nations and expand its role in international space exploration, science, and utilisation, thus properly supporting growth, security, and highly-skilled jobs. The UK is a major economy, but has fallen behind comparable countries in government space investment.
records.further_details: We believe space investment brings strong economic returns, supports innovation & skills, strengthens national capability, & helps the UK secure industrial, scientific, & inspirational benefits. The UK Space Agency says every £1 invested in space generates over £7 for the UK economy. We feel increased space investment would make the UK’s 2022 National Space Strategy & 2024 Space Industrial Plan viable & achievable. A 2025 House of Lords report warns the UK must act now to lead in the growing space economy.

records.title: Ban hormone and endocrine disruptors from all menstrual products
records.description: Introduce a law making it illegal for any period products—including pads, tampons, and reusable wear—to contain hormone disruptors. The government must mandate independent safety testing and set legal toxic limits to protect highly absorbent vaginal tissue from exposure.
records.further_details: Everyday period products—like pads, tampons, and reusable underwear—often contain hidden chemicals and plastics that can disrupt our hormones. The skin in our most intimate areas is incredibly thin and sensitive. Unlike food, chemicals absorbed here go straight into the bloodstream without being filtered by the body first. We are concerned that hormonal issues and fertility struggles are rising rapidly. Yet, it remains legal for brands to use these materials. The Government must act to ban these substances outright.

records.title: Lift Sanctions on Iran and Restore Trade Relations
records.description: We call on the UK Government to lift sanctions on Iran, work with international partners, including the European Union, to reverse the snapback of JCPOA-related measures, return to the nuclear deal, and restore lawful trade and economic relations with Iran.
records.further_details: Iran has suffered severe damage to its civilian infrastructure following the bombing by the United States and Israel. The country now needs urgent support to rebuild and help ordinary civilians recover.

records.title: Retain Disabled Students’ Allowance (DSA) assistive technology funding
records.description: We’re calling on the Government to protect Disabled Students’ Allowance (DSA) assistive technology funding and reject plans to restrict support to “exceptional circumstances” only. These changes risk widening inequality and must be evidence-based, not cost-driven.
records.further_details:
We are calling on the Department for Education and Student Finance England to protect Disabled Students’ Allowance (DSA) assistive technology funding and reject plans to restrict support to “exceptional circumstances” only.

These changes assume free or general tools can replace specialist support, despite limited evidence of equal outcomes. This risks widening inequality, increasing withdrawals, and reducing outcomes for disabled students. Reforms must be evidence-based, not cost-driven.

records.title: Seek international agreement not to develop super intelligent AI until safe
records.description: UK must ensure that until it is proven that advanced AI can be controlled with a scalable mechanism there must be an agreement between governments not to allow training, building, or progression of general super intelligence.
records.further_details:
Control must be peer reviewed in the government and scientific community until a broad consensus of safety is reached.
 
Anthropic and former OpenAI researcher Jacob Coxon resigned September 2026 with the following statements:
“The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade…”
“They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives…”
 
Anthropic Alignment-Science lead Evan Hubinger response:
“Jacob is correct here – we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade.”

records.title: Review sentences and punishments for sexual assault and rape cases
records.description: Introduce stronger sentences for sexual assault and rape on par with manslaughter and murder. Review training for investigators to ensure better survivor support and a justice system that ensures accountability, deterrence, and long-term public protection.
records.further_details: Sex offences should receive longer sentences similar to manslaughter and murder due to the severe, lasting harm they cause, often resulting in lifelong trauma. Stronger penalties could reflect the seriousness of the crime, deter offenders, protect the public, and maintain trust in the justice system while still allowing for proportionate sentencing and rehabilitation.

records.title: Use new questions on local election ballot papers to trigger a general election
records.description: Questions should be added to local election ballot papers in England about how the current government in charge of the country is doing Eg. Q1. Is the current Government following their manifesto they were elected on (A) YES or NO. Q2. Do you have confidence in the current government (A) YES or NO
records.further_details: We cannot call for a vote of no confidence in the government and get an early general election called. When a party goes against the mandate they were elected on and do not represent the public that voted them in, then adding these questions to a local election ballet paper would give an idea of how the people of this country feel about the current government. If an answer to the questions was a 65% in the NO direction then a general election should be called.

records.title: Remove age verification introduced by online safety act
records.description: We call on the Government to remove the age verification requirements introduced by the Online Safety Act, as we believe that parents should be in charge not the companies as it can be wrong and restrict the wrong people!
records.further_details: People may not want to share their ID to these companies due to concern for their privacy or leaks! In our view, kids could easily bypass it by getting their parents ID which would be their parents fault, so their parents are allowing them to bypass. This is why we think this should be removed and the parents should check what their kid is doing! At the end of the day they can help the kid bypass it.

records.title: Children of sex offenders/domestic abusers to change name w/out parental consent
records.description: I want children of sex offenders or domestic abusers to have the ability to change their name even if they are under 16. This is to prevent them from being identified as the child of a sex offender, as they may be viewed differently in social settings.
records.further_details: Children of sex offenders and/or domestic abusers may live in fear that someone may recognise their name. In some cases, there is concern that victims' family may be able to trace the family of the perpetrator. Being associated with a name can change how people view themselves.

records.title: Require trauma-informed guidance and training in rape investigations and trials
records.description: Require police and prosecutors to have more extensive trauma training to help them consider evidence in rape cases in a trauma-informed way. Include the psychological, physical and functional impact of the offence. Provide guidance to juries on the impact of trauma.
records.further_details: I feel strongly that the lasting impact of trauma after rape is not properly recognised in rape investigations and trials. I want the justice system to be better informed to help victims.

records.title: Review diagnosis of blood cancer in young people
records.description: Young people with leukaemia are often misdiagnosed as symptoms are mistaken for more common illnesses, and cancer is considered unlikely. The Government should review NHS guidance and training for healthcare professionals and access to blood tests when blood cancer is suspected.
records.further_details: Blood cancer symptoms are often misdiagnosed, so many people are not offered a full blood count. This affects young people as blood cancer is considered unlikely at their age and they may appear healthy or cope with symptoms for longer. Delayed diagnosis means many patients present to hospital as an emergency, increasing pressure on the NHS. Improving guidance and education for HCP's would ensure blood tests are requested when blood cancer is a possibility, leading to earlier diagnosis.

records.title: Require people who run over cats to stop and to report it, and impose fine
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce a fine for people who run over cats as Owners have to pay vet bill no fault of their own. We think it’s not right, and think a fine should be introduced even if it’s only a £50 fine
records.further_details: We believe that when someone hits a cat, they should get fined, because at the end of day it’s someone’s pet. I’m doing this petition because my baby got run over and left in a bush for a nearly a week. I did not know he was gone I thought he was still missing.

records.title: Review legal & social care use of ‘parental alienation’ and impact on families
records.description: Review cases where ‘parental alienation’ has been used as a reason to place children in foster care or placements, or to provide custody to parent who has been accused of abuse. Ensure that children are heard, and end use of these concepts in courts, criminal investigations & social work practice.
records.further_details: On 30 June 2026, Ministers told Parliament that parental alienation is a totally discredited concept. Yet we believe it still shapes decisions in family courts, criminal investigations and social work practice that may separate children from loving parents, grandparents, and siblings, often without their wishes and feelings ever being heard. For many abuse victims, the allegation itself can be a tool of coercive control. The Government's rejection of this theory must now be reflected in practice, not just words.

records.title: Urgently help protect greenfield land until the next NPPF is adopted
records.description: We want the Government to bring in emergency legislation to allow local planning authorities to block greenfield developments, with no appeal allowed, until the next National Planning Policy Framework is promulgated.
records.further_details: The last census revealed that Britain has around 1.5 million unoccupied properties; there is also capacity for 1.54 million more homes on brownfield land, and at least 220,000 planning permissions still unbuilt. Moreover, green spaces around motorway junctions are increasingly targeted for B2/B8 commercial and industrial parks, despite empty warehouses in towns and cities. We believe this development growth is harming food security, climate resilience and mental wellbeing. The NFU also reports reduced UK food-production capacity while food imports have risen 70% in 30 years – we believe losing more greenfield areas to development will only make this worse.

records.title: Nationwide vote to decide London's mayor
records.description: London is the capital city of our great nation, we believe there should be a nationwide vote for who runs it, as what happens in London, has a knock on effect for the rest of the country.
records.further_details: This is because London is the capital city and we feel it should be the country that votes for the mayor of its capital city.

records.title: Regulate companies supplying heating oil and LPG
records.description: We are concerned that liquefied petroleum gas suppliers of heating oil and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) are profiteering during geo-political crisis, and when any potential disruption to supply is reported by the media.
records.further_details:
As an example, the price of heating oil doubled in the first couple of weeks of March for oil which had already reached the UK side of the supply lines before the start of the war with Iran.

Currently suppliers are operating outside of any government regulation.
The industry should be regulated, and when necessary price capped by the government.

records.title: Review protection for survivors of post-separation domestic abuse
records.description: Review protection for domestic abuse survivors awaiting court proceedings. This should include cases of post separation abuse, indirect & direct online harassment and abuse, coercive control, and improved safeguarding restrictions for individuals awaiting trial for serious domestic abuse offences.
records.further_details: Many domestic abuse survivors continue to experience post-separation abuse while awaiting lengthy criminal court proceedings, despite bail conditions or non-harassment orders. This can include indirect and direct online harassment, coercive control, stalking, intimidation and smear campaigns. We believe stronger protections, faster action on breaches and improved safeguarding measures for individuals awaiting trial for serious domestic abuse offences is needed.

records.title: Fund free self-defence classes for young girls
records.description: We would like to see funding to help young girls learn to defend themselves in local council/community spaces. Classes could be once or twice a week.

records.title: Ban people from pulling out last minute in social housing exchanges
records.description: When doing a house exchange with someone, one person might be allowed to change their mind at right up until moving day. This should not be allowed, people are packing, changing schools, etc., and then other person pulls out. Once papers are signed is when there is no changing minds about the swap.
records.further_details: Some councils and housing associations may allow people to sign papers to swap with other people but then still allow people to pull out and change minds even up until the day of moving. This should not be allowed. By this stage you might have changes a child's school, book and pay for home removal vans, and so on, only to be told sorry I'm not moving now. We think this is so unfair to the other person that has put in so much effort for the move. Once papers are signed it should be a done deal.

records.title: Ban the sale and planting of invasive cherry laurel (Prunus laurocerasus)
records.description: Add cherry laurel to the list of invasive plants banned from sale and planting in the UK. Launch a strategy to tackle the spread of this invasive exotic shrub across our natural environment.
records.further_details: There are reports that invasive cherry laurel is spreading exponentially across ancient woodland and other natural habitats. We believe the ecological harm arising from the rapid spread of this vigorous exotic shrub is profound and poses an existential threat to our native woodland and wildlife.

records.title: Recognise nonbinary gender identities in law and in official identity documents
records.description: Make nonbinary gender markers possible on any official document where a gender marker is required, e.g. passport, gender recognition certificate, marriage documents, death certificate.
records.further_details: In the recent past the UK government repeatedly acknowledged the existence of nonbinary people, and it should provide documents accordingly.

records.title: Mandate sanitary bins in public loos for those with a colostomy bag
records.description: It’s necessary to not ostracise people that have a colostomy bag and allow them to use general facilities if disabled toilets are not available. Every toilet for customers in a venue/business and public loos maintained by local authorities should be required to have a sanitary bin.
records.further_details: There is a lack of sanitary bins in loos in public places, especially for those with a colostomy bag. There are times that those who have a colostomy bag endure an accident whilst in public, need somewhere to dispose their colostomy bag after changing it. What happens is that those with a colostomy bag after changing it end up having to walk around a public place carrying it until they find somewhere to place in the bin (somewhere outside the loos), this effects all walks of life.

records.title: Compel social media companies operating in the UK to make algorithms transparent
records.description: Introduce legislation requiring social media companies operating in the UK to make their content recommendation, ranking and amplification algorithms transparent to users, regulators and approved independent researchers. Publish explanations of how their algorithms operate and how users can opt out.
records.further_details:
Social media algorithms can strongly influence what people see online, including news, political content and material affecting mental health or public safety. Users often cannot understand why content is being shown to them or how to control it.

Transparency would not need to require publication of trade secrets or source code to the public. Companies could be required to provide meaningful public explanations, user controls, risk assessments and secure access for regulators or researchers.

records.title: Introduce new rules for B2B sales of telecommunication contracts
records.description: We call on the UK Government to introduce an immediate, mandatory 14-day cooling-off period for all business telecommunications contracts sold over the phone. Furthermore, we demand a review of the regulatory oversight and enforcement against predatory sales tactics.
records.further_details:
We call for Regulatory Changes to protect the UK small business economy from predatory telecom practices, through the following legislative and regulatory actions: 
Pre-Contract Disclosure Requirements: Mandate that no B2B verbal contract is legally binding until the business owner has received, reviewed, and signed a clear written summary of all costs and terms after the initial phone call.
Introduce Mandatory 14-Day Cooling-Off Period
Review Mis-selling Practices and Enforcement

records.title: Do not ban social media for under-16s. Ban for under-11s until they turn 16.
records.description: Rather than flat out banning social media for under-16s, it should be a gradual ban, currently banning under-11s who do not have social media as part of their daily routine until they turn 16. This is similar to the Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026
records.further_details: 11-16 year olds currently have social media as part of their daily routine. It would be unfair to ban it so abruptly. A vast group of people also use social media to dissociate from real world problems and may have no other source of happiness. Unless the government specifically have a solution to this problem, it would completely disregard the emotions of these people. The technology to currently handle this issue is non-existent. A wait could allow said technology to be developed adequately.

records.title: Require retailers to name the courier service they use
records.description: Mandate retailers to name the courier service before selling to a consumer so that an informed choice can be made by the consumer. The courier service stated should also be the one making the delivery and it should not be allowed for it to be sub-contracted to another courier service.
records.further_details: The Consumer Rights Act 2015 does not legally require online retailers to stipulate which courier service is used. In order for the consumer to make an informed choice, this should be part of their sales process. There have been multiple reports of items getting lost, damaged, delivered to the wrong address or not delivered at all. We believe couriers are not held accountable, so we need a choice at the point of purchase.

records.title: Ensure Equal Access to NHS Fertility Treatment for Same-Sex Couples
records.description: Establish national NHS standards to ensure same-sex couples can access funded fertility treatment without the burden of self-funded IUI cycles. We call for an end to the postcode lottery, a review of eligibility for those with existing children, and expanded access to options like reciprocal IVF.
records.further_details: Same-sex couples may need 6–12 self-funded IUI cycles before NHS eligibility, costing £10k–£25k and creating an unfair financial barrier. Access to treatment varies by postcode, some are excluded for already having children, and options such as reciprocal IVF are often limited. Fertility care should be fair, consistent, and reflect modern families. It is unfair that same-sex couples face this immense stress and financial worry while opposite-sex couples do not.

records.title: Require ICBs to offer IVF including couples with children from past relationship
records.description: The Government should require ICBs to offer IVF to couples, including those who have children from previous relationships. I want to express my concern and distress that some ICBs who offer IVF, do not let couples who have previous children access it, even if the child is from a past relationship.
records.further_details: I think it is unfair that some people who do not have children of their own are being denied the opportunity to experience pregnancy and motherhood due to factors entirely outside of their control. While I understand that eligibility criteria exist, this fails to recognise individual circumstances. One partner’s previous parenthood does not change the others’ medical need for fertility treatment, nor does it lessen the emotional impact of infertility on someone as an individual.

records.title: Create fund to celebrate 100th anniversary of women fully achieving the vote
records.description: We call on the Government to create a fund of £10million to help celebrate the 100th anniversary of women achieving the vote on equal terms with men in 1928.
records.further_details: The Government should create a fund of £10million for spending in 2026-2028 to celebrate the 2028 centenary. There would be a limit of £500,000 that would be spent on any one individual project.  Applications would be made via local MPs. The MP would need to support the project for it to succeed. Projects could be for permanent installations, such as murals or statues, or temporary, such as events

records.title: Fund and require early assessment, treatment and education on severe period pain
records.description: Fund and require the NHS to assess all severe period pain early, providing faster referrals, diagnostic tests, specialist treatment, and staff training. Expand menstrual health education in schools, including on severe period pain, to help conditions be identified sooner and reduce suffering.
records.further_details: Women and girls with severe period pain are too often dismissed or wait years for diagnosis. Conditions like Endometriosis, Adenomyosis and Uterine fibroids can damage health, education, work and wellbeing. Early assessment and faster treatment could reduce suffering, improve outcomes, and stop pain being ignored.

records.title: Require taxi & rideshare apps to disclose if a vehicle is wheelchair accessible
records.description: Require taxi and ride-hailing transportation services to display a clear 'Disabled Taxi' option to allow users to request a wheelchair accessible vehicle if one is available.
records.further_details: On transportation service apps, options such as 'Priority' 'Comfort' and 'Exec' are often available. On one app, there is an option for 'Assist', but this guarantees only 'special assistance from trained drivers', with no guarantee that the car sent will be wheelchair accessible. Wheelchair users should not have to simply hope that a suitable vehicle is sent, additionally some wheelchairs are only able to sit upright comfortably for a limited time - this should not be time wasted for another vehicle to be sent.

records.title: Ban public transport from operating without working AC when it is 25°C+
records.description: Ban public transport from being in operation without working air conditioning on board when outside temperatures reach 25°C. There should also be inspections for compliance with this ban and a website reporting vehicles in operation without fully working air conditioning.
records.further_details:
We believe we are seeing exponential changes to our climate, and the UK historically lacks AC. We feel this affects our hardworking public transport drivers the most. Drivers’ cabins can reach 10°c higher than outside temperatures, and without AC, it can become inhumane and dangerous to work in these conditions 8+ hours a day.
 
We believe all public transport vehicles should be fitted with working Air Con and regular maintenance. Companies or organisations that fail to do so should be fined per vehicle.

records.title: Commission a strategic review into social work pay, wellbeing and regulation.
records.description: We call for an independent review of the social work sector to address stagnant pay, outdated mileage rates, and excessive hours. Critically, the review must investigate Social Work England’s fitness to practise timeframes, which leave professionals unable to work for years pending completion.
records.further_details: The profession is in crisis. 76% of social workers report a mental health crisis, and 52% intend to leave within 18 months. Average weekly hours exceed contracts by 11 hours, while HMRC mileage rates haven't changed in 15 years. Furthermore, Social Work England's investigation backlog, with case examiner stages averaging 97 weeks, is forcing skilled workers out of the workforce during a staffing shortage. The Government must intervene to ensure the safety of the workforce and the public.

records.title: Make Remote Working a Legal Right Where Roles Can Be Performed From Home
records.description: Grant employees a legal right to work from home where their role can be performed remotely and performance standards are met. Employers must provide clear, evidence-based reasons to refuse, rather than relying on preference or assumption. This right should be enforceable in law.
records.further_details: Evidence since COVID-19 shows remote working can improve productivity, wellbeing, and reduce sickness absence, commuting costs and emissions. Despite this, many employers require office attendance without objective justification. Employees must prove remote work is effective, while employers can refuse it on broad grounds. A legal right would create fairness, consistency and evidence-based decisions. It would modernise UK employment law.

records.title: Government to urge Israel to withdraw from Lebanon
records.description: We call on the UK Government to urge Israel to withdraw from Lebanon, stop occupying Palestinian land, and respect the rights of Lebanese and Palestinians.  We believe this would ensure justice, peace, and recognition of their biblical heritage.

records.title: Mandate low noise fireworks, drone & laser displays instead of normal fireworks
records.description: Mandate the use of low noise fireworks (between 70-90 decibels), drone and laser displays in the place of traditional fireworks as viable alternatives.
records.further_details:
Cats and dogs both experience sounds at far greater intensity than humans. According to the RSPCA, fireworks appear for them as discordant noise without warning.
