During fireworks explosions, nearby resting birds will flee and can fly into buildings. When animals are nesting or in the early stages of rearing their offspring, the risks can be even greater. Babies can die of dehydration or starvation when terrified or disoriented animal parents cannot find their way back to their nests and burrows.

records.title: Link tax threshold increases for pensioners to the triple lock for pensions
records.description: We are concerned that the triple lock rise in UK State Pensions could pull those with a small pension into paying tax. We believe that if the triple lock was to rise by, for example, £400 above the tax threshold, that the tax threshold for pensioners should rise by £400.
records.further_details: This could effectively reduce the unfair impact of the triple lock rise. We feel it’s unfair to give effectively a smaller rise in the triple lock if a person has a small private pension. This would be the case if tax had to be paid on it. We believe the fairest way is to increase tax thresholds for pensioners in line with any rise of the triple lock for UK State Pensions.

records.title: Ban indoor fireworks, sparklers and pyrotechnics in public venues
records.description: We are concerned with the safety of fireworks, sparklers and pyrotechnics in public venues following recent mass casualty events in Europe. We would like to see tighter regulation and ban on indoor fireworks, sparklers and pyrotechnics.
records.further_details: We are concerned about the safety for fireworks, sparklers and pyrotechnics in public venues. Indoor pyrotechnics can result in devastating loss of life in public venues. In the last 50 years in Europe, over 550 people have died and more than 1,500 have sustained severe, life-changing burn injuries.

records.title: Fund community-led mental health services and preventative care
records.description: Fund community-led mental health services, supporting people and their families to have autonomy over their own care. We believe that funding community initiatives can help prevent the systemic failures that lead to mental health issues.
records.further_details: We think the UK mental healthcare model is broken, and some who need urgent care are experiencing punishment when requiring help. Poverty is a significant factor affecting mental health, with people from the Global Majority more likely to live in poverty in the UK. On top of that, Black people in the UK are 4x more likely to be sectioned. Care shouldn’t be based on who you are. We believe we need a community-led healthcare system, with additional support for the most vulnerable, to prevent sectioning.

records.title: Publish assessment of China’s Ethnic Unity Law & transnational repression risks
records.description: We call on the Government to publish a standalone assessment of whether China’s Ethnic Unity Law increases the risk of transnational repression for UK residents, and for the assessment to provide recommendations on measures to protect those who could be at risk.
records.further_details: The UK Government has recognised transnational repression as a threat to democracy and human rights. We are concerned China's Ethnic Unity Law may have implications for diaspora communities living abroad. We believe the UK Government should assess any potential impact on UK residents, including Hong Kongers, Tibetans, Uyghurs, Chinese dissidents and others, and publish recommendations to strengthen protections against intimidation, coercion and foreign interference.

records.title: Enshrine in Law Access to Hormone Replacement Therapy for Transgender Adults
records.description: It has been reported that NHS England is to lead a review into the ‘effectiveness’ of medications for Trans adults. The Government should commit to enshrining the right to medical care for Trans Adults in line with the scientific research that supports Transition.
records.further_details: A review into the effectiveness of HRT for Trans adults has been reported following the pause of prescription of bridging hormones for 16-17 year olds after the Equality and Health Inequalities Impact Assessment (EHIA) concluded that evidence for their effectiveness was ‘weak’. We take into account professional and academic dispute of the validity of study and thus dispute these findings. We are concerned that this report could aim to support a conclusion already decided.

records.title: Make consent training mandatory at all universities
records.description: The OfS found that 1 in 7 students experience sexual assault, with over half occurring in university settings. We believe consent training should not be optional and the Government needs to make it a legal requirement for universities to provide consent training to every student.
records.further_details: Sexual assault is widespread across universities. Some universities have introduced consent training, but it is not consistently provided. The University of Oxford found that 80% of students who completed consent training felt they had a better understanding of consent afterwards. The Government must make consent training a legal requirement for all universities, covering, at a minimum, consent, the law, communicating and checking for consent, and how to seek support after sexual assault.

records.title: Rescind the Discharge of Local Planning Authority Functions Regulations 2026
records.description: The draft Town and Country Planning (Discharge of Local Planning Authority Functions) (England) Regulations 2026 remove the ability for district councillors in planning committees to give input on almost all planning applications.
records.further_details:
We believe this would leave constituents without a say on the development of their communities and be disastrous for local democracy. Under the Regulations: no councillor would be able to call in a planning application; officers would make the final decision on most applications, bypassing planning committees; this means effectively no say for residents or councillors on the designs of new developments below 500 properties and no ability for residents to have their say in a committee meeting.
 
Maintaining democratic oversight and transparency over managing development is essential.

records.title: Require VED Expensive Car Supplement threshold to be uprated with inflation
records.description: Require the £40,000 Vehicle Excise Duty Expensive Car Supplement (ECS) threshold to be uprated annually in line with inflation and apply the uprated threshold to hybrid as well as electric vehicles. £30–32k in 2017 is very often £40k+ today, without being higher spec or more luxurious in real terms.
records.further_details: Tax on a vehicle is based on list price, not what you actually paid. Used car prices are irrelevant under VED rules. Hybrids get no ECS threshold relief, only pure EVs see the threshold raised to £50,000 from April 2026. Hybrids stay at £40,000. The ECS ignores inflation by design, unlike standard VED rates, which rise annually with inflation. The ECS threshold is fixed unless politically changed. The 2025 budget acknowledged £40,000 was outdated for EVs, and we believe we need to see the same logic applied consistently.

records.title: Ban ROTL & early release for offences related to death of a child
records.description: We want the Government to legislate to ban the early release and Release on Temporary Licence (ROTL) of anyone convicted of child cruelty in cases where a child has died, causing or allowing the death of a child, or manslaughter where the victim is a child.
records.further_details: We believe they should not be eligible for Release on Temporary Licence (ROTL) or any early release scheme before they have served their full custodial sentence. We feel allowing offenders convicted of these offences to receive Release on Temporary Licence (ROTL) or early release can undermine public confidence in the justice system.

records.title: Fund free school meals for all children up to the age of 16
records.description: The cost of food is rising daily and many families are struggling. We believe this can be addressed by giving all children up to the age of 16 free school meals. Families will save at least £199 a year per child per year & this would help with the cost of living crisis. Help support all families!
records.further_details: After receiving a letter from the Government saying that my children no longer qualify for free school meals I’ve decided it’s time to make a change. Having free school meals would give families peace of mind that children are having a hot healthy meal.  The Government’s policy change comes into force in September 2026 and means children will only get free school meals if their parents are in receipt of universal credit, guaranteed element of pension credit or under support of Part VI of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999. Please make a change for all children.

records.title: Apply to rejoin the European Solidarity Corps programme
records.description: Apply to rejoin the European Solidarity Corps programme to offer young people access to the same opportunities to build skills, experience and employability through international volunteering projects as those enjoyed by their EU counterparts and those from associated countries such as Iceland.
records.further_details:
The European Solidarity Corps is an EU initiative that provides young people aged 18 - 30 (up to 35 in certain cases) with access to funded opportunities to either volunteer abroad, or to set up their own projects responding to societal challenges in their own local community. Young people from the UK, however, are currently missing out.
 
The funding, structure and support offered by ESC opportunities could also help make participation in any UK-EU Youth Mobility Scheme more widely accessible.

records.title: Require labelling of natural rubber latex used in food packaging
records.description: Require clear labelling where natural rubber latex is used in food packaging materials, including packaging seals and cold-seal adhesives, so consumers with severe latex allergy can make informed choices.
records.further_details: People with severe latex allergy, including anaphylaxis, currently cannot identify whether food packaging contains natural rubber latex in cold-seal adhesives or packaging seals. Clear labelling would avoid life-threatening exposure/anaphylactic reactions and allow consumers to make informed choices to prevent these outcomes. Products such as chocolates, snacks and ice creams currently use these materials without disclosure. Please help us to make a hidden risk visible before a fatality occurs.

records.title: Extend Working Time Regulations to contracted freelance workers
records.description:
Mandate that freelance contracts must abide by the following Working Time Regulations:

• Maximum of 48 hours/week
• Right to rest
records.further_details: Many industries engage freelancers for lengthy contracts of 50+ hours per week, exceeding the working time limits which standard employees have the right to. I propose that the Working Time Regulations regarding maximum weekly working time and daily/weekly rest become a statutory right for freelancers who are engaged by a company, in keeping with the need to protect the health and safety of workers. Optionally, employers may offer an opt-out for freelancers who want to work in excess of 48 hours/week as overtime.

records.title: Provide public funding for UK air ambulances
records.description: We call on the Government to provide regular public funding to air ambulances to address funding issues faced by air ambulances. At present, the only regular funding they receive is via charity donations. We believe they are a vital service.
records.further_details: There are 43 air ambulances in the UK, all managed by 21 individual charities. Each air ambulance charity typically operates around four critical care cars or rapid response vehicles. The average cost of deploying an air ambulance can be up to £4,750. They respond to an average of 137 life-saving missions per day.

records.title: Fund autism & SEND specific water safety & swimming lessons, include in EHCP
records.description: Autistic children face higher drowning risk, yet no requirement for adapted swimming lessons/water safety training. We ask the Government to review this risk, and to fund autism and SEND adapted lessons with trained instructors and to include water safety in Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs).
records.further_details: I know personally how vital water safety is. Autistic children are several times more likely to drown, yet there are no autism adapted swimming lessons in many areas. I’m calling for mandatory SEND friendly water safety training in every area across the UK to prevent avoidable deaths.

records.title: Evacuate 50 Gazan children with complex trauma injuries to the UK
records.description: Nearly 4,000 children are in need of medical evacuation from Gaza. We are asking only for 50 children with life-threatening conditions to be medically evacuated to the UK for medical treatment.
records.further_details: We ask the UK Government to organise the medical evacuation of 50 children to the UK for treatment. They could be spread evenly through the regional major trauma centres, so no one area is not overburdened. Children with life threatening trauma injuries or health conditions such as acute renal failure which Gaza does not have the staff or facilities to treat should be prioritised.  There are insufficient health staff in Gaza, with around 1,722 health workers reported to have been killed.

records.title: Make St George’s Day a national bank holiday in England every year
records.description: Make St George’s Day (23 April) a national bank holiday in England each year, recognising England’s patron saint and bringing England in line with other UK nations that already have national day public holidays.
records.further_details: England has fewer bank holidays than Scotland and Northern Ireland, which recognise St Andrew’s Day and St Patrick’s Day. Creating a St George’s Day holiday would bring England in line with the rest of the UK, celebrate national identity and culture, and support tourism, community events and local economies. It would also help address the UK’s relatively low number of public holidays compared to many European countries.

records.title: Introduce Albanian GCSE and A-levels
records.description: We ask the Government to introduce GCSE and A-Level qualifications in the Albanian language. Many children attend Albanian supplementary schools and would benefit from a nationally recognised qualification in their mother tongue.
records.further_details: Community-led Albanian language schools across the UK have demonstrated sustained student participation and strong educational outcomes. Introducing GCSE and A-Level Albanian would promote equality of opportunity, support bilingualism, preserve cultural heritage, and recognise the contribution of the Albanian-speaking community to British society.

records.title: Allow people with Coeliac Disease into the UK Armed Forces
records.description: Anyone suffering with a gluten intolerance cannot join the UK armed forces. However, the Army, Royal Navy and RAF cater for those requiring Halal, Kosher and Vegetarian meals. We see this as discrimination against those with a food intolerance which can be managed and not life threatening.
records.further_details: Allow sufferers of coeliac disease to join any of the UK forces PROVIDING they sign a disclaimer in the event they may suffer symptoms.

records.title: Declare a one-off bank holiday if England win the World Cup
records.description: We call on the Government to declare a one-off national bank holiday on the Monday immediately following the World Cup Final, should the England Men’s Football Team win the tournament.
records.further_details:
Justification / Why it matters:
Winning the World Cup would be a historic, once-in-a-generation sporting achievement for the nation. A victory of this scale deserves a moment of national celebration, bringing communities together and boosting morale across the country.

Furthermore, a significant portion of the population will be staying up late to watch and celebrate the final. Declaring the following Monday a bank holiday would allow the public to celebrate safely, and support local businesses.

records.title: Publish a national food emergency plan and assess strategic food reserves
records.description: We want the Government to establish and publish a national food emergency plan for major or prolonged disruption to UK food supplies, and to assess the case for maintaining strategic reserves of essential foods.
records.further_details:
The UK food system relies on domestic production and complex international supply chains that can be disrupted by extreme weather, conflict, trade or energy shortages and other emergencies.

We want the Government to assess how essential food supplies would be maintained during a prolonged disruption, identify critical vulnerabilities, consider whether strategic reserves of staple foods would improve resilience, and explain how essential food would be distributed fairly, particularly to vulnerable people.

This is about preparedness, not predicting shortages.

records.title: Review ADHD and Autism Assessments to Better Recognise Women and Girls
records.description: Review ADHD and autism assessments for women & girls. We believe many tools are based on decades-old research, largely focused on male presentations. Assessments should reflect modern life, current neurodiversity research, masking & how ADHD and autism present differently in women and girls.
records.further_details: We call on the Government to review how ADHD and autism are assessed. The evidence base has historically focused heavily on boys & men, with autism research dating back to the 1940s. Although our understanding has developed, some assessment approaches may still overlook people who mask or camouflage their difficulties. Assessments should reflect current research, modern life & different presentations, including how ADHD & autism may be missed in women and girls.

records.title: Review handling of complaints by public bodies and their transparency levels
records.description: We call on the UK Government to thoroughly review complaint-handling practices within public bodies and introduce stronger enforceable safeguards to ensure transparency, accountability, and proper record-keeping.
records.further_details:
I am deeply concerned to have identified what seems to me to be a persistent and recurring pattern across multiple government bodies, including the Child Maintenance Service (CMS), Independent Case Examiner (ICE), and Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO), where:
 
Legitimate concerns are not properly addressed
Accountability is repeatedly avoided
Complaints go missing
Complaints are closed without notification
Evidence is not properly retained
Records and notes appear to be amended

records.title: Ban fires, BBQs & sky lanterns in England’s countryside & wild spaces year round
records.description: Create offences, punishable by substantial fines, for using open fires, portable barbecues or sky lanterns on or beside forests, woodland, moorland, heathland, peatland, grassland, sand dunes, nature reserves or agricultural land.
records.further_details: Hotter, drier conditions mean a flame or ember can ignite vegetation and cause a wildfire. These fires kill and displace wildlife, destroy nests, food and shelter, damage peat and soils, and erase habitats that take decades or longer to recover; some populations may never return. Guidance and signs are not enough. Exemptions should apply only to lawful land management and authorised sites with fire-resistant surfaces, fire-control equipment and complete extinguishment.

records.title: Review & strengthen sentencing for the most serious crimes against children
records.description: We ask the Government to launch a fundamental review into sentencing, bail and public protection for the most serious offences against children, including child murder, rape, sexual assault and organised child sexual exploitation.
records.further_details: The review should consider the following reforms: whole life orders for the most serious offences against children, introducing stricter bail and remand when there is a risk of reoffending, no early release, increasing sentencing for organised child sexual exploitation, deporting eligible foreign-national offenders guilty of these crimes and ensuring they do not evade sentencing, and considering capital punishment for the most serious crimes against children.

records.title: Fund and Improve Mental Health Service transition into the Community
records.description: Fund an improved mental health service enabling a seamless transition from acute crisis care (Home Treatment/Rapid Response) and community support. Establish a statutory "Continuity of Care" guarantee with a safety/care plan before a patient is discharged from intensive services.
records.further_details: With the additional funding, government should mandate that every mental health services user has a single point of contact responsible for coordinating referrals and responding to clinical deterioration. We believe the GP and 111 route to get help currently lead to a "black hole" in community care, and patients waiting for months to receive a risk assessment, and are only able to access online group sessions, regardless of their condition or state of deterioration as a result. Consistent and individualised support should be funded and prioritised.

records.title: Make students studying less than 35 hours a week eligible for carers allowance
records.description: The DWP states that anybody in “full time” education, even if they only attend classes 2-3 days a week, is not eligible to receive carer's allowance. We believe this is unsustainable. Anyone attending classes for less than 35 hours a week (equivalent to a full-time job) should be eligible.
records.further_details: Evidence shows young adult carers are 3x more likely to be out of education, employment, and training. Anyone making more than £204, or studying more than 21 hours per week, loses their carer's allowance, so the stats make sense. People should not have to choose between investing in their future and financial support. If I attend uni for 21 hours a week, I'd still care for my family member for more than 35 hours a week. It punishes people who still do care work for trying to improve their lives.

records.title: Prohibit restaurants from including tips on bills
records.description: Prohibit restaurants adding tips or “service charges” to bills, even if they are optional.
records.further_details: Restaurants are increasingly adding tips as service charges to bills. Although it is still often optional, many customers find it difficult asking for the charge to be removed. We believe this is an American culture that has no place in the UK.

records.title: Review current sentencing guidelines and immigration laws
records.description: Review sentencing guidelines and immigration laws to ensure the victims’ role in sentencing is strengthened & sentences given based on crime committed and not personal background. We want the Government to ensure serious foreign offenders are able to be deported promptly after serving their sentence
records.further_details: We believe that many people have lost confidence in the justice system due to inconsistent sentencing and lengthy deportation delays caused by repeated appeals. In our view victims often feel ignored while offenders’ circumstances are prioritised. Justice must be fair, transparent, and focused on those harmed by crime. Stronger, clearer rules could restore public trust and improve public safety.

records.title: Introduce a Mental Health Duty Law
records.description: Introduce a Mental Health Duty requiring institutions with power over people's lives such as workplaces, schools, healthcare, housing, justice & public services to proactively protect mental health. Require inspections, ratings & real consequences for non-compliance. Don't wait for people to break.
records.further_details: We believe UK law on mental health is reactive and institutions only act once someone discloses, suffers, or reaches crisis. Mental ill health costs the UK £300bn a year. 1 in 5 children has a mental health condition. We feel the Mental Health Act 2025 reformed how the state treats people in crisis but did nothing to prevent it. A Mental Health Duty would require workplaces, schools, healthcare, housing, justice and public services to proactively protect mental health. Prevention could save £5–£99 per £1 spent.

records.title: Fund ADHD/Autism Burnout Support in all GP Surgeries Before and After Diagnosis
records.description: Fund support for ADHD and autistic burnout so it’s available through GP surgeries for people both before and after diagnosis. Many people struggle to understand and manage their symptoms, including overwhelm, exhaustion, brain fog, emotional difficulties, and loss of everyday functioning.
records.further_details: GPs cannot diagnose ADHD or autism. Many people may be left without sufficient support while waiting for specialist assessments or treatment. We believe trained support is needed to help people manage symptoms before they reach crisis point.

records.title: Remove the need for planning permission for external shutters on properties
records.description: If residential properties could install wooden external shutters covering windows and doors, without planning permission, it would remove the need for expensive aircon units, cooling houses in heat waves but also help warm houses in the winter.

records.title: Introduce mandatory extreme-weather safety protections for delivery workers
records.description: Introduce mandatory national extreme-weather safety standards for delivery workers, including severe-weather risk assessments, temperature monitoring inside delivery vehicles, reduced workloads and clear rules to modify or suspend outdoor deliveries when conditions become unsafe.
records.further_details: Delivery workers spend hours outdoors in extreme weather, often using vans without effective air conditioning. Currently protections can vary between workplaces. We want one clear national standard that measures actual working conditions, including temperatures inside vans, and puts safety before delivery targets.

records.title: Provide Government funding, resource grant & guidance for home-schooled children
records.description: We are asking for the government to introduce financial and resource grants for families who choose elective home education for their children. Currently, many parents do not have support, nor direction on where to start with home-schooling alongside carrying the full financial burden.
records.further_details:
Parents who elect to home school their children for a variety of reasons i.e. SEND needs, anxiety or just because they know the classroom environment is not suitable for their child. They may not have support for resources, a guidance of coverage nor support for the funding of this.
 
We are asking the government to bridge this gap and provide financial support and guidance to support the rising costs of essential resources, curriculum materials, exam fees and extra curricula activities.

records.title: Cap tuition fees at £3000 retrospectively & write off the resulting student debt
records.description: We want the Government to retroactively cap tuition fees at £3,000 for all Plan 2 loans and Plan 5 loans. We call for all balances to be recalculated to this level, with the excess principal and all associated interest cancelled to restore financial fairness to an entire generation.
records.further_details: In our view, fees of £9k+ created a 'debt trap.' With fees rising to £9,790 in 2026 and repayment thresholds frozen until 2030, we believe this has become a lifelong stealth tax. We think this debt prevents home ownership and damages mental health. We call on the Government to correct this injustice, and think that recalculating debt to the £3k level provides a fairer start for graduates and addresses the sustainability crisis in higher education funding.

records.title: Require NHS hospitals to provide discharge support for sepsis survivors
records.description: We want the Government to require NHS hospitals to provide mandatory, standardised discharge support for patients recovering from sepsis, including written information, follow-up guidance, red flags for post-sepsis syndrome and access to rehabilitation and mental health support services.
records.further_details: Many people discharged after sepsis leave hospital without clear information about recovery, possible long-term complications or where to seek help for ongoing physical weakness, fatigue, trauma, anxiety, cognitive difficulties and other symptoms that can last months or years. We believe every sepsis survivor should receive a discharge information pack containing information about Post-Sepsis Syndrome, recovery guidance, signposting to charities, peer support and complementary support services.

records.title: Review security protocols for keeping deceased patient records confidential
records.description: We call on the Government to conduct a review of all NHS trusts and how they ensure deceased patient records are kept confidential. We suggest that such a review should consider the merits of requiring pre-authorisation to access patient records, removing routine staff access.
records.further_details: We are concerned that several recent cases of staff accessing patient records for unlawful and illegitimate reasons suggest that there are not sufficient protocols or safeguards in place. We therefore call for a review of practices, which could consider pre-authorisation requirements to access patient records, and a single national standard across NHS trusts which could ensure that patient records are kept confidential and accessed only by those with a legitimate need to do so. We think this is crucial to protect the dignity of the deceased patients and their families.

records.title: Extend the Skilled Worker visa grace period from 60 days to 12 months
records.description: The 60-day grace period can be too short to find new sponsored work. Recruitment and sponsorship often take months, some employers may wait until after probation. Extending it to 12 months could reduce hardship, protect children's education and help retain skilled workers who contribute to the UK
records.further_details: We urge the Home Office to extend the 60-day grace period for sponsored workers who lose their jobs to 12 months. Losing employment already brings significant emotional, mental, and physical stress, but the short timeframe creates further fear of losing homes, stability, and the lives families have built in the UK. A 12-month period could give people a realistic chance to find new sponsorship, protect children’s education, and allow skilled workers to continue contributing to the country.

records.title: Establish a National Freshwater Resilience and Stewardship Strategy
records.description: Establish a National Freshwater Stewardship and Resilience Strategy including an independent review of water governance, use, allocation, storage and major water users; independent regional catchment networks; and a Citizens' Assembly to support immediate actions and shape long term reforms.
records.further_details: Hosepipe bans and household water saving campaigns alone are no longer enough. Freshwater is a finite strategic national asset. We need a whole systems approach to water planning that improves drought, flood and wildfire resilience, strengthens food systems and restores biodiversity, while ensuring major water users are accountable and freshwater is managed in the public interest through stronger governance, national leadership, local stewardship and long term planning for future generations.

records.title: Fund free sanitary products for female pupils & endometriosis support
records.description: We urge the Government to increase funding for schools to provide free sanitary products for female pupils, so they can continue to attend school and receive an education, and dedicated funding to support pupils suffering from endometriosis, so they have appropriate support.
records.further_details:
In many areas, families may not be able to afford period products for their female family members. When this happens, girls may miss out on vital parts of their education and fall behind. We urge the Government to provide schools with appropriate funding to provide these products for free so girls can still attend schools.
 
We urge the Government to support young women and children suffering from endometriosis, a very painful condition, to ensure a good quality of life for them.

records.title: Ban the removal or felling of ancient trees
records.description: We would like the Government to ban the removal or felling of all ancient trees. We believe these trees are valuable and precious and we need them now and for future generations. Therefore, they should have full legal protections.
records.further_details: We call for the Government to protect all ancient trees on all categories of land as we believe we cannot afford to lose them. Under new rules, these trees would be protected from felling or removal for the rest of their lives. We are particularly concerned about protecting ancient oak trees.

records.title: Require medicinal (pill) packet producers to provide a recycling scheme for them
records.description: The recycling of medicinal (pill) packets is costly and difficult to do due to their composition.  If the manufacturers of pill packets were made responsible for recycling used packets, there would be a greater chance of less impact on the environment and/or more sustainable packaging being used.
records.further_details: Councils across England cannot afford to recycle medicinal (pill) packets due to their composition making the process very costly.  Direction from the UK Government to producers of the packaging to either create recycling facilities for the used packets themselves or use more sustainable materials will have a positive impact on our environment.

records.title: Set Up Statutory Independent Advocates for Bereaved Families Of Homicide Victims
records.description: Create a statutory right for families of homicide victims to have a state-funded Independent Advocate. They must be independent of police and legally empowered to act as a proxy for complex administration, including CICA claims and IOPC proceedings.
records.further_details: Families bereaved by homicide face profound trauma but must often navigate complex systems alone. Police FLOs and charities offer support, but cannot act as legally empowered proxies. We feel that grieving families are too often forced to act as legal experts— battling the IOPC for transparency and managing invasive CICA paperwork. We believe that grief should not be compounded by administrative exhaustion. We want this new statutory right to be known as James’s Law – to  provide an independent advocate to ensure no family fights these bureaucratic systems alone.

records.title: Amend adoption/kinship care laws to protect privacy rights of adult adoptees
records.description: Amend the Children Act 1989 and adoption guidance to explicitly state that local authorities cannot contact or assess an adopted person to act as a kinship carer for a biological sibling they have no prior relationship with unless the adoptee has explicitly opted into a contact register.
records.further_details: An adoption order legally cuts ties with the birth family. However, local authorities can still track down adult adoptees to take responsibility for new biological siblings they have never met. We believe this breaches the adoptee's right to move on with their life, creates intense emotional guilt, and compromises their right to privacy under the guise of family finding. For many families this can cause severe upset and turmoil. We believe we are not legally or morally Kin and therefore should not be considered so.

records.title: Mandatory safeguarding alerts for repeat injuries in children under 10
records.description: Government to mandate an NHS-wide alert if a child under 10 presents twice in 12 months with suspicious or non-age-appropriate injuries. This alert should trigger an immediate independent skin check and the alert should remain visible to all GPs and hospitals, regardless of where the child is seen.
records.further_details: When the "rule of two" (when a child has presented with suspicious injuries twice in 12 months) is breached, we request that relevant social workers and agencies are granted secure, shared access to these records to ensure a unified safeguarding response. We must prevent children from falling through gaps by ensuring all professionals have the same information.

records.title: Ban single-strike animal slaughter
records.description: We ask the Government to prohibit the single-strike slaughter method, regardless of stunning, and ensure legislation explicitly prevents its use in commercial slaughter.
records.further_details:
The method involves pre-stunning an animal followed by removal of its head in a single stroke.
 
We are concerned about the welfare implications of this method, including animal handling, restraint and the killing process. We ask the Government to prohibit single-strike slaughter, including where pre-stunning is used, and ensure that animal welfare legislation applies consistently to all slaughter methods, regardless of religious purpose.

records.title: Repeal the Online Safety Act and fund the enforcement of preexisting laws
records.description: Repeal the Online Safety Act and fund stronger enforcement of existing criminal, advertising, consumer protection, and data protection laws targeting harmful content, profiling, and algorithmic amplification.
records.further_details: We believe that many online harms are already illegal under criminal, advertising, consumer protection, and data protection laws. We also think that the profiling and recommendation systems amplifying harmful content could also be regulated under UK GDPR. We feel that under ECHR Articles 8 and 10, restrictions affecting privacy and expression should only be used where less intrusive alternatives are insufficient. We are concerned that it has not been clearly shown why stronger enforcement of existing laws is insufficient first.

records.title: Create a government body dedicated to safeguarding parental rights
records.description: Create a new government body which helps safeguard parental rights, including helping fathers, some of whom are paying child maintenance, to see their children.
records.further_details:
We want this government body to help any parent to see their children if they have been unlawfully prevented from seeing their children. We feel there is not enough support for fathers in helping them see their children. 
 
We believe the current system results in parents having to go to solicitors and pay thousands of pounds to be able to see their children, which we feel is very unfair.

records.title: Require over 65s to retake the hazard perception test every five years
records.description: I would ask the UK Government to require driving license holders, upon reaching 65 years old, to retake the hazard perception section of the driving theory test. They would then continue to be re-tested every 5 years.
records.further_details:
Some previous proposals can be seen as a bit much, and slightly discriminatory. However, the hazard perception section of the driving theory test is the best and most simple way to ascertain if a driver should be on the road. 

If someone is incapable of reacting to hazards on the road, they are a danger to everyone, from drivers to cyclists and pedestrians. I believe this simple change would have a larger impact on the safety of all of us. Thank you for reading this.

records.title: Require telecom providers to verify caller ID and block spoofed UK phone numbers
records.description: Require all UK telecom providers to implement network-level caller ID authentication across mobile, landline and VoIP services, and to block calls where a displayed UK number is identified as spoofed. Ofcom should establish and enforce a common verification standard.
records.further_details: Scammers can manipulate caller ID so calls appear to come from legitimate UK mobile or landline numbers. This makes blocking and reporting individual numbers ineffective, as criminals can simply display another number. Existing measures do not prevent all spoofed calls. A consistent verification system across UK networks would help stop fraudulent calls before they reach consumers, while allowing legitimate calls from businesses, hospitals and other genuine callers to continue.

records.title: Demand financial compensation from the US & Israel for damage to our economy
records.description: The US and Israel attacked Iran while US-Iranian negotiations were ongoing. We believe this war of aggression has had widespread global consequences, increased the cost of fuel, and places our economy, security, and way of life at risk. We require compensation for these effects on our country.
records.further_details:
In our view, America and Israel's war on Iran risks:
 
- causing steep increases in the price of food and utilities
- precipitating a UK recession and causing economic hardship for millions
- making foreign travel more expensive or difficult (not least due to a potential shortage of jet fuel)
- increasing Islamophobia and antisemitism by further polarising communities
- increasing the risk of Britain becoming involved in a major global conflict that places our infrastructure and country at risk

records.title: Require the NHS to offer full body (head to toe) MRI scans for cancer patients
records.description: My dad developed kidney cancer during lockdown. After having his left kidney removed, we were told that chemotherapy wouldn’t be needed because the cancer was to be gone with the kidney. Just a few weeks later, nodules were found on his lungs. He collapsed and we found it had spread to the brain.
records.further_details: I want to try and implement that all cancer or potential cancer patients are offered a 3 monthly MRI that covers head to toe. At the moment they usually do from neck down or just wherever the cancer is. If my dad had undergone a head to toe MRI his brain tumour could have been picked up early enough to be able to have treatment. I don't want other families go through what we had to. From the day we found out there was nothing else that could be done we only had 3 weeks with him.

records.title: Ban MPs & Ministers from using a 'disappearing message' function on work phones
records.description: In order for complete transparency to the UK taxpayer, and to speed up any possible future police enquiries, all MPs' and Ministers' work phones & other devices should not be allowed to have the 'disappearing messages' feature.
records.further_details: The taxpayer deserves to be able to hold MPs and Ministers accountable for their actions.

records.title: Urgently ban the import and sale of foie gras and fur products in the UK
records.description: Ban the import and sale of foie gras and fur products. The production of foie gras and fur products is already banned due to animal welfare concerns, but imports remain legal.
records.further_details:
We believe that the Government should close this loophole which we think undermines current UK animal welfare legislation and align import rules with UK standards.

Foie gras production involves repeatedly force-feeding birds to enlarge their livers beyond natural limits, causing pain and serious health problems. Fur farming confines animals such as foxes and mink in small wire which can lead to stress, injury and poor welfare.

These practices are banned in the UK, yet products are still imported and sold. In our view this undermines UK animal welfare laws and supports practices it has already deemed unacceptable. We call on the Government to act to ensure UK standards are upheld.

records.title: Abolish Stamp Duty Land Tax on residential properties
records.description: House prices have significantly outpaced wages for decades and higher mortgage costs have reduced affordability. We believe Stamp Duty places an unfair financial burden on home buyers and increases the cost of buying a home, so it should be abolished.
records.further_details: Stamp Duty can add thousands of pounds to the cost of buying a home, making it more difficult for first-time buyers and existing homeowners to move. It can discourage people from relocating to meet their changing needs, for example families needing to upsize their homes or older people wishing to downsize. Abolishing this additional fee would encourage greater movement within the housing market and reduce barriers to home ownership.

records.title: Make all UK Government websites free to access without mobile data charges
records.description: Require mobile network operators to zero-rate all UK Government websites and online services, so they never use a person’s data allowance or require paid data. The Government should work with Ofcom and operators, cover delivery costs and include linked content needed to complete a service.
records.further_details: People should not have to pay for mobile data to claim benefits, use health services, find safety advice, apply for work or understand their rights. Ofcom estimates that 3.8% of UK adults rely on mobile data alone and 0.9% rely only on external connections. New Zealand’s Zero Data service shows a practical model: participating networks provide free access to government sites, with sponsoring agencies covering the data cost. Public services should be free at the point of access.

records.title: Disability Confident must prove outcomes or employers lose the badge
records.description: Require an independent audit of disabled workforce representation, retention, and progression as a condition of retaining Disability Confident accreditation, with status revoked where unmet. Require DWP to report audit outcomes to Parliament. Embed both in the Disability Confident scheme overhaul.
records.further_details:
The Government's Reform Delivery Plan (2025 to 2026) concedes the Disability Confident scheme has lacked accountability, transparency, and measurable outcomes. The badge carries reputational value with no obligation to prove it is earned.

There should be an independent audit of Disability Confident employers, with status revoked where conditions are not met.  The audit should be a part of the scheme overhaul. The Government should propagate representation of disabled people in the workforce.

records.title: Introduce a Statutory Right to Independent Legal Review for Bereaved Families
records.description: Grant bereaved families the right to an independent judicial review of police and CPS actions following a homicide acquittal. This must apply when clear CCTV evidence exists, forcing a public report detailing why the prosecution failed, ensuring any systemic flaws are exposed.
records.further_details: When a jury acquits defendants in a homicide trial despite what many view as undeniable, objective evidence—like CCTV of a fatal hit-and-run or a victim's ignored pleas for help—bereaved families have no legal recourse. We are concerned that current laws treat acquittals as final, even if police or the CPS failed catastrophically. We demand a statutory right to an independent review of authorities' case handling when acquittals contradict clear evidence. This could force transparency and accountability for miscarriages of justice.

records.title: Legislate to give funeral processions legal right of way
records.description: Amend the Road Traffic Act 1988 to protect funeral corteges. Make it an offence to cut into a procession or overtake it in built-up areas, and require drivers to give right of way at roundabouts and junctions to corteges if safe to do so and to advise them refrain from overtaking.
records.further_details: Disrupting corteges often causes distress to grieving families and can create a severe physical danger for funeral directors paging (walking) in front of the hearse. All emergency service vehicles should continue to have priority. We believe laws are needed to ensure the safety and dignity of the funeral staff and the families.

records.title: Ban Fake Grass to Save Our Environment
records.description: We call on the government to ban the sale, import & installation of artificial grass for domestic & commercial landscaping.Natural, living gardens are essential infrastructure for climate resilience, well-being & wildlife conservation.We urge legislative action to stop the affect on our environment.
records.further_details: Fake grass harms the environment by blocking wildlife habitats, radiating intense heat, and shedding plastic pollution. Its overall impact involves destroying soil life, trapping high temperatures, and creating permanent landfill waste in addition to the damage to our wildlife.If we don't do something now, what is going to become of our environment? Our children are going to lose out on our beautiful countryside & animals if we don't act now.

records.title: Ban industrial developments being built next to any residential housing estates
records.description: We call on the Government to amend planning policy to prevent B8 warehouses and any industrial developments being built next to residential housing estates. Mandatory buffer zones should be established to protect residents from noise, traffic, pollution, flooding & loss of residential amenities.
records.further_details: Large industrial estates approved before nearby housing is built, may attract few objections as future residents are not living there yet. Phased warehouse building can make cumulative impacts difficult to assess or object to. These industrial developments can bring 24/7 noise, HGV traffic, light pollution, flood risk and visual intrusion. Similar concerns have arisen in Corby and Tyldesley, while proposals at Bingham 46 and Towcester Park, we believe, risk repeating these issues.

records.title: Make coercive control in under-16s relationships a criminal offence
records.description: Amend the Serious Crime Act 2015 so controlling or coercive behaviour in intimate relationships between under-16s is a criminal offence. Current law only applies where both parties are 16 or over, which can leave younger victims without protection.
records.further_details: Children under 16 can experience serious patterns of control, manipulation and abuse within relationships, yet current law does not allow this to be prosecuted as coercive control. We believe this creates a gap where harmful behaviour is recognised but not chargeable. Extending the law could ensure younger victims are protected and abusive behaviour in teenage relationships is properly addressed.

records.title: Allow self-employed single parents to claim childcare as business expense
records.description: Amend HMRC rules to allow self-employed single parents and self-employed households to deduct registered childcare and holiday club costs as an allowable business expense on their Self Assessment tax returns.
records.further_details: We believe HMRC rules penalise self-employed single parents ineligible for Universal Credit. Disallowing childcare as a business deduction can result in a double penalty during school holidays: parents may have to stop trading or pay holiday club fees from taxed net profits. Corporations can claim workplace childcare as a tax-deductible staff cost. Without childcare, self-employed parents may be unable to operate.  We feel childcare is an operational necessity, not a luxury. It should be an allowable business expense to ensure tax fairness.

records.title: Ban the sale of unvalidated food intolerance tests in the UK
records.description: Require food intolerance and sensitivity tests sold in the UK to have robust scientific evidence demonstrating their diagnostic validity. Tests that cannot demonstrate they reliably identify the food intolerances or sensitivities they claim to detect should not be sold or marketed for this purpose.
records.further_details: I regularly meet people who have spent hundreds of pounds on what I believe are unvalidated food intolerance tests, leading to unnecessary dietary restriction, food anxiety and risk of nutritional deficiencies. The BDA states that IgG testing is not reliable for diagnosing food intolerance and that hair analysis has no scientific basis. I believe consumers should be protected from tests that claim to identify food intolerances without robust scientific validation.

records.title: Ban chemical flame retardants in UK furniture to align with EU standards
records.description: Ban chemical flame retardant in UK furniture which may cause harm. Studies link such chemicals to cancer & other serious health risks. UK rules expose households to potentially higher levels than the EU. Reform fire safety laws to eliminate unnecessary toxic exposure in homes & protect public health
records.further_details: UK furniture contains very high levels of flame retardant chemicals due to current fire safety rules. Some of these chemicals have been linked to cancer, hormone disruption and developmental issues, and they can accumulate in household dust where families and children are exposed daily. We believe the EU achieves high levels of fire safety without using many of these chemicals, proving they are unnecessary. The UK should prioritise public health and urgently reform these regulations.

records.title: Allow under-25s to undergo cervical screening on request
records.description: I believe individuals should have the ability to discuss their concerns with a healthcare professional and make an informed choice about whether screening is right for them, rather than being restricted solely by age. Due to me losing my dad to cancer I'm extremely scared of getting cancer.
records.further_details: Living with anxiety means these thoughts can become overwhelming, and the uncertainty can be difficult to manage. As a parent, this fear is even more significant—I worry about the impact on my child if something were to happen to me. Having the option to access cervical screening before the age of 25 would provide reassurance and could have a meaningful positive impact on mental wellbeing for people in similar situations.

records.title: Extend UK Ancestry Visa to include Mauritius and former British territories
records.description: Currently the UK Ancestry Visa is only for those with grandparents born in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man. We ask the Government to extend it to also include grandparents born in former British territories including Mauritius, which was a colony until 1968.
records.further_details: We believe that this inclusion was considered by the Government, but discarded without any clear reason or explanation given. Mauritius was a British Colony until 1968, so those born there during that period have direct historical, legal and family ties to the UK. In our view, extending eligibility recognises our shared heritage, treats Commonwealth citizens equally and fairly, and lets eligible people live, work, pay taxes and contribute positively to the UK economy and society.

records.title: Review the social impact of the reduction of voluntary sector funding
records.description: Instruct an independent review into the extent of dwindling funds made available to voluntary sector organisations, and the social impact of this in the next 2-5 years.
records.further_details:
We believe the voluntary sector has been propping up the state. Whether it is food banks, lunch clubs, sports facilities, community spaces or other things, the UK should be proud of its voluntary sector and the role it plays in flourishing society.

However, the sources of underpinning funding for these activities are diminishing. This might be because economic circumstances have devalued grant making trusts, or government funding cuts.

We want this risk to be noticed and accounted for transparently.

records.title: Require parties to reimburse by-election costs caused by voluntary resignations
records.description: We want the Government to require political parties to reimburse any taxpayer-funded costs associated with by-elections caused by one of their elected representatives voluntarily resigning within 12 months of taking office or resigning early in their tenure to contest another elected position.
records.further_details:
We believe taxpayers should not bear the financial cost of by-elections caused by elected representatives voluntarily resigning for reasons that we feel are foreseeable and within their control, such as accepting nomination for another elected office, political strategy, or deciding not to continue in a role they recently sought and accepted.
 
The requirement should apply only to avoidable voluntary resignations. It should not apply where a resignation results from circumstances outside the elected representative's control, such as serious illness, the death or serious illness of a close family member, bereavement, caring responsibilities arising unexpectedly, or other exceptional circumstances.

records.title: Mandate Installation of Changing Places facilities in all Public Buildings
records.description: Make Changing Places standard facilities mandatory in public buildings so no child has to be changed on toilet floors or excluded from everyday life.
records.further_details: Older disabled children are often still being changed on toilet floors, in car boots or kept at home because most public buildings don’t provide adequate facilities. We feel this is discrimination and it can often isolate families. We believe Changing Places standard rooms are essential for dignity, hygiene and inclusion: every child deserves equal access to public life without shame, barriers or being treated as an afterthought.

records.title: Set minimum safety measures for health & social care workers in the community
records.description: Surveys reveal that nearly half of social workers face verbal abuse, & up to 25% are threatened with physical violence during their careers. I want the Government to consider mandating minimum protective measures for social workers similar to those for the police and other emergency workers.
records.further_details: Yesterday, my car was attacked and I was threatened by a family. I wish this was the first time that this happened in my career but it is not. Several times in my 8 year career, I have feared for my safety. Social Workers can have the hardest conversations with families and this can cause a reaction that is aggressive and threatening. All we have to protect ourselves is our lanyard. I am asking for the same protective measures as the police. I believe we need GPS trackers, body-worn cameras and a panic alarm.

records.title: Require & Fund Air Conditioning in all early years settings
records.description: Require all nurseries and early years settings to maintain temperatures below a safe specified temperature for children with funding for effective cooling systems where needed. As heatwaves become more common, no baby or young child or staff caring for them should be exposed to unsafe indoor heat.
records.further_details: Nurseries and early years settings should be required maintain temperatures below a safe specified temperature for children with funding for effective cooling systems where needed, as children and babies are more vulnerable to heat-related illness than adults. The Government should provide funding for cooling measures such as air conditioning where needed, and ensure all nurseries offer a safe, healthy environment for children to learn, play and rest.

records.title: Give State Pension to all at 60 and increase it to equal 48hrs of Living Wage.
records.description: We want the Government to make the State Pension available from age 60 & increase it to equal 48hrs a week at the National Living Wage. Hence from April 2026 a Universal State Pension should be £610.08 per week or about £31,724.16 per year as a right to all including expatriates, age 60 and above.
records.further_details: We think that Government policy seems intent on the State Pension being a benefit not paid to all, while ever increasing the age of entitlement. We want reforms to the State Pension, so that it is available to all including expatriates, from age 60, and linked to the National Living Wage, for security.

records.title: Make Tragedy Chanting and associated online content a specific criminal offence
records.description: Make Tragedy Chanting a specific criminal offence in arenas, stadiums and public places. It should also be a specific criminal offence to post videos, images or text mocking tragedies online. Give the police and CPS the powers needed to prosecute this vile behaviour.
records.further_details: It's not okay in society, so why is it okay when wearing a football shirt or online. The mocking of death, or Tragedy Chanting, can contribute to the deaths of survivors of disasters. No survivor of any disaster should ever have their trauma weaponised against them. I am a Hillsborough survivor, nearly driven to suicide by comments made by strangers online, and those close to me. It is not acceptable.

records.title: Publish a new Autism Strategy under the Autism Act & help improve autistic lives
records.description: Urgently publish an updated Autism Strategy for England. The previous strategy expired in July 2026, leaving the Government open to claims that it is in breach of the Autism Act 2009. The new strategy must be created in collaboration with diverse autistic voices to fix failing autism services.
records.further_details:
The Autism Act 2009 required the Government to publish a national strategy to improve support and outcomes for autistic people. However, the last strategy expired in July 2026 without a replacement, leaving a gap in the provision of a strategy envisioned under the law.

As per the House of Lords "Time to deliver" report, Autistic people continue to face severe inequalities across public services and healthcare. Without an up-to-date strategy, support systems will continue to fail and autistic lives remain at risk. Action is needed now to uphold the rights of Autistic people in line with the Autism Act 2009.

records.title: Make breakdown cover compulsory for all drivers
records.description: Make it a legal requirement for all drivers to have breakdown cover, particularly when driving on motorways and other high-speed roads, to reduce the number of deaths and serious injuries on hard shoulders and at the roadside.
records.further_details:
My grandson Harrison was tragically killed on the hard shoulder after breaking down and trying to change a tyre. He was hit by a driver, and the devastation to our family has been unbearable. Harrison was 26 and an experienced driver, showing this danger can affect everyone. 
 
If breakdown cover was compulsory, drivers could call for help instead of risking their lives at the roadside. This could save lives, reduce accidents, and help protect the public and emergency services. We ask for this change in Harrison’s memory.

records.title: Simplify tax compliance for sole traders and micro businesses
records.description: Introduce a simplified tax compliance system for sole traders and micro businesses, reduce bookkeeping and reporting requirements, and provide tax relief or allowances for mandatory compliance costs so civic duties remain proportionate and do not impose excessive unpaid administrative labour +costs.
records.further_details: Sole traders are forced to carry out unpaid tax compliance labour, absorb bookkeeping, software + reporting costs purely so HMRC can collect tax. It shifts government administrative burden onto individuals, reduces productive earning time, reduces real earnings below minimum wage. We believe the burden is regressive, hitting small businesses disproportionately as well as disabled self employed people with executive function difficulties. Civic duties shouldn't be disproportionate it harms business growth.

records.title: Mandate public consultation before privatising NHS services
records.description: The Government should make it mandatory to hold public consultations before any NHS services are privatised. Bring Public awareness to the forefront of decisions that will affect them directly and the fragmentation of our NHS services and the problems this causes.
records.further_details: Some NHS services are privatising their IT services this summer WITHOUT consulting the service users or going out to tender. We want mandatory public consultations and media coverage before making these important decisions. Many of the public have no understanding or any influence of how this affects them long term using the NHS.

records.title: Fund new roundabout signage that clearly maps lane routes
records.description: Introduce Australian-style roundabout signage to clearly map lane routes in advance for drivers approaching a roundabout. Conduct trials and allow these kinds of diagrams.
records.further_details:
We think this could reduce driver hesitation, sudden lane cutting, and accidents on roundabouts.
 
Current roundabout signs often only show exits, which can often leave drivers guessing at which lane to use until they are already at the junction or on the roundabout. This can cause confusion, congestion, and dangerous last-minute lane changes, especially on complex or unfamiliar multi-lane roundabouts.
 
We think Australian signs can solve this problem by showing the lanes on the diagram as well as the exits the lane routes correspond with.
 
This simple change could make our roads safer and less stressful.

records.title: Mandate bold, English allergen labelling on cosmetic and household care products
records.description: Require manufacturers to list common food allergens in plain English & bold text on all cosmetics, toiletries & household detergents. The Office of Product Safety & Standards must update cosmetic & detergent regulations to require clear allergen labeling, aligning them with UK food safety standards.
records.further_details: Allergic reactions don't care whether you swallowed an allergen or rubbed it onto your skin. UK food laws require top allergens in bold, plain English. Yet you need a Latin degree to decipher these ingredients on soap, lip balm, and detergent. A family member suffered a painful reaction from soap listing almond only as Prunus Amygdalus. This is about our right to know. Whether managing a life-threatening allergy or making an ethical choice, we believe nobody should need a Latin degree to read a label.

records.title: Review & compensate graduates whose student debt is higher than amount borrowed
records.description: Thousands of students were unaware that inflation-linked interest could increase their loan balance despite years of repayments. Many graduates now owe more than they originally borrowed for their student loans.
records.further_details:
We want the Government to launch an independent review into this phenomenon and whether student loans were mis-sold. The review should also look into ways to improve transparency so future students fully understand the long-term cost of borrowing.
 
The Government should fund writing off debt above the original amount borrowed for long-term borrowers who have consistently repaid and compensate those who have been found to be financially disadvantaged by inflation-linked interest. We believe borrowers who have responsibly repaid their loans for years should not find themselves owing more than they originally borrowed.

records.title: Remove all accrual of interest from student loans and recalculate the balances
records.description: Remove all accrual of interest from student loans and recalculate outstanding balances as if no interest had been applied since the loans were issued.
records.further_details: Student loan borrowers can see their balances grow substantially through interest, even while making repayments. We believe access to higher education should not result in decades of growing debt, particularly when borrowers have no choice over their plan or the terms that apply to them. In  our view, England’s student finance system should support access to education, not add to the financial burden of pursuing it, so removing interest and recalculating balances would create a fairer system and help ease financial strain.

records.title: Class all Double-Cab Pick Ups as N1 light goods for farmers and all construction
records.description: To allow farming, construction and land management to use all double-cab pick-ups as N1 light goods vehicles, and not classed as company cars. Government databases know which businesses sit within those trades so cross references can be made between DVLA and HMRC to ensure rules are not broken.
records.further_details:
All double-cab pick-ups used as company vehicles within the much-valued farming, land management and all construction sectors to retain their vehicle's classification as N1 light goods commercial.
People in suits are penalising those in overalls, hard hats and safety boots, and creating more financial burden upon them by changing the aforementioned pick-ups’ light goods vehicle classification in April 2029, meaning they will be classed as company cars. They are light goods vehicles, not cars!

records.title: Make First Aid Training a mandatory part of the curriculum in schools
records.description: Make first aid training mandatory in UK schools as part of the curriculum. We believe this will ensure a higher chance of survival for victims of attacks, medical emergencies & mental health crises. Not all students receive this now, and we feel the reward will be countless saved lives.
records.further_details: Currently, the UK sees a high number of sharp implement attacks, terror attacks and mental health crises. These, alongside regular medical emergencies claim many lives every year unexpectedly, many of which we believe could be prevented by comprehensive training in schools and colleges, which would not only teach the skills required, but develop the confidence to apply them. People don't rise to emergency situations, they fall back on their training.

records.title: Ban all development on green belt land
records.description: Ban all developments on green belt land. We believe green belt land should exist to protect our existing wildlife spaces for our future.
records.further_details:
We feel the development of new builds is harming our planet and local residents. Wildlife and plant life are dwindling and our breathable air is getting worse.
In addition, we already have old derelict buildings that can be rebuilt and it’s not taking away from the green spaces as they have already been used.

records.title: Ensure equal access to online ticket booking for disabled people
records.description: Make equally accessible ticket booking for all a legal requirement. Disabled people often have no alternative but to phone venues to book tickets, unlike everyone else who can book & access tickets online or via apps. This often involves repeat calling an creates extra barriers to face.
records.further_details: I want the Government to make accessible ticket booking a legal requirement because disabled people still face unnecessary barriers attending live events. In 2026, most people can book tickets instantly online, yet many disabled people must still phone venues, wait on hold, and repeatedly explain their access needs. Accessible ticketing should be built into standard booking systems so disabled people have the same independence, dignity, and equal access as everyone else. Equal access means equal booking.

records.title: Ban AI from imitating humans without clear labelling
records.description:
It should be illegal for AI to impersonate humans without clear labelling, across all industries such as AI music artists, Influencers, Chatbots, and more.
AI is becoming more and more realistic every day, and it is already so difficult to tell what is AI and what isn’t. This should be a crime.
records.further_details:
We are concerned AI is becoming more realistic everyday and is already difficult to differentiate between what is and isn’t AI. Recently, my grandma was excitedly recommending a blues music artist she found on Facebook, only to discover that it was AI. My dad called a hotel and was speaking to an AI chatbot, but it denied it when questioned.
 
AI is everywhere and is becoming increasingly realistic. We believe this should not be a guessing game. Change should be made and boundaries should be put in place.

records.title: Ban charging people to use public toilets
records.description: I would like the UK Government or Parliament to ban places charging people to use public toilets. I believe everyone should have free access to use public toilets.
records.further_details: I believe going to the toilet is a basic human right that should not be denied to anyone just because they have no cash on them to pay to go to the toilet. Furthermore, I feel it would be cruel to deny people access to using public toilets if they didn't have any money on them, especially if they were in an emergency, such as a period emergency. For example, I believe a woman should never be denied the opportunity to change her sanitary towel just because she had no cash to use public toilets.

records.title: Legal requirement that an MP must serve a year before becoming Prime Minister
records.description: We do not think that individuals should be parachuted into government to take up the post of Prime Minister without a minimum term of one years service from being elected.
records.further_details: We feel that it is undemocratic to bring in somebody who wasn't elected as an MP at the last election to become Prime Minister without a minimum term served as an MP.

records.title: Fund better rural post-diagnosis pathways for dementia patients & their carers
records.description: Fund improved post-diagnosis pathways for dementia patients and their carers in rural areas via GP practices, including specialised dementia care nurses, like Admiral Nurses, who can provide essential support, and more appointments for patients at their local GP within 7-10 days of diagnosis.
records.further_details: Memory Clinics, CST services, and other NHS resources are mostly in city hospitals. We believe resource should be shifted to rural areas through GP practices, which should have trained dementia care nurses (e.g. Admiral Nurses) for support. Patients should be offered a GP appointment within 7-10 days, including both the person with dementia and their carer or partner. A dementia nurse at the GP practice could also improve annual reviews. Smaller hospitals across the country could also host CST sessions.

records.title: Ban private jets in the UK within 4 years
records.description: In 2019, over 11,000 scientists worldwide collectively declared a state of climate emergency, with a scientific consensus that it is caused by human activity. We are concerned that our trajectory is preventably heading towards societal breakdown.
records.further_details:
In 2023 Oxfam reported that the World’s richest 1% are responsible for around 16% of CO₂ emissions. We believe private jets are incredibly wasteful and we should set a 4-year deadline to ban them.

Transport Environment’s 2021 report found that “private jets are 5 to 14 times more polluting than commercial planes (per passenger), and 50 times more polluting than trains”.

The Times reported in 2023 that “1 in 10 flights taking off from UK are private jets.”

records.title: Require HGV Parking for New-Build Industrial Estates at planning stage
records.description: The rapid expansion of industrial estates across the country has not kept pace with essential infrastructure—particularly safe, legal, secure and sufficient parking for HGVs. All new industrial estates should have HGV parking provisions included from the planning stage.
records.further_details:
Modern industrial developments generate significant freight activity. We believe it is neither reasonable nor sustainable to externalise the parking burden onto surrounding communities. National planning policy (e.g. NPPF, paragraph 87 (b)) supports infrastructure that meets development needs—HGV parking is a core part of that.
We ask that all future industrial planning applications include a minimum number of on-site HGV parking bays, calculated per square metre of warehouse/logistics space

records.title: Teachers & children allowed 5 authorised bookable days of leave a year
records.description: We want the Government to ensure that all teaching staff and children are allowed to book off a maximum of 5 school days within a calendar year. These days can but do not have to be consecutive days.
records.further_details: We believe the teaching profession must become more flexible. Important life events (weddings, funerals, hen dos, stag dos, your child’s play etc.) don’t just happen within school holidays. No job should make you miss out on your own life. Additionally, we feel that it is unfair that teachers are punished by their own profession by having to pay triple for holidays - likewise, parents having to pay premium prices to try to give their child an amazing life experience within school holidays.

records.title: Change urinary incontinence to bladder health for NHS strategies & fund campaign
records.description: Direct the NHS to replace the term "urinary incontinence" with "bladder health" as the primary term in all NHS strategies, including in England's Women's Health Strategy, neighbourhood women's health services and Women's Health Hubs.
records.further_details:
We would also like the Government to fund a national campaign for retailers and pharmacies to adopt the same terminology in store.

14 million people in the UK live with urinary incontinence, including one in three women, yet many hide it due to shame. Over half of women with pelvic floor symptoms never seek help; one in five say embarrassment is why.

We believe the term "urinary incontinence" is part of the problem. "Bladder health" could reframe the same conditions as something to manage, like heart or mental health. We're asking Government to require the NHS to make that change, and back the women who need it.

records.title: Act to mitigate costs & end re-mortgage restrictions for shared ownership homes
records.description: Introduce laws to require housing associations to pay their share of repairs in line with ownership; allow reasonable remortgaging; enforce low-cost staircasing timelines; limit rent increases; and ensure a clear, affordable route to sell. We believe this will make things fairer.
records.further_details: We believe shared ownership is leaving families trapped. Leaseholders pay 100% of repairs despite part ownership, face rising rents, and are blocked from remortgaging or buying more shares. Costly delays and restrictions can create debt and stress, especially for low-income households. We feel this system lacks fairness and accountability.
