Reform is needed to protect residents, prevent exploitation, and restore shared ownership as a genuine, affordable path to home ownership.

records.title: Standardise NHS prescription support for coeliacs
records.description: We want the Government to end what we feel is a postcode lottery for NHS coeliac disease food support. Ensure the introduction of a standardised national policy for gluten free staple foods, so people with this autoimmune disease can access medically necessary food support wherever they live.
records.further_details: People with coeliac disease need a strict lifelong gluten free diet as their only treatment. NHS support for gluten free staple foods now varies widely across England, with many areas reducing or removing help entirely. This petition calls for a fair national policy so patients can access essential gluten free foods wherever they live.

records.title: Grant full immunity from prosecution to homeowners from intruders
records.description: Amend Section 76 of the Criminal Justice and Immigration Act 2008 and grant homeowners have absolute immunity from prosecution when defending their home from intruders.
records.further_details: We feel current laws allow criminals to exploit loopholes by claiming a homeowner used disproportionate force, which may result in homeowners facing arrest. We feel a home is a sanctuary, and that masked, armed robbers who force entry to steal should accept the absolute risk of severe injury or death because of their crimes. Homeowners should not be framed as premeditated criminals for protecting their family. We believe the system should stand unconditionally with homeowners, not intruders.

records.title: Ban sunscreen containing oxybenzone & octinoxate and promote alternatives
records.description: We call on the Government to protect marine life by banning sunscreens containing oxybenzone & octinoxate and promote reef-safe alternatives through public awareness campaigns and clear product labelling. These measures could reduce pollution and help safeguard coral reefs and marine ecosystems.
records.further_details: We believe banning sunscreens containing oxybenzone and octinoxate is important as research suggests these chemicals can harm coral reefs, contribute to coral bleaching, and disrupt marine ecosystems. Healthy reefs support biodiversity, fisheries, tourism, and coastal protection. Replacing harmful sunscreens with reef-safe alternatives could help reduce marine pollution, protect vulnerable species, and preserve ocean ecosystems for future generations while still allowing effective sun protection.

records.title: Allow child minder grandparents to receive funding for related children
records.description: Recognise that Ofsted registered child minders are just as important and valued the same as nursery staff and should receive 15-30 hours funding for looking after related children.
records.further_details:
I would like Government to address this issue as the demand for high-quality child care is increasing rapidly with the onset of funding now available for children as young as 9 months old.
 
If grandparents could claim the funding for their grandchildren without their own children having to go through the process of trying to find places in other settings, which may be few and far between, this could help lessen the stress and upset of returning to work after maternity leave.

records.title: All planning decisions for council owned land to be made by independent body
records.description: Change the law so that councils cannot make planning decisions about land that they own. In these cases, we believe that the decision maker must be independent of the land-owning council. In our view, this could ensure complete impartiality of decision making, and avoidance of conflict of interest.
records.further_details: Currently, councils can approve planning on land they own with no independent review. We think this is a privilege not extended to others and has potential to deny justice to objectors to the planning proposal. We believe there are insufficient checks and balances in current practices to ensure that completely open, fair and impartial decision making occurs. Therefore, we think requiring a land owning council to face independent review of their planning proposals would create a fairer system.

records.title: Reform remand and sentencing laws for serious sexual offences
records.description: Change the law so there is a presumption of remand for suspects in serious sexual offence cases where compelling evidence exists. Review whether time spent on remand should count towards any custodial sentence after conviction.
records.further_details: Victims can wait months or years for serious sexual offence cases to reach trial while suspects may be released on bail. Where compelling evidence exists, such as video, photographic, DNA or admission evidence, the law should create a presumption that defendants are remanded in custody to protect the public and victims. If convicted, time spent on remand should not reduce the custodial sentence imposed by the court.

records.title: Establish a Review into NHS post-operative monitoring procedures
records.description: We want the Government to establish a Review into whether current NHS post-operative monitoring procedures are being carried out consistently and to a sufficiently high standard.
records.further_details: In September 2022, Julie Christina Wigzell died aged 43 following routine gallbladder surgery. After surgery she showed signs of serious deterioration, including vomiting, blood in urine, abdominal distension, reduced mobility and not passing stool. Her wife believes a review of current post-operative monitoring and escalation procedures, including checks for bowel function and deterioration, could help identify gaps in patient safety and prevent avoidable deaths after surgery. We want the changes that come out of this review to be called Julie’s Law.

records.title: Require employers pay employees in full when they're off for cancer treatment
records.description: We think employees should be entitled to full pay whilst going though cancer treatment. We want to help anybody going though cancer treatment, regardless of which type.
records.further_details:
Cancer treatment has a big effect on the body and patients can take months to recover. It not currently a legal requirement for them to get full pay.
 
We are concerned that the lack of full pay can cause extra stress to patients and might force them to go to work after treatment. We feel that statutory sick pay isn't enough. The law needs to change to stop extra stress to cancer patients and their families.

records.title: Review spouse income rules for UK citizens married 5 years+ with a British child
records.description: Launch a review into waiving or reducing the £29,000 minimum income requirement for obtaining a spouse visa for anyone who has been married for over 5 years and who has a child with British citizenship.
records.further_details: We feel the system, fails mixed-nationality families through rigid criteria genuine households cannot meet. We believe families like ours—married 7 years with a British child—are locked out by the £29k threshold, childcare realities, and visa work bans. Consequently, many British citizens are prevented from living in their home country with their spouse and family. We want the Government to look into changing the law to exempt long-term marriages and parents of British children from these income rules.

records.title: Fund more pet-friendly homeless shelters
records.description: I want the Government to fund more pet-friendly homeless shelters so vulnerable people aren’t forced to give up animals to access safe accommodation. Councils should provide or consider pet-friendly housing, recognising animals can provide vital emotional support, safety and stability.
records.further_details: Animals can provide vital emotional support, companionship, safety and stability. People fleeing abuse, homelessness or unsafe homes should not have to choose between a safe home and the animal they depend on. Separation can cause devastating distress.

records.title: Require SEND Transition Plans from age 14 to 25 to prepare for adult life
records.description: Require Local Authorities to provide all young people with SEND with a Transition Plan from age 14 to 25, covering education, employment, independent living, health and community participation, to improve preparation for adulthood and ensure consistent support during the transition to adult life.
records.further_details:
Too many young people with SEND face a "cliff edge" when moving into adulthood, with inconsistent support for education, employment, independent living, health and community participation.
 
We call on the Government to require a statutory Transition Plan for every young person with SEND from age 14 to 25. Plans should be reviewed regularly & set out clear goals and support to help prepare for adult life.
 
This could improve independence, wellbeing, employment opportunities for SEND young people.

records.title: Introduce mandatory licensing for all barbers and barber shop owners
records.description: We want the Government to introduce a licensing system requiring anyone working as or owning a barber shop to hold a recognised barbering qualification or meet an approved national standard. We believe this protects both customers and qualified barbers.
records.further_details: Barbers use sharp tools and work closely with clients, making hygiene, safety and skill essential. Yet there is no mandatory national qualification or licence to work as or own a barber shop in the UK. We believe the Government should introduce a licensing system with recognised training or competency standards to improve public safety, raise industry standards, and also to prevent any unqualified barbers from owning a shop – meaning barbershops will be run and owned by barbers for the good of the barbers’ profession.

records.title: Stop the proposed changes to the Government Food Standards for schools
records.description: I want the Government to listen to what I believe is an overwhelming feeling in schools catering that the proposed changes (made in April 2026) would be highly detrimental to an already broken school meals service.
records.further_details: School meals represent 35% of a child's lunch & evening meal intake and Fish & Chip Friday (one of the issues) is the best day of the week for pupils, schools & caterers. We think removing fat fryers will dramatically reduce uptake in primary and reduce revenues in secondary. In our view, the school commercial catering model and funding are already broken. When the fryers go, how will secondary schools deliver 800 (25% less) meals in 45 min? The govt won’t pay for additional ovens. The biggest travesty of my lifetime.

records.title: Reverse the decision to weaken planned oil sanctions on Russia
records.description: On 20 May 2026 the Government announced its decision to reduce its planned sanctions on Russian oil. In so doing we believe it is helping directly fund Russia's war machine against Ukraine.
records.further_details: We further believe this is a decision that will cost Ukrainian lives, civilian and military, as well as our moral leadership over this war: it must be reversed, now.

records.title: Increase passenger compensation if incorrectly denied boarding due to documents
records.description: It has been reported that since Brexit airlines have denied boarding by incorrectly alleging that passengers' travel documents are invalid for travel. When this happens, we call on the compensation to be increased to £2,000 to match the £2,000 penalty paid by airlines for the reverse scenario.
records.further_details: Section 40 of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999 imposes a £2,000 penalty on airlines that bring an incorrectly-documented passenger to the UK, but Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 as amended by Regulation 8(6)(a) of the Air Passenger Rights and Air Travel Organisers' Licensing (Amendment) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 requires airlines to compensate only £220, £350 or £520 for incorrectly denying boarding to a correctly-documented passenger. This imbalance should be eliminated in order to incentivise airlines to train their ground staff.

records.title: Require domestic abuse offenders to report new relationships to police
records.description: Require domestic abuse offenders to report new relationships to police so police can consider safeguarding and inform partners of risk.
records.further_details: Domestic abuse offenders should still have the right to live their lives and have relationships, but they should be required to report new relationships to police so risks can be assessed and safeguarding considered. This could help police inform potential partners sooner, where appropriate, and help prevent further domestic abuse. This would support earlier intervention where there is a clear risk of harm.

records.title: Strengthen planning & heritage protections for historic church buildings
records.description: We call on the Government to strengthen planning and heritage protections for historic church buildings at risk of closure or commercial redevelopment, including legal requirements for councils to prioritise community, charitable, cultural, heritage, or faith based uses wherever possible.
records.further_details: Church buildings have long supported communities through worship, food banks, youth work, counselling, charity activities, and public events. As more churches close, many historic buildings risk what we believe is unsuitable commercial redevelopment, that could damage their heritage and remove valuable community spaces. We ask the Government to strengthen planning policies, guidance and protections, so councils are legally required to prioritise community, charitable, cultural, heritage, educational, or faith based uses wherever practical.

records.title: Change priority for social housing guidance to people living in UK for 10+ years
records.description: Change guidance for local authorities on priority for social housing to make people who have lived in the UK for 10+ years eligible for priority allocation of social housing over newer residents with similar needs.
records.further_details:
Long-term residents can face homelessness after being evicted from private rented homes. Existing priority for urgent needs should remain.
 
We believe long-term residents should not face longer waits for social housing when housing is being allocated to people who have lived in the UK for less than 10 years. We are not seeking to remove existing priority for vulnerable people, such as those experiencing domestic abuse or with serious medical needs. This proposal would apply regardless of a person's nationality or country of birth. It is based purely on the length of one’s residency in the UK.

records.title: Ban domestic flights on routes that can be travelled by train in under 4.5 hours
records.description: Follow France’s lead and remove air routes where there is a direct rail link of 4.5 hours or less, to help rapidly bring emissions down in line with the UK’s legally-binding net zero targets.
records.further_details: With air emissions approximately 7 times higher than rail emissions (UK Government, 2022), we think removing the option to fly would make a significant impact on greenhouse gas emissions. At a time when we need to do all we can to cut carbon, we should follow the lead of France and Spain who have, or are considering, banning domestic routes where rail provides a viable alternative. The 4.5 hour cut-off includes Lon-Edinburgh and Lon-Glasgow, two of the UK’s most-used flight routes.

records.title: Make a public register of scam phone numbers & require providers to investigate
records.description: Create a national public register of scam phone numbers. Require these numbers to be reported in a free, searchable public register and require communication providers to investigate these numbers and remove them where appropriate.
records.further_details: Telephone scams can cause financial loss and distress, yet there is no single public database to check suspicious numbers. A national public register could help people avoid known scam calls, identify emerging fraud more quickly, and enable communications providers to investigate numbers receiving multiple independent reports and remove them where misuse is confirmed.

records.title: Introduce suicide prevention requirements for highway authorities
records.description: Require highway authorities to install higher and more secure bridge railings to reduce the risk of people accessing dangerous edges, to increase patrols and monitoring at known high-risk locations, and to introduce preventative measures such as signage and support points.
records.further_details: Too many lives are being lost at known locations. Simple physical barriers and increased presence have been shown to reduce incidents and give people time to reconsider and seek help. This is not just about restriction, but prevention—protecting vulnerable people while wider mental health support is improved. Requiring action now can save lives.

records.title: Make UK aid to Uganda conditional on action against online animal abuse & scams
records.description: Require safeguards on UK aid to Uganda so it is only provided if action is taken against organised online animal abuse and fraud. This should include cooperation with local authorities, improved enforcement of animal welfare laws, and action with social media platforms to remove abusive content.
records.further_details: Recent BBC News reporting has shown organised groups abusing animals online to generate money through scams and donations. This involves cruelty and public deception. We believe UK aid should not operate without safeguards where such exploitation can continue unchecked. Action is needed to protect animals, prevent fraud, protect UK citizens, and maintain trust in legitimate charities. Without conditions, animal abuse, fraud, and the risk to legitimate charities will continue.

records.title: Fund research into Post-Sepsis Syndrome to recognise its long term impact
records.description: We want the Government to fund research to help Post-Sepsis Syndrome (PSS) be formally recognised as a long-term condition and ensure patients can access appropriate assessment, rehabilitation, mental health support and disability-related assistance after sepsis.
records.further_details: Many people who survive sepsis experience long-term physical, cognitive and psychological effects known as Post-Sepsis Syndrome. Symptoms can include chronic fatigue, pain, mobility problems, memory and concentration difficulties, anxiety, depression and PTSD. Despite this, awareness and support remain inconsistent across the NHS. Many survivors struggle to access rehabilitation, benefits support, workplace adjustments and appropriate follow-up care.

records.title: Allow Kinship Carers to Receive Child Maintenance Without Reductions in support
records.description: We call on Government to ensure all kinship carers can receive child maintenance without it reducing financial support they get. Child maintenance is a child's entitlement & should support their needs. We believe kinship carers shouldn't be financially penalised for stepping up to care for children.
records.further_details: We ask the Government to ensure all kinship carers can receive child maintenance without it reducing allowances or financial support  they receive from local authorities or other bodies. Child maintenance is a parent's contribution towards their child's upbringing and should benefit the child directly. Kinship carers strive to provide loving, stable homes and often prevent children entering the care system. We believe they should not be financially disadvantaged for stepping up to care for family members.

records.title: Give PhD students full government funded childcare hours
records.description: Allow doctoral research to also receive the 30 funded hours for childcare regardless of taxable income.
records.further_details:
Post-graduate research students fall between the gaps for pre-school age funded hours for nursery places.
With nursery fees at an all time high, even with the funded hours, it leaves many PhD students with young children unable to afford to continue their studies.
Currently, the funded hours are tied to "working hours" (I.e. taxable hours). A majority of PhD stipends are untaxed, and therefore ineligible. Countless brilliant minds have therefore had to leave research in order to "afford" childcare.

records.title: Offer to deploy UK air and ground forces to Ukraine
records.description: We call on the UK Government to offer to deploy RAF fighter jets, air defence units and ground forces to Ukraine’s border regions to help secure Ukrainian airspace and free-up Ukrainian front-line troops.
records.further_details: Protecting Ukrainian airspace and securing non-combat border zones (such as northern or western borders) against potential threats could allow Ukraine’s military forces to deploy their troops where they are needed most. Providing air cover and ground support could help protect civilian infrastructure from aerial bombardment, bolster stability and defence across the region, and save innocent lives.

records.title: Stop means-testing heating oil support
records.description: We want the Government to provide heating-oil support that is not means-tested. Around 1.5m UK households rely on heating oil. Unlike gas & electricity users, they aren’t protected by the energy price cap and must often pay large upfront costs.
records.further_details:
The Government has announced support for heating-oil households, but this is means-tested.
Heating-oil users should be treated fairly and receive equivalent support or protections, and not be disadvantaged for living off the gas grid.
We want the Government to provide non-means-tested support.

records.title: Remove public pensions from elected officials found guilty of serious offences
records.description: We believe taxpayers shouldn't fund the retirement of those guilty of serious offences. We demand laws to remove personal pensions linked to service in elected office for those guilty of serious offences like child abuse.
records.further_details: Pensions for elected politicians can exceed £30,000 to £50,000 annually, funded by the public. When an official commits serious crimes like child abuse, taxpayers may be left footing the bill for their retirement. We demand an immediate law to stop funding criminal offenders.

records.title: Prevent MPs who resign their seat from standing for re-election for 12 months
records.description: If an MP chooses to resign from the UK Parliament during a parliamentary term, they would be ineligible to run for election for any seat, including the one previously held, for a minimum period of 12 months.
records.further_details: This would prevent the waste of resources caused by an MP resigning and immediately contesting the same seat again.

records.title: Hold a referendum on whether to mandate a general election when the PM changes
records.description: Give the British people the vote in a referendum to decide if a general election should be mandated when the Prime Minister changes between general elections.
records.further_details: We believe that a politician who did not lead a party at general election time should not be able to make decisions for the people.

records.title: Mandate that libraries must provide access to diverse and inclusive materials
records.description: The government must enact legislation to ensure libraries hold materials that provide a rich, ongoing discourse about diversity and inclusion in our communities.
records.further_details:
Libraries are the sanctuaries of knowledge and celebration of diversity, but we feel local councils may be able to influence what materials are available.
 
Libraries should be free to celebrate & educate on diverse issues independently. We are supporting the fight for a more inclusive society where education is truly free from prejudice and restriction.

records.title: Ban donations & fund parties with a government multiple of fixed membership fees
records.description: Political parties must be prohibited from accepting financial contributions beyond a standard, capped membership fee, eliminating the influence of wealthy elites. The government should match these fees by a fixed multiple, forcing politicians to build a broad public base of support.
records.further_details: We believe the UK's political party funding model is broken, causing widespread cynicism as citizens suspect wealthy donors are purchasing policy influence over a fair democratic process. This crisis is backed by data: a recent study suggests 87% of the public are concerned about potential corruption. Another study found that Electoral Commission investigations have declined by 89% since 2019. Some parties receive up to two-thirds of their total funding from a small number of donors. No individual has ever been imprisoned for breaching UK electoral finance laws.

records.title: Give the Senedd the same powers as the Scottish Parliament & its own Welsh Law
records.description: Senedd Cymru, or the Welsh Parliament, currently has fewer powers than the Scottish Parliament. I believe that the Welsh Government should have the same powers as the Scottish Government, creating true parity, and that Wales should have its own judicial region.
records.further_details: In October 2019, the Commission on Justice in Wales published its review of the justice system in Wales and concluded that “the people of Wales are being let down by the justice system in its current state”.  I believe devolving justice to Wales would allow the people of Wales to be properly served.

records.title: Ban destructive scanning of books used in AI training or digitising
records.description: We call on the Government to require that any company purchasing UK books in bulk for AI training use non-destructive scanning methods, and to bar AI models built on destructively-scanned books from commercial licensing in the UK.
records.further_details: There are reports of AI companies buying and destructively scanning millions of books for AI training; a 2025 US court ruled this lawful there under fair use. Non-destructive scanning already exists and is used by libraries, but some AI firms favour destructive methods because they are faster and cheaper. Booksellers in the Netherlands, Germany, Switzerland and Spain have since reported near-identical bulk requests from other AI firms, suggesting UK sellers could be next. Nothing currently stops AI models trained this way from being sold and used in the UK.

records.title: Ban messaging apps with unregistered accounts from enabling media sharing
records.description: The UK Government should introduce legislation requiring messaging services and apps that do not use verified user registration (such as phone number or email-based accounts) to restrict the ability to send or distribute media files, including images, videos, and audio messages.
records.further_details: Because these messaging services allow users to communicate without a verified registered account, there is a lack of accountability. Due to this, we believe these apps are at a higher risk of being used to distribute harmful media, such as child pornography and other illegal sexual content. Therefore, by restricting media sharing on services without verified user identities, we think the risk of these apps being misused in this way decreases significantly.

records.title: Mandate clear labelling of recipe/size changes in food products
records.description: Introduce a statutory requirement for clear labelling advising a purchaser when companies change the size or formulation of a product: e.g. "Size reduced by 30g" or "Beef content reduced by 15%". We believe  this will allow shoppers to make better choices.
records.further_details: We feel that UK shoppers in supermarkets are consistently being hammered by inflation, shrinkflation, and skimpflation. Prices, sizes, and formulation of products can change with little or no clear labelling to notify consumers. I would like to place requirements on companies to inform us of these changes, so we are able to make better choices regarding what we purchase and how much we are getting for our money.

records.title: Reform non-molestation orders: lifetime protection & mandatory action
records.description: Make Non-Molestation Orders lifetime once granted, covering aliases, online identities and proxy threats. Require police to investigate credible third-party evidence of breaches and prevent cases being closed solely because a frightened victim cannot or will not report.
records.further_details: Fixed-term orders can leave victims vulnerable when protection expires. Any breach should result in immediate arrest and detention pending investigation and court consideration. Repeated, deliberate or calculated breaches should lead to prosecution and custodial sentences. Victims should not repeatedly relive abuse in court to renew protection.

records.title: Stop the governments plan to cut the disability element of Universal credit.
records.description: The government plan to cut the "Health Element" of Universal Credit (LCWRA) in half for new applicants. Claimants who already receive LWCRA will have their allowance increased from £423.27 to £429.80 a month. However, from April 6th 2026, new applicants will only receive £217.26 per month.
records.further_details: This element of Universal Credit is life supporting financial aid for people who struggle to work due to their health. The aim is to "encourage work" amongst disabled individuals who have already gone through health assessments. The funds saved will be "reinvested into increasing the standard allowance for all UC claimant's". The government want to take benefits from disabled people and give more to those recieving Universal Credit, who do not have health issues preventing them from working.

records.title: Mandate Child-Resistant Caps on all Children's Cough Medicines
records.description: Make it a legal requirement for all children's cough and sore throat medicines sold over the counter be supplied in containers fitted with child-resistant caps. We also ask manufacturers to adopt this safety measure voluntarily while any regulatory changes are being considered.
records.further_details: Many medicines and household products already use child-resistant caps because they are proven to reduce the risk of accidental poisoning. In our view, there is no reason why medicines specifically designed for children should not follow the same standard.

records.title: Review endometriosis surgery protocols
records.description: The Government should review endometriosis surgery protocols. We believe that currently, many women are made to wait for more than a year after their surgery to establish the diagnosis. We think an excision surgery should be offered directly after a diagnosis has been made as a national standard.
records.further_details: In our view people can wake up from surgery and be told they have deep infiltrated endometriosis and they need to go back and plan surgery, when in reality they could have an MRI scan and expect a full day surgery where excision to remove the endometrial tissue is also removed. We do not think it is fair that women’s organs get messed with waiting for surgery for many months, waiting to get endometriosis removed. This is not fair on women’s body’s, life and mental health. Endometriosis should not be left to grow and grow and disrupt people’s lives.

records.title: Increase funding and information for families affected by dementia
records.description: Dementia affects millions and families are often left unsupported after diagnosis. We call on the Government to increase funding to help provide clearer information and a support package at diagnosis, to include guidance, services, and signposting, so no family faces dementia alone.

records.title: Review regulation of online creators providing advice they profit from
records.description: I want increased safeguarding for vulnerable people from social media creators offering mental health and domestic violence support but have no qualifications to do so. The Government should review the regulation of such online creators, to ensure they are not taking advantage of vulnerable people.
records.further_details: Some creators groom vulnerable people by offering emotional support, mental health advice and support for domestic abuse, without expertise to do so. I believe that these creators pay for large followings so that they appear popular. I think some of these vulnerable people believe the content creator loves them or cares for them and trust them. In my view we need to put an end to this grooming behaviour online by reviewing regulations of online creators

records.title: Ban PFAS harmful 'forever chemicals'
records.description: We want the Government to ban the manufacture, import, and sale of all consumer products containing PFAS ('forever chemicals'). We believe the UK needs to catch up with generally stricter EU restrictions to protect our rivers and citizens.
records.further_details: PFAS are indestructible "forever chemicals" that bioaccumulate in our bodies and ecosystems. When used in consumer goods like waterproof clothing, they wash into UK waterways, permanently polluting our drinking water and food chains. There is considerable evidence that exposure to PFAS is linked to severe health risks, including cancer, liver damage, fertility issues, and immune suppression. To protect our citizens and dying rivers, we believe the UK must ban these toxic chemicals entirely.

records.title: Fund Free TV licences for all pensioners.
records.description: We want the Government to fund free TV licences for existing pensioners and those who reach the official retirement age. When people reach retirement age, we think they should receive a state-financed free TV licence.
records.further_details:
Many pensioners live on the breadline with only the TV for company. With the cost of food soaring and utility bills ever higher, we feel there is a desperate need to provide all pensioners with at least this concession.

We feel it is a double outrage that those who have given their all to this country in taxes and raising children have to pay a TV licence fee and are only exempt if they receive means-tested Pension Credit. Meanwhile, some media figures draw huge salaries.

records.title: People over the age of 65 must retake their driving test every 5 years
records.description: I think at the age of 65 you should have a retake of your driving test and continue doing so every 5 years. I don’t feel a renewal of a driving license and providing medical records are quite enough.
records.further_details: I believe older people need to have the examiner in the car to assess how they drive and then make the decision as to whether they are still fit to drive. I have had experience of an accident caused by an older driver and I believe regular tests for older drivers may be an important step towards greater safety on the roads.

records.title: Fund sanitary products for women with endometriosis, PCOS or adenomyosis on NHS
records.description: I am calling on Government and Parliament to provide free sanitary products on the NHS for those diagnosed with endometriosis, PCOS, or adenomyosis. Heavy bleeding creates a medical need, not a choice, and should be supported with essential hygiene products to ensure dignity, health, and equality.
records.further_details: The Government and Parliament should ensure people with endometriosis, PCOS, and adenomyosis receive free sanitary products on the NHS. These conditions often cause heavy, prolonged bleeding, making sanitary protection a medical necessity, not a choice. The cost places a disproportionate financial burden on those already managing chronic pain and illness. Providing free access could protect dignity, improve health outcomes, reduce inequality, and ensure fair support within healthcare.

records.title: Set up no catch marine reserves in 30% of the UK seas & EEZ by May 2027
records.description: Set up 'no catch' marine reserves in 30% of the UKs territorial seas and Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) by May 2027. These must be protected from all human activity harmful to marine life (e.g. pollution, bottom trawling) and to maximize biodiversity and fish stocks.
records.further_details: Recent governments, including the current, have promised to deliver '30 by 30'. To reserve 30% of the UK's land and seas for nature by 2030. Unfortunately, we believe the climate and biodiversity crisis is too bad to wait that long and allocating the sea areas is much easier than land as the Crown already owns the seabed. The sooner these reserves are put in place the sooner our seas will recover. We think this will be to the benefit of both fish and fisherman.

records.title: Review 1980 Hague Convention Framework on International Child Abduction
records.description: We believe that the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction, 25 October 1980 must be reviewed, as it may not protect women fleeing abuse nor the children they are seeking to protect.
records.further_details: In our view, this convention is outdated and does not recognise domestic abuse, coercive control, economic abuse or child safeguarding. We believe that many parents fleeing domestic abuse are “branded” as abductors, and end up losing their children under the 1980 convention. 75% of the parents who are brought before the courts are mothers. We therefore call for a review of the convention framework, and of the support provided to the parents brought before the courts.

records.title: Make Public Transport Free For All Students
records.description: I want the Government to make all public transport free for students in full-time education, whether they are in school, college, or university.
records.further_details: Many families across the UK are already struggling with the rising cost of living, and student transport costs can add even more financial pressure on parents and young people. We believe making public transport free for students would help ease this burden, improve access to education and opportunities, and ensure that no student is disadvantaged because they cannot afford travel costs. We also feel it could encourage greater use of public transport, helping to reduce traffic and support environmental goals.

records.title: Ban all alternative remittance systems to disrupt small boat smuggling networks
records.description: Introduce a total statutory ban on alternative remittance systems such as the hawala banking system and parallel remittance ledgers. Operating or participating in an informal, trust-based money network must be made a criminal offence to force the closure of shops acting as physical cash hubs.
records.further_details: Channel people-smuggling syndicates rely heavily on informal brokers to act as a trusted escrow mechanism. These operators hold a migrant’s cash in front businesses—like tech repair shops or mini-mart. Current regulations require lengthy financial investigations to prove money laundering before a shop can be shut down. A total ban on these parallel ledgers could help allow the National Crime Agency and Border Security Command to dismantle local cash networks funding small boat logistics.

records.title: Exclude offenders convicted of causing death from the early release scheme
records.description: We call on the Government to exclude offenders convicted of causing death, including by dangerous driving, from early release under the Sentencing Act.
records.further_details: A prison sentence may end, but a victim's sentence never does. Families lose parents, children, grandparents and lifelong partners forever. Birthdays, Christmases and future memories are replaced by grief. We believe reducing sentences after an independent judge has imposed them undermines public confidence in justice. Exempt offenders convicted of causing death, including by dangerous driving, from early release. Justice should not be shortened. Grief cannot be.

records.title: Facilitate a referendum on Scottish independence from the UK
records.description: The current Prime Minister of the UK said he was determined to prove the First Minister of Scotland wrong when he said the current British Prime Minister would be the last Prime Minister of the UK. We believe the best way to do this is to facilitate a referendum on Scottish independence from the UK.
records.further_details: We believe a referendum on Scottish independence from the UK is better than telling the people of Scotland that they do not want independence, or that the majority of people in Scotland do not want a referendum. The UK Government should let the people of Scotland decide.

records.title: Tax all assets and profits over £1bn by 100% and abolish non-doms
records.description: Increase taxes on individual wealth over £1bn to 100% meaning that no-one can be a billionaire. Corporations or businesses profits over £1bn annually, again, taxed at 100% to be spent on schools and hospitals, roads, support for the disabled, housing the homeless, etc. Abolish "non-dom" status.
records.further_details: It's impossible to earn £1bn. We believe the only way people make that money is through exploitation. There is a cost of living emergency in the UK, and hoarding money is a huge problem. We think chancellor protecting non-dom tax avoidance over welfare for disabled people is abhorrent and demonstrates a clear security risk to actual constituents when such power can be wielded by any one person or business. Pathological hoarding of wealth should be a crime, taxing it appropriately is a step in the right direction.

records.title: Ban fossil fuel advertising
records.description: I would like Parliament to ban ads for fossil fuel and high-carbon products to lower consumption and make companies focus on sustainable alternatives.
records.further_details: We believe the climate crisis is a direct threat to global biodiversity and the well-being of future generations. Beyond the environmental impact, the WHO estimates air pollution is responsible for around 7 million premature deaths annually around the World. We must stop allowing the fossil fuel industry to mask its impact through advertising and portraying themselves as eco-friendly while they are not. We believe removing these influence channels could be a critical step in protecting public health and meeting our climate goals.

records.title: Review costs awards for proven false evidence in family court proceedings
records.description: Review the consistency of costs orders in family court cases where false or misleading evidence is proven. We think that courts should ensure that deliberate dishonesty results in fair and proportionate financial consequences while protecting genuine claims.
records.further_details: Family courts should protect vulnerable parents and ensure the process is not misused to maintain power or control through false or misleading evidence. Where a judge makes clear findings of deliberate dishonesty, we think costs orders should be considered more consistently and transparently. This would strengthen accountability, reduce harm from prolonged litigation, and improve confidence in the system, while still protecting genuine safeguarding concerns and judicial discretion.

records.title: Abolish Cafcass and replace it
records.description: We believe Cafcass is failing children and families across England. Some reviews and public reports show safeguarding concerns, delays, and inaccurate assessments. We ask the Government to review Cafcass and replace it with a more transparent, accountable child welfare service.
records.further_details: Some public reviews and professional feedback show repeated concerns about Cafcass practice, including safeguarding issues, delays, and inaccurate assessments. These problems appear across England, which we believe indicates systemic failings, not isolated cases. There are families and professionals that report that Cafcass is no longer meeting its duty to protect children or support the family courts. An independent review and replacement service are needed.

records.title: Establish a legal right to flexi-schooling
records.description: We believe flexi-schooling is a viable option for parents where education is shared between school and home. However, this agreement is at the discretion of the school. There is no formal process to apply or an appeals procedure. We call for there to be a legal right to flexi-schooling.
records.further_details: Full time education at school is not the best fit for every family. We feel a legal right to have the option of flexi-schooling is a legitimate one, but that the difficulty lies in the fact that it must be agreed upon by the school. We believe schools are not giving families the chance to trial this and instead are issuing a blanket no. There is no formal application process or appeals process, which we believe should be created to give families the opportunity to access this option.

records.title: Require agencies and employers to pay umbrella and payroll processing fees
records.description: Change the law so workers, agency workers and Construction Industry Scheme (CIS) subcontractors cannot be charged fees just to receive their pay. I am charged £25 a week. If an agency, hirer or employer requires a payroll or umbrella company, the business should pay the fee.
records.further_details: I work as a self-employed subcontractor under CIS and am charged £25 every week by a payment company just to receive money I have earned. Others I know are charged £27.45 a week. That can mean over £1,000 a year in compulsory payment-processing fees. Where an agency, hirer or employer requires a payroll, umbrella or payment company, the business should pay that cost, not the worker.

records.title: Make Ai generated images, logos, and audio ineligible for ownership & copyright.
records.description: AI-generated works should not qualify for copyright. Mirror U.S. courts that have affirmed that copyright requires human authorship.
records.further_details: This petition calls for AI-generated content created without meaningful human creative input to be ineligible for copyright or ownership claims. This aligns with current U.S. legal precedent established in Thaler v. Perlmutter, where federal courts affirmed that copyright requires human authorship. The U.S. Supreme Court declined to review the case, leaving this principle intact. Copyright should protect human creativity, not autonomous machine-generated works.

records.title: Review social media platforms actions on animal abuse, neglect and mistreatment
records.description: We want the Government to review if social media platforms are acting on content depicting animal abuse, neglect or mistreatment. Platforms should remove such content, prevent creators profiting from it, review repeated incidents at account level and escalate serious animal welfare concerns.
records.further_details: Animals can be harmed, frightened, neglected or mistreated to create content for views, engagement or profit. We believe content created through animal abuse, neglect or mistreatment should not be permitted on social media platforms at all. Platforms should identify repeated welfare concerns across accounts, remove such content and prevent animal suffering being exploited for entertainment, attention or financial gain.

records.title: Refuse UK entry to all convicted foreign nationals & strengthen checks
records.description: Amend Immigration Rules so foreign nationals with verified criminal convictions of any length are presumed ineligible for an ETA, visa or visitor entry, unless an exception is justified. Also strengthen pre-travel fingerprint and criminal-record checks.
records.further_details: Foreign nationals have no automatic right to visit the UK. We believe a verified criminal conviction should normally prevent a person from entering as a visitor, regardless of sentence length or where the conviction occurred. Fingerprint checks should help identify people using different names or passports and link them to overseas convictions. Safeguards should cover overturned convictions, mistaken identity and offences not recognised under UK law, with exceptions only where justified.

records.title: Fund a national awareness campaign on the Bereavement Support Payment
records.description: We ask the Government to fund a national awareness campaign on the Bereavement Support Payment to make it more well known. People may only find out about it by chance or word of mouth. The Government should ensure information about how to apply is available on the Tell Us Once Service.
records.further_details: We want the campaign to particularly target long term partners who didn't get chance to marry. We believe a national awareness campaign is necessary to ensure the needs of people who are already going through a difficult enough time are considered.

records.title: Review access to social media for under 18s in CAMHS wards/adolescent units
records.description: Introduce a nationally standardised digital safeguarding policy for all under 18 year olds during acute mental health admissions. Pause social media including smart phones on admission. Provide therapeutic alternatives. Children in crisis deserve space to recover.
records.further_details: Some children have posted images of their self harm wounds from hospital beds while algorithms provide more images from peers. Inpatient admission should mean safety. Instead, we think smartphones are turning wards into broadcasting studios for harm. Self-harm costs the NHS. We believe that unmanaged digital risk in acute admissions is negligent.

records.title: Review conditions for parental rights to be removed
records.description:
I want the grounds in which parental responsibility can be removed to change.
Some children may be exposed to numerous disturbing things due to a parent and are highly traumatised due to this. I think it's wrong that this is only possible after something like murder for this to actually happen.
records.further_details: There are children who live in fear of a parent daily, whether it be mum or dad and they still have responsibility over that child. There are cases where a child has been exposed to multiple violent episodes, pornography, taken on drug deals, and asked sexual questions by a parent, yet they still have parental rights over the child, and there are parents in worse situations. This is why I feel this would be a strongly supported petition.

records.title: Review standard degree lengths and increase support for two-year degrees
records.description: Review standard university degree lengths and support better access to 2 year degrees where students can achieve the same qualification and learning outcomes without reducing standards.
records.further_details:
Many countries deliver equivalent qualifications in that time, and some UK universities already offer accelerated 2 year degrees

This petition is not calling for all university degrees to be shortened. Many courses, particularly those involving placements, laboratory work or clinical training, require 3 years or longer. However, where the same qualification and learning outcomes can be achieved through more intensive study, we believe students should have the option to complete their degree in 2 years as this could reduce student debt, lower costs and help graduates enter the workforce sooner without reducing academic standards.

records.title: Review NHS approach & require national care pathway for severe childhood eczema
records.description: Review the NHS approach and require it to introduce a specific national care pathway for children with moderate to severe eczema. This should include more urgent referrals to dermatologists and dietitians, regular follow ups, action plans, and better education for GPs who will see a child first.
records.further_details: Despite severe pain and symptoms, or full-on allergic reactions, I worry that children are left waiting years to be seen by dermatologists and dietitians. I’m petitioning for faster access to specialists, clearer treatment pathways, better GP education. Separately, I also think labelling on steroid creams should include a TSW warning

records.title: Abolish NHS workers car parking charges
records.description: This petition is for the NHS Staff in England who have to pay for onsite parking to go to work. I would like to have this abolished and made illegal to charge NHS Staff for onsite parking.
records.further_details: Onsite parking for NHS Staff ranges from region to region in England (in excess of £25.00 per month), it’s free in Scotland and Wales and has been since 2008, it is about time NHS staff in England also benefited from free parking. Also most of the time there isn’t enough parking spaces onsite, therefore the staff don’t park to the rules and receive hefty fine’s. Private parking firms are making Millions out of the hard working staff, let’s get this abolished and made illegal, let’s help our NHS.

records.title: Add Allstar Cheerleading to the approved activities for GCSE and A-level PE
records.description: Allstar cheer demands elite athleticism, strength, and precision. We believe it is unfairly excluded from PE specs, depriving students of academic credit for their primary sport. We think updating the curriculum to include cheer ensures fairness, promotes inclusivity, and rewards true dedication.
records.further_details: Beyond its physical demand, allstar cheerleading is highly structured, governed by strict international safety regulations and scoring rubrics. We believe the standardized framework makes it just as measurable and rigorously judged as gymnastics or trampolining. By continuing to exclude it, the curriculum ignores one of the fastest, growing youth sports in the UK. Adding cheer provides an accessible path for diverse athletes to excel, driving engagement, ensuring the PE specification reflects modern sport.

records.title: Provide extra funding to primary schools for swimming and water safety
records.description: We believe this is a petition everyone urgently needs to get behind. Too many lives have already sadly been lost through open water incidents. Many of these tragedies can be prevented through proper swimming and water safety education.
records.further_details: Although water safety is now included in the national curriculum as well as learning to swim, we believe more funding specifically for this life saving education could ensure it is delivered to the high standard that is needed. We believe every child should leave primary school able to swim, float to live, understand water dangers, and know what to do in an emergency. This petition is calling for greater investment into swimming and water safety education in primary schools.

records.title: Create a cross-party Commission for Long-Term National Planning.
records.description:
We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation establishing a permanent, cross-party Commission for Long-Term National Planning.
It should develop and monitor 10–20-year national frameworks, starting with energy, housing and education, and report annually to Parliament on progress.
records.further_details:
Repeated changes in our political leadership and policy direction have weakened confidence in our economy, institutions and our future. Energy, housing and education require consistent planning and investment over many years, yet are too often shaped by short-term political priorities. The Commission should agree on the broad outcomes the country needs to achieve, while leaving elected governments free to decide how to deliver them. 
NB We have a precedent, namely The Climate Change Act 2008.

records.title: Guarantee a penalty-free transfer for LISA holders before its replacement
records.description: Government to formally confirm and legislate for a penalty-free transfer window for all current Lifetime ISA holders, allowing them to move their savings into the new ISA (as announced in 2025 budget)— or an alternative savings product — without incurring any withdrawal penalty by April 2028.
records.further_details:
The Government has announced that the LISA is being replaced by a new type of ISA in 2028. We believe thousands of holders are feeling trapped by the £450,000 property cap, unchanged since 2017. The average London house price exceeds £551,000. Withdrawing triggers a 25% penalty — removing not just the government bonus but also 6.25% of savers' own money.

In our view these savers followed government guidance and did nothing wrong. We call for the Government to legislate for a penalty-free transfer window before 2028 so no saver loses their own money.

records.title: Mandate all schools in England to have an SLT member trained for mental health
records.description: Require all schools in England to have at least one member of their senior leadership team (SLT) dedicated to student mental health and wellbeing.
records.further_details: The government recommends a mental health professional in school, it is not mandatory. Students who face bullying in person or even online may not feel ok asking for help from their parents or teacher. SLT is a high ranking position within the school and has a say in changes the school can make, if there is an SLT member trained for mental health students students can talk to a trained professional who can find how the school can accommodate their needs easier due to their position of power.

records.title: Increase sentences and end guilty plea discounts for child sex offenders
records.description: We want the Government to increase sentences for child sex offences, prohibit all sentence reductions for guilty pleas for these offences, and introduce stronger restrictions on where convicted offenders can live after release to better protect children.
records.further_details: Child sexual abuse causes lifelong harm to victims and their families. We believe current sentences often fail to reflect the seriousness of these crimes. We believe offenders should not receive reduced sentences simply for pleading guilty, and that stronger restrictions on where they can live after release would help protect children and increase public confidence in the justice system.

records.title: Fund a national awareness campaign for Clare’s Law
records.description: I call on the Government to fund a national awareness campaign for Clare’s Law, including working with police forces and public services to promote the scheme so people know that they can request a disclosure if they are considering starting a relationship.
records.further_details:
This petition is informed by my own experience. I became aware of Clare's Law only after circumstances had escalated to the point that police involvement was necessary. Had I known that the scheme existed and how accessible it was, I would have sought a disclosure much sooner. 
 
I believe awareness should not depend on someone already knowing what to search for. Greater public awareness could help people make informed decisions before they are at risk.

records.title: Review & Strengthen Child Protection Measures on Marketplace Apps & Websites
records.description: Review and legislate all marketplace apps & websites to implement stronger child protection requirements, including mandatory identity verification for sellers and buyers, improved reporting systems, and stronger child exploitation monitoring & cooperation with the police to combat safety concerns.
records.further_details: Many people are concerned that online marketplace apps and websites could be misused by people who seek to exploit children. We believe stronger safeguards are needed to help prevent abuse, protect children and families, and ensure these platforms have robust systems for detecting and responding to suspicious activity. We ask the Government to review existing regulations and legislate to introduce stronger child protection requirements for online marketplace apps and websites.

records.title: Enact a 2-6% wealth tax on all assets over £10 million
records.description: We call on the Government to enact a wealth tax between 2-6% (or higher depending on the individual’s net worth) on all assets that are over £10 million, with no exemptions or losses.
records.further_details: We believe a wealth tax could be a step towards closing the wealth gap and preventing any return to feudalism. The income generated could be used to support lower income families or to provide the Government with more money to increase public funding, or possibly a mix

records.title: Make it a specific criminal offence to impersonate a member of UK Armed Forces
records.description: We want the Government to make it a specific, standalone criminal offence for anyone to pretend to serve or have served His Majesty’s Armed Forces.
records.further_details: This offence should include anyone gaining any financial or any type of help by pretending to have served in the Armed Forces past or present and turning up to parades wearing military medals. We believe pretending to have served in our Armed Forces is an insult to those who have sacrificed and continue to sacrifice that people are able to gain socially and monetarily off our service.

records.title: Ban households from burning their rubbish in their gardens
records.description: We want the Government to ban people from burning rubbish in their garden instead of disposing or recycling it as I believe they should. I think having daily fires in built-up urban areas is beyond a joke. It can make people ill and affect people's daily lives.
records.further_details: While there are restrictions on what you can burn in your garden, where I live fires are still a daily occurrence around the whole area, with multiple garden fires a day. As a result I feel you cannot hang washing out to dry, let your kids play in the garden in the summer without having to call them in as the smoke is billowing and filling gardens, and you have to keep your windows closed even in the summer. It can affect people's health and breathing. I think most of the people in my area burn their rubbish instead of disposing of it accordingly.

records.title: Fund the installation and maintenance of litter cameras on highways
records.description: Fund the installation and maintenance of litter cameras on Highway Agency-maintained roads to catch and fine people littering. This could change people’s behaviours, reduce government costs, protect nature, and raise revenue through fines.
records.further_details:
We believe something needs to change and that our highways are an embarrassment. Litter has built up along many of our roads, which we feel is making our country look like a rubbish dump. 
 
Having litter cameras on roads maintained by the Highway Agency could discourage people from littering on country roads. We believe we need incremental fines for each offence, with the owner of the car being responsible.

records.title: Require warnings for social media content about open water swimming
records.description: Under the Online Safety Act, social media platforms have a duty to remove or restrict access to harmful content. This does not apply to open water swimming videos. I want the government to classify these videos as dangerous and require this content to carry warnings.
records.further_details: We believe open water swimming videos posted online are an encouragement to young people to get into the water, as these videos are often made to look like great fun, however it is extremely dangerous especially for younger people, and the videos do not have any warnings placed upon them. I speak through experience from 31 yrs in the fire service after attending many incidents for water rescue purposes. The Fire Service should also be given more funding for public education on water safety.

records.title: Implement a wealth tax, increase marginal income tax rates & lower working hours
records.description: Introduce a progressive annual wealth tax on the top 1%, increase marginal income tax rates for ultra-high earners, and legislate a structural framework to reduce standard working hours, in direct alignment with the macroeconomic models detailed in the 2026 Global Justice Report.
records.further_details: We believe the 2026 Global Justice Report proves societies can lower their material footprint and boost well-being via wealth compression by implementing progressive wealth and income taxes which would actively curb extreme inequality. Furthermore, structurally shortening the standard working week should shift focus from resource-intensive consumption to public health and education. The UK Government has the direct legislative power to reform these tax and labour laws to build a fairer, sustainable economy.

records.title: Increase New State Pension and pay to all, abolish the old Basic State Pension.
records.description: We think the government should put all our elderly onto the New State Pension, increase the New State Pension to a good percentage of average earnings and abolish the old 'Basic State Pension'.
records.further_details:
We believe those on the Basic State Pension should be paid the difference accrued, since the New State Pension's introduction, between the Basic State Pension and New State Pension.

Britain's basic State Pension is currently £184.90 per week.
Britain's New State Pension is currently £241.30 a week.
Britain's average weekly earnings (AWE) were estimated at £722 in March 2025, by the Office for National Statistics.

records.title: Ban 'scalping' of items for short term resale at inflated prices.
records.description: People purchase products en-masse (often on credit) to resell, such as trading cards, trainers and other limited edition items. For these items there can be markups of so much as 200% or more on resold products.
records.further_details: This has become a "viable" means of making a living for many individuals, using the internet to sell items via post after purchasing them in person at retailers. Scalpers will use digital means to buy up product online and they also travel around shops, purchasing as much of a given item as they can and often emptying shelves before an actual consumer can reach them. This has forced hops to often implement measures to limit purchases which has in turn resulted in threats or acts of violence to staff of retailers or simple theft of "high value" items. I wish for the government to ban immediate (within 6 months of purchase) resale of items purchased from a seller at retail price (or equivalent) with no modification at inflated prices.

records.title: Increase the minimum sentence to life imprisonment for all sexual offences
records.description: Keep anyone convicted of sexual offences locked up for life if they abuse any child, woman or male. Because they have committed a heinous crime we believe they should be locked up for life because what they do to people affects the victims for life.
records.further_details: Because we believe there are too many sex offenders in our country who despite having previous convictions and sexual harm prevention orders and may be on the sex offenders register, they still continue to commit these crimes.

records.title: Require all schools to have at least 70 minutes of outdoor break time per day
records.description: Require all schools to have at least 70 minutes of break time per day. We believe that this will provide the necessary development of all young people and will prevent health issues associated with inadequate outdoor exposure.
records.further_details:
Time spent outdoors is essential for the health and wellbeing of young people. Outdoor activity supports physical/mental health, and reduces the risk of developing eye conditions such as myopia - which reduces overall quality of life. Studies suggest around one in three children suffer from myopia, with rates steadily increasing.
 
Regular outdoor time has been linked to improved physical/mental health and preventing myopia.
 
We believe many schools currently provide insufficient break time for young people.

records.title: Restore continuous hard shoulders on smart motorways
records.description: We call on the Government to restore permanent hard shoulders on all-lane running smart motorways, including the M4. We believe removing hard shoulders creates unnecessary danger for stranded motorists and for drivers forced to take evasive action at high speed.
records.further_details: Official parliamentary evidence found live-lane breakdowns are nearly four times more common on all-lane running motorways than on conventional motorways with hard shoulders & around 40% of breakdowns occur in a live lane. We feel that removing hard shoulders creates unnecessary danger for stranded motorists and for drivers forced to take evasive action at high speed. We believe that “controlled motorways” which retain hard shoulders while using smart traffic systems have lower casualty rates and should be adopted instead.

records.title: Prevent seizure of dogs verified as being under breed minimum height limits
records.description: We ask the Government to amend the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991 to make it unlawful for authorities to seize a dog based on visual breed "typing" if the owner provides professional veterinary certification that the dog fails the statutory minimum height requirements for that banned breed type.
records.further_details:
Currently, the definition of an XL Bully used under this law includes strict minimum height thresholds. However, many responsible owners of shorter, non-banned bully breeds (such as Pocket or Standard American Bullies) live in constant fear. Because application of the law relies heavily on subjective visual profiling, dogs with a "bully look" are at risk of being seized purely on appearance, even if they do not meet the height criteria.
 
We believe prohibiting seizure when veterinary proof of height is provided will save innocent pets.

records.title: Increase speed limits for vans on A roads in line with cars
records.description:
Van drivers are the backbone of thousands of UK businesses and many run to time sensitive deadlines.
Travelling 50 miles at 60mph instead of 70mph on a dual A road adds just over 7 minutes to your journey. Over an eight hour day this can amount to almost an hour.
records.further_details: Many dual A roads can be the same as dual motorway roads. In my experience, speed restrictions to vans can be a make or break if times are not met. I understand that safety is paramount but at what cost to the economy and people’s livelihood.

records.title: End taxpayer funding for diversity & inclusion initiatives in the public sector
records.description: End taxpayer funding for any Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (EDI) initiatives in all public bodies, including EDI roles, departments, programmes, and staff networks, to ensure all employees and citizens are treated equally under a single standard.
records.further_details: We believe public bodies should serve all citizens equally and remain politically neutral. We feel taxpayer-funded EDI roles, programmes and identity-based staff networks can create division and reduce confidence in fairness. We believe recruitment, promotion, training and public services should be based on merit, qualifications, performance and individual circumstances, with public funds focused on frontline services.

records.title: Instruct Natural England to change grazing rules to protect endangered species
records.description: The Government must get Natural England to change its grazing rules to take account of unique local circumstances & species, like Dartmoor’s native ponies which are under threat unless changes are made. New contracts could remove up to 90% of them. Ensure these endangered heritage ponies are exempt.
records.further_details: Dartmoor’s native hill ponies have lived on the moor for over 3,000 years. Numbers have collapsed from 7,000 to under 1,000 in 25 years. New 'Natural England' contracts treat them as livestock and could remove up to 90% of remaining herds. We urge the Government to exempt these endangered native ponies from the cuts and protect Britain’s heritage.

records.title: Make the Royal Family to pay inheritance & capital gains tax on private assets
records.description: Close the loophole that allows the Royal Family to not be subject to UK tax, and require them to pay inheritance tax and capital gains tax just as every other UK resident is.
records.further_details: The King inherited most of his late mother's wealth and when she died he did not pay any inheritance tax on the transfer of these private assets. This Royal loophole saved the King millions of pounds. With so much pressure on public finances, we believe these taxes could help fund public services. Oxfam states that the top 1% own more wealth than the bottom 95% of humanity. We believe our Royal Family should be 'an example' for their subjects, not here to take tax exemptions from those they serve.

records.title: Do not scrap the Parliament education outreach service
records.description: We urge Parliament to protect face-to-face Parliament outreach for adults. We believe these programmes improve political literacy, inclusion, and democratic engagement—especially for those who missed civic education. We feel cutting them is short-sighted; they should be expanded, not reduced.
records.further_details: We believe Parliament outreach tackles low political literacy across the UK. Many lack basic understanding of politics, voting rights, and engagement. In Further Education, we feel this gap is clear, with learners often excluded. In-person sessions provide accessible, trusted learning digital methods can’t match. At a time of high disengagement and possible votes at 16, we believe cuts should be paused and reviewed through consultation to assess their impact.

records.title: Make it an offence to allow off-lead dogs to approach dogs on leads
records.description: Make it an offence to allow off-lead dogs to approach dogs on leads without permission. Dogs may be on leads because they are nervous, reactive, elderly, injured, in training or assistance dogs. Unwanted approaches can cause stress, injury, training setbacks and dog fights.
records.further_details: Many dog owners have experienced off-lead dogs running over without invitation, including dogs that are aggressive, poorly controlled or have no recall. These situations can cause fear, injury, conflict and training setbacks. Owners whose dogs have previously been attacked or frightened may also feel anxious when unfamiliar dogs approach. This change could promote responsible ownership and help prevent avoidable incidents.

records.title: Require immediate custodial sentences for animal abuse, cruelty & neglect
records.description: Require courts to impose immediate custodial sentences for anyone convicted of serious animal abuse, cruelty or neglect to ensure stronger punishment, greater deterrence and better protection for animals. We feel fines are not sufficient.
records.further_details: Animal abuse and severe neglect cause significant suffering, yet many offenders often receive fines, suspended sentences or relatively short bans on keeping animals. We believe these penalties do not reflect the seriousness of the offence or act as an effective deterrent. The Government should introduce mandatory custodial sentences for those convicted of serious animal abuse, cruelty or neglect, alongside appropriate lifetime bans where necessary.

records.title: Create a statutory duty of care for communities hosting asylum seekers
records.description: Create a Home Office statutory duty of care for communities hosting asylum seekers and asylum accommodation. The Home Office has a statutory duty of care toward asylum seekers, but no equivalent duty toward local residents affected by asylum accommodation decisions.
records.further_details:
A statutory duty of care to local communities could require the Home Office to carry out genuine & early consultation with local authorities & residents & assess community impacts, including safety, cohesion & local resources.

A statutory duty of care could improve transparency & accountability in placement decisions; support both asylum seekers & the communities they join; ensure community consultation is not reduced to a procedural formality & that residents’ wellbeing is properly considered in all accommodation decisions.

records.title: Withdraw from the UN due to UN Commission findings against Israel in Gaza
records.description: The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel issued a report on 18 June 2026 accusing Israel of deliberately killing children in Gaza. Therefore, we feel the UK must withdraw from the UN.
records.further_details: We believe the UN Commission of Inquiry reporting that Israel deliberately kills children evokes the most vile antisemitic tropes of the Middle Ages and UK taxpayers should not be funding the UN.

records.title: Change motor trader warranty period from up to 6 months to 30 days
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce regulations to ensure motor trader dealer liability for vehicles sold is 30 days, and not up to 6 months. We believe that a 6-month liability period is not realistic for smaller dealerships.
records.further_details: We are concerned that the current legislation allows some consumers to misuse their vehicle, and then blame any faults on the dealer, which may then have to be repaired and paid for by dealership.

records.title: Apply tapered VAT on turnover over £85k & reduce VAT on food for hospitality
records.description: Save UK hospitality: reform VAT to protect jobs and small businesses. Introduce a progressive system: only apply VAT to turnover over the VAT threshold and taper VAT rates based on turnover. In addition, reduce VAT on food served in hospitality while maintaining the standard rate on drinks.
records.further_details: This would support growth, protect jobs, and help prevent closures across the sector. The current VAT system gives a barrier to growth for small businesses, forcing many to limit expansion or risk becoming unviable after crossing the £85,000 threshold. In hospitality and other sectors, rising costs and tight margins are driving closures. A modernised, progressive VAT system and reduced VAT on food would help businesses grow sustainably, protect local jobs, and strengthen communities while still supporting government tax revenue through continued business survival and employment.

records.title: Provide funding for affordable electric vehicle charging points in local areas
records.description: We call on the Government to provide funding for local authorities to urgently expand access to affordable on-street electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure, particularly for residents living in flats and properties without off-street parking.
records.further_details: At present, many EV owners without private parking must rely on public or car park chargers.
