These options are often significantly more expensive per kWh than home charging tariffs available to those with driveways. We feel this creates a clear inequality: households with private parking benefit from cheaper, more convenient overnight charging, while flat residents are forced to pay higher costs and face limited availability.

records.title: Mandatory Device Wiping for Convicted Revenge Porn and Domestic Abuse Offenders
records.description: Require devices containing any intimate or abusive content linked to the victims of domestic abuse or revenge porn offences to be permanently kept by police or professionally wiped before they are returned, helping protect victims from ongoing fear, trauma, and exploitation and control.
records.further_details: This petition calls for stronger legal protections for victims of domestic abuse and intimate image abuse (“revenge porn”). Devices proven to contain any intimate or abusive content linked to the victim of abuse offences should either be permanently retained by authorities or professionally wiped before return. Victims should not have to live in fear that offenders may still possess exploitative intimate material after conviction. The law must help prevent ongoing coercion, intimidation, and emotional harm.

records.title: Require employers to respond to job applicants and disclose salary in job ads
records.description: Require employers to respond to all job applicants within a set timeframe, and to include salary or salary range in all job adverts. Applicants often invest significant time applying, and we think the least they deserve is a reply and transparent pay information from the outset.
records.further_details:
In our experience some employers “ghost” applicants and hide salaries behind vague terms like "competitive" or "DOE", which in our view wastes job seekers' time and causing real financial stress. We therefore call on the Government to legislate two minimum standards:

1- Employers must notify all applicants of the outcome within a defined timeframe.
2- All job adverts must include a salary or salary range. The EU Pay Transparency Directive requires this from June 2026. The UK must not fall behind.

records.title: Hold a referendum on reinstating capital punishment
records.description: We call on Parliament to legislate to hold a national referendum on whether capital punishment should be reinstated for the most heinous crimes.
records.further_details: We believe there should be a national referendum on whether the most heinous crimes - particularly those involving extreme cruelty against innocent and defenceless victims — require a sanction beyond imprisonment.

records.title: Increase all inheritance tax thresholds: singles £1M, married couples £2M
records.description:
Increase inheritance thresholds:
Single person raise to £1,000,000
Married couple raise to £2,000,000
Tax free gifting £ 10,000
records.further_details: We believe inheritance tax thresholds are out of date, when average house price is around £500,000 in the South East, many people will be subjected to 40% IHT

records.title: Reinstate opt-in consent for trade union political fund contributions
records.description: Amend Section 62 of the Employment Rights Act 2025 to restore explicit opt-in consent before any subscription is allocated to a union political fund.
records.further_details:
Since 18 Feb 2026, new members pay automatically unless they opt out. This reverses the Trade Union Act 2016 principle that consent must be actively given. Political funds support party politics — we believe your money should only go there if you choose it.
 
Refunds should be available to those who opted out promptly but from whom funds were deducted without consent.

records.title: Keep open local Army Reserve Centres and reopen recently closed ones
records.description: We believe local Army Reserve Centres must be maintained and kept open and recently closed ones reopened to maintain Regimental and local links and accessibility with local Cadet units, instead of grouping unrelated units together in so-called 'Super ARCs'.
records.further_details: As well as erasing our history of service, we believe this places Cadet units and Reserve units too far away from their target audience. Leaving those most disadvantaged who could benefit the most unable to benefit as well as cutting community links and a shared history, which has the potential to cut recruitment across the services.

records.title: Review eligibility for one bedroom-rate LHA for those under 35 leaving prison
records.description: We believe that the shared accommodation rate for Local Housing Allowance is too low and can create an immediate barrier to finding safe and stable accommodation for many people under 35 years old who are unlikely to qualify for the one bedroom-rate, especially those newly released from prison.
records.further_details: The shared accommodation rate can make it challenging to find private rented accommodation, and we believe that this can result in a significant higher risk of homelessness. I therefore ask the government to review this policy and consider allowing people under 35 who are leaving prison to receive the one-bedroom rate Local Housing Allowance. I think this change would give people a fairer chance to find stable accommodation, avoid homelessness and reintegrate safely into the community.

records.title: Neurodiversity: Fund police training, review of police custody & data collection
records.description: Government to review treatment of neurodiverse individuals in police custody, and to introduce specialised training for police officers to better understand the needs of neurodivergent adults and young people in police custody for the purpose of reducing the risk of harm and preventable deaths.
records.further_details: The review should consider the prevalence of neurodevelopmental conditions in police custody deaths, serious incidents and restraint cases. A review should also consider whether a mandatory recording of neurodevelopmental conditions in custody settings alongside standardised recording of ND conditions in IOPC reporting categories should be mandated. Training for police officers and custody staff should include recognition of associated behaviours in neurodiverse individuals under stress.

records.title: Reverse NHS England's decision to make its code repositories closed-source.
records.description: Previously, the NHS Service Standard held that “public services are built with public money, so unless there's a good reason not to, the code they're based on should be made available for other people to reuse and build on.” This is what the current policy should be reverted to.
records.further_details:
NHS England has issued guidance, called SDLC-8, which requires that all source code repositories be private from the 11th of May, 2026, unless there is an exceptional need, approved by the Engineering Board.

The Free Software Foundation Europe have warned that open repositories allow security researchers to inspect and report vulnerabilities, and that de-publishing code does nothing to prevent attackers from analysing already-deployed systems, binaries, or previously copied source code.

records.title: Ban unsafe barbed wire fencing alongside public rights of way
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce legislation prohibiting the installation of new barbed wire fencing immediately adjacent to public rights of way, including footpaths, bridleways and byways.
records.further_details:
We also call on the Government to require that where existing barbed wire fencing alongside public rights of way becomes damaged, collapsed or requires replacement, it must be repaired using safer alternatives rather than new barbed wire.
 
We believe current laws do not provide sufficient protection from foreseeable injuries caused by hazardous fencing positioned next to routes regularly used by walkers, cyclists, horse riders, children and dogs. Poorly maintained fencing can cause serious and avoidable harm to people, pets, livestock and wildlife.
 
The law should better protect public safety while allowing landowners to secure their land using safer fencing options.

records.title: Fund a national support scheme for registered animal rescue organisations
records.description: Fund a national support scheme for registered animal rescue organisations, including those dedicated to helping cats. The scheme should include grant funding, assistance with veterinary costs, tax relief measures, and stronger partnerships between local authorities and rescue organisations.
records.further_details:
Many rescue organisations are operating beyond capacity, face rising vet costs, and face high numbers of animals needing help.

We believe the Government has not fully recognised the scale of this crisis. We feel the situation affecting cats has become increasingly severe, with rescues reporting unprecedented numbers of abandoned, stray and unwanted cats. Many rescue spaces are full and waiting lists grow. If it weren’t for the dedication of many rescue organisations, many sick & vulnerable animals would be left on the street to suffer and die.

records.title: Require all businesses to offer a cash alternative to digital payments
records.description: Require all businesses to offer a cash alternative to digital payments for people that can't pay online. Some people need to pay cash as that's all they have access to for various reasons. Online booking systems and card only can prevent some people from living life to the fullest.
records.further_details: Many businesses, including in entertainment, only take online card payments for bookings. Some people for various reasons, including those with disabilities or who are elderly, cannot book online as they have no bank card or no access, so therefore need to pay cash. This includes those who are supported by carers who need to pay cash and keep receipts. This causes restrictions in peoples lives and prevents them from living there life to the fullest and enjoying the same things as people that can do online or card only.

records.title: Government to review process for child removal decisions
records.description: We want the Government to review how child removal decisions are made under an interim care order, to establish processes to guarantee that they are based on verified evidence, proper safeguarding checks, and fair process.
records.further_details: There are concerns that children can be separated from a parent after unverified or false reports without a full and fair investigation. We believe stronger safeguards are needed to protect children’s welfare, ensure decisions are evidence-based, and make sure parents are treated fairly. This petition is about improving the process for all families

records.title: Require every bus to have at least 2 spaces for wheelchairs
records.description: My wife and I are both wheelchair users when we want to go anywhere it’s impossible for us both to go by bus because many bus companies around the country will only allow one wheelchair on a bus at a time. It means that if we want to go out together we have to use a train although we have a bus pass
records.further_details: Bus companies around the country must have only space for a wheelchair user on a bus. There are lots of couples that have to use another means of transport or travel on separate buses, this is totally unfair. My wife won’t travel on her own, so it’s impossible for us to use our bus passes together. What makes it worse is there is sometimes only one wheelchair space, but they will allow 3 pushchairs, walkers, luggage etc. We are in an age with equal rights, it’s time buses had 2 wheelchairs spaces.

records.title: Strengthen UK animal welfare laws on breeding, sales, and cruelty bans for life
records.description: We call for stronger UK animal welfare laws: licensing for all breeding (incl. rabbits), better enforcement of cat neutering from unlicensed breeders, tighter online kitten/puppy sales rules, and lifetime bans for serious or repeat animal cruelty.
records.further_details: We are calling for stronger UK animal welfare laws to prevent cruelty, neglect, and irresponsible breeding. We believe current rules do not go far enough to stop unregulated breeding, unwanted litters, and illegal or irresponsible online sales of kittens and puppies. We want stronger enforcement of breeding controls, clearer responsibility for cat neutering outside shelters, tighter online sales regulation, and lifetime bans for serious or repeat animal cruelty.

records.title: Fund Tactile Maps in Accessible Toilets for Blind/Visually Impaired People
records.description: Non-standard toilets in public places can cause anxiety for blind/visually impaired people. We call on Government to fund installation of low-cost Tactile Maps in accessible toilets showing room layouts, controls & safety cords on doors/walls to restore independence & create truly accessible spaces.
records.further_details: Navigating public toilets shouldn't be a stressful guessing game for blind or visually impaired people. Non-standardized layouts can often lead to confusion, anxiety, and accidentally pulling emergency cords.  We believe this will help make accessible toilets truly accessible. Public UK venues—such as schools, supermarkets, and transport hubs—should be funded to have installed low-cost Tactile Maps on toilet doors and walls. Featuring raised symbols, these maps would clearly outline layouts, controls, and safety switches, restoring independence.

records.title: Ban vaping in indoor public places and designated outdoor public spaces.
records.description: Ban vaping in indoor public places and designated outdoor public spaces, including transport waiting areas, children's play areas and building entrances, and introduce appropriate fixed penalty notices for breaches.
records.further_details: Vaping is widely used in indoor and outdoor public spaces, exposing others (including children) to second-hand aerosol and making it difficult for people to avoid. Vaping should be subject to restrictions similar to those that apply to smoking in these locations. Appropriate fixed penalty notices should be introduced to ensure the ban is effective and consistently enforced. This would help protect public health, improve air quality in shared spaces, and reduce the normalisation of vaping.

records.title: Make solar-shading improvements a permitted development for homes and workplaces
records.description: Change planning rules so external solar-shading measures e.g. awnings, canopies, brise soleil, external blinds and shutters are listed and treated as permitted development to help reduce overheating in homes and workplaces, including in conservation areas, if heritage-sensitive conditions are met.
records.further_details: UK homes are overheating as heatwaves intensify, putting health at risk, especially for older, disabled, low-income and medically vulnerable people. External shading can help cut solar gain before heat enters, reducing reliance on costly air conditioning. We are concerned that planning barriers, especially in conservation areas, make this harder for those least able to cope. We believe a clear permitted-development right for external solar-shading measures, with design safeguards, would support fair, low-carbon climate adaptation.

records.title: Make individuals convicted of manslaughter eligible under early release scheme
records.description: We are calling on the Government to ensure those convicted of manslaughter are included in the Government’s early release scheme. We believe eligible prisoners serving SDS/SDS+ sentences for manslaughter should receive the same release provisions as other eligible offences.
records.further_details: We want the Government to ensure those convicted of manslaughter are included in the Government’s early release scheme and are removed from the list of excluded offences. Eligible prisoners serving SDS/SDS+ sentences for manslaughter should receive the same release provisions as other eligible prisoners. We ask the Government to ensure their eligibility and the fair and consistent application of rules, including to prisoners already serving eligible sentences.

records.title: Require mandatory national security vetting for all MPs
records.description: Require all Members of Parliament to undergo mandatory national security vetting as a condition of taking and holding office, with a defined baseline clearance level for parliamentarians.
records.further_details: Parliamentarians hold significant power and may access sensitive information through their roles, even informally. Yet many civil servants and contractors are vetted while MPs are not. We are concerned that this inconsistency risks undermining national security and public confidence. We believe a mandatory vetting framework would align standards and ensure those in positions of highest authority meet appropriate security checks.

records.title: Establish a Royal Commission on Intolerance in UK society
records.description: A Royal Commission on Intolerance would document, seek to understand, and make recommendations to counter increasing intolerance within UK society. It should be non-party-political and broad-based, and should be independent of government.
records.further_details: Intolerance is on the rise in the UK: intolerance of people from different cultures, backgrounds, religions and orientations. There are regular reports of acts of violence committed against individuals and against organisations representing minorities. Tolerance of others helps keep society civilized; the current public discourse is poisoning much of what makes the UK a good place to be. We believe a Royal Commission, independent of party, can help create a consensus on actions to help stop intolerance.

records.title: Make air ambulances free from fuel duty and VAT on fuel
records.description: The Government should remove fuel tax and VAT on fuel for the air ambulance services especially for their helicopters but for their associated land vehicles} as well
records.further_details: Air ambulance services throughout the country are having to rely more and more on the generosity of the British public to support their services due to the rising fuel cost caused by what is happening in the Strait of Hormuz. We believe a suspension of the fuel duty and VAT would be a great financial help and could allow more responses by the air ambulance rather than the cars that they are increasingly having to use at the moment.

records.title: Fund minimum wage for student nurses for their 2300-hour NHS clinical practice
records.description: Many student nurses get into thousands of pounds worth of student debt, can’t work alongside placement and get worked to the core, up to 40 hours per week of unpaid work, plus they have to pay for their NMC PIN number at the end.
records.further_details: We believe student nurses need to be paid for the 2300 hours they work during placements. We feel every hour worked on placement deserves at least the same wage as the national minimum wage.

records.title: Seek legally binding international rules on military AI and autonomous weapons
records.description: From Ukraine to Gaza to Iran, AI-powered weapons are increasingly making life-and-death decisions. In November, the UN will decide whether to begin negotiations on new weapons rules. The UK must support a legally binding treaty and ensure meaningful human control over every use of force.
records.further_details:
Autonomous weapons systems can identify and engage targets with limited or no human intervention. As AI becomes increasingly integrated into military decision-making, the risk of machines being given greater control over life-and-death decisions is growing.
 
In November, states will meet at the UN in Geneva to consider whether to begin negotiations on new international rules for autonomous weapons. The UK must join the global push to control military AI and autonomous weapons.

records.title: Fund Increased Housing Support for Veterans and Service Families
records.description: We call on the UK Government to fund housing support and reform the Service Family Accommodation eviction processes to protect veterans from homelessness after discharge.
records.further_details:
Service families should not be leaving the Armed Forces only to face courtrooms, debt, and homelessness as their reward for service.

Funding should also be allocated to mandatory homelessness prevention reviews for veterans and service families, and for grants to help cover council tax for those who require it. We believe that families with children, disabilities, and additional needs should not be forced into homelessness after service, and that veterans deserve stability, dignity, and proper support—not court orders, debt, and eviction after serving Great Britain.

records.title: Introduce a national Climate Resilient Schools Programme to protect education
records.description: Introduce a national Climate Resilient Schools Programme to ensure no child's education is disrupted by heatwaves, flooding or other extreme weather by funding school retrofits, resilience measures, adaptation planning and staff training.
records.further_details: Children should not lose learning because school buildings cannot cope with increasingly frequent heatwaves, flooding or other extreme weather. Many schools lack adequate cooling, ventilation and flood resilience. We call on the Government to fund school retrofits, climate adaptation plans, resilience training and safe learning standards so every child can access uninterrupted, safe education regardless of the weather.

records.title: Make accepted property offers binding and require compensation if withdrawn
records.description: Require accepted offers on residential property in England and Wales to become legally binding subject to conditions, such as satisfactory surveys and mortgage approval, and require a party who withdraws without good reason to compensate the other for costs, including legal and survey fees.
records.further_details: Property transactions in England and Wales often fall through after offers are accepted, sometimes late in the process. This can leave buyers and sellers losing thousands in fees with no consequence for the party who withdraws. In Scotland, accepted offers are binding subject to conditions, reducing fall-throughs. We believe a similar system, with compensation for unreasonable withdrawal, would make transactions more secure and fairer.

records.title: Make failure to report a child’s disclosure of abuse or harm a criminal offence
records.description: We call on the Government to make it a criminal offence for professionals working with children to fail to report a child’s disclosure of abuse, assault, neglect or other criminal harm. With no legal duty to record or report disclosures, concerns may go unreported without independent oversight.
records.further_details: The Crime and Policing Act 2026 creates a duty to report child sexual abuse, but it does not cover physical assault, neglect or wider criminal harm, and it introduces no criminal penalty for failing to act. There is currently no legal duty to record or report a child’s disclosure, meaning some families only become aware of unreported concerns when later accessing records. We think this should be called Luke’s Law.

records.title: Review BMI Use in NHS Treatment Decisions
records.description: We believe BMI is an outdated system that judges health using only height and weight. It ignores fitness, lifestyle and body composition, and can affect NHS treatment access and waiting list priority.
records.further_details: We call on the Government to review the use of BMI with a view to its being replaced with fairer, evidence-based health assessments.  We believe  that BMI is an outdated method of measuring health that relies only on height and weight only, while ignoring fitness, muscle mass, lifestyle and overall wellbeing. It can often label healthy people as obese and is often used to determine NHS treatment access and waiting list priority, unfairly delaying care for some patients. Health assessments should reflect modern science, individual circumstances and overall health, not just a number on a scale. Health is more than height and weight.

records.title: New permanent residence visa for skilled workers with no access to benefits
records.description: Create a new permanent residence visa with no access to benefits for existing skilled workers as a transitional arrangement under the earned settlement scheme.
records.further_details: In our view government plans to change settlement rules leave current Skilled Worker visa holders in crisis. These workers moved here trusting the government. Because they cannot go back in time to alter past choices, wages, or contracts, applying new rules to them mid-way is unfair. We therefore call on the Government to create a new permanent residence visa with no access to benefits for existing skilled workers as a transitional arrangement under earned settlement scheme.

records.title: Do not give elected mayors powers to overrule local council planning decisions
records.description: We want planning decisions to remain with local planning authorities and elected councillors.
records.further_details: We want planning decisions to remain with local planning authorities and elected councillors. We believe local communities should have a direct say in developments affecting their area through their local council. Giving metro mayors powers to call in, determine, or overrule major planning applications could reduce local democratic accountability and weaken community influence. We therefore call on the Government to keep planning decisions under local authority control.

records.title: Fund free dental treatment on the NHS for all cancer patients on treatment
records.description:
Unfortunately, on average 400,000 people are diagnosed with cancer each year in the uk.
Some drugs used in treatment can affect the teeth and jaws.
This is why dental treatment should be on the NHS for the duration of treatment.

records.title: Introduce license requirement for pet sitters and dog walkers
records.description: Introduce stricter controls on who can provide pet care services such as licenses required to provide any pet care related services as a business. Many of us have worked hard for qualifications and are now being muscled out of our industry by children and retired people who offer services for free.
records.further_details: In our experience, the pet care industry is being flooded by retired and young people (kids) offering free or substantially discounted services. We believe this is affectively pushing out those who have qualifications and the knowledge, forcing them to close business, while continuing to make walking dogs harder and less safe for members of the public and hard workers in the industry due to people who can't control dogs having responsibility over them.

records.title: Abolish VAT on bottled water
records.description: UK government classifies bottled water akin to soft drinks, subjecting it to Value Added Tax (VAT). Meanwhile, tap water is considered essential to life, and is exempt from VAT.
records.further_details:
I feel there seems to be a disconnect in recognising that natural mineral water and spring water are, in my view, more vital for health.
 
We think public trust in water regulators and providers in England and Wales is in decline, driven by concerns over sewage, pollution, and the perception that companies prioritise shareholder interests over the environment and customers.
Tap water is the cheapest water you can consume, natural mineral and spring waters are the premium of the category and the most expensive, and should not be subject to VAT.

records.title: Fund the creation of specialist autistic and PDA schools
records.description: We want the Government to fund the creation of new flexible specialist schools for autistic children, particularly those with a Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA) profile, who cannot access mainstream or traditional special schools.
records.further_details:
We believe children who experience severe anxiety, sensory difficulties and demand avoidance need education that adapts to them, including:
1.	Small, sensory-friendly settings
2.	Autism and PDA-trained staff
3.	Flexible attendance and reduced demands
4.	Greater choice and individualised learning
Children should not have to reach crisis point or lose years of education before receiving appropriate support. Every child deserves an education that works for them and enables them to reach their potential.

records.title: Introduce lifetime bans for all animal abusers and DBS checks for pet sitters
records.description: Recent cases of animal abuse, including those trusted to care for pets, have exposed gaps in current protections. There is no legal requirement for pet sitters to undergo background checks, and no formal system to prevent individuals with a history of animal cruelty from working with animals.
records.further_details:
Data from the RSPCA shows that thousands of cruelty complaints are investigated each year, with hundreds of prosecutions, yet we believe sentencing outcomes remain inconsistent and often do not act as a sufficient deterrent. Currently, there is:
• No requirement for background checks for those working with animals
• No automatic lifetime bans for the most serious offenders
• No system to ensure offenders are prevented from reoffending in animal care roles

records.title: Keep the legal age to buy tobacco at 18
records.description: Keep the legal age to buy tobacco at 18 and do not introduce a rolling age ban that permanently restricts future adults. Maintain current laws rather than creating a generational ban on legal tobacco sales.
records.further_details: A rolling age ban would treat adults differently based only on their birth year, which we believe is unfair and inconsistent. Adults aged 18 and over should have equal legal rights. Existing laws already restrict access for under-18s, and we think enforcement of that should remain the focus rather than introducing new long-term restrictions.

records.title: Introduce a no-halfway housing zone around schools
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce a no-halfway housing zone around schools to ensure that students feel safe getting to school.
records.further_details: My whole life I have lived next door to a halfway house, and I have had many poor experiences. I feel it makes the area feel less safe, and I don’t think children should have to walk through this to get to school.

records.title: Introduce enforceable processing deadlines and review oversight for CICA claims
records.description: We want the Government to introduce enforceable time limits for CICA claims, require early evidence requests, apply balanced deadlines to both applicants and CICA, publish clear processing time data, and review oversight of cases exceeding stated targets.
records.further_details: Many applicants to the Criminal Injuries Compensation Authority experience prolonged delays and unclear timelines. While claimants must meet strict deadlines, CICA operates mainly under non-binding targets, meaning cases can take years to resolve. We believe introducing enforceable time limits and greater transparency would improve fairness, accountability, and confidence in a scheme intended to support victims of violent crime.

records.title: Introduce guidance on provision or adaptation of stoma-friendly toilets
records.description: Over 200,000 people live with a stoma in  the UK, yet public toilets do not meet their needs. Many face stigma or are challenged when using disabled toilets. People with stomas need safe, hygienic facilities to manage their condition with dignity.
records.further_details: We call on the UK Government to issue robust guidance to ensure greater provision of stoma-friendly toilet facilities. Where new facilities are not possible, existing disabled toilets could be adapted with shelves, appropriate waste bins, accessible sinks, and sufficient space. Current facilities are often unsuitable and unreliable for safe ostomy care. Countries such as Japan already provide better support. Strong national guidance is needed to ensure consistent provision and dignity for people with stomas.

records.title: Stop convicted domestic abusers from using divorce proceedings to continue abuse
records.description: Change divorce law so victims of domestic abuse can finalise a divorce without obstruction by a convicted abuser
records.further_details:
I am calling on the UK Government to change divorce law to prevent convicted domestic abusers from using divorce proceedings to continue coercive control.
Victims can remain legally and financially tied to their abusers when proceedings are delayed or obstructed. I am asking the Government to introduce safeguards allowing victims to finalise a divorce without delay where the other party has been convicted of domestic abuse against them.

records.title: Review animal cruelty sentencing & enforcement and publish an action plan
records.description: We call on the Government to commission an independent review of the legal framework for animal cruelty sentencing and enforcement following 2021 sentencing reforms.
records.further_details:
If the review identifies shortcomings, an action plan should be published to improve sentencing consistency, strengthen enforcement and better protect animals.
 
Parliament increased the maximum sentence for the most serious animal cruelty offences in 2021. We welcome this change, but many people remain concerned that sentencing and enforcement do not always reflect the seriousness of deliberate animal cruelty. We ask the Government to review whether current sentencing and enforcement are achieving their intended purpose and introduce evidence-based improvements where necessary.

records.title: Reform the National Kidney Transplant List and Remove the Matchability Score
records.description: Remove the matchability score from the national transplant criteria and introduce a 3 tier approach rather than 2 tier. Tier A - 100CRF and 7plus years waiting, Tier B - Once you move past the average 2.5/3 year wait, Tier C everyone else
records.further_details: We believe the current 2 tier approach is not fit for purspose. We understand that there should be a tier A to support those with extreme situations such as 100CRF and 7plus years waiting, but currently with the matchability score which is where anyone on the list is run against a donor pool of the last 10000 donors and given a matchability score. If you are given a 10 you are moved to tier A the higher the number you get the more points you are given. 10000 equates to 0.018% roughly of the population.

records.title: Mandatory Custodial Sentence for Sexual Violence with a Weapon at any Age
records.description: Introduce a statutory minimum custodial sentence for any sexual offence under the Sexual Offences Act 2003 where the offender used, threatened, or carried a weapon. Remove age as a bar to custody in these cases.
records.further_details:
Sexual violence is recognised by the UK Government as a weapon of war and one of the most serious violations of human rights. We believe the use of a weapon in a sexual offence demonstrates premeditation, extreme threat to life, and lasting trauma for victims.

Yet sentencing guidelines allow significant judicial discretion, and age can be used as a mitigating factor even in cases involving weapons so the offender avoids prison. We believe this undermines public confidence and fails survivors.

records.title: Do Not Tax Uninvested Cash Held Within Stocks and Shares ISAs
records.description: Retain the full tax-free status of Stocks and Shares ISAs by cancelling the planned 22% tax on interest earned from uninvested cash held within these accounts from April 2027 onwards.
records.further_details: Stocks and Shares ISAs have always been promoted as tax-free savings and investment accounts. Taxing uninvested cash would undermine trust in the ISA system and penalise savers who temporarily hold cash while managing risk, moving between investments, or waiting for suitable opportunities.

records.title: Allow parents to receive cash equivalent to childcare support if they prefer
records.description: Give parents a choice in how they use Government childcare support. Instead of only funding childcare, give eligible parents the option to receive equivalent financial support to stay at home and care for their own baby or young child. Let parents choose what is best for their family.
records.further_details: Every family is different, and parents should have a genuine choice in how they use Government childcare support. Instead of only funding childcare, give eligible parents the option to receive equivalent financial support to stay at home and care for their own baby or young child. Let parents choose what is best for their family: childcare or more time at home.

records.title: Review and expand the definition of rape in law
records.description: Currently, under the law, men and women who are sexually assaulted by women cannot be seen as rape victims due to a definition focused on penetration with a penis, even though many people view this as rape. Female perpetrators can only be charged with other sexual offences. We think this is wrong.
records.further_details: The law should change to include all perpetrators. The government has a large majority and could expand the law or change it entirely to something gender neutral such as any form of sex that is without consent. We think this would better recognise victims in the law and would mean all victims are taken more seriously but is only the first step to support victims. We think the government could easily do this. If you sign this, you could contribute to it being in public debate and to there being the stated change.

records.title: Make it a legal duty to help someone found unconscious in public
records.description: We believe there should be a law that makes it illegal to walk past someone unconscious in the street, as is the case in certain countries, without at least calling an ambulance. This could potentially save someone’s life.
records.further_details:
In November 2023, my younger brother collapsed outside a neighbour’s house on the pavement. We could not see him from our living room window, nor did we know he had collapsed because there is a wall in said neighbour’s front garden and he was on the other side on the pavement. 
 
He was eventually brought into our home where he collapsed and died suddenly. We believe a legal duty to help someone found unconscious in public could have helped him and could help other cases like this.

records.title: Ban MPs from drinking alcohol when the House of Commons is sitting
records.description: Stop allowing MPs to drink alcohol when the House is sitting. MPs should not be able to drink alcohol whilst the House of Commons is in session.

records.title: Allow all public sector employees to stand as local councillors
records.description: We call on the Government to review Section 80 of the Local Government Act 1972 so eligibility rules reflect modern working lives. We believe public servants shouldn't be prevented from standing for local election as clear guidance & proportionate safeguards can protect democracy & public confidence
records.further_details: We are requesting the Government to remove barriers preventing public sector employees from standing and serving as local councillors once elected. Teachers, further education staff, and workers in essential services such as water, fire, and ambulance services dedicate their lives to their Local Authority and supporting communities. We believe that allowing them to contribute through local government would strengthen democracy, improve representation, and bring valuable experience into local decision-making.

records.title: Review laws relating to public filming intended to humiliate, bully or profit
records.description: Launch a review into laws relating to public filming intended to humiliate, bully or profit, which looks into closing any loopholes that allow people to secretly film and harass vulnerable people for hate and profit.
records.further_details:
We feel current laws are too weak and need to be updated to protect victims and prevent exploitation. We believe there are individuals and groups that are weaponising public filming to target women, children, LGBTQ+ individuals, and minorities. Many film without consent, share content to spread hate and profit, and cause real harm psychological trauma, fear, and even real-world violence.
 
We believe this isn’t an isolated issue - it’s a growing trend across the UK and we need stronger protections now as current laws are failing to stop it.

records.title: Review mandatory TB testing in Cattle
records.description: We are concerned that some cattle that have to be culled under current regulations may not have TB. The impact on farmers can be financially crippling. We think it time to review and improve the current system.

records.title: Make Contempt of Parliament a Criminal Offence
records.description: Currently The House of Commons typically refers allegations of contempt to the Committee of Privileges, a cross-party committee that investigates and reports on the matter. While historical powers once allowed for imprisonment. This needs to change to make it a Criminal Offence.
records.further_details:
Currently, "Contempt of Parliament"— for example misleading a House or refusing to testify—is not a criminal offence. We argue that Parliament’s ancient powers to punish contempt are now unenforceable, that this creates an accountability gap, and that witnesses can obstruct democracy without the legal consequences that might apply in a Court of Law.
 
We call for contempt of Parliament to be made a statutory criminal offence to:
 
Ensure Select Committees can compel evidence and are not mislead.
Show no one is above democratic oversight.

records.title: Require Local Authority to scan cats and dogs if found deceased
records.description: Require all Local Authorities to scan the microchip of cats and dogs if found deceased. So many pets go missing and although it is a requirement on responsible owners like myself to make sure they are microchipped, I believe that not all deceased pets are scanned. This must be addressed.
records.further_details: I call on the Government to make it a legal requirement for all deceased dogs and cats to be scanned after they have been found. I think this could stop the heartbreaking continued search for lost family members! My cat has been missing 5 weeks and only learned recently the microchip might not bring him back if picked up by the local council

records.title: Make subscription auto-renewal without clear renewal consent illegal.
records.description: Many people sign up to services that renew automatically without a clear reminder or fresh consent. People forget, their circumstances change, and they are then tied into another term and charged again when they may no longer want or use the service.
records.further_details: Subscriptions should have a maximum initial sign-up period of 3 months, followed by no more than 1 month’s notice to cancel. This would stop businesses locking people into long terms through automatic renewals, confusing conditions, and excessive small print that most ordinary customers cannot reasonably be expected to interpret.

records.title: Government must issue guidance on HGV re-routing across community boundaries
records.description: We believe there is a widespread problem of unmanaged HGV routing, where restrictions in one area simply displace traffic into neighbouring communities. Without Government guidance and oversight, we believe this creates unfair, inconsistent outcomes, increased pollution, and road safety risks.
records.further_details: A coordinated approach is therefore needed to ensure freight is managed fairly and sustainably across regions, rather than shifting the burden from one community to another. Byfleet, for example, already carries what we feel is disproportionate HGV traffic due to existing restrictions. Further diversions from New Haw, Woodham and Row Town would increase pollution, noise and safety risks. Change such as these should require a full impact assessment and a coordinated, borough-wide HGV strategy instead of just shifting the problem elsewhere.

records.title: Align legal protections for Cohabiting Couples with those for Married Couples
records.description: I call on the Government to urgently update family law, which has not been substantially changed in respect of adult relationships since 1973, to reflect modern developments. Long-term cohabiting couples with children should have financial & legal protection on separation similar to married couples.
records.further_details: I believe the current law is outdated, fragmented and unfair. Unmarried couples must rely on multiple legal routes CAO, TOLATA, and Schedule 1 child proceedings, often requiring separate costly court cases with inconsistent outcomes – leaving long-term partners and children without clear protection. A Private Member’s Bill on cohabitation reform has been introduced in the past but not passed. In some cases of domestic abuse, refusal to marry can leave one partner exposed, vulnerable and financially unprotected.

records.title: Amend law to extend statutory guidance on emergency injectors to early years
records.description: Access to appropriate allergy medication, such as adrenaline auto-injectors, can be more limited in early years settings compared to schools. The law needs to be changed to allow the statutory guidance to enter force in September 2026 to cover early years settings as well as schools.
records.further_details: In early years settings, children are frequently introduced to foods they may not have previously encountered. This increased exposure raises the likelihood of a child experiencing an allergic reaction for the first time while in care. Given the potential severity of allergic reactions, including life-threatening anaphylaxis, we believe it is essential that early years environments are equipped to respond promptly and effectively, with training and access to emergency medication.

records.title: Review the national framework governing the school year in England
records.description: Review if legislation and regulations governing the number and distribution of school days and holidays remain appropriate, including the role of school employers in setting term dates. Issue guidance or legislate if changes are needed.
records.further_details:
The review should consider alternative models to the typical school year, including requiring local authorities and other school employers to redistribute some summer holiday time across the academic year.
 
The current typical school year can create significant pressures for children and families. We want Government to assess its impact on children’s wellbeing, SEND, childcare affordability, parents’ ability to work and family finances, alongside educational outcomes and staff wellbeing. The same number of school days could potentially be distributed differently.

records.title: Review parental responsibility for their child’s violent behaviour
records.description: We ask the Government to review and strengthen laws so that when young people repeatedly carry weapons or commit violent crimes, and parents fail to act, there are appropriate consequences for parents such as penalties or mandatory interventions to help prevent further harm and protect communities.
records.further_details: We are calling for greater accountability when young people repeatedly carry weapons or commit violent crimes. This is not about blaming every parent, but when warning signs are ignored and behaviour continues, we believe there must be consequences. Parents can be fined for taking children on holiday in term time, so we ask the Government to consider introducing penalties for parents if they are found to have ignored repeated violent behaviour.

records.title: Fund an NHS fast-track route for ADHD/autism diagnosis, care, and treatment
records.description: Fund a fast-track route in the NHS to end years-long waits for ADHD and autism care. Guarantee fast diagnosis, timely treatment, and fair NHS access so patients aren’t denied prescriptions after private diagnosis. Stop the postcode inequality and fix a system that is failing thousands.
records.further_details: We believe people with ADHD and autism are being failed by a system that delays diagnosis for years, worsening mental health, education, and employment outcomes. Even after diagnosis, access to treatment is often slow or blocked, especially when GPs refuse shared care. This creates inequality and forces people to pay privately or go without help. Reform is needed to ensure timely, fair, and consistent care for all.

records.title: Fund and implement A Universal Basic Income (UBI)
records.description: We believe that we are in an era of economic uncertainty, growing inequality, and job insecurity and it is time for Parliament to introduce a Universal Basic Income (UBI). Some Economists argue, UBI is not just a welfare measure, it is an investment in people, and a foundation for economic security.
records.further_details:
We believe that a guaranteed, unconditional income would empower individuals, providing them with dignity and freedom from financial precariousness. It could support entrepreneurs, artists, and caregivers, those whose work we think is often undervalued yet essential to our society. UBI could reduce stress, improve mental health, offer a safety net in an age of automation and unstable employment.
 
We think UBI is a progressive, pragmatic solution to modern economic challenges, in contrast to systems that oppress and humiliate.

records.title: Statutory NHS passports for all children & young adults who are disabled
records.description: We are calling for a national statutory Health & Needs Passport, available in both digital and paper formats. The digital version would be accessible across the NHS, and the paper version would provide a quick access summary with a QR code linking to the full medical record.
records.further_details: Parents of disabled children and young adults are repeatedly asked to retell their child’s full medical history at every appointment. This can be exhausting & retraumatising, and lead to inconsistent care. This new system should ensure professionals have immediate, accurate information — reducing repetition and improving care. No parent should have to relive their child’s entire medical journey at each & every appointment.

records.title: More police powers to restrict intimidating protests near asylum accommodation
records.description: We want the UK Government to amend the Public Order Act 1986 to give police specific powers to impose conditions on protests near accommodation housing asylum seekers, where they reasonably believe a protest may intimidate residents and thereby deter them from safely entering or leaving.
records.further_details: Specifically, we want sections 12, 14 and 14ZA amended. Section 164 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026 introduced similar protections for protests near places of worship. We believe this should extend to asylum accommodation. Whatever someone’s views on asylum and immigration policy, we feel that asylum seekers should be able to enter and leave where they live without intimidation from protests immediately outside. They are not responsible for asylum policy and generally have no choice over where they are housed.

records.title: Create a public register of UK nationals serving in foreign militaries
records.description: We call on the Government to establish a public register of British citizens, including dual nationals, and UK residents serving in foreign armed forces. This should apply to all levels of engagement: active-duty combatants, reservists and any providing secondary or logistical support.
records.further_details: UK citizens’ participation in foreign military operations lacks transparency. We believe that to ensure compliance with the Geneva Conventions and the International Criminal Court Act 2001, we need a public record of all UK-linked service (direct or secondary). A register would assist the Metropolitan Police War Crimes Unit in monitoring returning individuals. We think this is essential to uphold international law and ensure that no British persons are involved in activities breaching human rights.

records.title: Strengthen wildfire response - funding for dedicated firefighting aircraft
records.description: Wildfires are becoming more frequent and more severe due to hotter, drier weather. Fire and Rescue Services often have to rely solely on ground crews, which can struggle to reach fires in remote areas such as moorland, forests and mountains.
records.further_details: Wildfires are becoming more frequent and severe, putting lives, homes, wildlife and firefighters at greater risk. Many countries use dedicated firefighting aircraft to tackle large fires quickly, but we do not have a national fleet. The Government should fund and establish dedicated firefighting aircraft to support Fire and Rescue Services and improve our response to wildfires.

records.title: Restrict data centre building & energy use
records.description: We believe the rate in which data centres are being built in the UK means there are little to no restrictions on them. We call for new nationwide regulations on data centres to minimise local and environmental impacts.
records.further_details: The proposal for restrictions, inspired by Australia, should include: requiring data centres fund their own grid connections and add as much new power to the grid as they consume, strictly consume renewable energy only or be fined, not be built within close proximity of schools or residential neighbourhoods, do not cause excess noise/light pollution that disturb local wildlife habitats, a 20% Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG), and a ban on their construction in the event of a drought/water shortage.

records.title: Allow people to take an oath of allegiance to the UK instead of the Crown
records.description: Allow members of the armed forces, the police, judges, and MPs to take an oath of allegiance to the nation (Great Britain and Northern Ireland), instead of the King. We believe that in a democracy, you swear allegiance to a people, whereas in a dictatorship, you swear allegiance to a single person.
records.further_details: Britain is one of the few countries in Europe where you take an oath of allegiance to the King. In 2012, the Sovereign Grant replaced the Civil List together with other grants. In 2012/2013, the Sovereign Grant was £31 million. In 2025/2026, the Sovereign Grant is £132.1 million. We can’t complete HS2, in spite of substantial revenues from North Sea oil. Other countries have completed high speed rail links without North Sea oil.

records.title: Issue national guidelines on exam preparation information
records.description: Introduce guidelines on publishing information relating to exam questions to make sure students are not misled by incorrect information. Such guidelines should include restrictions on publishing what are claimed to be "predicted papers" & make the publisher responsible for inaccurate advice provided
records.further_details: During exam season, many students are exposed to online content claiming to predict exam questions. Such information can for example encourage students to omit key topics from their revision or promise results through “hacks”. Much of this is information can be misleading, and creates unnecessary stress or false confidence for students who can waste valuable revision time and money on unreliable materials. We think clear guidelines could protect students, support fair preparation, and ensure accountability across online education platforms.

records.title: Fund more NHS support for gynaecological disorders and reduce diagnosis delays
records.description: We call on the Government to fund improved NHS support for gynaecological disorders and reduced diagnosis delays.
records.further_details: Thousands of women and people with gynaecological conditions wait years for diagnosis, and many suffer severe pain, fatigue, infertility and poor mental health. Delays can worsen symptoms and reduce quality of life. Faster diagnosis and better NHS treatment could prevent long-term complications and help people remain in work and education.

records.title: Change how people can qualify for carers allowance
records.description: We want the Government to grant an additional allowance for individuals who care for more than one person and to raise the £204 earnings limit to allow for more carers to get the help they need. You can still care 35 hours a week and work part time, yet doing so puts many people over the threshold.
records.further_details: We believe it is unfair that an individual cannot get a job due to caring for multiple family members yet can only claim benefits for one of them. You can still work long hours and then care for someone consistently as soon as you are home which is mentally and physically draining but the system then says you don’t qualify if you earn too much!

records.title: Require a general election if an MP elected via a by-election becomes PM
records.description: An MP elected via a by-election can become Prime Minister through an internal party contest alone. We want legislation requiring a general election within 3 months of an MP ascending to the office of PM if they were elected to the Commons in a by-election.
records.further_details:
We believe public trust in politicians is too low to assume electing an MP means accepting whoever their party later picks as leader — especially an MP not elected in a general election. 
 
A by-election winner can become PM via internal party vote alone, with no national level public vote of any kind. We ask Parliament to pass legislation requiring a general election within 3 months if any MP is elected via a by-election and then becomes PM. This law would not affect MPs elected in General Elections who then become PM mid-term, nor party leadership rules themselves.

records.title: Ban sexual AI chatbots
records.description: We are concerned about sexual AI chatbots having a catalogue featuring realistic people, which are used for sexual pleasure. We believe there is no way to block children from accessing material on sexual AI chatbots, which can severely damage the way kids think.
records.further_details: We call for the Government to ban sexual AI chatbots to fix this. We are concerned about the possibility of real people, who have uploaded their faces on the internet for mostly wholesome reasons, then being used by sexual AI chatbots in scenarios where you can do anything to them in virtual roleplay. We believe this is wrong and that it is practically the same as using AI to make sexual images of real people.

records.title: Introduce prison sentences for water company executives guilty of sewage spills
records.description: We call on the Government to pass a law which introduces prison sentences for water company directors and senior executives whose companies are guilty of illegally discharging sewage into bodies of water.
records.further_details: The Government should legislate to make water company directors and senior executives personally criminally liable for serious or repeated illegal sewage spills. Those found to have knowingly, recklessly or through gross negligence allowed unlawful discharges should face prison sentences where environmental laws have been repeatedly breached.

records.title: Add lifelong congenital heart disease to the NHS prescription exemption list
records.description: We want the Government to add congenital heart disease to the NHS medical exemption list so people who rely on lifelong, essential medication because of a heart condition they were born with can receive prescriptions free of charge in England.
records.further_details: People born with congenital heart disease may need lifelong, essential medication to stay well and prevent deterioration, yet CHD is not included on England’s medical exemption list. Some patients require complex surgery, repeated procedures and even heart transplant assessment. They should not face ongoing prescription charges for treatment they have no choice but to take, especially when prescriptions are free for everyone in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

records.title: Introduce a partial-capacity disability benefit for those reducing work hours
records.description: We want the Government to introduce a ongoing disability benefit to top up the income of working individuals with chronic illnesses who need to reduce their hours on medical advice, without facing financial hardship.
records.further_details: The UK benefits system can trap workers with chronic illnesses like fibromyalgia. Many can do daily tasks independently, making them ineligible for PIP. Yet, full-time work can cause severe pain and exhaustion. When occupational health advises reducing hours, they face a major pay cut. Means-tested benefits like Universal Credit are blocked if a partner earns well, leaving them trapped. We believe workers shouldn't have to break their bodies to pay bills - we need a financial bridge to support partial hours.

records.title: Require food labels to disclose painful procedures done without pain relief
records.description: Switzerland requires food labels to state when animals underwent painful procedures - such as castration or dehorning - without pain relief. We ask the UK Government to introduce similar mandatory labelling for meat, milk and dairy, so shoppers can make an informed choice.
records.further_details: Switzerland's law covers farming procedures but not slaughter. The UK already tracks stunning methods used at every abattoir through FSA surveys - this data already exists. We ask Government to require it on the label: how an animal was killed, whether it was rendered unconscious first, and whether it received any pain relief - for every method, not just some, so shoppers see the full truth and not part of it.

records.title: Make Tree Preservation Orders mandatory to protect all trees across the UK
records.description: To benefit the environment, health and wildlife make TPO (Tree preservation orders) compulsory across the whole of the UK. When on occasion a tree might need to be removed, then permission should be sought from the Council. This should apply to all trees in all areas. On private and public land.
records.further_details:
As trees are so vital for human health, the environment and wildlife it is crucial that they are protected.
Apart from the many other benefits from trees they are also known to give off phytoncides ( chemical compounds) that when released can boost the human immune system.
While there are Government and other funded tree planting schemes going on, there needs to be more to protect trees from unnecessarily removal.

records.title: Increase tax allowance to £15,000 for 80 yrs+ and remove 25p age addition
records.description: Raise the personal allowance at 80years to £15,000 and thereafter in line with inflation every 2 years. Abolish the 25p raise at 80 yrs. the weekly 25p has not increased with the cost of living since 1971 introduction. When it was roughly 4% of the £6 weekly pension.
records.further_details: Raising a frozen tax threshold aims at addressing financial pressures. The freezing has created a tax burden for many - e.g dragged into filling in a self assessment for first time because of small tax payments due to the freeze. A 15,000 threshold would protect many from this tax burden. Over Eighties face higher expenses related to health, care, and heating. An increased, tax-free threshold allows them to keep more of their income to cover these essentials. Not seeing it "vanish" to taxes.”

records.title: Amend the Civil Aviation Act 1982 to remove airport immunity from civil claims
records.description: Amend Section 76 of the Civil Aviation Act 1982 to remove the immunity of airports from nuisance/trespass claims where Satellite/PBN navigation is used. We also want a new statutory process allowing citizens to trigger flight path reviews via GP-certified medical evidence of noise suffering.
records.further_details: Current law assumes distributed noise. Modern Satellite (PBN) navigation concentrates noise onto a single "rail," which can inadvertently lead to ‘precision-targeting’ specific homes with 100% accuracy. This creates the equivalent to a clinical "Course of Conduct" that can aggravates severe health issues like Tinnitus & Anxiety. Because airports are immune from civil suits, residents have no legal redress for this. We believe the Government Parliament must restore the right to sue for nuisance and mandate path changes where medical harm is proven by a GP.

records.title: Fund access to regular heart health checks & improve awareness of heart health
records.description: Fund regular heart health checks every 2-3 years to improve early detection of heart defects. Increase awareness of symptoms and risk factors.
records.further_details: We think there aren't enough checks and regular testing being done for the heart. Heart disease is one of the biggest killers. My younger brother passed away in his sleep at age 33 due to a heart problem which he never knew about. More needs to be done.

records.title: Allow full transfer of Marriage Allowance in one-worker families
records.description: Allow the full transfer of personal tax allowance between married couples. We believe the current rules discriminate against couples with one earner. We feel it is not fair if the breadwinner is earning little over the personal tax allowance and is the only provider for both.
records.further_details: If only one partner of a married couple is working and providing for the dependent other, and is only earning a minimum salary £12.71 per hour (around £26,400 per year}, we believe it is unfair for them not to be able to benefit from the full personal allowance of the married partner. It seems grossly unfair to us to expect them to subsidise through part of their tax the benefits received by a similar family whose household income on benefits exceeds their own. We believe this injustice would be rectified easily with this proposed transfer rule.

records.title: Fund the procurement & delivery of insulin and diabetes supplies to Gaza
records.description: We are asking the UK Government to fund the procurement and delivery of insulin and diabetes supplies to Gaza without interruption, as insulin is a life-saving medicine for people with diabetes.
records.further_details: Insulin and diabetes supplies are not consistently available in Gaza due to disrupted supply routes and limited healthcare infrastructure. Even when supplies arrive, there may not be enough and may not always be able to be stored or distributed safely, putting people with diabetes at serious risk.

records.title: Require all HGVs to use mandatory vehicle-dimension-aware satellite navigation
records.description: Require every HGV operating on GB roads to use an approved commercial-vehicle satnav system and use this to calculate the route. We think this will reduce the number of bridge strikes and reduce damage to unsuitable roads.
records.further_details:
Drivers to enter the vehicle's weight, height and width before a journey.
 
The system to use the dimensions when calculating the route & take account low bridges, weight limits, width restrictions & unsuitable roads.
 
To apply to all HGVs operating in Great Britain regardless of whether they are travelling in, entering/leaving GB or passing through.
 
The requirement to apply to vehicles irrespective of ownership and enforced by law.

records.title: Amend the British Museum Act 1963 to Allow Repatriation to All Nations
records.description: Amend the British Museum Act 1963 so the British Museum can return artefacts acquired during colonial rule or conflict to nations that request them. We also ask the Government to work towards a treaty or international partnership framework supporting conservation facilities in nations of origin.
records.further_details:
Amend the Act so artefacts can be returned when any nations request them with educational replicas kept in British Museum. Online records show It holds:

over 110,000 objects from Egypt and Sudan,
64,928 items from Greece, including the Parthenon Sculptures,
52,518 items from India,
10,068 items from Australia, including Indigenous artefacts,
10,991 items from South Africa,
9,439 items from Ghana,
7,240 items from Kenya,
more than 900 artefacts taken from Benin, and 
80 Ethiopian artefacts, including 11 tabots.

We also ask the Government to work towards a treaty or international partnership framework supporting conservation facilities in nations of origin.

records.title: Require equal female representation in product and training design & testing
records.description: We call on the Government to legislate to require equal female representation when designing and testing products, such as safety equipment, and training, such as emergency procedures.
records.further_details:
From seat belts (which are commonly tested on male crash dummies - women are more likely to die in a crash) to CPR training, women should have consistently equal rights.
 
We believe women are significantly underrepresented and in many areas of design and testing, including vehicle safety, emergency response training and protective equipment design, where standards have commonly been based on male measurements and anatomy. We want the Government to require equal representation for women to ultimately ensure the consistency of the Equality Act 2010 and ensure women are safe and protected.

records.title: Regulate SEND advocates to protect parents needing legal advice
records.description: There has been a significant rise in advocates providing paid services for parents of children with special educational needs. Many parents are finding themselves desperately seeking guidance and support with the current complex legal framework. There is no regulation for advocacy services
records.further_details: The free statutory Information and Advice Services (IAS) that are provided by Local Authorities vary greatly in the level of support they are able to provide. With many having services cut. We feel both IAS services & registered charities are unable to cope with the colossal amount of parents needing legal advice. This means many parents are unable to access reputable free support. Any service providing advice around legal frameworks must be regulated to ensure parents are protected & not taken advantage off.

records.title: Reduce fuel tax to 20p per litre and VAT to 10% for petrol, diesel & heating oil
records.description: I would like the government to seriously consider reducing the fuel tax to 20pence per litre and vat to 10% for petrol, diesel and heating oil.
records.further_details: As petrol and especially diesel has risen to by at least 50p a litre and it affects everyone especially people who live in rural areas where public transport is not reliable for people get work etc. As everything is increasing in cost during the conflict in the Gulf. It is having a major effect on people's lives and the economy  with the rate of inflation and mortgage rates increasing. It could stabilise the economy and it could help the vast amount of the population who are on lower incomes.

records.title: Legal cap on how many HMOs can be approved in any area
records.description: We believe too many house of multiple occupation (HMO) approvals can ruin an area. It can create more mess, parking problems, and potentially attract trouble.
records.further_details: We want the government to think about the long-term problems that could be caused by a lack of legal caps. We think that many areas have gone downhill over the last 10 years — more crime, rubbish dumping, and parking issues. We see these problems as being created by the choices of the government, politicians, and councils who approve these plans without considering the impact on residents and the children who will have to live with the consequences for the rest of their lives.

records.title: Remove the 100% additional council tax premium on second homes
records.description: From 1 April 2025, billing authorities in England can charge a council tax premium of up to 100% (that is, up to 200% of the normal bill) on second homes. We think this is disproportionately discriminatory as there is no 100% increase in the authorities delivered services.
records.further_details: We see this as punishing the homeowner

records.title: Add “Jewish” to the list of ethnic group categories for all government forms
records.description: Add “Jewish” as a mandatory ethnicity option for all government forms that collect data on ethnicity, include the official census. According to current practice (including the census form) "Jewish" is listed only as a religion, which could exclude, say, ethnically Jewish atheists.
records.further_details:
Antisemitism has in recent history been a racial, not just religious, prejudice. Hitler's Nazis did not spare non-believing or converted Jews.
 
Like many people born into Jewish families, I claim "Jewish" as a definition of my ethnic identity (DNA testing identifies me as Ashkenazi Jewish). I have no religious beliefs. I believe listing "Jewish" as only a religion reflects and fosters ignorance about Jewish ethnicity, and the roots of antisemitism.

records.title: Ban use of student university work to train AI software without informed consent
records.description: We, the undersigned, do not want AI software companies to use our academic work to help train AI models without our prior informed consent.

records.title: Make it mandatory to pay enhancement for working on bank holidays.
records.description: Make it mandatory for companies to pay an enhancement for working on bank holidays instead of it being at the companies discretion.
records.further_details: It is very unfair that many people get bank holidays off work and get full pay while so many have to work and do not get paid any more than the normal minimum wage such as the private care industry.

records.title: Introduce Citizens’ Referendum System for Legislation
records.description: Introduce a citizens’ initiated referendum system, allowing the public to propose and vote directly on legislation when a minimum signature threshold is reached, modelled on Switzerland’s direct democracy system, which has operated successfully for over 150 years.
records.further_details: In our view, the UK’s current system gives citizens no direct say on the agreement or rejection of legislation between general elections. Switzerland allows its citizens to vote on legislation multiple times per year. We think this produces more accountable government, greater civic trust, and long-term political stability. We believe that giving UK citizens powers to initiate referendums on legislation could reduce political disillusionment, force Parliament to reflect genuine public will, and bring Britain in line with modern democratic standards seen in Switzerland.

records.title: Ban enriched and colony cages for hens
records.description: We believe enriched and colony cages are unfair for hens that live in them for their entire lives.
records.further_details: We feel they are inhumane and limit their ability to behave normally, such as running, perching, and dustbathing. We believe that they should therefore be banned, in order to safeguard the welfare of hens.

records.title: Add corn (maize) to the UK's list of mandatory food allergens
records.description: Review the evidence on corn (maize) allergy and amend food allergen regulations to require corn and maize-derived ingredients to be clearly identified and highlighted on food labels and menus.
records.further_details: Corn allergy can cause severe allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis. Corn and maize-derived ingredients are widely used in processed foods and may appear under many different names, making them difficult to identify. People with corn allergy face unnecessary risks when buying food or eating out. Mandatory allergen labelling could improve safety, reduce accidental exposure and help consumers make informed choices.

records.title: Introduce a wealth tax on assets over £10 million
records.description: Following the 'Proud to Pay' letter from 120 UK millionaires to PM Andy Burnham, we call on the Government to introduce an annual 2% tax on net assets over £10 million.
records.further_details: Over 120 UK millionaires recently wrote to the new Prime Minister asking to be taxed more on their accumulated wealth, not just their earned income. A 2% tax on assets over £10 million could raise around £24 billion a year, with further reform of capital gains tax raising more. This money could fund public services and reduce the tax burden on working people. The Government should take this offer seriously and set out a clear plan for taxing extreme wealth at the next Budget.

records.title: Ban fireworks, disposable BBQs & fires in public (Apr-Oct) bar official events
records.description: We want a new law to be introduced making the use of disposable BBQs, fireworks and open fires in public outdoor spaces between April and October a criminal offence.
records.further_details: Exemption for official or organised events where a proper risk assessment has been carried out.

records.title: Require environment impact assessments for all planning proposals in rural areas
records.description: I would like compulsory environmental impact assessments on all rural housing development proposals to protect unique habitats and protected wildlife such as bats, badgers and dormice. I'm concerned builders are rushing through proposed housing developments without these assessments.
records.further_details:
As an example, I have a proposed housing development to be built on farmland near my village. The farmland has established hedges, ponds and 200 year old trees. There are bats, badgers, dormouse, dears, and birds of prey in this area all this could be lost for future generations.
I would like all building proposals in rural areas to be required to have environmental impact assessments so building proposals cannot be rushed through destroying our beautiful countryside. Thank you for your support.

records.title: Legislate to ensure clear labels for products that have been tested on animals
records.description: Bring in a labelling law, for everything from toothpastes & weed killers to pharmaceutical drugs, to show if the products you’re buying or using are tested on animals. We want to be made aware of what has been tested on animals and how, so we can make an informed and ethical choice going forward
records.further_details: We have the Leaping Bunny program and other cruelty free labels but they are printed few and far between and sometimes products aren’t part of a program as such.
