We  feel we need to be made aware of what products have been tested on animals. We believe this transparency will help us make informed choices about what products we use as consumers. Often normal day to day items that you would think are cruelty free are not – we need the public to have the choice and to be made aware.

records.title: Require Motorway Services to provide physical security guards for truck parks
records.description: We call on the Government to require any motorway services which has truck parking to provide physical security guards. A lot of freight crime happens at motorway service areas, where many drivers fear becoming a victim. We believe that providing security guards can improve driver welfare.

records.title: Mandate SEND-awareness training for all staff in schools in England
records.description: As a teaching assistant myself, I feel school staff do not receive adequate training on helping SEND children. I believe this is vitally needed to help us support them with their educational journey as well as their speech & language, behaviour management, mental health and sensory training.
records.further_details: We want the Government to legislate to mandate all school staff to receive basic SEND-awareness training, in order to support SEND children in education effectively. This basic training could help with waiting lists and times for certain services and for progress to be made in schools first at least. This could lead to improved attendance and increased wellbeing of pupils and staff.

records.title: Review how airlines protect passengers with severe food allergies
records.description: Review if airlines provide clear, consistent safeguards for passengers with serious food allergies, including reasonable risk-mitigation measures, clear procedures following advance notification, and protection from unnecessary denial of boarding or removal from flights.
records.further_details: People with food allergies can face risks when flying, yet we feel airline procedures can be inconsistent. Passengers may notify airlines in advance, carry emergency medication and request precautions, but decisions can vary between airlines or crews. We believe clear UK-wide standards are needed so airlines can assess and mitigate allergy risks, and passengers are not denied boarding or removed when proportionate safety measures could be used. The rules should protect passengers from discrimination.

records.title: Prioritise defence by committing to defence funding at 10% of GDP
records.description: We want the Government to commit to 10% of GDP for defence spending and deliver this increase within months not years. Decisions about defence funding should not be taken by the Treasury, which we believe is not fit for purpose and unwilling properly to fund our defence.
records.further_details: Spending more than 10% of GDP on welfare while underfunding defence is, we feel, a bad joke. The Home Office states that “The first duty of the government is to keep citizens safe and the country secure”. The Government has a duty of care to protect us and our Armed Forces and we are being failed. Lord Robertson, ex-Secretary General of NATO, called out ‘corrosive complacency’ among politicians towards defence spending. We fear that party politics is more important than our safety and that of the Armed Forces. If there is no increase in defence spending to 10% of GDP the current Government should step aside.

records.title: Ban organisations seeking to replace the UK democratic system
records.description: Current law only allows banning terrorist groups. Organisations can still lawfully campaign to replace democracy with a theocratic or anti-democratic system if non-violent. Introduce legislation to close this gap and protect democratic rights and equal participation for all.
records.further_details: Current law only allows proscription of terrorist organisations. This means groups can lawfully advocate replacing democracy with a theocratic or anti-democratic system if they avoid violence. We believe this risks undermining democratic institutions, parliamentary sovereignty, and equal rights over time. Other democracies have legal safeguards against this. We feel that similar, proportionate powers with judicial oversight are needed in the UK to protect democracy and ensure equal participation for all.

records.title: Seek exemption from the EU Entry Exit System for haulage drivers
records.description: I would like the UK Government to negotiate with the EU for all UK Professional drivers to be exempt from the '90 out of 180' Entry Exit System. This is going to have a detrimental effect on the Haulage industry in the UK and the UK economy.
records.further_details: This petition is about the UK professional drivers being made exempt from the 90 days out of 180 entry exit system. The UK Haulage industry is in grave danger at the moment with the amount of drivers it is short of. I believe this is going to get worse as I know there are UK drivers losing their jobs to European drivers. I am concerned that this in turn is going to force drivers to look for jobs in different industries. The economy could take a big hit with this as companies will close and we will be reliant on EU drivers.

records.title: Review support, protection and timeframes for victims in sexual assault cases
records.description: Conduct a review with the aim to introduce clearer legal timeframes for CPS decisions, improve victim support, and strengthen protections for victims during sexual assault investigations.
records.further_details: Victims of sexual assault are often left waiting long and uncertain periods for decisions with little communication, which can seriously affect mental health and leave victims feeling isolated. Many continue to live in the same area as the alleged perpetrator, increasing fear anxiety. Stronger protective measures should be considered. We are also concerned there is a lack of local support services. We believe clearer timeframes, better communication, stronger protections and improved support would improve outcomes for victims.

records.title: Introduce new statutory standards for toilet access and lunchtime in schools
records.description: We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation and statutory guidance guaranteeing every pupil can use the toilet and eat lunch during the school day with dignity and adequate time. This should set enforceable minimum standards for toilet provision, privacy, and lunchtime access.
records.further_details: Using the toilet and eating lunch are not privileges; they are fundamental to a child's dignity, health, and ability to learn. Yet some schools fall below DfE toilet-to-pupil ratios, restrict access, or reduce privacy. Many pupils queue for much of their lunch break, leaving little time to eat. We ask for enforceable standards to ensure schools meet minimum toilet provision, maintain private facilities, provide reliable toilet access, and give every pupil sufficient time to obtain and eat a meal.

records.title: Allow independent search and rescue charities to use blue lights at emergencies
records.description: Require the Government to amend regulations to allow independent search and rescue charities to use blue lights and other emergency warning equipment when responding to authorised call-outs.
records.further_details: Independent search and rescue charities play a vital role in saving lives across the UK. They are often tasked by services such as HM Coastguard and police to attend time-critical incidents. Unlike Mountain Rescue England and Wales, many cannot use blue lights, causing delays. Allowing their use would improve response times, coordination, and help save lives.

records.title: Protect road verges for wildlife — stop non-essential mowing from April to Sept
records.description: Direct all local authorities and National Highways to suspend non-essential verge mowing from 1 April to 30 September annually. Safety-critical cuts at junctions, roundabouts and crossings remain exempt. Delivered as statutory guidance to ensure consistent protection across England.
records.further_details: UK insect populations have collapsed by over 60% since 1970. Road verges — 400,000 hectares of potential wildlife habitat — could help reverse this, but repeated mowing destroys wildflowers before they seed, removing food and shelter for bees, butterflies and hoverflies. Some councils already mow less, with measurable results. A national policy would make protection consistent across England, at little cost — and could save councils money. It aligns directly with the Environment Act 2021.

records.title: Appoint a mental health commissioner for all mental health care in England
records.description: The commissioner should be responsible for reviewing new and existing training in the NHS. There have been bad choices causing clients so many issues both personal and medical.
records.further_details: The whole system needs to be reviewed to help make sure bad choices does not happen ever again. Some clients have been given medication without reviewing side effects or knowing their medication records, and been given booklets to read about their current symptoms which is not in any way any help what so ever. Many have been let down by the system. Action needs to happen now so that people can feel assured that there is actual help and support out there that can suit the clients needs and support.

records.title: Hold a public inquiry into the balance of risks and benefits of SSRIs/SNRIs
records.description: We want the Government to hold a public inquiry into whether the current balance of risks and benefits of SSRI and SNRI antidepressants is acceptable, particularly in relation to long term use and under recognised side effects.
records.further_details: Antidepressants can cause emotional blunting and sexual dysfunction, and have been linked to impulsivity, mania, akathisia, withdrawal symptoms, and suicidal or, in rare cases, homicidal ideation. These effects can significantly affect relationships and family life, and many patients report not being fully informed about these risks. Withdrawal symptoms can be mistaken for relapse, and prescribing patterns may not always align with NICE guideline NG222.

records.title: Increase funding for staff in hospitals to support those in mental health crisis
records.description: Increase funding for more staff to ensure vulnerable patients cannot hurt themselves. When anybody, whatever age, is admitted to a general or psychiatric hospital, whether this be A&E or detained under the Mental Health Act, they must be kept safe.
records.further_details: Hospitals are places where sick and vulnerable people are meant to be looked after. I think the government need to increase funding so these places are safer for us.

records.title: Review animal welfare legislation to strengthen protections for horses
records.description: We call on the Government to review animal welfare legislation to strengthen animal welfare protections and standards for horses, and to strengthen accountability mechanisms for those who mistreat horses. We believe horses are intelligent, sensitive animals that deserve kindness, care, and respect.
records.further_details: We believe stronger action is needed to improve horse welfare. Every horse should have access to safe and secure shelter that protects them from extreme weather, clean water, nutritious food, regular veterinary care, and enough time to rest and exercise. We believe they should also be treated by kind, responsible owners who understand their needs and never use cruelty, fear, or neglect. By launching a review, we could help ensure that every horse has safe shelter, caring owners, and the kindness and respect they deserve.

records.title: Require shared e-bike rental operators to provide thirdparty liability insurance
records.description: Require all shared e-bike rental operators to provide third-party liability insurance covering personal injury, death and damage to third-party property caused while rented e-bikes are being used.
records.further_details: Shared e-bike schemes are growing rapidly across the UK. We believe operators should be legally required to provide third-party liability insurance covering personal injury, death and damage to third-party property caused while rented e-bikes are being used. This would help ensure victims can obtain compensation and increase public confidence in shared micromobility.

records.title: Mandate pre-issuance accuracy checks for all fines, bills & invoices
records.description: Introduce a “Proactive Billing Accuracy Act” to verify billing accuracy by mandating all organisations to carry out pre-issuance accuracy checks before issuing any bill, fine, invoice or enforcement notice.
records.further_details:
The Act would include mandating evidence-based accuracy checks, mandatory audit trails, clear correction processes, automatic pause of enforcement when an error is reported, proportionate penalties for repeated or systemic inaccuracies, and mandatory remediation where inaccurate billing or reporting has caused financial detriment.

There is currently no consistent legal requirement for organisations to verify billing accuracy before issuing invoices or payment demands. This Act would apply across public & private sectors to reduce avoidable financial harm and improve trust in the billing and enforcement system.

records.title: Mandate 25% urban tree canopy targets to protect public health and the NHS
records.description: Legislate to require a minimum 25% urban tree canopy cover target in the Environment Act and in the National Planning Policy Framework for all new developments and require existing urban areas to reach at least 25% tree canopy cover by 2050.
records.further_details:
Extreme heatwaves can place severe strain on the heart, causing spikes in cardiac arrests that put an unsustainable burden on an already stretched NHS. Surfaces like tarmac can turn housing into heat traps, leaving homebuyers vulnerable to unliveable conditions.

Trees provide vital cooling, dropping local surface temperatures by up to 15°C through shade and evapotranspiration. We ask Parliament to mandate 25% tree canopy targets, reducing NHS costs and relieving communities of unbearable heat.

records.title: Improve awareness of Clare’s Law and require earlier right to know disclosures
records.description: Require earlier Clare’s Law right to know disclosures from the police where there is clear risk, and improve awareness of right to ask through schools, workplaces and public information so more people know the scheme exists and can seek help sooner.
records.further_details: Many victims only learn of a partner’s abusive history after serious harm has already occurred. Earlier disclosure and more awareness could help people make safer choices sooner. Posters and adverts with Clare’s Law details in schools, workplaces and public spaces could help people recognise risk, understand coercive control and stalking, and know where to seek help.

records.title: Ban the playing of AI generated music in shops and commercial premises
records.description: Ban the playing of music generated entirely by AI in shops, restaurants, offices etc.
records.further_details:
AI music is jarring to listen to for staff and customers and damages creativity.

I understand why many premises do not want to pay the music licence but I think they should play old music that is out of copyright or not play music at all.

records.title: Amend section 19 of the Education Act 1996 to include up to 18 year olds
records.description: At the moment, section 19 of the Education Act 1996 allows children who are too unwell to go to school to access an alternative provision, including tuition from home. This ends at 16 years old. This needs to be amended to allow children up to 18 to access the same support.
records.further_details: Imagine finding yourself in a situation where your child is in Year 11 and so unwell that they cannot go to school. Section 19 allows that child to access an alternative provision from home. This ends when they are 16 years old. From then on, unless your child has an EHCP (Education Health Care Plan), your child will be expected to just access Further Education even when they are still unwell. I believe we need to extend current support to include children up to 18 years old.

records.title: Require Delay Repay to be automatic for online train ticket purchases
records.description: Require all UK train operators and ticket retailers to automatically assess eligibility for Delay Repay compensation and issue payments directly to passengers who purchased tickets online, without the need for a separate claim.
records.further_details: Train operators already know when trains are delayed and, for online ticket purchases, often know who is entitled to compensation. Yet passengers must usually submit a separate Delay Repay claim, meaning many miss out on money they are owed. The Government should require train operators and ticket retailers to automatically assess eligibility and pay Delay Repay compensation directly to passengers wherever journey data makes this possible.

records.title: Extend the bus fare cap in England to trams
records.description:
We call upon the Government to extend the England bus fare cap to trams.
Trams have often regenerated deprived neighbourhoods, yet bus services often reduce as a result, so poor neighbourhoods are left with little choice but to get the more expensive tram. There should be a level playing field.

records.title: Review speed limits on all roads with street lights or without white lines
records.description: Review relevant law so that a speed limit of 30mph (48 km/h), or 20mph (32km/h) in Wales, generally applies to all roads with street lights (excluding motorways) and all roads without central white lines unless signs show otherwise.
records.further_details: Apply the same simple logic of speed limits on specific urban roads to specific narrow rural roads where 60mph is also unsafe. We think this is needed to make the law sensible; to reduce road fatalities and to reset all modern Sat Navs that wrongly assume 60mph can be safely achieved on these narrow rural roads. The cost of this change is negligible (no signage necessary) and the benefits immediate.

records.title: Ban NHS services from purchasing accessibility overlays, plugins or toolbars
records.description: Prohibit all NHS bodies from purchasing or using accessibility overlays, toolbars, plugins or widgets. The Government should instead mandate that all NHS digital infrastructure meets WCAG 2.2 AA standards natively, ensuring full compatibility with users' own assistive technologies.
records.further_details: Accessibility overlays, toolbars and plugins often hinder disabled users by interfering with assistive technology. The NHS Service Manual advises against these "widgets," as they fail the 2018 Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations. We want a ban on spending any NHS funds on these products in favour of natively accessible code.

records.title: Review rules to protect voter freedom and ensure secure UK elections
records.description: We want the Government to set up a review of current electoral rules to ensure every vote is cast freely, securely & in secret. We believe it should strengthen polling station rules, tighten postal voting safeguards while keeping access for those who need it & review who should be eligible to vote.
records.further_details: Concerns have been raised by election observers, courts, and regulators about undue influence, inconsistent polling station enforcement, and postal ballot vulnerabilities. We believe a review of who should be eligible to vote, including non-British citizens, alongside safeguards, staff guidance, transparency, and public awareness, will ensure every vote is cast freely, securely, and in secret.

records.title: Do not align with EU food and drink standards
records.description: The Government plans to make a deal to align closer to the EU Single Market’s standards for food and drink. There are reports that the bill would enable any subsequent EU alignment to be enacted under secondary legislation with less parliamentary scrutiny than primary legislation.
records.further_details: We believe this planned deal is a thinly-veiled attempt to undermine the will of the people who voted for Brexit in 2016. We think it is undemocratic and is the first step in getting Britain back into the EU Common Market and all its regulation.

records.title: Reduce VAT on road fuel during the ongoing oil price uncertainty
records.description: Temporarily cut VAT on road fuel from 20% to 5%, matching domestic energy. Apply this reduced rate for the period of global oil price instability or until markets stabilise. Recognise road fuel as essential for workers, families, logistics and the wider economy.
records.further_details:
We call on the UK Government to temporarily cut VAT on road fuel from 20% to 5% while global oil prices remain unstable. Drivers pay VAT on top of fuel duty (52.95p per litre), so any rise in wholesale prices is amplified, unlike domestic heating fuel which has a 5% VAT rate.

A temporary VAT cut would ease pressure on motorists and businesses, reduce the tax on tax effect, support essential travel and supply chains, and bring road fuel into line with domestic energy.

records.title: Fund the construction of outdoor pools in England
records.description: Many young lives have been lost in Yorkshire alone, due to drowning in rivers and reservoirs. I believe open air swimming pools could prevent this by allowing children to take a dip somewhere else during the increasingly hotter summers; deterring them from swimming in rivers or reservoirs.
records.further_details:
The Government’s funding of the construction of open air public swimming pools in local areas could deter children from swimming in local rivers, where many children have died. Hotter summers can lead to greater danger for children, as they may swim in bodies of water that are less safe.
 
I believe we need to prioritise our future generations. The Government could fund the construction of public swimming pools in local parks or open air spaces.

records.title: Fund NHS clinical trials of psilocybin-assisted therapy
records.description: Fund and support NHS-backed clinical trials of psychedelic-assisted therapy for treatment-resistant mental illness, with approved research sites, licensed clinicians, safety screening, psychological support, patient follow-up, and published evidence to guide future UK policy.
records.further_details: Many people with treatment-resistant depression, PTSD and other serious mental health conditions do not recover with current treatments. UK research at King’s College London and Imperial College is already studying psychedelic-assisted therapy. NHS-backed trials could test safety, benefits, risks and long-term outcomes in a legal, regulated healthcare setting, and help guide future UK mental health policy.

records.title: Review Speed Limits for LGVs in the light of Modern Safety Standards
records.description: Review national speed limits for light goods vehicles (vans) on single and dual carriageways. Current limits are based on data collected decades ago. Modern vans now benefit from significant advances in braking systems, stability control, crash protection, tyres, and driver-assistance.
records.further_details: We call on the Government to review and update national speed limits for light goods vehicles (vans) on single and dual carriageways. Current limits were set decades ago and we believe no longer reflect reality. Modern vans are safer now more than ever, thanks to major advances in braking systems (including Automatic Emergency Braking), electronic stability control, superior crash protection, advanced tyres, and driver-assistance technologies such as adaptive cruise control and lane-keeping assist.

records.title: Create a National Register of Court-Proven Tenant Misconduct
records.description: Create a regulated national register of tenants found by courts or tribunals to have committed serious tenancy misconduct, in order to protect landlords while ensuring tenant rights, appeals, and fair data protection are safeguarded.
records.further_details: We call for a fair national register of serious tenancy misconduct where cases have been proven by courts or tribunals. It would include issues such as serious property damage, significant rent arrears, anti-social behaviour, illegal activity, or major tenancy breaches. The register could help landlords make informed decisions while protecting tenants through appeals, legal checks, and privacy safeguards. It aims to improve accountability and fairness in the rental sector.

records.title: Fund and coordinate local infrastructure development alongside new housing
records.description: We feel housing growth is happening faster than roads, schools, GP surgeries and other essential services can be delivered. We call on the Government to fund and coordinate the development of local infrastructure, so it is delivered alongside, not years after, new housing developments.
records.further_details: We believe housing growth is outpacing roads, schools, GP surgeries and other vital services. We call on the Government to fund and better coordinate the development of infrastructure, so it is delivered alongside, not years after, new housing developments. These funds should be invested in relation to large housing schemes and the combined impact of multiple smaller developments, ensuring communities have the facilities and services they need from day one.

records.title: Fund cancer awareness training for carers of those with learning disabilities
records.description: Fund and offer cancer awareness training to all professional carers and carers of family/friends of those with autism/learning disability. Carers need to be trained to teach their cared for different cancer checks but also how to look for signs and symptoms of cancer in those they care for.
records.further_details: We think this could help ensure cancers are picked up ASAP to reduce rates of mortality. People with autism/learning disabilities would benefit from correct knowledge and support from their carers to pick up on cancer symptoms, get diagnosed earlier, and access treatment earlier in order to survive. If carers don't have the training, how can they pass it onto their cared for? This training needs to be offered to all.

records.title: Require new homes have rainwater harvesting systems & fund retrofitting in homes
records.description: Mandate all new homes to have rainwater harvesting systems and fund grants to retrofit them in existing homes. Capturing winter rainfall for use during increasingly dry summers could reduce demand on mains water, ease pressure on reservoirs and help reduce flooding.
records.further_details: The UK receives substantial amounts of rainfall yet increasingly faces water shortages during dry summers. Too much winter rainfall can rapidly flow into drains, rivers and eventually the sea. Large-scale household rainwater storage could capture some of this water where it falls, for toilets, washing machines and gardens. With millions of new homes planned, we believe we should act now: mandate the fitting of rainwater storage systems in all suitable new homes and fund retrofitting these systems into existing homes.

records.title: Stop funding the annual Public Duty Costs Allowance for ex-PMs
records.description: We petition the Government and Parliament to remove the publicly funded annual allowance for former Prime Ministers, and to invest this saving in Defence for our Country.
records.further_details: Nearly 10m of taxpayers money has been spent to help fund the public lives of former Prime Ministers after they leave Downing Street, and over the last three decades three  former PMs have claimed over a million pounds. We believe this should be stopped and the resulting savings be used to help towards the Defence of our Country.

records.title: Stop all foreign aid to countries that seek reparations from the UK
records.description: We would like the UK Government to stop all foreign aid to any country which calls for reparations from the UK.
records.further_details:
We believe Britain led the way in ending the transatlantic slave trade and the UK took on a significant amount of debt when slavery was abolished, with the final portion cleared in 2015. British taxpayers funded the debt.
 
We believe people seeking reparations today were not personally subjected to slavery, and that they did not personally suffer slavery in the same way that British citizens of today were not responsible for it.

records.title: Require police SEND training & communication cards & sensory bags in police cars
records.description: Require police forces to give every officer mandatory accredited training on autism and learning disabilities, including approaches to missing people with autism. Mandate cards and a sensory bag in every police vehicle.
records.further_details: We are concerned that people with autism & learning disabilities are often misunderstood by police. Communication & sensory differences can look like non-compliance. Training is inconsistent. Health staff have mandatory autism & learning disability training; police do not. Communication cards & a simple sensory bag in every car could help officers communicate & calm someone in crisis.

records.title: Cap profits on Water/Gas/Electric/Internet & Fuels to 20% from cost value
records.description: We think owners of water/gas/electric/internet and fuel company make record profits whilst consumers pay increasingly high bills. We call on the Government to cap profits to 20% of the cost value of such products. In our view, profits should be kept to a minimum for such modern day essentials.
records.further_details: We believe water, Gas, Electric, Internet and Fuels are an absolute must in a modern world and the current profiteering in these industries is killing the spirit of the people, and that operating costs are spiralling out of control. Considering such industries are consistently reporting ridiculous profit margins year on year, we think there is obviously a spiralling problem with the costing and value of such services. In our view people need confidence in their government and ultimately, their providers of security and services. Every day essentials should always be cheap and easy to access, no one should struggle to keep a bare necessity going in the modern world. It's actually worrying to see the path that we have taken.

records.title: Ensure provision of women-only carriages on trains
records.description: British Transport Police data, as recently reported by Nation.Cymru, show that more than a third of women are likely to be assaulted during their commute. That is why I'm asking the Government to ensure that each train has a proportion of women-only carriages.
records.further_details: This is done in areas like Japan where up to 2/3s of women used to be groped on trains, which rate, after women-only cars were introduced, has reportedly dopped by c3% per year since then. We believe this shows that this clearly does work, along with raised awareness on this matter, and , in our view, will lead to an overall drop in sexual assaults in trains, and hopefully a collective consensus that further pushes sexual harassment against women on our streets in general.

records.title: Remove VAT on all school uniform
records.description: We think the Government should remove VAT from all compulsory school uniforms. We feel this would be an easy fix to help  parents struggling with the cost of living.

records.title: Require schools report restrictive interventions to LAs after exclusions
records.description: Require schools in England to report details of any restrictive interventions, including physical interventions, involving a pupil to the local authority whenever the incident results in a suspension or a permanent exclusion.
records.further_details:
Schools should be required to record uses of restrictive interventions and inform parents when it results in a suspension or exclusion. There is no consistent national requirement to provide this information to the relevant local authority when the incident is linked to a suspension or permanent exclusion. 
 
We want a statutory requirement to ensure local authorities are automatically informed, to help identify patterns, safeguarding concerns and additional needs, and ensure appropriate support is provided.

records.title: Local Councillors to be limited to represent one council only
records.description: Change the law to prevent local councillors from being elected & sitting on more than one council. We believe this would immediately remove any conflict of interest & ensure that councillors' time is devoted to just one ward - an exception being to also sit as a Borough Councillor for the same ward.
records.further_details: There are a number of local councillors who sit on more than one local council. We believe this, by definition, must produce a conflict of interest and, as such, cannot result in a councillor who is 100% committed to a specific council. It could also be viewed by some as a political power grab resulting in a councillor who has to decide how much time and effort they allocate to one specific council over another. We feel that residents should be able to cast their vote for candidates knowing they represent them and only them.

records.title: Ban airport charging for drop off and pickup
records.description: We want the Government to remove charges for picking up or dropping off at airports. We believe it's taking advantage of the public and the first 10 minutes should be free.
records.further_details: Having recently picked up two family members at 01:00, I was charged £6.60 for being in a pick-up area for less than 4 minutes.

records.title: Abolish 'green' taxes and VAT on energy and fuel and reduce the fuel levy
records.description: Remove 'green' taxes and VAT on energy and fuel for households and businesses and incentivise the drilling of oil and gas in the North Sea by reducing the fuel levy. We believe we need a pluralistic approach to energy that helps the present and the future, not the current net zero approach.
records.further_details: We believe we need our North Sea oil and gas industries re-energised given our dependence on imports. The more gas drilled closer to home, the greater the UK’s energy security could be in such volatile times. Such changes could reduce our energy costs, among the highest in the developed world, which cripple UK business competitiveness and households struggling with cost of living. They could ease market concerns on our dependence on imports and investment could increase jobs.

records.title: Ban digital age verification
records.description: Ban any form of digital age verification, regardless of purpose.
records.further_details: We believe that digital age verification comes with extreme risks, such as digital security, privacy and potential unfair censorship.

records.title: Launch an independent review into retail price margins on essential goods
records.description: Commission an independent review into retail price margins on essentials. The review should compare actual supplier costs against retail prices to identify how much of the final cost is due to inflation versus retailer markups.
records.further_details:
The review should investigate implementing statutory margin caps to prevent profiteering on basics. We believe the Government should stop retailers from driving costs beyond official inflation rates. We feel we are being price-gouged on fuel, milk, baby food, and meds. We demand a review into "greedflation" and the wholesale-to-shelf spread. 
 
During WWII, the Government set a precedent by managing rations to ensure survival for all. We believe that same duty must apply now. We believe we need statutory margin caps to ensure profiteering is illegal. No one should be outpriced on basics while some retailers report record profits.

records.title: Improve Origin Labelling and Enforcement Against Honey Adulteration in the UK
records.description: We call on the UK Government to introduce mandatory country-of-origin labelling and percentage share origin for all honey sold in the UK. We request stronger enforcement against honey adulteration, ensuring that products diluted with non-honey sweeteners are not marketed as pure honey.
records.further_details: As part of updated EU labelling rules, new honey labelling and composition requirements will apply from 2026. We wish that similar measures be implemented in the UK, 1) to protect bees, which are essential pollinators, supporting biodiversity and food production, 2) to protect consumers from fraud by preventing misleading labelling, and 3) to support UK beekeepers.

records.title: Make CCTV in taxis (including private hire taxis) mandatory nationwide
records.description: Given what we feel are increasing risks in society, particularly for women, we believe the Government should prioritise public safety. We want all taxis, including private hire vehicles, to be required by law to have operational CCTV.
records.further_details: Drivers who refuse to comply with this nationwide law should face a ban from operating.

records.title: Stop funding NHS translation services and make use of AI instead
records.description: We feel that money is being wasted on translation services for people who do not speak English and who use the NHS. We think that AI could be used to save money instead.

records.title: Require firms to protect children and vulnerable people from in-game purchases
records.description: Introduce law to require gaming companies to protect children from exploitative in-game purchases and manipulative monetisation. In our view, games aimed at children should not use excessive prices, exclusive rewards or fear of missing out to encourage spending.
records.further_details: In-game exclusive items can be harmful. Children cannot earn the kind of money required for some of the items in the games, yet games use exclusive rewards to create fear of missing out. For vulnerable children and families, this can have devastating consequences. The Government should introduce laws to protect children from exploitative in-game monetisation and require games to put wellbeing before profit.

records.title: Require 51% support from residents to approve planning applications
records.description: Pass a law that requires the consent of 51% of local residents to approve a planning application for a development that affects them. If a majority of local residents oppose the application, it must be rejected and any appeal should solely go back to residents.
records.further_details:
Under this law, it should be mandated that their decision must not be overridden by any person or body, local or national. We feel our current planning laws provide no way for residents to have the final say on planning. They can voice their opinions to the local authority.

The local authority may on occasion reject it. But then, the appeal for a planning application can be overturned by the Planning Inspectorate, a body acting on behalf of the Secretary of State. We want this to stop and to ensure that those affected by the building have the final say, no-one else. This could bring planning power back to residents.

records.title: Fund Free Childcare for all Full-Time Student Parents (Not Means Tested)
records.description: Fund free childcare for parents who are full-time students. This support should not be means tested. Many student parents struggle to continue their education because childcare costs are too high. Current support is limited, excluding full-time students or depends on income thresholds.
records.further_details: Providing free childcare could help student parents complete their education, improve their future employment prospects, reduce financial pressure on families, and increase access to higher education. We do not think student parents should be forced to choose between caring for their children and completing their studies. We believe student parents are investing in their future and the future of the economy, and they should not be prevented from accessing education because they cannot afford childcare.

records.title: Increase the 45ppm fuel allowance for all community care staff.
records.description: Increase the 45 pence per mile allowance for the fuel and wear and tear of our own cars when we are using them to travel between individuals as out job, this amount has not increased for years.
records.further_details: Community support staff travel miles each day to provide care for vulnerable people in their own homes, this service is essential to thousands of individuals who need support in their day to day lives. We are given 45 pence per mile allowance for the fuel and wear and tear of our own cars which we use every day for work. This is no where near enough when at present we are having to pay nearly £2 per litre  for diesel.

records.title: Change the day elections are held to Saturday
records.description: We call on the UK Government to hold all major elections on Saturday instead of Thursday, to improve accessibility, participation, and democratic engagement. The UK is one of the few major democracies that still holds elections on a weekday. Thursday voting can create barriers for working people.
records.further_details:
At a time of growing political disengagement, we feel the UK should modernise its electoral system to reflect modern working and family life. We believe that democracy works best when voting is easy, accessible, and convenient. We therefore call on the Government to move general elections, local elections, and referendums to be held on Saturdays.
 
Many countries that hold elections at weekends achieve consistently higher voter turnout than the UK. For example, Australia regularly exceeds 90% turnout and Sweden often achieve 75–85%.

records.title: Require water companies to issue automatic bill rebates during hosepipe bans
records.description: We want the Government to introduce legislation requiring water companies to provide automatic, pro-rata financial rebates to household customers for every day a Temporary Use Ban (hosepipe ban) is in place.
records.further_details: Water companies charge customers fixed rates for a continuous, unrestricted supply of water. When a company enforces a hosepipe ban, they are restricting the service that consumers are paying for – in our view, this is often to compensate for their own failure to manage leakages and infrastructure. We believe that it is unfair that consumers bear the full financial cost of restricted usage while water companies continue to collect full fees and pay dividends.

records.title: Do not include partner’s income when applying for means-tested benefits
records.description: The moment a disabled person falls in love, moves in or marries their partner, their welfare support can be reduced or completely stopped. This can place an unfair financial burden on households and destroy relationships & lives.
records.further_details: We call on DWP to end their policy of counting a partner’s income against a claimant’s benefits claim. The DWP’s current policy can leave some disabled people with no income and solely reliant on their employed partner. This then can create barriers to qualify of life, relationship and financial dependence on a partner which may result in relationships falling apart or a partner having to leave work due to costs.

records.title: Ban summer firework sales & use, restrict permits & hold venues strictly liable
records.description: Impose a statutory ban on the consumer sale, domestic personal use and unpermitted public display of fireworks from 1 March to 30 September. Make it a criminal offence and impose fixed penalty notices (FPNs) of £1,000 for breaching this ban.
records.further_details:
​We also call on the Government to mandate strict permits for summer firework displays, and to hold venues strictly liable—including for breaches by patrons on or adjacent to their premises—triggering mandatory licensing reviews and closure orders.

​Unregulated summer firework use can result in severe antisocial behaviour, distress vulnerable groups of people, terrify pets, cause livestock losses and create wildfire risks. This statutory ban and increased penalties could tackle antisocial behaviour, wildfire risks and animal distress.

records.title: Fund more NHS dental care & prevent dentists from stopping NHS dental care offer
records.description: We want the Government to fund a greater availability of NHS dental care & prevent dentists who currently offer NHS care from going completely private as many people can’t afford private dental care.
records.further_details: We believe the price of private dental bills is ridiculous and disturbing and as a result many people cannot afford to go private.

records.title: Allow learner drivers to resit only the part of the theory test they fail
records.description: Allow learner drivers to resit only the part of the theory test they fail. This would let candidates retake the multiple‑choice or hazard perception section separately, instead of repeating both, reducing barriers for disabled and neurodivergent learners.
records.further_details: Learner drivers must pass both parts of the theory test in one sitting. For many disabled and neurodivergent candidates, the concentration needed for the multiple‑choice section can cause fatigue that affects their ability to complete the hazard perception. Vocational licence theory tests already allow candidates to resit only the part they fail. Extending this to learners would reduce barriers without affecting safety.

records.title: Fund an urgent referral pathway for vascular compressions
records.description: Fund an urgent referral pathway for suspected vascular compressions like superior mesenteric artery syndrome (SMA) and median arcuate ligament syndrome (MALS). This would be similar to the urgent cancer pathway.
records.further_details: This is incredibly important as so many people especially frail and young people get misdiagnosed with IBS and live in pain. We don’t want more people to suffer.

records.title: Review time limits and communication standards in school safeguarding cases
records.description: The Government must review the need for time limits for safeguarding investigations involving schools & agencies like the LADO, DBS & TRA to ensure they are clear & to promote better & quicker sharing of information between organisations.
records.further_details: The Review is also needed to ensure that cases affecting teachers & staff are not left open longer than necessary. At the moment, cases can drag on even after decisions have been made, mainly because agencies we believe don’t always share information quickly. This can leave teachers and staff in long periods of uncertainty, affecting their wellbeing and ability to work. We feel clearer timelines and communication would make the process fairer and more efficient.

records.title: Mandate neuro-competence for workplace managers
records.description: We call on the Government to mandate a statutory "neuro-competence" standard for workplace managers in businesses with 50+ staff. This must include undergoing complete accredited training to safely manage diverse cognitive, processing, and communication needs and differences.
records.further_details: Untrained management can cause severe occupational stress, burnout and unnecessary unemployment. We call on the government to direct the HSE to integrate "neuro-competence" into its standards. This must verify a manager's practical capability to proactively prevent psychological injury by: 1) eliminating volatile, unpredictable scheduling changes; 2) utilising structured, documented communication formats; and 3) identifying and mitigating localised sources of sensory overload and task fragmentation.

records.title: Require plants for sale to be labelled with animal toxicity information
records.description: This petition is about being able to buy flowers for loved ones and knowing that their furry friends are going to be safe. As an owner of 2 cats I can't get flowers as I don't know when they are safe. And many other people need to know if they are doing more harm than good for their pets.
records.further_details: This petition is to support owners with pets and having flowers. As a pet owner I struggle to get flowers has I don't know which are safe, and I have friends come round and they bring me flowers and they have to be binned for not being safe. For people who don't have any pets this is something not many people think about although they also really love animals and then feel really guilty if anything happens. I think it's time owners should be able to confidently buy flowers knowing our furry friends will be safe.

records.title: Create a right to opt-out of having your personal information processed by AI
records.description: Give citizens the legal right to opt out of having your personal information processed by AI when accessing services or products that contain or are designed by AI, which includes health records and purchases. Clear warnings which explain possible exploitation or harm should be added.
records.further_details: We believe an opt-out option and warnings about AI risks should be provided. AI processes data at fast speeds so it can learn about psychology and other important information. We are concerned it could then be used to play on your insecurities or your children's insecurities and may make you vulnerable to manipulation and exploitation, which leads to it selling you products or worse.

records.title: Include AI and its environmental impact in England's national curriculum
records.description: We want the Government to include education about AI , including its environmental impact, within England's national curriculum. This should be taught through existing compulsory subjects such as Computing, Science, PSHE or Careers education, rather than creating a separate subject.
records.further_details: Teaching AI in schools is vital so young people understand how it works and its environmental impact. Large AI systems use huge amounts of energy and water, and students must learn how this affects their future so they can make informed, responsible decisions. It is really necessary to be teaching the younger generation what impact AI has on their futures and earth its self.

records.title: Ban indoor vaping in all enclosed workplaces and enclosed public places
records.description: Smoke-free legislation only bans smoking tobacco indoors, leaving e-cigarettes unregulated in workplaces. We want the Government to amend the law to legally ban indoor vaping in all enclosed workplaces and public places, preventing second-hand vapor and securing a healthier working environment.
records.further_details: Current law only bans tobacco indoors, leaving workplace vaping unregulated. This loophole leaves staff with no legal protection from second-hand vapor. Exposure to chemical aerosols can cause headaches and breathing issues, especially for those with respiratory sensitivities. We urge the Government to amend the law to include e-cigarettes, legally banning vaping in all enclosed workplaces and enclosed public places to ensure safe, clean air for everyone.

records.title: Mandate mental health awareness training for at least one staff member
records.description: We want the Government to make it a legal requirement for at least one staff member to be trained in an accredited mental health awareness course. Workplaces already provide physical safety training, but not a mandatory course for mental health.
records.further_details: Making this a legal requirement could help reduce work related stress, improve early intervention, support managers, and protect employees — especially men, who are statistically less likely to seek help. This law could ensure every workplace has someone equipped to respond appropriately, helping to create safer, healthier working environments across the UK.

records.title: Reform the system for NHS clinical negligence claims and cases
records.description: We call on the Government tot introduce urgent reforms to the system regarding NHS clinical negligence claims and cases to ensure that patients who have suffered avoidable life-changing injuries receive a fair, transparent and independent investigation.
records.further_details: The Government should implement the following reforms: create a national panel of medical experts that assess all clinical negligence cases, establish a dedicated, independent body to investigate concerns regarding experts’ evidence and introduce meaningful sanctions against expert witnesses found guilty of deliberately misrepresenting medical evidence or failing to meet their professional duties.

records.title: Make producers pay the end-of-life costs of short-lived plastic products
records.description: Introduce Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) requirements to producers and importers of short-lived, and difficult-to-recycle plastic products, which currently are outside of the EPR framework. Proposal shifts the burden from the taxpayers and local authorities, to the producers and importers.
records.further_details: We call on the Government to use the Environment Act 2021 to introduce Extended Producer Responsibility for short-lived and difficult-to-recycle plastic products. Producers and importers should pay charges reflecting each product’s environmental and end-of-life costs, with lower charges for durable, reusable, repairable and recyclable products. This should incentivise better product design and shift waste costs from taxpayers and councils to those placing products on the UK market.

records.title: Decouple electricity prices from gas prices
records.description: This government should decouple our gas price from electricity. It has been reported that this alone could cut bills by £200.
records.further_details: The United Kingdom has the one of the highest electricity prices in Europe. By simply decoupling our gas price from electricity, we believe this could bring everyone's bill's down.

records.title: Fund increased capacity at SEN schools
records.description: The special educational needs (SEN) system is broken. There are high needs autistic people who have a legally binding Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). Yet, every single special provision school in a district can refuse them admission.
records.further_details:
Despite having an EHCP, they are denied their legal right to education. We feel ignored by our MPs. Families nationwide face this crisis alone.
We demand change:
 
The Government should provide funding to expand SEN school places and hubs in every district so no child is rejected due to "lack of capacity."
Legal Accountability should be enforced when Section 19 duties are not met for alternative education. No child is "too difficult" to educate. Sign to demand equal education now.

records.title: Require UK-trading companies to provide a contactable phone number
records.description: Many companies operating in the UK have removed all phone contact options, forcing customers through chatbots, forms, or endless email chains. We call on the Government to legally require any company trading in the UK to provide a working phone line to speak to a human agent.
records.further_details:
Most companies are removing phone support entirely leaving customers unable to resolve urgent issues or complaints without speaking to a human. This disproportionately affects elderly and disabled people, and anyone without reliable internet access.
We believe any company legally trading in the UK should be required to provide a working telephone number, allowing customers to speak with a live agent within a reasonable time, and ensuring companies cannot hide behind automated systems.

records.title: Require manifestos be accessible to those with sensory & intellectual impairment
records.description: Around 25% of the UK’s population are reported as disabled and their right to vote is protected by law. However, party manifestos are not routinely available in accessible formats, which can remove their right to make informed political choices and may contravene international human rights laws.
records.further_details:
We call on party manifesto documents to be legally required to be made available in braille, BSL, Easy Read, Large Print & Audio versions to ensure equal opportunity for all voters to compare policies.
 
They should be published on websites compliant with international accessibility guidelines (WCAG2.2AA) to ensure readability & compatibility with screen readers. We believe this would comply with domestic & international human rights legislation (Equality Act 2010 and UNCRPD 2008) which we feel are not currently being met.

records.title: Increase minimum wage to £15 per hour
records.description: Due to the current crisis as well as the rapid rate of inflation, we believe it is necessary for the standard minimum wage for those who are 18 and over to be brought up to a liveable £15 per hour.
records.further_details: We want young adults and those suffering from the brink of poverty to be able to acclimatise better to the growing financial difficulties. We think raising the minimum wage to £15/hour  allows for those who can work to assist the country as a whole. In our view it can improve the aspect of fundamental tasks of life which ensures an enhanced quality of living amongst the population.

records.title: Reverse the new tax on vape liquids
records.description: Reverse the new vaping products duty tax rate. We believe it is way too high and could cause more strain on the NHS because people might go back to tobacco and other substances.
records.further_details: 1 Oct 2026 Vaping Products Duty charges 2.20 per 10ml on all vape liquids including nicotine-free plus 20% VAT making 2.64 tax per bottle 3 bottles weekly means 7.92 extra tax or 411.84 a year. We believe this hits those who have quit smoking hardest, and they might return to smoking which could increase pressure on the NHS.

records.title: Implement Permanent Closure for Stores Selling Illegal or Laced Vapes to Minors
records.description:
We want the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014 amended to remove the 3-month limit for "problem premises" involved in the supply of illegal substances to minors.
In our region, dozens of shops have been closed temporarily, only to reopen and repeat the same offenses.
records.further_details:
Permanent Closure Orders for shops selling vapes containing controlled substances.
A "One-Strike" ban on business owners caught selling harmful products to minors.
Greater accountability for landlords who rent to repeat offenders.
Temporary bans are not enough when a child's life is at risk. Make the closures permanent.
The current "revolving door" of temporary closures is failing to protect our children.

records.title: Automatically remove parental responsibility from convicted domestic abusers
records.description: We believe that convicted domestic abusers should automatically have their parental responsibility removed. This is to safeguard the children from further abuse, preventing the abusive parent from leveraging their legal parental rights to inflict additional harm.
records.further_details: Domestic abuse, including when witnessed by children, cause significant harm. We do not believe that domestic abusers should retain their legal right to exercise their parental rights which can be used to cause further trauma despite all the abuse they put their family through, and call for parental rights of domestic abusers to be automatically removed.

records.title: Fund & require all public venues to have allergy treatments including EpiPens
records.description: We want the Government to fund and require all public venues, including restaurants and shops, to be equipped with allergen medication, including EpiPens, in first aid boxes.
records.further_details: In the event of a severe allergic reaction, immediate access to EpiPens or other appropriate treatments is essential. This measure could provide critical support to both children and parents during emergencies, particularly given the number of lives that have been tragically lost due to delayed treatment.

records.title: Allow automatic divorce after fleeing domestic violence & review processes
records.description: If you flee a domestic violence relationship - man or woman - and you are married, you should automatically be granted a divorce. Review the process to address any barriers, risks and trauma which can be faced by survivors as they navigate divorce proceedings.
records.further_details:
When fleeing a domestic violence relationship to safety, the victim shouldn’t have to worry about contact with their abuser and putting themselves at risk. In many cases victims have restraining orders in place due to the domestic violence and the safety of themselves and their children. There should be no circumstances in which victims have to find their abuser is and risk disclosing any personal information. 
Improve protection for victims: automatically grant a divorce when there is DV.

records.title: Increase Local Housing Allowance rates
records.description: It is estimated that Local Housing Allowance rates cover less than 3% of advertised private rentals in England. However, it is estimated that around 45-50% of private renting households are claiming Universal Credit.
records.further_details:
When the LHA was introduced in 2008, it covered 50% of private rental market properties in a given local area. If tenants secured a property priced below their designated LHA rate, they could be paid up £15 per week.
 
However, now only less 3% of properties cost low enough for the LHA rates to cover the full cost. We call on the Government to increase LHA rates so they cover 50% of local properties to reduce the chance of the families needing to rent them becoming homeless.

records.title: Prevent animals from working or travelling in temperatures over 30 degrees
records.description: We believe animals should be protected from working and travelling in hot weather conditions which can cause extreme suffering and death. It is outrageous to us that cows and pigs were transported, and that events like horse racing and agricultural shows went ahead during June's 36 degree heatwave.
records.further_details: Dogs can die in hot cars even with the windows open - so can pigs and cows transported in lorries in hot weather. They very often have no access to water, and are routinely deprived of food as this makes the slaughter process easier and cheaper.  Responsible owners don't take their animals out to events in extreme heat because they know the risks; unfortunately there are always those who do not put the animals' welfare first.  Legislation needs to be put in place to stop animals working & travelling in temperatures over 30 degrees.

records.title: Cap net migration at 25,000 people per year to stop mass immigration
records.description: We call on the Government to establish a cap on net migration levels to 25,000 people per year. We believe current levels of immigration are putting pressure on the NHS (especially GP services), housing and council services, and integration and social cohesion.
records.further_details:
Between 2015 to 2025, it is estimated that over 8 million immigrated to the UK. These are record levels of immigration. We believe the Government must act and cap net migration at 25,000 people per year in order to control immigration and ensure it reaches more sustainable levels.
 
On 27 July 2026, 69% of people on a YouGov poll said that the Government were handling immigration "Badly".

records.title: Abolish Homes England & distribute its funding to Mayors to build council houses
records.description: Dissolve Homes England & distribute the up to £46B budget allocated to it for the next decade to the regional mayors, ringfenced to build council & social housing & affordable schemes, helping people to buy their first home at a reasonable price.
records.further_details:
We want to prevent any subsidisation from the public purse of private rental schemes & corporate investors.
 
We are concerned that the multi-million pound development plan for Buxton’s town centre is what we see as an example of a national funding model undermining local accountability & control. Mayors should be encouraged to increase the number of small & medium sized local housebuilders delivering housing – which have declined by around 80% in number since 1980 according to some data. We believe these companies would help ensure that money stays in the local area & secures long-term employment for local people, supporting council house building and a skills strategy.

records.title: Increase allowances for foster carers to match the minimum wage
records.description: We believe foster carers deserve to be paid fairly at the basic minimum wage per hour at least. Foster carers work 24 hours a day for under £2 an hour on the current allowance. We think it’s a disgrace.
records.further_details: The allowance foster carers receive means that they are paid under £2 per hour for 24hour a day care. Foster carers are therapists, comforters and care givers to children. The children that come into their care are often severely traumatised and require around the clock care. We believe that the very least they deserve is the national minimum wage for the job they do which will also mean there will be more carers who can afford to help the children of our future.

records.title: Government to commit to stability for UK work and graduate visa rules
records.description: We want the UK Government to commit to a stable, long-term immigration framework and halt sudden, restrictive shifts to salary thresholds, visa durations, and settlement paths.
records.further_details: We believe migrant workers & businesses are vital drivers of the UK economy. HMRC records show immigrants pay over £20bn annually in direct taxes, with non-EU migrants yielding a £4.6bn net surplus. Immigrants own 27% of UK businesses, creating over 1.1 million jobs. Home Office accounts also show £23.19bn was extracted via visa fees and levies (2019-25). We believe abrupt visa rule changes can create severe anxiety & damage talent retention.

records.title: Regulate the UK's precious metals buying market to protect sellers
records.description: We call on the Government to regulate the UK's precious metals buying market. This should include mandatory price transparency, regulated postal and travelling buying services, a cash payment threshold, and mandatory ID checks on sellers, to protect consumers and prevent stolen goods being sold on.
records.further_details: Anyone can start buying gold and silver from the public tomorrow, with no licence, no accreditation, and no obligation to disclose rates. Some operators pay a fraction of true value with no upfront transparency. Scrap metal dealers have been banned from paying cash and required to verify sellers' identities since 2013, to stop stolen goods being sold on. We believe gold and silver deserve the same basic protection. I run an accredited gold buying business and support these changes myself.

records.title: Zero-rate VAT on UK-manufactured goods sold in UK to support UK manufacturing
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce a zero rate of VAT on goods manufactured in the UK and sold domestically. This could encourage people to buy British-made products, protect skilled jobs, boost investment, strengthen UK manufacturing and support long-term economic growth.
records.further_details: We want the Government to introduce a zero rate of VAT on goods manufactured in the UK and sold in the UK. We believe this would encourage consumers and retailers to buy British-made products, helping to protect manufacturing jobs, support investment, strengthen local supply chains and rebuild communities that rely on UK industry, while making British businesses more competitive against imports.

records.title: Ban the sale, manufacture, import and release of sky lanterns
records.description: Ban the sale, manufacture, import and release of sky lanterns. We believe sky lanterns pose severe risks of fatal injury to livestock and wildlife from ingested wire/bamboo, present an uncontrolled wildfire hazard to farmland and property, and cause widespread litter.
records.further_details: Sky lanterns travel unguided for miles before landing as hazardous waste on land and in water. Fallen frames can cause horrific internal injuries or death if eaten by livestock, while open flames can cause costly wildfires in crops, moorlands, and property. Though many local councils heavily restricted their releases on public land, we believe a total national ban on sales and releases is the only solution to protecting rural communities, rescue services, and wildlife across our country.

records.title: Light Big Ben in Ukraine’s colours for the 5th anniversary of Russia's invasion
records.description: On the fifth anniversary (24 February 2027) of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Big Ben’s clock faces should be lit blue and yellow for the first time ever, sending what we feel would be a powerful message of solidarity with Ukraine.
records.further_details: The Elizabeth Tower (commonly called Big Ben) is recognised around the world as a symbol of British democracy. The clock lights can be changed to other colours, but never have been. We hope the war will end, but if it hasn't by 24 February 2027 (5th anniversary of Russia’s full-scale invasion), we ask that the clock faces are lit blue and yellow. We believe  this would send a powerful message of solidarity with Ukraine, reinforcing support for our ally, those who have made the UK their home and those still on the front line.

records.title: Ensure funding for SEND pupils to have a 1-1 teacher
records.description: Ensure funding for each SEND pupil to have a supporting teacher to help their difficulties during school time
records.further_details: There are reports that some pupils with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) may no longer have the one-to-one support they need in school. Children with SEND are individuals. They have different needs, different abilities and different challenges. Removing the support they rely on can have a huge impact on their education, confidence, independence.

records.title: Increase Passenger Carrying Vehicle GVW limits to accommodate air conditioning
records.description: Current maximum permitted Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) restrictions for buses & coaches often do not allow for air conditioning to be fitted to some buses. We believe this needs to be addressed as it’s putting Bus Drivers and others at risk.
records.further_details: Every summer we see news reports about excessive heat in bus driver’s cabs, reaching as high as 50 degrees on occasion. We believe the limits need to be amended to accommodate the extra weight of a properly functioning air conditioning system. The high temperatures experienced in some bus driver’s cabs are putting them at high risk of heat stroke which can cause them to lose control of the bus. Such loss of control can be fatal for many.

records.title: Ban employers from using AI tools to sift job applications
records.description: We ask the government to regulate the use of AI for recruitment and hiring, directly resulting in systemic application rejection and job prospect paralysis for qualified citizens.
records.further_details: Unemployment is a big issue and the use of such tools can directly result in systemic application rejection.

records.title: Require employers to pay for DBS checks
records.description: Require employers to pay the full cost of any Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check that are a condition of employment, including Basic, Standard and Enhanced DBS checks. Employers should not be permitted to require applicants or employees to pay these costs.
records.further_details:
DBS checks are required for many roles in health and social care, education, and other regulated sectors.

Employers often require applicants or low-paid workers to pay the cost themselves. This creates a financial barrier to work and can discourage people from applying for essential roles, especially in sectors facing recruitment shortages.

As the check is required for safeguarding, the cost should be treated as a business expense rather than a charge on individuals seeking work.

records.title: Ban school uniforms
records.description: I think school uniforms are uncomfortable. They’re way too hot in the summer, and not warm enough in the winter, so I think students should be able to wear their own clothes. Some people might have sensory issues. I also think they limit people expressing themselves
records.further_details: They also can be expensive, and a lot of students break the rules and don’t wear the uniform properly. People say it’s good to be unique but then they don’t let kids express themselves.

records.title: Mandatory vet scanning of cats’ and dogs’ microchips
records.description: We want the Government to ensure by law that every time a living cat or dog goes to the vet regardless of what the appointment is for they must scan the animal to a check whether it has been properly chipped and whether the pet is recorded as lost or stolen.
records.further_details: It is reported that up to 680 pets are lost or stolen every day in the UK. All cats and dogs are legally meant to be chipped now but we cannot see the point of the chip if vets don’t check the chip on every visit. This petition is to ensure that every animal is scanned every time they are taken to the vets to make sure there is no stolen or lost flag on the chip and help put an end to animal trafficking and theft and make it easier to reunite lost pets with owners.

records.title: Ban ministers removed from Cabinet from returning during that Parliament
records.description: The frequent removal of Cabinet ministers damages government stability and accountability. When ministers are removed, it often signals a failure or a shift in direction, yet those same individuals are frequently reappointed to top frontbench roles shortly afterward.
records.further_details: We believe recycling the same politicians hurts public trust, drags down the quality of governance, and erodes the political merit system. We’re calling on the government to pass a law that would automatically stop any minister who’s been removed from Cabinet from returning to any Cabinet role for the rest of that parliamentary term. This would improve accountability, break the cycle of underperformers, and help restore public confidence in British politics.

records.title: Consult on a national system to report suspected pet-food-related illness
records.description: Consult on a standardised system in England to collect and analyse health problems suspected to be associated with dog and cat food. Examine who should report, which events qualify and whether additional reporting duties are needed. Seek UK-wide coordination with devolved governments.
records.further_details: Pet food is already regulated, with incident reporting and surveillance in place. Standardised reports from owners, vets and manufacturers could help identify emerging patterns across products and places. Reports and patterns alone do not establish causation. The consultation should consider direct reporting routes and how reports would be assessed and integrated with existing systems. The Government should publish its findings and next steps.

records.title: Review laws on electoral bribery & treating & consider competitions for voters
records.description: Review laws on electoral bribery and treating and consider whether these should extend to political parties running voter competitions and prize draws which might encourage voters to vote for them.
records.further_details: We do not think political parties should be able to pay for potential voters’ expenses such as energy bills, or to give them money due to a lottery/prize draw. Although a lottery may not require the winner, or others who take part, to vote for the party, we do not think that this should be allowed. If we continue to allow this it would be shameful.

records.title: Strengthen Immigration Fraud Reporting with Verified Incentives Scheme
records.description: We ask the Government to strengthen action against immigration fraud, including sham marriages and false claims. Review the reporting system, introduce stronger financial verification, and stricter penalties where fraud is proven, while ensuring fair investigation and legal process
records.further_details: We propose identity verification for complainants with optional anonymous reporting. All reports must be evidence-based and investigated fairly. Strengthen financial/relationship checks via tax and employment records and post-arrival checks for high-risk cases. Where fraud is proven, ensure visa cancellation, removal and re-entry bans. Introduce a regulated compensation scheme for verified reports leading to proven fraud, with safeguards against misuse, improving integrity and reducing public cost

records.title: Stop schools posting images of students on public social media platforms
records.description: We want the Government to ensure that schools use secure, closed platforms for sharing student images, and to prohibit the use of public social media for this purpose. Schools should set the example for social media use.
records.further_details:
Many secure, access‑controlled platforms already exist for schools to communicate with parents. Despite this, schools often default to free, public social media channels. 

Consent is usually given by parents, but children reach an age where they have the legal right to make decisions about their own data. In a school environment, the power imbalance makes it difficult for children to refuse or withdraw consent.

records.title: Require all eligible UK citizens to vote with a "None of the Above" option
records.description: Introduce compulsory voting in UK general elections, with reasonable exemptions. Ballots must include a “None of the Above” option so voters can formally reject all candidates without being forced to support any party.
records.further_details: Recently, turnout has often been low, meaning Governments are elected without significant participation. We believe mandatory voting ensures everyone takes part, while a “None of the Above” option protects freedom of choice by allowing voters to reject all candidates. We feel this strengthens legitimacy and public trust in elections.

records.title: Ban people with criminal records standing for local government or Parliament
records.description: Pass a law that blocks anyone who has a criminal record from running for position in Parliament or local government

records.title: Require family of those arrested for child sexual offences to be informed
records.description: I want a law to protect families who have a member of their family that has been arrested for child sexual offences but may not know about it.
