The law should state all close family members should be alerted instantly - guilty or not - so they can protect their children and any close friends.

records.title: Require energy providers to auto-switch pensioners onto the cheapest tariff
records.description: Legally require energy providers to automatically move people above the State Pension age onto the cheapest energy tariff option, and for this to be reviewed every 3 months and in line with the energy price cap.
records.further_details: We believe pensioners shouldn’t need to worry about variable rates or missing out on fixed or flexible tariff energy deals. Instead, we believe energy companies should be legally required to automatically move people over the State Pension age onto the cheapest energy tariff option. This should be reviewed every 3 months in line with the energy price cap.

records.title: Launch a review into strengthening regulation of diet replacement programmes
records.description: We call on the Government to launch a review into strengthening the regulation of very low energy and total-diet-replacement programmes.
records.further_details:
We want the review to look into introducing standards that require clinical screening, professional oversight, statutory medical and eating disorder safeguards, maximum durations and structured food reintroduction that align with NICE guidance.
 
Very low energy diets can have a legitimate clinical role for some people when appropriately selected, monitored and supervised. We believe people undertaking this level of dietary restriction should receive appropriate clinical protection, regardless of whether a programme is delivered by a commercial provider or within the NHS.

records.title: Ban councils from having prayers as part of formal meetings
records.description: Ban local authorities from having prayers as part of the agenda for their formal meetings.
records.further_details: We believe that there is a very worrying trend of councils passing rules making saying prayers part of formal council meetings. We are a country where we respect the freedom of religion, and we believe that forcing others to passively participate in one religion's traditions is absolutely contrary to the free choice of religion. We believe it is exclusionary to anyone not following that faith, which is a growing proportion of the country, to require there to be prayers during a council meeting.

records.title: Public financial support only for ex-Prime Ministers who served a minimum 4 year
records.description: Require Prime Ministers to complete a full parliamentary term, or serve four years in office, whichever is the longer, before becoming eligible for full state-funded benefits and allowances associated with being a former Prime Minister.
records.further_details: Recent years have seen several Prime Ministers leave office after short periods. We believe the full suite of state-funded benefits for ex-Prime Ministers should only be available to those who complete a full parliamentary term or serve at least four years, whichever is the longer. We believe this would improve accountability, encourage stability and ensure fair value for taxpayers: benefits should reflect service to the country and be subject to greater transparency. Long service should be rewarded, not short tenure.

records.title: Abolish electricity standing charges for consumers
records.description: Many major energy companies are making record profits, yet consumers continue to be charged electricity standing charges. Many people with solar and smart meters are actively working to consume less energy, yet we feel electricity companies still prioritise their profits.
records.further_details: We believe electricity standing charges make no sense as the customers end up paying for something that is not based on the amount of electricity they consume.

records.title: Strengthening GMC Safeguards Against Vexatious and Abusive Complaints
records.description: Review and strengthen the GMC’s safeguards against systematic, vexatious, malicious & stacked complaints. Legislation should require assessment of complaint patterns & their cumulative impact, independent oversight, & effective protection for doctors against abuse of the fitness-to-practise process.
records.further_details: In our view, the GMC’s complaints process is vulnerable to weaponisation when individuals or organisations use repeated, coordinated and strategically timed allegations to trigger investigations, prolong regulatory scrutiny or damage a doctor’s reputation. We believe stronger safeguards could help identify patterns, scrutinise motives and evidence, and prevent regulatory processes from being exploited for purposes unrelated to patient safety. We are concerned that multiple doctors have experienced unfair treatment as a result of such complaints.

records.title: Review and change Universal Credit identity checks
records.description: End the use of identity checks on Universal Credit claimants such as passport selfies, doorstep photos and images of people's homes. We call for proportionate, dignified alternatives.
records.further_details: Some claimants may be asked to photograph their passport next to their face and open their front door for photos. We believe this is humiliating, raises safeguarding and security risks, and could be discriminatory. Claimants are not criminals. They are vulnerable people who depend on this support to survive.

records.title: Legally restrict charges after death by care homes & assisted living providers
records.description: We ask the government to introduce a legal limit on the number days care homes & assisted living providers can continue charging after a resident’s death. Many families face unexpected and continuing charges after a loved one dies. We believe there should be a fair national limit on post-death fees
records.further_details: Many families discover only after bereavement that substantial fees may continue to be charged after death or recovered from the deceased's estate. We believe clearer national rules are needed to prevent disproportionate charging practices and protect bereaved families from financial distress. We call on the government to cap post-death charges.

records.title: Require prisoners with sufficient assets to pay the cost of their incarceration
records.description: We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation requiring prisoners with sufficient financial means to pay the cost of their incarceration through a fair, means-tested system, the same as paying for your care, should you need to, in later life.
records.further_details:
This should operate in a similar way to existing arrangements under the Care Act 2014, where individuals with assets are required to contribute to the cost of their care. Contributions should apply where offenders have the ability to pay.
The cost of imprisonment places a substantial and growing burden on taxpayers. At a time of pressure on public finances, it is neither fair nor sustainable that individuals with significant assets can serve custodial sentences entirely at public expense.

records.title: Guarantee PSA tests for all men over 50 to help reduce prostate cancer deaths
records.description: Increase funding to guarantee provision for all men over 50 to receive a PSA test on request from their GP. Prostate cancer is the leading cause of cancer deaths in men. We believe the recent DHSC guidance for GPs to decide who gets a PSA test and who doesn't is wrong.
records.further_details: Over 12,000 men die of prostate cancer in the UK every year. It is the leading cause of cancer deaths in men, yet the Department for Social Care has just released guidance for GPs that men over 50 are not to be automatically entitled to a PSA test and their GP should assess who should have a test using "risk factors". Leading experts in the field have said this will lead to more unnecessary deaths. We believe it is wrong and immoral to rely on a postcode lottery for men's lives.

records.title: Give consumers legal rights, remedies and choice over delivery companies
records.description: We want the Government to give consumers direct legal rights and remedies against delivery companies, require retailers to identify the courier before purchase where reasonably practicable, and improve consumer choice and accountability in the parcel delivery market.
records.further_details: We want the Government to legislate to give consumers direct legal rights and remedies against delivery companies when goods are lost, damaged, delayed or mishandled. Retailers should, where reasonably practicable, tell consumers before purchase which delivery company will be used. The current system weakens competition because retailers choose couriers based largely on cost, while consumers bear the consequences of poor service and have little choice or direct recourse.

records.title: Make protective motorcycle clothing a legal requirement
records.description: We want the Government to make the wearing of protective safety equipment for the body as important as wearing a helmet by making it a legal requirement for motorcyclists. We believe this is about saving lives.
records.further_details:
By signing this petition, you can help us call on the Government to do the right thing, by protecting some of the most vulnerable road-users in the country. In 2019, 336 bikers were killed in the UK. My father was one. Since then I have watched my family battle with the consequences of losing him, and it's not something I want others to face.

The current law is firm about the wearing of motorcycle helmets but this isn't the case for other forms of safety equipment, although studies show such equipment can reduce the risk of and severity of injuries. We want to close this loophole in our laws, and make 'dressing for the slide and not the ride' a legal need.

records.title: Ban employers from issuing warnings/dismissing employees for serious illnesses
records.description: We ask the Government to introduce national rules requiring employers to always exempt people with serious illnesses from any sickness absence triggers or dismissal. Serious illness should never result in disciplinary action simply because someone is ill.
records.further_details:
We think this practice is cruel and unnecessary. It can create fear, affect mental health and imply illness is a failing. No one recovering from a stroke, cancer treatment, major surgery, organ failure or other life changing illness should face disciplinary action for being ill. 
 
Some workers have received warnings instead of support at the moment they most need compassion. This harms mental health, creates fear, and undermines dignity. Serious illness must never be treated as misconduct.

records.title: Review use of plea deals in domestic violence and abuse cases
records.description: Victims deserve accountability, transparency, and sentences that reflect the true severity of domestic abuse, strangulation, threats to kill, and repeated violence. Protect survivors and review the use of plea deals now. These changes could be known as Leoni's Law.
records.further_details: We are concerned that too many violent abusers avoid full accountability by pleading guilty to lesser charges while victims are left with lifelong trauma. Domestic abuse, strangulation, threats to kill, coercive control, and repeated violence must be treated with the seriousness they deserve. We call for reforms to stop serious offences being minimised through plea deals, ensure victims’ voices are heard, and make sentencing reflect the true impact of abuse.

records.title: Fund more NHS Dental Services for people on lower incomes
records.description: I have just got a cost from a private dentist to improve my teeth at a cost of £2100 this is unavoidable at a time when the cost of living is so high. We need more NHS dental services for working class people & people on lower incomes.
records.further_details: We believe the prices at private dentist are just too much for so many people. We need help with regards to being able to access NHS dental services. I was on the waiting list for 8 years with no luck. We need help from the Government to fund dental services across the nation.

records.title: Revise the school mobile phone legislation for KS5 students (aged 16 and above)
records.description: We think the new legislation banning mobile phones in school should be revised to cater to KS5 students (aged 16-18). We believe these students need the freedom to endeavour in self study without being restricted by phone bans.
records.further_details:
We are concerned that this ban could have a serious negative effect on the performance of students. Whilst overall the ban could be beneficial to a school environment, we think it creates problems for KS5 students (aged 16-18). This is because in a digital age, most resources for independent study are online. Allowing KS5 students more freedom could improve performance and results. 
 
We also think it is unfair to confiscate a 17 or 18 year olds phone. These are people who are near adulthood.

records.title: Make youth councils mandatory for all new unitary authorities from 2028 (LGR)
records.description: Require all new unitary authorities created through Local Government Reorganisation from 2028 to establish and maintain a democratically elected youth council, with a duty to consult it on decisions affecting children and young people and provide sufficient funding and officer support.
records.further_details: Require all new unitary authorities created through Local Government Reorganisation from 2028 to establish and maintain a democratically elected youth council. These councils should be adequately funded and supported by dedicated officers, and local authorities should be required to consult them on policies and decisions affecting children and young people. Youth councils should be representative of their communities and have a clear role in local democratic decision-making.

records.title: Raise the Personal Tax Allowance to £30,000 for recipients of the State Pension
records.description: We call on the UK Government to raise the Personal Tax Allowance to £30,000 for anyone who qualifies for and receives the State Pension.

records.title: Review safeguards for those with mental health issues during police encounters
records.description: We ask the Government to urgently review legal safeguards for those with mental health issues during police encounters, particularly during and after restraint. We want reform including mandatory safe handovers to hospitals and timely mental health interventions. This could be called Xavier’s Law.
records.further_details: This review should seek to recommend legal reforms to better protect mental-health patients following police restraint, ensuring accountability.

records.title: Full child benefit for kinship children regardless of other children in the home
records.description: The government should treat every kinship child as a first child and should not be classed as an additional child when child benefit is calculated.
records.further_details: Kinship families do not spend years planning and saving for these children as they may have done if they were their own.  We are concerned these families often do not qualify for kinship payments from local authorities based on outdated means-tested finance forms. They save the government thousands of pounds for fostering each year.  An only child can become a kinship child and that family receives an additional child payment when its own parents would have received a full first child payment.

records.title: Ban schools from recording lateness as absence and ban related fines
records.description: I would like the government to stop letting lateness for school affect attendance percentages and ban schools from issuing fines because a child is late. Some children suffer getting into school and have SEN or anxiety.
records.further_details:
I believe it's unfair for parents to be told "get them in when you can" and for it then to go against attendance and be fined for it.

We are concerned that many parents are suffering and being penalised.

records.title: More items on prescription for individuals who have coeliac disease in England
records.description: Only bread and flour are available on prescription for people with coeliac disease in England. I would like this to be changed as gluten free foods are very expensive.
records.further_details: I am a single parent and struggle to pay for gluten free foods for my family.  Prices of gluten free foods are very expensive. More items on prescription or an amount to spend on gluten free food would support many across England who have this auto immune disease. This is a disease that is with you for life and there is not a cure for it. Not adhering to the strict diet for coeliac disease can make an individual very poorly.

records.title: UK Government to call on Pakistan to end killings in Pakistan-Azad Kashmir
records.description: We urge the UK Government to act immediately to call on the Pakistan Government to help stop the killing of innocent civilians in Pakistan-administered Kashmir. The UK Government must condemn these killings, call for an end to the violence and protect civilians, using the threat of sanctions.

records.title: Recognise cetaceans as non-human persons under UK law
records.description: Formally recognise cetaceans (whales, dolphins, and porpoises) as non-human persons under UK law. Modernise our legal framework to protect their rights to life, bodily integrity, and natural liberty, establish criminal offences for harm, and oppose international wild hunts and exploitation.
records.further_details: Science confirms cetaceans are highly intelligent, self-aware, and conscious. While no sovereign state has passed national laws declaring cetaceans as non-human persons, momentum is growing. Indigenous Pacific leaders recently signed the He Whakaputanga Moana treaty, and Tonga is drafting formal personhood acts. Current UK laws treat these sentient beings as mere property. By modernising our legal framework, we protect vital apex predators and ensure justice follows modern scientific reality.

records.title: Fund improvements to local parks, particularly for children with SEN
records.description:
Fund:
* Inclusive and accessible play equipment for children of all abilities
* Sensory play areas designed for autistic and SEN children
* Safe, secure fencing where appropriate
* Better-maintained equipment and play surfaces
* More seating, shaded areas, and accessible pathways for families
records.further_details: We think our local parks should be a place where every child feels welcome, safe, and included. Unfortunately, we feel the current facilities don’t meet the needs of many children, especially those with Special Educational Needs (SEN) and disabilities.

records.title: Raise the legal age for appearing in pornographic content from 18 to 21
records.description: We want the Government to increase the age to produce, appear and perform in pornographic content from 18 years old to 21 years old. We believe this would improve protections for those seeking to earn money in harmful ways at such a young age.
records.further_details: We feel that 18 years old, despite being the age when someone legally becomes an adult, is too young to make decisions to appear in pornographic content which stays forever on the internet. Although we feel 21 years old is still quite young, this change could give young people a chance to mature first and think through their decision.

records.title: Fund hypermobility screening in schools
records.description: We believe hypermobility screening in schools could support millions of children silently living with this condition. Many go undiagnosed, struggling with pain, fatigue or vision issues without understanding why. Early identification could allow for tailored PE, safer movement and more support.
records.further_details: Parliament should back hypermobility screening in schools to protect pupils early. Too many children don’t know they have vision issues or flexible joints, leading to avoidable injuries. Early action could ensure safer PE, clearer learning, and long-term wellbeing.

records.title: Mandate recorded and signed transcripts for all formal workplace investigations.
records.description: Unverified minutes can cause unfair dismissals & disputes. Mandating audio recordings, free automated smartphone transcripts, & signed confirmation from all attendees would help protect workers, remove cost barriers, and ensure absolute clarity.
records.further_details: We call on the Government to legislate for formal work investigations to be audio-recorded, transcribed, and signed by all participants. Unverified, one-sided minutes can cause severe confusion, disputes, and unfair dismissals. Mandating audio recordings, free smartphone transcripts, and mutual sign-offs would help ensure transparency and protect workers. This tech would help to remove financial barriers for small businesses and save thousands in avoided tribunal fees.

records.title: New statutory standards for staff and fees in the care industry
records.description: We want the Government to set new statutory minimum standards for staff and fees in the care industry to ensure a safer industry for clients.
records.further_details:
There needs to be a law regarding care & nursing homes to ensure the safety of residents to:
- have a minimum staff to resident ratio
- mandate transparency & full breakdown of care fee calculation to be provided when required
- ensure care fees should be the same regardless of who pays the fees. Those self-funding currently pay more than council funded residents to balance the books.
- require a good command of the English language to ensure better communication with people being supported

records.title: Ban MPs who have resigned from standing in resulting by-election for same party
records.description: If an MP resigns and triggers a by-election, they should not be eligible to compete in that by-election unless they are standing for a different party. By-elections cost the public purse and other parties money. An MP in a safe seat can resign just to make a political point and be re-elected.
records.further_details: This is about preventing the abuse of the parliamentary system. An MP who has been elected has a duty to their constituents. If they genuinely need to resign, or they feel that they must change party and therefore want to give voters a chance to choose again, then that is fair enough. But they should not resign if they are intending to stand again for the same party.

records.title: Fund & mandate standardised empathy & accessibility training for NHS A&E staff
records.description: Fund and mandate empathy and accessibility training that is designed to help disabled, chronically ill and neurodivergent patients for all NHS A&E staff. It is reported that they face lower quality healthcare than other patients, sometimes encountering dismissive or neglectful staff.
records.further_details:
We believe this training is vital for safe and equitable care, so patients don't avoid urgent help. Mistreatment can lead to preventable harm, worsening health conditions, sensory overload, severe psychological trauma and a loss of trust in healthcare providers, which can result in patients developing a dangerous avoidance of seeking emergency service help at times of critical urgency.
 
Anyone can become disabled, and we believe every patient deserves safe, equal care.

records.title: Review information rights of families when LPAs are in place
records.description: We call on the government to review current laws and rights of immediate family members (except where safeguarding concerns exist) to receive medical, financial and welfare updates when a person lacks mental capacity and has a lasting power of attorney (LPA) in use.
records.further_details: We want the government to review the law to ensure that close family members are automatically notified when a lasting power of attorney is registered and used for a family member who lacks mental capacity. We want to see a legal right to receive appropriate financial, medical and welfare updates on an information-only basis. We believe attorneys should not be able to block appropriate information from being shared unless there are domestic abuse or safeguarding concerns. Families should have a clear route to challenge withheld information.

records.title: Criminalise recording someone without consent & posting it on social media
records.description: Make it a criminal offence to record someone without their consent, which includes covert recording with smart glasses, and posting it on social media, in order to protect vulnerable people from exploitation.
records.further_details:
We want it to be illegal and a criminal offence to deliberately record identifiable people without consent for social-media content, including recording via phones, wearable cameras and smart glasses. Being in public should not mean consenting to secret filming or becoming someone’s online entertainment or income.
 
We feel vulnerable people, including homeless people, children and those who are intoxicated or distressed, need stronger protection. The new law should cover all recording technology, with tougher penalties for covert, exploitative or monetised filming. Being in public does not mean content.

records.title: Require restaurants and fast food chains to provide free sanitary products
records.description: I have endometriosis. And I can never access period supply when I start randomly. I want all restaurants and fast food places to legally have to have supplies in their bathrooms, period pads, tampons, female cleansing wipes and anything else important. For all periods we can’t choose when it starts.
records.further_details: As someone living with endometriosis, I experience heavy, unpredictable periods and severe pain that can strike at any time — including when I’m eating out. Right now, there is no legal requirement for food businesses to stock tampons or pads. When I’m caught short, I have nowhere to turn: staff often don’t keep them, shops aren’t always nearby, and asking for help can be embarrassing and distressing. This needs to be fixed so we can access free sanitary products when needed.

records.title: Seek to negotiate third-country removal schemes & deport all foreign criminals
records.description: We call on the Government to seek to negotiate and establish more third-country removal schemes and to automatically deport all foreign nationals who are convicted of criminal offences and anyone whose claim has been refused, without delay.
records.further_details: The UK is under significant financial pressure with regards to housing, welfare support, the NHS, schooling and security costs for our country. We believe illegal immigration is fuelling these financial pressures and that it is now time we put UK residents and taxpayers first. We want to ensure our children and grandchildren are protected, and that our island nation is protected too.

records.title: Ban AI use with intent to discriminate against minorities & spread extremism
records.description: We believe that with negative intent, AI can help fuel racial discrimination and hate within the politics of our country and strips away critical debate and thinking especially in social media, and online safety is then harmed.
records.further_details: We call for further restrictions on the use of AI, or a temporary ban of social media for those who use AI to discriminate, are possible solutions that could be considered by people with the expertise. There should not be hateful AI generated songs or hateful images that spread the idea that one race is superior to the other, especially in the comment sections of a social media app for many vulnerable young children to see.

records.title: Increase funding for Ambulance and A&E services to reduce waiting times
records.description: I want the government and Parliament to provide the NHS with more funding for A&E departments and ambulances so we can reduce care being provided in corridors. Also to improve the wages of staff as well as ambulance wait times.
records.further_details: I want the government in Parliament to do this, because I think at the moment the conditions in the NHS are bad; and I’m pioneering for change. This is especially needed for the Northwest.

records.title: Cap fares for wheelchair-accessible taxis and fund improved access
records.description: Cap wheelchair-accessible taxis cost at the same rate as a standard taxi for the same journey. We also call on the Government to provide funding to ensure access to wheelchair-accessible taxis is improved so disabled people can access taxis at all times, including evenings and nights.
records.further_details: As a wheelchair user, I often have to pay more for accessible taxis and must pre-book, especially at night, due to limited availability. This is not just a problem in my area and I am not the only person who struggles with this. Wheelchair users across the UK face higher costs and reduced freedom because accessible transport is limited. Transport should be fair, affordable and available to all. The Government should act to address this inequality.

records.title: Cancel the 2% Increase in Tax on Savings Interest scheduled for April 2027
records.description: The tax rates on income from savings interest are scheduled to increase by 2% from April 2027 on all rates. This will take the basic rate of tax from 20% to 22%. We object to this 2% raise on all rates from April 2027 and call on the Government to cancel this scheduled increase.

records.title: Stop use of facial AI age assessment for unaccompanied asylum seeking children
records.description: We believe using facial AI age recognition is unreliable and ethically unsustainable. Government must stop this approach and develop a multidimensional tool assessing biological, cognitive, developmental and emotional age of traumatised unaccompanied asylum seeking children.
records.further_details: The Government plans to legislate very soon to use facial AI to determine the age of unaccompanied asylum seeking children. There is strong evidence that such a method of physical age assessment can be highly inaccurate, and technically as well, as it does not necessarily capture relevant aspects such as child development, their level of understanding, and emotional maturity. Thus we believe age assessment methods that solely focus on physical features are unethical, and risk vulnerable children being treated as adults.

records.title: Allow the creation of global BBC iPlayer for international audiences
records.description: We believe we should prioritise commercial growth over cuts. We feel BBC dramas, documentaries and children’s programmes are some of the best and appeal to global audiences. Millions bypass geo-blocks to watch them. We call on the Government to allow a global BBC iPlayer.
records.further_details:
The Government is deciding the BBC’s future now. The Charter Review sets the framework to 2038. On iPlayer: millions already use VPNs to access BBC content; charging £5–8/month could unlock major new revenue. 
 
In 2024, it was reported the number of BritBox International (BBC) subscribers grew by 300%, with nearly 4m subscribers. We believe the BBC has strong global appeal in children and nature content.

records.title: Introduce Mandatory Ventilator Safety Protocol for Neonates
records.description: Mandate a national safety protocol, to be known as "Rosie's Protocol", for the ventilation of newborn babies requiring cuffed endotracheal tube changes from an un cuffed Tube.
records.further_details: The protocol should require clinicians to safely reduce ventilator pressures before inflating a cuffed tube, to minimise the risk of sudden excessive airway pressure causing catastrophic lung injury. We believe this simple safety measure could help prevent avoidable deaths and serious harm to newborn babies and should become standard practice across the NHS.

records.title: Create and fund a new body to oversee the provision of palliative care
records.description: We believe the NHS was not set up to provide palliative care, and that we need a new body to oversee provision of all palliative care. We think the NHS is about treatment and prevention and that care for those with life ending diseases and dementia needs to be better overseen with greater focus.
records.further_details: In our view, too many complain about palliative care in the NHS without understanding that it is not resourced or fit to provide palliative care. We think care homes both private and publicly funded need to be better overseen by experts through a separate body. People with life ending diseases and dementia deserve better from us but it's our belief that this is not nor should it be within the NHS remit except where cross pollination may advance medicine through research and trials etc. We believe our proposal could also enable us to better address issues such as euthanasia.

records.title: Tax kerosene used by private jets
records.description: We believe kerosene should be taxed for private jets in the UK. Private jet usage contributes much higher carbon per passenger than conventional commercial air travel and therefore should be taxed accordingly. Private jet travel is a luxury that causes environmental damage.

records.title: Require mandatory lifetime ban from keeping animals for causing death to them
records.description: We want harsher sentences for people who cause animals to die through neglect. Introduce a mandatory lifetime ban for all cases of this nature

records.title: Create an earned muzzle-exemption pathway for exempt XL Bully dogs
records.description: Develop and pilot a regulated pathway allowing exempt XL Bully dogs to earn exemption from compulsory public muzzling, subject to Government-approved responsible-owner certification and an independent dog-and-handler behavioural and handling assessment.
records.further_details: Current rules require exempt XL Bully dogs to be muzzled in public for life, regardless of individual behaviour. We believe public safety must remain the priority, but Government should test whether responsible-owner education and independent dog-and-handler assessment can identify suitable teams for an earned muzzle exemption. A controlled pilot should measure safety and welfare outcomes, with exemptions monitored, suspended or revoked where necessary.

records.title: Amend Human Medicines Regulations 2012 to allow Nursing Associates to use PGDs
records.description: We call on the Government to amend Part 4 of Schedule 16 of the Human Medicines Regulations 2012 to explicitly include Registered Nursing Associates as a profession permitted to supply and administer medicines under Patient Group Directions (PGDs).
records.further_details: Established post-Francis enquiry (2013), Registered Nursing Associates hold foundation degrees to assess needs and secure consent. Duty-bound by the NMC Code to Prioritise people and Practice effectively, these registered professionals enhance care. Yet, outdated 2012 laws lock them out of PGDs. This forces GPs and RNs to duplicate clinical assessments and deliver routine jabs themselves, creating clinic backlogs and delaying preventative care. We must modernise the law to put patients first.

records.title: Exempt military families from paying stamp duty when moving homes
records.description: Exempt military families from paying stamp duty when moving homes (e.g. after paying stamp duty for the first time, it is not incurred on subsequent moves).
records.further_details: Many military personnel move frequently, and although subsidised housing is an option if eligible, military families may prefer to own property for reasons such as being on the property ladder. We believe stamp duty expenses are not an equitable or reasonable cost to incur for military families who may have to move every 2-3 years.

records.title: Legally require lingerie-specific fitting rooms to be women-only
records.description: Legally require that lingerie-specific fitting rooms are reserved exclusively for women.
records.further_details: To ensure the safeguarding of young girls and women in lingerie-specific fitting rooms. Lingerie bra fittings are intimate and personal and leave the women and young girls in a vulnerable position. Whether it be their first fitting or they have undergone a mastectomy and they now need a post-surgical fitting. All women deserve the privacy and respect that is owed to them during these fittings. Allowing men into these specific fitting rooms undermines all safeguarding and increases risk of safety.

records.title: Launch an independent inquiry into family court’s handling of domestic abuse
records.description: We call on the Government to launch an independent inquiry into the family court system regarding their handling of domestic abuse allegations.
records.further_details:
We are asking for the inquiry to include:
	Investigating decisions made in domestic abuse-related family court cases to identify failures in protecting victims and children.
	Mandatory evidence-based trauma training for all judges and professionals whose assessments influence court outcomes.
	A full review of the welfare checklist to prioritise child and adult safety over the presumption of contact with an abusive parent.

records.title: Laws relating to children must use "must" not "should"
records.description: Laws involving children often uses the terminology of the word "should", which we believe leads to ambiguous expectations regarding professional responsibilities. We propose changing this language to "must," thereby establishing a clear legal duty for professionals within the child welfare sector.
records.further_details:
Transformation of Terminology: “must” conveys obligation while “should” implies no more than a strong recommendation. We must change all instances of "should" to "must" in current law relating to children, especially:   

1. child protection legislation, ensuring that professionals are legally required to adopt a child-centred approach in their practice. This change must affect all future child protection laws to help establish clear legal obligations.
2. parental and carer rights legislation - amend the legislation to guarantee that parents and caregivers have unequivocal rights in legal circumstances, including the recognition that their voices "must" be heard.

records.title: Legalise the right to carry concealed small firearms
records.description: Change the law to legalise the right to carry concealed small firearms in public. We believe this right should be heavily regulated – all ammunition must be accounted for, and it should require a 2-week minimum training course on first aid, firearm maintenance, and de-escalation.
records.further_details: We believe this is necessary due to the rise in knife crime and violence in our country. We feel upstanding British citizens should have the right to carry concealed firearms. This would need to be approved in a controlled strict way and should not be as easy as obtaining a shotgun licence.

records.title: Require Discharge Permits be removed from water companies in SSSI & SAC areas
records.description: We ask the UK Government to instruct the Environment Agency to cancel or remove any Discharge Permits granted to water companies in areas where the discharge empties into a river that has SSSI and/or SAC legal protection.
records.further_details: A Discharge Permit (specifically an environmental permit issued by the Environment Agency in England or Natural Resources Wales) can allow water companies to discharge into or within the vicinity of Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and Special Areas of Conservation (SAC) rivers. Water companies discharging sewage are killing the globally unique chalk streams which are protected SSSI and SAC ecosystems. Once these rivers are dead it is impossible to revive them to their original state.

records.title: Referendum on placing a cap on the UK population of 75 million
records.description: Further to the recent referendum vote in Switzerland regarding limiting their population to 10 million, I would like our Government to hold a referendum in the UK in similar terms to make it legal under statute to take measures to limit the UK population to 75 million.
records.further_details: We believe it is arguable at best that the only way to ensure growth is through ever increasing population sizes. We feel it is also arguable as to whether it is ethically correct to take the best and most trained individuals from developing nations to bolster western European nations. I would like the UK to strive to develop its economy without reliance on continued high levels of immigration. Surely AI can help with this.

records.title: Ban cameras with AI capability within works vehicles
records.description: Ban the use of cameras with AI capability within any works vehicle. We find this tool to be very intrusive, and are concerned about breaches of data protection laws. Most companies use the argument of driver safety over driver privacy but we disagree.
records.further_details: I am endeavouring to address the deployment of AI-enhanced cameras, as we believe their implementation appears to infringe upon our privacy, which some organisations seem to be overlooking.

records.title: Require universities to explain degree career routes and job prospects
records.description: Require universities to give prospective students clear information about the full career route before they enrol or become financially committed, including what the degree does and does not qualify them to do, & further training, exams, professional requirements, work experience, time and costs.
records.further_details: Universities should provide clear recent information and statistics on graduate employment prospects, including the reality of finding work and where entry-level roles may require previous experience. Students may commit years, savings, family support or debt. Before doing so they should understand the full career route, what the degree does and does not qualify them to do, further steps required and realistic job prospects. This is not about guaranteeing jobs or discouraging university, but transparency and informed choice while students still have a genuine choice of degree and career route.

records.title: Independent review of laws and police practices affecting freedom of speech
records.description: The Government should commission an independent national review of laws and police practices affecting freedom of speech in the UK. The review should examine laws governing online speech, communications offences and protest, and make recommendations to ensure free speech is protected.
records.further_details:
We believe free speech is in serious decline in Britain. Thousands of people have been arrested for controversial speech, online jokes and peaceful protest. We feel a patchwork of laws no longer fit for purpose has given police a wide license to censor and arrest people for the things they think and say.
 
We want the Government to restore Britain’s long and proud tradition of upholding free speech. The Prime Minister must launch a free speech reset.

records.title: Police stations to be open 24/7 with constables on reception & more on patrol
records.description:
Require all police stations to:
Be open 24 hours a day
Man all police station reception desks with constables and not allow civilians to work on police reception duty
Put more police constables on patrol
Have monthly community Q & A meetings with constables.
records.further_details:
Restore police reception desks to the same level as 2007.
 
The constabulary are an essential part of society and are sworn to protect and serve the people under the law.  With less and less police stations open for less hours, if at all and less and less constables on the beat.  It follows that Police Constable integration into society is at an all time low.  Recently I wanted to attend my local police station to see a Constable, but it is closed. 
I needed to travel and have only been able to see a civilian who is not sworn to protect and serve me.

records.title: Free school meals for all pupils and cover compulsory school uniform costs
records.description: Education is compulsory, yet most families are required to pay for essential items such as school meals and uniforms. These are not optional costs, and for many households they place a significant financial strain on families.
records.further_details: We want the Government to take action to ensure that all children have equal access to education without financial barriers. Expanding free school meals to all pupils and introducing national measures to cover the cost of compulsory uniforms would, in our view, promote fairness, reduce stigma, and support children’s health and learning outcomes.

records.title: Protect our Churches. Extra funding for security and safety of our Churches
records.description: Provide extra monetary funding for Churches so security can be improved. In the year 2025 crimes against churches were recorded at 3,824 crimes. This averages more than 10 a day. These crimes include Arson, Criminal damage, Vandalism and Burglaries.
records.further_details:
Extra money would enable Churches to increase security measures such as CCTV, Alarms and improved Security Lighting.
 
Majority of the time the church has to pay for the damage caused to the property and this can create a financial problem for the church.

records.title: Mandate Better Police Training & Presence to Make the Night-Time Economy Safer
records.description: We call on Government to help public safety within the NTE by mandating police training on SIA guidelines & customer service, strengthening communication with venues, staff & door supervisors, & increasing policing & visible presence. We believe this will reduce violence and make nights out safer.
records.further_details:
Requested actions:
• Mandate SIA training for police on door supervisors, licensed premises & operations to boost collaboration/enforcement.
• Provide customer service & de-escalation training for effective engagement in night-time situations.
• Establish formal protocols for communication, support & rapid response between police, venues & SIA door staff.
• Increase proactive policing & visible presence in night-time hotspots during peak hours to deter crime

records.title: End Compulsory Branded Skirts in School Uniforms
records.description: Amend school uniform legislation and statutory guidance to prevent schools from requiring compulsory branded skirts where a plain skirt of the correct colour and style would meet the same purpose.
records.further_details: The Government introduced statutory guidance to reduce school uniform costs, but some schools still require branded skirts for girls while boys can usually wear plain supermarket trousers. This creates unnecessary costs and limits choice. Families should not pay more simply because their child is female. Parents should have the same freedom to compare prices, buy from different retailers and choose affordable uniform options for girls as they already do for boys.

records.title: 5 years employment & tax contributions for non-UK citizens to claim benefits
records.description: Require 5 Years of employment and Tax Contributions in the UK for Non-UK citizens before they are eligible to claim Benefits, including Universal Credit.
records.further_details: We call on the UK Government to restrict access to Universal Credit and state benefits for non-UK citizens until they have completed at least five consecutive years of UK employment and tax contributions. We believe that state support should be earned through sustained work, not granted immediately. Individuals should not be allowed to pay a lump sum or upfront tax equivalent to bypass the five-year requirement. We call for this to take effect immediately, and for current claims to be stopped to those who have not yet met the 5-year requirement.

records.title: Fund transportation for compulsory school age children to catchment schools
records.description: Ensure children can access free school transport to their school where transport is required regardless of school choice. We think current rules financially penalise families for choosing a catchment or feeder school and undermine genuine parental choice and access to suitable education.
records.further_details: We think school transport guidance is outdated following the introduction of academies and does not reflect modern school admissions. For example, in Nottinghamshire, families can face paying £720 a year to attend a designated catchment and feeder secondary school, even though bus travel is also required for the alternative local school. We believe the policy is particularly unfair to rural communities, where public transport is unavailable and walking on country roads is unsafe.

records.title: Limit all political offices to sole British citizens, no dual citizens
records.description: The Government should legislate to allow only British citizens to stand for the UK Parliament and councillor positions in England. No dual citizenship allowed. They must also be able to speak and write English to a satisfactory level.

records.title: Replace Parenting Orders with an end-to-end accountability framework
records.description: Replace Parenting Orders in England & Wales with a statutory framework requiring schools and youth justice to identify pressures & log interventions. Action against parents must then follow an independent review & relate only to deliberate refusal to participate without reasonable excuse.
records.further_details: Parents can face fines and children can face exclusion or other consequences without the requirement for proof that warning signs were acted on or later interventions were suitable. This new statutory framework would use daily pupil and teacher check-ins, preventative pastoral action and referral to family, safeguarding, mental-health or specialist services. It would track referrals, waits, delivery, adaptations, engagement and outcomes. Safety measures may remain, but we believe consequences must not replace earlier intervention.

records.title: Extend transition period for local government funding reforms
records.description: We want the Government to extend the transition period for its local government funding reforms from the Fair Funding Review so councils facing significant funding changes have more time to adjust without having to resort to excessive tax increases on local taxpayers.
records.further_details:
For example, Wandsworth Council faces significant pressure from the new local government funding reforms. Wandsworth Council says the reforms could reduce its funding by £84 million a year. Despite identifying £79 million in annual savings, it says Council Tax for a Band D property could rise by £958 in 2027/28 — from around £1,020 to £1,978 – around a 94% increase.

The Institute for Fiscal Studies identified Wandsworth among councils facing particularly large funding reductions. Wandsworth Council has asked the Government to extend the 3-year local authority funding transition period to 8 years. We are asking the Government to extend the transition period to give affected councils more time to adapt and reduce the risk of exceptionally large council tax increases in a single year.

records.title: Require enhanced DBS and barred-list checks for MPs and councillors
records.description: Change the law so that holding elected office as an MP or councillor makes a person eligible for, and legally required to undergo, an Enhanced DBS check including checks of both the Children’s and Adults’ Barred Lists.
records.further_details: MPs and councillors hold positions of public trust and may come into contact with children and adults in vulnerable circumstances. Current law restricts who is eligible for Enhanced DBS and barred-list checks. I want elected office to become a specifically eligible category, with the checks mandatory. I believe this would establish a consistent safeguarding standard for elected representatives and provide an additional safeguard for members of the public who approach them for assistance.

records.title: Condemn & sanction Pakistan for the Kabul hospital bombing & halt arm exports
records.description: Impose Magnitsky-style sanctions on Pakistani officials responsible for the March 16 bombing on the Kabul rehabilitation hospital. Suspend all military aid and arms export licenses to Pakistan. Formally condemn this bombing and the mass forced deportation of Afghan refugees from Pakistan.
records.further_details: On 16 March 2026, Pakistan's bombing of the Omid Addiction Treatment Hospital in Kabul killed hundreds of civilians. This bombing of a medical facility could be a potential war crime. Afghans suffer under an unelected regime, historically empowered by Pakistan, while facing alleged state-sponsored aggression from them. We believe Pakistan cannot claim to fight terrorism while bombing hospitals and forcibly deporting refugees. The UK should ensure tangible consequences for these actions, not just words.

records.title: Require a 2/3 majority in the HoC to scrap/withdraw from human rights provisions
records.description: We call for a two thirds majority of all sitting MPs to be required to abolish or withdraw from:  the Equality Act 2010, GDPR laws, the Data Protection Act 2018, the European Convention on Human Rights, the European Court of Human Rights, the 1951 Refugee Convention, and the CRPD.
records.further_details:
I am concerned that some political movements are calling to abolish vital rights legislation to benefit large corporations. I believe it is important in safeguarding civil society that we make no compromises in protecting human rights for future generations.
 
I believe disregard and contempt for human rights have resulted in barbarous acts which have outraged the conscience of humankind. No matter our politics, I feel it is our duty to uphold human rights for all and protect our children from political corruption.

records.title: Mandate availability of basic water safety equipment at all open water locations
records.description: We want the Government to mandate by law the availability of basic safety equipment such as life rings and whistles at open water locations, irrespective of ongoing swimming bans that may be in effect at those locations.
records.further_details: Recent events have shown that members of the public want access to, and will continue to use, swim sites such as reservoirs despite bans. We believe that, irrespective of the swim bans in order, basic lifesaving equipment such as life rings should be available to reduce loss of life. This is common practice in a number of other European nations and showcases the need to prioritise practical safety over unenforceable guidance. We also believe that safety measures should be accompanied by signage reiterating dangers.

records.title: Fund improvements in access to specialist support for people with BPD
records.description: Fund a national 24-hour support line for people with Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD/EUPD). We feel that too many people are left without specialist support until they reach crisis and that help should be available when someone is struggling, not only when they are in crisis.
records.further_details: People with Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD/EUPD) often experience intense emotional distress, self-harm urges, fears of abandonment and overwhelming feelings. Many cannot access specialist support until they reach crisis point. We believe a dedicated 24-hour support line staffed by trained professionals could provide early intervention, reduce crises, and ensure people receive support when they are struggling, not only when they are in crisis.

records.title: Mandate deaf awareness training for all employees
records.description: Mandate deaf awareness training for all employees in all businesses to allow accessibility for deaf individuals. Create an inclusive, diverse space and bridge the gap with the deaf community and the hearing world. Understanding deaf culture more could allow for better communication.
records.further_details:
We want to break down the current barriers we see across all businesses. We feel there is currently a lack of awareness and understanding and no real consideration around how to communicate to deaf individuals.
 
In retail and hospitality for instance, there are assumptions that someone can hear, which can lead to members of the deaf community facing barriers relating to communication. This can make deaf individuals feel excluded from society and alienated. A lack of inclusivity affects individuals in many ways.

records.title: Update school uniform guidance for extreme weather in England
records.description: We feel schools respond inconsistently and should do the following in high temperatures: Yellow – permit wearing secure sandals; Amber –no blazers and ties and option to wear PE kit; Red - students to wear own light, comfortable clothing.
records.further_details:
Similar adjustments should be considered for other weather warnings, like boots for snow.
 
The Government already advises relaxing uniform rules in extreme weather, yet responses in different schools can vary. One school may close in response to the heat, while another nearby keeps pupils in full uniform. Schools have other policies to ensure a child-centred and coordinated approach to children’s safety and wellbeing. We believe our proposal aligns with that intention - ensuring children are safe, comfortable, and able to learn—at a time when many adults already receive similar adjustments at work.

records.title: Raise the Personal Allowance to £20K funded by a 2% tax on incomes over £100K
records.description: We believe this change could allow ordinary people to pay off their debt, save and invest more securely, spend more on holidays, retail, home improvements and services, and support local businesses and jobs.
records.further_details:
By having more disposable income, people could reinvest it into the economy, and the benefits could ripple outward.
 
This proposal should be funded by those who can afford it. It could provide financial benefits that are brave and potentially revolutionary. Money would go back into the economy and could genuinely reward working. If the goal is to truly redistribute wealth and close the poverty gap, then we believe that such ideas should be considered.

records.title: Increase funding to support mothers whilst on the maternity ward
records.description: Provide funding to increase the number of appropriately qualified, trained and vetted childcare professionals who can provide additional support to mothers with their newborn babies, including overnight support where appropriate.
records.further_details:
Having an extra childcare qualified staff these professionals could provide mothers with practical support, including caring for newborn babies for periods overnight, with the mother's consent and subject to appropriate safeguarding and clinical arrangements.
Mothers may be recovering from labour, surgery, complications or a long and demanding birth, while immediately being expected to care for their newborn baby throughout the day and night.
I believe mothers need care and support too.

records.title: Prohibit the restriction of literary works in school libraries
records.description: Make it an offence for schools to restrict pupil access to literary works in school libraries. Our children deserve access to diverse perspectives and ideas through literature, limiting their access based on individual biases curtails their intellectual and moral development.
records.further_details:
The UK, stands on a decision-making brink. We can either choose to narrow the minds of our youth or open their horizons by allowing them access to a vast range of literature, even those with challenging themes. Encouraging critical thinking should be at the forefront of our educational policies, and this means protecting the availability of diverse and sometimes controversial literature.
 
Multiple studies confirm that exposure to a wide array of ideas through reading and discussing different viewpoints results in better performance in critical thinking assessments. Our county has a responsibility to provide an environment where students can learn and question freely, preparing them to be informed, conscientious citizens.

records.title: Create a Cross-Departmental Strategy to end "Zero-Consequence" Culture for Crime
records.description:
The government should consider:  
Mandated police attendance for all retail crime, even "low-value" theft
More legal protection for staff from dismissal when upholding the law
Updated curriculum to teach more accountability
More direct consequences for offenders to replace collective school bans
records.further_details: We are concerned that UK communities may face a systemic collapse of order due to what we see as a "zero-consequence" culture. We think that policing "low-value" theft has become optional, effectively decriminalizing some crime and eroding public trust. Shifting any accountability to schools via collective bans is a failed strategy that ignores individual responsibility. Furthermore, we feel that current frameworks penalize integrity, leaving staff vulnerable to dismissal for upholding the law. We must restore the rule of law, protect moral action, and realign educational values.

records.title: Review laws on burglary and increase penalties
records.description: We call on the Government to review current burglary laws and to increase penalties. These crimes not only cause financial loss but also inflict emotional trauma on the victims. We believe the current penalties for convicted burglars are not effective enough to deter these criminal activities.
records.further_details:
We believe that harsher penalties and a better system will serve as a stronger deterrent and help reduce burglary rates. We are concerned that burglary is increasing, especially in Barnsley.  

Burglary is not just a property crime it's an invasion of our homes and personal spaces. It leaves victims feeling violated, unsafe in their own homes. Current legal consequences do not reflect the gravity of this crime.

records.title: Do not require online platforms to promote selected media organisations
records.description: We urge the Government to abandon proposals in the “Watch This Space” consultation that would require online platforms to promote selected media organisations through recommendation systems, and protect viewer choice by keeping recommendations based on users’ interests.
records.further_details: Many commercial platforms succeed because they recommend content based on each person’s interests. Whether someone watches educational videos, gaming, history, science or independent journalism, recommendations should reflect those choices. Public Service Media should compete by creating content people choose to watch, not through regulatory preference. In our view, government should not influence what content platforms recommend to viewers.

records.title: Ban unsolicited marketing or doorstep cold calling and scams
records.description: Ban all forms of unsolicited doorstep marketing and commercial cold calling to protect consumers, with a specific focus on safeguarding elderly and vulnerable individuals from what we believe can be predatory sales tactics and scams.
records.further_details: We call on the government to introduce legislation that makes unsolicited doorstep selling & cold calling a criminal offense. Every year, thousands mainly the elderly, isolated, and vulnerable are targeted on their own doorsteps by rogue traders, aggressive salespeople, and sophisticated scammers. Home should be a safe haven, yet we believe it has become a hunting ground for exploitative financial practices. In our view "No Cold Calling" zones and window stickers offer a minor deterrent, they lack strict legal teeth.

records.title: Mandate domestic violence training for all family court & social workers
records.description: Make accredited domestic abuse, coercive control and trauma-informed training mandatory for social workers and family court professionals, with regular updates, so every worker has high-quality training to safeguard survivors and children.
records.further_details: Some survivors and children are still being failed, misunderstood and victim-blamed by professionals without specialist knowledge. Every social worker must receive high-quality, regularly updated training to improve safeguarding, challenge harmful assumptions and prevent unsafe decisions.

records.title: Scrap the £2,000 National Insurance cap on pension salary sacrifice
records.description: Scrap the planned £2,000 National Insurance cap on pension salary sacrifice before it takes effect in April 2029. Were the cap to be retained, it should be substantially increased & uprated annually with earnings or inflation, so pension saving is not discouraged or penalised.
records.further_details: From April 2029, pension salary-sacrifice contributions above £2,000 will be subject to National Insurance. This will increase the cost of saving, and, we believe, will discourage millions from contributing more and leading to smaller pension pots and lower retirement incomes. With 3.3 million employees affected, we think this cap risks increasing future reliance on the State Pension and taxpayers. Parliament must scrap it and protect retirement security.

records.title: Introduce food allergy cards for those with allergies
records.description: This petition calls on the government to introduce a food allergy card. The food allergy card could be issued to anyone with a food allergy, detailing their allergy and severity. Cardholders could present their allergy card to any food establishment before placing an order.
records.further_details:
I want a standard allergy card introduced so people with diagnosed allergies can clearly communicate the allergen and severity to food businesses. I am concerned that too many people claim an allergy simply to change a dish.
 
This creates confusion for staff, adds pressure on kitchens and risks warnings being treated less seriously. A card could help ensure customers with genuine, potentially life-threatening allergies receive the care they need.

records.title: Tax cyclists for road use
records.description: We want the Government to tax cyclists, a personal tax for every adult who rides a bicycle on roads.
records.further_details: The Government needs money and I believe that cyclists should have to pay a personal tax to ride their bikes on the roads. They use our roads, they have cycle lanes that are all painted up for them in a lot of places. It doesn’t have to be expensive, e.g. £30 per year or more; but, if everyone who rides a bike paid it, then I believe it surely would put more money in the Government’s bank.

records.title: Ban euthanasia of healthy pets, create register of owners who have attempted it
records.description: Ban euthanising healthy pets. I personally know of instances where pets have been put to sleep just because they were not wanted, the vets offered to rehome the pet but the owners refused.
records.further_details: Such owners should be banned from owning pets again and be placed on a national register. When an animal is not sick, then euthanasia should not be allowed. Instead of euthanising these pets should be rehomed.

records.title: Strengthen enforcement of child maintenance for absent parents
records.description: Require the Child Maintenance Service by law to take automatic enforcement action after two missed payments, including automatic bank account deductions, travel restrictions for parents with arrears who move abroad, and mandatory review of self-employed income based on assets and lifestyle evidence.
records.further_details:
Too many parents are able to avoid paying child maintenance for extended periods by declaring low self-employed income or moving abroad.
Although enforcement powers exist, they are not applied quickly or consistently, allowing arrears to build and leaving children without the financial support they are entitled to.
A clear legal requirement for automatic enforcement after repeated missed payments could close loopholes, reduce delays, and ensure consistent action is taken to support children.

records.title: Provide funding for nit nurses to visit schools
records.description: We believe that we need nit nurses back in schools. We think there needs to be more in place than just an email to parents instructing them to check their child’s hair.
records.further_details: Schools do not physically check students' hair, but the nit nurse could.

records.title: Fund more school holiday clubs for children of working parents aged 5+
records.description: Provide funding to increase access to and the number of school holiday clubs for children over 5 in order to support working parents. Many areas have little to no childcare available for children over 5 during the school holidays.
records.further_details:
We feel existing options are limited and many focus only on sports activities, which may not suit every child or family. As a result, many parents are unable to work full-time or are restricted in the jobs they can take because they cannot access reliable childcare during school holidays.
 
We call on the Government to fund the expansion of affordable, inclusive school holiday clubs for children over 5, in order to give working parents the childcare support they need during school holidays.

records.title: Do not introduce social media curfew for 16 & 17 year olds
records.description: We believe that the proposed social media curfew for 16 & 17 year olds in the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Act 2026 should be urgently reviewed because it will fail miserably to truly protect our young people. We want effective legislation which helps and protect them to be passed.
records.further_details:
We oppose a mandatory social media curfew on 16 and 17-year-olds. We feel young people at this age are already trusted with significant rights and responsibilities: they can vote in the UK, they can drive at 17, join the armed forces, consent to sex, work and pay taxes. 
 
We believe a blanket social media curfew is inconsistent with these responsibilities and unfairly restricts personal freedom without treating young people as responsible individuals.

records.title: Hold social media companies accountable for publishing scam investment adverts
records.description: The social media companies accepting payment from illegal scam investment companies should be stopped from doing this. They should be treated as publishers & made responsible for what they promote to the public.
records.further_details:
The Government needs to take sufficient action against social media companies to prevent innocent members of the public being taken in by scam investment companies, apparently endorsed or run by celebrities.

Innocent people lose their life savings believing these scam adverts. Celebrities used to endorse these schemes without their consent have their reputations damaged. We need to do better by those harmed by these illegal scams & stop criminals/social media companies making money from them.

records.title: Count and Publish Postal and Polling-Station Votes Separately
records.description: Require postal and polling-station votes to be counted and published separately for every candidate and constituency before being combined for the official result. This would allow comparison of voting methods while protecting ballot secrecy.
records.further_details: Current election data records how many postal ballots are issued, returned, accepted and rejected. The declared constituency result records each candidate’s total votes, but does not show how many were cast by post or at polling stations. Publishing separate candidate and rejected-ballot totals for each method before combining them would enable meaningful comparison, improve transparency and strengthen electoral scrutiny while protecting ballot secrecy.

records.title: Priority Queues for Parents with Young Children
records.description: We ask the UK Government to introduce legislation or national guidance requiring shops and supermarkets to provide priority checkout access for parents and carers who are accompanied by babies or young children.
records.further_details:
Waiting in a long checkout queue can be extremely difficult for parents caring for babies and young children. Babies may cry, need feeding or changing, while toddlers and young children can become distressed, restless or unable to remain safely and calmly in a queue for a prolonged period.

Parents should not have to abandon their shopping, struggle with a distressed child, or face embarrassment and confrontation simply because they are unable to wait in a long queue.

records.title: Add 'None of the above' as an option to every list of constituency candidates
records.description: I want the Government to add 'None of the above' to the list of constituency candidates. If that gets most votes, then none of the candidates is elected & the election must be run again c6 weeks later, but none of the candidates from that first vote will be allowed to stand in the re-run election.
records.further_details: At present, nobody is able to express their dissatisfaction about the candidates standing in an election in any clear and meaningful way. They can choose to not vote, but this can be interpreted as apathy. They can spoil their ballot, but this has no clear meaning. We believe this proposal, as well as potentially changing the election result, provides a unique measure of public dissatisfaction.

records.title: Limit the number of properties landlords can own to three
records.description: Create a limit on the number of properties owned by landlords to increase the number of properties for sale and help the housing market to return to affordable prices; making it possible for people who can’t afford to buy their own home to enter property market.
records.further_details:
We believe this could also help reduce rental costs.

I believe my children and all young people deserve a chance of owning their own property. We feel today’s property prices make this impossible as property tycoons owning huge portfolios of property has grown out of control, which also affects rental prices. This leaves thousands/millions of people unable to enjoy life as financial pressures can become overwhelming.
 
I want the Government to limit the number of properties one person/company can own to release homes back into the market.

records.title: Require clear signage to warn drivers in advance of yellow box junctions
records.description: Please consider requiring traffic authorities to install signs that are clear for drivers to see prior to meeting yellow box junctions. All cameras are high up & are not seeing what the drivers see as they are not at eye level. At night & when weather is wet, they can be extremely difficult to see.
records.further_details: Many drivers are caught and see these yellow boxes as a way of making money. At least if there is adequate signage, they should help keep traffic flowing smoothly.

records.title: Require removal of online content taunting deceased people & introduce penalties
records.description: Legislate to require social media platforms to remove harmful taunting content, introduce penalties for individuals who create or share it, and recognise digital taunting as a driver of violence, retaliation, and trauma.
records.further_details: Online taunting of deceased individuals and victims of violence is escalating across social media. It fuels retaliation, traumatises families, and contributes to cycles of harm. Existing laws do not cover this behaviour clearly, and enforcement is inconsistent. A dedicated law is urgently needed to protect young people and communities.

records.title: Ban the police from strip searching children and replace with doctor examination
records.description: Remove the right to strip search minors from the police and replace child strip searches with examinations by doctors.
records.further_details: The government must change the policy that gives the police the right to strip search children. In the event that an intrusive search is necessary, it should be done by a medical professional qualified to do the examination.

records.title: Recognise the Islamic Nikah as a legal form of marriage
records.description: Amend the Marriage Act 1949 to recognise Islamic Nikah ceremonies as a legal form of marriage, granting them similar legal status as Anglican, Jewish and Quaker marriages.
records.further_details: Anglican, Jewish and Quaker marriages can all be legally recognised under the Marriage Act 1949. Nikah-only couples are legally cohabitants, denying women financial and property rights on divorce. The 2018 Sharia Review backed reform. We ask Parliament to amend the Act to give Nikah ceremonies equal legal status.

records.title: Introduce a statutory duty to track and provide notifications for DWP complaints
records.description: We want the UK Government to introduce a statutory duty requiring the DWP to notify claimants about their complaint digitally or by letter at every stage including opened, escalated, or changed, and to legally prohibit closure of any complaint without a claimant's explicit, recorded consent.
records.further_details: We think the current DWP complaints system lacks transparency and has poor tracking. Claimants often have no formal record when a complaint is made, making it difficult to get a fair resolution. Not only is MPs' time taken up with complaint administration to the DWP, the DWP must spend time updating claimants as to the progress of a complaint. We believe accessible complaints will address serious concerns from coroners, safeguarding bodies, human rights, and disability organisations - who protect rights and lives.

records.title: Ban sharing photos of children under 18 on social media
records.description: The Government should ban sharing images of under-18s online. Child predators use innocent photos of children for sexual purposes, even when accounts are private. Children deserve the right to privacy and protection from online exploitation.
records.further_details: I believe the Government should introduce laws to prohibit or significantly restrict sharing images of under 18s online. Child protection agencies warn that offenders collect and misuse innocent photos, including faces and everyday activities. Private accounts do not guarantee safety, as images can be copied or shared. Stronger laws are needed to protect children’s privacy, reduce exploitation and give young people control over their digital footprint.

records.title: Create a statutory body to investigate failures in the criminal legal process
records.description: No statutory body examines failures across the whole criminal legal process spanning police, prosecutors and courts. This includes witness contamination or Section 28 of the Youth Justice and Criminal Evidence Act 1999 breaches.
records.further_details:
