We want an independent body to establish facts, identify failings and refer misconduct to relevant authorities.
 
When failures span several organisations, no independent body examines the whole process. This can leave witness contamination, Section 28 breaches, false evidence, missing records and safeguarding failures across the criminal legal process without proper investigation. The proposed body could establish facts, identify systemic failings, refer suspected misconduct and recommend improvements.

records.title: Ban local authorities refusing housing to domestic abuse victims with mortgages
records.description: I would like the government to make it illegal for local authorities to decline housing support for victims of domestic abuse who have a joint mortgage with their abuser. Currently local councils can decline housing support due to the victim already owning a home and because they have equity.
records.further_details: We are concerned that victims can be told to "go home" to their abuser or simply don't leave due to homelessness and no income. Abusers use the joint mortgage as a form of control and threat to stop the victim from fleeing. Children can remain in unsafe homes due to this rule. Victims can be told that the local authority "cant help" as they have equity. The process to sell a home is long & dangerous with an abuser. Post separation is where the risk of fatality is at its highest. Private rent is often too expensive.

records.title: Review laws & fund better mobile coverage in rural regions of England
records.description: We call on the Government to review laws and regulations to ensure network operators meet coverage standards across rural regions, not just urban areas, and strengthen Ofcom’s powers to hold providers accountable for failing coverage.
records.further_details: People across the South West pay the same as customers in cities with reliable 4G and 5G, yet many cannot depend on a basic mobile signal at home or work. On many occasions, calls drop, messages fail, and poor coverage can be dangerous in emergencies. In a developed country, we believe this is unacceptable. We feel there is no clear accountability or timetable to fix it. We believe the South West deserves the same reliable service as the rest of the UK.

records.title: Conduct review of asylum decisions granted on basis of applicant's sexuality
records.description: We want the government to launch an investigation into all successful asylum applications over the last 20 years that granted leave to remain where a contributing factor to acceptance was based on the supposed sexuality of the applicant and the corresponding risk in their home country.
records.further_details: A recent BBC investigation has revealed an industry behind bogus asylum applications. We feel that the industry of processing bogus asylum claims is not just fraud, it is serious organised crime. We think the government has a duty to find out how deeply this criminality has spread and how long it has been going on.

records.title: Review access to ultrasound scans for babies showing signs of pyloric stenosis
records.description: Review whether there is adequate access to ultrasound scans for newborns as soon as they show signs or symptoms of pyloric stenosis. We believe quicker access could help stop newborns being misdiagnosed with other conditions, reduce unnecessary use of medications and protect newborns from early on.
records.further_details: My son was put through 5 weeks of misdiagnosis and unnecessary medications. He had surgery at 8 weeks old to treat his condition (Pyloric Stenosis). This could have been treated earlier on if the signs/symptoms had been acted on earlier. A scan takes 3 minutes to confirm if a newborn has PS.

records.title: Require teachers disclose AI usage when producing class materials
records.description: Require secondary and further education teachers to disclose AI usage when a significant portion of a class material, such as a handout sheet, presentation, images and videos, have been generated using Artificial Intelligence. We think AI sits in an ethical and legal grey-area due to how it is made.
records.further_details: AI use is seen by many as lazy and unprofessional due to the speed it can output content at. AI can also get information wrong or skip out on needed context, which can be important when teaching certain topics. AI generated work also needs to be checked for misinformation which oftentimes eliminates the potential time save of AI generated content.

records.title: Require social medias to have an opt-out for short-form scrollable content
records.description: The government should mandate for social media platforms to have an opt-out feature for short-form scrollable content on their platforms. The algorithms that social media platforms employ are addictive by design, and are most effective on short-form content such as 'Reels'  on Instagram.
records.further_details: I feel that the implementation of such a regulation would reduce the addictive nature of such platforms and hence would improve productivity. The short-form content of these sites is addictive by nature and can cause individuals to spend hours upon hours stuck on these platforms due to the dopamine rush that it brings. The opt-out feature would allow individuals to take back control of their social media without having to give up access to it, reducing addiction and likely improving mental health.

records.title: Make all visa holders eligible for ILR after 5 continuous years of residency
records.description: Allow holders of any visa, including a student and graduate visa, to apply for ILR after 5 years of continuous residency in the UK.
records.further_details:
We believe five years of continuous residency in the UK should be legally sufficient to allow people holding Student, Work, or Family visas to apply for Indefinite Leave to Remain status.
 
We believe if these people are required to pay Council tax, Income tax, the NHS annual fee, visa application fees, and contribute to the UK economy through payment of housing and cost-of-living expenses, they should have the right to remain in the UK.

records.title: Abandon planned cuts to the annual Cash ISA subscription limit
records.description: Abandon planned reduction of the Cash ISA annual subscription limit from £20,000 to £12,000 and associated measures. We believe these changes add complexity, reduce ISA clarity, and do little to improve financial education or encourage informed investing.
records.further_details: The Government plans to reduce the Cash ISA annual subscription limit from £20k to £12k and introduce further restrictions such as taxing interest in Stocks & Shares ISAs. We believe these changes add unnecessary complexity to an already poorly understood system, increasing admin burdens for savers and providers. With average Cash ISA subscriptions around £7,000, the reforms affect relatively few people and in our view do little to improve financial education, encourage investing, or create noteworthy revenue.

records.title: Amend Equality Act so “sex” refers to gender identity, not biological sex
records.description: Amend the Equality Act 2010 so “sex” refers to someone’s gender identity, acquired via the Gender Recognition Act 2004 if different to their biological sex. This would not mean self-ID or removing standards from single-sex spaces but would adjust the definition to match today's society.
records.further_details:
We feel the UKSC ruling For Women Scotland Ltd v The Scottish Ministers has introduced a myriad of issues for trans people across the UK and is based upon technical definitions within the Equality Act. 
 
By amending the Equality Act, the position of gender in law can be better aligned with the position of gender in society. This could allow for better protection of trans rights without necessarily diminishing women's rights or the importance of safe places. We feel the current system isn't fit for purpose.

records.title: Review care pathways for women with suspected endometriosis
records.description: We call on the UK Government to review care pathways for women with persistent symptoms of suspected endometriosis. They should be given a clear pathway to appropriate specialist care, further investigation where clinically appropriate and ongoing symptom management.
records.further_details: Endometriosis can cause severe, life-changing symptoms, yet many women face long waits, repeated appointments and investigations without a clear diagnosis or plan. When investigations are inconclusive, women can be left without support despite continuing to suffer. We want the NHS to provide a clear pathway, including specialist review, further investigation where appropriate and symptom management while women wait. An inconclusive investigation should not mean the end of a woman’s care.

records.title: Review accessibility of public transport for people with mobility disabilities
records.description: I believe all public transport should be made more accessible to those with mobility issues. Although most train stations have lifts, sometimes wheelchair users still need to book in advance and if lifts aren't available, they have to plan longer alternate journeys.
records.further_details: I believe that the government are in a position where they can work with all transport networks in order to build a more accessible world. In this day and age, I think people are defined by what they can do and I believe that empowering the disabled community would allow for more opportunities to be made available to them, and it starts with the ability to be self sufficient.

records.title: Scrap RPI +3% interest on plan 2 & postgrad student loans & charge RPI only
records.description: I am concerned about the interest rate that is charged on Plan 2 and Postgraduate student loans. These are much higher than other student loan plans. We urge the Government to only charge interest at RPI on plan 2 and postgraduate student loan repayments
records.further_details: The current rate of interest on these loans is often higher than most mortgages and young people are unlikely to be able to pay both. I am concerned motivation to earn may be lost as some mid-high earners may end up paying a high marginal tax rate plus NI until they retire. I am also concerned that women may be adversely affected as interest still accrues while on parental leave, which could potentially be contributing to the already low birth rate.

records.title: Mandate all school times to start at 9am
records.description: I want the UK Government to require all schools to begin at 9am nationwide. I believe this would create safer, less rushed mornings and allow time for breakfast and travel, and this policy would support students’ health, improve learning conditions and create a fair standard across all schools.
records.further_details: I feel that school in the UK should start at 9am to match teenagers’ natural sleep cycles. Research, such as the Sleep Foundation’s studies on adolescent sleep, shows later starts improve focus, attendance and academic results, while reducing stress and tiredness. I believe a 9am start would support better mental health, safer journeys and more effective learning, helping students achieve their full potential.

records.title: Legalise psilocybin in the UK
records.description: Legalise psilocybin for adult recreational use in the UK through a tightly controlled licensing framework. Ensure products are tested for safety, consistently dosed, clearly labelled, age-restricted, and fully traceable from production to sale.
records.further_details: Psilocybin is used in varying doses, from microdoses to higher experiences, with anecdotal reports of improved mood, creativity, and perspective. Research suggests potential value in studying conditions like depression, PTSD, and anxiety in controlled settings. We believe a regulated adult framework could improve safety, consistency, and information, reduce illegal supply risks, and support public health guidance, education, and further research into both benefits and risks.

records.title: Reform the 60% effective tax rate on income between £100,000 and £125,140
records.description: We want the Government to remove the 60% effective tax rate created by the tapered withdrawal of the Personal Allowance for people earning between £100,000 and £125,140. We think this should be replaced with a clear, fair tax band, such as a 45% rate on income over £100,000.
records.further_details:
We believe that the current system is unfair and creates a hidden penalty for professionals who increase their earnings. In our view, many people in this bracket are not wealthy, yet face one of the highest marginal tax rates in the UK, discouraging career progression and additional work.
Higher earners already contribute significantly more in tax. We think the taper adds an excessive burden that punishes ambition and undermines fair taxation, and reform is needed so people are rewarded, not penalised, for progressing in their careers.

records.title: Make Mental Health First Aid a Legal Requirement in Workplaces
records.description: Require workplaces to include Mental Health First Aid in their first-aid provision, ensuring staff have access to someone trained to recognise signs of poor mental health, start a supportive conversation, provide initial support and signpost them to appropriate professional help.
records.further_details: Mental health can affect anyone, including at work. Mental Health First Aid training gives people the skills and confidence to recognise signs of poor mental health, listen without judgement, start supportive conversations and respond appropriately, including during a crisis. It also teaches people how to signpost someone towards appropriate professional support. We believe mental health should be taken as seriously as physical health in workplace first-aid provision.

records.title: Change the law for pet food so manufacturers have to announce recipe change
records.description:
I want parliament to enforce pet food companies to have to announce when they add or change recipes by adding a sticker to all bags containing this new recipe. 
Many animals have allergies and companies change recipes without any warning making pet owners have to figure out why their pets are ill.
records.further_details: My dog has a severe chicken allergy and sensitive foods which start off with no chicken in, secretly add chicken or chicken oil which causes him severe pain, sickness and diarrhoea. Many dogs have this same allergy as well as many others.

records.title: Introduce a mandatory deposit on vapes and electronic cigarettes
records.description: The Government should introduce a mandatory deposit of at least £5 on all vapes and e-cigarettes. Backed by waste firms such as Biffa, we believe this simple, fair, efficient and cost-neutral measure would reduce fires and explosions from improper disposal while helping to tackle vape littering.

records.title: Ban bicycles on roads with a speed limit above 30mph
records.description: Ban bicycles on roads with a speed limit above 30mph, as the majority of the cyclists never go above this speed.
records.further_details: We believe cyclists cause unnecessary stress and traffic build up when they ride on road with 40 and 50mph speed limits. Some cars are able to overtake and are often still at risk of hitting the cyclist. We believe it is not safe enough on the roads where cars travel above 30mph for cyclists, whether they're cycling leisurely or as fast as they're able.

records.title: Prisoners with financial equity should pay for their own incarceration
records.description: We ask that the Govt considers charging Prisoners, who have financial equity, to pay for the expenses of their incarceration. This should not only help to finance the building of new Prisons but could also act as a deterrent and could help prevent the necessity of early release of offenders.
records.further_details: We believe tax payers should not be expected to pay for the incarceration of offenders who have the financial equity to pay it themselves. This money could then go towards the building of new prisons negating the need to release offenders early; which we feel is not only disrespectful to the victims but could also puts the public at risk. If they own property it should be sold to pay for their care just it applies to elderly people who go into Nursing / Residential care. There should be no exception on this ruling.

records.title: Mandate human auditing of police evidence processed by AI
records.description: Mandate independent human auditing of all AI police evidence summaries. We believe automated triage of intimate victim data poses severe privacy risks and causes automation bias. AI must never replace human review or compromise critical victim confidentiality.
records.further_details: We believe the £75m PoliceAI rollout introduces severe judicial and privacy risks. Under new Home Office disclosure overhauls, algorithms could automatically summarize case files. This over-reliance could trigger severe automation bias, where overworked officers blindly trust machine output. If PoliceAI misses exculpatory evidence, we think trials could collapse under the 1996 CPIA framework, denying justice. Crucially, intimate victim data may face catastrophic privacy violations. We do not think weak internal guidelines can stop this.

records.title: Ban employers from disadvantaging Armed Forces spouses and partners
records.description: We are concerned that military spouses and partners are facing backlash from jobs for being married to serving personnel. This is due to having an unstable location and not knowing where we will be posted next.
records.further_details:
Military spouses and partners can struggle to find work in isolated areas, which can lead to them to have to take certain benefits.
 
We feel this is discrimination. Due to our partner's jobs, we can get posted to different locations. Businesses sometimes worry about our loyalty.
 
Ban employers from disadvantaging Armed Forces spouses so discrimination cannot happen any longer. We give up a lot too and it is unacceptable for us to face this discrimination. Something needs to be done.

records.title: Give international researchers equal access to all funded childcare
records.description: Change eligibility for all free childcare for working parents so international researchers and research students lawfully living and working or studying in the UK can access all funded childcare regardless of visa restrictions on access to public funds.
records.further_details: The UK recruits talented researchers from around the world, but many cannot access some funded childcare because of visa restrictions. This can make returning to research after having a child financially difficult, particularly for women. We believe international PhD students, postdoctoral researchers, fellows and other research staff should not face an additional childcare barrier simply because of their immigration status.

records.title: New fund for councils to support High Street regeneration
records.description: We want the Government to set up a new fund for local councils to revitalise their High Streets and town centres, which currently are experiencing a strikingly low footfall and loss of local shops.
records.further_details: We believe the High Street issue is bigger than many think and  current Government funds are insufficient. This isn't about a return to tradition; we feel it's about bringing hope to local communities who can look for a place to socialise and celebrate the town's local culture. It can provide a safe haven for local businesses and entrepreneurs to feel empowered to begin new cafes, retail stores and more. This can make communities stronger together, whilst also making sure that the economy can benefit from increased enterprise.

records.title: Require standardised classifications for accessible hotel rooms.
records.description: Introduce a mandatory, standardised classification system for accessible hotel rooms (e.g. Type 0–Type 5), with clearly defined minimum accessibility features for each category, and require this classification to be displayed at the point of booking.
records.further_details:
Currently, there is no consistent definition of what an “accessible” hotel room includes. This means disabled people cannot reliably know whether a room will meet their needs before booking.

Rooms described as accessible vary widely. In some cases, rooms lack sufficient space for wheelchair users, include unsuitable bathroom facilities such as baths instead of level-access showers, or have fixtures positioned in ways that make them unusable.

This creates unnecessary barriers, reduces independence, and undermines the intention of the Equality Act 2010.

A clear classification system would improve transparency, allow informed choice, and support consistent standards across the hospitality industry.

records.title: Create a national plan to protect pets and livestock during emergency disasters.
records.description: I ask the Government to create a UK-based animal emergency response plan. This should include national guidance to protecting pets, farm animals and wildlife during emergencies, and create a helpline for animals specifically.
records.further_details: During floods, fires and other natural disasters people are often helped to safety, but animals are generally left behind in the struggle of nature. We all love our pets and farm animals, and they play a great part in our lives, so why aren’t we helping them?. I think animals should have as much help as humans and that communities, emergency services, local authorities and anyone in general should have clear plans in place and know how to help, don’t you?

records.title: Make British Sign Language (BSL) compulsory in high schools in England
records.description: The Government should make British Sign Language (BSL) a compulsory lesson in secondary schools across England, ensuring pupils have regular opportunities to learn and develop practical BSL communication skills.
records.further_details: This petition calls for British Sign Language (BSL) to become a compulsory lesson in secondary schools across England. Deaf people face communication barriers every day, yet most hearing people leave school unable to communicate with them. Teaching BSL from an early age would break down these barriers, promote equality and inclusion, improve understanding of Deaf culture and give every young person a valuable life skill they can use throughout their lives.

records.title: Requiring all businesses with public toilets to have baby changing facilities
records.description: Parents and carers shouldn’t be forced to change their child on dirty floors or anywhere with no privacy. I am asking for a law that requires all businesses and venues that provide toilet facilities for their customers should also provide suitable baby-changing facilities.
records.further_details:
We are calling for a basic standard that if a venue provides customer toilets, parents and carers should be able to safely and hygienically change their baby there.

Parents should not be forced to change their baby on a toilet floor, in a pram, on a chair or in another unsuitable public space simply because the venue has chosen not to provide a changing facility.

records.title: Ban doctors from making decisions to make do not resuscitate (DNR) orders
records.description: Ban doctors from making decisions not to attempt cardiopulmonary resuscitation. A DNR order should only be put in place by a person themselves or by their family who have the power to do so. Make doctors request a court order to otherwise make a DNR order.

records.title: Fund national scheme for disabled person's free bus passes to include peak times
records.description: Only in London are disabled people allowed free transport before 9.30am – we believe the rest of the country deserves this freedom as well. Often we have hospital appointments in the early morning or need to get to work. Disabled travel passes nationally should include peak times to account for this
records.further_details: We are disabled not werewolves! Like other people, we also need to go out between the hours of 11pm - 9am.

records.title: Change SEND acronym to ‘SPECIFIC Educational Needs' in government publications
records.description: We want change. The word ‘Special’ has had negative connotations for the last 40 years, so why should we continue using this derogatory term for young adults and children in this day and age? Why not change this to ‘Specific’ a term that is individual and tailored to each student?
records.further_details: As someone who is undertaking a University degree in Education and as someone who has familial links to people with ‘Specific’ Educational needs, something needs to change. I find it difficult to become a teacher in an educational system in which we are still calling children and young adults ‘Special’ for requiring Specific educational needs. This petition asks you to consider those children. In addition, why change an already established name. SEND but change the S from ‘SPECIAL’ to SPECIFIC

records.title: Introduce a £6,285 tax-free allowance for second-job income
records.description: About 1.26–1.35 million people in the UK work second jobs, often due to rising living costs. As Personal Allowance is usually used by a main job, second-job income is taxed immediately, reducing extra earnings for workers trying to cover essential expenses.
records.further_details:
A dedicated £6,285 allowance for second jobs would support working people who are contributing more to the economy through additional employment. It could help key workers, part-time workers, carers, students, and low- to middle-income households keep more of what they earn.

We believe this change would encourage employment, reduce financial pressure on households, and reward hard work without removing the existing Personal Allowance for primary employment

records.title: Require outdoor venues to ban dog access in extreme hot weather
records.description: Require all outside event venues to ban dog access when the weather is considered too hot and dangerous for dogs.
records.further_details: So many people don’t understand the risk of walking dogs in extreme heat. It’s hard to educate everyone however if venues banned dog access when the temperature is too high, less dogs would face the heatstroke, suffering and potential death caused by overheating.

records.title: Require and fund all schools to provide swimming lessons in Key Stages 2 to 4
records.description: Given the recent events we want Government to ensure all school children are given mandatory swimming on the curriculum at every school, from key stage 2 right until the end of key stage 4. Too many children are leaving school unable to swim and this is unacceptable and is a key survival skill.
records.further_details: When we grew up, we went swimming every week and then in secondary school on a cycle so during every year would swim for around six weeks once a term. We feel many schools without pools do not offer enough swimming time for children during PE and funding needs to be made to ensure every school can get children to pools regularly during key stages 2 - 4. This must be compulsory and at least six weeks per year should be allocated per child.

records.title: Fund and mandate suicide barriers in all train stations
records.description: I want the Government to fund the construction of mandatory suicide barriers in all train stations to save lives. I feel suicides at train stations not only impact families and friends, but the staff working on train lines and in stations, as well as the wider community.
records.further_details: My mission is to make it mandatory for all train stations to have suicide barriers to protect vulnerable and suicidal people. Not only could this protect individuals who are suicidal but also train drivers and members of staff. It could also protect commuters who need to travel by trains. Suicide can significantly impact families, friends, and wider communities.

records.title: Mandate Air Conditioning in New Build Homes and for Vulnerable Residents
records.description: Require all new build homes, and current homes for vulnerable people, to include energy-efficient air conditioning and heating systems. Update building regulations to ensure homes remain safe during increasingly frequent extreme heat and cold caused by climate change.
records.further_details: Require all new build homes and homes intended for vulnerable people to be fitted with energy-efficient air conditioning and heating systems that provide safe indoor temperatures throughout the year. Climate change is causing increasingly frequent and intense heatwaves across the UK. Excessive indoor temperatures can lead to serious health problems, hospital admissions and preventable deaths, particularly among older people, disabled people and those with long-term health conditions.

records.title: Require same-sex intimate care in schools and childcare settings
records.description: Require schools and childcare settings to ensure pupils receive same-sex intimate care wherever reasonably practicable. When this is not possible, a second member of staff should be present to safeguard vulnerable children and reassure parents.
records.further_details:
Many children with disabilities are non-speaking or unable to communicate if they are uncomfortable or something goes wrong during intimate personal care. We believe parents should have confidence that their children’s dignity, privacy and safety are protected. 
 
Schools and childcare settings should be required to provide same-sex intimate care wherever reasonably practicable and require a second member of staff to be present if this is not possible.

records.title: Introduce a national car park and toll zone offer to auto-pay
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce a national car park and toll zone offer to opt-in to an auto-pay register, charging registered drivers automatically instead of requiring individual payments, which, if missed, can lead to fines.
records.further_details: ANPR can be used to identify vehicles using a car park, LEZ, toll or bridge, public or private. Currently used to catch non-payment, at penalty rates — with no equivalent system to make paying easy. We ask Government to introduce a national opt-in payment register linking a plate to a card or wallet. Any operator using ANPR to enforce payment must be required to accept it: registered vehicles are then auto-charged the standard rate, no penalty issued. Non-registered vehicles remain enforceable as now.

records.title: Fund free NHS embryo & egg freezing for endometriosis patients
records.description: We call on the Government to fund free egg and embryo freezing on the NHS for people with endometriosis who are at risk of infertility. We believe no one should lose the chance to have a family due to this condition or be denied treatment based on where they live or what they can afford.
records.further_details: For many people, having a family is one of life's greatest hopes. Endometriosis can damage fertility, leaving patients to face painful treatment while fearing they may lose the chance to become parents. We call on the UK Government to fund the provision of free and fair access on the NHS to egg and embryo freezing for endometriosis patients, so decisions are based on clinical need, not where someone lives or what they can afford.

records.title: Ban schools from punishing children for poor attendance
records.description: Ban schools from punishing children for poor school attendance, for example by not allowing them on school trips or to attend prom.
records.further_details: Some children in mainstream schools across the country are being excluded from school trips and their prom due to poor attendance. We feel this is discrimination against those with SEN, health and mental health needs who might be physically or mentally unable to attend school frequently, not through lack of trying. We believe punishment is detrimental to the mental wellbeing of those excluded from school events and should be stopped.

records.title: Ensure local authorities cannot impose an overnight 'tourist tax' on UK citizens
records.description: Plans to allow local authorities to charge an overnight visitor levy 'tourist tax' must not apply to UK Citizens.
records.further_details: Ensure that any local authorities who choose to impose an overnight tourist tax on people for visiting their areas cannot apply it to UK citizens who often already pay substantial taxes for living in the country.

records.title: Review NHS care for women experiencing miscarriage
records.description: We want the government to review NHS care for women experiencing miscarriage. I've had 7 miscarriages and I'm fighting for answers. I've experienced miscarriages, ectopic pregnancy, surgery and devastating uncertainty.
records.further_details:
We think women experiencing pain or bleeding should have a clear pathway including HCG blood tests and results guiding the next step. Women can be left waiting for appointments/scans or told there is no one available at weekends. 
 
Miscarriage can affect mental health enormously. Please review the system and give women faster answers, better support and more compassionate care.

records.title: Prevent publication of addresses of people charged but not convicted of a crime
records.description: Change the law to prevent the publication of the home addresses of people who have been charged but not convicted. Police should also be required to respect requests for media anonymity where a person is vulnerable or at risk, unless there is an overriding legal or public interest.
records.further_details: A vulnerable person may be arrested while experiencing severe anxiety or mental health difficulties and feel unable to answer police questions, resulting in a “no comment” interview. They may later be charged without a court having determined their guilt. Publishing their home address, particularly when they live alone, can create serious safety and welfare concerns. The law and guidance on the publication of defendants’ addresses should be urgently reviewed to prevent addresses from being published.

records.title: Review & reform improved care and support for young hysterectomy patients
records.description: Review and reform care and support for young hysterectomy patients, including setting national standards for full, evidence-based information on hysterectomy risks, benefits, alternatives, as well as mandatory pre-operative counselling and access to specialist care and multidisciplinary teams.
records.further_details:
There should also be structured, long-term follow-up support including hormonal, physical & mental health support.
 
We call on the UK Government to improve care for women offered hysterectomy for endometriosis and adenomyosis. Many are not fully informed of long-term risks, alternatives, or ongoing symptoms. We urge a review and reforms like mandatory pre-operative counselling, clear information for informed consent, and structured post-operative follow-up including physical, hormonal, and mental health support. Women deserve safe, informed choices and consistent long-term care.

records.title: Fund fully paid student paramedics placement hours
records.description: Student paramedics work really hard within the ambulance service and they don’t get the recognition that they should. They don’t get paid for their placement hours, although they are also experiencing a cost of living crisis with inflation.
records.further_details: Many students have to travel to their placement and have to fund their own education. We think paying student paramedics for placement hours would give them more recognition and support for their hard work.

records.title: Recognise Chagossian community as a distinct category in official UK statistics
records.description: Many Chagossians are former residents of the British Indian Ocean Territory, removed in the 1960s–70s. The UK recognises them as a community while stating there is no permanent population. We call for formal recognition as a distinct ethnic group in UK official statistics.
records.further_details: Chagossians were removed from the British Indian Ocean Territory in the 1960s–70s and share a distinct history, culture and identity. We believe that formal recognition in official UK statistics would ensure coherence across legislation, policy and public administration, including official classification and status.

records.title: Require & fund more safe housing & mental health support for released prisoners
records.description: Require and fund more safe housing and mental health support for vulnerable prisoners on release, in order to stop the release of mentally ill and high-risk prisoners becoming homeless and without support.
records.further_details:
It should be a statutory requirement to provide safe accommodation and mental health care to prisoners who leave jail. Release plans should also be created for prisoners before their release date.
 
We believe the Government must ensure that vulnerable prisoners who are released receive safe accommodation, mental health care, addiction support and crisis intervention before release.

records.title: Ban animal farming for meat & dairy purposes and release animals into the wild
records.description: Ban animal farming for meat & dairy purposes, and release farm animals into the wild away from humans. They are a separate species from us, and we don't need to consume them or animal-derived products as we have other alternatives and meat and dairy free products on the market already.
records.further_details: We believe we should be looking to increase our vegan options. We feel humans should not be killing animals or farming them for animal-derived products that are only meant to be used by animals of their own species.

records.title: Ban fashion firms burning clothes and contributing to emissions. Recycle instead
records.description: This law would ban the burning of used clothing or unsold stock and rather require that big companies opt for recycling schemes instead.
records.further_details: Globally, the equivalent of one garbage truck of textiles is burned or landfilled every second. The UK alone sees 300,000 tonnes of used clothing end up incinerated annually. A YouGov survey for Keep Britain Tidy reports that 79% of adults feel that the UK buys too much stuff. This law would reduce the amount of emissions released due to the burning of used clothes, and would ban the burning of unsold stock if it is able to be recycled. Additionally, it would hopefully discourage excessive buying.

records.title: Review conventions relating to MPs’ dress in the Commons Chamber
records.description: Electoral law allows candidates to stand under a commonly used name. However, Commons rules by convention require business-like attire, with guidance issued and enforced by the Speaker. Consequently, a Member elected in character might not be able to sit in the attire they campaigned in.
records.further_details: The House should review conventions relating to dress. We urge the House to refer the matter to the Procedure Committee or pass a resolution permitting attire worn by candidates in election campaigns in the Chamber if identity can be verified for the oath, voting, and security.

records.title: Regulate creator management agencies to protect adult content creators
records.description: Creator management agencies operating in the adult content industry are largely unregulated, leaving creators vulnerable to exploitation. We’re calling on the Government to introduce mandatory commission caps, minimum service standards, and contract protections to safeguard creators.
records.further_details: Creator management agencies face zero regulation. Creators can be signed into unfair contracts, lose control of their accounts and earnings, and pay excessive commissions for substandard services. This exploitation is widespread and well documented. Creators deserve the same basic protections as any other worker.

records.title: Require parliament to approve publicly funded second office for the PM
records.description: We call on the UK Government to cancel plans for a publicly funded second location for the PM’s office without a clear public mandate to do so, and without publishing the costs, and evidence that it represents value for taxpayers.
records.further_details: The Government plans to create a second base for the Prime Minister. We believe taxpayers should not fund an additional Prime Ministerial office without a clear public mandate, full transparency over the costs and evidence that it offers value for money. We think the Prime Minister should work from the existing official office at 10 Downing Street unless Parliament approves a different arrangement.

records.title: Ban plastic glitter and non-biodegradable slime.
records.description: Plastic glitter and non-biodegradable slime are unnecessary sources of plastic pollution. Used for minutes but persisting for centuries, they create microplastics that contaminate nature. The UK should ban their sale and support biodegradable alternatives, as it did with plastic microbeads.
records.further_details: Most commercial slime cannot be recycled because it is made from synthetic polymers and often contains plastic glitter, foam beads, dyes and other additives. Once used, it typically ends up in landfill or is washed away, where it can contribute to microplastic pollution. With over 400 million tonnes of plastic produced each year and less than 10% of plastic waste ever recycled, the UK should eliminate unnecessary plastic products that cannot be effectively recovered.

records.title: Review women's health care regarding unwanted effects of birth control
records.description: We want a review of what support GPs and sexual health clinics provide regarding the unwanted effects of birth control. There should be more investigation into what is causing said symptoms, and more support and care for these symptoms, such as medication or switching to a different method.
records.further_details: We believe a lack of emphasis on the side effects of birth control is incredibly damaging. We feel the NHS can be very dismissive of this matter, often guessing rather than providing informed estimates on how a medication may affect a specific individual. This is causing young people and women alike to suffer the consequences through unnecessary trauma. With all the technology provided, it should not be a guessing game or down to women to figure it out and risk horrific side effects.

records.title: Introduce a cap on how much companies can charge for public EV charging
records.description: I would like the government to review how much some companies are charging for public EV charging and introduce a cap on the prices.
records.further_details:
With more energy companies now offering EV/Eco5/Eco7 tariffs at home for cheap overnight charging at less than 10p per kWh and more people going "green" by purchasing an EV, I find it astonishing that companies are charging between 70-90p per kWh which for a long range battery would cost around the same price as a petrol car.

I believe the government should review this and introduce a cap to encourage more people to go green.

records.title: Increase penalties for non-payment of child maintenance & strengthen CMS powers
records.description: We ask the Government to strengthen CMS powers, improve data sharing with HMRC and Companies House, close loopholes for self-employed parents and company directors, speed up arrears enforcement, and introduce tougher penalties for persistent non-payment.
records.further_details: We believe the current levels of penalties and enforcement action are insufficient. It can take years to get a child maintenance payment out of a parent. We are concerned that non paying parents are taken at their word - if they say they cannot afford arrears nothing is done about this. We feel there needs to be serious reform in this space including serious penalties.

records.title: Introduce mandatory licensing for professional carers in England
records.description: Create a national licensing and professional registration system for carers and domiciliary care workers who provide personal care, safeguarding support and assistance to elderly, disabled and vulnerable people across England.
records.further_details:
Professional carers support elderly, disabled and vulnerable people with medication, personal care and safeguarding, often inside private homes without supervision.

Care agencies are regulated by the CQC, but individual carers in England are not nationally licensed like nurses, doctors or security staff. I have seen firsthand how inconsistent care can affect vulnerable people and families.

Carers should have mandatory training, DBS checks and accountability through a licensing system.

records.title: UK Government to step up efforts to promote peace and accountability in the DRC
records.description: We call on the UK Government to formally acknowledge the victims of war in the DRC, and to review UK policy towards seeking peace and accountability in the DRC
records.further_details: For over two decades, the continued conflicts in the east of the DRC have claimed millions of lives. Civilians, including women and children, continue to suffer from violence and displacement. This must stop. We are not calling for military intervention by the UK. We are calling for the UK Government to show the UK's solidarity with victims, increase awareness of the situation in the DRC, and to use stronger diplomatic efforts to encourage lasting peace and justice in the DRC.

records.title: Require ceiling hoists in all NHS A&E accessible toilets and cubicles.
records.description: Require all NHS A&E departments to have ceiling hoists in accessible toilets and treatment cubicles to ensure safe, dignified care for disabled patients.
records.further_details:
Many disabled people require ceiling hoists for safe transfers and dignified care. We ask the Government to require all NHS A&E departments to provide at least one ceiling hoist in an accessible toilet and one in a treatment cubicle.

Without this equipment, patients may face unsafe transfers, delays, discomfort, and loss of dignity. Providing ceiling hoists would improve accessibility, protect patients and staff, and ensure disabled people receive equal, safe emergency care.

records.title: Include the Endocannabinoid System and Omega-6/3 Balance in GCSE/A-Level Biology
records.description: We call on the Government to include the Endocannabinoid System in the GCSE/A-level curriculum. We believe that this vital system is missing from the curriculum, leaving students completely unaware of how diet can drive chronic disease.
records.further_details: The endocannabinoid system (ECS) regulates mood, sleep, appetite, and immunity, yet is absent from UK biology lessons. Equally missing is how omega-6/omega-3 imbalance can disrupt ECS signalling fuelling chronic inflammation and disease. We call on the Government to review the science curriculum and make ECS biology and omega balance required topics at GCSE and A-level, with exam boards updating specs and teacher training. Students should learn what anandamide is and how to optimise its signalling.

records.title: Create a Norwegian-style UK Sovereign Wealth Fund
records.description: Create a UK Sovereign Wealth Fund, based on Norway’s model, to invest wealth for future generations. Use long-term investment returns to strengthen public finances, reduce debt, fund infrastructure and public services, and build a more resilient economy.
records.further_details: We believe a UK Sovereign Wealth Fund should be established as an independent, professionally managed investment fund owned by the British people. Initial capital could come from revenues generated by natural resources, energy projects, selected government asset sales, and other one-off receipts. The fund should invest globally and reinvest returns, creating a permanent national asset that strengthens public finances and benefits both current and future generations.

records.title: Review 5G mast planning laws
records.description: Review 5G mast planning laws to ensure that their visual impact is mitigated and people are safe from any potential long-term harm to health, especially in areas close to homes, schools, nurseries and parks.
records.further_details:
Relaxed 5G planning laws have seen much larger masts installed across towns - close to where people live, work and children go to school, creating a huge visual disturbance.
 
The appearance of towns must be protected and any potential long term health impact of 5G taken into greater consideration. Potential health impacts are considered in the European Parliament's Panel for the Future of Science and Technology report on the 'Health Impact of 5G'.
 
This petition would like the government to enact more stringent 5G planning laws.

records.title: Improve safeguarding and support for dementia care
records.description: The Government must appoint a Minister for Dementia Care, ensure all nurses are aware of their obligation to report harmful practice to the barring service and NMC, appoint a safeguarding nurse for every dementia care setting and mandate statutory CCTV in all dementia care settings.
records.further_details:
Also, the Government should:
- Review the effectiveness of the legal obligation to provide a reference
- work to ensure that, where there have been legitimate concerns about the suitability of an employee, these can be conveyed without fear of litigation or reprisal 
- Ensure all staff are trained in iatrogenic harm
- make sure all dementia settings have mental health nurses present  
- issue guidance making clear that a staff member's DBS check cannot be a guarantee of future behaviour.

records.title: Limit postal voting to elderly, disabled, people overseas & military personnel
records.description: Limit postal voting to people who are elderly, disabled, overseas and part of the armed forces. We believe voting should otherwise be in person in the voting booth. This could ensure that every vote is private, free from pressure or influence, and could protect trust in our democracy.
records.further_details: We believe postal voting is increasingly open to pressure, organised handling, block voting, and the risk of inducements or improper influence. To safeguard voter independence and public confidence, we believe it should be limited to genuine need, with in-person voting as the default.

records.title: Remove and ban hostile architecture from public spaces
records.description: We would like the government to ban hostile architecture. This could include spikes outside buildings, curved and segregated benches, 'leaning' benches or gated doorways - anything that prevents homeless people from finding comfort. We would also require existing examples to be removed.
records.further_details:
Homeless people have reported being affected by hostile architecture. For example:
 
- 60% reported an increase in defensive architecture that made sitting or lying down impossible.
 
- 35% said they were unable to find a place to sleep or rest due to these measures.
 
We believe hostile architecture should be banned because it is unfair for homeless people to endure this hostile treatment. No one deserves to be unable to access safe spaces to sleep at night.

records.title: Require all diversity training in employment settings to cover ADHD
records.description: Require all diversity training programmes in employment settings to include ADHD alongside Autism. We believe this disorder is widely misunderstood by employers, causing employees to face prejudice and avoidable consequences. Education of ADHD traits (time blindness, overstimulation).
records.further_details: Many diversity training programmes in employment typically now include the awareness of typical traits seen in autistic individuals, and common ways to support their specific needs. As ADHD is a neurodiverse disorder alongside Autism, it can cause those suffering from it equal distress in the workplace when support requests are ignored. As many individuals do not look beyond the word of the ‘H’ for ‘Hyperactivity’, those diagnosed are commonly misunderstood.

records.title: Ban all fuel refined from Russian crude oil now, full transparency on origins
records.further_details:
We call on the UK Government to immediately close the sanctions loophole allowing the import of any refined fuel products made from Russian crude oil via third countries.
 
The UK public was told sanctions would reduce Russia’s ability to finance aggression. We believe allowing Russian-origin crude oil to be effectively processed through third countries before entering the UK weakens public trust in sanctions enforcement and damages the UK’s credibility in supporting Ukraine.

records.title: Create a public register of individuals convicted of violent crimes and abuse
records.description: Anyone convicted of serious offences such as emotional, mental or physical abuse, domestic abuse and violence, stalking, harassment, violence against children, child abuse, sexual abuse, assault, rape, attempted murder, or murder should be placed on a publicly accessible register
records.further_details: This register would show offences they have been convicted of. It would be available through a secure government run website, allowing members of the public to carry out a simple search when it comes to their safety and the safety of their families. My concern is by the time it takes to apply through Claire’s Law they may already be emotionally involved, living with, or trying to leave them which can be the most dangerous time and sometimes too late. This could be known as "Stacey's Law".

records.title: Legalise public use of private e-scooters for over 18s with helmets
records.description: We want the Government to make public use of privately owned electric scooters legal for over 18s wearing a helmet.
records.further_details: We see e-bikes being allowed in public and think e-scooters should be allowed too. E-scooters are an environmentally friendly way of getting around. I agree their use needs to be regulated and that's why I think their use should be restricted to over 18s and a helmet should be worn for safety reasons. We feel that the fact that e-scooters hired from the local council are allowed in certain areas but not privately owned ones ridiculous. We want the Government to allow people the right to travel around their local area using their own e-scooters safely – reducing traffic on the roads could be a bonus.

records.title: Increase full-time Carer's Allowance to at least £840 per week.
records.description: We want the government to increase the Carer’s Allowance to at least £840 per week. We believe carers should be valued within society and their worth should be reflected in the help and benefits they receive. Carers can receive £83.30 a week, however they must provide care for at least 35 hours pwk.
records.further_details: The weekly rate for round the clock professional care can be thousands of pounds. We feel there is a massive difference between the carer’s allowance and the amounts charged by private companies. I don't think carers are paid enough to live on. Carers can carry out the same, if not more work, than paid carers, looking after individuals. I feel that the amount they are paid demonstrates the disdain and lack of appreciation that they receive.

records.title: Allow phones in schools
records.description: Allow phones in schools. Students should not have too go to attendance or an office to speak to their parents. Students also want to have fun with their friends and take photos which should be normal and so they have stuff to look back at.
records.further_details: Phone rules are making students recieve sanctions, which many can agree shouldn’t be normal. Nowadays students get in trouble if your phone is seen. It shouldn’t be such a big issue just to have ur phone seen. In most schools, you get your phone confiscated, or even have to get a carer or parent to collect it from the school which is a bit of an exaggeration. Detentions, isolation even suspensions and exclusion take place over something that shouldn’t be such a big deal.

records.title: Appoint a Minister for Men and Boys to lead national change
records.description: We call on the UK Government to appoint a Minister for Men and Boys to lead a national strategy addressing challenges affecting boys and men, including serious violence, suicide, education, health, employment and wellbeing, ensuring coordinated prevention and support across government.
records.further_details: Boys & men face significant challenges across violence, suicide, education, health and employment. These issues span multiple government departments, creating a need for stronger coordination and accountability. Recent deaths of young men through violence highlight the importance of prevention, early intervention and long-term investment in opportunity, support and wellbeing. A dedicated Minister would help ensure these issues receive the national leadership they require.

records.title: Bring all Social Care into the Public Sector under the NHS & stop means testing.
records.description: We demand the government bring all Social and Community Care under the NHS, fully funded by general taxation. We believe neither Social Care, Community Care, nor the NHS should be for profit, but remain free at the point of use.
records.further_details:
We want to reverse the changes to Social Care, made over decades, which have resulted in parts of it being transferred to local government, privatised and/or means tested.

We believe that trends in local authority budgets and Social Care funding since 2010 have harmed the sector and that immigration policies have contributed to staffing problems.

records.title: Legalise pepper spray, review street intimidation legislation & fund more police
records.description: We call on the Government to legalise licensed carrying of pepper spray for self-defence for the public, review legalisation regarding individuals who intimidate or harass women or girls in public particularly at night and fund an increase in police forces in high-risk areas at night.
records.further_details:
Many women and girls feel unsafe walking alone at night due to intimidating behaviour from individuals often under the influence of drugs or alcohol. UK law currently bans pepper spray under the Firearms Act 1968, leaving limited self-defence options. We want the Government to legalise the right for members of the public to carry pepper-spray for self-defence and would require a license.

The Government should also launch a review into strengthening legislation such as the Public Order Acts and Protection from Harassment Act 1997, which includes strengthening penalties for street intimidation.

records.title: Abolish grammar schools & reallocate funding to SEND & mainstream schools
records.description: Require phase out of remaining state-funded selective grammar schools. Reallocate funding to SEND support. Require local authorities to redirect resources from selective testing (11 plus) toward an inclusive, mainstream-first education system.
records.further_details: Require local authorities to abolish the 11 plus & integrate funding into mainstream education support, specifically the Government’s goal of providing core support for SEND within mainstream settings, ensuring more children can access multi-disciplinary services without needing lengthy statutory assessments. The government funding that we think is wasted on the 11 plus system can be used for other parts of the education system.

records.title: Mandate AI Transparency in hiring practices for UK Based Businesses
records.description: We want the Government to force UK Based Employers to provide clarification in rejection emails as to whether an AI system (such as Applicant Tracking Software (ATS)) was used to provide the initial rejection and to provide a means for a 'Right of Reply' if jobseekers feel this was made in error.
records.further_details: The Government should require UK employers to disclose when ATS or other AI systems are used to automatically reject job applications. These tools often scan for keywords without context, which can disadvantage dyslexic and neurodivergent applicants, undervalue apprenticeships and hands-on experience, and reinforce class barriers in hiring. Applicants should also have a clear right of reply where they believe an automated rejection has been made in error.

records.title: Restore a national EV charge point database with new enforced data standards
records.description: The government decommissioned the National Charge Point Registry and created what we see as unenforceable regulations. Data on EV charge points, many built with public money on public land, is held by private companies. Drivers often have to rely on charge point information from commercial apps.
records.further_details: The Public Charge Point Regulations 2023 requires operators to publish open data but sets, we believe, inadequate quality standards and enforcement mechanisms. The NCR was decommissioned in 2024 leaving no government-backed, central source of truth. We are concerned that many operators are international or foreign-owned companies receiving UK public grants to install chargers, then publishing what in our view is insufficient data or locking some behind commercial platforms.

records.title: Review Children’s Social Care Repeated Placement Moves to Prevent Harm
records.description: Review children’s social care repeated placement moves, with an aim to ensure proper support is in place for children, improve safeguarding of foster placements, and introduce stronger accountability when systems fail. We urge action now to review the system and protect vulnerable children.
records.further_details:
The review should consider limits on repeated placement moves, with mandatory independent review after multiple disruptions and guaranteed access to trauma-informed mental health support for all children. We call for stronger safeguarding of foster placements, including substance misuse screening and drug testing and better support to prevent family isolation, ensuring families are included and supported where appropriate.

The review should also consider support for women in the justice system to help reduce separation of mothers from children.

records.title: Make unpaid trial shifts illegal in all circumstances
records.description: Make it illegal for employers to use unpaid trial shifts. Require all trial work to be paid at least the National Minimum Wage, with clear rules to prevent misuse.
records.further_details: Unpaid trial shifts can be unfair and leave people out of pocket, especially when they last several hours or lead to no job. We believe this mostly affects young people and those in certain sectors. In our view, everyone should be paid for the work they do, and banning all forms of free trial shifts could stop employers taking advantage.

records.title: Review Protections for Children Against Coercive Control in Family Court Process
records.description: Review safeguards in family courts to address coercive control, to ensure children’s voices are heard, and prioritise their wellbeing. Improve training, guidance, and use of supervised contact where manipulation or emotional harm is identified.
records.further_details: We believe that children are often not properly heard in family court, leaving them distressed and unheard in decisions affecting their lives. The process can be emotionally damaging, with repeated hearings and forced contact causing long-term harm. When coercive control is overlooked, it can affect a child’s mental health, development, and future relationships. Stronger protections are needed to ensure children’s voices matter and their wellbeing is prioritised.

records.title: Introduce National Driving Safety Rules for Licensed Taxi Drivers
records.description: Introduce national safety standards for taxi and private hire vehicle drivers to prevent them from interacting with phones/booking systems whilst driving, and from working excessive hours without mandatory rest periods. We believe this could better protect passengers and other road users.
records.further_details: Unlike HGV drivers, taxi and private hire vehicle drivers are not subject to consistent nationwide limits on driving hours or mandatory rest breaks. Research estimates fatigue may contribute to 10–20% of road crashes. In 2022, 22 people were killed and 652 injured in crashes where mobile phone use was recorded as a factor. Taxi drivers regularly rely on phones and booking apps while driving, increasing distraction risks. Stronger national safety regulations are needed to protect road users.

records.title: Mandate drinking areas for wildlife in outdoor shopping centres
records.description: Wildlife struggle with the heat & often hide under cars during hot weather. As wildlife is a vital part of our ecosystem we believe we need to support them during hot seasons.
records.further_details:
The Government must make it mandatory for all outdoor shopping centres to have areas with cover & drinking water for animals.

Due to climate change, we are getting hotter heat waves which puts a strain on our wildlife. We believe we have a duty of care to ensure that they have access to drinking water, and cover from the sun to prevent them from seeking cover from under cars and putting themselves in danger. Access to drinking water for wildlife should ensure they do not dehydrate or suffer from heat related illnesses. We believe we need to care for our ecosystems, and ensure that animals are safe and have access to water.

records.title: Seek visa agreements with GCC countries for UK Refugee Travel Document holders
records.description: We want the UK Government to use diplomatic engagement with Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries to improve visa access and recognition of UK Refugee Travel Documents.
records.further_details:
UK refugees who hold these documents can face difficulties travelling to Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE because recognition visa
 
We ask the Government to raise this issue with GCC governments and seek clearer arrangements for UK Refugee Travel Document holders, including whether visas can be issued and what requirements apply.

records.title: Ban liquid plastics in household products and introduce clear labelling
records.description: Introduce a total ban on Polymers in Liquid Formulations (PLFs) in all household cleaning and toiletry products due to health and environmental harm, alongside mandatory clear product labelling.
records.further_details:
UK law currently restricts certain solid microplastics in specific rinse off cosmetics but does not regulate synthetic liquid and semi-solid plastics (PLFs). These polymers are often poorly biodegradable and can persist in the environment, contaminating waterways and the food chain, which raises concerns for ecosystems and health. 
 
The Government must ban PLFs in consumer formulations, starting with toiletries and detergents where green alternatives exist. Until a full ban is achieved, the Government must introduce clear packaging labels so consumers can identify and avoid liquid plastics.

records.title: Stop the Government raising Veterans' reserve commitment to 65
records.description: Veterans signed a contract with the Monarch and Government to serve this country with their reserve commitment extending until they are 55. The Government must abandon what we firmly believe is a breach of contract made by extending the reserve commitment to 65.

records.title: Reduce fuel duty for HGV owner drivers & small hauliers
records.description: We call on the Government to reduce fuel duty for HGV owner drivers and small operators across the UK to help deliver fair fuel support.
records.further_details: Owner drivers keep Britain moving — delivering food, supplies and essentials every day. Fuel makes up 40–50% of owner-drivers’ costs. While big fleets can get discounts, owner-drivers cannot — and pay more per litre and earn less per mile than big fleet owners. We believe the 5p duty cut is not enough. Many drivers often work below minimum wage just to stay on the road. If owner-drives have to stop working, supply chains will suffer and prices rise for everyone.

records.title: Stop serious offenders changing their names to hide their criminal past
records.description: Change the law to prevent people convicted of serious offences from concealing their criminal history through name changes, including after release from prison.
records.further_details: A new name should not hide a serious conviction. We want stronger restrictions on name changes for people convicted of serious offences, including after release from prison. Any permitted change should remain traceable to previous identities and convictions in police records and relevant safeguarding checks. The aim is to protect victims and the public by preventing offenders from using a new identity to conceal a history that is relevant to others’ safety.

records.title: Ban the production, sale and import of lab-grown meat for human consumption.
records.description: We ask the Government to legislate to ban the production, sale and importation of cell-cultivated (lab-grown) meat for human consumption in the UK. No such product is yet authorised here. Parliament, not a regulatory process, should decide whether it enters our food supply.
records.further_details: The Food Standards Agency is assessing several applications and aims to complete safety assessments by early 2027. Italy banned cultivated meat in 2023. These products have no long-term record in the human diet, and reviewers have raised open questions about their safety and nutrition. We believe a ban would protect British livestock farming and rural communities, uphold UK food sovereignty, and take a precautionary approach to a technology not yet tested over the long term.

records.title: Review how GPs and A&Es identify paediatric infections
records.description: Review whether all GP practices have the necessary paediatric equipment to monitor blood pressure, heart rate and oxygen levels, and whether A&Es routinely use blood tests to screen children for sepsis. I think that ensuring this will save a lot of unnecessary hospital trips.
records.further_details: I feel a lot of the time children are seen by doctors either at the surgery or hospital A&E and told it is viral and there is not a need for medical treatment and some of the time it an infection is missed that requires medical treatment. I therefore think a review should be conducted to investigate this further.

records.title: Reform statutory leave so all workers have enough paid leave to truly live
records.description:
I want the Government to reform statutory annual leave so that all workers:
 
Receive roughly the same number of paid holidays as school children (~13 weeks per year). Have flexible leave options for personal projects, mental health, and family commitments.
records.further_details:
Workers currently are entitled to only 5.6 weeks paid leave including bank holidays, while school children have around 13 weeks off each year.
We feel this imbalance reduces life satisfaction, limits time for family, hobbies, and personal growth.
Life is for living, not just working. Paid leave laws should reflect that reality.
Flexible leave for wellbeing could allow people to recharge, care for family, and pursue meaningful life experiences, creating happier, healthier and productive communities.

records.title: Give the same support in law to police veterans as military veterans receive
records.description: Military veterans are afforded an enhanced status in law and greater provision of support in recognition of the trauma they may have suffered in conflicts as well as in recognition of the difficulty of leaving public service and adapting to life. We want police officers to be afforded the same.
records.further_details: Evidence suggests that more police officers are retiring with ill health or choosing to leave the service because of health impacts caused by policing, such as police assaults, feeling under constant threat, and often dealing with death and injury. They suffer 600-800 traumatic events in a lifetime when the general public may suffer between 4-8. More officers are reporting PTSD/CPTSD as well as physical issues that prevent them from doing their job. We believe adapting to private life is proving difficult and help is needed.

records.title: Fund multi-billion pound plan to restore railways in towns & rural areas
records.description: We call on the UK Government to fund a new, large-scale railway restoration and improvement plan to reconnect towns and rural communities across the UK. Local communities could submit proposals, in addition to investment in areas identified by the Government as needing transport investment.
records.further_details: Many towns and rural areas remain without adequate rail links, limiting economic opportunities. A nationwide, multi-billion pound plan could create jobs, support local economies, and reduce reliance on cars. Fund a new multi-billion pound plan to reopen railways in towns with populations over 5,000, taking advantage of the recent fall in net borrowing to create jobs and support green travel. Integrate with nationalised rail to provide reliable, affordable, and connected services for all.

records.title: Change the law for opposite-sex couples to convert civil partnership to marriage
records.description:
Allow opposite-sex couples to convert civil partnerships into marriage without dissolution, Remove mandatory waiting period linked to dissolution, Introduce a simple administrative conversion process
Set fees similar to those paid by same-sex couples
This would ensure equal treatment
records.further_details:
We believe this is unfair. Couples who wish to remain together and simply change their legal status should not be required to “end” their relationship in law, face long delays, or pay significantly higher costs.
This creates inequality between same-sex and opposite-sex couples and could place unnecessary emotional, legal and financial burdens on families.

records.title: Ban smoking around bus stops (for at least 9 metres)
records.description: I want the Government to ban smoking around bus stops. I feel it is unfair that one person’s smoking can affect and inconvenience everyone who needs to use public transport, including children.
records.further_details:
Second-hand smoke is highly toxic and contains numerous cancer causing chemicals. Decades of evidence show that passive smoking increases a non smoker’s risk of heart disease and stroke.
 
Bus stops are tight, crowded spaces where commuters, children, and people with asthma wait for transport. I believe that being forced to inhale harmful toxins from second hand smoke at bus stops is an unnecessary and avoidable health risk. Smoking simply does not belong in these confined public areas.

records.title: Mandate timebound reasonable adjustments and introduce appeals body
records.description: Mandate a time limit by which reasonable adjustment decisions must be made by an employer, following a request from an employee. We also call for any refusal to such a request to be made in writing with full reasons, and for an independent appeals body to be created to assist employees.
records.further_details: Many employees struggle to have necessary adjustments recognised and implemented in a timely manner, can experience cursory considerations of their requests by untrained employers, or may struggle to understand why an adjustment hasn't been considered reasonable, and have no clear process to appeal. We believe that these systemic shortcomings in how these requests are processed and responded to, result in employees not being able to sustain employment due to stress and forces others into grievance and tribunal processes.

records.title: Legislate to abolish royal prerogative powers & give them to Parliament
records.description: Parliament should legislate to abolish the Crown’s royal prerogative powers, including dissolution, prorogation, Royal Assent, appointments, treaties, Head of the Armed Forces, and King’s Consent over certain legislation. We want to place these powers under Parliament’s authority.
records.further_details: The Crown’s prerogative are powers held or exercised in the Monarch’s name. They include dissolving/opening Parliament, proroguing it, Royal Assent to Bills, appointing Prime Ministers/ministers, agreeing treaties, and being Head of the Armed Forces. King’s Consent give the Crown advance sight of, and special consent procedure for bills affecting the Crown’s powers. We believe all these powers should be handed to Parliament by statute.

records.title: Fund free meals for disadvantaged children in registered early years settings
records.description: We call on the Government to fund free meal entitlements for all disadvantaged children accessing government-funded early education in registered early years settings, comparable to the support available through free school meals.
records.further_details: Many families struggle to meet the additional cost of meals charged by early years providers, potentially limiting children’s access to funded early education. Early years settings also face significant financial pressures and cannot always absorb these costs. We believe the Government should fund free, nutritious meals for eligible disadvantaged children directly, ensuring that early years providers can remain financially sustainable and that no child is excluded because of their family’s financial circumstances.

records.title: Conduct review of use of wildlife warning signs on UK roads
records.description: We want the Government to consider a review of how wildlife road-casualty hotspots are identified and the process for installing appropriate wildlife warning signs and other measures to reduce animals being killed or injured on roads.
records.further_details: Every year, large numbers of wild animals are killed or injured on Britain’s roads. Road traffic is a significant and largely preventable threat to wildlife, particularly where roads cross established wildlife corridors, habitats and migration routes. The Government already provides warning signs for wild animals, small wild animals and migratory toad crossings. However, we are concerned that the use of wildlife warning signs is inconsistent, and many roads where animals regularly cross have no warning to motorists. A review is therefore needed.

records.title: Add the topic of indentureship as required content to the school curriculum
records.description: Between 1838 and 1917, approximately half a million indentured labourers from India and China were transported across the British Empire from Asia to the Caribbean. We call on the Government to include British indentureship as required content in the school curriculum.
