records.further_details: Indentureship expanded after the abolition of slavery, when Britain recruited workers, particularly from India, to labour on plantations across its colonies. Many faced harsh conditions, restricted freedoms and exploitation. We believe that teaching this history would help pupils better understand Britain’s colonial past and have a fuller understanding of the diverse communities that have shaped Britain today, such as the Indo-Caribbean and Chinese-Caribbean descendants of indentured labourers, who were also part of the Windrush generation.

records.title: End the Use of Bearskin in the Kings Guard Headgear
records.description: The Ministry of Defence must find suitable faux-fur alternatives for the King's Guard headgear that fulfil the necessary criteria. Currently, the hats require Black Bear Skin, costing over £2000 each, making them both expensive and ethically questionable.
records.further_details: Using black bear skin for the King's Guard clashes with the UK's ethical stance on animal welfare. It is imperative that the government mandate the MOD to implement a program exploring faux-fur alternatives that meet the criteria for the headgear. This program must be managed by an independent watchdog to guarantee transparency and ensure that animal welfare, alongside cost efficiency, remains central to the transition. Once an alternative is identified, it must be implemented promptly.

records.title: Provide funding to triple the current number of immigration enforcement officers
records.description: The Government should provide funding to triple the number of immigration enforcement officers, in order to deport more illegal immigrants.
records.further_details: It has been estimated that there are around 600,000 - 800,000 illegal immigrants in the UK. We believe more immigration officers could mean more deportations of illegal immigrants.

records.title: Reverse excluding death by dangerous driving from the early release scheme
records.description: We ask the Government to reverse its decision to exclude people convicted of causing death by dangerous driving and serving Standard Determinate Sentences from the Government’s early release scheme, and to restore their eligibility under the safeguards applying to other eligible prisoners.
records.further_details:
We recognise the devastating impact on victims and their families. However, we feel death by dangerous driving covers very different cases, and that courts already reflect seriousness and culpability in the sentence imposed. 
 
We believe a blanket exclusion removes any recognition of rehabilitation, good behaviour or reduced risk, and that it also affects innocent families and children. We feel the early release scheme still protects the public through supervision and licence conditions.

records.title: Do not ban imports from Israeli settlements in the West Bank
records.description: We call on the Government not to introduce its proposed ban on imports of goods from Israeli settlements in the West Bank, announced on 8 September 2026.
records.further_details: We urge the Government to reject a blanket geographical trade ban and retain the existing customs and origin rules for goods from Israeli settlements in the West Bank. We believe any action should target individuals or organisations responsible for proven unlawful conduct, rather than penalising lawful businesses, workers and consumers through broad restrictions on trade.

records.title: Introduce new offence for murder, dismemberment and concealment
records.description: There is currently no specific crime for a murder where the perpetrator has also dismembered and concealed the body. We think such an offence should be introduced with a mandatory life sentence with a minimum tariff of 40 years before eligible for parole. This should be known as Chantel’s Law.

records.title: Amend equality law to ban religions from barring women from leadership roles
records.description: The Equality Act 2010 still contains exemptions that can permit sex-based restrictions in some appointments for the purposes of an organised religion. We ask Parliament to amend the law so that no religion operating in the UK may bar women from clerical or leadership roles.
records.further_details: We believe Dame Sarah Mullally’s enthronement as the first female Archbishop of Canterbury shows that female religious leadership is both possible and legitimate. Religious freedom should not extend to institutional sex discrimination. We believe that no organisation operating in the UK should be permitted to exclude women from leadership by rule, custom or doctrine.

records.title: Change the law on minimum age for ear piercing to a minimum age of 12 years old
records.description: Remove the right for parents to inflict unnecessary ear piercing on children too young to care for the piercings themselves or have an educated opinion in the matter. Babies as young as a week old are having their ears pierced.
records.further_details:
Introduce a minimum age to an appropriate age of 12. Where children are of secondary school age and can make the decision themselves with parental agreement. 

Remove the ability for parents to take their new born babies and toddlers to have their ears pierced for no benefit to the child at all.

It causes disruption in school with having to take earrings out for PE lessons and increases the risk of infections and accidents for the child.

records.title: Fund legal support for parents in international child custody or recovery cases
records.description: Fund support for parents who need legal representation overseas in child custody or recovery cases to ensure financial barriers do not prevent them from accessing legal support.
records.further_details: Many parents in the UK cannot afford international legal costs when their children are overseas. This could leave them unable to challenge custody decisions or seek reunification. In our view, access to justice should not depend on financial circumstances. Support is especially important for vulnerable individuals, including those affected by domestic abuse or coercive control.

records.title: Repeal Pensions Schemes Act provisions on investment of private pension pots
records.description: The Government recently had legislation enacted to seize powers over the investment of private pension pots. I want these powers to be abolished.
records.further_details: I believe these new powers are not in the best interests of the pension holder and could possibly yield a significantly lower return on future investments.

records.title: Provide funding so all shops can offer free period products
records.description: Fund access to free menstrual products for all women. Most women have periods and sanitary products are a need not a want. We believe women shouldn't have to suffer with the cost of their essentials on top of the suffering of a natural cause.
records.further_details: Women can suffer with a variety of different physical inconveniences with their periods. The current cost of living is hard enough and having to budget and worry about how you will pay for sanitary products could be easily avoided if women's needs were put first. Not everyone has easy access to basic necessities and this petitions goal is to eliminate the stress of highly priced period products. I believe this will create a positive relationship between women and their periods.

records.title: Ban nicotine pouches
records.description: Please support parents and carers by banning nicotine pouches, an addictive substance that can harm children and young adults. We believe addressing this is vital to protect our youth's well-being and future.
records.further_details:
Nicotine pouches can be highly addictive and we are concerned they endanger children and young adults. Nicotine pouches can deliver high levels of nicotine, which is highly addictive, and their use can lead to nicotine dependence and expose children and young people to nicotine-related health risks. Many see it as a quick mood booster.
 
To protect youth, we believe banning nicotine pouches is essential. We urge the government to ban these substances and help parents and carers protect children, young adults, and their future. Please help ban this harmful substance from our country.

records.title: Change law so that bus drivers' hours align with other drivers
records.description: Change the law for bus drivers' hours so the maximum driving hours are 4.5 not 5.5 before needing a break of 45 mins rather than just 30, as bus driving involves stop-start driving & keeping up with high pressure timetables just like other delivery drivers, but with an arguably more valuable cargo.
records.further_details: We believe more and more bus drivers are suffering the effects of fatigue and mental exhaustion as bus companies push the drivers hours to the limit: it's not safe anymore and something needs to be done.

records.title: Abolish the High-Income Child Benefit Charge
records.description: Abolish the High-Income Child Benefit Charge so that Child Benefit remains a universal payment for all children, without any income-based repayment or restrictions. The policy should ensure equal support for all families regardless of income level.
records.further_details: We believe the current system unfairly penalises working families who already pay high taxes. We are concerned it could create inequality between households with similar incomes and does not reflect rising living costs. We feel this policy is outdated and the threshold no longer reflects real financial pressures in the UK. Child Benefit should support all children equally, without income limits.

records.title: Review school absence fines & pricing practices during school holidays
records.description: Launch a review into school absence fines and pricing practices during school holidays. The review should look into transparency rules on airlines regarding pricing, Air Passenger Duty, and how school holidays affect the market.
records.further_details: Many parents are constantly faced with a dilemma: either paying significantly higher travel costs during school holidays or being fined and/or prosecuted for taking their children out of school during the school year. Travel prices (especially flights) are much higher during school holiday periods. We feel this situation leads to unfair financial pressure on families, reduced access to family time and rest, and inequality in society.

records.title: End spousal maintenance payments after divorce
records.description: Simplify the divorce laws even further. No fault divorce = split assets equally. No more spousal payments. Divorce should be end of financial commitment to the ex-spouse. We believe it is completely unfair for one person to keep paying another even at end of divorce.
records.further_details: We believe that since the laws around divorce have been simplified e.g. no-fault divorce in 2022 spousal maintenance should also be abolished completely. We think it predominantly benefits female partners. This should not be allowed in today's day and age of gender equality.

records.title: Review into deaths of young people leaving the care system to include over 25s
records.description: The review into the deaths of young people leaving the care system should include over 25s. Many struggle throughout their life with the trauma and experience from before, and during, being in care, including with mental health issues, addiction, homelessness and to feel understood, seen and heard.
records.further_details: In our view, care experienced adults over 25 rarely feature in reviews, yet many sadly continue to struggle throughout their life to such an extent that they are no longer with us. We believe that trauma is often misunderstood without adequate Trauma Release Specific Mental Health interventions within the NHS, resulting in many concluding that mental health services don't work. We must develop a better understanding of Trauma in older Care Experienced and recognise gaps in care & support.

records.title: Change the definition of the Child Abduction criminal offence
records.description: We believe it should be forbidden for one of the parents to take the child out of its home of residence and deny that child any contact with the other parent, so factually denying their parental right. We want such an act to be included in the legal definition of Child Abduction.
records.further_details: We believe there are too many people undergoing this terrible situation and having their parental right violated and cancelled by the other partner. We feel this is a form of violence not only for the partner but mainly for the child himself.

records.title: Mandate insurance for electrically assisted pedal cycles
records.description: Require by law all electrically assisted pedal cycles (EAPCs) used on public roads to be registered and insured to improve accountability, support police enforcement, protect victims of collisions and help reduce dangerous and antisocial use. This rule already applies to e-scooters and most e-bikes.
records.further_details: We call on the UK Government to require all EAPCs used on public roads to be registered and insured. We believe this would improve accountability, help police identify offenders, protect victims through insurance, and help reduce dangerous and antisocial use, making roads and communities safer for everyone.

records.title: Fund free bus travel for children during all school holidays
records.description: We want the Government to provide funding to expand the free bus travel scheme for children to cover every school holiday break, rather than just the month of August.
records.further_details: While the initiative providing free August bus travel for under-16s has given families a vital cost-of-living boost, household financial pressures do not stop when summer ends. Families can face intense financial strain during the October half-term, Christmas, Easter, and spring breaks. Extending free bus travel to all school holidays could permanently reduce family outgoings, lower traffic congestion, improve safety, and encourage long-term sustainable travel habits among young people.

records.title: Allow a 5 day ‘holiday leave’ for children, anytime during a school year
records.description: Allow children up to 5 days of authorised term-time holiday each school year. This would make family breaks more affordable, support children’s mental health and wellbeing, and provide valuable family time, while keeping good attendance and education a priority.
records.further_details: Current rules can unfairly affect families who cannot afford peak school-holiday prices or whose jobs restrict when they can take leave. Travel can also give children new cultural, social and educational experiences. A 5-day allowance would recognise that learning and development happen outside the classroom too, while giving families greater choice, reducing financial pressure and supporting a healthier balance between school and family life.

records.title: Fund accessible swimming and water safety lessons for every disabled child
records.description: Provide ring-fenced funding for children with SEND to receive free, accessible swimming and water-safety lessons, including specialist instructors, one-to-one or small-group teaching and reasonable adjustments, until they achieve the safest level possible for their individual needs.
records.further_details: Swimming is a lifesaving skill, but many children with SEND cannot access standard group lessons due to sensory, communication, physical or learning needs. They may need specialist teaching and much longer to learn, leaving families facing high costs or no suitable local provision. Although swimming is in England’s primary curriculum, adapted lessons and continued support are not guaranteed. No child should be denied the best possible chance of being safe in water because they are disabled.

records.title: Make neurodiversity education a mandatory part of the national curriculum
records.description: Make it a compulsory part of the national curriculum to teach children about neurodiversity, including autism, ADHD, and other additional needs, in an age-appropriate way.
records.further_details:
I am the parent of a child with additional needs, including autism, who is non-verbal & has complex needs. In public places like parks, I see other children react negatively towards him—shouting if he doesn’t play as expected, saying he is too loud, or pointing when he is stimming.
 
Children are naturally curious, and questions are okay. But without understanding, this can lead to unkind behaviour, exclusion, and bullying. Teaching neurodiversity in schools could help children understand differences and promote kindness and inclusion. This is not consistently taught and making it mandatory could benefit all children.

records.title: Fund direct employment routes for prisoners upon release
records.description: Fund direct routes into employment for prisoners after release in order to reduce reoffending rates and increase national cohesion. The introduction of job-related facilities in prisons with partnered businesses could lead to direct employment routes for prisoners upon release.
records.further_details: A larger workforce can support economic growth. Research shows that a lack of employment has been a leading factor for higher reoffending rates; decreasing community cohesion. Introducing these direct routes into employment could increase the active workforce and community cohesion, which can work to break social constructs.

records.title: Review availability and speed of access to Right to Choose autism assessments
records.description: Review how well Integrated Care Boards are facilitating access to autism and ADHD assessments under Right to Choose to enable quick access and to ensure patients already on waiting lists are assessed within a reasonable timeframe.
records.further_details: Across England, there are reports that families are being told that Right to Choose autism and ADHD assessments are being restricted or paused by Integrated Care Boards. Some children already on waiting lists face long or indefinite delays. Without assessment, they cannot access support in education or evidence for DLA, leaving families without help. We believe this is undermining the Right to Choose system as it delays early intervention, risking long-term harm to children’s development and mental health.

records.title: Introduce Mandatory DBS Checks for Private Landlords
records.description: Require all private landlords in England to complete a basic DBS check before letting property, to prevent individuals with relevant criminal histories from operating as landlords, strengthen safeguarding standards, and improve tenant safety and accountability across the private rented sector.
records.further_details: There is no requirement for most landlords to undergo criminal record checks, despite tenants facing Right to Rent checks. We believe this creates a safeguarding gap, as landlords hold keys and direct access to homes, including those of vulnerable renters. We believe allowing individuals with sexual or violent offences to operate undermines the UK’s VAWG strategy. DBS checks already inform “fit and proper” tests in other licensing schemes and should apply nationally, as a basic safeguarding standard.

records.title: Mandatory police recording of where child abduction/coercion began online
records.description:
We believe recording this information would:
- improve national understanding of online enabled risks
- support evidence based safeguarding policies
- help police identify patterns and intervene earlier
- strengthen child protection
Data is not routinely collected on if abductions begin online
records.further_details:
Police forces report rising levels of online grooming, yet there is no national system to track when digital communication leads to a child being persuaded, coerced, or moved.
We believe recording this information would:
- improve national understanding of online enabled risks
- support evidence based safeguarding policies
- help police identify patterns and intervene earlier
- strengthen child protection across the UK
We want Government to introduce a statutory duty for police forces to record online involvement in abduction cases.

records.title: Prohibit Punitive Siting of Infrastructure
records.description: Legislate to specifically prohibit the punitive siting of national infrastructure, such as detention centres, based on the voting records of constituencies. Ensure all infrastructure placement is determined by logistical suitability and administrative necessity, rather than political retaliation.
records.further_details: We believe policy proposals to prioritise high-impact facilities in areas that vote for specific parties constitute intimidation. Using infrastructure to punish communities for exercising their democratic rights violates the principle of neutrality in governance and threatens the integrity of our elections.

records.title: Review state pension system to reflect lifetime workload and job intensity
records.description: We want government to review the state pension system to reflect lifetime workload and job intensity. Consider flexible or earlier retirement access for physically demanding sectors like hospitality, recognising long hours, shift work, and health impact versus less intensive roles.
records.further_details: We are calling for a review of how the UK state pension system reflects real working conditions. Many people in hospitality and similar sectors work long, irregular hours, often 45-60+ per week, with physical demands, stress, and limited recovery time. Over a lifetime, this creates a different health impact compared to less physically intensive or desk-based work. We are asking for a fairer approach that considers lifetime workload, job intensity, and occupational strain in retirement access.

records.title: UK Government must raise human rights concerns with Bangladesh Government
records.description: We urge the UK Government to raise concerns about human rights, political freedoms and due process, including prolonged detention without trial, with the Bangladesh Government and encourage fair judicial processes there.
records.further_details: Bangladesh is a Commonwealth country with strong diplomatic ties to the UK and a British-Bangladeshi population in the UK exceeding 800,000. Since the political transition of 2024, concerns have been raised regarding prolonged detention, due process and political freedoms. We believe the Government should act on the basis of these concerns and encourage respect for human rights and fair justice in Bangladesh.

records.title: Establish a UK UAP Reporting Centre and maintain data and report to the public
records.description: Establish a public unidentified aerial phenomenon (UAP) reporting office and publish non sensitive data via a public website. The US has AARO with major funding for investigations. We feel the UK’s silence is unacceptable; the public deserves a national UAP reporting service and, the truth.
records.further_details: This petition seeks a national UAP reporting office to handle incidents relevant to UK security and to share that data with the public.

records.title: Lifetime animal ownership ban for animal killers & mandatory custodial sentence
records.description: We call for a lifetime ban on owning animals for anyone who has killed an animal, and for offenders of such crimes to be automatically given a custodial sentence which must be served in full.
records.further_details: We want this to be known as ‘Minnie’s Law’.

records.title: Rolling Blackouts to automatically trigger a General Election within a month
records.description: Defence of the Realm & Energy Security are primary responsibilities of the government. We feel a rolling blackout would represent a fundamental failure to meet that responsibility, which should automatically give the electorate opportunity to remove a mandate through a general election.
records.further_details: We believe current government policies are sacrificing energy security in favour of virtue-signalling. We feel 'renewable' technology is being favoured over stable, reliable, despatchable at scale CCGT & nuclear baseload power generation. We are concerned that the more 'renewable' generation with which the UK power grid is burdened, the greater is the risk of grid failures, brown-outs & blackouts which are direct results of government energy policy. Government must be held fully accountable for these.

records.title: Make all MP investments public to help stop personal gain harming the country
records.description: We call for full public transparency of all MP investments to ensure decisions in Parliament are made for the good of the country, not personal financial gain. Mandatory disclosure of all investments could help protect democracy, prevent conflicts of interest, and rebuild public trust.
records.further_details: We view full transparency of all MP investments - not just those above established thresholds - as essential to help protect democracy & public trust. When financial interests are hidden due to falling below established disclosure thresholds, the risk of decisions being influenced by personal gain can increase. Making all investments public could help ensure accountability, prevent conflicts of interest, & reassure citizens that policies are shaped for the country’s benefit, not private profit.

records.title: Increase the age of consent to 20 with exceptions for young people 16-19
records.description: The age of consent should be raised to 20, to protect young people. There should be a clause so that those aged 16-19 are not criminalised for having consensual sex below the age of consent.
records.further_details: Our current age of consent law allows for an adult, of any age, to have sex with a 16 year old, however a 16 year old is still considered a child by law. This law leaves young people vulnerable to abuse and exploitation. Raising the age of consent to 20 will protect young people, while having a clause so that they are not criminalised will allow them to have consensual, age appropriate sex.

records.title: Review existing laws and rules to ensure asylum seekers can access transplants
records.description: We are concerned that the “ordinary residence” rule and related NHS policies are preventing asylum seekers from being placed on transplant waiting lists, even in life-threatening cases.
records.further_details: We call on the Government to review existing rules to ensure access is determined by clinical need rather than immigration status, guaranteeing fair, life-saving care for all.

records.title: Fund free university and higher education
records.description: The average fees per year for an undergraduate degree in the UK is £9,000, and that’s not including housing fees. Just tuition alone. We believe that due to this, millions of students and their family are suffering from huge financial issues because of this.
records.further_details: I believe this can impact the future and economy of the UK. Tuition fees rose by 3.1% in the last few years and student debt will increase and increase over time.

records.title: Legislate to apply current abuse laws to historic cases, including sentencing
records.description: We urge the Government to pass a law to apply current abuse laws to historic abuse cases and ensure all laws and sentencing frameworks reflect our current understanding of trauma and barriers to disclosure; ensuring survivors receive fair treatment and meaningful access to justice.
records.further_details: We believe the law has changed to reflect society's understanding of the seriousness & lasting impact of historic abuse. However, many legal cases and decisions are governed by laws that existed when the abuse occurred. We believe this risks creating injustice, as it fails to recognise the realities faced by many victims. Survivors do not always disclose abuse immediately due to fear, trauma, shame, manipulation, or a lack of support. In many cases, disclosure can occur years or even decades after the abuse.

records.title: Require police to notify parents if child 18+ with additional needs is arrested
records.description: We call on the Government to require the police to notify the parents of a person over 18 if that person is known to have autism or ADHD, have mental health issues, or if they suspect that the person has diminished mental capacity.
records.further_details: We believe that people over 18 with additional needs do not have the mental capacity to speak for themselves, especially if in a mental health crisis, and that they are being majorly let down when their parents are not allowed to liaise with them because they are over 18. We therefore think the Government should introduce a requirement for the police to notify the parents in such cases so that parents can speak to services involved to help their child.

records.title: Restrict the use of generative AI to healthcare professionals
records.description: Pass a law that limits generative AI use to healthcare professionals, to help detect cancer earlier for example. I believe generative AI in society is ruining the planet as well as people’s mental health and social skills.
records.further_details: I believe generative AI is rapidly increasing climate change, is detrimental to the environment, and that it should only be used for things such as detecting cancer, as it can detect cancers earlier than most machines can. We need to restrict access to generative AI to help our planet and give our future children a chance at a good life.

records.title: Ban all counter protests happening on the same day in the same town or city
records.description: There are often counter protests at times where large protests are happening. This causes a vast amount of pressure on police presence and is a huge factor on public money paying to keep counter protests peaceful. There can be violent behaviour, so it needs to stop.
records.further_details: The time has come to put an end to counter protests as they can be unruly and violent. The police are under a lot of pressure to police these counter protests, so they should be banned from happening at the same town or city as any protests happening. People need to be able to attend protests peacefully without counter protesters, some of who act violently or irrationally, by bullying and violently harassing the protesters or speakers. We need to stop this bullying!

records.title: Review police treatment of certain groups or certain behaviours
records.description: We call for a review into what we consider to be two tier policing.
records.further_details: In our view, examples of two-tier policing include different treatment of certain groups of people, or some behaviour (for example protests and demonstrations), where some people are dealt with more harshly, more robustly, than others by law enforcement.

records.title: Review & strengthen sentencing for child sexual offences by trusted adults
records.description: Review and strengthen sentencing laws for child sexual abuse offences committed by teachers and other adults in position of trust to create meaningful deterrent, and restore confidence in the justice system and ensure that the protection of children remains at the heart of the law.
records.further_details: These offences can devastate victims, families and the wider community. I believe that too often those who abuse positions of trust receive suspended sentences or punishments that do not reflect the seriousness of their crimes. The law must ensure offenders against children in positions of trust face stronger consequences, creating a real deterrent and restoring confidence in the justice system.

records.title: Remove higher income tax rates: only 20% rate for all
records.description: Make the 20% income tax rate apply to everyone, from the lowest paid to the richest, on all earned income above the basic tax-free allowance. We want no higher tax rates, no exceptions & no loopholes or tax breaks so that tax is unavoidable & easy to understand & in our view fair for everyone.
records.further_details: At the moment billionaires and large business can avoid tax with loopholes and tax breaks, and the use of tax havens etc.,. We believe this not only gives the impression of not being fair, it is not fair and deprives the country of tax income it desperately needs to fund the NHS and the increases needed in defence etc.,. So I propose a flat rate of income tax so the rich don't feel penalized for success, and the lower earners feel the rich pay their fair share.

records.title: Mandate neurodiversity training for staff in children’s sports & arts
records.description: We call on the UK Government to mandate neurodiversity training for any staff members working with children in the sports and arts sectors, including in grassroots sports clubs, football academies and the arts.
records.further_details: We believe neurodiversity training could provide staff with basic awareness of autism, ADHD and other neurodivergent conditions. Many children have hidden needs and may be excluded without understanding or adjustments. Schools must make reasonable adjustments under the Equality Act 2010; we believe the same support should apply outside school.

records.title: Lifetime ownership bans & fines for animal cruelty offenders to support rescues
records.description: Implement lifetime animal ownership bans for anyone guilty of animal cruelty offences and require them to pay a £10,000 fine to fund animal rescue organisations. We believe too many animals are being dumped because of boredom or illness, and that rescues can’t cope with the demand and costs.
records.further_details:
Animal cruelty is a serious ongoing concern for all rescue organisations. Many do not have enough funding and solely rely on public donations. With recent cost of living increases, we are concerned it will put greater pressure on the people working there and severely impact their mental health. 
 
We want stricter rules enforced and big fines imposed to help poor, defenceless animals and support the people who are saving them.

records.title: Ban recreational vaping: prohibit sale, manufacture, and importation
records.description: Ban vaping. Prohibit the sale, manufacture, and importation of all non-pharmacy vapes, restricting legal sales to pharmacies, and limiting flavours to tobacco, mint, or menthol.
records.further_details:
Make it completely illegal for convenience stores, supermarkets, and specialized vape shops to sell any vaping devices or e-liquids.
Reclassify all legal vapes as pharmacy-controlled products. They should only be dispensed by qualified pharmacists to adults using them strictly for smoking cessation. 
Eliminate all remaining brand imagery, device colours, and appealing flavour names, enforcing strict pharmaceutical packaging across all remaining legal cessation products.

records.title: Require new data centres to be energy net zero via local production
records.description: Requite new /in planning stage data centres to be energy net-zero by making them produce enough power locally through renewables to cover their own usage. Apply large fines and triple energy costs for noncompliance, with the proceeds going to public renewable projects.
records.further_details:
Data Centres are large, power-hungry buildings, where large amounts of power are used, which can end up as waste heat. In our view, these data centres could be powered by renewables.

We believe this could have the following benefits:
- Push the focus onto energy efficient solutions. 
- Reduce the impact on the power grid, allowing construction in more remote
areas, away from residential areas.
- Opportunities for innovation, promoting the UK as leaders in this area.

records.title: Stop funding free entry to national museums and galleries for foreign nationals
records.description: Significant public funding is allocated to maintain free entry to major British museums for all visitors, including foreign nationals: £484m grant aid in 2024-25 alone. A solution is for museums to institute an entry fee for foreign nationals visiting these institutions like in other countries.
records.further_details: I am deeply aware of the current cost of living crisis affecting our nation. Significant public funding is allocated to maintain free entry to major British museums and cultural institutions for all visitors, including foreign nationals. Charging foreign nationals an entry fee is a fair and tested model already in place in several countries. This petition urges the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport to conduct a feasibility study and consider implementing this change.

records.title: Amend Law to address historic coercive control & post-separation domestic abuse
records.description: I want historic coercive control to be recognised and properly considered by the law. Survivors can endure years of abuse, inc manipulation through children, finances & false allegations, yet be left without justice simply because the abuse occurred before coercive control became a criminal offence.
records.further_details: This petition calls for the Government to review how historic coercive control and post-separation abuse are dealt with. Survivors can endure years of psychological, financial and emotional abuse, including manipulation through children, interference with employment and false allegations. We want historic patterns to be properly recognised and considered, with lawful routes to accountability, while respecting the prohibition on retrospective criminal liability.

records.title: Review and reform the tax status and structure of Judicial Pension Schemes.
records.description: We call on the UK Government to launch an independent review into the structure of the Judicial Pension Scheme (JPS), specifically focusing on whether the tax-unregistered status of the scheme aligns with public sector fairness and fiscal responsibility.
records.further_details: Currently, under schemes like the JPS 2022, judicial pensions operate as tax-unregistered schemes. This structure means standard annual and lifetime tax allowances do not apply to these benefits in the same manner as they do for most other public and private sector employees.  We believe all publicly funded pension schemes should be subject to independent oversight to ensure transparency, public value, and equity across the civil service and broader public sector workforce.

records.title: Demand reparations from the US for impact on the UK economy
records.description: Under the current US administration, western economies have been significantly impacted by unprecedented US tariffs, which have affected global markets. More recently, US attacks on Iran have caused an energy crisis. This directly impacts the cost of living in the UK.
records.further_details: We believe the US Government must be held accountable for trying to drag NATO into supporting its attack on Iran and that the US has caused the passage of oil through the Strait of Hormuz to all but cease. We believe it is way beyond time for the UK Government to stand up to the US. The UK economy may take years to recover. We must therefore demand reparations from the USA.

records.title: Sites, apps & channels to have an opt-out button for gambling adverts
records.description: I want the Government to bring it in a law to make sure that all apps, streaming channels & websites have to have a simple way for a person to opt out of seeing gambling ads.
records.further_details: Gambling has ruined lives, that's no secret. It's proven that a gambling addiction can be an illness, so I don’t understand why it is allowed to be dangled in front of your face or your children's face when you watch these channels. Let's stop the issue before it becomes an addiction.

records.title: Ban routine overbooking on UK flights
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce a ban on routine overbooking of flights. Every day, thousands of flights are overbooked and as a result, many consumers are left at a massive inconvenience. We ask for a legal ban of this practice.

records.title: Ban all identify verification checks online
records.description: The Government should pass a law which removes all ID checks on the internet as we feel there is fundamentally no way of safely securing that stores ID information. We believe the idea you can check IDs without having to connect to a database is absurd and that there are massive security risks.
records.further_details: We feel it creates backdoors for malicious users and hackers to manipulate operating systems. We are concerned about foreign companies storing British citizens’ data, the possibility of deleted traces of data still existing, and significant safety risks existing even if the data is temporarily stored.

records.title: Change the law to have a general election every three years
records.description: A maximum of a three year parliamentary term would allow voters to replace Governments more frequently. We ask the Government to introduce legislation reducing the maximum term limit for a Parliament to three years.
records.further_details: We believe this would ensure greater accountability for Governments in power and prevent economic instability. It would also enable stronger democracy as the global economy system is dynamic and consistently needs adaptability and resilience. We feel this change would lead to better performance for leaders and Governments in power and enable a stable government and leadership, further promoting inclusive democracy and scrutiny. It would also prevent our leaders staying too long in power when they are underperforming.

records.title: Ensure dog theft is always treated as a criminal matter, not a civil dispute
records.description: I believe the law on dog theft needs to be changed again. I am concerned that too many dogs are being stolen, and in many cases the police treat it as a civil matter.
records.further_details: When there is a dispute about who has the right to keep a dog (e.g. after a shared care arrangement or break-up), police often classify it as a civil dispute instead of investigating it as theft. Having a dog stolen is hard enough without having to fight to get them back. Dogs are family and I'm concerned this is happening to too many dogs.

records.title: Base CMS payments on NET income not gross
records.description: Calculate child maintenance payments on NET income not GROSS.

records.title: Mandate pre-trial training for jurors in rape and sexual assault trials
records.description: Research shows that misconceptions about rape and trauma can influence jurors’ decisions. The UK Government must introduce mandatory training for jurors serving on rape and sexual assault trials to help ensure fairer, evidence-based verdicts, and to reduce the risk of unconscious bias.
records.further_details: Rape and sexual assault cases often rely on witness testimony, making jurors’ understanding of trauma and consent particularly important. Academic research has shown that rape myths can influence jurors’ decisions, with jurors who hold these beliefs being less likely to find defendants guilty. Mandatory, evidence-based training on trauma, consent and victim behaviour should be introduced to jurors serving on sexual violence cases, to help ensure verdicts are based on evidence rather than misconceptions

records.title: Protect DLA and linked disability support during PIP challenges at age 16
records.description: We want the Government to change the DLA-to-PIP transition rules so that, when a young person is required to transfer to PIP at 16, their existing DLA award & linked disability-related UC entitlement are protected while an adverse PIP decision is challenged, up to the original DLA award end date.
records.further_details:
Disabled young people must move from DLA to PIP at 16. An adverse PIP decision can end an existing DLA award and linked UC disability support, although their needs and costs remain.

Families may then wait many months for an appeal, with no control over delays, causing debt, poverty and lost opportunities in education, work and independence.

Backdating cannot undo this harm. Existing DLA and linked support should continue during a challenge, up to the original DLA end date.

records.title: Review protections for investors in off-plan and unregulated property schemes
records.description: Launch a review into protections for UK-based and overseas investors in off-plan and unregulated property schemes, including protection of deposits, use of investor funds, solicitor duties, developer corporate structures, regulatory oversight and representation of overseas investors.
records.further_details:
Investors can pay substantial deposits into UK property developments yet find that funds are not ring-fenced, may move between related companies, and normal financial protections may not apply.
 
When projects fail, investors can become unsecured creditors despite having regulated legal advisers. Developers may operate through multiple SPVs while the wider business continues raising investment. Many overseas investors also have no Member of Parliament to represent them. We believe these gaps require urgent review.

records.title: Introduce compensation & statutory time limit for the CMS to enforce non-payment
records.description: We call on the Government to legally require the Child Maintenance Service (CMS) to initiate formal enforcement action within 90 days if a paying parent fails to make payments.
records.further_details: Furthermore, if the CMS fails to collect or enforce payments within six months of a case being opened, the receiving parent should be entitled to statutory compensation from the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP).

records.title: Automatic access to disability benefits for working people with cancer
records.description: We demand automatic access to Universal Credit Health Elements and disability benefits for working people with cancer who have paid National Insurance contributions.
records.further_details: You pay into the system through years of taxes and National Insurance contributions, trusting it will provide a safety net during serious illness. A cancer diagnosis shatters that trust for far too many because, despite contributing responsibly, the current rules for Universal Credit (UC) and Personal Independence Payment (PIP) can fail to recognise the unique realities of cancer patients. We want cancer to be a recognised priority in UC and PIP.

records.title: Make smoking in homes with kids illegal
records.description: We want the UK Government to make it illegal to smoke tobacco inside a home where children (under 18) are living or present.
records.further_details: We believe children should not be exposed to second-hand smoke in their own homes. Breathing in cigarette smoke can cause serious health problems, including asthma, chest infections, and long-term increased risk of diseases and cancers. Now, children have no control over the environment they live in, which means they can be exposed daily to harmful smoke without protection.

records.title: Government to provide funeral costs for veterans from their pension funds
records.description: Service persons normally serve a minimum of 3-4 years from enlistment & can accrue a pension from the age of 17 & a half years. Money from that service pension could be put into a Government fund by an opt-in scheme & invested via bonds or another scheme to pay for a veterans funeral post discharge
records.further_details: Many veterans face trauma, divorce, suicide, addiction, or financial ruin after service. To spare grieving families the stress of funeral costs, we ask the MoD to automatically set aside a portion of service pensions into a protected fund. These funds, invested securely, could be released within 24 hours of death upon simple proof of service. We believe this safety net ensures no veteran is buried in debt, honouring their sacrifice with dignity and peace of mind for their loved ones during their darkest hour.

records.title: Allow additional voluntary student loan repayments through salary sacrifice
records.description: Allow UK employees to make additional voluntary student loan repayments through salary sacrifice, with employers able to pay the sacrificed amount directly to the Student Loans Company via payroll.
records.further_details: Many graduates make mandatory student loan repayments through payroll, but any extra voluntary repayments must come from take-home pay after tax and National Insurance. We believe this gives little incentive to repay faster, and we think allowing salary sacrifice for voluntary repayments would help workers reduce student debt, improve financial wellbeing and give employers a practical graduate support benefit. This could include safeguards such as annual caps and minimum wage protections.

records.title: Review domestic abuse case handling by police and CPS
records.description: Review the police and CPS' handling of domestic abuse cases and the case for independent oversight. This should include case reviews if failings are suspected to have occurred, with recommendations for accountability for errors, and consideration of improved evidence handling and communication.
records.further_details: We believe that repeated failures in domestic abuse cases, including poor evidence handling, delays and misinformation, show current systems are not working. In our view, these issues can continue even when raised, showing a lack of accountability. We think this risks undermining justice and causes victims to lose trust, and a review is needed to ensure accountability and prevent these failings continuing. This petition is informed by my own experience of the handling of a domestic abuse case.

records.title: Review how domestic abuse allegations are investigated for ILR applications
records.description: We are concerned that there is currently not sufficient investigation of domestic abuse allegations made by foreign spouses before granting indefinite leave to remain (ILR).
records.further_details:
British spouses can face severe mental distress and years of legal costs after allegations are made before evidence is properly tested. Meanwhile claimants may be granted ILR and receive public housing, Universal Credit, NHS support, education assistance, and legal aid by taxpayers.

We believe genuine victims must always be protected, but there must also be safeguards against unsupported or fraudulent allegations used for immigration, financial support or child custody advantage. Proven misuse should lead to refusal of settlement, repayment of public funds where possible, and lawful removal from the UK.

records.title: Mandate testing of women and babies for group b streptococcus
records.description: We want the Government to ensure that pregnant women and new-born babies of mothers who are positive for group b streptococcus are tested routinely.
records.further_details: I was tested positive at the beginning of my pregnancy with group b streptococcus I was only tested due to going in with blood spotting when I read up about this 20-40% of people get this and can be harmless but for babies it can be serious like my son did because he was not tested for strep b when he was born we went home for a week after being in hospital for 9 days & then while home my son was clearly ill and I nearly lost him and I don’t want anyone else to go through this too.

records.title: Set a statutory sugar limit for baby and toddler food
records.description: We want the Government to set a statutory sugar limit for baby and toddler food and to review packaging that could serve to obscure high sugar content.
records.further_details: Many commercial baby and toddler foods are packed with hidden sugars, including concentrated fruit purées, designed to sweeten products and, we believe, to build early brand loyalty. Packaging often uses potentially misleading claims like "no added sugar" or "one of your 5-a-day," masking the high total sugar content. This can help drive childhood obesity and potential cancers, while we believe it also hooks children on overly sweet tastes. The Government must introduce legally binding sugar caps on infant food and mandate honest, clear ingredient labelling on the front of packs to protect children's health.

records.title: Stop proposed change to financial rights for cohabiting couples without children
records.description: Limit the proposed changes to financial remedies on divorce for cohabiting couples to those with shared children only. Unmarried couples without children should not be given a 3 year time limit after which one of them can apply for the proposed financial remedy.
records.further_details: We believe the proposed changes give people a 3 year time limit to financially commit or to break off the relationship. In our view, couples working at their problems, approaching 3 years, may just decide to break up. This could be a huge burden on the property market. We believe  many relationships may  be broken off and those with weaker finances will be left searching for a home, with people focussing on matching with someone at a similar financial level to themselves to ensure they aren't going to be left after 3 years and lose half their wealth.

records.title: Fund & make mandatory solar panels in every large single level car park
records.description: Fund solar panels to roof existing large single-level car parks and make it mandatory for developers to install them on new car parks of that type.  We believe this would benefit achieving net zero while also stopping cars from getting too hot.

records.title: Require the Home Office to confirm settlement eligibility with visa decisions
records.description: Require the Home Office to provide every visa holder on a route to settlement with a written statement confirming their settlement route, whether previous leave counts towards settlement, and the earliest date they can apply for Indefinite Leave to Remain based on its current assessment.
records.further_details: Many people receive visas that can eventually lead to settlement, but are not told how previous immigration decisions affect their qualifying period. This can leave applicants uncertain about when they are eligible to apply for Indefinite Leave to Remain, risking expensive applications made too early or unnecessary delays. Clear written information would improve transparency, reduce avoidable applications and help people understand their immigration position.

records.title: Prevent MPs under investigation from resigning from the House of Commons
records.description: An MP wishing to resign their seat applies to the Chancellor of the Exchequer to be appointed to be the Crown Steward of the Chiltern Hundreds or similar. We ask that the Chancellor should refuse to make such an appointment if the MP is under active investigation by parliamentary standards bodies.

records.title: Reject the Gibraltar Treaty and reinstate full frontier border security
records.description: We call on Parliament to exercise its powers under Section 20 of the CRAG Act 2010 to vote against final ratification of the UK-EU Gibraltar Treaty, remove foreign law enforcement from British territory, and reinstate full frontier border security.
records.further_details: On July 15, 2026, the land border fence was removed and Spanish police were installed inside Gibraltar Airport with entry-veto authority on British soil. We believe handing a foreign state police jurisdiction over a strategic British territory during severe global instability is a grave national security risk. Parliament should vote against final ratification under the CRAG Act 2010, remove foreign police from British soil, and restore complete frontier border security.

records.title: Pay every UK adult £100 on the first of every month
records.description: Introduce a tax-free, triple-locked Citizens’ Payment guaranteeing every UK adult a minimum monthly state payment of £100 on the first of every month, funded by an annual tax on net wealth above £10 million.
records.further_details: Make £100 the universal monthly minimum for every UK adult. Smaller benefits would be replaced by the higher payment, while anyone entitled to more would keep their full support. With no means test or application, it would be simple, hard to exploit and cheaper to administer. It would help people afford essentials, boost spending in local businesses and share some of the gains from AI and automation. Taxing only wealth above £10 million would protect ordinary workers and small businesses.

records.title: Appoint a Government Commissioner for Learning Disabilities
records.description: I would like the government to appoint a Commissioner for Learning Disabilities. Their focus would be on tackling inequalities faced by this under represented group within all aspects of life such as education, work, home, training, health in order to improve quality of life and life expectancy.
records.further_details: Appointing a Government Commissioner for Learning Disabilities would allow for specific government focus on improving the quality and length of lives for those that fall under this category. Although, it would encompass a broad range of areas to cover for responsibility, work in this area could be focused on one area then could gradually progress onto another. Working on preventable health inequalities which exist would make a great difference to their wellbeing.

records.title: Strengthen UK law to prevent unsafe interference with scaffolding and access
records.description: Amend the Work at Height Regulations 2005 to introduce specific legal controls for unauthorised interference with installed scaffolding, a mandatory visible inspection-status system, and competent-person requirements for the installation, removal, relocation and alteration of scaffold ladder access.
records.further_details: Scaffolds can become unsafe after inspection through interference. We ask Government to: 1) prohibit unauthorised scaffold alteration by users and other trades, with interference reported and affected areas stopped pending assessment; 2) require a visible standardised SAFE TO USE/DO NOT USE inspection status; and 3) require competent installation, removal or alteration of scaffold ladders, with safer access controls considered.

records.title: Create a new visa route for elderly, dependent parents of British citizens
records.description: Introduce a simplified, compassionate visa route allowing elderly, dependent parents of British citizens, specifically parents suffering from ill-health and who have no remaining family members in their country of residence, to be able to enter and settle in the UK.
records.further_details: We feel Current Adult Dependent Relative (ADR) rules are nearly impossible to meet. Parents may need long-term care that is entirely unavailable abroad. If a parent is frail, isolated, and struggling to live independently—but not completely incapacitated—they could be barred from joining their child. Paid care cannot replace family support. We feel it is cruel to force aging, lonely parents to live alone when British children can fully house and support them without public funds. We want a new compassionate visa route.

records.title: Intervene to freeze energy bills for the foreseeable future
records.description: We believe the ill, aged, poor, hardworking people of Britain cannot withstand any more energy increases. We are demanding a total freeze on energy bills. We believe Ofgem have been ineffective in easing the cost of living and we note the vast profits earned by energy companies. Freeze bills now.
records.further_details: We feel we are suffering at the hands of our own government's policies and are tired of the same excuse of blaming wars for our current woes. In our view, there were no wars that initially led to the spiralling cost of energy, but rather it was the government's decision to stop Russian gas, Net Zero Energy policies and what we see as the destruction of the gas sector that saw fees rocket by the introduction of such things such as the green levies and shipping in offshore energy. We are concerned this has made energy unaffordable for many.

records.title: End Prime Ministers’ power to nominate resignation honours and peerages
records.description: End the convention allowing departing Prime Ministers to nominate resignation honours and life peerages. Replace it with a transparent, fully independent process based on demonstrated public service, not loyalty or proximity to a political leader.
records.further_details: Resignation lists allow departing Prime Ministers to recommend advisers, political colleagues and associates for honours and life peerages, regardless of how briefly they served. Even when recipients are deserving, this creates an appearance of personal or political patronage. Life peerages ordinarily confer membership of Parliament and influence over legislation, potentially for life. Honours and parliamentary membership should reflect public service, not loyalty or political proximity.

records.title: Review support for single parents to reduce poverty and costly childcare
records.description: Parliament must address the growing pressures on single parents, who are often forced to work yet can struggle to afford childcare or basic needs. Limited support can risk child development and deepen poverty, highlighting the urgent need to review financial and childcare schemes and expand access.
records.further_details: Parliament should review systems of support for single parents, assessing levels of financial aid and affordable childcare. It should investigate expanding access to subsidised childminders, flexible working rights, and increased benefits. These could ease pressure on parents forced to work. Strengthening community support services and ensuring stable income assistance would help reduce poverty and support children’s development and wellbeing.

records.title: Extend pet keeping rights to social housing tenants
records.description: Extend the Renters' Rights Act 2026 to social housing tenants, giving them the same right to keep pets as private renters. Prohibit councils from forcing owners to surrender or foster bonded pets.
records.further_details: Studies have found that cats and dogs can form attachment bonds with owners similar to those between a parent and child. Forcing separation can cause measurable psychological harm to both owner and animal, and physical harm where stress-related illness exists. The Renters' Rights Act 2026 banned pet bans in private rentals but excluded social housing, leaving the most vulnerable people with the least protection.

records.title: Require all alcohol in shops to be stored in a closed cabinet, like cigarettes
records.description: I think alcohol should be treated in the same way cigarettes are and be kept in an area of all shops that can be covered up with shutters. Alcohol is one of Britain's biggest killers and can cost the NHS millions. I believe alcoholics struggle to stay sober as it is in their face wherever they go.
records.further_details: Many experience addiction and the struggles to get clean can be phenomenal. For example, whilst it is illegal to purchase drugs, you can buy cigarettes and alcohol over the counter. I believe alcohol is one of the most dangerous substances and should be a class A drug. We can access this in shops, but it’s highly addictive and people that are in recovery suffer from it being so public, which can make relapse more common.

records.title: Ban the public display of drug paraphernalia in shop windows
records.description: We want the Government to prohibit retailers from displaying drug paraphernalia, including bongs, drug pipes, and similar items, in street-facing shop windows and other publicly visible displays.
records.further_details: We believe the public display of drug paraphernalia normalises drug use and exposes children and young people to products associated with illegal drugs. While some of these items may be legal to sell, we think they should not be openly advertised or promoted in public-facing displays. We believe restricting their display would help create a healthier public environment while still allowing retailers to sell legal products within their premises, subject to existing laws.

records.title: Allow Universal Credit claimants to keep house-purchase savings above £6,000
records.description: We want the Government to exempt house deposit savings from Universal Credit capital limits.Current rules reduce benefits above £6,000 in savings and usually stop entitlement above £16,000 We believe people should be able to save towards buying a home without losing support helping more to buy house
records.further_details: Universal Credit is reduced when a claimant has savings above £6,000 and usually ends when savings reach £16,000.This can make it difficult for people on low income to save for a house deposit,even when they are trying to become financially independent.We believe savings that are clearly set aside for purchasing a home should be disregarded when calculating Universal Credit entitlement,subject to suitable checks and evidence requirements.This would encourage responsible saving and home ownership

records.title: Call a Citizens’ Assembly to consider Stewardship Democracy for the age of AI
records.description: Call a Citizens’ Assembly to examine whether our current democratic system should be complemented or replaced by participatory democracy such as Stewardship Democracy, in order to minimise risks arising from advanced AI whose capabilities may soon profoundly affect democratic decision-making.
records.further_details: To help prevent unprecedented social disarray, we believe our system of governance should be urgently reviewed. We feel this is especially important as public trust in politics declines and political polarisation increases. We therefore ask Parliament to establish a Citizens’ Assembly to examine the introduction of models of participatory democracy such as Stewardship Democracy, to strengthen democratic legitimacy while minimising disruption to existing constitutional and judicial institutions.

records.title: Seek to negotiate a freedom of movement agreement with the US Government
records.description: We urge the UK Government to seek to negotiate an agreement with the US Government that allows UK and US citizens to live, work, study and retire in both countries with minimal barriers. This could boost economic growth, innovation, trade & skills exchange, and strengthen the Special Relationship.
records.further_details:
It could boost economic growth by enabling workers to move to where their skills are most needed. Enhanced labour mobility could also increase productivity, innovation, bilateral trade, and investment.
 
Young people could gain easier access to international experiences and education, fostering long-term collaboration in research and entrepreneurship.
We believe this is a bold, positive post-Brexit opportunity: it deepens our closest ally and expands opportunities for British citizens.

records.title: Ban the import of dogs into the UK from areas where Brucella Canis is endemic
records.description: Brucella Canis is an emerging zoonotic disease introduced into the UK by the unregulated import of dogs for rehoming. Those most at risk are people working within the veterinary industry and associated professions.
records.further_details: Brucella Canis is a zoonotic disease that can pass from dogs to people. It is a hard disease to diagnose as many dogs don’t show signs of illness. When infected people can suffer a variety of signs. There is some evidence that fertility can be affected and if latently infected it could prevent people from having appropriate chemotherapy should they get cancer.

records.title: Give police emergency powers to return children withheld by a parent
records.description: We call on the Government to amend the law to grant police immediate emergency powers to recover a child when a parent withholds them in breach of an active Court Order or shared care agreement.
records.further_details: Currently, when a parent breaks a family court order and refuses to return a child, the police often refuse to intervene, calling it a "civil matter". Parents are forced to wait months for new court hearings while their children are alienated and legal orders are ignored with impunity. The law has a dangerous gap. We need emergency police enforcement powers to protect children and uphold court decisions immediately, instead of allowing parents to break the law while waiting for future court.

records.title: Require all horse breeders to be licensed
records.description: Introduce legislation requiring anyone who breeds, or allows a mare to be bred, in England to hold a local-authority licence. Licensing should apply from the first breeding event and set enforceable welfare standards for mares, stallions and foals, including housing, handling and veterinary care.
records.further_details: Horse breeding can expose mares, stallions and foals to serious welfare risks, yet breeders are not specifically licensed. Licensing should apply from the first deliberate breeding event, regardless of profit or scale. It should require suitable facilities, competent handling, veterinary and breeding records, emergency plans, responsible planning for every foal, and safeguards against breeding from horses with known serious hereditary conditions.

records.title: Accelerate renewable energy adoption with increased investment
records.description: Increase investment in UK renewable energy infrastructure. Increase the number and accessibility of grants and incentives for households to adopt solar, heat pumps, and other low carbon technologies. Strengthen regulation of industrial emissions and accelerate the transition away from fossil fuels.
records.further_details: The UK is facing record heatwaves, flooding and unstable weather. This is becoming the new normal and threatens the future we leave our children. We call on the Government to urgently cut emissions, expand renewable energy, support households to adopt low carbon technology, and invest in climate adaptation to protect communities from extreme weather.

records.title: Replace fines for water companies with transfers of shares to public ownership
records.description: Fines of water companies by Ofwat have proven to be ineffective; they are ultimately paid for by higher bills for consumers. Neither the behaviour of these companies or their performance has improved. Instead companies should be compelled to transfer the same value of shares into public ownership.
records.further_details: By swapping fines for share transfers, water companies would not be able to 'pay' for their transgressions at the expense of their users. Increased public ownership would provide far more leverage to influence the behaviour of these companies (decisions on dividend payments, bonuses for company executives and infrastructure spending programs, etc). Companies (e.g. Thames Water) that are demonstrably unable to deliver the public service they exist to meet could ultimately become renationalised.

records.title: Support UK innovation & reform copyright law to curb tech giants
records.description: We believe the anti-circumvention rules and digital locks brought in by the UK’s 2003 Copyright and Related Rights Regulations have enabled powerful tech monopolies to grow, stifled UK innovation, blocked the right to repair, and slowed development of a circular economy for e-devices.
records.further_details:
Parliament should reform this law.

We believe that reviewing this legislation could allow more opportunities for UK tech development. Such a review should consider the licensing models of software companies and the effect they have on consumers and the longevity of electrical products. Changes could for example allow farmers to fix their own tractors without paying thousands for a code to unlock the software, and a renewed approach to longevity of products could extend product lifespans to reduce the mining of critical raw materials. We call on Parliament to act.

records.title: Introduce rules to stop online platforms requiring children to scan their faces
records.description: We ask the UK Government to introduce rules preventing popular online platforms geared towards children from requiring facial scans or facial data for access to core services.
records.further_details: Some platforms popular with children, such as gaming platforms, have introduced facial age checks using third-party software. Many parents are concerned about their children’s faces being scanned and how that data is handled. We also request that the government investigate other apps that use these systems.

records.title: Appoint a Guardian ad Litem for every child under 18 at first point of arrest
records.description: Introduce legislation requiring the mandatory appointment of an independent Guardian ad Litem for every child under 18 at the point of arrest, before any interview or formal process begins.
records.further_details: Children are arrested daily without a single independent adult whose legal duty is to protect them. Over 4.6 million children grow up in homes shaped by poverty and abuse. Many are groomed into county lines and exploitation. At arrest they face the most critical moment of their lives alone. An Appropriate Adult is procedural. A duty solicitor protects legal rights. Neither acts solely for the child. The Guardian ad Litem exists in Family Court. It must now extend to the point of arrest.

records.title: Review funding for social prescribing to tackle the UK's loneliness epidemic
records.description: Loneliness affects millions across the UK. 3.1 million adults feel lonely often or always, costing the NHS an estimated £850 per person each year, around £2.6bn in total, and linked to a 29% higher risk of coronary heart disease and a 32% higher risk of stroke.
records.further_details: Social prescribing connects people to community activities and support, alongside medical care, to improve health and wellbeing. A two-year government pilot referred over 8,500 people to nature-based activities, achieving an 85% uptake rate and delivering £2.42 of social value for every £1 invested. Yet we believe provision remains patchy and underfunded. We ask the Government to review funding for social prescribing, including a 10-year £1bn Shared Investment Fund across all 42 Integrated Care Systems, as proposed by NASP, so people can access meaningful human connection before reaching a crisis point.

records.title: Human Oversight and Safeguards Use of AI for Asylum,  Vulnerability Seekers
records.description:
•  No AI as the sole decision-maker for asylum, disability or vulnerability cases
•  Mandatory human review for all AI-assisted decisions
•  Clear explanations for affected individuals
•  Strong safeguards for disabled people and those with mental health conditions
Fairness and human judgment
records.further_details:
We want to stop the UK Government from using Artificial Intelligence as the main or only decision-maker in asylum claims, disability assessments, and vulnerability decisions for people with mental health conditions.
AI can be unfair, biased, or inaccurate. We demand mandatory human review, clear explanations, and strong protections for vulnerable people. Human judgment must remain central.

records.title: Abolish IPSA and set MP salaries to 160% of the 'National Living Wage'.
records.description: We want the government to abolish The Independent Parliamentary Standards Authority pay settlement function and set MP pay at 160% of the 'National Living Wage'.
records.further_details: We feel that Politicians have too many privileges currently and we think this will make them a little more sensitive to poverty in Britain.

records.title: Strengthen right to repair legislation by including motor vehicles
records.description: We want the Government to prevent car manufacturers from creating or removing features to hinder the ability to maintain a vehicle, as well as to ensure that they continue to produce parts for their most popular models dependant on how many are left on the road.
records.further_details: This petition asks for legislation to prevent car brands from adding or removing features to hinder the ability to maintain a vehicle such as some current examples like the removal of sump plugs on some cars, and screws only the dealership can undo on others. This should include the having to access the car's software for repair purposes. In addition the petition asks that cars regardless of age, as long as there is (example number) 100 cars left on UK roads, the manufacturer must continue to make parts for it.

records.title: 'Right to know' disclosure scheme for repeat romance fraudsters
records.description: We call on the government to introduce a disclosure scheme, similar to Clare's Law, allowing individuals to ask the police if a romantic partner has previous convictions for fraud, theft or financial exploitation. Serial romance fraudsters inflict devastating financial and emotional ruin.
records.further_details: Serial romance fraudsters routinely target multiple victims, using deception to inflict devastating financial and emotional ruin. Currently Clare's Law covers domestic abuse and economic control but pure fraud convictions remain hidden from new partners. This means victims who suspect a partner is a convicted scammer cannot get information from the police. Introducing a 'RIGHT TO ASK' for a financial fraud convictions will protect people and stop scammers finding new victims.

records.title: Equal access to all for Student Loans regardless of family income
records.description: Make the Student Maintenance Loan standardised to all students rather than allocating it on the basis of household income on the assumption that our parents can afford to pay for university fees.
records.further_details: We believe education should not come at the price of impoverishment of one’s family. Some areas have a higher or lower cost of living. Some families have more heads to account for, or more debts, or extraneous circumstances that mean that they cannot spent the extra money for food/living costs for one person for university.

records.title: Deploy UK forces to Sudan to help end the crisis
records.description: Innocent people in Sudan are being tortured, murdered, & forced from their homes. Peace talks have failed to stop atrocities. We call on the UK Government to deploy British Armed Forces to Sudan on a peacekeeping mission to protect civilians, save lives, & help restore peace and stability.
records.further_details: People in Sudan are enduring unimaginable trauma, with reports showing atrocities against innocent people, including children, who are being subjected to rape, torture, and murder. We believe the UK has the capability to help. Peace talks alone have not worked quickly enough to save lives. We call on the UK Government to deploy British Army personnel for a peacekeeping mission to protect civilians and help bring peace to Sudan.

records.title: Review BMI limits for NHS breast reduction surgery
