records.description: We call on the Government to commission an independent clinical review into BMI thresholds for NHS breast reduction surgery, ensuring criteria account for tissue weight, chronic pain, and modern safety guidelines.
records.further_details: We believe access to NHS breast reduction is currently an unfair postcode lottery. Local Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) set widely different rules, with some enforcing strict BMI cut-offs as low as 27. This rigid metric can completely ignore the actual physical weight of dense breast tissue, which directly inflates a patient’s BMI on the scale. Denying treatment based solely on BMI can force patients to live with debilitating, chronic back, neck, and shoulder pain. This pain causes long-term health issues.

records.title: Stop ICB Funding Caps on Right to Choose access for Autism & ADHD Assessments
records.description: We ask the Government to stop Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) from imposing funding caps on Right to Choose providers until an immediate, actionable plan with strict, legally binding timescales is implemented to eliminate the assessment backlog.
records.further_details:
Funding caps mean providers will have to cut services once limits are reached, potentially leading to years-long waits and fewer assessment options. Without an immediately actionable plan, this can leave vulnerable young people and adults in a state of uncertainty, delaying diagnoses and access to support.

Right to Choose was created to ensure fair, timely access to care. We believe that delaying this pathway does not speed up other NHS pathways for autism and ADHD diagnosis, but adds pressure to an already overloaded system.

records.title: Urgently make Cuckooing a specific offence and increase penalties
records.description: We need government action, I’m aware the government is criminalising it through the Crime and Policing Bill but it needs to be passed and then implemented urgently. It also needs to be discussed more openly to make people aware of the signs of exploitation and Cuckooing.
records.further_details: This been debated since 2025. The part on cuckooing won't be law until ministers commence it. Cuckooing victims are vulnerable people who are exploited by drug dealers. We feel this Act does not do enough to punish these criminals. We believe 5 years in prison for criminals is not worth the mental and physical toll cuckooing has on the victim, it is an awful injustice and needs to be spoken about more because the victim is often forced into horrible living conditions in their own home.

records.title: Car Insurance Coverage to Be Vehicle-Based, Not Driver-Based
records.description: Change insurance laws so that cars themselves are insured rather than each driver on each car.
records.further_details: We think this will make it far easier to get car insurance, and could save hundreds if not thousands of pounds for drivers other than the registered owner who want insurance on a car they don't own.

records.title: Advocate confiscation & dismantling of any undisclosed Israeli nuclear weapons
records.description: We call on the UK Government to support in the confiscation and dismantling of any undisclosed Israeli nuclear weapons. The UK Government should drive this effort through the United Nations to ensure that no state operates outside of international nuclear regulations.
records.further_details: The UK should lead the effort to support nuclear non-proliferation consistently. Undeclared nuclear weapons risk undermining global security and trust in international relations. By raising this issue through the United Nations, the UK could drive efforts to promote transparency and equal enforcement of nuclear regulations in order to strengthen global security and help reduce the risk of conflict.

records.title: Introduce statutory standardised simplified energy tariffs & automatic renewals
records.description: We call on the Government to legislate for a standardised simplified tariff offer which each supplier put forward to their customers, and making renewals automatic to the supplier’s cheapest equivalent deal (with easy opt-out), and standardising bills to clearly show the total yearly cost.
records.further_details: We believe that the energy market confuses millions of households. Complex tariffs, standing charges, and renewal deals make bills hard to understand and comparisons difficult. We think this leads to many people overpaying by staying on expensive default tariffs. In our view, requiring the system to be simpler with fewer tariffs, automatic renewals to the cheapest equivalent (easy opt-out), and clear annual cost displays on bills would reduce confusion, prevent bill shocks, increase competition, and help everyone manage costs better.

records.title: Fund optional gynaecological health consultations for girls aged 11-16
records.description: Fund and offer all girls in state and independent secondary schools in England: a pelvic ultrasound at start and end of secondary school (age 11–12 and 15–16), screening for endometriosis, PCOS (PMOS) and uterine fibroids, plus a confidential gynaecological specialist consultation.
records.further_details: Endometriosis, PCOS (PMOS), and fibroids affect millions of UK women. Endometriosis takes on average 9 years to diagnose and 39% of women visited their GP 10+ times before being taken seriously. There is peer-reviewed research that suggests endometriosis exhibits all 8 hallmarks of cancer, yet receives none of its screening urgency. A study suggests that women with endometriosis are 4x more likely to develop ovarian cancer. Undetected, these conditions can cause infertility, organ damage, and cost the UK £8.2 billion annually. Early detection starts at puberty.

records.title: Require mobile networks to explicitly state expiration dates on saved voicemails
records.description: Mandate that UK mobile network providers explicitly state and notify customers of the exact deletion date whenever a customer saves a voicemail, either through an automated voice prompt or SMS alert at the point of saving.
records.further_details: Telecom companies delete saved voicemails after a short period without what we believe to be sufficient transparency. This leads to irreversible loss, such as final messages from deceased loved ones. Many users may naturally assume that selecting "save" secures a file indefinitely. We believe requiring network operators to clearly communicate expiration limits—via an automated voice prompt or an SMS alert at the point of saving—will help ensure transparency, support vulnerable customers, and help prevent further emotional distress during bereavement.

records.title: Legally binding deadlines to fit all homes with solar upgrades + refits
records.description: UK homes pump millions of tonnes of carbon yearly. We demand legally binding deadlines to retrofit all existing housing with solar, batteries, and insulation. We must treat this as an emergency to slash energy bills, end fuel poverty, and secure a zero-carbon future.
records.further_details: The UK’s 29 million homes pump millions of tonnes of carbon into our atmosphere. While many new-build regulations will require solar panels, much of our ageing housing stock remains locked into fossil fuels. We want the Government to treat home energy efficiency as a national climate emergency and accelerate its Warm Homes Plan by setting legally binding annual deadlines to retrofit existing domestic properties with solar, batteries, and insulation. This will help slash carbon, protect families, and end fuel poverty.

records.title: Place location restrictions on vape shops & standardise vape product packaging
records.description: We call on the Government to place restrictions on the location and number of vape shops, as we believe this will improve health and safety of communities. We also call on vape shop signs and vape product packaging to be made plain in line with tobacco products and sellers.
records.further_details:
We believe the following restrictions should be placed on these vape shops:
• No vape shop should operate within 200 metres of residential housing
• No vape shop should operate within 800 metres of 0-18 education spaces such as nurseries, primary or secondary schools
• Vape shops to be exempt from using "skilled worker" visas
• Vape shops signs and vape product packaging to be made plain, similar to how to tobacco products are now

records.title: Mandate accessible public toilets in railway stations and near bus stops
records.description: We call on the Government to make it a legal requirement for all railway stations and bus stops to provide accessible public toilets. No one, especially diabetics, elderly people, or disabled individuals, should be forced to hold it in due to a lack of nearby facilities.
records.further_details: Access to a toilet shouldn't depend on luck, timing, or how far you're willing to walk. For people with diabetes, IBS, pregnancy, disabilities, or age-related conditions, holding it in isn't just uncomfortable; it's painful and even a health risk. Yet many stations and bus stops have zero public toilets. We ask for toilets as standard transport infrastructure, not an afterthought. Everyone deserves dignity, not desperation, on their journey.

records.title: Implement £20,000 fee for ILR or British citizenship
records.description: As a resident of the United Kingdom, I am deeply concerned about the rising costs of social care, health and other public services. One potential solution that I propose is the introduction of a £20,000 fee for individuals who wish to obtain indefinite leave to remain (ILR) or a British passport.
records.further_details: I propose the introduction of a £20,000 fee for individuals who wish to obtain ILR or a British passport. If immigrants want a British passport, which automatically gives them the right to the UK benefit system which in my view is suffering, I’m sure they will pay the £20,000 fee. I don’t think immigrants should automatically be eligible to become British after for example 5 years of residency, and I think getting a British passport or ILR should be a privilege.

records.title: Fund "Recycle-for-Cash" machines at supermarkets
records.description: Littering is a problem but setting up recycling machines where people can recycle for money could help to prevent this. I would like the government to set up the machines in supermarkets because this is where items are bought most.
records.further_details: If these machines are used there may be less littering because the public might rather have a bit of money than litter. This might also help with poverty. A bit of money can make a big difference.

records.title: Give consumers the right to back up physical media they legally own
records.description: Introduce a statutory private-copying exception allowing consumers to back up physical media they legally own for personal preservation. The right must cease if the original is sold, prohibit distribution, and permit narrow DRM bypass for archiving.
records.further_details:
Physical media can become unusable through disc degradation, defects and hardware obsolescence, causing owners to lose access despite reasonable care.

UK law gives computer programs a backup exception, but no equivalent right exists for physical games, films, TV or music.

The Government should introduce a private-copying exception allowing owners to back up physical media for personal use, provided the original is retained, copies aren't shared, and DRM may be bypassed for archival use only.

records.title: Mandatory toxicology reports for every sudden, unexpected or unexplained death
records.description: The Government should mandate toxicology investigations for every sudden, unexpected or unexplained death, including suspected suicides, to ensure consistent, scientific, and reliable investigations. We believe coroners should not have discretion to omit essential evidence.
records.further_details: Sudden deaths must be investigated using full toxicology. We are concerned that current coronial practice is inconsistent, and essential evidence is often missing. Ministry of Justice guidance already recommends toxicology even in suspected suicides, but it is not mandatory. Government should require toxicology in every sudden, unexpected or unexplained death to ensure accurate, scientific and consistent investigations.

records.title: Fund free period products in public toilets in England
records.description: We want the Government to fund free period products in public toilets in England.
records.further_details: Periods are not a choice. Period products are not a luxury they are essential to female life. Women already have to deal with a pay gap - we should not have to pay for a natural monthly occurrence.

records.title: Do not treat student maintenance loans as unearned income for universal credit
records.description: We believe maintenance loan payments for students should not affect universal credit at £1 for every £1. Other personal loans do not affect UC. Also if you work your UC is reduced by only 55p for every £1 earned, and we don’t know why this isn’t the case for maintenance loans.
records.further_details: We want such loans to be disregarded completely in UC calculations. The students entitled to UC are mainly mature students going back to studying and have a family and children. We feel that the government is penalising mature adults wanting to study later in life. Instead of helping struggling students the government is making it more difficult. Mature students are wanting to build a career and working life for themselves instead of relying on benefits but we believe UC rules make it impossible for people to do this. Government should help people get in to work and study.

records.title: Change distance units in road transport from miles to kilometres
records.description: We want the Government to change distance units from imperial (yards and miles) to metric (metres and kilometres), because we think using two different sets of units is more work in the long run, and metric distances are easier to work with.
records.further_details: The vast majority of the rest of the world use the metric system

records.title: Stop letting agents charging landlords to forward the free RRA Information Sheet
records.description: Amend Schedule 6, Para 7(3) of the Renters' Rights Act 2025 to let landlords serve the Information Sheet themselves and satisfy the duty for both parties. Update GOV.UK guidance to clarify where an agent serves it, this is part of their existing management duties, not a separate chargeable service.
records.further_details:
The RRA Information Sheet is a free 4-page government PDF landlords must give tenants by 31 May 2026. No tenancy agreement needs to change. Yet some agents charge landlords £100-200+ per tenancy to forward it, sometimes calling it an "addendum" when none is required.
 
Schedule 6, Para 7(3) creates a duplicate duty: agents must also serve the sheet, even if the landlord already has. We believe this lets agents charge for a task taking minutes, and these costs then reach tenants via higher rents — defeating the Act's aim.

records.title: Make it a criminal offence to take direct pictures of other people’s children
records.description: It shouldn’t matter if it’s in a shopping centre in a park or on the bus please make it a criminal offence to take direct pictures of other people’s children without consent.
records.further_details: If they are standing in a public place, anyone can have the right to take the pictures of your children, even in your own back garden. We think it’s disgusting and it’s wrong and could help to protect predators. Let's start protecting every child instead.

records.title: Require all motorways and roads to be lit
records.description: Require Highways Authorities to ensure that all Motorways and Highways are lit. Review current standards to ensure installed lighting is adequate.
records.further_details: For utmost safety of all drivers on roads.

records.title: Allow Category D licence to drive private motorhomes over 3.5 tonnes
records.description: We think licence holders of a full UK Category D driving licence should be able to drive privately owned motorhomes exceeding 3.5 tonnes without requiring separate Category C1/C entitlement, subject to standard medical requirements.
records.further_details: In our view category D drivers have often already demonstrated the competence required to operate large vehicles safely on public roads, for example many buses and coaches exceed the size and weight of private motorhomes. We believe existing licence rules should better reflect proven driving competence and remove unnecessary duplication of testing for private motorhome use.

records.title: Fund Port-a-Cath training for nurses across hospital departments
records.description: Provide funding to ensure every hospital department has nurses trained to use Port-a-Caths. Patients may receive these devices because years of treatment can damage their veins. No patient should face delays, repeated cannulation attempts or avoidable complications due to a lack of staff training.
records.further_details: As a person with Cystic Fibrosis, I recently attended A&E and was later admitted to a hospital ward. Despite having a Port-a-Cath inserted due to years of treatment damaging my veins, staff were unable to use it because they lacked the necessary training. A peripheral cannula was used instead, which failed during treatment, causing swelling, bruising and pain in my arm. Better Port-a-Cath training could help prevent delays, complications and unnecessary trauma for patients like myself.

records.title: Mandate mental health & disability awareness training for customer-facing jobs
records.description: We believe the Government should introduce a law which requires semi-regular online training courses on how to recognise and appropriately respond to those with mental health needs or disabilities for any job involving face-to-face work with customers, like train stations and pharmacies.
records.further_details:
We believe staff working in these positions, such as train stations, should be trained in what to look out for and how to respond regarding people who may be disabled or have mental health issues.
 
For example, staff should not respond to an autistic person being harassed on the train by moving the victim, rewarding the harasser with their seat, trying to hug the victim, or putting them in an unsafe situation. We believe autistic people are being mistreated too often due to a lack of basic understanding.

records.title: Require every baby changing room to have a toilet for the parent
records.description: I want it to be mandatory that every baby changing room should have a toilet. If you are out on your own, with your baby, and you need the toilet, there is usually nowhere to go. You can’t leave your baby and use the women’s/men’s toilet, and 80% of baby changing rooms I’ve used don’t have a toilet.
records.further_details: I believe having a toilet in a baby changing room would also help families. As a mother who has had a baby and a small toddler, it’s impossible to take your baby in the pram, or carry them into a toilet cubicle to help your toilet trained toddler. I want to be able to use the toilet, knowing that baby is safely in their pram, within my sight. “Family changing rooms” should include a nappy changing station, a toilet and a sink, meaning that every member of the family can go to the toilet safely.

records.title: Increase Compensation for Jury Service to National Minimum Wage Requirements
records.description: Compensation for lost earnings in jury service is a maximum of £65 per day which does not match minimum wage requirements. We believe such compensation must be raised to national minimum wage levels as the current system causes great financial hardship to jurors through no fault of their own.
records.further_details: We feel that citizens are forced into jury service under the draconian threat of criminal fines if they do not comply. For many, this can mean forfeiting a minimum of 2 weeks wages. We believe the fact that jurors receive so little compensation despite the increasing living costs as well as potential travel and childcare costs is unfair and untenable. Furthermore, we think that loss of earnings may cause jurors to feel resentment towards the accused, thereby negatively impacting the right to a fair and impartial jury of their peers.

records.title: Require same-day refunds for failed grocery and essential goods orders
records.description: Require retailers to provide a same-day refund, payment reversal, or equivalent same-day credit when they fail to supply groceries or other essential goods after taking payment.
records.further_details: When grocery or essential goods orders fail, refunds can take 3-5 working days. For low-income families, this can cause immediate hardship, including being unable to buy replacement food or essentials, even though the failure was caused by the retailer. The law should ensure customers are not left without money for essentials while waiting for refunds.

records.title: Require convicted sex offenders to disclose their criminal history to partners
records.description: Introduce a new law that requires all convicted sexual offenders to disclose their conviction to any partners prior to physical intimacy. We believe consent must be well-informed and this is a pivotal piece of information regarding whether consent would still be given.
records.further_details:
If your sexual partner has been previously convicted of rape or other sexual offences, we feel this is a hugely pivotal piece of information in regard to whether a partner would still be willing to consent to sexual activity with said person.
 
Finding out that a person you have been intimate with has a history of rape/sexual assault could be traumatic and cause feelings of violation, especially if you yourself have previously been a victim of rape or sexual assault.

records.title: Set up a cross-sector framework to deliver national food and farming education
records.description: We call on the Government to use its work in response to the 2025 Curriculum and Assessment Review to establish a cross-sector delivery framework that links commercial food supply chains to the classroom & strengthens workforce pipelines for Critical National Infrastructure.
records.further_details: We believe our country needs a joined-up approach to food, farming and education. By using its work in response to the Curriculum and Assessment Review to establish a mandatory cross-sector framework, Government should connect schools, farmers and food supply chains, remove barriers to participation, build future workforce pipelines, strengthen food security and enable industry's existing investment in farming to deliver measurable public value through education.

records.title: Increase Statutory Sick Pay to match minimum wage
records.description: I want the Government to make Statutory Sick Pay equivalent to the minimum wage. I feel the current weekly rate is too low and it's unfair to expect people to be able to live on that amount. I'm concerned that employees who do not get company sick pay are going into debt.
records.further_details: Many employees don't take time off sick unless it is absolutely necessary. Some people who are genuinely sick (and cannot take company sick pay) are being forced to live on less than the minimum wage.

records.title: Require inheritance tax to be paid after probate is granted & equalise interest
records.description: Change the requirement to pay inheritance tax from before probate is granted to after probate has been granted to enable all types of assets to be used to raise the tax due. We want this requirement to apply to any similar tax that may replace inheritance tax in the future.
records.further_details:
Inheritance tax is normally paid before probate is granted, but most assets cannot be accessed until probate has been granted. We believe this causes unnecessary stress at a difficult time. With ever-increasing house prices and pensions being included in the value of a person’s estate in April 2027, more people may be caught in the Inheritance Tax web and face this problem.

We want the Government to equalise interest on unpaid and overpaid tax.  6 months after death, unpaid inheritance tax is subject to a 7.75% interest rate, yet there is only a 2.75% interest rate when refunding overpayments.

records.title: Ban or Cap Administration fees
records.description: We believe companies are exploiting administration fees, and have been doing so for years. Why should we pay extortionate admin fees for a letter? Or a process done yourself online or an AI bot has processed? We want fees to be capped or banned as many companies use them to make bigger profits.
records.further_details:
Does it really cost £30 for a bank letter, or £20 to process an online insurance claim? Why pay £7 admin fee for something AI has processed instantly online?
This petition is to try and get companies capped or banned for charging admin fees unnecessarily to make more profit, especially when things are processed automatically online without any human intervention from the company.

records.title: Ban ALL outdoor fire ignitions under extreme heatwave conditions
records.description: When environmental conditions across the UK warrant hosepipe bans, they may also warrant ignition bans. With extreme heat and dry fuels elevating wildfire risk, restricting avoidable human ignition sources - the leading cause of wildfires globally - is a logical step in wildfire prevention.
records.further_details: Wildfire conditions are worsening across the UK. High temperatures, low rainfall, and increasingly dry, combustible fuels are creating growing risks to rural and urban communities. With human activity the leading cause of wildfire ignitions globally, wildfire experts are calling for restrictions on outdoor ignition sources during high-risk periods, including cigarettes, disposable BBQs and bonfires.

records.title: Remove living rooms from overcrowding standards in Housing Act 1985
records.description: We call on the Government to amend Part X of the Housing Act 1985 to state that a household’s living room cannot be legally counted as a bedroom space when calculating overcrowding space standards.
records.further_details:
We believe the current statutory overcrowding standard is 40 years old and broken. We feel it allows landlords to count a family’s only living room as a bedroom on paper to bypass overcrowding thresholds. This can force vulnerable and non-vulnerable families living in social housing to lose their only communal area.

No modern family should be trapped in bedrooms day and night with nowhere to eat, relax, or spend time together. We want the law to be modernised to protect all families facing this.

records.title: Review legal safeguards for people and businesses affected by debanking
records.description: We want the Government to review legal safeguards for people and businesses affected by debanking, including whether there is fair review, transparency where lawful, and meaningful routes of challenge.
records.further_details: Debanking can leave individuals and lawful businesses unable to access money, pay staff or suppliers, meet essential costs, or continue trading. Financial institutions must be able to prevent fraud, money laundering and sanctions breaches, but restrictions should be proportionate, regularly reviewed and subject to meaningful challenge. We want clearer safeguards, greater accountability and a fair route to resolve cases where access to banking or funds is restricted or removed.

records.title: Review provision of fertility advice offered around an endometriosis diagnosis
records.description: We want the Government to establish an independent review to ensure that comprehensive advice is offered consistently on how endometriosis can affect fertility. I believe people diagnosed with endometriosis who want children in the future should be offered personal fertility advice.
records.further_details: Endometriosis can affect fertility, but its impact varies between individuals. I believe people who want children in the future should not have to wait until they think about trying to conceive or experience difficulties conceiving before discussing their fertility. Earlier, personalised information about their fertility, even before they have been formally diagnosed, and including how their individual condition may affect their fertility and what reproductive options may be available, could help them make informed decisions about their future. Full and consistent advice about this should be available as part of endometriosis care, recognising the impact and stress a diagnosis can have on future fertility.

records.title: Ban the manufacturing of single-use plastic bottles
records.description: Plastic bottles are extremely harmful to our environment. Around 80% of marine litter is plastic. I am calling for a ban of plastic bottles to be replaced with recyclable materials such as glass or bio-plastic.
records.further_details: Plastic bottles can affect marine wildlife, who ingest microplastics, which can then enter the human food chain. We have bio degradable options available to us, so why are we not using them? Switching to reusable bottles could save an average UK citizen approximately 94.4KG of co2 per year. This needs to be a priority.

records.title: Increase NHS funding to prevent recruitment freezes or roles being cut
records.description: We call on the Government to increase funding to all NHS trusts to ensure they do not have to impose recruitment freezes and roles being cut. We believe a lack of funding of NHS trusts negatively impact patients, nurses and other health professionals.
records.further_details: We are concerned that newly qualified and experienced staff who are ready to work are not being recruited due to budget constraints, and that this is putting further pressure on an already stretched workforce. In our view, recruitment is essential to ensure adequate patient care, staff wellbeing and the long-term sustainability of the NHS. We therefore call on the Government to increase funding to NHS trusts.

records.title: Income tax relief for chronically ill people to access private treatment
records.description: Many people with chronic conditions pay for private treatments, diagnostics, therapies, prescriptions, and vital equipment out of pocket. We feel that chronically ill individuals are taxed twice: on earnings and to survive. We call for income tax deductions to offset these unfair costs.
records.further_details: We are concerned that delays in NHS care forces individuals with chronic conditions to self-fund their own medical procedures, diagnostics, prescriptions, therapies, and essential equipment. We believe that stringent state eligibility rules and record waiting lists leave patients with no choice but to pay privately just to live a dignified life. We call for income tax deductions to offset these costs.

records.title: Introduce a mandatory annual review mechanism for HMRC mileage allowance rates
records.description: Introduce an annual review mechanism for mileage rates
records.further_details: HMRC’s mileage rate of 45p per mile has remained unchanged since 2011. During this time, motoring costs such as fuel, insurance, maintenance and vehicle prices have changed significantly. There is no requirement for regular review or update of the rate, meaning it can drift out of step with real-world costs. We call on the Government to introduce a mandatory annual review mechanism for HMRC mileage rates, assessed against inflation or motoring cost data.

records.title: Cap service charge on retirement village properties during resale period.
records.description: We urge the government to limit the period that service charges might apply on retirement village properties, based on fees due over a period of time considered reasonable for resale (e.g. 6 months).
records.further_details: While service charges due are recognised as being tied to the deceased’s estate, and not the individual beneficiaries or executors, capping the service charges due over a period (e.g. 6-months, at a value equivalent to when the property was first acquired) would not only encourage the management companies to promote a sale, but also encourage prospective purchasers with the knowledge of a known maximum financial commitment due from the estate (also assisting the probate process).

records.title: Review sentencing guidance for harassment, stalking and threats of violence
records.description: Review sentencing guidelines and punishments for harassment, stalking and threats of violence, include tougher penalties for repeat offenders and breaches of protection orders. Ensure sentencing reflects the impact on victims and provides stronger protections against abuse and intimidation.
records.further_details: Harassment, stalking, threats of violence can cause severe and lasting harm. Victims experience fear, anxiety, trauma and major disruption to daily life, sometimes changing homes, jobs or routines for safety. Many believe current penalties do not reflect the seriousness of these offences, particularly for repeat offenders. This petition calls on the Government to review sentencing, strengthen penalties, enforce breaches of protective orders and ensure courts fully recognise the harm caused.

records.title: Revise Government bullying guidance to better protect victims
records.description: We think that when a child/children have made an allegation of bullying in school, the named bullies should be suspended to allow the victim to continue their learning uninterrupted in peace. The Government's guidance on preventing bullying should reflect this.
records.further_details: We believe that schools often alienate bullying victims and the victim feels that they need to remove themselves from the setting/problem, but their learning suffers. The perpetrator is being rewarded for their bad behaviour and the victim is being victimised. This is wholly unfair and the victims learning is suffering. In so many cases, the victims are the ones who do not fall into the 'In Crowd' or stand out for other reasons that children find them to be an easy target.

records.title: MPs who resign from the HoC should be banned from standing for five years
records.description: Parliament should introduce a bill that bans MPs who resign from standing in any subsequent by-election or general election for 5 years.

records.title: Fund mandatory air conditioning in every council property
records.description: We call on the Government to make air conditioning mandatory for all council homes with full funding. Rising temperatures can pose severe health risks, and upper floors overheat most. Safe cooling should be a basic standard for every social housing tenant.
records.further_details:
Summers are getting hotter. Council homes especially top floor flats can get dangerously warm. This puts older people, disabled people, children and vulnerable residents at risk.
 
We are concerned that overheating is a housing hazard but no rules or funding exist for cooling. We ask the Government to:
- Make cooling or air conditioning required for all council homes
- Start with top floor flats
- Pay all costs so tenants pay nothing
 
We believe cooling is now an essential need, not a luxury!

records.title: Commission a review of racialised and identity-amplified media targeting
records.description: Commission an independent review of UK media and online regulation and introduce statutory safeguards against sustained, disproportionate targeting of individuals where race, ethnicity or another protected characteristic amplifies media and online scrutiny.
records.further_details: Scrutiny of Black and other minoritised people can become amplified by wider debates about their identity and belonging. Public and media scrutiny of individuals can become entangled with debates about race, disability and EDI. Accountability matters, but it must not become disproportionate public hounding. We need safeguards against serious cumulative and identity-amplified targeting.

records.title: Update the curriculum to include more detail about where food comes from
records.description: Require schools to provide detailed, factual and independent education about animal agriculture, teaching children what happens to animals from birth to plate. This must be transparent & evidence-based, without promoting veganism or animal agriculture, so children can form their own informed views.
records.further_details: We believe children should understand where the food they eat comes from. Education should cover different animals and farming systems including intensive, conventional, free-range and organic, following each animal from birth through its living conditions, treatment, routine procedures, separation from offspring, transport, slaughter and processing. It must show typical conditions, not only the best or worst examples, using accurate, independent and evidence based information without promoting either side

records.title: Increase the State Pension and link it to 100% the national average earnings
records.description: Government must allow todays pensioners, and the rest of us on reaching the official retirement age, to share in the nation’s wealth, because our taxes help to build our economy, and our country.
records.further_details:
In 1980 the increase in state pension's link with average earnings was severed and linked to inflation only. We believe the state pension has been allowed to whither on the vine to date. The state pension is now worth around just 27 per cent UK average earnings.

We believe our pensioners have been marginalised and discriminated against by a low state pension, and means tested handouts. This needs to change and the state pension should be equal to the UK average earnings.

records.title: Legalise members of the public listening to Air Traffic Control
records.description: Under the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006, intercepting and listening to ATC radio transmissions is a criminal offence. I want the Government to update the law in line with other countries to make it legal for the public to do so with an airband or radio scanner without any legal consequences.
records.further_details:
Under the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006, it is currently a criminal offence in the UK to listen to Air Traffic Control transmissions without authorisation, even though these signals are unencrypted and broadcasted in the clear.
 
We call on the UK Government to update the law to legalise the public’s right to non-commercial, passive listening to ATC transmissions. Aviation is a major UK industry. Listening to live ATC serves as an educational tool for student pilots, air traffic control trainees, hobbyists and could modernise the UK by supporting student pilots and aviation enthusiasts.

records.title: Fund early state pension access for working age people with terminal cancer
records.description: Allow working-aged individuals, diagnosed with incurable stage four terminal cancer, early access to their full State Pension from the point of diagnosis, regardless of their immediate life-expectancy prognosis.
records.further_details: Many people spend their lives contributing to National Insurance, only to lose financial stability when diagnosed with stage 4 terminal cancer. While many private pensions allow early access under terminal rules, the State Pension does not. We propose immediate policy changes to grant early access verified medically. This could provide dignified financial security to patients who have actively worked and supported the system, ensuring a fair return on what is rightfully theirs.

records.title: Increase Funding and Research for Adenomyosis Diagnosis and Treatment
records.description: Living with adenomyosis can mean constant pain, exhaustion, and not being believed. It took years to get answers and proper help, affecting my daily life, work, and mental health. I have struggled to be taken seriously and to access the care I need. No one should have to suffer like this.
records.further_details: Adenomyosis is widely considered to be misunderstood and underfunded, leaving many suffering without proper diagnosis or care. Many are often dismissed or misdiagnosed for years, causing unnecessary pain and distress. We believe more research is needed to improve understanding, develop better treatments, and ensure earlier diagnosis. Greater awareness could help healthcare professionals take symptoms seriously and provide the support patients deserve.

records.title: Ban vaping inside cars with children under 18
records.description: Ban vaping inside cars with under-18s in order to reduce their exposure to harmful chemicals.
records.further_details: Vaping is already a health concern amongst children, and we believe normalising it by allowing people to vape in very enclosed spaces with children is problematic.

records.title: Fund more initiatives to stop pollution
records.description: We want the Government to provide more funding for dedicated teams to clean more beaches, sea and rivers, plant more trees, encourage more recycling and limit cars in residential areas. We also want them to invest in more clean energy.
records.further_details: So that we can have a better planet, healthier kids, fewer sick people and less disease, better mental health which could save the government money and have happier people.

records.title: Call for review of US military presence on UK territory.
records.description:
Review US military presence on UK sovereign territory.

Recent rhetoric and policy positions raise questions about the US commitment to UK, NATO, its approach to allied co-operation, and potential impact on our economic and strategic interests.
records.further_details:
Review of US military presence on UK territory in light of increasing concerns about consistency and reliability of current leadership. We urge the government to establish clear conditions governing continued presence of US forces, ensure operational transparency, and allow for the suspension or withdrawal of access.

Develop and implement a framework that enables the reduction or removal of US military presence on UK soil if determined that such presence no longer aligns with our interests.

records.title: Government to introduce structured, supervised vocational work in year 9-11
records.description: We want the UK Government to introduce structured, supervised vocational and work experience programmes for students aged 13–16 (Year 9 to Year 11), available both during school holidays and in school time.
records.further_details: We think secondary school students have limited access to structured activities which can lead to boredom, disengagement, and missed opportunities to develop important life skills. We believe work experience programmes could allow students to gain hands-on experience in areas such as construction, hair and beauty, catering, childcare, and other trades, helping them build confidence, responsibility, and practical skills. This should be conducted within safeguarding and child employment laws, with suitable limited working hours.

records.title: Require warning signs at least 500M before speed cameras
records.description: We are calling on the government to make it mandatory for signs to be displayed at least 500 meters before any operational speed camera. We believe this shift would prioritise safety over penalisation, and aid in creating a more transparent system for all road users.
records.further_details: Driving can already be a stressful experience, but the sudden and unannounced appearance of stealth speed cameras can make it even worse. I recently found myself overtaking on a road, ensuring minimal disruption to other drivers and maintaining safety. Suddenly, I received an unexpected fine in the mail because I exceeded the speed limit by a fraction just to overtake safely. We think this is not fair, and I know others have experienced the same.

records.title: Require accessible, SEN-friendly menus in school canteens
records.description: Require all primary and secondary schools to provide SEN-friendly menus. Current menus can be overwhelming, with complex language and unfamiliar choices. Menus should use simple language, visuals, clear allergens, and consistent layouts to reduce stress and support independence.
records.further_details: Many pupils with SEN, including autism and sensory processing difficulties, struggle with current school menus. This can cause anxiety and exclusion at lunchtime. SEN-friendly menus would improve accessibility, confidence, and ensure all pupils can make informed, comfortable food choices.

records.title: Ban graphic anti-abortion images in public spaces
records.description: Introduce laws banning graphic abortion images in public places like streets, near schools, and transport hubs, with enforcement powers for local authorities.
records.further_details: Graphic images are distressing, especially for children and vulnerable people. The public should not be exposed to shocking material in shared spaces. This would balance free expression with public wellbeing.

records.title: CMS to include voluntary redundancy payments in income calculation
records.description: Voluntary redundancy payments are not classified as current income for the purposes of child maintenance, meaning they are not always reflected in a child maintenance calculation. We think this is unfair to the other parent who might be financially impacted.
records.further_details: I would like redundancy payments which have been taken voluntarily to always be included as income for the purpose of child maintenance payment calculations. This is not always the case, but in a voluntary redundancy situation I think this seems unfair. The parent receiving the child maintenance payment may not have had a choice in the paying parent taking the voluntary redundancy, yet it can impact them and the children financially.

records.title: Review laws protecting employees from dismissal for lawful speech outside work
records.description: Review legal framework for protecting staff from dismissal by their employers for lawful speech outside work. A review could establish stricter duties on employers to show clearer and more demonstrable harm to legitimate business interests before a dismissal can take place.
records.further_details: It has been reported that employees have been disciplined or dismissed for opinions expressed in their private lives. We think this creates a chilling effect on free expression. People should be able to hold and express lawful views outside work without fear of losing their job. We think current protections are unclear and inconsistently applied, which can leave employees vulnerable to unfair dismissal.

records.title: Make November 11th a bank holiday
records.description: I want the government to change the 11th of November to a bank holiday for Remembrance Day. This is to remember the soldiers lost in battle in both World War 1 and World War 2.
records.further_details: I want the government to do this because I believe the soldiers deserve a day of remembrance and not just two minutes of silence. Remembrance Day is already a recognised bank holiday in numerous other countries and I think it should also be a bank holiday in England. This day could be used to spread awareness about the soldiers who lost their life protecting us and our future generations.

records.title: Require all secondary teachers to pass the same exams their students sit
records.description: Require all GCSE and A-level teachers to pass the same exams as their students in exam conditions to ensure they have the relevant knowledge in their subject to teach it well and to reduce hypocrisy in the education system.
records.further_details:
I want to make all GCSE and A-level teachers pass the same exams as their students in exam conditions to ensure they have the relevant knowledge in their subject to teach it well and to reduce hypocrisy in the education system.
We believe teachers who do not know their subject well enough to get a good grade in the same exams they expect their students to sit should not be teaching the subject. We think this will ensure all teachers have up to date knowledge of their subjects.

records.title: Fund free access to all swimming pools during a heatwave
records.description: My petition is for the government to require swimming pools to open to all during heatwaves and for the government to fund free access to allow people to swim safely for free to prevent deaths from open water.
records.further_details: We see an increased number of deaths from people swimming in open water (rivers, reservoirs and lakes) during heatwaves. We ask the government to require swimming pools to open to the public during heatwaves to allow them stay cool and swim in a safe environment monitored closely by lifeguards. The Government should fund this. We think this could reduce unnecessary deaths caused by open water and reduce the amount of incidents caused.

records.title: Require local authorities to have a cooling strategy
records.description: We need all local authorities to have a cooling strategy to deal with increasing heat, causing unnecessary deaths from drowning etc. Each Local Authority (LA) must publish its strategy including things like free swimming on heatwave days, and provision of indoor and outdoor cooling facilities.
records.further_details: Each LA must have a cooling strategy to include free provision of cooling facilities accessible to all. Current access to swimming and other cooling activities is based on ability to pay, which could lead to tragic deaths of young people in particular trying to cool down in increasingly hot weather not of their making. Deaths due to drowning could also be published annually by the LA. We believe mechanisms such as free access to local pools on days above a certain temperature and indoor and outdoor cooling spaces must be introduced. We feel annual death reporting by LAs could encourage action.

records.title: Require menus to be available in hard copy
records.description: We are concerned that many people don't have devices to scan QR codes or have sufficient signal especially in rural areas. Some of us are also blind or disabled and can never use a QR code menu. There should always be a physical menu available.
records.further_details: We believe that to have only QR code menus makes society less inclusive for all. It can be confusing not only dietary wise but also QR codes could have malware or expose you to scams

records.title: Fund faster processing of NIHL civil claims against MoD
records.description: We want the Government to help settle NIHL civil claims more quickly. Many veterans have already provided full medical evidence, service records, audiology reports and causation assessments, yet are left waiting months or even years without clear updates or predictable timelines.
records.further_details: These delays can cause financial hardship, uncertainty, and prevent injured veterans from moving forward with their lives. NIHL is a recognised service-related injury, and the MoD has already accepted liability principles for post-1987 service.

records.title: Require schools in England to end the academic year in June
records.description: Require schools in England to match Scotland’s typical late-June finish. This protects students and staff from dangerous July heatwaves caused by climate change, ensuring they aren't trapped in overheated, uncooled classrooms during peak summer, aiming for a safer, climate-resilient school year.
records.further_details: We urge the government to mandate an England-wide academic calendar aligned with Scotland’s model, ending the school year in late June. Climate change has made July heatwaves dangerously intense. Most schools lack air conditioning, leaving pupils and staff trapped in classrooms exceeding 30°C, which harms health and learning. Shifting to a late-June finish protects children from peak summer heat, prevents disruptive emergency closures, and modernises our education system for a warming world.

records.title: Mandate employers where 40%+ jobs cut due to AI to reduce working hours by 20%
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce regulation to safeguard AI's impact on jobs. We think such legislation should require employers in sectors where there has been 40%+ AI-driven job losses to reduce working hours by 20% with no pay cut, protecting workers and sharing AI's benefits fairly.
records.further_details: We think AI's benefits must be shared fairly. We call on the UK Government to regulate AI by requiring employers in sectors with 40%+ job losses to reduce working hours by 20% with no pay cut. Long weekends and free time for all—not just the wealthy. In our view this protects jobs and ensures workers fairly share in AI's economic value.

records.title: Introduce a wide ranging criminal trespass law
records.description: Introduce a new specific criminal trespass law which makes it an offence to be on any private property without consent of their representative. The intent of the law would be to fill what we see as a gap in legislation which allows urban explorers, base jumpers & prospective thieves to walk free.
records.further_details: Current civil trespass laws  mean that when people are found committing trespass they cannot always be dealt with by the police. I have personally witnessed urban explorers, base jumpers, and perspective thieves who have simply denied their intent to commit theft walk away with no further action being taken. A specific vehicular paragraph in the law should also give police powers to remove temporary encampments and vehicle meets.

records.title: Disqualify resigned MPs from standing until 4 years after next General Election
records.description: If a sitting MP chooses to resign their seat for whatever reason, then that MP should be blocked for standing as an MP at the next General Election and for four more years or until the subsequent General Election, whichever is lesser.
records.further_details: We have seen recently that there seems to be this loophole in which elected Members of Parliament can resign their seats and then stand in the same by-election they have triggered at a massive burden to the taxpayer. If any MP resigns their seat, they should be blocked from standing at the next General Election and only be allowed to stand four years after or at the subsequent General Election, whichever is the least amount of time.

records.title: Require parties to repay costs of PM resignations & cabinet reshuffles
records.description: Introduce legislation requiring governing political parties to reimburse the Exchequer for the direct administrative costs of resignation of a PM as party leader, or cabinet reshuffles.
records.further_details: Taxpayers should continue to fund general elections and the resulting transfers of power. However, when a governing political party voluntarily replaces its party leader (the Prime Minister) or reshuffles the Cabinet due to an internal leadership decision, the party should reimburse the Exchequer for the direct administrative costs. This would ensure taxpayers are not solely responsible for the costs of avoidable internal party decisions.

records.title: Amend Access to Neighbouring Land Act 1992 to include green energy installations
records.description: We call on the Government to update the Access to Neighbouring Land Act 1992 so that property owners can gain reasonable, temporary access to neighbouring land, where access cannot reasonably be avoided, to install microgeneration technologies, such as solar panels, on their own property.
records.further_details: The Access to Neighbouring Land Act 1992 allows access for basic property repairs, but classes green retrofits like solar panels as "improvements". As a result, householders have no statutory right to temporary access, such as for essential scaffolding. Uncooperative neighbours can completely block renewable installations. To meet Net Zero goals and lower energy bills, the Government should seek to extend access rights to include green energy upgrades, with fair safeguards for property owners.

records.title: Require a UK referendum before independence referendums or transfer of powers
records.description: I believe the whole country will be affected by any further transfer of powers to parts of the UK. Therefore I feel all voters should be given the chance to vote in a UK-wide referendum so all voices are heard. I believe further devolution of power isn’t legitimate without absolute majority consent
records.further_details: I believe that our national politicians always should seek beyond any doubt to represent us all in everything they pursue for the national benefit. I feel we all have a legitimate interest in any structural change to our nation, and that it remains a great strength that the majority's voice is represented, not just that of a local majority. Therefore, there should be a UK-wide referendum for all citizens to give approval for the further devolution of powers, or even moves for independence, before any decision relating to devolution in the component nations of the UK are agreed upon.

records.title: Introduce a Two-Week Educational Family Holiday Allowance During Term Time
records.description: Allow parents to take children out of school for up to two weeks during term time without fines, using holidays as educational experiences. On return, children could incorporate what they learned into the curriculum, supporting family time, wellbeing and real-world education.
records.further_details: Allow parents to take children out of school for up to two weeks (10 school days) during term time without fines, provided the absence is notified in advance. Holidays can provide valuable learning through different cultures, history, geography, languages and real-world experiences. On return, children could share and incorporate what they learned into suitable curriculum activities. Safeguards could apply for poor attendance and exam periods, balancing education with family time and wellbeing.

records.title: Require visible GMC/GDC/NMC numbers when offering Aesthetics/Cosmetics treatment
records.description: Require anyone calling themselves a healthcare professional while offering aesthetic or cosmetic treatments to display their current GMC, NMC or GDC number next to their name on all advertising and promotions.
records.further_details: I'm a UK-registered doctor. I want aesthetic care to be safer for patients. Too many people book treatments from titles that look official. Having a live GMC, NMC or GDC number next to the name would let patients check before they book. An overseas degree can be real but does not always mean UK registration. We believe this rule would help patients without stopping anyone who is properly registered.

records.title: Mandate higher minimum wage for night shift workers
records.description: We call on the Government to actively increase the rights of night shift workers by instituting a higher minimum wage specifically for those working nights, along with more comprehensive well-being services.
records.further_details: Night shift workers are acutely aware of what we give up for our jobs: our health, our social lives, and our overall well-being. These roles can predispose us to a variety of health complications. Studies have demonstrated a link between night work and increased risks of depression, loneliness, low energy, and even serious cardiovascular problems. The lack of sunlight affects us greatly, both physically and mentally, diminishing our quality of life and making simple social interactions a struggle.

records.title: Make suicide prevention training mandatory for frontline public sector workers
records.description: Suicide remains one of the leading causes of death in the UK, with many having contact with public sector services before they die. Most workers receive no training on suicide and don’t feel confident asking about it or connecting someone to help.
records.further_details:
A person's safety shouldn't be up to luck on whether they happen to come across a trained staff member or not.
 
According to Samaritans, suicide costs the UK £1.5 million per life lost, totalling £9.58 billion in 2022. Providing training to all frontline public-sector workers would cost only a fraction of this, making it both morally and financially beneficial.

records.title: Strengthen child maintenance enforcement powers and increase payment rates
records.description: The Government really needs to strengthen the law relating to the enforcement of child maintenance payments towards the cost of raising a child. Especially SEN children as this comes with additional costs. Also, to re calculate the amounts, as we think the £7 a week flat rate is outdated and poor.
records.further_details: The Child Maintenance Service is supposed to be a solid security/network for enforcing the law on financial contributions/responsibilities towards children. Yet this is often not the case and many families/children are being failed by this service. The law has to change, and the amounts need re calculating. The law on enforcement needs serious attention and change, as do the amounts that are presented as adequate to raise a child - £7 a week as a flat rate amount is not remotely acceptable.

records.title: Ban the use of bots to bulk-buy products & reselling them at inflated prices
records.description: Ban the act of buying limited-supply products via bots and reselling them at inflated prices when people cannot purchase those products any other way, as so-called “scalpers” have bought them all.
records.further_details: I believe to fix this problem and not interfere with people’s rights, there should be a ban, and shops should either limit the amount of stock than can be bought from one account when stock is low or limit the amount of the said product going to the same address.

records.title: Trimethylaminuria (TMAU): Fund research and awareness
records.description: We call on the Government to provide funding to conduct more research for possible treatments of TMAU, and to fund initiatives raising awareness of the condition and of the detrimental effects it can have on those diagnosed. We believe it often isn't recognised as a disability when it should.
records.further_details: This has affected my confidence and my life, and I believe there needs to be more awareness and action. We call on the Government to recognise when it is a disability, and consider how employers can support us, including by offering remote jobs. The mental and physical effects of this disease can be devastating. I am aware of people who say they haven’t been outside for years because of the abuse and some who have who have gone home crying because of the way they have been treated.

records.title: Require all domestic abuse family court cases to include a Fact Finding hearing
records.description: Automatically make all domestic abuse, including coercive control, family court cases include a ‘Fact Finding’ hearing as a statutory procedure when there are allegations of domestic abuse and coercive control.

records.title: Require lasting power of attorney applicants undergo enhanced DBS check
records.description: Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) applicants should have to undergo an enhanced DBS check before the OPG grants them power over an individual. Current LPA's should have these checks done as they haven’t thus far and some may have been putting the Donors in danger.
records.further_details: LPA's are given the power to make decisions for the elderly in every way. From financials to health. We are concerned that some elderly people have their basic rights stripped away by their LPA, their voice taken away and are treated poorly mentally and physically. Some can be isolated from friends and loved ones, abused, coerced into things they don't want to do and some may endure all of it. LPA's to these people hold all the power and some don’t face consequences. Background checks should be mandatory.

records.title: Establish a Strategic Cryptocurrency Reserve from confiscated, forfeited crypto
records.description: We ask HM Treasury to create a Strategic Cryptocurrency Reserve using cryptocurrency, such as Bitcoin, lawfully confiscated, forfeited, or already held by the state, rather than automatically selling it. We think it could strengthen long term fiscal resilience and UK digital competitiveness by 2030.
records.further_details:
The UK Government currently confiscates and sells cryptocurrency such as Bitcoin obtained through criminal seizures and forfeiture.
 
We believe HM Treasury should instead establish a Strategic Cryptocurrency Reserve using lawfully confiscated or state held cryptocurrency, similar to how nations manage strategic assets.
 
Rather than automatically selling cryptocurrency, the UK should assess if retaining a portion in the Bank of England could strengthen long term fiscal resilience, financial innovation, rivalry and national security.

records.title: Make water safety and open water danger education compulsory in all schools
records.description: We want the Government to make water safety education mandatory in secondary as well as primary schools and work for improvements in warning signage at rivers, lakes, reservoir's and beaches.
records.further_details: Every summer children and teenagers drown in open waters. Many do not understand cold-water shock, hidden currents or the dangers of jumping into lakes and rivers. All schools should teach water safety yearly and councils should be made to install clearer emergency and warning signs at all public water areas. We need a summer and water awareness campaign which includes: what to do if a friend/person is drowning, CPR and basic rescue awareness.

records.title: Create national guidance for ‘Slow for Cats’ warning signs in rural communities
records.description: Introduce national guidance for local authorities to install “Slow for Cats” warning signs and related traffic-calming measures in rural and semi-rural areas where there is evidence of frequent domestic cat road deaths.
records.further_details:
Domestic cats are killed or injured on roads in villages and rural areas annually. There is no national system for recording cat road deaths in place.

Cats are not included in road traffic casualty statistics, and there is no requirement for incidents involving pets to be reported. As a result, local authorities lack consistent evidence to identify high-risk areas.

Rural communities have high numbers of free roaming cats, with fast-moving country roads. This can lead to preventable collisions.

records.title: Make NHS healthcare bodies statutory consultees for major housing developments
records.description: Amend planning legislation so relevant NHS healthcare bodies are statutory consultees on major housing developments and Local Plans where development is likely to have a significant impact on healthcare services.
records.further_details:
Major housing developments increase demand on GP practices, hospitals, mental health, community health and ambulance services, yet consultation with NHS organisations is not consistently required before planning decisions are made.

The Government should require local planning authorities to consult relevant NHS bodies on major planning applications and Local Plans, and consider their assessment of healthcare capacity and infrastructure needs before making decisions. This would help ensure healthcare infrastructure is planned alongside housing growth and protect access to NHS services for existing and future residents.

records.title: Abolish the limitation period for any child abuse claims
records.description: I believe the Government should change the law so that a victim of any form of child abuse cannot be denied justice because they were unable to fully disclose abuse within a statutory time frame.
records.further_details:
Children may often delay or limit disclosure due to trauma or fear. In some cases, further allegations may emerge months or years later, but some offences cannot be prosecuted as statutory time limits have expired. I believe this can leave victims without access to justice through no fault of their own. 
 
I want the Government to introduce a new law that removes the statutory time limit on all child abuse cases.

records.title: Taxable income to be assessed on a household basis for single-income families
records.description: We want the Government to assess income on a household basis for single-income families to make their income tax contribution equal to dual-income families.
records.further_details: Currently, income tax is assessed entirely on an individual basis. This means a single-income family earning, for example, £60,000 pays significantly more tax and National Insurance than a couple earning £30,000 each. Despite having the exact same household income to support a family, a household is left with far less take-home pay simply because of how the income is split.

records.title: Introduce minimum staffing requirements for hotel hospitality workers
records.description: Legislate strict minimum staffing laws for hospitality venues. Require a minimum of two staff members during front-of-house or late shifts. Ban employers from unsafely combining reception, security, maintenance, and cafe/bar service duties into a single lone worker's shift.
records.further_details: Legislate mandatory minimum staffing rules for hospitality. Require at least two staff members on front-of-house shifts. Ban employers from forcing lone receptionists to run venues alone, facing abuse and security risks without physical backup. Stop employers from relying on lone-working safety devices that frequently fail in emergencies. Ban unsafely combining roles; workers must not handle check-ins, building maintenance, and cafe/bar food or drink service simultaneously.

records.title: Require councils in England to provide free, accessible public toilets
records.description: We want the Government to introduce legislation requiring councils in England to provide free, clean and accessible public toilets that meet local need, supported by a national minimum standard for availability, accessibility and maintenance.
records.further_details: Councils can provide public toilets, but they are not legally required to do so. This has created inconsistent provision, with some communities having few or no free facilities. Poor access can restrict daily life for older and disabled people, parents with young children, and people with health conditions. Councils should assess local need and provide sufficient free, clean and accessible toilets, supported by government funding.

records.title: Launch a review into investigating gender-based price differences
records.description: We want the Government to launch a review that investigates gender-based price differences (“pink tax”) and recommend measures to prevent businesses charging more for similar products marketed towards women or girls, unless the difference can be reasonably justified by genuine costs.
records.further_details:
The “pink tax” is when products marketed towards women and girls cost more than equivalent products marketed towards men and boys. We believe consumers should not pay more because of gender-based marketing.
 
We want the Government to investigate these price differences, publish its findings and measures it plans to introduce to prevent unjustified higher prices for equivalent or substantially similar products. This could help protect young people and families from unfair costs and promote greater equality.

records.title: Make learning about current affairs a legal requirement for students
records.description: We would like for the Uk Government to make it a legal requirement for students aged 11-18 to have 2 hours of education a term about current political and economic affairs so that they have a better understanding of the world as of right now and how these choices will affect our future.
records.further_details: Politics is changing rapidly and affects our daily lives, often without us realising. We believe education should go beyond exam content and better prepare students for the real world. Many young people rely on outdated classroom material or biased social media, which can create false or harmful views. Schools should teach current political issues from different perspectives, helping students think critically and understand the world around them.

records.title: Create a hardship scheme for vulnerable leaseholders facing major works bills
records.description: Create a statutory means-tested grant scheme for low-income, disabled and vulnerable leaseholders facing unaffordable major works, remediation or exceptional service-charge bills, so qualifying households are not forced into debt, required to sell, or put at risk of losing their homes.
records.further_details: Some leaseholders, including Right to Buy and former social-housing residents, face major works and remediation bills potentially running into tens of thousands of pounds, which they simply cannot afford. Disabled people, carers, pensioners & households on very low incomes may have no savings & little ability to borrow or repay loans. A national means-tested grant scheme could help landlords meet necessary costs while protecting vulnerable residents from debt, forced sale or losing their homes.

records.title: Ban Members of Parliament from holding shares in energy and supermarket firms
records.description: Ban MPs from holding any financial interests or shares in major fuel suppliers and supermarkets. We believe this creates a direct conflict of interest, especially during a cost-of-living crisis. All holdings must be fully banned.
records.further_details: We believe allowing lawmakers to hold stakes in firms profiting from high prices is a conflict of interest. While working people struggle, many firms make massive profits. We are concerned that when politicians profit from these margins, the public cannot trust them to regulate these industries. Public service must be separate from corporate gain. We demand a total ban on MPs holding any financial interests in essential food and energy supply chains. All holdings must be divested.

records.title: Ban the sale of methanol to the public without a licence or ID
records.description: Methanol is a highly toxic product but is only regulated in amount upwards of 500 tonnes, however small doses can be deadly to children and adults. Despite being a toxic product, it's readily available in large quantities online without maximum order quantities or age verification.
records.further_details: Methanol is highly toxic, with as little as 30ml potentially fatal if ingested. Someone I loved was able to buy it without sufficient regulation, with devastating consequences. We believe stronger controls are needed to ensure safe handling, clearer labelling, and restricted access to prevent accidental poisoning, misuse, and avoidable deaths.

records.title: Ban music venues from stopping solo people visiting
records.description: I want the government to stop venues refusing entry purely based on the person being alone. I recently visited Manchester to attend a gig and several venues refused entry due to being on my own.
records.further_details:
I think this is discrimination at its finest. People on their own are no different to the next person going into a venue. Being solo or in a group shouldn’t matter. It shouldn’t be allowed that solo visitors are refused entry purely based on the fact they're on their own.
 
I chose to go out on my own. I feel like I have been victimised on the basis of being solo.

records.title: Require all schools to carry out autism, ADHD & dyslexia testing
records.description: Many people struggle without an official diagnosis, and requiring schools to carry out testing could help pupils if they have autism, ADHD, or dyslexia, especially if teachers suspect this is the case. This could also help teachers better communicate with and help their students.
records.further_details: Over 1.7 million pupils in England have special educational needs.  Even though it may seem like a lot, it is actually around 1 in 8 students who have either been diagnosed or have suspected special educational needs. We believe this requires changes to the education system as many children are being left behind with work and aren’t getting the help they need. Also, many students struggle, but without the necessary support, they may be unable to reach their highest potential.

records.title: Write off student loans for nurses trained after 2016
records.description: Since the NHS Bursary was removed in 2016, nursing students have taken on significant student debt. We believe this creates inequality & may discourage people entering or staying in the profession – writing off this debt would support recruitment, improve retention & recognise nurses’ contribution.
records.further_details: In 2016, the NHS Bursary Scheme was removed, leaving nursing students to fund their education through loans. We feel this has created inequality between nurses trained before and after 2016, and, with ongoing NHS staffing shortages, may discourage people from entering or staying in the profession. We believe writing off this debt would support recruitment, improve retention, and recognise the vital role nurses play.

records.title: Require all schools to expel bullies when cases are proven
records.description: Where a school has determined that bullying has occurred, make it mandatory for the school to expel bullies, and for the victims of bullying to receive support.
records.further_details: Too often bullying goes unpunished, and we are concerned that some schools do nothing about it. They might make pupils change seat or change class, but the problem is still there. Telling pupils to ‘just ignore them’ or ‘just stay away from them’ is not good enough. It's serious. It takes lives. Ensure bullies are appropriately punished and investigated and victims are properly taken care of with school counselling. I know what it’s like. I didn’t get help. I’m trying to help all the other victims get the help they need to not be traumatised forever.

records.title: Cap concert ticket prices
records.description: We propose a regulatory cap on concert ticket prices. Analysis should be undertaken to ensure that the cost aligns with the average fan's ability to pay. Organizations such as the Competition and Markets Authority set guidelines that promote fairness in ticket prices and accessibility.
records.further_details: The ever-increasing cost of concerts has made it nearly impossible for fans like me to attend even once a year. Popular artists such as Harry Styles and Olivia Rodrigo are charging hundreds of pounds for seats that aren't even close to the stage. We believe this isn’t justifiable or fair. Prohibitive ticket pricing is excluding many from experiencing the joy of live music, a cultural cornerstone that transcends socioeconomic barriers.

records.title: Reform the local highways maintenance funding formula
