records.description: Require the Department for Transport to reform the local highways maintenance funding formula so councils receive road funding based on actual vehicle usage levels per mile.
records.further_details: Current local road maintenance funding is mainly based on the length and category of roads maintained by councils. This is unfair as roads with far higher traffic volumes experience greater wear and deterioration. Areas with heavy commuter, freight and commercial traffic should receive funding that reflects the actual strain placed on their road network. We believe the funding formula should include traffic levels, vehicle miles travelled and heavy vehicle usage alongside road length.

records.title: Require police to preserve incident-linked body-worn video for 6 months
records.description: Legislate to require police to retain body-worn video footage linked to recorded police-public interactions for 6 months, with extension where a complaint, subject access request, disclosure request, safeguarding process or investigation arises.
records.further_details: Body-worn video linked to police-public incidents can be deleted before people reasonably know it may be relevant. It may later be needed for complaints, subject access or disclosure requests, safeguarding, investigations or review of police conduct.  A 6-month period, set by law or statutory guidance, would reduce premature deletion while still allowing routine, unrelated footage to be deleted sooner.

records.title: Fund expansion of apprenticeships and entry level jobs
records.description: Youth unemployment affects young people up and down the UK. Lack of experience often blocks entry-level jobs, creating a cycle of no opportunity. We believe the Government must expand apprenticeships and encourage employers to hire young people.
records.further_details: Youth unemployment affects young people up and down the country. Many cannot access jobs due to lack of experience, creating a cycle of exclusion. The Government has repeatedly discussed this issue but has, we believe, failed to take meaningful action. We feel that expanding apprenticeships and entry-level opportunities would give young people experience, improve life chances, and may help reduce crime linked to financial pressure and lack of opportunity.

records.title: Provide more funding to support GPs
records.description: We are concerned that underfunding is pushing NHS GPs to collapse. The BMA is balloting doctors on other models, including more freedom to provide private services. We feel this could mean millions are priced out of care. Government must fund a fair contract to protect free, universal GP access.
records.further_details: We believe underfunding and unmanageable terms are pushing NHS general practices to collapse. The British Medical Association is balloting family doctors on alternative strategies to the core contract. Potential models include more freedom to move to a means-tested, private subscription service. We feel this could mean millions of NHS patients risk being priced out of basic care. We call on the Government to agree a fair contract and protect free GP access. Protect NHS care.

records.title: Fund increased Perinatal Hospice Services nationwide
records.description: We want the Government to help fund dedicated perinatal hospice services across the country and to ensure families can be informed about perinatal hospice and palliative care options following a life-limiting prenatal diagnosis. We believe this will give families hope.
records.further_details: Such services would provide specialist counselling and emotional support from diagnosis onwards, Improve access to multidisciplinary care for babies with complex medical needs. We believe this will make sure that no family faces this difficult journey alone and will help them realise that the best option isn’t abortion but to give the baby the best quality of life they can.

records.title: Accept all valid biometric EU/EEA/CH national identity cards for entry to the UK
records.description: On 1 October 2021, the UK ceased accepting visitors' EU/EEA/CH national identity cards for UK entry, even very secure biometric cards. We want to reverse this decision & configure the UK's passport e-gates & the ETA system to accept all biometric EU/EEA/CH national identity cards and passport cards
records.further_details: Since 1 October 2021, it has been reported that the UK has suffered an enormous fall in inbound tourism from EU/EEA/CH citizens who have identity cards but not passports. Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1208 requires identity cards issued since 2 August 2021 to conform to a common format specified by ICAO Document 9303, including a biometric chip and machine-readable zone, making them secure and compatible with e-gates. The Home Office says it costs an estimated 75p more to process an entry to the UK at a desk compared to an e-gate.

records.title: Require that every public playground has adequate shade available
records.description: Ensure existing and new public playgrounds provide adequate shade for children through solutions such as shade sails, canopies, tree planting, or other suitable shade structures.
records.further_details: We call on the Government to introduce national guidance requiring local authorities to assess shade provision in existing public playgrounds and fund a programme of improvements where needed, while ensuring all new public playgrounds include adequate shade to protect children from heat and UV exposure.

records.title: Extend the Universal Credit Holiday Limit from 28 Days to 40 Days
records.description: Many Universal Credit claimants have close family living overseas.They may need to visit elderly parents, care for a seriously ill relative,attend funeral, settle family matters,or support loved ones during a crisis. These situations are often unexpected and cannot always be resolved within 28 days.
records.further_details: The Government must modernise these rules to reflect the realities of modern family life. Universal Credit should not punish people for doing the right thing in a family crisis. No claimant should be forced to choose between standing by a loved one in an emergency and keeping the support they need to pay for rent, food, and basic living costs.

records.title: Raise the standard tax-free Personal Allowance to £50,000.
records.description: The Personal Allowance is the amount of income a person can get before they pay tax. It stands at £12,570 since 2025. We would like the standard Personal Allowance raised to what we think is a more realistic figure of £50,000.
records.further_details:
We think that the Personal Allowance, as termed by the government, has been kept unreasonably low for far too long, at the expense of the poorest, most needy people in our society.

We feel that the poorer majority should pay substantially less than the wealthy. We think that the tax system seems designed to make the divide between rich and poor increase exponentially.

records.title: Create an early state pension access scheme for 28 to 40-year-olds
records.description: Create a scheme which allows 28 to 40-year-olds access to their pension pots, using a tax-free lump sum of around £12,500 of pension in exchange for delaying receipt of their state pension by a year. This could help address inequality, cost of living pressures and getting onto the property ladder.
records.further_details:
We feel young people are facing major hurdles when it comes to buying a home as house prices have grown much faster than wages. High rent costs stop many young people from saving money for a deposit, and stricter lending rules and higher mortgage rates can make monthly loan payments hard to afford.
 
Property costs are often many times higher than an entry-level yearly salary, and high monthly rent payments can leave little room to save for a large cash deposit. Banks require higher incomes and larger deposit percentages to approve big mortgages.

records.title: Inflation uprate the £12570 Personal Allowance in April 2027 or earlier
records.description: As we all know the personal allowance has been frozen at £12570 since 2021 and it is currently planned to remain that way until 2031. We call on the UK government to inflation uprate it at least once in April 2027 or earlier to give the tax-payer a 'cost of living' breather.

records.title: Fund the provision of backup stair-access equipment in disabled people’s homes
records.description: Fund the provision of back-up stair-access equipment, such as stair lifts, in homes where disabled residents cannot use the stairs safely or independently. This could allow them to move safely up & downstairs in an emergency if their usual equipment fails and ensure they are not stuck on one floor.
records.further_details: When essential mobility equipment such as a home lift fails, a disabled person who cannot safely use stairs may become trapped on one floor of their own home, potentially losing access to their bedroom, bathroom or a safe way out. Backup stair-access equipment could provide a second way to move safely between floors during an emergency. There should be priority consideration for those who live alone or do not have someone available who can safely operate the equipment.

records.title: Mandate offer of literal-language GCSE papers for students with autism
records.description: Mandate the offer of literal language GCSE papers for autistic pupils. We want the Government to direct Ofqual to ensure exam boards provide an optional, literal-language GCSE exam pathway for autistic students across all subjects to remove unfair communication barriers.
records.further_details: GCSE exams rely on figurative language, idioms, and double negatives. Many students with autism interpret language literally, meaning they are penalised for wording rather than their actual academic knowledge. Adjustments like extra time do not solve this. We want an optional "Direct Paper" path. These papers must keep identical academic standards, but require questions to be written straight to the point with abstract language removed. Let’s give all children a fair chance to show what they know.

records.title: Require compensation when a buyer or seller withdraws from an agreed house sale
records.description: Introduce a law requiring a buyer or seller who withdraws from an agreed house sale without a reasonable cause to reimburse the other party for reasonable costs already incurred, including solicitor fees, property searches and surveys.
records.further_details:
In England and Wales, buyers and sellers can withdraw from a property sale before contracts are exchanged, even after the other party has spent hundreds of pounds on legal costs.
We have experienced this twice. After having offers accepted on two homes, we paid £450 and £500 in solicitor and search fees, only for both sellers to decide not to proceed. We lost around £950 through no decision of our own.
We believe that if a buyer or seller withdraws without reasonable cause after costs have been incurred, they should reimburse the other party's reasonable costs. We think this would create greater accountability and protect people from unnecessary financial loss.

records.title: Require compensation for call centres wasting customers’ time
records.description: I want Government and Parliament to implement legislation that limits the time that a customer has to spend on the phone to call centres and AI agents. It should allow the customer to claim financial compensation from the service provider for the time wasted over a set time limit, say 30 minutes.
records.further_details: In our view many of us waste hours and hours of our lives on the phone to call centres, often sorting out very simple issues or the service providers' own mistakes. Many of these centres were originally created by the company to reduce costs within the organisations, but we think these costs have effectively been passed to customers by way of wasted time. I seek a way of limiting the amount of time wasted on such calls and allowing for some form of redress where appropriate.

records.title: Ban HMO Conversions in Properties with 3 Bedrooms or Fewer
records.description: Ban HMO conversions in properties with three bedrooms or fewer to protect family homes. We believe too many small houses are being turned into HMOs, leaving families with nowhere suitable to rent. We need national rules to keep smaller homes available for families.
records.further_details: Many families are losing access to small homes because two bed and three bed houses are being turned into HMOs. These were intended as family homes, not multi tenant properties. We feel this is breaking communities and leaving families with nowhere to rent. The Government must stop HMO conversions in properties with three bedrooms or fewer.

records.title: Require mental health support in secondary schools
records.description: Require every secondary school to provide accessible, confidential mental health support for students.
records.further_details: This matters because it focuses on access to help for young people

records.title: Require Ofgem price cap for heat networks and no heat costs via service charges
records.description: Require Ofgem to introduce a price cap for domestic heat networks, covering unit and standing charges, and prohibit heat-network supply, operation, maintenance, repair, replacement and upgrade costs from being recovered through residential service charges.
records.further_details: Heat-network customers often cannot choose their supplier or switch networks, yet are outside the existing energy price cap. The Government should require Ofgem to set maximum heat-network prices and ensure costs of supplying and operating heat networks, including maintenance, repair, replacement and upgrades, cannot be shifted into residential service charges or recovered twice.

records.title: Make it mandatory for all police cars to use dashcam to ensure safety
records.description: We believe that some people are wrongly arrested, accused and convicted due to faulty evidence provided by police whilst others are correctly arrested and accused but not convicted due to a lack of evidence. Make it mandatory to fit all police cars with dashcams to ensure evidence is recorded.
records.further_details: Not all police cars are fitted with cameras, and we believe that this is a missed opportunity to collect evidence to support convictions and evidence gathering. We think it could also be helpful in cases where police have driven dangerously, and may make police drive better, give better coverage of any incidents that do happen and prevent mishaps.

records.title: Review Local Authority process in child removal cases involving medical disputes
records.description: Review Local Authorities (LAs) powers to remove children due to medical disputes. We believe where appropriate, tertiary specialist referrals should be mandatory when parents and LAs disagree on complex care, and “medical neglect” charges should not be brought while expert opinion is sought.
records.further_details: We think a review of these powers should also include considering how parents can be better protected and supported, including child protection process and the provision of legal aid. We also think Local Authorities must be prevented from using medical disputes to accuse the parents of 'child neglect' until a Tertiary Specialist opinion is obtained. We call on the Government to protect parents' rights to act as Litigants in Person to ensure their voice is never silenced by the Local Authority.

records.title: Reduce school homework to the core (English, Maths, Science) & GCSE subjects
records.description: I want the Government to ensure that homework can only be given for core subjects English, Maths and Science and for subjects being taken for GCSE.  Pupils often find that homework can have an effect on them and other classmates, increasing anxiety and stress levels which then leads on to sleep loss
records.further_details: We believe this can have a large impact on a child’s mental and physical wellbeing, also their education. So we feel it would hugely increase and impact children’s health positively if we could reduce homework!

records.title: Create a fast-track system for people who need to retake a driving test
records.description: Create a different booking system that recognises the driver has previously failed and wants to retake
records.further_details: We believe it would benefit both people looking for their first test and retakers. Waiting 6 months to retake a test can become costly and frustrating especially when the driver doesn't necessarily need 6 months worth of practise and is close to being test ready again. First time test takers would also not need to compete with people looking for cancellations and they are more likely to need the 6 month wait.

records.title: Restrict babies and children in nail salons for their safety and health
records.description: Introduce regulations to restrict or prohibit babies and young children in nail salons due to exposure to chemical fumes and substances used in treatments, to protect their health and reduce potential harm.
records.further_details: I am concerned about the health of babies and young children exposed to the chemical fumes in nail salons. I recently saw an 8-week-old baby coughing, crying and very distressed in this environment which was upsetting to witness. Nail salons often contain strong fumes that may harm developing lungs, so we believe protections are needed.

records.title: Fund a simpler and fairer England wide toll and parking charges payment system
records.description: We call on the Government to fund a simpler and fairer toll and parking charges payment system across England. We think this should have timely digital alerts, and fair and proportionate penalties with first-time cases allowing payment of the original charge plus a reasonable fee.
records.further_details: In our experience drivers often receive large fines because payment systems are fragmented and unclear, especially when travelling outside their local area. Charges can escalate before drivers are even aware, as communication relies on post which may be delayed or not received. We think a simpler system that allows drivers to use a single account, with alerts and fairer penalties, would reduce accidental non-payment while still allowing proper enforcement.

records.title: Hold a referendum if council tax rises by 4.99% for 3 consecutive years
records.description: Currently, a referendum is triggered by a local authority if they want to increase council tax by more than the amount specified in the principles determined by the Secretary of State currently 5% for many authorities.
records.further_details: Some councils have raised the tax by 4.99% year after year. I call for the law to change so a local referendum is triggered if a 4.99% council tax increase is applied consecutively for 3 years.

records.title: Keep the presumption of parental involvement & review fairness in family courts
records.description: We call on the Government to keep the presumption of parental involvement and review the fairness of family courts particularly when contact orders are breached or false accusations are made. Children need both safe parents.
records.further_details: We are concerned that repealing the parental involvement presumption risks weakening children’s right to relationships with both safe parents. We want processes to be reviewed to ensure fair evidence thresholds, accountability for proven false claims, and tougher sanctions for breaches. Family courts should not treat parents as suspects based solely on allegations. We believe unproven claims can trigger intrusive psychological and hair-strand tests, while contact orders may be breached without real sanctions.

records.title: Fund improvements to Fertility Testing and Investigation on the NHS
records.description: Allocate funding to improve NHS fertility testing. This could allow more in-depth investigations for women and men, reduce postcode disparities, and help ensure affordable access to advanced tests before a diagnosis of unexplained infertility is given.
records.further_details: More funding could enable to expansion of NHS fertility testing for women and men before diagnosing unexplained infertility. It could also facilitate more consistent national testing standards, improve access to specialist hormonal, genetic & reproductive health investigations, strengthen male fertility assessments, provide subsidised or capped-cost advanced testing where NHS funding is unavailable, & ensure patients receive clearer information about tests completed & further options available.

records.title: Require a Commons confidence vote within 14 days of a new PM taking office
records.description: Amend House of Commons Standing Orders to require the Government to table a formal confidence motion within 14 days whenever a new Prime Minister takes office between general elections, and require the House to debate and vote on it.
records.further_details:
When a Prime Minister changes between general elections, the Government may continue without the House of Commons being required to hold an explicit vote confirming that it retains confidence under its new leader.

We believe a mandatory vote within 14 days would provide a clear, transparent and consistent test of parliamentary support, strengthen democratic accountability, and apply equally to every political party and future Government.

records.title: Children attending nursery/school must have up-to-date vaccinations like the MMR
records.description: We want the Government to require all children attending nursery or school to be up to date with their routine childhood vaccinations, including the MMR vaccine, unless medically exempt. We believe this would help prevent outbreaks, protect vulnerable people, and keep children and communities safer.
records.further_details: Vaccines protect children from serious preventable diseases like measles, polio and flu. We want the Government to require children attending nursery or school to be up to date with routine vaccinations, unless they have a medical exemption, to help prevent outbreaks and protect public health. Unvaccinated children are at much higher risk of severe illness, including complications such as brain swelling, permanent blindness, or death from measles.

records.title: Hold referendum on hereditary monarchy or a democratically chosen Head of State
records.description: Hold a national public vote on the future of the UK's Head of State, allowing the public to decide whether the current hereditary system should continue or, if changed, how the Head of State should be selected democratically.
records.further_details: The UK’s Head of State is currently determined through hereditary succession. We believe the public should have a direct say. The Government and Parliament should hold a national vote on whether the hereditary system should continue. If the public chooses a democratic system, Parliament should establish a democratic process for selecting the Head of State.

records.title: Urge international partners to ban the use of wild animals in circuses
records.description: We want the UK Government to use its diplomatic influence, trade discussions, and international forums to encourage global partners including Germany, the US, and Australia to implement full bans on wild animals in circuses.
records.further_details: The UK successfully banned wild animals in travelling circuses in 2019. However, animals like elephants, bears, and big cats are still legally forced to perform in other major nations. The UK should lead on animal welfare globally and pressure international partners to end this practice.

records.title: Raise cap for High Income Child Benefit Charge and apply to household income
records.description: The High Income Child Benefit Charge is a tax charge. We want the Government to change the criteria for the High Income Child Benefit Charge so that it doesn't penalise single income households which have no greater income than some double income households.
records.further_details: At present the High Income Child Benefit Charge is determined by the highest income earned in the household. This means that a single income household with earnings above £60,000 starts to pay the charge, while a household with two earners below £60,000 total each does not. We want this to change so that the cap is £120,000 total income for the household where the children reside. We believe tax systems should not penalise single income households and in particular single parents, or those with majority co- parenting responsibilities.

records.title: Create new compensation scheme and mandate automatic delay repay for UK flights
records.description: Legislate to mandate an automatic refund system for flight delays over 1 hour, irrespective of cause. The original retailer, broker or airline must pay passengers, and NATS must be legally mandated to reimburse them when ATC is at fault.
records.further_details: Passengers face a broken system where loopholes deny payouts. Parliament must enact automatic refunds: 25% for 1-hour, 50% for 2-hour, and 100% for 3-hour delays. Calculations must include the full basket price (fare, taxes, luggage, seats, extras). Whoever took the payment - retailer, broker, travel agent, airline - must refund the passenger within 14 calendar days. Crucially, NATS's financial immunity must end so ATC legally reimburses the supply chain when their failures cause the disruption.

records.title: Make elected governments legally accountable for manifesto commitments
records.description: Require elected governments to be formally accountable for the manifesto commitments on which they were elected. Create an independent system to track delivery and require explanations for broken pledges, with meaningful financial penalties for parties that unjustifiably abandon them.
records.further_details: Voters make decisions based on the commitments parties put before them at an election. Yet once elected, governments can abandon or reverse major manifesto pledges with little formal accountability. This damages public trust and weakens confidence in democracy. An independent body should track manifesto delivery, require public explanations for significant departures and, where pledges are unjustifiably abandoned, impose substantial financial penalties on the governing party.

records.title: Keep the State Pension Triple Lock
records.description: We want the Government to keep the State Pension triple lock. It protects pensioners against rising living costs and ensures pensions keep pace with earnings. Scrapping it could leave millions of pensioners worse off over time and undermine financial security in retirement.
records.further_details: We want the Government to keep the State Pension triple lock. It ensures pensions rise by the highest of inflation, earnings growth or 2.5%, protecting pensioners from rising living costs and falling behind working people. The State Pension is vital for millions who have paid National Insurance and rely on it for food, energy and housing. Weakening the triple lock could mean lower increases that compound over time, leaving pensioners worse off, undermining financial security in retirement

records.title: Require learning disability nurses in all SLD SEND specialist schools
records.description: Make it a legal requirement for all severe learning disability (SLD) SEND specialist schools to have a qualified learning disability nurse on site during school hours to safely support pupils with complex medical and care needs.
records.further_details: Children with learning disabilities often have multiple and complex health conditions and are at significantly higher risk of conditions such as epilepsy. NHS England’s Learning Disabilities Mortality Review (LeDeR) programme shows people with learning disabilities are more likely to die from avoidable causes. Many children in SLD schools require support with feeding, medication and seizures. Without a qualified nurse on site, responsibility could fall to non-medical staff. We believe this increases risk and could delay essential care.

records.title: Review and cap increases on Motability advance payments
records.description: We ask the Government to review and cap rising Advance Payments on Motability vehicles, ensure suitable vehicles remain affordable, and consider Universal Credit savings limits, to protect disabled people from being priced out of essential mobility.
records.further_details: For disabled people, Motability is a lifeline, not a luxury. Many disabled people rely on it to work, attend medical appointments, and live independently. We are concerned that rising advance payments are making suitable vehicles unaffordable, while benefit rules prevent saving enough to afford them. This can create an impossible situation where people lose access to independence. Forcing disabled people into unsuitable vehicles or off the scheme entirely could risk isolation and hardship.

records.title: Legislate to require hidden disability training in all public services
records.description: While the Equality Act 2010 protects people with disabilities, we believe it must go further to foster a culture of inclusion for those with hidden disabilities. Existing responsibilities are not supported by mandatory training, especially for those with neurodivergence, this can limit support.
records.further_details: We are calling on the government to ensure that public sector services are equipped to help and support people with hidden disabilities. Currently, while there is legislation to support reasonable adjustments to avoid discrimination, there is no mandatory training to ensure that public sector workers know enough about hidden disabilities to be able to deliver this effectively.

records.title: Review of Sentencing in Youth Sexual Offence Cases and Judicial Training
records.description: We call for a review into the sentencing in youth sexual offence cases involving coercion, filming, humiliation and rape, and funding for improved judicial training in such cases. We believe this can help improve public confidence that girls and women are equally protected under the rule of law.
records.further_details: We believe such a review could help ensure stronger recognition that coercion, filming, humiliation, planning and group offending are aggravating factors demonstrating serious intent. We also think that judicial training on coercive control, safeguarding, abuse escalation and victim impact can help ensure safeguarding is balanced with rehabilitation, victim protection/ongoing support, accountability, public confidence and deterrence.

records.title: Government grants for companies offering paid internships & entry jobs to 18-24s
records.description:
The Milburn report showed there are systematic failings creating barriers for Gen Z looking to get jobs.

We are calling for the government to implement grants to companies hiring young people aged 18-24 in paid internships & entry jobs to help make starting a career actually affordable.
records.further_details:
One million young people are not in employment, education or training, with the government-issued Milburn report suggesting a huge economic impact.

Young people are being systematically failed, faced with employment barriers that are increasingly competitive, unequal, and financially unviable.

We are petitioning for the government to implement policy to directly address this, offering grants to companies hiring aged 18-24s into paid internships or entry jobs to help stimulate youth employment.

records.title: Reform planning law to protect property access rights and deed restrictions
records.description: The Government must by law require planning authorities to take account of property deeds, restrictive covenants and legal access rights before granting planning permission.
records.further_details: This reform must prevent planning authorities from approving developments that would block legal access when deeds and conveyance documents expressly prohibit it. Even after providing evidence that the proposal would substantially interfere with legal access, safety and use of property, permission can still be granted. Councils habitually consider deeds and property rights outside the scope of the planning process. We believe homeowners shouldn’t be forced into highly costly civil court proceedings to enforce rights already protected by legally binding documents.

records.title: Regulate the sale of hidden cameras disguised as everyday objects
records.description: Require licensing, registration or stricter controls on the sale of hidden cameras disguised as everyday objects, such as chargers, smoke alarms, plug sockets, clocks and other household items, to help protect children and vulnerable people from exploitation and abuse.
records.further_details: A parent can check a room for cameras and still miss a device hidden inside a charger, smoke alarm or plug socket. A victim of domestic abuse may never know they are being watched. A child may be recorded in a place where they should be safest. These devices are intentionally designed to avoid detection and have been used in criminal offences across the UK. Greater safeguards are needed to prevent harm before it occurs.

records.title: Review council housing eligibility for hidden homeless and those in unsafe homes
records.description: Review council housing eligibility to ensure people in unsafe or unsuitable accommodation can receive help before reaching crisis point or becoming homeless.
records.further_details: Eligibility rules should recognise hidden homelessness, including sofa surfing. They should prioritise people fleeing domestic abuse and pregnant people living in unsuitable accommodation. Councils should always assess whether a home is safe and suitable, not simply whether someone has a roof over their head.

records.title: Speed up the law to allow hybrid attendance by councillors at council meetings
records.description: I believe there has not been enough progress by the Government in facilitating hybrid attendance by councillors at council meetings. I believe facilitating such attendance would provide a perfect opportunity to enable a wider range of people to put themselves forward as candidates to be councillors.
records.further_details: In June 2025 the Government said it would do this. I think that there are still so many people with all of the necessary talents who are currently locked out of being councillors. I believe there is no urgency at the moment with regards to the timescale to bring in these changes. I think a perfectly reasonable timescale would be to ensure hybrid attendance of councillors is implemented at least six months before next year’s local elections. This should be priority for the Government and Parliament.

records.title: Statutory Public Inquiry: University Corruption, Toxic Culture & Staff Silencing
records.description: We urge the Government to establish a Statutory Public Inquiry into English universities. We believe that institutional self-preservation hides corruption, systemic governance failures and toxic cultures.
records.further_details:
We call for a duty of candour to compel evidence, expose any use of NDAs to silence staff, and enforce reform.

We believe that systemic governance failures have resulted in staff bullying, victimisation and discrimination, and the misuse of NDAs are silencing whistleblowers. An inquiry must urgently compel evidence, scrutinise whether public funds have been used for legal settlements, and enforce structural reform.

records.title: Update guidance on secondary uniform to support inclusion & comfort
records.description: Update national guidance to urge secondary schools to transition from rigid formal attire (blazers, shirts, and ties) to comfortable, accessible alternatives such as polo shirts and tailored trousers.
records.further_details:
We believe secondary school uniforms are outdated, and that replacing shirts, ties, and blazers with polo shirts and trousers would benefit all students.
 
Rising temperatures and frequent heatwaves due to climate change can make heavy, formal uniforms uncomfortably hot; relaxed attire could help ensure year-round comfort and focus.
 
In our view, it would also help lower costs for families, mirror modern workplaces, and ease the transition for Moderate Learning Difficulties (MLD) pupils in mainstream schools who struggle with sensory-heavy formal wear.

records.title: Review NHS patient access to essential medical equipment & supplies
records.description: Launch a review into NHS patient access to essential medical equipment and supplies and ensuring consistent access regardless of their postcode or ability to pay. People with chronic illnesses depend on essential equipment and supplies to stay alive and prevent complications.
records.further_details:
However, access and quantities may vary based on postcode and funding. Some patients may need to purchase necessary supplies or equipment themselves. We believe this is unacceptable and that medical needs should not depend on postcode or ability to pay.
 
We want the review to look into establishing national access and quantity standards based on individual medical needs, ensuring patients are not required to self-fund, and addressing postcode variations in medical supply access and quantities.

records.title: Require safer taller fencing & secure child-proof gates at children’s play areas
records.description: Introduce minimum safety standards for enclosed public children’s play parks, including taller secure perimeter fencing and child-resistant gates that young children cannot simply push open, with particular consideration given to autistic children and other children who are at risk of elopement.
records.further_details: Many autistic children are at serious risk because they elope or run without understanding danger. Most playground gates can be pushed open easily, and many parks are beside roads or other hazards. This excludes autistic children from places they should be able to enjoy. Taller secure fencing and childproof, self-closing gates would make public play parks safer and more inclusive.

records.title: Mandate frontline emergency service staff training on mental health crises
records.description: Mandate mandatory training for all frontline emergency service staff to recognise and handle mental crisis situations, especially if someone is in immediate danger. This training should include training on mental health awareness.
records.further_details: We believe there is currently a very fractured and scattered knowledge amongst emergency service staff regarding handling mental health crisis situations, and very often, the emergency services are the first people somebody sees or talks to when they or somebody they care about is in a mental health crisis. This fractured knowledge could cost lives. By ensuring all staff are trained properly, they could potentially save many more lives.

records.title: Create new guidance for schools as well as parents on screen time for children
records.description: We call upon the Government to create new guidance on screen time for children that is also directed at schools and educational settings as well as parents. This should include ensuring schools are transparent with parents about screen time in school.
records.further_details: The government have provided new guidance with evidence to back the reduction of screen time for children aged 2-5 to 1 hour per day for parents. However, it has not considered the time spent on screens during the school day which can often exceed 1 hour. Educational or not it’s still screen time. The Government has said that evidence backs the guidance that children shouldn't use screens for more than 1 hour so why is this only for parents to follow and not schools. There should be transparency from schools to parents about screen time at school and guidance for them to follow as well.

records.title: Limit rent increases to once per year per property, regardless of tenant changes
records.description: We want the UK Government to introduce legislation limiting rent increases to once per year per property, regardless of how many tenancies apply to the property within that period.
records.further_details: Recent rental reforms aim to improve tenant protections, but may create unintended consequences. Landlords can advertise rent at a higher rate each time a tenant moves out; if there is increased tenant turnover this could lead to multiple increases on a property within a year between tenancies. In high-demand areas like London, this risks worsening affordability and housing instability. We propose limiting rent increases to once per year per property to ensure fairness, stability, and prevent abuse.

records.title: Keep 24 month post-study visa for international graduates
records.description: Reverse the planned cut to the Graduate Route visa from 24 to 18 months. We think international graduates should keep the right to stay and work in the UK for two years after their degree instead of the proposed 18 months, giving them a fair chance to contribute their skills to the economy.
records.further_details: International students contribute £41.9 billion to the UK economy and £560 per citizen per year. They pay full tuition fees, fill skills shortages, and support local economies. From January 2027, the Graduate visa drops from 24 to 18 months, leaving graduates less time to secure skilled work before their visa runs out. In our view, the UK actively recruits global talent, trains it at world-class universities, then makes it leave before it can give back. We do not think that this is a strategy - It is a waste.

records.title: Fund more research to extend availability of medical cannabis on the NHS
records.description: I want the Government to provide funding to make medical cannabis more available on the NHS than it is at present, for all who need it, in a similar way to other current medications.
records.further_details: I want the Government to fund more research to help make medical cannabis more freely available on the NHS because I believe many people could benefit from this. Myself I have ADHD etc and I feel it would help my brain focus and many others and also help people with many conditions physical or mental or neurological. It's already a proven medicinal plant and I don’t think people should have to spend a lot of money to get it from private companies.

records.title: Formally recognise the killing of Armenians in 1915-1923 as genocide
records.description: We want the Government to align itself with those international communities which recognise the Armenian Genocide of 1915-1923 by: Officially recognising the genocide, declaring April 24th ‘Armenian genocide Memorial Day’ and bringing it into the education curriculum.
records.further_details: We believe the issue of labelling genocide has never been more important than today. The Government's current stance is it is up to institutions to determine whether genocide has occurred. We feel this leaves us open to losing our voice as a nation to call out injustices. Furthermore, the implications of a Memorial Day and teaching of the genocide are massive for our history and victims alike. Recognition serves not only to teach, but to honour and remember.

records.title: Transition to a digital voting system
records.description: We call on the Government to develop and implement a secure digital voting platform for use in General and Local elections. This system should be designed to modernise our democracy, increase accessibility, and significantly reduce the recurring multimillion-pound burden on the taxpayer.
records.further_details: We believe the current system is an expensive relic. Spending over £150 million on a single general election with millions wasted on paper, postage, and manual labour feels indefensible to us  when public services are struggling for funding. People do almost everything else securely online, from banking to taxes, so our democracy shouldn't be stuck in the 19th century. We believe digitising the process would slash administrative overheads, save local councils a fortune, and finally make voting accessible for everyone.

records.title: Create a SEN Commission to inspect and enforce disability support in education
records.description: Establish an independent SEN Commission with powers to inspect SEN provision in schools and colleges, investigate complaints from disabled students, and enforce compliance with the Equality Act 2010 and Children and Families Act 2014.
records.further_details: We are concerned that Disabled students in schools and colleges are routinely failed by institutions that do not meet their legal duties under the Equality Act 2010 and Children and Families Act 2014. Education has no independent body to inspect SEN provision or investigate complaints. We feel Ofsted does not adequately scrutinise SEN support. Students can lose opportunities, qualifications and university places as a result. We believe an independent SEN Commission would provide accountability and enforcement.

records.title: Amend Part IV of Family Law Act 1996 for Abuse Survivors Without Shared Children
records.description: We call on the Government to bring forward an amendment to Part IV of the Family Law Act 1996 to close the Family Court gap for abuse survivors without shared children.
records.further_details: This amendment should require that rules of court and practice directions provide, for non-molestation and occupation order proceedings, protections equivalent to those in Practice Direction 12J: consideration of fact-finding where domestic abuse is alleged, treatment of abuse as a pattern of behaviour, restrictions on undertakings and cross-undertakings where violence has been used or threatened, and provision for special measures.

records.title: Change plans for Social Media Bans to instead a Law Enforcing Parental Controls
records.description: Instead of banning Social Media as proposed for Under 16's instead create a new law requiring parents to set up Parental Controls on their children's devices. This still secures the safety of children through Parental Responsibility while eliminating online ID Checks for all accessing social media.

records.title: Repair roads first before new projects & make those who cause potholes fix them
records.description: Require all existing roads to be repaired before new projects, create one national road fund, ensure potholes caused by poor reinstatement after digging up the road are fixed by those responsible, and introduce public reporting and repair‑tracking so all repairs meet the required five‑year lifespan.
records.further_details: Many potholes form because road surfaces are not properly reinstated after being dug up for utility or repair works. We want those responsible for the reinstatement to fix any resulting potholes to the required five‑year standard. Creating one national road fund would prioritise repairs before new projects. A public, outsourced and self‑funding reporting and tracking system would let people report issues, follow progress, and ensure repairs are completed properly with clear accountability.

records.title: Public inquiry into pattern of withdrawals of local funding for pride events
records.description: Many local councils have pulled support for local pride events that which had previously received funding, resulting in trade unions paying for expenses. I ask for a statutory public inquiry into the reason why funds have been withdrawn from these LGBT Pride events.
records.further_details: I think they have been removed without a good reason.

records.title: Review and fund the addition of routine NHS newborn tongue-tie assessments
records.description: Review and fund the addition of routine tongue-tie assessments for all newborn babies as part of standard NHS newborn examinations in the first days after birth, alongside existing newborn checks and appropriate referral pathways where needed.
records.further_details: Tongue-tie (ankyloglossia) is a condition present at birth that can restrict tongue movement. In some babies, it can cause feeding difficulties, poor latch, maternal nipple pain, prolonged feeding times, and poor weight gain. The NHS recognises tongue-tie can affect both breastfeeding and bottle feeding, yet some cases are only identified after problems develop. We believe assessment during routine newborn checks could help identify feeding issues earlier and enable access to support sooner.

records.title: Provide prescription sports goggles free on the NHS to children under 16
records.description: I would like the Government to provide free prescription sports goggles on the NHS to children under the age of 16 who have a prescription for glasses.
records.further_details: It has only just dawned on me that my daughter needs prescription sports goggles while doing sports as normal glasses are very impractical and if she removes her glasses her vision is impaired. I would like the Government to provide free prescription sports goggles to children under 16 years of age who are in the same situation as her.

records.title: Fund extension of  stem cell therapy trialling for men with lichen sclerosus
records.description: In the UK there is an experimental treatment using stem cells derived from autologous fat grafting and platelet rich plasma therapy. It is being trialled for people suffering with the debilitating condition of lichen sclerosus which is an inflammatory condition that mainly affects the genital skin.
records.further_details: The programme, known as PETALS for women and PEARLS for adolescent girls is available on the NHS. But for men there is no such trialling for funding reasons and because there are more women with the condition. Reports indicate that this treatment has so far seen some amazing results. As men with the condition are entirely excluded, I would like the Government to fund an extension of the trial to men also who are also at risk of cancer and the destruction of their genital tissues.

records.title: Grant anonymity to individuals accused of sexual assault until a guilty verdict
records.description: Automatically grant anonymity to individuals accused of rape or sexual assault, which prevents them from being named publicly, until a court reaches a guilty verdict.
records.further_details: This could help protect the reputation and privacy of those who may be innocent, and will result in individuals only being named until they are found guilty in a court of law.

records.title: Ban any government claims that people are increasingly living longer.
records.description: We ask the government to ban the use of the claim that longevity is constantly on the increase in policy decisions, official statements and documents. The ONS's most recent data for 2022-2024, shows it was at the same level for females as 2017-2019, pre-pandemic and below that level for males.
records.further_details: The claim appears in a response to one of our petitions (728656) calling for a decent state pension from an attainable age: "As longevity has increased and our society aged...". We are concerned it could be used in upcoming policy decisions and reports. We see this issue as literally a matter of life and death, for all of the population. We believe this is a fallacy that has been pedalled as a fact, for too many years.

records.title: Make paternity tests compulsory before paying child maintenance
records.description: Legislate to require paternity tests to be taken before a father makes child maintenance payments.
records.further_details:
We believe that fathers find themselves in a precarious situation when they are compelled to pay child maintenance for a child whose paternity they are uncertain of. There are also countless mothers who are denied the financial support they deserve for their child because the issue of paternity remains contested.
 
This can lead to confusion, unfair financial responsibilities, emotional distress for all parties involved, and children missing out on vital support.

records.title: Ban pay by phone on gambling websites
records.description: Ban pay by phone on gambling sites, where people can have credit added to a phone bill. With this payment method a phone bill can end up over £300 a month, this method is to easily used by gambling addicts and can go undetected to other family members
records.further_details: This method of payment is used by many gambling companies online and the amount taken to gamble with is then added to the phone bill and can go undetected for months to family members. This is an easy way for a gambler to get money and use on these sites. This can take months to be detected and does not help if you are trying to help someone to stop gambling. The mobile phone companies say they can not block this even if you have settings to stop high bills. This needs to be stopped

records.title: Review of urology care for women
records.description: We call on the Government to conduct a review of urology care for women, focusing on women who experience urinary retention, the extent to which patient choice and consent is respected, and the quality of the care. Patients deserve to be heard, supported and involved.
records.further_details: Patients deserve to have their symptoms, concerns and evidence taken seriously, with clear explanations, informed choices and respect for consent. No woman should leave an appointment feeling dismissed, pressured or unheard. We therefore believe a review is needed to ensue that patients have their symptoms, concerns and evidence taken seriously, with clear explanations, informed choices and respect for consent.

records.title: Require travel companies ensure hotels meet minimum animal welfare standards
records.description: We want the Government to require UK travel companies and package holiday providers to ensure overseas hotels they work with have minimum welfare procedures for stray animals on their premises, including access to veterinary care, clean water and humane population management.
records.further_details: Stray animals are common at many overseas holiday resorts, yet sick or injured animals can be left without care. Some companies already operate an optional Stray & Working Animal Welfare Award that supports measures including veterinary care, neutering, access to food and clean water. We believe this shows such standards are achievable. We believe basic welfare procedures should not be optional and travel companies should ensure contracted hotels have appropriate measures in place.

records.title: Government to begin the process to officially recognise Somaliland
records.description: Somaliland declared independence from Somalia in 1991 after the collapse of the Siad Barre regime, with the UN reporting that it had been subjected to genocide. For over 30 years we believe it has operated a stable, democratic state with its own government, currency, military and elections.
records.further_details: Somaliland has demonstrated all the hallmarks of a functioning state although it as yet remains unrecognised by any nation: peaceful democratic elections, rule of law, and regional stability in one of Africa's most volatile areas. We believe recognition would unlock trade, investment and development opportunities for its people, who have built this nation without international aid. We feel that the UK, with its historic ties to the region and commitment to democracy, is well-placed to lead on recognition and encourage allies to follow.

records.title: Launch the "national conversation on defence and security" by 1st August 2026
records.description: A core recommendation of the Strategic Defence Review there should be a national conversation on defence and security. Providing a proper strategy and programme, in line with the SDR recommendations, for the conversation to springboard from and be sustained by.
records.further_details: The UK has not had to consider war reaching our shores and skies for many years. We now must. The national conversation is the first step to being ready for the new type of war we see in Ukraine today, and to deter our enemies. It is a core recommendation of the SDR, accepted by the Government, and PM. But time is running out. As a regular citizen who has been to Ukraine, with teenage children, I feel our society is not properly aware and prepared for the risks ahead, and maybe not far ahead.

records.title: Require all GP surgeries to offer online triage plus phone pre-booking
records.description: We want the government to require all GP practices to keep a phone booking option alongside online triage. This could help people with inflexible work hours, caregiving roles, or long-term health needs, ensuring fair access to care for all
records.further_details: The shift to online triage has left many patients behind. People with rigid work hours, caregiving responsibilities, or chronic health conditions may struggle to access timely care. Without a phone booking option, they face delays in diagnosis, heightened stress, and worsening conditions. Fair access to NHS care must ensure that all patients, regardless of circumstance, can plan ahead and secure routine appointments. This is vital for equitable, effective healthcare for all

records.title: Fund plans to transition publicly funded schools to open source software
records.description: We call on the Government to fund the transition of primary and secondary schools away from closed source private software and operating systems (like Windows and MS Office) to what we believe are secure, low cost and open source alternatives (like Linux and LibreOffice)
records.further_details: Many schools default to teaching with expensive closed source tools and licences, which in our view limits school budgets when there are free alternatives. We believe that by teaching youths exclusively closed source software in school they continue to pay the expense of these tools into adulthood, increasing ICT costs for households and businesses. Other European nations have already begun the change, which we think improves digital sovereignty and national security. In our view, the change is inevitable, it’s just which generation will be part of it.

records.title: Review National Security Act to regulate creators sharing foreign state content
records.description: We feel the National Security Act 2023 lacks clear provisions to hold online creators accountable for sharing harmful information from foreign state actors. We call for the law to be reviewed to improve measures to tackle online creators spreading foreign state content for profit or influence.
records.further_details:
We urge the Government to ensure the review clarifies and strengthens enforcement of the National Security Act 2023 against UK-based online creators sharing hostile foreign material. 
 
We believe the law's focus on state linked groups overlooks individuals profiteering from or spreading foreign propaganda, especially on unauthorised platforms. A full review could facilitate investigations into commentators and ensure transparency and legal accountability for those profiting from foreign misinformation.

records.title: End the “Reasonable Punishment” defence for children under five
records.description: We believe it should be standard to protect children under five who should receive the highest level of safety and legal protection from harm. The “reasonable punishment” defence currently allows parents and carers to legally hit children if the force used is judged “reasonable”.
records.further_details:
We believe adults should not decide what a toddler is capable of tolerating when they cannot fully grasp their developmental needs and experiences.
 
These are vulnerable members of society, not yet able to regulate their emotions sufficiently or conceptualise the timeframe ‘next month’, and should not be expected to understand what it means when a parent hits them. Children under five would not recognise when the threshold of “reasonable punishment” has been exceeded, nor is it their responsibility to endure the long-term effects on their cognitive and emotional development, such as altered brain chemistry.

records.title: In-person checks as part of Blue Badge assessment
records.description: We want the Government to review and update the assessment and assignment of Blue Badge holders in order to ensure an in- person check as part of the process.
records.further_details: The current Blue Badge assessment does not have an in-person check as part of the process. Currently, a badge can be assigned to someone with a mental health disorder, while someone with severe mobility and balance issues might not receive one, as they can dress and bathe themselves as part of the tick box check list. We believe there needs to be visual, in-person checks so people can be better assessed in respect of need to determine fairer badge allocation. We don’t 'believe  the current checklist by itself is fit for purpose.

records.title: Fund the construction of more wheelchair accessible parks
records.description: I want the Government to fund the construction of many more wheelchair accessible parks. I believe that more such parks should be built considering there are many children who use a wheelchair in the UK.
records.further_details: Children in wheelchairs often miss out on a lot of the childhood basics and one of the main things they may miss out on is being able to go to parks as there are not enough wheelchair accessible parks. Where I live there isn't even one wheelchair accessible park and I personally believe that is outrageous. Being in a wheelchair is already difficult, never mind not having anywhere to actually go and have fun. This needs to change now.

records.title: Amend motorcycle laws to make full protective wearable gear mandatory
records.description: The law currently only mandates for motorcycle riders to wear helmets. We think this needs to change so riders are required by law to wear full protective wearable gear, including jackets, footwear, trousers and gloves.
records.further_details:
With too many accidents still taking place each year, safety for all parties is priority. Currently motorcycle riders are only mandated by law to wear a helmet when on the roads.

We believe this needs to be amended to include protective jackets, footwear, trousers and gloves as a matter of urgency to keep our loved ones safe.

records.title: Set and/or increase minimum sentences for all terrorism offences
records.description: We want the UK Government to establish and/or increase minimum sentences for all terrorism offences where appropriate. The aims are to ensure that penalties better reflect the seriousness of terrorism offences, to protect the public, and to maintain confidence in the criminal justice system.
records.further_details: Current terrorism sentencing laws should be reviewed to ensure they reflect the seriousness of modern terrorist offending. Cases such as the member of the “The Beatles”, who received an eight-year sentence after being convicted of a terrorism offence on his return to the UK, have prompted debate about whether existing penalties are sufficient. We ask the Government to review minimum sentences and strengthen the law where necessary to better protect the publics best interest and safety.

records.title: Introduce income tax relief for single occupancy households
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce an income tax relief for single occupancy households, to help single households who also pay tax, outgoings and experience the cost of living, but all on a single income.
records.further_details: In our view, single occupancy households have similar outgoings as those where both partners are working, and very often bring in double the income, yet have similar outgoings to households who only have one income. Cost of living is making our lives increasingly difficult. We call for tax relief for single occupancy households.

records.title: Call on the UN to launch a review into the location of the UN Headquarters
records.description: We ask the UK Government to propose and support, through the United Nations, an independent UN review of whether their principal headquarters should remain in New York City or be relocated to what we believe is a more neutral host state, with Geneva in Switzerland considered as an alternative.
records.further_details:
We believe the United Nations should guarantee unhindered access to its headquarters for all Member States and authorised representatives, regardless of their bilateral relations with the host nation. 
 
We believe the UN headquarters’ long-term location should be reviewed against principles such as neutrality, diplomatic access, security, international accessibility and existing UN infrastructure. Our proposal is not directed against any particular country, but seeks to ensure the UN's principal home best serves impartial, multilateral diplomacy.

records.title: Require online platforms to provide bulk removal tools for children's data
records.description: Require major social media and online platforms to give users and organisations simple bulk tools to find, restrict and permanently remove historic personal data involving images and videos of children previously posted on their accounts.
records.further_details: Many schools, charities and organisations have posted images and videos of children on their online accounts for several years. We believe there is a risk that these are being copied, scraped, manipulated into deepfakes or used in attempts to harass, exploit or blackmail children, families or organisations. Yet, we think that many platforms make large-scale review and removal of such material difficult. We think organisations need simple tools to audit and delete historic content so they can reduce risk and meet safeguarding and data-protection responsibilities.

records.title: ​Create a single payment portal for all UK road tolls and emission zones
records.description: Create a single national portal for all road tolls and emission zones. This should allow drivers to register once for automatic nationwide Direct Debit payments, or opt-in for email/SMS reminders before penalty charges are issued.
records.further_details: In our view motorists face a confusing patchwork of payment systems for tolls and emission zones. We believe most drivers intend to pay, but genuine mistakes happen when forced to juggle multiple portals. We think that if authorities can seamlessly check the DVLA to issue a Penalty Charge Notice, they can check a central system to take a Direct Debit or send a reminder first. A single national portal could help eradicate accidental non-payment, simplify travel, and reduce long-term administrative costs.

records.title: Repeal section 14 of the Public Order Act 1986 to safeguard protest rights
records.description: We want the Government to repeal section 14 of the Public Order Act 1986 because we believe it is being abused on a daily basis when people gather together to protest in peace against certain things that are going on in our country today
records.further_details: We need to get rid of section 14.  We feel it is being abused on a daily basis to stop us protesting against things that are happening in this country that we do not agree with. We think section 14 can be used as a weapon by the police to stop our protest and our freedom and God-given birth-right to peacefully protest against something that we think is injustice, and this is the case for the Metropolitan police & all police throughout the United Kingdom.

records.title: Review council tax banding rules for shared ownership homes
records.description: Review council tax banding rules for shared ownership homes so it reflects the actual share owned or the resident’s ability to pay, instead of full market value, to ensure fairness and affordability for thousands of residents in London.
records.further_details: Thousands of shared ownership residents in London, including young families and key workers, are paying excessive council tax based on full property value even though they only own a fraction. Many struggle to cover bills, mortgage, and daily costs. Parliament should ensure council tax reflects what people actually own and can reasonably afford.

records.title: Fund more registered care placements for children, ban unregistered placements
records.description: Government to fund more registered Ofsted inspected placements for children in care and ban the use of unregulated providers for all children under 18. We think increasing the number of places with regulated providers could address systemic inequities and children in care will be better protected.
records.further_details: We believe that for many years, children placed in unregulated settings were largely “out of sight”, however recent reporting has highlighted both how children are unsupported when leaving care and how some children have been sent to placements where they have been subject to physical, sexual and emotional abuse, and neglect. In our view, the insufficient oversight of some children’s care makes them vulnerable to being targeted by criminals, and that the state is not meeting its legal duty towards children & young people by allowing unregulated care providers.

records.title: Require all supermarkets to stock "Free From" foods (allergen free)
records.description: Many stores do not stock foods that are free from allergens, leading to many being unable to buy the food that's needed. Having a law in place so that all stores have this option could make them accessible to those with dietary restrictions.
records.further_details: Some stores have stopped selling "Free From" foods because they are not profitable. Profits are important, but so is being able to eat. This law could mean that people with allergies don't have to go without food like bread, flour, cereal etc, which many don't have to give a second thought to buying.

records.title: Fund student support centres in every school
records.description: We call on the Government to fund Student Support Centres in every school. Student Support Centres could be there to help students with safeguarding and mental health.
records.further_details: This could help students feel safer going to school across the country and, being based in school, would have good connections with teachers and would be more able to help solve the problem. I would like this to happen as it could help students who are struggling with school feel safer and calmer knowing they could go there when they needed it.

records.title: Fund permanent, 24-hour police patrols to protect Muslim communities
records.description: In the face of a significant rise of anti-Muslim hate crime, we ask the Government to fund permanent 24-hour police patrols in communities with significant Muslim populations.
records.further_details: We believe the Muslim community needs a visible and permanent police presence that is on patrol 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

records.title: Make Nut labelling more Visible on food packaging
records.description: Require clear, standardised nut allergy labelling on menus and food packaging, similar to vegan, vegetarian and halal labels. Nut allergies can be fatal within minutes, yet allergen information can be unclear. Clear front-facing labels could help save lives and prevent avoidable deaths.
records.further_details: People with nut allergies face life-threatening risks every day because allergen information is often unclear, inconsistent or difficult to find. Restaurants, cafés, takeaways and food packaging should clearly display nut warnings in the same visible way foods are labelled as vegan, vegetarian or halal. A simple, standardised system would help people make safer choices quickly, reduce anxiety for families and prevent avoidable allergic reactions and deaths.

records.title: Seek to negotiate with France to permanently keep the Bayeux Tapestry in the UK
records.description: We ask the Government to seek to negotiate with France to permanently keep the Bayeux Tapestry in the UK. As a masterpiece which many historians believe was created by Anglo-Saxons, depicting Norman England's birth, we think this foundation monument of our monarchy and state belongs in the UK.
records.further_details: We believe the Bayeux Tapestry is a UK treasure in exile. Many art historians agree it was stitched in England by Anglo-Saxon needleworkers, in our view the finest in medieval Europe, and its narrative captures a key moment in the birth of our modern state and royal lineage. While it will be loaned to the British Museum, we think it should remain here permanently. We call on the Government to open formal diplomatic negotiations with France to agree its permanent future in the UK, securing a vital piece of our national identity.

records.title: Make Domestic Abuse a specific offence with a minimum 2 year custodial sentence
records.description:
1. A minimum 2 year custodial sentence for anyone charged with ‘domestic abuse’. Make this a specific standalone offence.
2. Sentences for additional / related offences should not run concurrently 
3. Remove prosecution time limits.
4. Create a public Domestic Abuser Register.
records.further_details: Today, a DA-related call is made to the police every 30 seconds. What we find more shocking is that as of 2026, in England & Wales, DA in itself is not a specific punishable offence like it is in Scotland. We currently do charge for assault, non-fatal strangulation etc. Good start! However, what this means in practice though doesn’t seem as good. This fails to call out the abuse that both men and women may be taking at home. The is evidence suggesting  that 80% DA cases aren’t reported.

records.title: Mandatory back up of all government phones for senior officials and Ministers
records.description: Introduce mandatory back up of all phones of all senior officials and ministers, allowing continuously back up all communications to cloud storage. We think this will ensure that important communications are available to future inquiries, regardless of events such as the loss or theft of a phone.
records.further_details: Over the past years, ministers and senior officials have claimed they have lost their phone immediately before an important inquiry. It is also a common practice to use "disappearing messages" features of chat apps to destroy messages shortly after they are sent. In our view these practices severely erode trust in the government and the civil service. Regardless of which app is used for ministerial chats, we think these should be continuously and safely backed up to the cloud so that a proper record is kept.

records.title: Extend Awaab’s Law to leasehold homes where the council is the freeholder
records.description: Extend Awaab’s Law to protect children and vulnerable residents living in council-owned leasehold homes from damp and mould caused by defects that the freeholder (the council) is responsible for, giving them the same legal rights and protections as social housing tenants.
records.further_details: Children can become seriously ill and, in tragic cases, die from prolonged exposure to damp and mould. A child’s health, lungs and life should never depend on whether they live in a council tenancy or a council-owned leasehold home. Where councils remain responsible for structural defects, communal pipes or other freehold infrastructure, they should be under the same legal duty to investigate and remedy damp and mould for consequential damages. Every child deserves equal protection.

records.title: Create a legal route to write off coerced debt for victims of economic abuse
records.description: Coerced debt is debt an abuser forces, or tricks, a victim into taking on. It has been reported that around 1.6 million UK adults have experienced it. A conviction for the abuser does not automatically remove the debt from the victim's name.
records.further_details: We ask the Government to legislate a route to remove proven coerced debt. Only 28% of victims who disclose coerced debt get any of it written off, and 48% are left with damaged credit records. We ask the Government to create a statutory discharge route for evidenced coerced debt, modelled on the reversal of fraudulent transactions; make the currently voluntary Financial Abuse Code mandatory for lenders; and require credit reference agencies to record coercion markers and repair victims' credit files. Fraud can be reversed. We believe coerced debt needs the same route.

records.title: Fund wave-powered desalination systems
records.description: Invest in wave-powered desalination systems. With around 300 million people worldwide relying on water desalination for fresh water, we believe the Government could harness wave power and turn seawater into fresh water, providing an energy-secure, scalable solution to water scarcity.
records.further_details:
In Canada, there are already start-ups which produce wave-powered buoys that turn seawater into drinking water without electricity or fuel.
 
The Government has planned to build 9 new reservoirs by 2050 and 9 new desalination plants in England from 2040 but it has received opposition in the southwest due to cost and environmental impact concerns. 
 
We believe wave-powered desalination offers a sustainable water source. The Government should therefore invest in wave-powered desalination to tackle water shortages.

records.title: Mandate that Previous Employers Provide References for Ofsted-Regulated Roles
records.description: Require employers to provide factual references for former employees applying for Ofsted-regulated roles. Ban employers from withholding references as retaliation or unfairly blocking access to future employment.
records.further_details: Many employers require references for Ofsted-regulated roles. Some former employers refuse to provide them, unfairly preventing suitable people from finding work. We believe the law should require employers to provide a fair, factual reference.

records.title: Ban the media from reporting on cause of death until emergency services confirm
records.description: Ban media outlets from reporting on the cause of death until confirmed by emergency services, out of respect for families who may not yet know their loved one is involved — speculation can cause terrible, avoidable suffering. This includes not reporting on deaths on coastal or inland waters.
records.further_details:
Media outlets should never run stories that make claims on the cause of death and may spread speculation about incidents on coastal or inland waters —until every detail is fully confirmed by emergency services.
 
We call for this out of deep respect for families who may not even know their loved one is involved - unconfirmed reports can cause terrible, avoidable pain. We believe families have the right to be told directly by specially trained officers, properly and privately, before any information is released publicly.

records.title: Mandatory 5-year minimum sentence for carrying any bladed weapon
