records.description: We call on the Government to be firm and legislate to introduce a mandatory 5-year minimum custodial sentence for anyone found guilty of carrying any bladed weapon, including bladed weapons that are religious articles.
records.further_details: We believe knife crime is a huge problem throughout our country and following high-profile incidents in the news, I can see no reason as to why this law shouldn’t be introduced.

records.title: Mandate Nursing Associates Inclusion in Bank Shifts Across All NHS Services
records.description: Nursing Associates are regulated healthcare professionals who work alongside registered nurses across NHS services. However, in our experience, access to nursing staff banks varies between organisations, limiting opportunities for flexible working, professional development and workforce utilisation.
records.further_details: Nursing Associates are regulated healthcare professionals who work alongside registered nurses and multidisciplinary teams across NHS services. They complete accredited training and undertake a range of clinical responsibilities. However, in our experience, access to nursing staff banks varies between NHS organisations, meaning Nursing Associates with the same qualifications and skills may not have the same opportunities for bank work, flexible working, career development or service contribution.

records.title: Require pre-marriage personal rights advice before religious marriage ceremonies
records.description: Mandate people having a religious marriage ceremony without legal recognition to receive pre-marriage safeguarding and personal legal rights advice covering legal marital status, financial, housing & inheritance rights, ways to access domestic abuse support, and written consent to their marriage.
records.further_details:
People can enter religious-only marriages where the religious ceremony is only performed, without understanding that they may not have the same legal protections as spouses with a civil marriage.

This can leave people vulnerable following abuse, separation or bereavement. We want a mandatory pre-marriage process for people which informs them of their legal status, financial and housing rights, inheritance, how to access domestic abuse support, and to provide written consent to their marriage so they can make informed decisions before entering a religious-only marriage.

records.title: Mandate neurodiversity training for leaders and managers in all workplaces
records.description: I would like the government to make it mandatory that all management in the workplace undergo training in how to best support their neurodivergent staff. This would help prevent people being alienated and rendered useless. A disability does not mean we are incapable. We could be your best employee.
records.further_details: After reaching 32 years of age and having a total of 34 jobs, as a neurodivergent woman with ADHD the workplace is truly exhausting. The stigma that surrounds this, the ridicule, the closed minded native attitudes of some management and being made to feel incapable just because I require different things and not getting my needs met has made going to work day to day unbearable. Let’s try and make it so we can speak up and be open without fear of judgement and dismissal.

records.title: Integrate a lifelong dental record into the NHS App and Single Patient Record
records.description: We want the Government to integrate a lifelong, interoperable dental record into the NHS App and Single Patient Record, so relevant dental history can follow patients between providers and patients can access their dental history, treatment plans and relevant records in one place.
records.further_details: Dental records can remain fragmented when patients move between NHS, mixed and private providers. We believe dental health should be connected to the wider NHS record. An NHS Dental Passport could provide a structured dental history, treatment plans and relevant imaging, while improving NHS/private treatment transparency and supporting future NHS dental booking and access to urgent appointments.

records.title: Require social workers to wear body cameras for use as evidence in family courts
records.description: We would like social workers to legally wear body cameras. We think this would improve evidence and families' trust in the system. Social workers' decisions can lead to children being removed and put into care, affecting women's mental health.

records.title: Legalise keeping raccoons as pets
records.description: I believe that raccoons should be legal to keep as pets in households, not just in specialized, licensed settings
records.further_details: Raccoons are highly intelligent creatures that can be described as playful and engaging. These animals can be somewhat comparable to mischievous cats. Allowing raccoons to be legally kept as pets without licences or other conditions would allow people to learn more about wildlife behaviour and learn how to care for them. It would also be highly educational and people could gain a new interest in them. It could stop illegal breeding and allow them to be properly cared and looked after.

records.title: Stop the use of nuclear energy and prioritise renewable energy
records.description: The Government should phase out the use of nuclear power and urgently commit to developing renewable energy resources such as wind, solar, and hydroelectric power.
records.further_details: Nuclear power produces waste that remains hazardous for thousands of years. We believe there are safety concerns with long term disposal solutions. Renewable energy reduces reliance on imported fuels, improving the UK’s energy security and it protects against global price fluctuations. The UK is also well suited to tidal and wind energy. Not only are renewable energy sources faster to construct, they can be notably cheaper than nuclear power, which is expensive and carries risks.

records.title: Do not place wind turbines on mountains
records.description: We want the government to change planning rules to stop the placing of wind turbines on mountains to prevent the destruction of our uplands and preserve them for future generations.
records.further_details: We do not believe they are environmentally friendly, or that we need any more of them. We think the will of the public is being ignored.

records.title: Protect Vulnerable People: Fully Reinstate DoLS Safeguards
records.description: The frequent reviews of Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards help ensure that those most vulnerable in society are given as much freedom as possible. After the Supreme Court ruling on the DoLS, these safeguards need to be fully restored to help ensure people's right to autonomy and minimal restriction.
records.further_details: Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards (DOLS) are a series of checks used to ensure someone who ‘lacks capacity’ is given as much freedom as possible and that all restrictions placed upon them are in their best interests. We think the recent Supreme Court ruling takes away the rights of autonomy for the most vulnerable, including those with severe learning disabilities, complex mental health and advanced dementia.

records.title: Reform Army applications: replace online portal with in-person applications
records.description: We want the Government to replace the current online application process for the Army, which we think lacks the personal interaction needed to properly assess candidates and build confidence in their decision to serve.
records.further_details:
Replace it with in-person contact with staff which we believe would help applicants better understand Army life, values, and expectations.
 
I believe that joining the Army is a significant commitment that requires dedication and trust. During my application I found that I wanted a more direct relationship with my recruiter.
 
For those who have a strong personal desire to serve their country, the recruitment process should reflect the importance of that commitment by providing meaningful human interaction. We think this reform would strengthen recruitment and reinforce the values of service and commitment that underpin the British Army.

records.title: Require safe space training for businesses which advertise as safe spaces
records.description: Amend consumer protection laws to require businesses to provide recognised training for staff in order to market themselves as safe spaces, display safe space signage, or advertise participation in safety initiatives. Failure to do so should be classified as a misleading commercial practice.
records.further_details: We believe a safe space claim is a promise that carries real weight for LGBTQ+ people, disabled people, women, and people from marginalised communities, who calculate whether a place is safe before walking in. Any business can make that claim, through signage, posters, websites, or marketing, without training a single member of staff. The public cannot always tell the difference as many people trust these signs. When a crisis occurs, the illusion of safety can be shattered as the staff on duty may not be equipped to respond.

records.title: Fund an anti-bullying 24-hour reporting service for students
records.description: Fund an anti-bullying system for students at schools which allows students to report bullying that takes place outside of school and is open 24-hours a day.
records.further_details: We believe all schools should have this service advertised on their school websites which allow students, as well as parents or carers to access it and report any bullying taking place outside of school. It should be accessible for everyone and available 24 hours a day to report bullying to a safeguarding lead.

records.title: Fund a portal which allows crime victims to track their case
records.description: I feel crime victims have been failed for too long and it is time for change. I call on the Government to fund a victim’s portal so victims can track the progress of their case and be able to contact a police officer more easily. This could reduce victim anxiety and trauma.
records.further_details: I would like to see the Government fund the creation of a victim portal where victims can track the progress of their case and be able to contact a police officer on the case to get an update on the case, which I feel could go some way to reducing the anxiety that many victims have endured along with their trauma.

records.title: Classify bamboo as a controlled waste in the UK
records.description: Bamboo spreads rapidly & causes damage to pavements, buildings & anything that stands in its way. We believe bamboo is more dangerous than Japanese knotweed but doesn't carry the same legal implications when buying property & dealing with neighbour disputes as it isn't classified as controlled waste
records.further_details: Currently, there is no law against planting bamboo, despite the absolute chaos we feel it can cause within neighbourhoods. We believe bamboo is more dangerous than Japanese knotweed in many ways, yet it doesn't hold the same legal implications, which means bamboo doesn't get flagged on housing surveys, despite it causing considerable damage to residential dwellings. We would like the classification of bamboo to fall into line with that of Japanese knotweed.

records.title: Make repeatedly feeding another person’s pet after being told to stop an offence
records.description:
Create a specific criminal offence where a person, without lawful authority or reasonable excuse, feeds or attempts to feed another person’s pet on two or more separate occasions and the owner or lawful keeper has clearly instructed them to stop.
The offence should require proof that:

records.title: Fund free air-conditioning installation and maintenance in all homes
records.description: Fund the free installation of air conditioning in all homes, at no cost to homeowners, with the Government providing funding for installation, maintenance and operation where necessary.
records.further_details: The UK is facing more frequent heatwaves, while many homes trap heat. The rising cost of living means many people cannot afford air conditioning, leaving many vulnerable people at risk. We want the Government to fund the installation and maintenance of air conditioning in all homes, and running costs. This could protect public health, reduce heat-related illness and deaths, tackle inequality, and help our country adapt to climate change fairly.

records.title: Reform the limitation period for NHS clinical negligence claims for stillbirth
records.description: I urge the UK Government to change the law so that parents of stillborn babies caused by NHS clinical negligence are not prevented from bringing a claim solely because more than three years have passed. Families dealing with bereavement, often spend years focused on surviving.

records.title: Reverse ban on puberty blockers for Under-18s
records.description: We call on the Government to reverse the ban on puberty blockers for under-18s when clinically appropriate.
records.further_details: Young people and their families should be able to make healthcare decisions with qualified clinicians based on individual clinical need and the best available evidence, not a blanket ban. We urge the Government to review the impact of the current restrictions on young people’s wellbeing and restore access under appropriate clinical safeguards.

records.title: Assess mobile coverage by independently tested availability, speed & reliability
records.description: Coverage maps and phone indicators can show 4G or 5G while data, calls, maps and payments fail. Reliable mobile connectivity is essential for work, education, travel, public services & emergencies. Current coverage measures may not reflect congestion, indoor reception or performance at busy times.
records.further_details:
We want the Government to set statutory minimum standards for speed, availability and latency when it comes to measuring mobile coverage, instead of measuring signal alone. We want the Government’s measurement of speed, availability and latency to be independently tested, and publish the results by operator and location.
 
As part of the standards, the Government should set and publish geographic targets, deadlines to align with the standards as well as for rural areas, transport routes & urban not-spots, and penalties for operators that miss them.

records.title: Make feeding seagulls a criminal offence & introduce fines
records.description: I would like the Government to pass a law that makes feeding seagulls a criminal offence and introduce fines for people who breach this law.
records.further_details:
Feeding seagulls can unsettle people’s lives, which include impacting people’s sleep quality due to being woken up by seagulls, as well as seagulls scratching car roofs, damaging plants, and fouling in gardens, cars and paths which can act as a health hazard. In addition, it can impact people’s quality of life, especially when seagulls swoop down towards adults and children.
 
In addition, feeding seagulls can result in rats and other vermin being attracted. The feeding of seagulls has become a serious issue not just for myself, but for many residents in my local community.

records.title: Mandatory smoke-free and vape free areas at outdoor concerts
records.description: I am calling on the Government to introduce legislation requiring organisers of open-air concerts, festivals, gigs and other ticketed outdoor events to provide clearly designated, adequately sized and enforced non-smoking and non-vaping areas for attendees. At the moment, there is no legislation.
records.further_details:
This is NOT a call to ban smoking/vaping at outdoor events but rather a call for a fair system that provides designated areas for smoking and vaping while guaranteeing those who require it have genuinely smoke-free and vape free area.

In outdoor concerts and festivals, people can spend several hours in large, tightly packed crowds. Unlike on an ordinary street, attendees may not be able to move away from smokers and so be forced to inhale the fumes.

Do not leave this to organiser's discretion.

records.title: Review enforcement of Equality Act for inaccessible venues
records.description: We are concerned that in the existing Act the owner of an inaccessible venue only has to say "no it is unreasonable to alter it" to be exempt from making reasonable adjustments. Civil Court is then the only way to challenge this.
records.further_details: We want an amendment that includes provision for free arbitration prior to any court action.

records.title: Introduce a sports fund for children from low-income households
records.description: We would like the government to introduce financial support for children from low-income households who struggle to pay for costs such as club fees and equipment.
records.further_details:
Over a third (34%) of UK parents said the cost of their children's participation in sport has had a significant impact on household finances, affecting their ability to pay for necessities such as bills and food.
 
As the cost of living continues to mean households need to cut back on outgoings, sports clubs and physical activity often fall victim. However, physical activity plays a vital role in supporting children’s mental and physical wellbeing.

records.title: Fund baby hatch programme across the country to protect vulnerable newborns
records.description: We call on the UK Government to fund a programme of regulated baby hatches across the country, allowing newborn babies to be surrendered safely and anonymously in emergency situations.
records.further_details: Recent tragic cases involving newborn babies have left many people asking whether more could be done to prevent avoidable deaths. While those responsible for harming children must face the full consequences of the law, there should also be a safe, legal option available for parents who feel unable to care for a newborn.

records.title: Enact a Private Parking Code of Practice, regulator & invalid charge penalties
records.description: Enact the single government-led regulator under the Parking (Code of Practice) Act 2019, cap parking charges, ban arbitrary debt recovery fees, and mandate a statutory £20 compensation payout to motorists for successful appeals against invalid charges.
records.further_details: We feel that private parking has become a racket designed to fleece hardworking citizens through intimidation. Operators can issue baseless charges and automated rejections with zero financial risk. We think that industry claims that regulation threatens their viability prove their business model relies on ripping people off; any resulting operator failure is justified. The Government must exercise its powers under the 2019 Act and mandate a £20 payout for successful appeals, mirroring other regulated sectors, to stop frivolous ticketing.

records.title: Review Social Services and Child Protection Procedures for Section 20 powers
records.description: We call for an urgent review into the use of section 20 powers. We are concerned that there is a lack of oversight, transparent decision-making, proper recording of consent, regular reviews and accessible complaints procedures. Parents must be told how to challenge decisions and raise concerns.
records.further_details: We call for an urgent review to look at how to reform the child-protection system to prevent unnecessary separation, confusion and long-term harm to children and families. Parents must not be pressured or misled into agreeing to Section 20 accommodation. They must receive clear, accurate information, independent legal advice and a genuine explanation of their rights. We believe if they have demonstrated that no solicitor was present during the period they signed, then the application ought to be automatically denied.

records.title: Fund paid leave for parents with a child with a short-time illness
records.description: We ask the UK Government to introduce paid parental leave for parents who need to care for a child at home with a short-term illness such as flu, fever, vomiting or infection.
records.further_details:
Parents should not have to choose between caring for their child at home and losing income, using annual leave or taking unpaid time off work.
 
Parents may need several days to care for their child or follow medical advice. No parent should have to lose wages, use annual leave or take unpaid time off to care for their child because of a short-time illness.

records.title: Fund early rehabilitation care for all patients after their hospital discharge
records.description: Fund early and appropriate rehabilitation care for all patients after they are discharged from hospital, and ensure there is formal NHS, private and voluntary-sector collaboration so all available capacity is used.
records.further_details:
Access to this care should be based on clinical need and apply equally to litigation and non-litigation cases. We believe leaving hospital should be the start of recovery, not the point where support disappears.
 
Delayed rehabilitation can mean lost mobility, lost independence, greater pressure on families and people never regaining abilities they might have recovered. We want the Government to fund essential rehabilitation from discharge and require the NHS, private and voluntary sectors to work together, using all available capacity, to provide care.

records.title: Tax Relief for Families Battling Serious Illness
records.description: We want the UK Government to introduce temporary Income Tax and Council Tax relief for families affected by cancer and serious illness. Supporting family carers recognises the vital care they provide, reducing pressure on the NHS while helping families cope with rising costs of treatment and care.
records.further_details: The scheme would provide temporary Income Tax and Council Tax relief to patients and key carers during treatment. A family’s monthly costs do not disappear when someone becomes seriously ill; treatment, fuel, food, parking, travel, energy and care are added to existing bills. Most families have little or no savings or disposable income, so these extra costs can force them into debt. Tax relief would provide breathing space, recognise carers and reduce pressure and costs on the NHS.

records.title: Use emergency phone alerts to help find missing children in the UK
records.description: Create a UK Amber Alert-style system allowing police to send emergency mobile alerts to people in relevant areas when a missing child is believed to be at serious risk. Alerts should include key identifying details and information that could help the public assist police.
records.further_details: The UK already has a location-based Emergency Alerts system. I want the Government to establish a clear national protocol allowing police to use it for high-risk, missing-child cases, similar to Amber Alerts. Where police believe a child is in immediate danger, people in the relevant area should receive an alert with approved identifying details, the last known location and clear instructions on how to report information.

records.title: Make all non-working royals exempt from taxpayer-funded security
records.description: We believe UK taxpayers should not be responsible for funding security for non-working members of the Royal Family.

records.title: Reform Education and Assessment to be Accessible to Neurodivergent Students.
records.description: We ask the UK Government to review and reform education and assessment so they are accessible to neurodivergent students. Standardised exams and teaching do not always reflect how these students learn or demonstrate knowledge, so more flexible teaching and assessment methods should be available.
records.further_details: Many neurodivergent students struggle to achieve GCSEs and A-levels because standardised exams do not reflect how they demonstrate knowledge best. Some perform better through oral assessment, discussion or one-to-one supervision. Teaching should also adapt through visual, practical or discussion-based methods. We are not asking for a total overhaul, but reasonable flexibility so students can meet the same standards in accessible ways.

records.title: Require Smoking & Vaping Rooms at All Airports in Arrivals & Departures
records.description: Require all airports to provide enclosed, separately ventilated smoking and vaping rooms in both arrivals and departures. Smoking and vaping would remain prohibited elsewhere inside airport terminals, protecting non-smokers while giving passengers a designated place to smoke or vape.
records.further_details:
Airports can involve waiting times, while smokers and vapers may have limited options inside terminals. This can lead to people leaving the airport or secretly vaping in toilets.

Enclosed, separately ventilated smoking and vaping rooms would provide a controlled alternative, while protecting non-smokers and making rules easier to enforce.

They could also make UK airports more convenient for international tourists and visitors and should meet appropriate safety, hygiene and security standards.

records.title: Require social media platforms to allow users to opt out of AI-generated content
records.description: We want the Government to require social media platforms operating in the UK to provide users with a clear setting allowing them to opt out of identified AI-generated images, videos and other content in their recommended feeds.
records.further_details:
AI generated images and videos are increasingly common on social media and can be difficult to distinguish from content created by people.

Some platforms already identify and label AI generated content. We believe users should have the choice to prevent this content from appearing in their recommended feeds.

This would not ban AI generated content. It would simply give users greater control over what is recommended to them and allow those who prefer human created content to opt out.

records.title: Make allowing dog attacks on cats a specific offence
records.description: Amend the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991 to make allowing a dog to be out of control when it attacks a cat a specific offence.
records.further_details:
We believe owners rarely face prosecution if their dog attacks a cat. Update the law to enable criminal police investigations, grant courts the power to issue ownership bans, or impose prison sentences for multiple attacks.

We want grieving owners to be protected by establishing a specific offence. We are concerned that currently some dangerous owners escape prosecution. This petition seeks to reform the law to ensure proper accountability, public safety, and justice for families.

records.title: Ensure students are notified before student finance payments are blocked
records.description: I am aware of many students who had student finance payments blocked without prior notice who believe universities failed to inform them that failing to attend classes in person could trigger this issue. We demand immediate payment release, clear communication and accountability for this failure.
records.further_details: Some students have been left without essential financial support due to sudden Student Finance payment blocks. In our opinion, universities failed to clearly inform students that attendance could affect eligibility or trigger payment issues. We believe that this lack of transparency has caused financial hardship, stress, and risk of missed rent and bills. Immediate action is required to restore payments and ensure clear communication going forward.

records.title: Review powers to impose community protection warnings and notices
records.description: We call on the Government to conduct a review the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014 focused on CPWs and CPNs and associated processes. In our view, the current system does not allow procedural fairness.
records.further_details: We believe that the current CPW/CPN processes lack transparency and judicial scrutiny. We think such notices are often issued based on hearsay without allowing the accused to provide a defence. This can lead to the "weaponisation" of police powers in neighbour disputes and the automatic withdrawal of safeguarding for victims before any wrongdoing is proven. We need a review of this Act to consider whether to introduce stronger evidence tests to protect civil liberties and prevent administrative overreach by police and local councils.

records.title: Review employment pathways for newly qualified nurses
records.description: Work with NHS organisations to improve workforce planning, develop transition-to-practice initiatives, and provide equitable and prompt hiring opportunities for newly qualified nurses upon registration.
records.further_details: In order to facilitate the employment of newly qualified nurses following registration, we want the Government to collaborate with NHS organisations to enhance workforce planning and recruitment. More entry-level nursing positions should be created, supported transition-to-practice and preceptorship programs should be expanded, university-employer collaboration should be strengthened, and fair and prompt hiring procedures should be ensured. This could improve patient care, lessen a staff shortage, and help retain qualified nurses.

records.title: Make pet-sitting apps request an Animal Activities Licence for pet boarding
records.description: Require all pet-sitting apps to request an Animal Activities Licence from people or businesses carrying out pet-boarding activities before allowing listings for doggy day and boarding in a home to be posted.
records.further_details: Studies suggest that 95% of pet carers on some online platforms who offer pet boarding are unlicensed to care for animals in their own home. We feel it is a serious ongoing issue for the safety and welfare of animals.

records.title: Classify birds trapped in chimneys as an emergency hazard
records.description: Landlords and social housing providers should be required to treat trapped birds as an emergency hazard. Property owners would then be legally required to provide immediate access and urgent help to rescue birds stuck down chimneys or behind fires, ensuring these animals receive timely attention.
records.further_details: Every year, birds fall down chimneys or get stuck behind fireplaces. Because this is not legally classed as a housing hazard, landlords and social housing providers are not obligated to act quickly or grant immediate property access to wildlife rescue teams. Tenants can face delays, leaving helpless birds to suffer and die from starvation or dehydration. We need legislation to make trapping an emergency hazard, which would force housing providers to allow swift rescue access and save lives.

records.title: Require employers to have adequate cooling devices i.e. fans or aircon
records.description: I ask the government to mandate that all employers have adequate cooling devices in place i.e. fans or aircon. Consider the health implications especially the health and safety of workers in work environments without such measures.
records.further_details: While we lack a maximum working temperature, extreme heat is a serious health and safety risk. The government must mandate cooling measures, explicitly requiring businesses with built-in air conditioning to turn it on or bringing in portable fans. As temperatures inevitably rise, employee protection is vital; businesses cutting costs over worker safety cannot continue.

records.title: Increase funding for sodium-ion battery research and manufacturing
records.description: Sodium-ion batteries can reduce reliance on critical minerals such as lithium, cobalt and nickel, while supporting cleaner energy storage, renewable electricity and affordable electric vehicles. Increased investment could help the UK become a leader in next generation battery technology.
records.further_details: Lithium-ion batteries are currently the dominant technology for electric vehicles and energy storage, but extracting lithium, cobalt and nickel can have significant environmental and social impacts, including high water use, habitat disruption and pollution associated with mining operations. Sodium-ion batteries are promising because sodium is abundant, and can reduce reliance on several critical minerals. They also have strong potential for storing renewable energy from wind and solar.

records.title: Launch a review into strengthening the Hunting Act 2004
records.description: We want the Government to launch a review into strengthening the Hunting Act 2004, which includes closing loopholes that allow hunting with hounds to continue under exemptions, looking into whether current penalties are strong enough, and improving enforcement and prosecution of illegal hunting.
records.further_details: We ask the Government to review and strengthen the Hunting Act 2004 to ensure it is fully effective in preventing the illegal hunting of wild mammals with hounds. It should look into closing any loopholes that allow hunting with hounds to continue under exemptions, and improving enforcement so suspected illegal hunting can be properly investigated and prosecuted. It should also consider whether current penalties are sufficient to deter hunting activities and whether stronger sanctions are needed.

records.title: Require signs to “use both lanes until merge in point” at lane closures
records.description: To avoid congestion and confusion, we want a requirement that partial closures of lanes for roadworks should include written signs stating to use both lanes until the point at which vehicles need to merge with the open lane. We think it will avoid an unnecessary empty lane and cause less congestion.
records.further_details: We are concerned there has been confusion about when to merge into a lane before closure. We believe too many vehicles are merging into the open lane too early and thereby blocking other motorists from making use of all lanes until the point at which they need to merge. This can cause issues such as heavy unnecessary congestion, and may contribute to road rage or in some cases collisions. We think that if there is a mandatory rule to add signage stating to use both lanes until the merge in point, motorists will understand to use both lanes which will ease these issues.

records.title: Ban Isolation as a sanction in schools
records.description: The isolation sanction, which is widely used in schools, should be banned and replaced with something more effective and less psychologically distressing for students.
records.further_details:
Schools can use isolation (reflection or seclusion) as a punishment, placing 11-16 year olds in silent rooms with side partitions and limited toilet breaks. We are concerned that for some students this could cause severe distress and lasting damage including:
 
Chronic Anxiety & Panic: Triggering ongoing anxiety disorders and panic attacks in structured settings.
Depression & Apathy: Clinical depression, loss of pleasure, and a feeling that effort is meaningless.

records.title: Pause prison sentences for those moved to secure hospitals until back in prison
records.description: We call for the time spent by prisoners undergoing mental health treatment to not count towards the time spent on their sentence. We think the sentence should be paused until they are back in prison.
records.further_details: This petition is to ask that whilst any prisoner serving a prison sentence is moved to psychiatric hospital, or other similar facilities for treatment under the Mental Health Act, the prison sentence given by the judge should be paused. Ensuring that once treatment concludes they go back to prison and recommence serving the full prison sentence awarded by the judge. Time spent in a treatment facility should not count towards their jail term.

records.title: Domestic Violence Prevention Law
records.description: Provide the public with access to a Gov monitored database containing the name, DOB, and county of residence of individuals convicted of domestic abuse or other violent crimes. An offender's details would remain accessible for 10 years and would be removed if they don't re-offend during that period.
records.further_details:
The purpose of this law is to prevent domestic violence. We need prevention as much as we need protection; with easier and faster access to violent offenders and domestic abusers basic information we will be able to prevent substantially life changing crimes happening and it will promote early intervention.
The aim of this is to prevent domestic abuse and reduce repeat incidents through evidence based information and protect persons at risk.

records.title: Require parents pay for damage caused by their children and introduce penalties
records.description: Teenage vandalism and anti-social behaviour are growing concerns for many. We want the Government to require parents to pay for any damage caused by their children, and to introduce meaningful penalties for serious or repeated offences, better victim compensation, and stronger early intervention.
records.further_details: We believe parents and guardians should also play a greater role in addressing their children’s behaviour. Where appropriate and legally justified, they should be expected to accept the consequences and provide full compensation arising from deliberate damage and expenses caused by their children.

records.title: Introduce fire services medal for fighting wild fires across the UK
records.description: We call on the UK Government to introduce an official medal recognising firefighters, emergency personnel and volunteers who have shown courage and dedication while tackling devastating fires and protecting our communities. Their service and sacrifice deserve national recognition.
records.further_details: Across the UK, firefighters, emergency crews and volunteers work tirelessly during major fires, often in extremely difficult and dangerous conditions. Alongside those fighting fires directly, volunteers support communities, provide supplies and help people affected. We believe their courage, dedication and public service deserve lasting national recognition through an official UK Government medal, honouring everyone who steps forward when communities need them most.

records.title: Ban charities from posting donation bags through letter boxes unless requested
records.description: Ban all charity shop bags from being delivered to homes. These generate lots of plastic waste and sometimes they are posted through letter boxes regardless of need or want. We think this would save plastic waste and prevent distressing dogs.
records.further_details: These bags should only work on request to prevent plastic waste.

records.title: Pilot a four-day school week in England
records.description: I am calling for the Government to permit and independently evaluate four-day school-week trials, while maintaining educational standards and protecting pupils who need additional school-based support.
records.further_details: This isn't about having a day off school. It's about organising the school week differently so pupils have time for independent learning and wellbeing while still having access to school.

records.title: To legally require that everyone be registered with an NHS counsellor
records.description: Make it a legal requirement that everyone must be assigned and registered to a counsellor on the NHS. Many people are already registered with a GP. We want everyone to be registered with a counsellor too.
records.further_details:
We believe this would:
1. Reduce stigmatism and anxiety around asking for support
2. Help everyone get support more easily
3. Help family and friends know where to find support for the person needing support without the barriers of searching for support or not knowing who is the right person to approach
4. Help increase openness to talk with someone before things get very serious.

records.title: Review guidance recommending 2 scans to confirm miscarriage
records.description: Review guidance recommending 2 scans to confirm miscarriage. 2 scans a week apart should not be needed if the pregnancy has stopped more than 4 weeks ago.
records.further_details: We think a second scan shouldn't be necessary when the pregnancy has stopped so long ago. This may prolong the couple's trauma and pain, not allowing them to grieve their loss.

records.title: Support the construction of public and private bomb shelters for our citizens
records.description: In light of the rising threat of conflict, we believe it is imperative that we prioritise the safety and security of our citizens.
records.further_details: One avenue through which the Government can enhance public safety is by supporting and/or funding directly the construction of accessible public and personal bomb shelters across our nation

records.title: Strengthen legal protections for SMEs when using B2B contracts
records.description: Introduce new statutory protections for SMEs against predatory B2B contract practices by banning non cancellable terms and automatic renewals. Cap penalties, and ban aggressive debt collection, while requiring transparency, cooling off periods, and fair dealing obligation.
records.further_details: We are concerned that many SMEs suffer financial harm each year from misleading B2B contract practices that exploit gaps in UK law, leaving them unprotected against misleading sales tactics, hidden terms, non cancellable provisions, punitive fees, and aggressive enforcement. These practices can cause business failures and financial distress, making urgent reform essential to ensure fairness, transparency, and proportionality in SME contracting.

records.title: Abolish employer National Insurance contributions
records.description: Not to be confused with Employee PAYE or Employee National Insurance contributions, we want the Government to abolish Employer National Insurance contributions as we believe it is a direct tax placed on businesses for each employed person based and on their employee’s earnings.
records.further_details:
It is currently set at – 15% rate for each employee and charged to the business. We believe that if the Government are serious about increasing employment, it should let employers employ people without requiring them to pay this additional tax.
 
We believe it is a direct tax that employing businesses must pay on top of employees’ wages. We believe we should help businesses employ more workers without penalising the business for each worker they employ. If a business is successful, it could instead pay more corporation tax, but sadly, many businesses are failing due to current tax burdens.

records.title: Exclude Commission & Incentive-based Pay from National Minimum Wage Calculations
records.description: Change the law so base salary alone meets National Minimum Wage. Employers now can pay a base wage below the legal rate using earned commission to top up the difference. Staff often feel they have to work more just to reach the legal baseline rather than commission serving as a reward on top of it.
records.further_details: Amend regulations so commission is excluded from minimum wage calculations. Some employers legally pay base wages below the legal rate, using commission to cover the shortfall. Some employers claim that this serves to motivate staff, but it can feel like exploitation. If a worker cannot fill the gap with commission, the  extra effort deployed yields zero reward since the boss must top up the amount of pay anyway. We feel this destroys motivation as commission should be a reward on top of a guaranteed baseline, not a subsidy for employers.

records.title: Ban social media and smartphone use for under 16s
records.description: We want to Put Childhood Before the Scroll and  Campaign for a safer childhood by calling ion the Government to ban smartphone and social media use for under-16s.
records.further_details: We believe children deserve more time for real friendships, outdoor play, family, sport, creativity and learning — not endless scrolling. We want the Government to help protect childhood from the harms of smartphones and social media. We support age restrictions for under-16s to help promote real-life connections, play, sport and wellbeing.

records.title: Fund work experience placements for all young people
records.description: Too many young people cannot access meaningful work experience because employers do not offer enough placements. We want the Government to fund grants to medium and large employers to provide work experience opportunities to help tackle youth unemployment and skill gaps.
records.further_details: Work experience can help young people develop employability skills, confidence and career awareness. However, many students struggle to secure placements because many employers do not offer opportunities. This can leave young people feeling disheartened and unprepared for the world of work. We want the Government to provide funding to encourage or incentivise medium and large employers to provide meaningful work experience opportunities to help tackle youth unemployment, skills gaps and improve social mobility.

records.title: Fund a national awareness campaign for drivers about emergency vehicle safety
records.description: Fund a national awareness campaign in the form of adverts on how to respond to an approaching emergency vehicle.
records.further_details: We believe there has been a clear deterioration in the overall standard of driving when appropriately responding to an approaching emergency vehicle. Many drivers seem to not understand the need to pull over to the left to allow emergency vehicles to safely pass, or that stopping on blind bends or continuing to drive but slowing slightly is both dangerous and unhelpful. We feel the only way to improve this is through widespread education for new drivers and those already on our roads.

records.title: Require A&E to inform social services if adopted child visits twice in 6 months
records.description: Make it mandatory for hospitals to alert social services when a child visits any A&E department in England more than once with a serious injury in the first 6 months of an adoption placement. A full explanation and medical review must then be conducted by social services.
records.further_details: In our view this is about safeguarding children who have been recently adopted, and to ensure that hospitals share information not only with each other but with social services too. We think it’s not only about sharing information but also ensuring that an appropriate follow up and investigation is conducted too.

records.title: Require weekly physical examinations of babies in local authority care
records.description: We want the UK Parliament to pass legislation that requires nurses to carry out weekly physical examinations of all babies who are living under the care of local authorities, including babies in the foster and adoption system.
records.further_details: We call for weekly examinations of babies in care to help reduce the risk of child abuse by foster or adoptive parents.

records.title: Ban the sale of rabbits as domestic pets
records.description: We want the Government to ban the sale of rabbits as domestic pets. We feel that too many rabbits are neglected, kept in unsuitable hutches, and abandoned.
records.further_details: Rabbits can be classified as exotic pets due to their specialised care needs and unique physiology and need to be looked after correctly. They are bought mainly for children and then they can get neglected as the novelty wears off. Pet shops often sell hutches not fit for purpose, and rabbits can often be kept in them 24/7. We believe there are far too many rabbits needing to be re-homed because people realise they are not easy or cheap to care for properly.

records.title: Empower councils to penalise landlords and seize crime-linked commercial units
records.description: We call on the Government to grant local authorities statutory powers to penalise commercial property owners who repeatedly allow premises to harbour criminal activity or fall into severe decay. This must include expedited compulsory purchase powers to repossess and repurpose such units.
records.further_details: Temporary closure orders and small fines against transient operators fail to deter illegal activity on our high streets. Commercial landlords currently face minimal liability when their properties host persistent crime or rot into dangerous disrepair. Elevating penalties for negligent property owners and giving councils the authority to seize chronically offending premises will disrupt organised crime, restore town centres, and give legitimate independent businesses a fair opportunity.

records.title: Require NHS verification before issuing Baby Loss Certificates
records.description: Require applicants for Baby Loss Certificates to undergo NHS verification before a certificate is issued. This should help prevent fraudulent applications, protect the integrity of the scheme, and ensure certificates are only issued to those who genuinely meet the eligibility criteria.
records.further_details: Baby Loss Certificates are intended to recognise the loss experienced by bereaved parents. I believe the current application process should include full verification through NHS records before a certificate is issued. This should help prevent fraudulent applications, protect the integrity of the scheme, and ensure the certificates remain meaningful for families who have genuinely experienced pregnancy or baby loss.

records.title: Review the quality and oversight of Child DLA decision-making
records.description: Review the Child Disability Living Allowance (DLA) decision process, including how decisions are assessed and ensure they are regularly independently overseen. A review should include considering initial decisions, Mandatory Reconsiderations (MR) and tribunal outcomes.
records.further_details:
We call for such a review to consider:
• Whether child DLA decisions accurately reflect the evidence and give clear reasons to claimants.
• Where decisions change at MR or tribunal, examine why and whether issues could have been resolved earlier.
• Recurring problems and inform improvements using root-cause analysis.
• Whether changes improve first-time decision quality and reduce avoidable disputes and stress for families.
• Lessons from changed decisions should feed back into future decision-making.

records.title: Require food delivery companies to employ & give workers more legal protections
records.description: Require food delivery companies to employ deliverers, not classify their workers as self-employed and extend employed worker rights to them. Mandate food delivery companies to provide workers with insurance, training and safety equipment, e.g. lights, helmets & high visibility clothing.
records.further_details:
We think this change could result in many benefits, which include creating a safer working environment, having fewer people working illegally in the sector and making these jobs safer and more attractive for young people. It could also increase the price of junk food and therefore reduce obesity rates and other associated health issues.
 
It could also ensure better accountability within the food delivery sector and reduce the number of couriers who are using food delivery as a cover for other acts.

records.title: Mandate car manufacturers to install ghost immobilisers as standard
records.description: Legislate to require all car manufacturers to install an industry- and insurance-approved ghost immobiliser system on every new vehicle sold in the UK prior to first registration. This will place more responsibility for ensuring vehicle security with the vehicle manufacturer rather than the consumer
records.further_details: We believe automotive companies adopted keyless entry systems for their cars without sufficient consideration of the insecurity of these systems. This decision has created multiple new attack vectors which the motorist now must defend themselves against (key relay attacks, key cloning), often requiring expensive modifications to property or cars. Car makers should fix this issue. Ghost immobilisers ensure only the owner can start a vehicle, and should be fitted as standard.

records.title: Change UK law to recognise ownership of purchased digital products
records.description: Change UK consumer law to establish that consumers legally own the digital copies of digital products they purchase outright, rather than merely receiving a licence to use them.
records.further_details: More products are now sold online instead of as physical copies. When someone buys a physical product, they own the copy they bought, even though they do not own the copyright. Digital products can instead be sold as a licence, meaning the buyer may not legally own what they paid for and the publisher may be able to withdraw access under its terms. We believe buying a digital product outright should give the buyer ownership of that copy.

records.title: Launch a review into improving women’s hormonal & reproductive care in NHS
records.description: Launch a review into improving NHS care for women’s hormonal and reproductive health by ensuring better training, timely assessment and access to evidence-based treatment for Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD), pregnancy, miscarriage, postnatal health, mental health and menopause.
records.further_details: Women’s hormonal health can have a profound impact on physical and mental wellbeing, yet symptoms may be overlooked or treated in isolation. This can be particularly difficult during pregnancy, after miscarriage, postnatally and during menopause. Better training, joined-up care and access to evidence-based treatment could help women receive the right support at the right time.

records.title: Legally require owners exchange details when their dog attacks another pet
records.description: Make it a legal requirement for anyone in charge of a dog that attacks or injures another person’s pet to provide their name, address and relevant insurance details. If they refuse, there should be a process for the police or local authority to provide or ascertain the details needed.
records.further_details:
When a dog attacks another pet, the victim’s owner can be left facing significant veterinary bills for injuries they did not cause, while being unable to pursue the other party if their details are withheld. 
 
As with a road traffic accident, there should be a clear duty to exchange details. If an owner refuses, there should be a legal route to obtain the information needed to pursue veterinary costs.

records.title: Compensate UK citizens affected by 9-month carry over passport rule
records.description: Compensate affected UK citizens unable to travel/lost money despite passports expiry dates being valid due to the Government’s decision to carry over months from previous passports, whilst EU/Schengen rules stipulate that a passport can only be valid for 10 years from issuing.
records.further_details: Until 2018 UK passport rules were to carry over additional months from previous passports, which would lead to a passport being valid for more than 10 years. However, EU/Schengen Area countries do not allow travel on a passport if it is more than 10 years since it was issued. In our experience, this has, and continues to have, daily impact on hundreds of UK citizens who have been turned away at Airports and lost their money. Many have and continue to be unable to claim back from insurance companies, credit cards or Airlines. Millions may continue to be impacted by this.

records.title: Extend Widowed Parent’s Allowance until children leave university/apprenticeship
records.description: Change the rules so widowed parents do not lose Widowed Parent’s Allowance when Child Benefit ends because their children start university or an apprenticeship. We believe support should continue while children remain financially dependent.
records.further_details: Widowed Parent’s Allowance ends when Child Benefit stops because a child starts university or an apprenticeship. Yet these children may remain financially dependent. We want the Government to review the rules so bereaved parents do not lose support while supporting dependent children.

records.title: Remove Wels catfish non-native invasive status, review restrictions on stocking
records.description: We want the Government to reclassify Wels catfish (Silurus glanis) from "non-native invasive" to "non-native" only, similar to Common Carp. Alongside this, review and update the Import of Live Fish Act 1980 to allow more flexible licensing for stocking in managed, low-risk fisheries across the UK.
records.further_details: Wels catfish have been in UK waters since 1880. Despite their "invasive" classification, they have existed in managed fisheries for over 140 years without, in our view, damaging local ecosystems. We believe they provide a significant economic boost to the UK angling industry and rural economies. Following the British Record Fish Committee’s recent decision to accept a Wels record, we think that our proposed change to classification would better reflect their status as a valued sporting fish rather than an invasive alien species.

records.title: Introduce strategy to ensure access to public services for vulnerable people
records.description: We want the Government to introduce a strategy to ensure public services are accessible and coordinated for vulnerable people. This includes improving communication between departments and ensuring those without digital access are not excluded from housing, support, or legal rights.
records.further_details: Vulnerable people, including those who are homeless or experiencing domestic abuse, often face complex systems requiring repeated applications across multiple departments. These systems often assume access to email, phones, and stable housing, which many do not have. This can result in exclusion from basic support and rights. A more accessible and joined-up system is needed to protect fairness and dignity.

records.title: Voluntary scheme for armed forces to assist civilian emergency services
records.description: I propose a voluntary scheme enabling armed forces personnel to routinely support emergency services. Their skills could assist the police, fire services, and the NHS, helping to ease pressure, improve response, and strengthen overall service stability during times of increased demand.
records.further_details: Our emergency services must receive the full support they need to operate effectively. While there are ongoing assurances that improvements are being made, we think progress is not happening quickly enough. This is reflected in persistent challenges such as rising crime, incidents of arson, and the continued strain on the NHS. These issues affect communities daily and highlight the urgent need for meaningful, lasting change and faster, more visible improvements across all emergency service sectors.

records.title: Do not allow polling stations in schools while children are in attendance
records.description: Given the severe UK terror threat level effective April 30th, we call on the Government to not allow polling stations to be located in schools while children are in attendance.
records.further_details:
We believe that doing so allows unvetted individuals access to school facilities and raises significant safety concerns for the children.

In our view this situation poses a significant risk to the safety of our children, particularly given the current severe threat of terrorism.

records.title: Abolish the requirement for spousal consent from the Gender Recognition Act 2004
records.description: Currently, the Gender Recognition Act requires married applicants to obtain a spouse’s consent or for the marriage to be ended to receive a full Gender Recognition Certificate. We believe this creates a spousal veto that can undermine individual autonomy and be used to delay legal recognition.

records.title: Abolish compulsory jury service for those over state pension age
records.description: Allow all pensioners the option of whether or not they attend jury service. After all the UK population is growing at a steady pace thus creating a larger pool of working age individuals to be called upon. Let pensioners enjoy their retirement.

records.title: Make it the law for every town to have a lido.
records.description: Too many young people die every year, trying to cool off by taking risks entering dangerous bodies of water. This is bound to increase as summers get hotter, the number of existing lidos decrease and much of avaliable natural water sites are polluted. Available lidos would help.
records.further_details: We feel safety messages issued after such deaths are not deterring young people from risking their lives in hot weather. We believe investing in new lidos would be an investment in saving lives as well as improving public health and an opportunity to build additional architectural character in our towns. Adjustable cover could facilitate year round use and provide a business opportunity.

records.title: Require Local Authorities to Quantify EHCP Hours
records.description: Mandate local authorities to quantify 1:1 support hours in Section F of EHCPs.
records.further_details:
Amend the Children and Families Act 2014 to explicitly forbid Local Authorities from issuing unquantified EHC Plans on the basis that professional reports do not state specific hour figures. Introduce mandatory penalties.
 
We believe councils can exploit a loophole to avoid funding 1:1 support. In draft EHCPs, they can omit specified hours—like 1:1 TAs—claiming they cannot lawfully add a figure if specialists didn't state a number. We are concerned that this could violate High Court case law (L v Clarke and Somerset), which rules it is the Council's job to translate needs into specific hours. We feel that unquantified plans unlawfully dump the financial burden onto schools, leaving vulnerable children unsafe. We want strict regulation to stop this systemic failure.

records.title: National Minimum Wage to be £30,000 pa by September 2026
records.description: I say, National Minimum Wage £30k a year, period.
records.further_details: £30k pa NATIONAL minimum wage. Not much more to it.

records.title: STOP APPLYING COMMERCIAL WASTE LAWS TO HOME BAKERS AND SOLE TRADERS
records.description: home based sole traders are not corporations, we need to stop penalising small volume businesses, are stunting their growth.
records.further_details: Home-based sole traders operating from residential addresses already contribute to household waste collections. We believe applying commercial trade waste requirements to people running small businesses from home is disproportionate and unworkable. A home baker fulfilling two orders a year faces the same legal waste obligations as a commercial restaurant yet generates a fraction of the waste. This creates an unfair financial burden that could push compliant micro-businesses to either operate illegally/close

records.title: Review options for homeowners/landlords to combat aggressive seagulls
records.description: Review whether homeowners/landlords should have easier access to effective pest control methods such as nest removal and culling of young where necessary, such as a proven health and safety threat to residents and pets.
records.further_details:
Currently residents may have their hands tied when seagulls nest and could be simply told to avoid the area.

We learnt how important people's gardens are during covid. Losing a safe outdoor sanctuary at home can be extremely detrimental to some people's mental health.

Where spikes and roof deterants have proven unsuccessful prevention, we petition the goverment to allow for the removal of seagull nest from all domestic properties as a matter of health and safety.

records.title: Fund Meningitis B (MenB) Vaccine for all university students
records.description: In June 2026, the NHS only offered the MenB vaccine to students starting university in the coming autumn. We believe university students of all years should be offered the vaccine, particularly those who study medicine, nursing, or veterinary studies.

records.title: Introduce a maximum safe temperature for Early Years settings
records.description: Introduce a legal maximum indoor temperature for nurseries and early years settings. Require providers to take action when temperatures become unsafe, to protect babies, young children and staff during periods of extreme heat.
records.further_details: Many nurseries and early years settings have small windows, poor ventilation and no air conditioning. During heatwaves, indoor temperatures can become uncomfortably high, and fans alone are often not enough. Babies and children under five are particularly vulnerable to overheating and dehydration, and some are unable to communicate when they feel unwell. The Government should introduce a maximum safe indoor temperature and require action when this is exceeded.

records.title: Enact a 20% tax on all taxable UK earnings made by non-resident tennis players
records.description: Enact a fixed 20% income tax rate on all income that is taxable in the UK by non-resident tennis players. We believe this will attract top players to UK tournaments, boosting competition, spectator revenue, and broader economic activity.
records.further_details:
UK tax law can result in non-resident professional tennis players paying income tax at rates up to 45% and uniquely taxes a share of players' global sponsorship income too. Top players have avoided UK warm-up tournaments as a result.
We want a simple, final 20% tax rate on all earnings that are taxable in the UK for non-resident players. This could attract more top players, improve competition, and generate far more tax revenue from venues, hotels and fans than is lost from players.

records.title: Replace multiple forms of taxation with a simple universal income tax
records.description: We want the Government to reform the taxation system, replacing forms of taxation such as Capital Gains Tax, VAT, Stamp Duty, Inheritance Tax, Business Rates, National Insurance & Council Tax, with a simple universal tax on income with the primary aim being to make tax simpler & fairer.
records.further_details: We believe growing inequality, stagnating growth, and a rising cost of living are fuelling deep societal problems across the UK. No political party has provided us with a clear, cohesive vision to fix our fundamental economic problems, nor have they fully addressed the growing sense of unfairness in the system. Small changes and additions to the system usually increase complexity and inevitably result in unintended consequences and loopholes. Instead the system needs radical change.

records.title: Require and fund more structured support for 1-4 year olds with SEND needs
records.description: We believe our Councils are failing our most vulnerable children 1-to-4-year-olds with developmental delays because the council's SEND support "umbrella" rarely kicks in until primary school. We want the Government to ensure there is funded provision for early yeas SEND children.
records.further_details: We believe that funding shortages have left early-years provision in crisis. Children without a formal diagnosis can face a chaotic maze, while overstretched nurseries are sometimes left drowning without the council funding needed to hire extra staff. We need Immediate funding for nursery staff to be made available by the Government through councils, along with clear healthcare pathways for undiagnosed children & fast-tracked early-years EHCPs.

records.title: Ensure Consumer Rights to Digital Material & Introduce Refund Rights
records.description: Introduce consumer rights to retain purchased digital material & prevent platforms from removing access to it after store closures by requiring protection of digital accounts. We also call for a statutory refund rights, when what in our view us unfair terms, remove paid content without compensation.
records.further_details: Digital purchases such as games, films, TV shows, e-books and software can be removed because of licensing disputes, store closures or account deletion, even after consumers have paid for them. We call on the UK Government to strengthen consumer rights by protecting purchased digital content, guaranteeing continued access where possible, introducing fair statutory refund rights, protecting digital accounts, and preventing unfair contract terms.

records.title: Fund skin removal surgery on the NHS following weight loss
records.description: Fund reconstructive skin removal surgery on the NHS for patients who have achieved substantial weight loss and are suffering significant physical or psychological harm because of excess skin.
records.further_details: Excess skin after major weight loss can cause significant physical and psychological harm, including reduced mobility, skin problems, anxiety, low self-esteem and social isolation. Research shows body-contouring surgery can improve quality of life and wellbeing. Current NHS access is inconsistent and often depends on where a person lives. We believe recovery from obesity should include access to reconstructive surgery when excess skin causes significant harm.

records.title: Fund an official register of disability status to prove eligibility for rights
records.description: Please establish a government-managed register, or similar official scheme, to help ensure disabled people can more easily demonstrate their eligibility for the rights, reasonable adjustments, and protections provided under the Equality Act, reducing unnecessary barriers and promoting equal access.
records.further_details: There is no official government register for disabled people. Some employers ask whether a person is "registered as disabled", even though no such register exists. We believe this can create confusion and make it harder for people, particularly those with non-visible disabilities, to access reasonable adjustments and exercise their rights under the Equality Act 2010.

records.title: Create an independent oversight body for social services
records.description: In the same way that police forces must refer themselves to the Independent Office  for Police Conduct, which investigates deaths or serious harm to an individual from police contact, we want the same for social services.
records.further_details:
We call upon the Government to establish an independent oversight body akin to the IOPC for social service workers to refer themselves for deaths or serious harm to individuals who social service workers have come into contact within the work done by social services. 
 
We believe that in doing so, it could enable vital recording and investigation of these deaths or serious harm, foster a culture of prevention, and make way for an up-to-date, responsible, accountable and transparent oversight body.

records.title: Stop the mandatory fitting of any cameras in new cars and vans
records.description:
Stop the mandatory fitting of any cameras in new cars and vans.
We call on the Government to reject all proposals requiring cameras (driver-facing or otherwise) in new vehicles and focus instead on non-intrusive road safety measures that respect civil liberties.
records.further_details:
The Government is consulting on mandating driver monitoring cameras in new vehicles that track eye movement, head position and behaviour. Similar rules apply in the EU.
We believe this is unacceptable surveillance. It invades privacy and has insufficient proven safety benefits.
We urge the Government to reject all camera mandates and focus on proportionate, non-intrusive road safety measures that respect civil liberties and driver freedom.

records.title: Make 16-17 year olds eligible for child train fare discounts, without a railcard
records.description: We want 16 and 17 year olds to be made eligible for the same child train fare discounts as those aged 5-15, and train operators required to provide them with these discounts, without the need to purchase a railcard to continue receiving child discounts.
records.further_details: 16 to 17 year olds do not automatically receive the same child train fare discounts as those aged 5-15. This results in additional costs even though most 16 and 17 year olds still go to some form of education. This could be sixth form, college or something else but in any case many students will still have to use public transport to get there, and some of them trains, but now the costs are higher for them. We aim to have them receiving the same child train fare discounts.

records.title: Review Ideological Neutrality in UK Public Bodies and Public Sector Services
records.description: We call on Parliament to launch a public inquiry into ideological neutrality and the use of evidence-based standards and transparency in public-sector policy and training. We are concerned that for example Critical Social Justice ideology has become increasingly common.
records.further_details: We believe that partial views such as Critical Social Justice ideology would undermine impartial governance, evidence-based standards and public trust. Such approaches risk introducing divisive, contested concepts like equity, decolonisation, gender identity policy and elevating "lived experience" above testable evidence. We are worried these ideological perspectives may now widely shape Civil Service training, school curricula, police response and NHS guidance.

records.title: Fund the NHS to provide all health-related services free at the point of use
records.description: We demand the Government to provide NHS funding to ensure all services are free to all and are based on clinical need rather than an individual’s ability to pay. We want the NHS to be free at the point of use for all for any medical, mental, age-related, optician and dental services
records.further_details:
We believe it’s time to recognise the holistic nature of all health aspects, from mental and physical health to elderly care, providing robust services that cover these areas comprehensively.
 
Some health services, such as dental and optician care, require fees or private contributions, making them less accessible to many. We believe expanding the NHS to cover these areas comprehensively could ensure that healthcare needs are met equitably across the population.

records.title: Reinstall a national physical warning siren network as a civil defence backup
records.description: We call on the Government to reinstate and modernise a nationwide physical siren network to act as a resilient, analogue backup to the digital Emergency Alerts system.
records.further_details:
The current UK Emergency Alerts system relies entirely on mobile networks. While efficient, we are concerned that digital infrastructure is highly vulnerable to cyber attacks, severe power grid failures, and Electromagnetic Pulses (EMPs) that could instantly disable mobile networks.
 
Many European nations maintain physical horn or siren networks as a vital civilian safety layer. We believe the UK requires a robust, non-digital fail-safe to alert the public of immediate homeland threats when digital and cellular communications fail.

records.title: Call for UN action to protect all children from hazardous sea crossings
records.description: Propose a UN initiative under the Convention on the Rights of the Child to require member states to prevent minors, regardless of origin, from being placed on unseaworthy vessels and subjected to life-threatening sea crossings, treating maritime child endangerment as a global safeguarding crisis.
records.further_details:
Every child has a fundamental right to safety, regardless of nationality or background. Placing children onto unseaworthy vessels across hazardous shipping lanes puts them in extreme danger, even when departing safe nations.
​Under the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, states must safeguard children's right to life. The UK Government should lead at the UN to ensure member states actively intervene to prevent maritime child endangerment at launch points.

records.title: Give victims the right to view a recent photograph of their convicted offender
records.description: Give victims of serious sexual and violent offences the right to request to privately view a recent photograph of their convicted offender during their custodial sentence, with appropriate safeguards. Victim choice should matter, not only immediate risk or proximity to release.
records.further_details: Victims can lose so much control through crime and the justice process. Some never want to see their offender again; others need to know what they look like. Current decisions can focus on risk management or approaching release. Victims should have greater choice throughout a sentence, including for reassurance and reducing uncertainty. A recent photo could be viewed privately and securely, without providing a copy, with appropriate safeguards.

records.title: Require safe interim child contact when contact stops before a court decision
records.description: Require safe interim contact, including supported or supervised contact, when one parent stops contact before a Family Court decision without an established safeguarding reason. Contact costs should also be addressed so children maintain relationships during court delays.
records.further_details: When parents separate, a child may lose contact with one parent before a Family Court hearing. Proceedings can take months, disrupting important relationships. Where there is no established safeguarding concern, there should be a prompt process for safe interim contact, including supported or supervised contact where appropriate. The Government should ensure agencies consider this and address reasonable costs.

records.title: Require socialising activities to be offered to people in care homes
records.description: The Government should require care homes to offer certain activities and opportunities for the elderly to socialise while always being taken care off.
records.further_details: Activities should be designed using an understanding of how not letting them have opportunities to socialise can lead to loneliness which can also impact bonds with family and friends leading to a great upset.

records.title: Fund a national road safety campaign to protect children
records.description: We want the UK Government to fund a nationwide road safety campaign to protect children. It should teach drivers, parents, and children about safe behaviour near roads, highlight the risks faced by young pedestrians and cyclists, and encourage safer driving near schools and residential areas.
records.further_details: We want every child to feel safe travelling to school. A national campaign could help keep us and our friends safe. Every day, children are killed or injured on UK roads. Awareness of road safety rules and hazards can save lives. A national campaign could provide consistent messaging across the country, stress careful driving near schools, and give practical safety tips. The Government can help prevent accidents and make roads safer for every child.

records.title: Launch a review into the NHS 111 out of hours service
