records.description: Launch a review into the NHS 111 out of hours service which investigates the following proposals: only using call handlers for contact details & basic problems, first line assessments by GPs, and nearby assessment centres and home visits for those who can’t attend for advice / treatment.
records.further_details:
The review should also look into an easy call-back option if a condition changes. We feel the 111 service has failed to provide an appropriate alternative for GP services. We believe the triage system is slow and not operated by people with clinical knowledge, which can delay appropriate responses. 
 
A clinician could assess a situation much faster and advise on an appropriate response to a problem, especially if it’s complex. You may need to be very insistent to avoid repeat call handlers’ questioning. Delays could result in death.

records.title: Eliminate wine duty for pubs and restaurants and help socialising
records.description: UK consumers pay some of the highest wine taxes in Europe, with duty on a standard bottle of wine now reaching c£3.33 (February 2026). Applying this equally to wine bought for home use & wine bought to serve in pubs creates a massive price gap between supermarket home drinking & socialising in pubs
records.further_details:
Reduce wine duty for hospitality venues to match European levels like Italy. We think high prices fuel isolation by making socialising unaffordable, forcing people to drink alone. We believe lowering the tax burden will:
 
Boost Mental Health: Make pubs affordable community hubs again.
 
Promote Safety: Encourage drinking in regulated social settings over high-volume home consumption.
 
Save Pubs: Increase footfall to stop venues closing and support the UK economy.

records.title: Review how law distinguishes between BDSM/CNC and sexual assault
records.description: Review the legal framework which distinguishes BDSM from sexual assault. This framework should guide police and courts in assessing consent, including whether it was freely given, ongoing and could be withdrawn and outline prior discussion, agreed boundaries and absence of coercion or incapacity.
records.further_details:
The aim is to ensure that BDSM or CNC (consensual non consent) cannot be used to obscure or justify assault, while providing professionals with clear standards to assess these cases fairly and consistently.
As established in R v Brown [1993], consent is not a general defence to actual bodily harm, yet we are concerned that current legal ambiguity makes it difficult for the justice system to distinguish between genuine consensual BDSM practices and cases of domestic abuse or assault.

records.title: Remove day 1 Statutory Sick Pay and revert back to 3 day qualification
records.description: We feel this is a poorly conceived plan that is already getting abused from Day 1.
records.further_details: Revert back to 3 days qualification. We believe this system IS and WILL be abused on a regular basis and considering how much business are taxed currently and the state of the country its yet another kick to employers who pay the majority of all income tax. Surely GOV understand that it’s too much of a cost burden to volume employers?

records.title: HMRC to itemise everything on self-assessment tax payment request
records.description: We call on the HMRC to set out more details on self-assessment tax payment requests. We think HMRC should explain what it is that a self-employed person owes in detail.
records.further_details: In our view, when HMRC asks self-employed people to pay money, notices should clearly explain what the charge is for, not just include a overall SA BALANCING CHARGE. Detail should set out how it was calculated, which tax year it relates to, and any penalties or interest added.

records.title: Include hair colour as a protected characteristic under the Equality Act 2010
records.description: I want justice and respect for people with ginger hair in the UK, which I feel have suffered from an acute problem with discrimination in this country. I call the Government to include hair colour as a protected characteristic under the Equality Act 2010 to ensure this.
records.further_details: I want respect and protection for future generations so they will not suffer the way I did.

records.title: Require Driving Assessments for all licence holders every 5 years
records.description: We currently don't have general regular assessments for people after they pass their driving test but we believe they should have to sit an assessment every 5 years to keep up-to-date with their skills.
records.further_details: We believe driving has got so bad nowadays that people think it's acceptable to go over speed limits, overtake in dangerous areas and just basically take too many risks. As a driving instructor I see so many people taking risks and I have been hit 5 times over the past 4 years. We believe that having an assessment every 5 years will help drivers to keep up-to-date with all the road rules and to become better and more confident.

records.title: Review service charge transparency laws and measures to enforce them
records.description: Laws should ensure freeholders, managing agents and estate management companies provide itemised accounts, supporting documents and estimate breakdowns with service charge demands, within fixed legal deadlines and with penalties for non-compliance
records.further_details: Leaseholders and homeowners often pay service charges for management, insurance, repairs, maintenance, reserve funds, utilities, security, concierge services, shared facilities and major works without clear evidence of how costs have been calculated, allocated or approved. We believe service charge demands should always include itemised accounts or estimate breakdowns, invoices, contracts, tender evidence and commission details, within fixed legal deadlines and backed by penalties for non-compliance.

records.title: Raise the minimum wage for under 18 year olds to £10 per hour
records.description: Raise the minimum wage for all workers under 18 to at least £10 per hour to ensure they are paid fairly for their work and to help with the rising cost of living as many 16 and 17-year-olds are financially independent and struggle to cover essential living costs on the current minimum wage.
records.further_details: Many 16 and 17-year-olds work in jobs with the same responsibilities as older employees but are paid significantly less because of their age. Some young people are financially independent or help pay for essential costs. We believe the current minimum wage does not reflect the rising cost of living and can make it difficult for young workers to support themselves. Raising the minimum wage for under-18s to at least £10 per hour would, we feel, ensure fairer pay and better support young workers.

records.title: Include Wales in the Union Flag
records.description: I would like a new version of the Union Flag to include Wales. As a country I feel we are extremely divided and I believe having a flag to represent us all will bring greater unity as well as greater understanding for the future, everyone equal and everyone heard.
records.further_details: I would take the most iconic part of the Welsh flag and add it to the Union Flag. I believe this change will make England and Wales closer and help us prosper more for the future. England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales are all proud and beautiful nations but I believe the importance of a united Britain is the best chance we have in the coming future to remain a global power and haven for growth and prosperity.

records.title: Scientific & research assessments for all new laws & statutory guidance
records.description: Require all new laws and statutory guidance to include a published Scientific and Research Impact Assessment (SRIA). The SRIA must use systematic reviews of independent data from multiple sources. A new independent scrutiny body must ensure that these are unbiassed and reflect the evidence.
records.further_details: We believe policies are currently open to legal technicalities, political ideologies, and cherry-picked data due to there being no statutory requirement to audit underlying research. A prime example TO US is the ongoing public confusion over equality and single sex spaces guidance, which relies on consultations rather than peer-reviewed data. Current frameworks also fail to stop payee bias. Mandating literature reviews and strict funding filters will, we believe, anchor law to reality and guarantee backing by uncorrupted evidence.

records.title: Add the Welsh dragon to the union flag
records.description: I think that for the union flag to be fairer and more inclusive it should be altered to feature the Welsh dragon in the middle.
records.further_details: I feel the Welsh community are underrepresented despite Welsh culture being an important part of the UK. For this reason, I think our union flag should offer more coverage and include the Welsh dragon in the middle.

records.title: Change the law to give next kin access to medical records at the end of life.
records.description: Change the law to give recognised next of kin full access to medical records when a patient lacks capacity and is receiving end-of-life or palliative care, except where there are domestic abuse or safeguarding concerns.
records.further_details: Families are expected to contribute to best interests decisions but are often denied access to the information needed to advocate effectively. The law should define who qualifies as next of kin and include safeguards where there are domestic abuse or other serious safeguarding concerns. This would improve transparency and help ensure patients' wishes are respected.

records.title: Require CCTV in all schools
records.description: Implementation of cameras in all school classrooms, hallways and playgrounds covering all areas entrances and exits including bathroom entrances to protect all children and adults and prevent bullying.
records.further_details: Every child deserves to learn in a safe environment. CCTV covering classrooms, hallways, playgrounds, and entrances and exits, while respecting privacy by excluding bathroom interiors but monitoring bathroom entrances, can help deter bullying, protect pupils and staff, provide objective evidence when incidents occur, and improve accountability. Used responsibly with appropriate safeguards, it supports safeguarding, transparency, and faster, fairer investigations.

records.title: Mandate all schools to provide outdoor learning & teach hands-on gardening
records.description: We call on the Government to mandate all schools to provide outdoor learning and teach hands-on gardening to build vital survival skills and fight climate anxiety. We believe our children need nature, and that this proposal can protect their future and Earth.
records.further_details: We feel our children are disconnected from nature and unprepared for a changing planet. Outdoor learning could improve mental health, reduce eco-anxiety and teach vital self-sufficiency. Textbooks alone cannot protect our future. We should give the next generation the practical tools and ecological literacy they need to survive.

records.title: Fund & mandate full examination of cervical screening samples every 2-3 years
records.description: I call on the Government to fund and mandate all cervical samples from cervical screening tests to be examined for abnormal cells - — not only those that test HPV positive. Tests should be required every 2–3 years, or sooner if needed.
records.further_details:
Not all cervical cell changes or cancers are HPV related. We feel relying only on HPV testing removes a vital safety net, puts people with a history of abnormal cells at risk and ignores evidence that HPV negative disease exists.
 
We want to mandate the examination of all cervical samples, so they are checked for abnormal cells, not just those that are HPV-positive. We also want routine tests to happen every 2-3 years instead of automatic 5-year screening interval for HPV-negative individuals. Testing and examinations should be based on inclusive, evidence based care that protects everyone, not just average cases.

records.title: Require VAWG safeguards in asylum and immigration policy
records.description: Require VAWG risk assessments in asylum and immigration policy, publish anonymised nationality and immigration-status data for serious VAWG offences, and ensure foreign nationals convicted of serious VAWG offences are considered promptly for lawful deportation.
records.further_details: The Government has pledged to halve violence against women and girls and now gives asylum seekers guidance on consent, domestic abuse, child sexual activity and harassment. Yet national crime data cannot show VAWG offending by immigration status. If Government identifies a safeguarding risk, it should measure it, publish the evidence and act where individuals present a danger. Women and girls should be protected regardless of an offender’s nationality.

records.title: Close the "Freeholder Loophole": Give Flat Tenants the Fair Right to Keep Pets
records.description:
Close the Loophole: Stop freeholders from unreasonably blocking pet requests.
Demand Transparency: Require written, evidence-based reasons for any refusal.
Equal Rights: End arbitrary head-lease bans for flat renters.
records.further_details: The Renters’ Rights Act promised to end unfair pet bans, but we feel a major loophole leaves flat renters behind. While your immediate landlord can agree to a pet, the building’s freeholder can step in and outright deny the request without giving any reason. Because the Act does not cover the relationship between leaseholders and freeholders, arbitrary "no pets" clauses in head leases remain legally binding. Pets provide vital mental health support and reduce loneliness. Sign if you agree.

records.title: Review Recall of MPs Act 2015 to strengthen public accountability
records.description: Launch a review into strengthening the Recall of MPs Act 2015 by extending the grounds under which a recall petition can be triggered.
records.further_details: We feel the current Act only allows a recall petition in limited circumstances. We believe constituents should have greater powers to hold their elected representatives to account when an MP has been found guilty of serious misconduct, corruption, abuse of public office, deliberate deception when performing public duties, or any other serious breaches of public trust.

records.title: Require food businesses to state on packaging if products may contain gluten
records.description: I want it to be required by law for any food business to label on packaging if a product may contain gluten. This is not currently required and has affected me many times as a coeliac. Clear gluten risk labelling should be mandatory.
records.further_details: Companies and businesses currently do not need to say on the products packaging if the product may contain gluten. This has led to a huge amount of coeliacs being given gluten by mistake, including me, which has severe effects. I want every company/business to have to state on their packaging if the product may contain gluten.

records.title: Remove VAT from hearing aids
records.description: People with a physical disability can reclaim the vat on some disability aids. The same should be available to people with a hearing disability with regard to hearing aids.

records.title: Change statutory redundancy pay to include partial years of service
records.description: We want the Government to amend the rules for statutory redundancy pay so that, once an employee qualifies for statutory redundancy pay, completed months of continuous employment are included on a pro-rata basis instead of only complete years of service being counted.
records.further_details: Statutory redundancy pay only counts complete years of employment. This can unfairly disadvantage someone dismissed shortly before a service anniversary, as almost a full year's additional service is ignored. We believe completed months should be counted pro rata, creating a fairer system that better reflects actual length of service, recognises employees' full contribution and reduces the disproportionate impact that the timing of a termination can have on redundancy pay.

records.title: Inquiry into Pakistani and Indian state influence on UK politics & democracy
records.description: We want the Government to launch an independent inquiry into the extent to which the governments of Pakistan and India may be attempting to influence MPs, peers, political parties and UK public institutions, and whether current rules are strong enough to protect UK sovereignty.
records.further_details: The UK is a sovereign country and its decisions should serve the British public. We believe any influence from the Pakistani or Indian governments through lobbying, funding, paid trips or pressure on community groups should be fully transparent. The inquiry should review the operation of the Register of Members' Interests, All-Party Parliamentary Group rules and the Foreign Influence Registration Scheme, and recommend stronger safeguards. This petition is about the conduct of these governments, not British communities.

records.title: Ban shock and prong collars for dogs
records.description: Ban the use of shock and prong collars for all dogs, including working dogs. We are concerned that scientific papers and welfare reports show that electronic shock collars cause physical pain, elevated stress and long-term psychological harm to dogs.

records.title: Increase stamp duty threshold for 1st time buyers in Southern England to £400K
records.description: Many people who live in Southern England facing expensive prices to pay to buy a house. First time buyer stamp duty relief are the same for both North & Southerners. Increase the first time buy Stamp Duty threshold from 300K to 400K, so buyers pay 0% stamp duty on property that is £400K and less.
records.further_details: We support this as it is very hard for many to buy a decent house in the South for £300K, and this proposal of increasing the threshold for first-time buyers paying 0% stamp duty from £300K to £400K could help them to put that money elsewhere when they buy a house. The North of England is relatively cheaper when compared to towns in the South and it may be easy for people to buy a decent-sized house for £300K. Considering cost of living in South and increasing it to £400K for the first time buyers could provide a lot of relief.

records.title: Introduce a one-day-a-week community programme for people seeking work
records.description: We call on the government to introduce a mandatory one-day-a-week community volunteering programme for people seeking work - building skills, providing fulfilment, and strengthening local communities for the benefit of individuals and the places they live.
records.further_details: Unemployment can be isolating and demoralising. People seeking work often want to contribute but lack the opportunity. A weekly community volunteering programme gives them purpose, structure, and real skills - while improving local areas. It builds confidence, fosters community belonging, and strengthens CVs. This isn't about obligation - it's about empowerment. The benefits last long after someone returns to work, for both the individual and the community they've invested in.

records.title: Support democratic elections in Nigeria and sanction anyone who threatens them
records.description:
• Publicly advocate for free, fair, and transparent elections in Nigeria
• Review diplomatic engagement with Nigerian electoral bodies where concerns of partisanship and impartiality arise
• Implement targeted visa bans and sanctions on individuals found to be responsible for electoral malpractice
records.further_details:
Recent electoral concerns have raised questions among members of the Nigerian diaspora and the international community regarding transparency and impartiality in Nigeria’s democratic processes.
 
We call on the UK Government to use its diplomatic influence to support credible, free, and fair elections in Nigeria.
We further urge the UK Government to implement visa ban for those whose action are responsible for weakening Nigeria’s opposition and or the credibility of Nigeria’s election.

records.title: Lower the voting age to 16
records.description: I want the government to lower the voting age to 16
records.further_details: I want the government to lower the legal voting age so people of a younger age can have a say in what they think is right.

records.title: Require licence plates on all hire cycles
records.description: Issue regulations to require cycle hire companies have licence plates on their cycles.
records.further_details: Increased safety and responsibility for hire cycles. Hired cycles should follow the rules of the road like everyone else. Currently many hired cycles break the rules of the road at great danger to both themselves and other users of the road (eg running red lights). Many mechanisms enforcing the rules of the road rely on licence plates to fulfil their function. We see this as a common sense and easy to implement requirement that could bring them in line with other vehicles on the road.

records.title: Reinstate the Local defence Volunteers across the United Kingdom
records.description: "We call upon the UK Government to explore the creation of a modern Local Defence Volunteer organisation to strengthen community resilience, support emergency response efforts, and encourage public service in the face of growing domestic and international challenges."
records.further_details: The United Kingdom faces a range of modern challenges, including terrorism, cyber disruption, natural disasters, severe weather events, infrastructure emergencies, and increased international tensions. A modern Local Defence Volunteer force could help strengthen national resilience

records.title: End "Retrospective Regularisation" of sewerage infrastructure
records.description: It is currently possible for water companies to operate sewerage infrastructure by applying retrospectively for the relevant environmental permits or planning permission. We believe this amounts to the avoidance of scrutiny, and that the Environment Agency is not fit for purpose.
records.further_details:
We call on the Government to:
End the practice of retrospective regularisation for sewerage infrastructure operating without valid permits.
Mandate automatic prosecution by the Environment Agency for all unpermitted sewerage assets to ensure corporate accountability.
Establish a transparent national registry of all water assets. 
The EA must obtain and document explicit informed consent from landowners before granting any permit for sewerage infrastructure operating on the landowner’s property.

records.title: Bring 18-20 minimum wage in line with adults 21 and over
records.description:
I propose bringing the national minimum wage for 18-20 year olds in line with 21 year olds and above.

Currently minimum wage for 18-20 year olds is 	£10.85 while for 21+ year olds its £12.71. 

I believe it should be the same.
records.further_details:
I believe bringing the wage in line with the rest of the adult population can make a difference in mental health in young people, help them get on the property ladder and not be as financially stressed.

Also, it can help bring more young adults into work which is becoming more of a problem lately.

records.title: Extend mandatory calorie labelling to all food businesses including SMEs
records.description: We call on the Government to require all restaurants, cafés and takeaways to display calorie information for all menu items, regardless of the size of those businesses. Consumers currently lack consistent access to basic nutritional data when eating out.
records.further_details: Consumers currently receive inconsistent nutritional information when eating out, making it difficult to make informed dietary choices. While supermarkets provide full calorie labelling, restaurants and takeaways often do not. Modern tools allow calorie values to be easily calculated quickly and accurately using standard recipes and ingredient data. We believe that requiring all businesses, including small independents, to display calories, would improve transparency, combat obesity, and support public health.

records.title: Require that delivery vehicles have air conditioning and legal max temperature
records.description: Create legislation to ensure future delivery vehicles are created with a maximum working temperature in mind, and cooling to achieve that goal.
records.further_details:
Since the pandemic, delivery vehicles & workers have become more common, however there is still no legal requirement for air conditioning despite the increased frequency of heatwaves.

Temperatures can easily reach over 38°C in these vehicles, presenting health dangers. This could risk the ability for companies to attract more workers in the transport sector.

We believe adjustments for future vehicles to include climate control should be made standard to ensure the safety of vital workers.

records.title: Introduce Laws to Regulate how organisations post Children/Youth on social media
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce legislation regulating how organisations publish images/videos of kids online, banning public posts of under 12s except safeguarding/public interest and introducing strict legal safeguards for 12–17-year-olds on consent, commercial use and privacy protection
records.further_details: Children’s images are shared online by organisations, without consistent mandatory safeguards. Once posted, these images can be copied, reshared or misused beyond the original context. This petition calls for stronger legal protections: prohibiting public posting on under 12’s by organisations (except safeguarding/public interest purposes) and introducing strict safeguards for ages 12-17, which limit commercial use, use stronger protections than consent alone and implement privacy protections.

records.title: Ensure accurate and accessible gestational diabetes testing
records.description: Require NHS England to address known risks in gestational diabetes testing, including sample degradation, inconsistent practice and barriers to access, and take action to ensure every pregnant woman can access accurate and equitable testing and prevent missed diagnoses that can cause serious harm.
records.further_details: NIHR-funded research found that under routine NHS conditions more than half of gestational diabetes cases are being missed. Unless blood samples are processed correctly, glucose degrades, producing falsely low results that can leave women undiagnosed. Missed GDM increases risks for mothers and babies, including stillbirth and future type 2 diabetes. Hospital-based testing can also create access barriers. Women should be able to trust their test result.

records.title: Geofenced 5 km/h limits & more accountability for e-bike and e-scooter providers
records.description: We propose mandatory national standards for rental e-bikes and e-scooters. We think operators should use existing technology to enforce 5 km/h geofenced speed limits in pedestrian zones and be required to improve age verification. The Government should introduce fines for non-compliance.
records.further_details: We want to make our streets safer by requiring rental e-bike and e-scooter operators to use the safety technology already built into their fleets to impose lower speeds on their products. Currently, GPS and 'geofencing' allow operators to exercise precise control over speed and location. We are calling for national standards that mandate 5 km/h speed limits in pedestrian zones, mandate strict age checks, and for the Government to impose fines on operators who fail to comply. We are not calling for a ban, but for responsible, regulated use.

records.title: Review the legislation governing Ofcom’s enforcement of the Broadcasting Code
records.description: Review the current legal framework governing Ofcom’s enforcement of the Broadcasting Code, to investigate whether it remains fit for purpose. The review should look into legislating to strengthen the regulatory framework, improve accountability and maintain public confidence, if deemed necessary.
records.further_details: Ofcom has significant enforcement powers, but some broadcasters have been found by Ofcom to be in breach of the Broadcasting Code on multiple occasions. We believe the Government should review whether the current legal framework provides sufficient deterrence against repeated serious breaches, and whether legislative reform is needed to ensure the framework remains effective, proportionate and able to maintain public confidence in the regulation of UK broadcasting.

records.title: Protect children's privacy, dignity and future consent in the digital age
records.description: Create legislation to protect children's privacy, dignity and future consent online by requiring safeguards before vulnerable or identifiable content is publicly shared and giving young people the legal right to request removal of content shared about them during childhood.
records.further_details: Children are increasingly having personal, vulnerable and identifiable moments shared online before they are old enough to understand or consent. Medical experiences, emotional struggles and private childhood moments can become part of a permanent digital footprint. This petition calls for legislation to ensure children's dignity, privacy and future autonomy are considered before such content is shared and to give young people greater control over content published about them during childhood.

records.title: Don’t require disclosure of domestic abuse victims’ medical info in family court
records.description: We call on the Government to legislate to protect domestic abuse victims’ personal medical records in family court proceedings by ensuring they cannot be required to be disclosed to the other party by the court.
records.further_details: We believe the current system can allow family court proceedings to become a continuation of post-separation abuse. Requiring victims to disclose highly personal medical records directly to an alleged or proven abuser can cause further trauma, discourage victims from seeking medical or mental health support, and undermine confidence in the justice system. We believe stronger safeguards are needed to protect victims’ privacy while ensuring courts retain access to relevant evidence when necessary.

records.title: Amend GPs’ contracts to require them to enter shared care agreements
records.description: Amend GPs’ contracts so they are required to accept Shared Care Agreements for NHS Right to Choose patients once stabilised by an NHS-commissioned specialist. Currently, GPs can refuse shared care, forcing patients onto remote providers.
records.further_details:
Under NHS Right to Choose (RTC), patients on long waiting lists see NHS-commissioned specialists. However, GPs retain the legal right to decline Shared Care Agreements once a patient is stabilised.
 
We believe refusals force patients onto remote RTC providers for repeat prescriptions, causing severe delays, health risks, and higher costs for private dispensing. We want the Government to amend GP contracts to require them to accept Shared Care Agreements for patients stabilised by NHS-commissioned RTC providers.

records.title: Make all major supermarkets use a form of cover/shelter for all baked goods.
records.description: In many major stores, baked goods are open to contamination via physical touch, insects and more. We therefore call upon the government to require all supermarkets with a bakery section, to have some sort of cover for all bakery items to ensure hygiene is kept up to standard.

records.title: Establish a National Skills & Service Programme
records.description: We want the Government to set up a National Skills & Service Programme (NSSP) for young adults to help support the c981.000 people aged16-24 (13% of that age group) who are not in education, employment or training (NEET).
records.further_details: We believe a National Skills & Service Programme would help young adults who remain outside employment, education or training for a defined period. This would combine structured service, accredited training and work experience, followed by a strong bridge into ordinary paid employment. It should include civilian routes as well as service-based options and should not be designed as compulsory recruitment into the regular Armed Forces. We believe public spending should do more than maintain inactivity.

records.title: Require schools give first aid training to a higher level as part of curriculum
records.description: I want schools to stop teaching first aid to a basic level. First aid should be taught as part of the core curriculum and should be built on to eventually give students the same level of knowledge as the First Aid At Work qualification provides.
records.further_details: Right now, I feel that, students are being taught very scarce first aid in schools. I want it to be mandatory for pupils to learn first aid to a more advanced level as they go through school. They could start with basic first aid and finish with a more advanced level qualification. Research suggests that up to 59% to 60% of pre-hospital deaths from injury could be prevented if more people had basic first aid knowledge before emergency services arrive. Surely if schools did more training, people would be more confident?

records.title: Ban insurance auto-renewal at a higher price without fresh consent
records.description: Change the law to require insurers and brokers to obtain fresh, explicit consent before renewing a policy at a higher total price for the same, substantially similar or reduced cover. Include mandatory fees and finance charges and compare costs over the same period and payment basis.
records.further_details: Agreeing to automatic renewal should not mean agreeing to an unknown future price. When the price rises, customers should decide whether to renew after seeing the new amount. Require a clear comparison with the previous total price, a simple way to accept or decline, and advance warning if cover will end without consent. Silence or an old auto-renewal instruction should not count as agreement to the higher price.

records.title: Create and fund opportunities for ages 13+ to work on heritage rail preservation
records.description: Create and fund visible opportunities for younger people of 13+ to work on heritage railway preservation, teaching them skills to help uphold the standards of preservation, and potentially creating a bigger future workforce. Work closely with relevant regulatory and rail bodies to make it happen.
records.further_details: The government, and many in society, have sometimes boasted of our heritage and the great past. I think the heritage railway scene is great and that enabling young people to take part in it would help steer some youths who may otherwise be at risk of involvement in crime into something meaningful and certainly interesting. It could allow the force of young people to help keep the culture of steam railways and rockstars of the steam world alive. It would be there to teach young people essential skills of preservation.

records.title: Make duty for schools to prioritise admission to children within 30-minute walk
records.description: We call on the Government to place a duty on schools & local authorities to ensure no child is allocated a school more than 30-minutes walk from home, otherwise transport must be provided. Academies & all state-funded schools must be required to expand capacity where local provision is insufficient
records.further_details: We believe long school journeys raise serious safety concerns, particularly in areas such as London (where knife crime/gang violence is high), and can require parental collection, which is not feasible for many working families. Travelling further limits access to extracurricular activities that build cultural capital and development. It also increases tiredness and reduces study time, negatively affecting attainment. As a result, we feel that children travelling long distances do not have equal access to education.

records.title: Make GCSE Maths optional and introduce an alternative, easier qualification
records.description: I want to introduce an alternative, easier maths qualification for people for whom GCSE Maths isn’t attainable. This qualification could have different requirements that are more achievable.
records.further_details: Many people struggle with numbers, and the requirement to pass GCSE Maths puts them under pressure. This can cause stress and anxiety.

records.title: Stop changes to tariffs on stainless steel imports due to come into effect 1/7
records.description: We want the government to stop the changes to tariffs on imported stainless steel coming into effect in July 2026
records.further_details: We believe that if this comes in it to effect, it will destroy manufacturing in large and small business throughout the UK. In our view, this has been brought in to force people to buy British stainless steel, which may be a great idea but the UK does not produce enough stainless steel. Therefore we believe that us manufactures have no choice but to buy it from overseas. These tariffs will mean a 100% price increase on our material costs which we believe in effect will price UK manufacturers out of all markets here in the UK as well as exports

records.title: Review penalties for shoplifters under 18 years old, consider community orders
records.description: Shoplifting has a substantial impact to the economy including significant losses for businesses, which can then end up being passed to the end consumer. Shopworkers face abuse and violence which can be daunting. We think penalties for under 18 shoplifters are insufficient and should be reviewed.
records.further_details: In our view, community based orders could be effective as it can allow offenders to build empathy, gain life-skills, and better understand the repercussions of their actions. We urge policymakers to review the current penalty system for shoplifting and consider implementing alternative penalties as standard practice for a more responsible society & approach to crime prevention. This could enable to achieve brighter future and protect our community and our businesses.

records.title: Make it an offence to leave delivery vehicle doors open when making deliveries
records.description: We call on the Government to make it an offence for any vehicle used for delivery of goods to be left with its doors open whilst the delivery professional is making a delivery.
records.further_details: This is to prevent pets such as cats and dogs entering unnoticed and then becoming unintentionally trapped and removed from their local territory. We believe that many pets are going missing and that this is an avoidable event which should be legislated against so safeguard pets.

records.title: Grant Six-Month Grace Period for Workers Affected by Sponsor Licence Revocation
records.description: Allow sponsored workers whose employer’s sponsor licence is revoked to remain for six months, enabling them to find a new sponsor, switch visa routes, or make arrangements to leave, particularly where they have complied with immigration rules and contributed to UK society.
records.further_details: We call on the Government to grant a six-month grace period to workers affected by sponsor licence revocation. Many have complied with immigration rules, paid taxes, contributed to the economy, bought homes and built families in the UK without accessing public funds. A six-month period would allow them to find a new sponsor, switch visa routes or make arrangements, reflecting the UK’s values of fairness, compassion and responsibility.

records.title: Require all new cars sold in the UK to be fitted with dashcams
records.description: Make it a law that requires all new cars sold in the UK to be factory fitted with back and front dash cameras.
records.further_details: Making it a legal requirement for new cars to have dash cameras fitted in the front and back of the vehicle and working at all times could result in less ambiguity regarding whose responsibility it was for an accident, and it could give insurers an idea of the insurance risk that their customers if their accident history is recorded.

records.title: Make air conditioning mandatory in nursing/care homes and introduce max temp
records.description: Make air conditioning or proven cooling systems a mandatory requirement in all nursing and residential care homes. Introduce maximum indoor temperature standards for care settings.
records.further_details:
We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation requiring all nursing homes and residential care homes to install and maintain effective air conditioning or equivalent cooling systems in resident bedrooms, communal areas, and staff working areas.

Many residents are at high risk of heat-related illnesses such as dehydration, heat exhaustion, heatstroke, and worsening of existing medical conditions. Care staff could also become unwell while working long shifts in these excessive temperatures, making it harder to provide safe, high-quality care.

records.title: Introduce fatality prevention strategy for rail networks
records.description: Government to introduce a fatality prevention strategy specific to rail networks, delivered alongside train operators to improve safety measures at high-risk railway locations to help prevent fatalities. I witnessed the death of a young person and believe more could be done to save lives.
records.further_details: I witnessed the tragic death of a young person on the railway. No family should have to lose a loved one in this way, and no member of the public, train staff or emergency services should have to experience preventable tragedies if more can be done. I recognise that not every incident can be prevented, but I believe the Government should do more to reduce the number of deaths and serious incidents on the railway. This should include working with train operating companies, mental health services and safety experts to identify high-risk locations and implement effective preventative measures.

records.title: Require retailers and supermarkets to offer a self-checkout discount
records.description:
We call on the UK Government to require supermarkets and large retailers to give customers a 20% discount for using self-service checkouts.

Customers do work once done by paid staff. Retailers save money through automation, so customers should share those savings.
records.further_details: Self-service checkouts are now common in many supermarkets, with fewer staffed tills available. Customers often have little choice but to scan, bag and pay for their own shopping while still paying the same prices. Retailers benefit from lower staffing costs and improved efficiency, yet those savings are rarely passed on to consumers. A 20% discount would ensure the financial benefits of self-service technology are shared more fairly with customers.

records.title: Establish a specific night time residential noise offence enforceable by police
records.description: Unreasonable amplified music/noise that is audible within another person's dwelling and substantially interferes with their ability to sleep or peacefully enjoy their home becomes an enforceable night-time noise offence.

records.title: Remain Neutral In Foreign Conflicts.
records.description: We demand the government declare Britain a neutral state. We believe that neutrality will protect British interests, safeguard our national security and uphold our tradition of diplomacy and peacekeeping in an increasingly polarised world.
records.further_details:
We think the world is entering a new phase of global tension, with increasing confrontations between major powers. In our view, the UK is at risk of becoming entangled in these geopolitical conflicts. We propose a neutral stance that we think could prioritise British security, protect our economy: allow Britain to serve as a mediator, promoting diplomacy and peace on the international stage.

We think Britain is no longer a super power on the level of America, China, or Russia.

records.title: Mandate reducing leaks & protecting the environment for water surge-pricing
records.description: The Government should introduce minimum requirements for water companies before they are permitted to implement surge-pricing for water bills, which include not breaching any environmental regulations in place, and reducing leaks to no more than 5% of total daily water supply.
records.further_details:
Water companies are considering surge-pricing, which would lead to consumers being charged more during periods of drought. 

We believe this should not be allowed if their infrastructure suffers from significant leaks. It was found that South East Water is estimated to be losing around 20% of its daily supply to leaks. Consumers should not have to pay more if they are losing that amount of water.

There is also evidence of water companies breaching environmental regulations. We believe that if they breach or have breached them, companies should not be allowed to enact surge-pricing measures.

records.title: Require landlords to check for lead pipes and test drinking water
records.description: Require landlords of older rented properties to check for lead water pipes. Where lead pipes are found, landlords must regularly test drinking water for lead, give tenants the results, and take action if levels are elevated.
records.further_details:
Many older UK properties still have lead water pipes. Tenants may live there for years without knowing lead pipes are present or whether lead is entering their drinking water.

Landlords should check for lead pipes instead of leaving tenants to discover them by chance. Where lead pipes are found, tenants should be informed and given regular water test results. Lead pipes should ultimately be replaced. Until then, identifying them and testing the water would help protect tenants and their families.

records.title: Make a statutory oversight body to investigate failures in family justice system
records.description: We want the Government to create an independent statutory oversight body for the family justice system, with powers to examine any failures across the judiciary, Cafcass, social care, complaints and appeals, and make recommendations to improve transparency, accountability and public confidence.
records.further_details:
Families can struggle to find an independent route to challenge serious concerns about how their case has been handled. Accountability is divided between courts, Cafcass, children's social care, complaints bodies and appeal processes, creating gaps where concerns may fall between systems. 
 
We want independent oversight to identify systemic failures, improve transparency and ensure that children and families can have confidence that serious concerns are properly examined and learned from.

records.title: Make 12 July 2027 a one-off Bank Holiday for 1100th anniversary England's birth
records.description: By making Monday 12th July 2027 a bank holiday in England, to commemorate the 1100th anniversary of the birth of England, Parliament will help most people in England celebrate the occasion. The Government should financially support those charities who are organising celebrations for the occasion.
records.further_details: Most English historians recognise the meeting arranged by King Æthelstan on 12th July 927 at ‘Eamotum’ in Cumbria represents the original unification of the English people, rightly described as the Birth of England. After this date King Æthelstan styled himself as Rex Anglorum - King of the English. For the first time all the people of England lived under one ruler and one law code. The 12th July is to England as 4th July is to America. England's creation in 927 should be officially recognised.

records.title: Change the sentence for rape to a mandatory life sentence
records.description: We believe the punishment for rapists is not nearly harsh enough and a mandatory life sentence is the only way to protect the public from them and to prevent repeat offences.
records.further_details: We believe current sentencing is clearly too lenient on people who can cause severe mental health issues that can lead to death, the same eventual consequence that murder has - and murder has a mandatory life sentence. We feel it's genuinely a disappointment that the legal system can allow such a severe crime to be punished by something less than a mandatory life sentence.

records.title: Require schools to provide carbohydrate information for school meals.
records.description: Require all state-funded schools in England to provide the total carbohydrate content, in grams, for meals, snacks and drinks supplied to pupils, so that children with Type 1 diabetes and those supporting them can accurately calculate insulin doses.
records.further_details:
Children with Type 1 diabetes need to calculate mealtime insulin based on the amount of carbohydrate they are going to eat.
Schools may provide menus and other nutritional information but carbohydrate information is not consistently available. This can leave parents, school staff and children estimating the carbohydrate content of meals when calculating insulin.
I believe carbohydrate information should be readily available for every school meal and portion.

records.title: Implement restricted airspace around all active emergency service incidents.
records.description: There is an increase in drone footage being shared online of potentially serious life threatening incidents, in some instances affecting the use of emergency services' own aircraft. I would propose that for all incidents and immediate 100m no-fly-zone is enacted to allow emergency services to work.
records.further_details: What dealing with a recent man-in-water situation I observed a social media post where the local fire service had found it necessary to request people ground their drones in the area as People using them to observe the ongoing incident were creating a situation where coast guard and police helicopters were Not able to operate to maximum efficiency. This is not an isolated incident it is not uncommon to see drone footage circulating on social media before family members have been told.

records.title: Make Sexual Education Mandatory For Academic Years 3 and Up
records.description: The Children’s Commissioner found that 10% of children are exposed to pornography by age 9 (academic years 4 and 5) - that jumps to 27% by age 11(academic years 6 and 7). Yet, despite studies linking porn to aggressive sexual behaviour, sexual education is still not mandatory in all primary schools.
records.further_details: A government literary review, published in 2021, concluded that pornography viewing was a factor in poor attitudes against women and girls, including 1. Viewing women as sex objects; 2. Shaping men’s sexual expectations of women; 3. Acceptance of sexual aggression towards women; and 4. Perpetration of sexual aggression. Yet, the governments recent policy paper, aiming to "halve violence against women and girls in a decade" has no plea for mandatory sexual education within all primary schools.

records.title: Review all employment laws relating to unfair treatment in the workplace
records.description: I want the Government to review all employment laws to ensure all forms of unfair treatment in the workplace are treated equally – not mainly those linked to protected characteristics. I feel employees facing unfair or targeted treatment should have equal legal protection and access to justice.
records.further_details: Many employees experience unfair treatment, bullying or exclusion at work that may not fall under protected characteristics in the Equality Act 2010. I believe this can leave workers without proper legal protection or support. I believe all forms of unfair treatment & bullying in the workplace should be taken seriously and addressed equally under employment law to create fairer, safer, and more respectful workplaces for everyone.

records.title: Ban multiple interviews for jobs paying under £15p/h & prioritise UC claimants
records.description: Make a law that companies hiring for roles paying under £15 an hour can’t hold more than one interview round, and must prioritise those currently on Universal Credit. All jobs under this threshold must be posted to JobCentre sites.
records.further_details: Many companies are hosting multiple interview rounds for basic wage jobs. We think this wastes interviewee time and where that individual is on UC, government funds. Many people applying for those roles are willing to get back into work ASAP, and able to do the role, that’s all that’s necessary for those roles. £15 an hour is above minimum wage but we think a fair threshold and helps those willing to take any role, even if they’re over qualified, because they want to work, pay their bills, and carry out their normal life.

records.title: Require all retailers to follow Sunday Trading Hours during Bank Holidays
records.description: We want all retailers in England and Wales to be required to follow Sunday trading hours (only allowed to be open for 6 consecutive hours between 10am-6pm) on all bank holidays, ensuring consistent restrictions on trading hours and protecting workers’ rights to rest days.
records.further_details: Currently, many large retailers operate extended hours on bank holidays. We believe Bank holidays are intended to provide time for rest, family life, and community activities. In our views, extending trading hours on these days undermines a fair work/life balance for retail employees, who may miss out on shared time off when most other sectors are closed.

records.title: Exempt parents in work from the under-35 Shared Accommodation Rate
records.description: Exempt working parents from the under-35 Shared Accommodation Rate renting privately. We believe the Government should reform Universal Credit housing rules so that full-time working adults who pay tax and hold parental responsibility are not penalised solely on the basis of age.
records.further_details:
The Shared Accommodation Rate (SAR) assumes under-35s can share housing. But we think working adults paying full tax and holding parental responsibility cannot fulfil those duties from a shared room as a parent must provide a safe, private space for a visiting child. In our view, the SAR makes this financially impossible, punishing equal contribution with unequal rights.

We believe this policy breaches the Equality Act 2010 and Articles 8 and 14 of the ECHR.

records.title: Review delayed RSS and payment to retirees in receipt of public sector pensions
records.description: Review delayed issuing of Remediable Service Statement (RSS) for public sector pension fund claimants. We want these RSSs to be issued without delay alongside a timeframe for payment, and a mandatory notification for claimants about individual case progress throughout the process.
records.further_details: Following the McCloud judgement, which set out the age discriminatory actions of some government schemes, all affected retirees were to be issued RSS addressing how their pension would be compensated if necessary. Currently there is no published timescale for this and people have been waiting 4+ years even to receive a RSS. Others have submitted the RSS and 3+ years later have not received the financial redress.

records.title: Make child maintenance deductions from earnings by default
records.description: We want child maintenance to be automatically deducted from earnings by default, similar to tax, National Insurance and pensions. This would provide reliable support for children, reduce conflict and prevent payments being delayed, withheld or used as leverage between parents.
records.further_details: Children should not miss out on financial support because of disputes or non-payment between parents. We want child maintenance to be automatically deducted from earnings by default, similar to tax and pension contributions. This would provide greater financial security for children, reduce conflict and remove the need for parents to repeatedly chase payments intended for their children. Children’s financial support should be automatic, not dependent on one parent choosing to pay.

records.title: Add Anti-Racism as a subject into the National Curriculum
records.description: Make anti-racism education a compulsory subject in the national curriculum. We believe all students should learn about racism, prejudice, unconscious bias, equality and inclusion to help create safer, more respectful schools and better prepare young people for life in a diverse society.
records.further_details: Racism and racial prejudice continue to affect many young people in schools and wider society. We believe all students should receive age-appropriate anti-racism education that promotes understanding, respect and inclusion. Teaching about the history and impact of racism, unconscious bias and discrimination can help challenge harmful attitudes, reduce prejudice and create safer, more welcoming school environments for everyone.

records.title: Prevent court staff blocking applications from reaching judges
records.description: Legislate to prevent court staff from blocking properly filed court applications and supporting evidence from reaching a judge for judicial determination, and require every such administrative decision to be transparent, recorded, legally authorised and subject to independent judicial review.
records.further_details: Access to an independent judge is a fundamental constitutional safeguard and an essential part of the rule of law. We believe properly filed court applications and supporting evidence should not be prevented from reaching a judge by administrative action unless expressly authorised by law. We want the Government to strengthen safeguards, increase transparency and accountability, and ensure every person has effective access to independent judicial determination.

records.title: Extend the 1968 Medical Exemption List to Include all needing Lifelong Supplies
records.description: We feel the 1968 Medical Exemption Certificate list is outdated & no longer reflects healthcare today. We believe that no-one with a lifelong condition needing ongoing treatment or essential supplies should be excluded.
records.further_details: We think the 1968 Medical Exemption Certificate list is outdated and no longer reflects healthcare today. Many people with lifelong conditions who need ongoing medical supplies can face financial strain, delayed treatment, worsening symptoms, and poorer health outcomes when they are excluded from free support. This petition calls for the exemption list to be updated so that all lifelong conditions requiring essential medical supplies are included, ensuring fairness, equality, and better health for everyone.

records.title: Review and update health and safety laws to protect vehicle workers from heat
records.description: We call on the Government to launch a review into updating health and safety laws to ensure they specifically address and protect workers who spend much of their day in vehicles from excessive heat.
records.further_details: We believe many proposals made by people on workplace temperatures do not clearly cover workers whose workplace is a vehicle. Millions of postal workers, delivery drivers, healthcare staff, utility engineers and others spend much of their day in vehicle cabs, where temperatures can greatly exceed those outside. The Government should update health and safety legislation and statutory guidance so that it explicitly addresses how employers of vehicle workers should assess and manage heat risks in workplace vehicles.

records.title: Mandatory data collection on deaths linked to ‘chemsex’
records.description: Require the UK Government to introduce national recording of chemsex-related deaths and publish annual data to improve prevention, support and harm reduction
records.further_details:
In our view, if we don’t count chemsex-related deaths, we can’t understand the scale of the problem. If we can’t understand it, we can’t prevent more lives being lost.

Every life matters. Every death tells a story. But right now, the UK does not record when a drug-related death happens in the context of chemsex.

This petition calls for better recognition through better data collection, and as a result better support — not to judge people, but to save lives.

records.title: Immediately start a programme of constructing desalination plants around the UK
records.description: Immediately begin construction of a network of desalination plants to supplement existing water resources.
records.further_details: Given climate change, we believe additional water resources must be found as part of a water resilience strategy.

records.title: Higher Council and Income taxes for holiday homes to preserve local communities
records.description: We want the Government to mandate a separate higher council tax band for former private dwellings that are let as holiday homes and to legislate for income received from such properties to be taxed at a minimum rate of 90%.
records.further_details: We believe this will help prevent the destruction of local communities by holiday home investors.

records.title: Make Highway Code Rule 223 mandatory for buses, coaches and trams
records.description: We want the Government to change the law to make Highway Code Rule 223 mandatory, requiring motorists to give priority to buses, coaches and trams when it is safe to do so, especially when they signal to pull away from stops, to improve the safety of passengers and other road users.
records.further_details: Some motorists accelerate past buses, coaches or trams instead of giving priority, sometimes entering the path of oncoming traffic and forcing others to brake suddenly. Bus passengers may be standing or without seat belts, so sudden braking can cause serious or potentially fatal injuries. A bus may carry dozens of people. Making Rule 223 mandatory could discourage dangerous manoeuvres, protect passengers and other road users, and improve public transport safety and reliability.

records.title: Fund free buses for all people under 18 in England
records.description: Easy transport to and from a place of school/work.

records.title: Modernise the law on mental health and criminal responsibility
records.description: Review and reform the law on criminal responsibility in England and Wales so courts can consider whether a recognised mental, developmental, neurological or personality disorder substantially impaired a defendant’s rational judgment, understanding or behavioural control.
records.further_details: The current insanity rules date from 1843 and lag behind modern psychiatric understanding. Although prosecutors can consider mental health when deciding whether prosecution is in the public interest, we want a stronger statutory framework requiring relevant expert evidence to be considered before prosecution and, where a case proceeds, when determining criminal responsibility, not only at sentencing. Diagnosis alone should not be an automatic defence.

records.title: Extend Employment Tribunal Time Limits to 10 Years
records.description: We call on the Government to extend the time limit for Employment Tribunal claims from 3 months 90 days to at least 10 years. We believe the current limit is too short and prevents many workers from seeking justice for issues such as unfair dismissal, discrimination, whistleblowing, & unpaid wages.
records.further_details:
People often cannot act in time due to lack of awareness, emotional distress, ongoing grievances, fear of retaliation, financial barriers. In other areas of law, serious cases can be brought years later, recognising that victims may not come forward immediately. We feel that employment law should reflect similar fairness. 
We believe extending the limit would: Give workers a realistic chance to claim, Increase employer accountability, Improve compliance with employment law, Better protect vulnerable workers.

records.title: Make media get consent from people in vaccination queues before taking photos
records.description: Students, young adults and others queuing in vaccination queues at universities, clinics and elsewhere should not have to be subjected to the media taking photographs of them without getting individual consent. If individual consent is not gained faces should be blurred. Consent matters.
records.further_details: In a digital age people should have full control over their image, and being photographed in all medical settings must include queueing outside all temporary and permanent medical facilities. These queues must be treated as controlled settings where an identifiable image of a person who is about to receive medical care is considered sensitive personal data. Neurodivergent people and others may be discouraged from getting vital medial treatment when photographed by media without consent.

records.title: Amend the 2013 Code of Practice to help support essential mobile food providers
records.description: We call for changes to the 2013 Code of Practice on Noise from Ice-Cream Van Chimes to exempt or reasonably adapt rules for essential mobile food providers, including butcher vans serving vulnerable communities.
records.further_details: Mobile butcher vans & other regular mobile food vans provide essential food access to vulnerable, elderly, and housebound people who cannot reach shops. The current 2013 noise rules inadvertently treat such food vans like ice cream vans. Without a simple sound signal, many customers won’t know we’re there. We feel the law is outdated and must allow reasonable audible signals for essential services over a longer period of time each day.

records.title: Increase the minimum age to purchase paint aerosols to 18
records.description: Increase the law on the age for buying paint aerosols to 18 years old.
records.further_details: We believe the benefits of allowing youths between 16-18 to buy spray paint aerosols do not outweigh the cost and effort of removing graffiti and the risks of sniffing aerosols. Many States in USA have a minimum age of 18.

records.title: Fully subsidise core vaccinations for every dog
records.description: Fully subsidise core dog vaccinations so that no dog misses out from them and suffers from preventable and fatal diseases. Although charities offer subsidies to those eligible, the subsidies remain limited in supply.
records.further_details:
According to BSAVA, in 2023, it was estimated around 20% of dogs were unvaccinated - which leaves hundreds of thousands of dogs prone to illnesses.

It currently costs up to £100 for dog owners to vaccinate their dogs with core vaccines and around £60 for annual boosters. If the government subsidises core vaccinations for dogs, it may mean no dogs would miss out and suffer from preventable illnesses (e.g. leptospirosis).

records.title: Require all fuel stations to sell HVO
records.description: Government to mandate that HVO (Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil) must be available at the pump as a suitable alternative to diesel. This is already available at a handful of fuel forecourts in the UK, which provides a greener and cleaner alternative to diesel.
records.further_details: We think this will help the UK to reduce the net CO2 emissions, while reducing the reliance on the volatile and heavily politicised oil markets.

records.title: An independent review body for miscarriages of justice involving racial bias.
records.description: We call on the UK Government to establish an independent body to review criminal convictions where credible evidence suggests racial bias, discrimination, or unequal treatment may have contributed to a miscarriage of justice.
records.further_details:
Justice must be equal for all. Where racism may have influenced investigations, prosecutions, court decisions, or sentencing, there must be an independent route to review convictions.

This is in the public interest because racial injustice damages trust in the courts, harms communities, and risks innocent people remaining wrongfully convicted. An independent review body would improve accountability, restore confidence, and help prevent future miscarriages of justice.

records.title: Review how long prostitution related convictions stay on criminal records
records.description: Current disclosure periods can last up to 100 years from the date of conviction, meaning offences can follow people for life and make it hard to find work or change careers. We believe that people who have left or are trying to leave the sex trade shouldn’t be held back for life by old convictions.
records.further_details: We are calling for a review of these time limits.

records.title: Require full forensic autopsies for all unexplained deaths
records.description: We ask the UK Government to introduce legislation requiring that all unexplained deaths are subject to a full forensic autopsy as standard practice.
records.further_details:
Unexplained deaths leave families without answers and may risk important evidence being missed. While coroners currently investigate such deaths, we believe that practices are inconsistent and may not always include a full forensic post-mortem examination. A mandatory forensic autopsy would help ensure Greater accuracy in determining causes of death, Improved detection of criminal activity or negligence
Consistency in investigations across all regions
Increased transparency for bereaved families

records.title: Replace council tax for properties worth over £1M with a tax of 0.7%
records.description: We call on the Government to tax properties worth more than £1M by 0.7% of their value.
records.further_details: We believe that by replacing council tax for properties over £1M and taxing the property value by 0.7% per annum would bring them inline with a lot of the poorest property owners. We think this would create fairness.

records.title: Raise the legal age to buy and consume alcohol to 25
records.description: Raising the drinking age to 25 could help protect young adults’ developing brains, reduce alcohol-related accidents, and ease pressure on the NHS. Studies have found later drinking onset decreases addiction risk and improves public health, making this policy a smart, preventative measure.
records.further_details: As someone who knows the risks of alcohol and its impact on people, I think urgent action should be taken. With exam season in full swing, young people who hit the bottle if they fail their exams could be risking their own health for a substance with an unpleasant taste.

records.title: Fund targeted care package to support children with SEND during hospitalisation
records.description: Many children diagnosed with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) can face extra challenges during hospital stays, from communication, parental respite, to extra safety risks. I am calling on the government to fund targeted a care package for children with SEND during hospitalisation.
records.further_details: We call on the Government to introduce a targeted care package to improve hospital care for SEND children. We think this should include specialised beds on all children’s wards, private spaces, assigned SEND support workers, respite support for parents, better awareness of rare conditions, improved communication between teams, and recognition of parental observations during admissions, as SEND children may struggle to communicate needs or deteriorate suddenly.

records.title: Review Emergency Veterinary Care for Birds and Exotic Pets in the UK
records.description: Review the availability of 24/7 emergency veterinary care for exotic pets, including parrots and small animals. Exotic pet owners should have equal emergency support, clearer guidance, and more available emergency clinics to help prevent avoidable suffering and loss.
records.further_details: On 5 April 2026, I lost my beloved parrot, Twinkie. During an emergency, I struggled to find urgent exotic veterinary care in time. Many exotic pet owners across the UK face the same problem, with limited access to 24/7 emergency vets for birds and other exotic animals. It has now been 79 days, and I am still suffering with depression and heartbreak after losing Twinkie. No family should suffer this pain because emergency help was not available fast enough.

records.title: Review accessibility of driving tests for people with SEN
records.description: I call on the Government to review the accessibility of the driving theory test, to make it more accessible for children with special educational needs (SEN).
records.further_details: I would like the theory test to be more accessible to have two tests one for hazard perception and then another one for the multiple-choice. With all the support in place.

records.title: Severely restrict press reports on UK defence capabilities
records.description: We want the Government to place severe restrictions on the media reporting on the strength or weakness of our Army, the Royal Navy and Royal Air Force. We believe the public do not need to know this information know while our enemies do.
records.further_details: On 7 June 2026 The Mail on Sunday reported: “Entire fleet of UK attack subs is unfit for war and stuck in dock.” Sunday Express states “Labour delays leave Britain weak’ at time of war” and on 6 June 2026 the Daily Mail reported that HMS Prince of Wales has “…broken down again” and the Daily Mirror reported that the £6.3 billion Ajax armoured vehicles are “…not fit for use” in combat. We think these reports undermine our national defence.

records.title: Make Emergency Adrenaline Auto-Injectors Available in Public Venues
records.description: Allow and require public venues, including restaurants, shopping centres, leisure centres, entertainment venues and community spaces to hold emergency adrenaline auto-injectors and ensure staff receive basic anaphylaxis awareness training.
records.further_details: Anaphylaxis is a life-threatening allergic reaction that can occur within minutes. Not everyone experiencing anaphylaxis has access to their prescribed auto-injector, may require more than one dose or people may experience a severe reaction for the first time without knowing they have an allergy. Having emergency adrenaline auto-injectors available in public venues, alongside trained staff, could help save lives and improve safety for millions of people living with allergies across the UK.

records.title: Exempt OAPs from tax on interest for cash held within stocks and shares ISAs
records.description: The Government plans to charge 22% tax on interest paid for cash held within stocks and shares ISA, to stop savers trying to circumvent the new rules on ISA savings that limit cash savings to £12,000. OAPs are exempt from the limit and we believe they should be exempt from the tax.
records.further_details: OAPs can have a mixture of savings accounts with a bias towards cash savings; however, many take advantage of generous cash savings rates within stocks and shares ISAs that allow them to hold amounts of cash and stocks and shares in the same account and have made forward plans depending upon this. The ISA system was always a tax free savings system that we believe now appears to be in danger of being seriously eroded and complicated: taxation on interest within an ISA should be exempt for OAPs.

records.title: Create a statutory timescale for CQC registration & lower registration costs
records.description: New domiciliary care providers must pay for premises, software, training and a phone line before applying to CQC, with no income until registered. The CQC has no legal deadline to decide. The Government should set a statutory timescale and fund lower registration costs.
records.further_details: CQC registration can place enormous demands on applicants: complex policies and paperwork with little guidance, alongside costly requirements — all before a single client can be taken on. Yet CQC has no statutory timescale to reach a decision on registration, and we feel there is no consistency across the registration process. Applicants can face open-ended financial pressure with no certainty. The Government should reform the process to make it structured, properly supported and time bound.

records.title: Pass law to require authorities to meet needs of people with Edwards' syndrome
records.description: Give Edwards / Trisomy 18 — including mosaic forms — same legal recognition & guaranteed NHS care pathways as Down’s Syndrome Act 2022. End unfair, unsafe gaps: no automatic discharge; ensure named neuro disability leads & joined up lifelong care based on need, not diagnosis name.
records.further_details: Edwards / Trisomy 18 — including mosaic — is lifelong, complex & multi system, but no legal duty like Down’s Syndrome Act 2022. Often wrongly called “short term”, leading to unsafe early discharge from therapies & paediatrics, no named neurodisability lead & preventable harm. Support should follow need, not diagnosis prevalence. Equal law = equal safe, joined up care.

records.title: Put diplomatic pressure on Pakistan to protect human rights & democracy
records.description: We urge the UK Government to apply diplomatic pressure on Pakistan to end human rights abuses, protect free and fair elections, restore freedom of speech, stop political persecution and forced statements, uphold the rule of law, and ensure democratic rights for all citizens.
records.further_details: We ask the UK Government to use diplomatic pressure on Pakistan’s military leadership and Government to protect human rights, safeguard democracy, ensure free and fair elections, end political persecution, ensure the release of any political prisoners or guarantee fair trials, protect freedom of speech, media and peaceful protest, stop any possible use of forced political statements, uphold the rule of law, ensure an independent judiciary, and investigate any alleged human rights abuses.

records.title: Fund the purchase of empty houses & property reconstruction training
records.description: We call the Government to fund the purchase of empty houses across the country, and partnerships with local colleges to train tradesmen in converting properties back into use. This could provide relevant training & employment, create affordable rental properties and over time, become self-funding.
records.further_details: This funding policy could help train a new generation of tradesmen. It could provide affordable social housing more quickly and cheaply than building new properties, and once completed and rented out, the original investment could be paid back overtime. If the Government were to fund partnerships with local colleges, it could benefit everyone involved. We feel the original outlay is the drawback, but it would be an investment worth making for the future.

records.title: Reform Education Inspection Framework to value pupil progress
