records.description: Reform the Education Inspection Framework so that schools are assessed by individual pupil progress, inclusive practice and quality of education, not primarily overall attainment and aggregated performance data.
records.further_details: Schools should be judged fairly, recognising that some pupils with SEND or complex needs may not reach the same attainment levels or be able to access standard assessments. We believe the current inspection framework should place greater emphasis on individual pupil progress, quality of teaching and inclusive practice, so inspections better reflect the work schools do to help every child achieve their potential.

records.title: Make sporting events involving UK nations Category A events so it’s free-to-air
records.description: Make all international sporting events involving UK national teams Category A events to ensure they are not blocked by paywalls and are free-to-air and view on television for the entire country to see and enjoy.
records.further_details:
The recent Commonwealth Games were moved behind a paywall that so many could not access and therefore watch. We feel this is terrible for sport, as those athletes lose the chance to gain recognition, and it’s terrible for the country as many people cannot afford pay per view or are not tech savvy to use apps to stream these events.
 
We believe everyone should be able to get behind and support national teams and sportspeople competing for national teams, and we risk losing our national identity and pride when only some of the nation can view these events.

records.title: Require stronger safeguarding standards for social media live streaming.
records.description: We want the Government to introduce stronger safeguarding and moderation requirements for social media live-streaming platforms, including real-time moderation, improved reporting tools, intervention procedures for high-risk broadcasts, and enhanced protections for vulnerable users and children.
records.further_details: Live streaming is a major feature of platforms such as TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and Twitch. We believe current safeguards do not always provide adequate protection from harmful, abusive or high-risk behaviour broadcast in real time. We want stronger regulatory standards to improve moderation, reporting, intervention procedures and protections for vulnerable users and children, helping to create safer online environments and reduce the risk of harm.

records.title: Ban Politicians from Profiting off Social Media Engagement
records.description: Prohibit MPs and elected public officials from earning financial income - including ad revenue, creator pay-outs, platform subscriptions, and brand deals - from social media platforms while holding public office, ensuring public service remains focused on constituents rather than private profit.
records.further_details: Politics and social media monetization should never be mingled. Under current rules, elected representatives can profit from online algorithms that reward sensationalism, creating a direct conflict of interest. The sole duty of Members of Parliament must be public service, not generating revenue through digital platforms. We call on the Government and House of Commons to amend parliamentary rules and ban all sitting MPs from earning ad revenue, creator pay-outs, and sponsorships online.

records.title: Remove VAT from sunscreen and sunblock
records.description: Skin cancer is increasing in the UK, with around 3,800 deaths reported annually. We believe sunscreen and sunblock should not be subject to VAT due to being a cosmetic product, and should be fully exempted from VAT.

records.title: Make deliberate parental alienation a criminal offence & review child abuse law
records.description: We want the Government to make deliberate parental alienation a specific criminal offence. The Government should also launch a review into laws such as the Children Act 1989 and other laws to examine any gaps and recognising deliberate parental relationship abuse as a form of psychological abuse.
records.further_details: The Children Act 1989 and subsequent legislation provide family-law remedies but no specific offence for deliberate parental alienation. While the Domestic Abuse Act 2021 and Serious Crime Act 2015 can cover some controlling or coercive conduct, we feel neither specifically addresses deliberate destruction of a parent-child relationship. We believe the Government should close this gap with a proportionate, evidence-based offence and safeguards for genuine safeguarding concerns.

records.title: Apologise for Britain’s role in the Partition of British India in 1947
records.description: We call on the Prime Minister to issue a formal apology for Britain’s role in the Partition of British India in 1947, and for the innocent lives that were lost, which is estimated to be up to 2 million.
records.further_details:
For hundreds of years, diverse communities in India co-existed prior to the British colonisation of India, which lasted over 200 years. We feel British rulers separated Hindus and Muslims into different political groups, which resulted in religious identity becoming more important than a shared national identity.
 
We believe that Britain, which was bankrupt after the Second World War and eager to withdraw, introduced the Indian Independence Act 1947 and asked a British lawyer to draw the new border, leading to the Partition, which caused mass migration, regional disparities and impacted millions of lives.

records.title: Require AI agents to identify themselves when making unsolicited contact
records.description:
Introduce legislation requiring any AI agent that initiates unsolicited contact with a person to clearly disclose that it is an AI at the beginning of the interaction.

This should apply to AI agents contacting people by phone, voice call, text message or other conversational messaging services.
records.further_details:
AI systems can increasingly hold natural conversations, use realistic human voices and present themselves using human names.

When an organisation chooses to use AI to initiate contact with someone who has not asked to be contacted, we believe the recipient has a basic right to know immediately that the interaction is with AI.

Disclosure should not depend on the person asking.   If AI initiates the conversation, AI should identify itself.

records.title: Restore the £100,000 care fee threshold and £86,000 lifetime cap on care costs
records.description: We call on the Government to implement the adult social care charging reforms legislated through the Health and Care Act 2022: raising the upper capital threshold for means-tested support in England from £23,250 to £100,000, and introducing an £86,000 lifetime cap on eligible personal care costs.
records.further_details: In our view under the current system, families who spent decades saving and paying off a home lose everything they built, effectively asset stripped, to pay privately owned care homes, which can charge in the region of £5k to £10k a month. The reforms we are asking for were scrapped in July 2024 by the incoming Labour government. We ask that the current government immediately reverse this, in order to protect working families across England.

records.title: Make Insurance and coaching Qualifications Mandatory for Sports Coaches
records.description: Make it a legal requirement for all sports coaches to hold an Enhanced DBS, appropriate First Aid qualification, insurance and recognised coaching qualification before coaching independently. Allow trainees to coach only under the direct supervision of a qualified coach or mentor.
records.further_details: This petition calls for a consistent legal minimum standard for anyone coaching sport. Coaches should hold an Enhanced DBS, First Aid qualification, suitable insurance and a recognised coaching qualification. This would improve safeguarding, safety and professional standards across all sports. Trainee coaches, volunteers and those gaining experience should still be able to coach under the direct supervision of a suitably qualified coach or mentor, providing a clear pathway into coaching.

records.title: Review regulations & legal protections in relation to people in supported living
records.description: People in supported living may face inconsistent standards & limited oversight. Families & deputies are not always fully involved in decisions. We call for a review of the regulations and legal protections in place to improve accountability, safeguard rights, to ensure consistent standards of care.
records.further_details: We believe that supported living lacks full regulation, creating gaps in oversight. We want the Government to extend regulation, strengthen the role of families and deputies, and provide clear legal guidance, including on restricting contact and decision-making.

records.title: Review ASB’s cumulative harm and improve system coordination
records.description: Antisocial behaviour (ASB) can have a serious cumulative impact on health, sleep and the ability to work. In our view, responses are often uncoordinated, with no clear accountability. This petition calls for recognition of ASB and improved response coordination between services.
records.further_details: In our experience ASB is often treated as low-level crimes, but repeated exposure can harm the surrounding community leading to poor sleep, health and negative impact on the ability to work. ONS data shows high volumes of ASB, and local authorities receive hundreds of thousands of noise complaints annually. Yet we believe responses are often fragmented across authorities with no clear responsibility, leaving people living with ongoing harm despite repeated reporting.

records.title: Fund Psychiatric Liaison Practitioners in all GP surgeries
records.description:
Fund the employment of a dedicated psychiatrist in all GP surgeries to help 
support surgery with the drafting and oversight of titration and cross-tapering plans, and providing medication reviews as needed.
records.further_details:
GPs manage the mental health support for many patients, but often lack the specialist training. In our view, the lack of specialist input can lead to:
• Patients left on doses that are too high or switched between medications without adequate protocols, leading to severe withdrawal,
• Side effects like "emotional numbness" or "akathisia" being mismanaged, leading to loss of quality of life and, in some cases, increased risk of suicide
• Patients reaching crisis point, putting pressure on A&E

records.title: Bring all vehicle insurance into public ownership
records.description: I want the Government to bring all vehicle insurance completely into public ownership, which I believe would bring pricing down for younger drivers and stop the guessing games regarding the average claim/crash data causing surcharges in insurance.
records.further_details: I want the Government to do this to stop the exploitation of young drivers who already earn barely anything and are expected to pay thousands just because of the area they live in, their age or the vehicle they chose. Bringing vehicle insurance completely into public ownership will allow for the Government to set a specific rate based on age or vehicle, increasing costs for any declarations such as penalty points etc. this will increase the amount of money going into the public budget as well and allow full control.

records.title: Fund legal aid for all SEN parents to take SEN Teams to court for loss of job
records.description: Due to local council SEN team failures, many children are unable to access education and as a result parents lose careers and incomes to care for their children. These parents have no access to legal aid to get compensation.
records.further_details: Enable SEND parents/Carers to access legal aid to take legal action against SEND Teams within local authorities for loss of secure employment, careers and the financial loss caused by failures to follow the SEND law, statutory guidance and responsibilities. We are concerned that many Parents and Carers are forced out of jobs due to consistent, repeated, avoidable failures by Local authority SEN Teams resulting in relying on benefits, financial difficulties and poverty.

records.title: Ban pet-owner discrimination during the tenancy application process
records.description: Make it unlawful for landlords and letting agents to discriminate against prospective tenants with pets during the rental application and screening process. The Renters’ Rights Act must protect applicants, not just existing tenants.
records.further_details: We believe the Renters’ Rights Act protects existing tenants but fails prospective ones. We are concerned that landlords and agents routinely use pre-viewing questionnaires to screen out applicants who disclose they have a pet. Because some protections only apply after signing a contract, we feel responsible pet owners are systematically excluded before they can even view a property. We want robust measures during the application phase to ensure everyone has equal access to housing.

records.title: Require those selling a property to provide a survey instead of the buyer
records.description: We want the Government to require in law people who are selling a property to provide a full survey for potential buyers.
records.further_details: Currently, sellers have little to no visibility of the details of surveys undertaken on their property, which are often used as a bargaining tool, while buyers often pay for expensive surveys even when purchases end up falling through. We believe there needs to be more transparency for all parties involved.

records.title: Mandate statutory licensing for installing and maintaining solid fuel appliances
records.description: We call on the UK Government to mandate statutory licensing for installing, servicing, or sweeping solid fuel appliances, mirroring the Gas Safe Register.
records.further_details: We are concerned that unregulated "cowboy" operators can pose severe carbon monoxide and fire risks, while broken "sign-off" loopholes in current Competent Person Schemes can be exploited. We believe voluntary associations fail to enforce safety and resist reform. For public safety, we want those who work with solid fuel burners to be legally regulated like gas and oil with strict, binding protocols.

records.title: Protected Community and Public Service Flags category in flag-flying regulations
records.description: We want the UK Government to create a Protected Community and Public Service Flags category in planning regulations, allowing recognised NHS, Armed Forces, veterans, emergency services, Pride and disability flags to be flown without planning consent for clear, consistent rules.
records.further_details: Recent uncertainty around the display of Pride flags has highlighted inconsistencies in current guidance. Some recognised flags can be flown without consent, while others may require permission, creating confusion for councils, schools, NHS bodies and community groups. This petition calls for a new Protected Community and Public Service Flags category to provide clear, consistent rules for recognised NHS, Armed Forces, veterans, emergency services, Pride and disability flags.

records.title: Fund better availability on the NHS for CBD oil for autistic people
records.description: My son as well as many other children & others who have severe autism, as well as many other struggles & are suffering, need help fast to give them access to better quality of life & treatment accessible through the NHS to end their & their families suffering. We believe CBD oil can help them
records.further_details: My 8-year-old son is severely autistic and faces extreme challenges every day. He experiences behavioural hypervigilance, frequent meltdowns, self-harm, and lashing out. His struggles with ARFID lead to refusal to eat and consequential weight loss. As a parent, I am desperate to find solutions that allow my son and other individuals to live a better life, and I believe that being able to access CBD oil on the NHS could be a vital part of that solution. Reports show that there is a growing body of evidence that supports the efficacy of CBD oil.

records.title: Ban alcohol advertising in petrol stations
records.description: We call on the Government to ban alcohol advertising, including promotional displays and marketing, in petrol stations. Alcohol can be linked to addiction, poor mental health, physical illness and social harm. Yet, petrol stations display alcohol through signs, offers and promotions.
records.further_details:
For people in recovery, this can be a trigger and may increase the risk of relapse during routine activities such as refuelling.
 
We believe petrol stations are essential services, not places where people should be confronted by alcohol promotion. Reducing exposure could support public health and protect vulnerable people. We therefore urge the Government to introduce legislation prohibiting alcohol advertising, promotional signage, and marketing displays at petrol stations.

records.title: Limit Motorway Speeds to 60mph for all vehicles
records.description: To reduce emissions, fuel consumption, accidents and maintenance, we call for a limit on motorway speeds for all vehicles to 60mph. Fuel consumption and C02 emissions varies strongly with speed so we think this is more than proportional.
records.further_details: Vehicle emissions contribute strongly to climate change and action is required to limit the damage. No one can ignore the growing frequency of extreme weather and yet we believe that little strong action is taken unilaterally. In our view fuel spending sends UK money abroad and a reducing speed can also save fuel. This change may feel like inconsequential government intervention but, like seatbelts, we think it’s the right thing to do. Slower speeds can also mean less car maintenance is needed.

records.title: Fund Behavioural Coaches in all UK primary schools
records.description: The government to fund dedicated behavioral coaches or therapists in every primary school. Many neurodivergent pupils, particularly those with autism, display distress behaviors that are communication, not intentional misbehavior. Without specialist support, these children are often misunderstood.
records.further_details: ​Providing in-school behavioral specialists will help pupils understand their own needs, equip teachers with vital strategies, and reduce permanent exclusions. This proactive approach will relieve pressure on overstretched CAMHS services and ensure every child receives the right support at the right time.

records.title: Legislate to ensure second hand cars remain affordable for ordinary people.
records.description:
• Open OBD2 diagnostic and part coding.
    • Mandate 10-year transferable warranties.
    • Enforce service schedules that promote longevity.
    • Ban proprietary fastenings.
    • Standardise VED to a flat rate.
records.further_details: The soaring cost of used vehicles prices working people out of essential transit. Public transport is often non-existent, making a private car necessary for jobs and childcare. High dealer fees, software locks, and a corporate culture of planned failure artificially drive up prices. Protecting independent garages and guaranteeing parts availability will lower repair costs and keep cars affordable.

records.title: Introduce an emergency Universal Credit top-up for 66-year-old citizens.
records.description: Implement the Work & Pensions Committee's 2026 report recommendations. Introduce an emergency Universal Credit top-up for 66-year-olds by late 2026. This boost must bridge the severe £600/month income gap between working-age benefits and Pension Credit caused by the State Pension age rise to 67.
records.further_details: The State Pension age rise from 66 to 67 leaves 66-year-olds on standard Universal Credit (£425/month), a £600 shortfall from Pension Credit (£1,031/month). Only 42% can work due to health and age barriers. When the State Pension age rose to 66 in 2020, poverty more than doubled to 24%. The Treasury will save £10.5bn from the change; we believe investing £600m of this windfall to fund this top-up by December 2026 is an economic and moral necessity to protect vulnerable citizens from destitution.

records.title: Ban food delivery companies from paying riders 'per delivery'
records.description: Many delivery apps such as Uber Eats and Deliveroo currently pay riders a 'per delivery ' fee, instead of an hourly rate. We think the government should ban this and enforce hourly pay of at least minimum wage.
records.further_details: Many delivery apps such as Uber Eats and Deliveroo currently pay riders a 'per delivery ' fee, instead of an hourly rate. We think the government should ban this and enforce hourly pay of at least minimum wage.

records.title: Review requirement for B2 English language for experienced HealthCare Workers
records.description: We want the Government to review the need for B2 English language requirement for Health and Care Worker visa applicants and allow experienced workers who have already demonstrated effective English communication in UK health and social care roles to be deemed to meet the B1 English requirement.
records.further_details: Many Health and Care Worker visa applicants have already worked in the UK for two or three years before applying for a Skilled Worker visa. They communicate daily in English with patients and colleagues. We ask the Government to review this policy and allow experienced workers to be deemed to meet B1 English or prove their English through an Ecctis-recognised degree.

records.title: Ban travel insurance companies’ premium hikes for people who take medication
records.description: Ban travel insurance companies charging a premium for people who take medication, for example for high blood pressure and cholesterol. We think this is unnecessary if the person is taking their medication has their condition under control.

records.title: Review and strengthen CMS investigations of paying parent income
records.description: We want the Government to review and strengthen Child Maintenance investigations to ensure hidden or understated income are identified, including through financial and lifestyle evidence, ensuring children receive a fair contribution from both parents.
records.further_details: We call on the Government to review and strengthen Child Maintenance investigations to ensure that when declared income may not reflect true financial means this is addressed. Investigations should consider hidden cash income, businesses held in partnership or other names, assets, dividends, property and significant lifestyle spending, inc holidays. In our view, receiving parents should not have to uncover hidden income themselves. Child maintenance is money for children, not a loophole for adults.

records.title: Add the FA Community Shield to the listed events regime to make it free to view
records.description: For over a century, the FA Community Shield has been a symbol of unity & charity. Originally the Charity Shield, it raised funds for grassroots football & was free for all to watch. Pay per view excludes this. We call on the Government to ensure that the Community Shield becomes free to view again.
records.further_details: For over a century, the FA Community Shield originally the Charity Shield has been a symbol of unity, tradition, and charity, raising funds for grassroots football. For decades, it was free for all to watch on TV, embodying football’s inclusive spirit. In 2025 it became pay per view. Football is the people’s game, and its traditions should reflect accessibility and community. We call on the Government to ensure that the Community Shield is again free to view. Sign to reclaim our shield!

records.title: Mandate that child benefit is paid in full alongside SGO allowance
records.description: We call on the Government to mandate that local authorities pay special guardianship order allowance in full, no matter if the family is receiving child benefits. SGO carers provide children with stable homes and should be provided with full financial support.

records.title: Speed up Innovator Founder Visa decisions and enforce processing deadlines
records.description: Require the Home Office to resolve Innovator Founder visa applications within the 8-week service standard and create a priority escalation channel for delayed business visas. Protracted delays can harm UK startup growth, disrupt international investment, and damage Britain’s tech economy.
records.further_details: Startup founders in the UK often face Home Office processing delays, some exceeding 12 months for 8-week Innovator Founder visas. These extraordinary delays can force companies to cancel investor meetings, miss international launches, and pause critical operations, threatening business survival. We want the Government to enforce statutory deadlines, introduce mandatory progress updates for delayed files, and establish a dedicated business help desk to protect UK innovation and economic growth.

records.title: Fund statutory grants for all suicide-prevention third sector organisations
records.description: Fund permanent statutory grants that are directly paid to third sector suicide prevention and crisis organisations, so that their core operating costs are fully paid for.
records.further_details:
We believe national suicide prevention funding is unsustainable, as many vital, non-profit organisations rely on unstable public donations to survive. When they fail, the impact can be devastating. We have already seen this with Papyrus entering administration, forcing its Hopeline247 service to close.
 
The closure of vital charities and third sector organisations that aim to prevent suicides have diverted vulnerable people back to an overstretched NHS. We believe the Government should provide secure, ring-fenced funding for frontline suicide prevention charities and third-sector organisations.

records.title: Exempt GP surgeries from the recent increases in employer national insurance
records.description: We call on the Government to exempt NHS GP surgeries from the recent Employer National Insurance increases. We are concerned that GP surgeries are being taxed like private businesses, draining vital funds directly from frontline patient care.
records.further_details: We believe General practice is in need of saving more than ever. We are concerned the recent NIC increases and wage uplifts are costing average surgeries unprecedented amounts each year. Unlike private businesses, practices cannot pass these costs onto patients. Without an exemption or full financial reimbursement, we are concerned surgeries will be forced to cut clinical staff, reduce appointments, or close their doors permanently. We urge the government to protect our local GPs to prevent the deterioration of community healthcare."

records.title: Extend the Riding Establishments Act to cover all commercial horse activity
records.description: We call on the Government to extend the Riding Establishments Act, so anyone running a commercial business providing riding, horse care, equine therapy, instruction, horse loans or other organised activities involving horses must meet appropriate licensing, welfare, safety and competency standards.
records.further_details: Commercial riding establishments under the Act already require licensing from councils, with inspections and welfare standards. However, gaps can exist where businesses provide other equine services, such as horse care, equine-assisted activities, therapy, horse loans, instruction or livery. We call on the Government to extend the legislation and introduce proportionate licensing covering commercial activities involving horses, ensuring consistent welfare, safety, competency and accountability standards.

records.title: Introduce statutory safeguarding checks for users of online dating platforms
records.description: Introduce legislation requiring regulated dating apps to verify users’ identities and participate in a government-administered Dating Safety Check for serious sexual, domestic abuse, stalking and violent offences, without giving dating companies access to users’ criminal records.
records.further_details: Millions now use dating apps to meet strangers, yet users may have little way of knowing whether someone has a serious history of sexual violence, domestic abuse, stalking or violence. People have been assaulted and killed after meeting through dating apps, and offenders can move between platforms. A government-run Dating Safety Check could add protection while keeping criminal-record data out of private companies' hands and preserving privacy, appeals and rehabilitation.

records.title: Allow nursing homes to have a stock of anticipatory medication for all users
records.description: Nursing homes should be permitted to hold a central stock of anticipatory end-of-life medication
records.further_details: Nursing homes should be permitted to hold a central stock of anticipatory end-of-life medications for use when prescribed and clinically indicated for any service user. This would enable rapid symptom control, prevent distress caused by delays in accessing medication, and reduce unnecessary hospital admissions at the end of life. Timely access to these medications supports compassionate, person-centred care and allows individuals to remain in their preferred place of care.

records.title: Mandate First Aid Kits in all cars & defibrillators in cars listed over £49995
records.description: Make it a legal requirement for a first aid kit (meeting BS 8599-2) to be provided at the point of sale of all new cars and all used cars when sold through a motor trader, and a defibrillator to be fitted in new cars with a list price over £49995.
records.further_details: At the scene of a serious road traffic collision, another motorist is often the first person on scene. The Highway Code gives guidance on what to do in an emergency (Annex 7) and advises that motorists carry a first aid kit. First aid kits are mandatory in many EU countries but not yet in the UK. Single use "defibs" cost around £300 and could be cost-effective to fit in new cars with a list price over £49,995.

records.title: Ensure a minimum wage for work experience which is educationally mandatory
records.description: I want  the Government to make employers pay their work experience interns (e.g. a T-Level, BTEC, etc.). I believe that this would give students a more realistic view of working, be motivational & encourage qualifications other than A-Levels. This wage can be at level lower than the minimum wage.
records.further_details: Students on vocational qualifications like T-Levels and BTECs must complete work placements as part of their course, yet unlike apprentices, they receive no pay despite contributing real work. We believe this is financially unfair and discourages students from choosing vocational routes over A-Levels. A reduced minimum wage for placement students would make these qualifications more attractive, support students financially, and give them a genuine experience of working life.

records.title: Introduce regulation for infant care and sleep advice providers
records.description: We want the government to ensure individuals who work in the parenting space, advising on the health and wellbeing of infants, toddlers, children and families to be tightly regulated to prevent harm.
records.further_details:
Introduce regulation for infant care and sleep advice providers, including mandatory standards for training courses and qualifications.
This should include:
Regulation and quality assurance of training courses and certification pathways
Recognised minimum qualification requirements
Supervised practical experience before working with clients independently
A requirement to follow evidence-based guidance aligned with NHS and public health recommendations
Oversight by an appropriate body

records.title: Exempt Electric Vehicles with an RRP up to £60,000 from Expensive Car Supplement
records.description: Call on the Government to raise the list price threshold for the Vehicle Excise Duty (VED) "Expensive Car Supplement" (Luxury Road Tax) for zero-emission vehicles from the current limit to £60,000 for all such vehicles manufactured from April 2025 onwards
records.further_details: The current £50,000 threshold still captures many essential family-sized EVs, effectively penalising drivers for making a sustainable choice. Increasing this to £60,000 would better reflect the current market prices of long-range electric vehicles and further incentivise the transition to net-zero by making cleaner transport more affordable

records.title: Require audio recordings of supervised contact sessions in family court
records.description: We call on the Government to require audio recordings of supervised family contact sessions, including social work interviews and safeguarding meetings, to be played in family court proceedings.
records.further_details: Families may often rely on written notes that can affect court outcomes and their children’s futures. Recordings could improve transparency, accuracy, accountability and fairness, reduce disputes, and protect children and vulnerable families. We believe parents and carers should be allowed to make recordings, with safeguards for confidentiality and welfare.

records.title: Review evictions of care home residents
records.description: We call on the Government to conduct a review of the use of evictions in care homes. We are concerned that some care homes issue evictions when they receive complaints from residents.

records.title: Youth-only referendum on all decisions directly targeting those aged 11-18
records.description: On all laws directly targeting young people aged 11-18, young people of those ages should be consulted via a youth-only referendum. For example the Social Media ban or lowering the voting age to 16. We believe this can be easily achieved by having votes in form times across secondary schools.

records.title: Fund a memorial to recognise the Royal Indian Navy’s contribution in WW2
records.description: Fund a memorial that formally recognises the Royal Indian Navy’s WW2 service and Royal Indian Navy veterans. Eighty years later, there is no standalone memorial. We feel their families have carried this erasure long enough.
records.further_details: The Royal Indian Navy served the full duration of WW2, growing more than tenfold by 1945. Ratings received no equal pay, no compensation, and faced racial discrimination. After victory, those who struck for dignity were furloughed or punished. No UK memorial exists. My grandfather served 1938–1946 as a signals specialist, earned the VSM, and was honourably reinstated. Britain never formally acknowledged him. We are asking for the UK Government to do this at last.

records.title: Mandate assessment of manual handbrake use in practical driving test
records.description: Require automatic handbrake and hill hold assist, to be switched off during a driving test, to check if a driver can use a handbrake. The coordination required for a hill start isn't to be ignored.
records.further_details: Driving tests do not always assess the use of a handbrake, but many cars 17yo's are guided to buy by motoring organisations typically have one. Nobody should be expected to do a hill start using the handbrake, for the first time, after passing. What if someone parked behind them on a hill? Some instructors are teaching in cars that lack the basic controls learners need to manage. I feel if you don't learn to use a manual handbrake, then like with a manual gearbox, you're not ready for it.

records.title: Review Universal Credit assessment periods for monthly paid workers
records.description: We ask Government to review Universal Credit assessment rules and introduce an optional monthly earnings averaging method for claimants with regular monthly pay to reduce artificial fluctuations caused by assessment period timing.
records.further_details: Many claimants are paid monthly, but Universal Credit assesses earnings by fixed assessment periods linked to payment dates reported via HMRC RTI. This can cause artificial fluctuations in entitlement, including months with £0 payments or adjusted overpayments, despite stable income. We believe an optional monthly averaging method would better reflect real earnings and improve financial stability for working households.

records.title: Make travel insurance compulsory for UK residents travelling abroad.
records.description: Require UK residents travelling overseas to hold travel insurance that includes emergency medical treatment and repatriation cover before departure.
records.further_details: Many UK travellers go abroad without travel insurance, leaving families exposed to huge costs if a medical emergency, serious accident, or death occurs overseas. Medical treatment and repatriation can cost tens of thousands of pounds, often leading families to seek public donations. Travel insurance is usually inexpensive compared to the cost of a trip and can prevent significant financial hardship. Mandatory cover would encourage responsible travel planning and protect families.

records.title: Exempt video-sharing platforms from any proposed social media bans
records.description: Exempt video-sharing platforms from any proposed social media bans for under-16s.
records.further_details: We call on the government to legally classify video repositories separately from social messaging apps. Proposed social media bans threaten to block sites like YouTube, which lack user-to-user private messaging. For millions of young people—especially neurodivergent individuals—such platforms can be an essential lifeline for education, creative expression, and cognitive regulation. The government must safeguard access by regulating these platforms under a separate framework rather than a blanket ban.

records.title: Introduce Hot Weather Payments
records.description: Some people already benefit from cold weather payments to offset high utility bills in winter. The same should be avaliable for hot weather to offset higher utility bills
records.further_details: Every winter, we benefit from cold weather payments, which provide crucial support to manage the increased utility bills when heating our homes. However, the scorching summer months present a similar issue, with utility costs rising significantly due to the need for air conditioning and fans to combat the extreme heat. For many households, the financial strain of keeping cool is just as burdensome as heating in the cold months.

records.title: Require FCA-regulated Open Banking providers to offer personal-use data-access
records.description: Open Banking rules let banks share account data with FCA-authorised companies, but most only offer this to businesses, not individuals. We ask the Government to require FCA-authorised Account Information Service Providers to offer an Applicant Programming Interface (API) for personal-use tier.
records.further_details: Open Banking regulation was meant to give consumers control of their own financial data, but live access is provided to business only, often requiring £100+/month with Know Your Customer (KYC) checks individuals cannot meet. Some banks offer no personal API at all, even to premium customers. We believe this stops ordinary people using their own data-access rights for personal budgeting or tracking tools. We want FCA-authorised providers to be required to offer low-barrier (i.e. cost) API access for individuals, separate from business pricing.

records.title: Make 10 years to get ILR to All Care Workers & Low-Income Workers already in UK
records.description:
Extend the ILR Route to 10 Years for Care Workers and Low-Income Workers Already in the UK
We call on the UK Government to extend the ILR qualifying period from 5 to 10 years for care workers and low-income workers already living and working in the UK.
records.further_details: This could allow more time for economic contribution through work, taxes, and NHS surcharges. ILR granted under this route should not provide immediate access to public funds, helping to ensure fairness for taxpayers and protecting public services.

records.title: Introduce use of drug-detection dogs to the House of Commons
records.description: We call on the House of Commons to implement certified drug-detection dogs to detect and deter the presence of illegal substances and to be used to conduct regular, unannounced sweeps of the House of Commons estate.
records.further_details:
We think this could help:
 
Maintain integrity: Parliament must uphold the laws it creates.
 
Ensure safety: A drug-free workplace ensures a safe environment for all staff, visitors, and officials concerned with decision-making in public office.
 
Public confidence: Implementing visible deterrents restores and maintains public trust in democratic institutions.

records.title: Ban hardware manufacturers from monopolising storefronts & limit media ownership
records.description: Require hardware manufacturers to allow third-party digital storefronts and open media distribution on their devices. Update consumer law to introduce the right to resell digital media, and ban platforms from selling revocable licenses as ownership.
records.further_details: Hardware manufacturers often restrict all digital media sales to their own marketplaces. In our view, this gives manufacturers full control over sales, ownership and the sources of digital media. Customers can often not resell digital media after use, with licenses for media being presented and sold as ownership while reserving the rights to revoke access to the content from the customer. We believe that forcing open media distribution routes will increase competition and revive the industry of small/independent artists.

records.title: Make “Making Tax Digital” voluntary for businesses with turnover below £120,000
records.description: Make “Making Tax Digital" (MTD) voluntary for businesses with a turnover below £120,000.
records.further_details: This could help small businesses avoid any extra costs, complexities, and labour required to convert to MTD. It could also provide businesses the option to change to MTD if it suits their businesses.

records.title: Introduce regional stamp duty thresholds for first-time buyers
records.description: Create a fairer stamp duty system for residential first-time buyers by introducing region-specific, tiered stamp duty thresholds based on regional housing costs, with independent review, five-year updates, and consideration of transitional relief for those affected by April 2025 changes.
records.further_details:
We believe the current £300,000 first-time buyer Stamp Duty threshold does not reflect regional housing costs. A first-time buyer’s home may cost around £180,000 in Yorkshire compared with around £465,000 in London, meaning support varies by location. 
 
We want a tiered threshold system based on regional housing costs, reviewed every five years against inflation, house prices and affordability. This could help more people move from renting into ownership, improve housing mobility and support the wider market.

records.title: Combine time spent on Skilled Worker & dependant visas to count towards ILR
records.description: We believe skilled workers, their children and families are suffering from current rules. We call on the Home Office to allow visa holders to combine their time on a Skilled Worker visa as a dependant and the main applicant, so it counts towards their 5-year Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) route.
records.further_details: Currently, switching between main applicant and dependant statuses resets the ILR qualifying time to zero. We believe this rule is unfair and forces legal, taxpaying families who have lived and worked continuously in the UK for 5 years to start over. It can result in severe financial distress through redundant visa fees and HIS surcharges. We call on the Home Office to change this rule.

records.title: We need a Cabinet Minister for Mental Health immediately.
records.description: This post would work together with the Health Secretary to join up NHS, charities and other existing services, to share knowledge, stop silo working between organisations which wastes money and resource, spearhead new initiatives and push much-needed mental health reforms.
records.further_details: The Prime Minister has previously described mental health as the issue of our times. Reports have suggested that two-thirds of the UK population will suffer from mental ill health in their lifetime. Many children, young people and adults cannot get the care, help and support they need. We believe this MUST be national priority and this area requires specific expertise, focus and dedication that a Health Secretary cannot provide. We feel a Mental Health Minister would provide that total focus to benefit millions who are suffering.

records.title: Update DfT guidance & give motorcycles access to all bus lanes
records.description: We call on the Government to update DfT guidance and make it a universal default rule to allow motorcycle access to bus lanes. We feel fragmented regulations and conflicting signage create unnecessary confusion, leading to unfair fines for riders moving between different council boundaries.
records.further_details: Allowing motorcycles into bus lanes could improve road safety by reducing the need for risky traffic filtering. It could also ease overall congestion and lower emissions without hindering bus operations. We ask the Government to update national guidance and make bus lane access the default rule for motorcyclists.

records.title: Inquiry into historic forced labour in laundries
records.description: Launch a national public inquiry into the forced labour of girls in mostly Catholic-run laundries. Investigate state oversight failures and establish a financial justice scheme for victims.
records.further_details: For decades, vulnerable girls were confined in church-run laundries under conditions amounting to modern-day slavery. Residents endured unpaid forced labour and psychological abuse, often enabled by a complete breakdown in state oversight and social services. While Northern Ireland has opened historical investigations, we feel national accountability is urgently required. The public must know how authorities allowed this to happen. We demand total transparency and formal accountability.

records.title: Fund free bus travel for unpaid carers
records.description: We want the Government to extend and fund free bus travel for unpaid carers. We believe it is prudent to raise this issue due to the money unpaid carers lose in travel time when doing carer duties, as well as the money they save the Government by doing their role.
records.further_details:
We believe unpaid carers serve both the person they're caring for and the country, and that the service they offer saves the Government costs in social care, and often results in carers incurring their own unpaid expenses.
 
One example is bus travel to collect shopping, medicines and other caring duties. These costs add up but the service they provide save the country money at the same time by reducing reliance on other public services. We should offer free bus travel to unpaid carers.

records.title: Fund retraining schemes for employees displaced by AI
records.description: Provide funding for proactive retraining schemes targeted at workers displaced by AI. Investing in upskilling now can protect the UK tax base, reduce the future burden on the welfare system, and fill skill shortages in emerging sectors. Failing to act may lead to severe economic inequality.
records.further_details:
AI risks mass unemployment in the UK, shifting any new tech jobs and tax gains to the USA. The UK government must plan for such an event with retraining schemes:
 
- Prevent structural unemployment
- Protect the tax base
- Maintain consumer spending
- Proactive training is cheaper than long-term Universal Credit payments.
- Lower NHS strain
- Fill existing skill gaps

records.title: Reform Army medical entry standards to reduce unnecessary rejections
records.description: The UK Government should urgently review and reform Army medical entry standards, including JSP 950, so applicants are assessed on current health, prognosis and role suitability, with greater use of individual assessments, medical waivers and independent appeals.
records.further_details: Around 32,000 Army applicants were reportedly rejected on medical grounds in 2024–25, while the Army continues to struggle to meet recruitment targets. Medical standards are essential, but applicants with historic or resolved conditions may be excluded despite being fit to serve. The system should focus more on current health, individual circumstances, prognosis and the requirements of the role, rather than relying too heavily on past medical history.

records.title: Require manifesto delivery plans & general election if not met
records.description: Require every elected UK Government to turn its manifesto into a measurable delivery plan with independent scrutiny, clear KPIs and milestones. Major deviations must be transparent and evidence-based, with consequences for persistent failure, triggering an early General Election.
records.further_details:
Governments should be independently assessed against their published manifesto delivery plans, with clear performance thresholds and critical milestones established at the start of their term. 
 
We believe persistent failure to meet these commitments should trigger a mandatory, independent review and a parliamentary accountability process. Any significant changes to commitments or performance targets should also be transparently justified using independently verified evidence. Where predefined failure thresholds are reached without sufficient justification, a formal mechanism should be established and triggered to enable an early General Election. We also want to ensure the Government does not have sole discretion to waive or redefine these requirements.

records.title: Align UK standards on pesticides with equivalent EU standards
records.description: The Government has failed to ban some pesticides that the EU has already prohibited as being harmful. These include Dimethomorph, for which there is evidence that it can harm human reproduction, and Benthiavalicarb, for which there is evidence linking it to cancer.
records.further_details: This petition calls on the UK Government to align UK standards on pesticides with the EU and to ban pesticides already prohibited by the EU.

records.title: Require employers to have inclusive job application processes for neurodivergent
records.description: Require employers, regardless of sector, to have fully inclusive application procedures. Prospective employees should be allowed to apply by whichever means is appropriate for them, provided they supply all information required (e.g. full employment and education history for safeguarding purposes).
records.further_details: We believe the current system, whereby employers can have their own application forms in differing formats and often will not accept a CV (despite all the information on the form being in a standard CV), is not at all inclusive. For many neurodiverse people, the mere idea of a longwinded form can make our brains freeze due to executive disfunction. This can be highly frustrating, particularly if form requires completion in one sitting or the job is advertised on a site that already holds all relevant information.

records.title: Commission an independent review of NICE guidance on Lyme disease treatment
records.description: We ask the Government to urgently set up an independent review of the effectiveness of NICE’s Lyme disease guideline NG95. We believe further treatment should be based on each patient’s clinical findings, response and risks—not a fixed, one-size-fits-all limit.
records.further_details: Many patients report remaining severely unwell after standard Lyme disease treatment but also report being told they are adequately treated, without further investigation or a clear NHS pathway. Many can then spend tens of thousands seeking private care in the UK or overseas. We believe a review is needed to ensure those who require more than two rounds of antibiotics can access them, with individual assessment, specialist oversight and safety monitoring, rather than imposing a fixed, one-size-fits-all limit that may leave patients without care.

records.title: Provide funding to offer free continuous glucose monitors to all type 2 diabetic
records.description: In order to help type 2 diabetics manage glucose levels the government should provide funding to offer continuous glucose monitors to all type 2 diabetics. We think this measure could help save the NHS money by helping to educate and thus reduce diabetic complications such as amputations.

records.title: Criminalise care provider abuse of Skilled Worker license & stop judicial review
records.description: We call for immediate revocation of license to sponsor care workers for companies who have been found to extort or abuse their sponsored staff, without the option for judicial review. This behaviour should be criminalised.
records.further_details:
We also call for funding for training for those involved in investigations around care worker license abuse.

In my view, health care in the UK has been buttressed by migrant workers since the 1940s. The certificates of sponsorship effectively delegates immigration duties to licensed CQC registered care providers, however some care providers abuse this and breaches the conditions of their license, by extorting or abusing their sponsored staff.

records.title: Introduce a public right to trigger a national vote of no confidence
records.description: Introduce legislation giving UK voters the right to trigger a national vote of confidence in the Government if a petition reaches a defined threshold of verified support, with clear rules for the vote and its constitutional consequences.
records.further_details: Create a legal right for UK voters to trigger a national vote of confidence in the Government between General Elections. If a petition reaches 5% of the registered UK parliamentary electorate within six months, verified by an independent authority, a national vote must be held. Parliament must establish safeguards against fraud and repeated votes, and define the constitutional consequences if the Government loses the vote.

records.title: Fund subsidised school uniforms
records.description: Please help many families by funding subsidised school uniforms so that people don't have to go into their overdraft or use buy now pay later to be able to afford them. This is becoming more of a reality for many people that simply don't have the funds to afford it.
records.further_details: Most would agree, this can really help the people and families who don't have that much wealth to afford a mandatory thing.

records.title: Hold a referendum on the use of military force or assets for overseas actions
records.description: We want the Government to hold a public referendum on the use of military force overseas and the use of UK military assets by foreign powers for their own affairs (unless not using military force or allowing asset use would directly contravene a treaty with such as NATO, for example).
records.further_details: We live in a democratic state and we feel the people should have some say in our military affairs - this would avoid our nation becoming involved in unnecessary and/or unpopular conflict. We believe our military should fight on behalf of the British people - not for powerful foreign states.

records.title: Recreate Northumbria and grant it nation status
records.description: We believe Yorkshire, Durham, Tyne and Wear, Cumbria and Northumberland should come to together and be Northumbria again. We believe being a part of England has limited us so much and having a bit of independence and leaving England to be our own nation within the UK will be the best for us.
records.further_details: We need the government to help us get the ability to vote for our nation status and to gain it so we have our own Northumbrian government and our own country within the UK.

records.title: Introduce cost protections and transparency of charges for commercial tenants
records.description: Cap costs for commercial tenants by requiring landlords to limit electricity resale rates at Ofgem’s Maximum Resale Price, ensure transparent and challengeable service charges, ban hidden building insurance commissions, and establish a Commercial Tenant Tribunal for dispute resolution.
records.further_details: Commercial tenants have fewer legal protections than residential tenants. In our view, landlords can charge any electricity rate they choose, profit from inflated building insurance commissions, and issue unjustified service charges. The only recourse is civil court, inaccessible for most small businesses. We therefore call for a cap on electricity rates, a transparency requirement for service charges and building insurance commissions alongside a Commercial Tenant Tribunal.

records.title: Review the Evidence Allowed in Domestic Abuse Investigations
records.description: Review the evidence allowed in domestic abuse cases including loosening rules on admitting psychological assessments of lie detector tests, access to school and youth offending records to look at past aggression and violent tendencies, family cycle of abuse, and statements from ex partners.
records.further_details: We are concerned that domestic abuse that happens in private behind closed doors rarely leads to convictions because there is so little evidence to prove a pattern. Many cases collapse as “he said/she said.” Making it possible or easier to use psychological assessments, lie detector tests, school and youth offending records, family abuse history, and ex partner statements could give CPS the tools to show repeated harm and hold abusers properly accountable.

records.title: Reform Hospitality Visa Rules to Protect Rural Tourism and Local Economies
records.description: Reform hospitality visa rules to support rural and coastal businesses. Introduce regional salary thresholds, expand shortage occupations and simplify sponsor licences to reduce costs for SMEs. Without urgent action we are concerned staffing shortages will continue damaging tourism & local economies
records.further_details: Many hospitality businesses across rural and coastal Britain are facing severe staff shortages despite active recruitment and rising wages. We believe current visa sponsorship rules and salary thresholds are heavily weighted toward London economies and are unrealistic for regional operators. Without urgent reform, many businesses are reducing opening hours, limiting services and risking closure, damaging tourism, local employment and the wider economy.

records.title: Remove references to Roman Catholics as popish & papist in British legislation
records.description: In the Claim of Right 1689 & Bill of Rights 1689, Roman Catholics are referred to as papists & popish. These references should be removed from these statutes & from any others that are currently in force.
records.further_details: It is expressly stated in the countries’ most reputable dictionaries that these terms for Roman Catholics are offensive, yet they are embedded in British legislation in provisions which are stated on the legislation website to be live.

records.title: Ban debt collection when domestic abuse is being investigated
records.description: Require banks and lenders to stop debt collection from suspected victims of domestic abuse while their cases are being investigated.  This could be called the TAB law.
records.further_details: This proposed law would make it entirely illegal for collectors and bailiffs to attempt to enforce debt collection once domestic abuse has been identified or is being investigated to give the victim time to escape their abuser. Courts can then confirm what will happen with the debts after investigations are concluded. Debt collection may proceed only after it has been established who the debt belongs to.

records.title: Increase funding for Hyperhydrosis treatment and reduce NHS wait times
records.description: I want the UK government to increase funding for NHS dermatology services and introduce measures to reduce waiting times for patients seeking treatment for hyperhidrosis. This could include expanding specialist services, increasing staffing, and improving access to effective treatments.
records.further_details: The effective treatments include treatments such as iontophoresis, medication and other clinically approved options. Hyperhidrosis is a medical condition that can severely impact daily life, confidence and mental health. Many patients face long NHS dermatology waiting times and limited access to effective, affordable treatment. Faster care and better funding is needed to improve outcomes and quality of life. Hyperhidrosis impacts work, education and finances. Due to daily task difficulties+more

records.title: Require consumer communications in the UK to use UK or ISO date formats
records.description: We want the Government to require digital services and consumer communications provided to people in the UK, including websites, apps, emails and documents, to display dates using either the UK date format (DD/MM/YYYY) or the internationally recognised ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD) by default.
records.further_details: The US month/day/year format is confusing for UK users because dates such as 7/1 or 5/8 can be interpreted differently. Many services already adapt currency, language and units based on a user's location. We believe dates should be treated the same way. Consumer-facing websites, apps, emails and documents provided to people in the UK should use either the UK date format (DD/MM/YYYY) or the internationally recognised ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD) by default.

records.title: Limit MPs' early resignation to specific circumstances & impose penalties
records.description: Although MPs cannot resign from the Commons midterm they can circumvent this restriction by use of archaic procedure and Crown offices. This may allow inappropriate change that disrupts the operation of the Commons. This petition is to limit use of this loophole to genuine need.
records.further_details:
There should be documented well-defined criteria describing circumstances that would allow MPs to resign before the end of a parliamentary term.
 
The entity that grants the right to an early resignation should be independent of any political party e.g. The Speaker, not the Chancellor of the Exchequer as at present.
 
There should be a penalty to deter MPs from resigning early including repayment of any parliamentary allowances received and being barred from standing as an MP in the future.

records.title: Review Accessibility Standards for Disabled Guests at Concert Venues
records.description: Require concert venues and ticket providers to provide equal access for disabled guests. Review fairness of ticketing, suitable accessible seating, enforced visibility protections, trained accessibility staff, and mandate refunds where accessibility failures prevent enjoyment of events.
records.further_details: Disabled concertgoers often face barriers when booking tickets and attending events. Accessible tickets may be harder to obtain, unavailable online, or released later than general tickets. Accessible seating can have poor views or be obstructed by standing spectators. Venues vary in how they manage these issues, leaving disabled guests with an inconsistent experience. Clear legal standards are needed to ensure equal access, fair treatment, and proper support at live events.

records.title: Remove the age cap on the Lifelong Learning Entitlement (LLE)
records.description: We want the Government to remove the maximum age limit of 60 to be eligible for tuition fee loans under the Lifelong Learning Entitlement (LLE), ensuring that adults of all ages have equal access to higher education and skills training.
records.further_details: We believe restricting Lifelong Learning Entitlement (LLE) loans to the under-60s is ageist and undermines true lifelong learning. As people work longer and state pension ages rise, continuous upskilling is vital for older adults. We feel barring those aged 60+ from tuition loans ostracises a growing demographic, blocks career transitions, and sends a harmful message that older citizens' personal development no longer matters. We urge the government to remove this age cap immediately.

records.title: Provide direct funding to charity shops
records.description: Some charity shops are closing down due to rising costs of rent and energy bills. We urge the government to cut rent and energy bills for charity shops, give grants to shops that are struggling financially and pledge to support them.
records.further_details: Charity shops provide vital income for charities - some are struggling due to the cost of living and decreased donations, and this is limiting their impact. Charity shops are also essential as they give young people chances to volunteer, reduce waste in this climate crisis and help families buy used items during the cost of living crisis. The closure of further charity shops will be devastating.

records.title: Allow Migrant Skilled Worker to do 20 hours of supplementary work in any sector
records.description: Remove sector-specific occupation restrictions on the allowed 20 hours of supplementary work. Let visa holders use these part-time hours to, for example, help struggling local independent businesses, across any industry, rather than limiting them to their primary code or the Immigration Salary List.
records.further_details: We think the current 20-hour rule is flawed. Some contracts ban working for competitors in the same sector, which we think can result in some visa holders feeling trapped. We think removing sector limits can let skilled workers help struggling high street businesses facing staffing crises. As a second job under HMRC’s tax codes, a significant portion of every pound earned is instantly paid as income tax. This can generate vital revenue to boost public funds and support public services, all from existing skilled workers and without increasing net migration.

records.title: Fund new university routes & support for disadvantaged mature students with ADHD
records.description: Fund the creation of new, accessible pathways for adults from disadvantaged backgrounds who were diagnosed with ADHD or similar conditions later in life, including alternative entry routes and financial support, particularly for mature students pursuing essential professions such as dentistry.
records.further_details:
Many adults grow up with trauma, alcoholic or absent parents, and little educational support. They are then diagnosed with ADHD later in life and may leave school with grades that do not reflect their ability.
 
We ask the Government to fund the creation of new university pathways, alternative entry routes, and support for disadvantaged adults with late diagnoses. We believe childhood trauma and undiagnosed conditions should not prevent someone from reaching their potential.

records.title: Scrap the proposed 20p return scheme for single-use containers
records.description: We want the Government to scrap the planned Deposit Return Scheme (DRS) scheduled for October 2027. We believe charging an extra 20p per bottle or can acts as an unfair upfront tax on everyday households and creates a massive logistical and financial burden for small independent retailers.
records.further_details:
We believe the scheme penalises families by artificially inflating the cost of a weekly grocery shop before they can claw their money back. It could also force small convenience shops to store empty, dirty containers or face heavy fines. 
 
We feel existing kerbside recycling bins are already widely used and highly effective. Instead of introducing a complex 20p deposit system that disrupts local businesses and increases living costs, the Government should focus on improving the current recycling infrastructure.

records.title: Require Family Inclusion During Treatment for Psychosis and at Discharge
records.description: We call for a mandatory family inclusion protocol when someone is admitted and treated for psychosis under Section 2/3 of the Mental Health Act (MHA) and when they are considered for discharge.
records.further_details:
We think this can ensure families receive clinical information needed for safety, continuity of care, and relapse prevention. 
 
In our view current consent based practices for including families do not fully account for impaired capacity, delusions, or lack of insight. We think families are denied information about medication, risk factors, therapeutic interventions, deterioration, and discharge planning. We believe this exclusion places families at risk, undermines relapse prevention, and leads to repeated crisis. Furthermore we think discharges are being done back into family homes without stabilisation, safety planning, or information that families need to provide effective support.

records.title: Ensure emergency alerts in Wales are received in English & Welsh simultaneously
records.description: During the recent wildfire alert in Wales some people received a Welsh-only message that triggered an alarm but could not be understood by some. In our view this caused confusion and unnecessary stress.
records.further_details:
Issuing alerts in both Welsh and English simultaneously could ensure vital safety information is available to all.

When people cannot interpret an emergency message instantly, they can experience a physical stress response before they can assess the situation. This reaction can increase heart rate, blood pressure and breathing which can be a dangerous physical trigger for vulnerable people such as the elderly or anyone with heart conditions, hypertension, COPD or asthma. Everyone should be able to understand the message immediately in order to respond safely and not experience unnecessary panic and confusion.

records.title: Give employees mandatory three-month warning before redundancies can take effect
records.description: We want redundancy law changed so employers must give at least 3 months’ formal warning when redundancies are being seriously considered, before dismissal. Employers should explain general business reasons and impact, without sensitive info, giving time to find work, retrain and prepare financially.
records.further_details: Redundancy can leave people facing a sudden loss of income with little time to find another job or prepare financially. Current rules do not always give employees enough warning, particularly where fewer than 20 people are affected. A three-month early warning period would give employees time to look for work, attend interviews, retrain and plan their finances, while still allowing businesses to restructure when necessary. Employees deserve time to protect their financial security too.

records.title: Make Postnatal Mental Health Training Mandatory for Employers
records.description: Consistent requirement for employers to understand postnatal mental health and recognise how it can affect somebody returning to work.
records.further_details:
1. Mandatory postnatal mental-health training for employers – understanding PND, its symptoms and its impact on work.
2. Clear guidance for managers – supporting employees returning from maternity leave without assumptions or stigma.
3. Stronger protection from discrimination – ensuring employees aren’t disadvantaged because of postnatal mental-health difficulties.
4. A workplace support pathway – requiring employers to have clear policies and appropriate support for postnatal mental health.

records.title: Remove the Primary Earner Income Cap on the Marriage Allowance
records.description: The combination of rising living & childcare costs can force families onto one income. The £50,270 Cap stops single earners from receiving the £1,260 Marriage Allowance transfer. If removed this would provide vital £252 tax relief, ending what we feel is an unfair penalty on single-earner households
records.further_details: This cut-off seems to unfairly arbitrary & penalises single-earner households. A family where one parent earns £55,000 receives zero benefit from the unused personal allowance of the stay-at-home parent. In stark contrast, a dual-income household earning £50,000 across two jobs benefits from two full personal allowances, totalling £25,140 tax-free. This creates a severe tax penalty for families shouldering the burden of single-handedly providing for their household in a punishing economy which removing the Primary Earner Income Cap would go some way to mitigate.

records.title: Require the installation of kill switches in all new cars
records.description: Due to deaths during police pursuits, we urge the Government to require the installation of mandatory kill switches in all new cars, so they can be remotely operated in case a car fails to stop for the police.
records.further_details: With ever-evolving car technology, we want the Government to mandate the installation of remote kill switches in all new cars. This could be made available to the police to operate remotely should a car fail to stop for them.

records.title: Allow children’s homes to recruit skilled overseas care workers
records.description: We believe children’s care homes should be allowed to recruit and sponsor skilled workers from overseas to work in front line care for children. There are many skilled workers that children’s homes cannot recruit due to restrictions.
records.further_details: This change could eliminate the skilled worker crisis, where many skilled workers cannot work in the UK due to immigration restrictions. These people are skilled and many children’s homes require their services as they can provide care to children.

records.title: Funding for Postgraduate Loans to cover actual course fees & living costs
records.description: Provide funding to increase the maximum Postgraduate Master's Loan allocation provided by Student Finance England (SFE) and introduce a separate maintenance element to ensure postgraduate education is financially accessible to all students from all socio-economic backgrounds.
records.further_details: A person's financial status should never be a barrier to their academic ambitions. The current maximum Postgraduate Loan (SFE) of £13,206 is expected to cover both tuition fees and basic living expenses. Many postgraduate students do not have the capacity to work as much as they need to support themselves. The government must urgently review this. Improving postgraduate finance is not a luxury; we believe it is a structural necessity to fuel the Government's own Local Growth Plans.

records.title: Review the regulation of new-build warranty providers
records.description: Review current regulations to make new-build warranty providers strictly liable for structural defects. We are concerned about flawed local authority sign-offs being used to reject claims or deflect liability to developers when independent structural evidence is provided.
records.further_details: Mortgage lenders often require new-build warranties to release funds. Yet when surveyors expose severe structural defects, warranty providers can refuse to act. We believe there are loopholes which can be exploited, using flawed council sign-offs to deny liability, bouncing buyers back to developers who endlessly delay repairs. A review must look at how to ensure warranty providers are legally compelled to honour claims and introduce strict financial penalties.

records.title: Require exam boards to provide resources to new A-level/BTEC students & teachers
records.description: We want the UK Government to require exam boards to provide accessible revision materials and mock papers for new first-year A-level and BTEC students, and clear communication with teachers about assessments, marking requirements and grade boundaries.
records.further_details: We are concerned that students studying new AS-level, A-level and BTEC qualifications can face a significant disadvantage because there are fewer revision resources, mock papers and past papers available while they are being introduced. Teachers can also lack clear information from exam boards about assessment and marking expectations. All A-level students should have access to basic, free online revision materials and sufficient practice papers, with clear communication between exam boards and teachers.

records.title: Require frontier AI firms to fund independent public-safety oversight
records.description: Require frontier AI developers to collectively fund an independent UK public-safety capability, with competitive technical pay and guaranteed access to relevant systems and evidence. Developers must have no influence over its staff, methods, priorities or conclusions.
records.further_details: Frontier AI companies employ many of the people best able to assess their systems, while equity and salaries make it difficult for public bodies to recruit and retain comparable expertise. Voluntary access can also be withdrawn. A statutory industry levy should fund independent evaluators, secure compute and long-term recruitment and retention benefits, with guaranteed access to qualifying systems and safety evidence and no industry influence over their work.

records.title: Review penalties for disruptive and dangerous parking
records.description: We want the Government to conduct a review of existing powers to issue fines where cars are blocking emergency gates or parked in an anti-social way, for example leading to others having to reverse dangerously on main roads when cars are blocking turn around areas.

records.title: Regulate education guardians and residential summer courses for under-18s
records.description: Introduce statutory regulation of education guardians acting in loco parentis for international pupils in UK schools: mandatory registration, enhanced DBS checks and safeguarding and mental health training. Set minimum standards and inspection for residential courses for under-18s.
records.further_details: Schools require overseas parents to appoint an education guardian, but there are no legal requirements for the training, safeguarding qualification or criminal record check of the education guardian. Over 21,000 non-British pupils whose parents live overseas board at UK independent schools (ISC Census, 2026); in 2019 fewer than a quarter had an accredited guardian (IICSA, 2022). Residential summer courses for under-18s have no specific national minimum standards. In 2022 the Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse recommended licensing and registration of guardians, but this has not been enacted.

records.title: Require specific child-safety assessments for AI companion products
records.description: Require companies developing AI companion or toy-like products likely to be used by children to complete and publish a child-safety assessment before the product is sold in the UK, including evidence that children with SEND have been considered in testing.
