records.further_details: There are currently no clear, specific requirements to assess the psychological or developmental safety of AI companion products before they reach the UK market. These products can give inaccurate, biased or age-inappropriate responses and may encourage emotional attachment, dependency, over-trust or simulated friendship. Assessments should consider impacts on social development and specifically assess risks for children with SEND. Parents should be given clear risk information before purchase.

records.title: Exempt UK on-call firefighters from income tax on their fire service earnings
records.description: We want the Government to change tax policy to make all earnings, allowances, and fees paid to on-call (retained) firefighters completely exempt from income tax.
records.further_details: Many fire and rescue services have reported difficulties recruiting on-call retained firefighters. Some on-call engines are routinely unavailable due to staffing shortages. We believe it is unfair to tax those protecting communities as a secondary job. Retained firefighters often disrupt their primary careers and families. We think taxing this emergency care deters new recruits. Exempting these earnings could boost recruitment, retain vital crew, and keep the public safe.

records.title: Review and amend ‘balance of probability’ criteria for police misconduct
records.description: Review and amend the “balance of probability” standard in police misconduct cases. We believe the current low threshold risks dismissal following flawed or incomplete investigations, with inadequate disclosure. Stronger safeguards are needed to ensure fair, thorough, and evidence-led outcomes.
records.further_details: Decisions in police misconduct cases can end careers and damage lives. We are concerned that the “balance of probability” standard allows dismissal even where investigations are incomplete or evidence is not fully disclosed. This can risk unfair outcomes and undermine trust in the system. We think stronger safeguards are needed to ensure investigations are thorough, transparent, and evidence-led before such serious decisions are made

records.title: Review compliance process for financial orders in divorce settlements.
records.description: We believe similar enforcement to CMS mechanisms should exist for financial orders made in divorce proceedings, so that once a court order is made, compliance is monitored and enforcement action can begin automatically if the order is not followed.
records.further_details:
Currently, if a person refuses to comply with a court-ordered financial settlement, the other party must return to court and apply for enforcement, causing further financial hardship, delay, and stress. This system can allow ongoing financial or economic abuse after separation.
 
We believe that once a judge has made a legally binding financial order, the court system should be made to monitor compliance and begin enforcement automatically if the order is not followed.

records.title: Increase Upper Capital Threshold to qualify for social care financial assistance
records.description: We want the Government to increase the £23,500 Upper Capital Threshold to qualify for financial assistance for social care by at least the rate of inflation. We believe it’s wrong that since 2010 it's not increased. If it shad increased, it would be over £37,000 by now.
records.further_details: People work all their life to buy a home or save to help their children only to become old and frail & then have to sell their homes to pay for care. Some may then only leave £23,250 for their children and loved ones minus their funeral expenses.

records.title: Issue guidance to schools on packed lunches for SEND students
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce guidance to schools, ensuring that children who have SEND needs are allowed to have their safe foods in their lunch boxes, including puddings at nursery.
records.further_details: We believe that preventing students with SEND needs from having their safe foods in their lunch boxes risks these children going hungry as a result.

records.title: Review the requirements for permission to take children on holiday
records.description: The Government should review the current requirements for parents who are sole carers of children but share parental responsibility to take their children out of the UK for a holiday.
records.further_details: The sole carer will usually have the passports and birth certificates. We believe they should not need to rely on another parent to decide whether or not they can go on holiday abroad. We are concerned that this allows abuse and control over the parent who wants to go on a family holiday with their children. This affects many victims of domestic abuse.

records.title: Mandate that local authorities provide community spaces for everyone
records.description: Introduce a new statutory duty requiring local authorities to meet a minimum standard of community space provision. Every resident must have access to a free or low-cost community space within a 15-minute walk (approximately one mile) of their home, or via accessible public transport.
records.further_details:
Despite recognition in planning policy that community facilities are important, provision is inconsistent and declining.

There is no statutory minimum standard for access to community spaces. Hundreds of community facilities, libraries and day centres have closed in the past decade

As a result, individuals — particularly those experiencing addiction, homelessness, mental health challenges or social exclusion — are increasingly left without safe, supportive environments.

records.title: Introduce Mortgage Interest Tax Relief & Help First-Time Buyers Keep Their Homes
records.description: Some first-time buyers who spent years saving for their home are now facing repossession, not through recklessness, but because of unexpected increases in interest rates. We are asking the Government to temporarily exempt mortgage interest from tax for those most at risk, before it is too late.
records.further_details: First-time buyers on high interest rates are in danger of losing homes they often spent years saving for. We propose a simple scheme: anyone paying above 3% interest on a first home gets partial tax relief on monthly interest, capped by property value and income. We believe  this should be time-limited, regionally adjusted for London, and automatically end when rates fall to 3% or below. We think this is targeted, fair, and far cheaper than the cost of multiple repossessions.

records.title: Integrate the EASS into the EHRC and restore EHRC statutory duties
records.description:
My petition calls on the Government to:
- Integrate the Equality Advisory and Support Service (EASS) into the EHRC.
- Restore the EHRC’s statutory duty to provide legal advice, conciliation, and strategic casework.
records.further_details:
In 2010 the EHRC’s helpline and conciliation services were removed. Reports indicate that this, along with cuts to legal aid, resulted in a 50% reduction in the number of disability discrimination claims.
 
In 2016 the House of Lords Select Committee on the Equality Act 2010 and Disability called for:
 
1. return of the EASS helpline to the EHRC
2. restoration of conciliation and direct legal advice.
3. integration of helpline data into strategic enforcement.
4.development of in-person and accessible legal support.
 
We feel these changes are long overdue.

records.title: Review traffic policing priorities, powers and resource allocation
records.description: We want Government to set up an independent review of traffic policing priorities, enforcement powers & resource allocation to ensure resources are focused on serious crime, dangerous driving, road safety threats & accident response, & ensuring traffic enforcement is proportionate to actual risk.
records.further_details: Many people believe police resources should prioritise tackling robbery, theft, violent crime, dangerous driving and serious road safety risks rather than low-risk traffic offences with limited impact on public safety. This review should consider greater use of camera networks and automated enforcement where appropriate, whether penalties are focused on conduct that creates a genuine safety risk, and whether offences such as middle-lane driving on otherwise empty roads should attract penalties where no danger, obstruction or disruption has occurred. The Government should publish the findings and consider reforms that improve public safety and confidence in traffic policing.

records.title: A Degree Should Lead to Opportunity, Not Unemployment
records.description: I want the UK government to introduce a National Graduate Employment Guarantee to ensure every UK graduate has access to paid work experience, internships or graduate employment within 12 months of completing their degree.
records.further_details: Thousands of graduates leave university expecting their degree to lead to a career, but many spend years applying for entry-level jobs only to be told they lack experience. Many graduate with significant student debt but have no guaranteed access to meaningful work experience. We believe every graduate should have the opportunity to gain paid work experience or graduate employment within 12 months of completing their degree through a National Graduate Employment Guarantee.

records.title: Require utility companies to provide ongoing accessible advice on charges
records.description: Require utility companies to provide ongoing, accessible reminders when contracts end & cheaper options are available. We think customers shouldn’t face avoidable charges because they miss a single notification, and that companies must improve support, including disabled and neurodivergent people.
records.further_details: Many people miss renewal points due to busy lives, disability, or complex admin systems. We do not think that a single email is enough protection when companies can change prices significantly at contract end. Providers should be required to actively alert customers multiple times and through different channels. The same systems they already use to sell and promote upgrades should be used to warn customers and offer cheaper options. This could reduce the “loyalty penalty” so people are not overcharged.

records.title: Impose a one-year 1% additional tax on all annual salaries to fund UK defence
records.description: Impose a temporary 1% tax on the annual salaries of all working individuals for one year. The revenue would go solely to funding improvements in the UK’s military capabilities.
records.further_details: This could bolster the UK’s defence and protection during potential future conflicts, and thereby safeguard the security of future generations.

records.title: Introduce a statutory right to paid caring leave
records.description: Introduce paid statutory leave for employees who are caring for seriously ill or elderly relatives.
records.further_details: Current carer’s leave is often unpaid, forcing many to take annual leave, reduce their working hours or leave work. As the UK’s population ages, more employees will have caring responsibilities. This could help reduce financial hardship, support mental wellbeing and recognise the vital contribution of unpaid carers.

records.title: Remove the speed limit on motorways
records.description: We believe the current rules are outdated and there is no need for them anymore, as cars are much safer now than they were 60yrs ago - so remove the speed limit on motorways.
records.further_details: Current rules were brought in 1965 when cars were much different and more dangerous than they are to us now. We believe cars have been much safer for years, and there’s no reason at all to not remove the speed limit, with a lot of European countries upping theirs. Make the English motorways like most German autobahns. Having driven on there myself a quite a few times, I feel it is far safer driving there than UK motorways.

records.title: Retrospective ban on restrictive NDAs and non-derogatory clauses
records.description: We urgently call on the Government to amend the Employment Rights Act to ensure that the proposed bans on restrictive NDAs and non-derogatory clauses apply retrospectively.
records.further_details: We demand amendments to the Employment Rights Act to make the NDA ban retrospective. We believe the 2027 draft leaves past victims permanently silenced under threat of legal penalties, letting predatory employers hide historic wrongdoing. We demand: Retrospective Effect: Void all historic clauses silencing disclosures of workplace abuse and harassment. Victim Amnesty: Grant legal immunity to individuals speaking out about past abuse.

records.title: Require airport drop-off payment window to be at least 7 days before penalties
records.description: We call on the Government to require airports to allow reasonable payment window, such as 7 days, before issuing penalties for drop-off charges. In our view, drivers who intend to pay should not face disproportionate fines for missing short deadlines. Penalties should target deliberate non-payment.
records.further_details: We understand that airport drop-off charges can help manage congestion, but we think that the move to automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) systems has created unfair penalties for simple mistakes. As airports rely more on online payments, drivers may not realise they must pay straight away after leaving. A longer payment window, such as 7 days, could allow airports to recover fees while ensuring penalties target deliberate non-payment rather than honest short-term forgetfulness.

records.title: Swap the rates of Class 1 National Insurance contributions
records.description:
Currently, Class 1 NI contributions are (annually):
 
0% for income between £12,570,
8% for income between £12,570-£50,270,
and 2% for income above £50,270.
 
I want the Government and the Treasury to commit to making the lower band pay 2%, and the higher one paying 8% instead
records.further_details:
People with incomes up to £88,000 could see a reduction in their National Insurance bill under this proposal, which accounts for the vast majority of the formally employed workforce.
 
I think this would be a good policy to help alleviate cost of living pressures for the most vulnerable and for the majority of working people, whilst ensuring that those on higher incomes contribute more to our welfare system and our NHS, both of which are under significant pressure at the moment.

records.title: Fund textbooks for core subjects in all primary schools
records.description: We call on the Government to provide funding to ensure primary schools in England provide curriculum-aligned textbooks for core subjects. Textbooks help support structured learning, independent study, home learning and equal access, while complementing—not replacing—teachers and digital resources.
records.further_details: Many children with SEND benefit from routine, repetition and consistent learning resources. We call on the Government to provide funding to ensure all primary schools provide curriculum-aligned textbooks alongside existing teaching. Textbooks can help pupils revisit learning at their own pace and support parents at home. They could reduce anxiety caused by fragmented resources and help promote equal access to education. We believe they can also encourage independence, improve confidence and provide a familiar resource throughout the school year.

records.title: Make it a legal requirement to have a fire extinguisher in your house.
records.description: We want the Uk government to make it a legal requirement for every house hold to own a fire extinguisher. This is to save lives and to help people financially.
records.further_details: This petition is about decreasing the risks of a house fire and people dying from fires. Not only can it be used in house holds, but a fire extinguisher can be used in near by fields or woodlands. Fire fighters may not have the time to get to your house, so it is always a wise idea to have a back up option.

records.title: Make Deaf Awareness Training Mandatory for All Social Work Students
records.description: Social workers work with deaf children, deaf adults, deaf parents and families every day. Yet we are concerned that many social work students can qualify without receiving what we believe to be meaningful training on Deaf awareness, communication barriers, accessibility or the rights of deaf people.
records.further_details:
We believe this needs to change, and that every student training to become a social worker should receive compulsory Deaf Awareness training before qualifying, including practical education on:
 
- Communicating effectively with deaf and hard-of-hearing people.
- Understanding the limitations of lip-reading and spoken communication.
- Understanding British Sign Language (BSL), interpreters and other communication support.

records.title: Amend the Patient Safety Commissioner’s remit to cover all NHS-funded healthcare
records.description: Amend the Medicines and Medical Devices Act 2021 so that the Patient Safety Commissioner’s core duties extend beyond medicines and medical devices to promoting patient safety across all NHS-funded healthcare in England.
records.further_details:
Patient safety concerns can arise from diagnosis, treatment, communication, clinical records and continuity of care, and can involve several NHS services or organisations.

The Patient Safety Commissioner’s statutory remit is currently focused on medicines and medical devices. We believe patients should have an independent national commissioner able to identify systemic safety concerns across NHS-funded healthcare and ensure patients’ experiences inform improvements in safety.

records.title: Require the publication of value-for-money assessments for asylum accommodation
records.description: Require the Home Office to publish standardised, value-for-money assessments before approving new asylum accommodation. This should compare all suitable options and explain any possible decision to not select the option offering taxpayers the best overall value.
records.further_details:
We support a fair distribution of asylum accommodation across the country. An area’s affluence should neither exclude it nor justify spending more taxpayer money.
 
Assessments should compare whole-life costs, including acquisition, adaptation, security, transport and impact on local services. Safety, suitability and residents’ welfare should remain essential.
 
Where a costlier option is selected, the Government should publish its reasons. Fair distribution and responsible spending should go together.

records.title: Tighten rules for triggering emergency alert system notifications
records.description: On August 14th 2026, we believe the EAS was misused. UK government used this vital safety system to push an informative message to the nation despite, in our view, there being no active threat to life. Many have now disabled the notification meaning they won’t have it when a threat arises.
records.further_details:
The emergency alert system should be used for active threats to life. Not having a BBQ is not that in our opinion. We think the message sent nationally in August was merely informative.
 
Millions found this to be an anxiety inducing event as the EAS is seen by the public as a serious emergency. Many are disabling this on their phones, reducing public safety in the event of a true emergency in the future. The conditions around what should be an acceptable trigger need to be reviewed and tightened to prevent mis-use of the system in the future.

records.title: Require clover seed in grass seed mixtures sold for lawns and amenity use
records.description: Amend the Seed Marketing Regulations 2011 so that grass seed mixtures marketed for domestic lawns and general amenity use must contain at least 5% white clover seed by weight, with an exemption for fine and sports turf, and publish the evidence assessment underpinning that threshold.
records.further_details: England’s species abundance is about 67% of its 1970 level (Defra, EIP 2025), and the Environment Act 2021 requires Ministers to halt that decline by 2030. Four species now provide around half of Britain’s nectar (Baude et al., Nature, 2016). White clover is native, and its short flower tube feeds honeybees, short-tongued bumblebees and solitary bees. It also fixes nitrogen, cutting fertiliser use and run-off. It was standard in lawn seed until herbicides recast it as a weed.

records.title: Fund rapid assessments and early intervention for non-verbal autistic children
records.description: We are concerned that thousands of non-verbal autistic children in the UK miss the peak neuroplasticity window (ages 0-5) to gain speech due to multi-year SEN wait times. We urge the Government to fund guaranteed immediate, specialised speech therapy upon referral for non-verbal autistic children.
records.further_details: Multi-year waiting lists force parents to watch their children lose out on essential communication skills during their peak developmental years (ages 0-5). Leaving non-verbal children without early intervention can limit their future independence and increases long-term social care costs. We urge the Government to guarantee funded, specialised communication support immediately at the point of referral, reduce diagnostic backlogs, and ensure no child is left behind due to system delays.

records.title: Review child maintenance loophole of including stepchildren in child support
records.description: The government need to review the loophole paying parents use of adding a new partners children who are not the paying parents children to lower the payments they make as money is being taken away from biological children they rightfully deserve for non biological children
records.further_details: Often paying parents exploit the loophole of adding a new partners children to their child maintenance account as a way to lower the payments and take money from their biological children who they legally have to support in favour of no biological children who they legally don’t have to support and who are already supported by two parents so the biological children are losing out on money they are legally entitled to which is unfair on the children and puts strain on the other parent

records.title: Independent body for Clare’s Law applications involving serving police officers
records.description: Change the law to require Clare’s Law applications involving serving police officers, police staff or other persons creating a police-related conflict of interest to be handled independently of the police, and strengthen mandatory training and confidentiality protections for Clare’s Law.
records.further_details: I am bringing this petition because of concerns about conflicts of interest, confidentiality and safeguarding where the subject is a serving police officer. I call for the law to require independent handling in such cases, better national training for police on DVDS, and clear statutory duties to record, investigate and independently review suspected confidentiality breaches. This would strengthen accountability and public protection.

records.title: Give Local Authorities Powers to Remove Vehicles from Private Driveways
records.description: Current laws leave homeowners powerless when vehicles are left on their driveways without permission. We call on the Government to give local authorities powers to identify owners, require removal within 48 hours, and recover all associated costs from offenders.
records.further_details: We believe homeowners should have a quicker legal remedy when vehicles are left on private driveways without permission. Current laws often treat these incidents as civil matters, leaving property owners with limited practical options. We call on the Government to introduce powers allowing local authorities or accredited recovery operators acting on their behalf to identify vehicle owners and remove unauthorised vehicles after a 48-hour notice period.

records.title: Exempt reproductive coercion victims from child maintenance obligations
records.description: Change the law so parents who were victims of legally proven reproductive coercion, including being lied to about their partner’s fertility or contraception, are exempted from compulsory child maintenance obligations.
records.further_details:
The UK Government’s statutory guidance framework on controlling or coercive behaviour recognises deception around contraception as reproductive coercion, yet we feel there are no protections within child maintenance law for parents who can prove they were deliberately deceived into parenthood.
 
We believe reproductive autonomy and informed consent should apply equally to men and women, while ensuring the resulting child’s welfare is protected. Individuals should only be exempted if it is legally proven that they were a victim of reproductive coercion, rather than situations where contraception simply fails.

records.title: Government should pay National Insurance for full-time students aged 16-21
records.description: Young people aged 16-21 are encouraged to stay in education as full-time students but lose out on National Insurance contributions that would count toward their state pension. We want the Government to pay these contributions so students' pensions don't suffer a penalty for pursuing education.
records.further_details: Young people in full-time education often miss out on National Insurance contributions that would count toward their state pension. This creates a lifelong retirement penalty for doing what the Government recommends. We believe paying NI contributions for full-time students aged 16-21 would protect their retirement security while supporting education goals. We think this would be a modest investment that would remove a barrier to staying in education.

records.title: Introduce a National Parent & Child Parking Permit for children aged 4 & under
records.description: Introduce a national Parent & Child Parking Permit for parents and carers of young children, with eligibility for children aged 4 years old and under.
records.further_details: Parent-and-child spaces are to make parking safer & easier. However, there is no nationally recognised permit for these. This means parents can arrive at a car park & find spaces being used by vehicles without young children, with no consistent national system for checking eligibility. We propose the permit remain until the child’s fifth birthday. Parents face difficulties in busy car parks, including safely removing children from seats, managing pushchairs & keeping children away from traffic.

records.title: Fund more entry level roles for NHS graduate paramedics
records.description: Each year, many graduate paramedics find themselves unable to find work in their profession. We ask the Government to fund the creation of more structured, supervised early-career graduate paramedic roles across the NHS.
records.further_details:
The Royal College of Paramedics estimates that up to 50% (~1,200) of new paramedic registrants this year may not progress into professional roles on completion of their university education.
 
We believe the Government should work with the Royal College of Paramedics and NHS bodies and fund the creation of more supervised preceptorship roles (like the ambulance NQP programme) for graduate paramedics. This could ease increasing pressure on sectors such as primary and urgent care, whilst utilising a valuable workforce.

records.title: Establish UK- wide standards for accessible & ready-to-use public defibrillators
records.description: We want the UK Government to work with the devolved administrations and relevant organisations to establish consistent UK-wide standards ensuring public AEDs are accessible, registered, maintained and ready when needed.
records.further_details:
The framework should:

Set minimum standards for AED access and readiness, inc signage.
Ensure AEDs are registered on The Circuit and locatable by ambulance services.
Consistent standards for placement.
Improve integration with ambulance services.
Collect data on AED location, access, readiness Etc.
Set rules for maintenance, governance readiness.
Address geographical and socioeconomic inequalities in AED access.
Promote UK-wide standards and best practice.

records.title: Amend Administration of Estates Act 1925 to include long term fostered children
records.description: Give children and adults who were fostered by the same parent(s) for a long time the same rights as adopted children in the rules of intestacy.
records.further_details: My mother was fostered in 1952. She was with the same family for over thirteen years, leaving to get married. Mum never knew her birth parents. Mum cared for her foster mum in her old age and is named on her death certificate as 'daughter'. In 2025, mum's cousin died with no spouse or children. Under intestacy rules even though mum is the only surviving relative from her foster family she is not eligible to inherit anything because she was not adopted.

records.title: Create a national programme of police-led safety workshops for primary schools.
records.description: We ask the UK Government to create a nationally funded programme that works with police forces and schools to provide regular police-led workshops in schools for years 5 and 6 on online safety, gangs, drugs and alcohol, mental health, behaviour, future choices and transitioning to secondary school.
records.further_details: Many primary schools have previously benefited from police-led workshops on online safety, gangs, drugs and alcohol, mental health, behaviour, future choices and preparing for secondary school. These visits can help children make informed decisions, stay safe and build positive relationships with trusted adults. However, many of these locally organised visits have stopped for the foreseeable future due to staffing, availability, and approval processes. We want a nationally funded programme so all children can access this support.

records.title: Rebrand the National Living Wage as the National Minimum Wage
records.description: We call on the Government to rename the National Living Wage as the National Minimum Wage. We believe the current title is misleading, as it implies the rate is sufficient to live on when many workers still struggle to meet basic living costs.
records.further_details: We believe the term "National Living Wage" is misleading because it suggests the rate is sufficient to meet the cost of living. In reality, many full-time workers earning this wage still struggle to afford essentials such as housing, food, energy and transport. We feel the title should accurately reflect what it is: the legal minimum employers can pay, so renaming it back to "National Minimum Wage" would improve transparency and reduce public misunderstanding.

records.title: Review safeguarding & education standards in non-mainstream education settings
records.description: Launch a review into education and safeguarding standards in non-mainstream full-time education settings in England, including homeschool groups and religious settings operating as schools.
records.further_details:
We want the review to look into how to ensure these settings meet all statutory education standards, including inspections, safeguarding standards, and children attaining mainstream recognised qualifications, e.g. GCSEs.
 
We want the Government to protect children from religious extremism. The Government should close any loopholes that allow settings to avoid following mainstream school standards, and ensure all children receive a suitable education and recognised qualifications.

records.title: Establish a public inquiry into the operational performance of CQC staff & Board
records.description: The Government must set up an independent statutory public inquiry under the Inquiries Act 2005 into the operational and regulatory performance of the Care Quality Commission (CQC) staff & Board over the last decade. We feel they have failed in their duty & responsibility & must be held to account.
records.further_details: Recent independent reviews have shown that the CQC is failing in its duty to safely regulate NHS services. Some of these operational failures have resulted in patients harmed or dead. A full statutory inquiry must investigate how the CQC's leadership, inspection models, and internal cultures failed to identify or act upon systemic NHS abuses and substandard care. We believe the public and NHS patients deserve to see the CQC staff, executives and Board held accountable for their failure to keep people safe from harm.

records.title: Shorter Citizenship Pathway for foreign-born Spouses of British Citizens
records.description: Create a new shorter pathway for foreign spouses of British Citizens to apply for citizenship. The current 5 year visa, followed by an application for ILR before being allowed to apply for Citizenship is, we believe, costly and distressing for couples trying to settle in the UK.
records.further_details: Many Commonwealth nations have specific paths for foreign born spouses gaining sponsorship and residency. In Australia, Spouses can apply immediately with a 2 year visa that ends with eligibility to apply for Permanent Residency. The only delay beyond this is processing time. The process is the same in Canada, whereby a Canadian Citizen can sponsor their spouse for 2 years whilst awaiting their PR application to process. We do not understand why the UK insists on a minimum of 5+ years and what we consider to be extortionate fees.

records.title: Fund relocation support & a specialist office for grooming & abuse survivors
records.description: We call on the Government to fund a specialist office and relocation support, including security (cameras, alarms, panic buttons, identity changes) for domestic abuse/grooming survivors & families to relocate safely in the UK or abroad. This could prevent repeated trauma & mental health problems.
records.further_details:
Grooming gang and domestic abuse survivors may face repeated forced moves due to threats. A lack of support can cause unstable housing, loss of belongings, and upheaval. Many survivors endure anxiety, nightmares, & breakdowns, and cannot work. Children can suffer fear, instability, & trauma.
 
Government funding for a new specialist office and relocation support, including security (cameras/alarms/panic buttons), identity changes, and ongoing provision of benefits support, could break this cycle, enable safe new starts & strengthen the Domestic Abuse Act 2021.

records.title: Provide funding for women & girls participation in all grassroots football clubs
records.description: I would like the government to provide enough funding for every grassroots football club to offer women and girls opportunities to train and play by 2030.
records.further_details: Too many clubs have decided to pull the women and girls sectors because they want to focus on the men’s game. This is not okay with the development of female football again it feels as though females are being excluded.

records.title: Review guidance and training relating to topical steroid withdrawal
records.description: Review NHS prescribing guidance for topical corticosteroids, introduce clearer patient risk warnings for topical steroid withdrawal (TSW), and improve NHS diagnosis, treatment and staff training to prevent avoidable harm and sepsis.
records.further_details: Many people report topical steroid withdrawal (TSW) after using prescribed topical corticosteroids. Many face delayed diagnosis, inadequate support and serious complications. I developed life-threatening sepsis after being prescribed increasingly potent steroid creams for a small rash. Patients need better warnings, safer prescribing, and improved training so healthcare professionals can identify and treat it before avoidable harm occurs.

records.title: Restore universal early years support through Sure Start centres across England.
records.description: The Government should invest universal in early years centres providing parenting support, speech and language,  health visitor access, breastfeeding support early intervention. Early support can improve school readiness, reduce inequalities and help families before problems become crises.
records.further_details: Sure Start centres provided an invaluable service to families and communities by offering accessible, preventative support during the earliest years of a child's life. We believe the Government should restore a network of Sure Start-style centres across England to give every child the best possible start and ensure parents can access support. Sure Start centres offered practical help, including health visitor access providing opportunities for children to develop social skills before starting

records.title: Hold an early census in England & Wales in 2027
records.description: Hold an early census in England & Wales in 2027 to provide up-to-date demographic data, rather than waiting until 2031.
records.further_details:
We believe the UK has experienced significant population change since the 2021 Census. Decisions about healthcare, education, housing, transport and other public services should be based on the most current information available.
 
An early census in 2027 could provide Parliament, local authorities and the public with an updated picture of our country’s population. This could improve planning, increase transparency and allow informed discussion about how the country is changing.

records.title: Ban the practice of’ free pitching’ by agencies and freelancers to brands
records.description: Ban 'free pitching' in law so that brands must remunerate agencies and freelancers for pitches or use other ways of selecting whom to work with - e.g. brands could look at past work, pricing and reputation as grounds to engage them, as you would in other professions (e.g. trade).
records.further_details: Brands ask agencies to pitch work for free as standard in the UK Creative Industry. The process is extractive, impacting independent business the hardest. Brands with multi-million dollar budgets should not be allowed to ask agencies to embark on work for their business as part of a pitch without paying them for that service. Business intelligence and creative IP is being extracted by brands in some instances - and work that has been created “for free” is being used without engaging the agencies the ideas were stolen from.

records.title: Change the driving test so candidates are not failed for theory questions alone.
records.description: Ask the UK Government and DVSA to stop candidates being failed in the practical driving test for struggling with theory questions asked during the test. The practical test should assess safe driving, while the separate theory test assesses knowledge. Keep safety standards fair for all learners.
records.further_details: Ask the UK Government and DVSA to review the practical driving test so candidates are not failed for struggling with theory questions asked during the test. The practical test should focus on safe, competent driving, while the separate theory test assesses knowledge. No one should fail solely because they struggle to recall or explain theory under pressure. This would keep safety standards high while making the test fairer for everyone.

records.title: Fund & mandate autism sensory kits and AAC devices in all police vehicles
records.description: Fund and mandate all police vehicles in England and Wales to carry autism-friendly sensory kits and Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) devices or tools. This could support autistic individuals with regulation, communication, and officer interactions during encounters.
records.further_details: Requiring all police vehicles to carry autism-friendly kits and AAC tools should paired with adequate training in the use of these life-saving tools for officers across the force. Recent incidents involving police officers and autistic people show force is often the default response. US police forces have used these tools to safely de-escalate situations. Officers should be equipped to communicate, protect autistic individuals, and prevent avoidable deaths.

records.title: Introduce a specific offence banning protests outside people's homes
records.description: Protests that target homes or take place on residential streets should be made illegal to prevent harm to communities, families and individuals. People have a legal and moral right to live in their homes or other accommodation with privacy, security and dignity, and this should be protected.
records.further_details:
We think the country is experiencing increasingly violent and intimidating protests outside the homes of refugees, immigrants, MPs, local authority workers, and other groups, including incidents where houses have been attacked.

Even without direct violence the protests are terrifying for the targeted people and their neighbours. We feel that allowing such protests fails to protect people’s rights under Article 8 of the Human Rights Act.

records.title: Make fire extinguishers mandatory in cars (in light of recent wildfires )
records.description: Mandate car fire extinguishers now. The A31 New Forest van fire became a massive wildfire, burning 1.6 sq km of nature and tying up 169 fire engines. We urge the government to legally require mini extinguishers in all UK passenger cars to stop small vehicle sparks from causing huge disasters.
records.further_details: The recent A31 New Forest van fire shows why we need new safety laws. A small vehicle spark quickly became a massive wildfire, burning 1.6 sq km of nature. It destroyed rare habitats and put the forest’s famous wild ponies, cattle, and wildlife in grave danger. It took 169 fire engines eight days to stop. We ask the UK government to make mini fire extinguishers mandatory in all passenger cars. This simple tool will protect our roads, save taxpayers, and keep our animals safe.

records.title: Commission a new review into systemic and institutional racism
records.description: We urge the Government to commission a new review to investigate systemic and institutional racism, engage with communities, and make recommendations for policy and legislative reforms, enhancing education, and supporting vulnerable groups, to combat racism and promote equality in the UK.
records.further_details: In our view, the 2021 Race and Ethnic Disparities report was not a full reflection of lived experiences. Since then, we believe further evidence has shown why a new review is needed. The 2023 Casey Review exposed serious failures in policing. The 2023 Black British Voices report highlighted distrust in education and healthcare. We are also concerned about NHS race inequality, ethnicity pay gaps, and how academia and media institutions can also fail vulnerable ethnic communities.

records.title: Ban councils from charging for on-street disabled parking applications
records.description: It should be mandatory for the cost of assessment and application of a disabled bay to be waived or heavily discounted for people who aren’t eligible for a drive at their property and who require disabled parking outside their home.

records.title: Mandate availability of digital blue badges by law throughout the country
records.description: Disabled parking permits are physical blue badges which require users to remember to display them. They're often stolen so cars with blue badges are more liable to break-ins. We feel digital badges (with an option of physical ones) would allow for safer street & public parking for disabled drivers.
records.further_details: There are digital parking permits available to those who pay for permits or parking fees, but drivers who hold blue badges have to rely on displaying the physical badge. The technology to enable digital blue badge permits exists, but implementing it isn't mandatory so it hasn't been. Disabled drivers are fined if they forget to display their badge, while drivers with digital permits don't need to remember them at all. Make both physical and digital badges available to blue badge holders by amending  the law.

records.title: Review and reform the care system
records.description: We call on the Government to reform the care system. We are concerned that high social worker turnover, unstable placements and failures to follow policies can cause further trauma. Care must nurture, not simply sustain survival.
records.further_details:
Every child deserves stability, opportunity and a childhood.
 
Some vulnerable children face neglect, instability, repeated placements, high social worker turnover and serious mental health challenges. Tragically, some care leavers lose their lives after leaving a system that was meant to protect them. We believe the Government is failing in its role as a corporate parent. Care must nurture, protect and support, not simply keep children alive. Children in care deserve stability, opportunity, dignity and a genuine childhood.

records.title: Allow Skilled Workers to change employers without a full visa reapplication
records.description: Create a streamlined sponsorship-transfer process for Skilled Worker visa holders moving to another licensed sponsor in the same occupation code and meeting the same skill and salary requirements. They should not need a full visa reapplication or repeat visa/IHS charges for leave already granted.
records.further_details: Once the Home Office has assessed and approved a Skilled Worker’s immigration status, skills and eligibility, moving to another licensed sponsor in the same or substantially similar occupation should not mean repeating the full visa process. Reapplication fees, IHS, sponsorship charges and legal costs can run into thousands of pounds, discouraging job moves and leaving workers unnecessarily dependent on one employer.

records.title: Legally require those using the title "Engineer" to have an engineering degree
records.description: The title Engineer is protected in many other countries. Unfortunately, in the UK it is not so technicians, plumbers etc, use and abuse the title freely. Legislate that you must hold an engineering degree to use the title "Engineer".
records.further_details: We believe mis-use of the title "Engineer" is impacting the respect and value of professional Engineers, meaning less study the discipline. Engineers have formed the backbone of economies for centuries around the world. We feel that in the UK this has been eradicated, with the title of an engineer mis-used for plumbers, electricians and technicians. In our view, this is an insult to the profession which demands one of the hardest degrees, further study and training to earn the title.

records.title: Amend family law to include unwanted indirect contact within “molestation”
records.description: We want the Government to amend the Family Law Act 1996 to expressly provide that “molestation” can include unwanted contact made through, encouraged through, or facilitated by a third party connected to the respondent, whether or not that contact is threatening.
records.further_details: The Family Law Act 1996 does not define “molestation”, leaving courts to interpret whether indirect contact meets the threshold. We believe the law should expressly recognise unwanted contact made through relatives, friends or other third parties where it is instigated, encouraged or facilitated by the respondent, even if the contact itself is not threatening. A clear no-contact boundary should not be circumvented through others.

records.title: Add Plant-Based Milk to Healthy Start
records.description: Include fortified plant-based milk alternatives in the Healthy Start scheme, so eligible families can use Healthy Start payments to buy suitable non-dairy milk instead of cow’s milk.
records.further_details: Healthy Start supports families to buy nutritious food and milk, but plant-based milk is not included. Families may choose plant-based alternatives for ethical, religious or dietary reasons, including allergies and intolerances. Fortified plant-based milks can provide important nutrients such as calcium and vitamin B12. We believe eligible families should have the same freedom of choice and be able to use Healthy Start payments towards fortified plant-based milk instead of cow’s milk.

records.title: Fund free NHS laser hair removal/electrolysis for diagnosed hirsutism in PCOS
records.description: Fund free NHS access to clinical laser hair removal and electrolysis for women diagnosed with hirsutism linked to Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), to remove the need for patients to self-fund what we feel is essential medical care.
records.further_details:
Hirsutism is a core clinical symptom of PCOS, caused by elevated androgens that produce thick, male-pattern hair growth on the face, neck, and body. Despite the proven medical cause, NHS routinely categorise hair removal as a 'cosmetic' procedure.
 
We believe there is an unfair financial barrier to accessing laser hair removal and electrolysis, meaning thousands of women have to spend thousands of pounds on private clinics or endure severe psychological distress, anxiety, depression, and skin damage from daily shaving and plucking.

records.title: Fund employment security buffer for all working and tax paying adults
records.description: We think that a small, defined portion of the taxes people already pay should be ring-fenced and attributed to them individually, building up over time as a dedicated reserve in case they lose their job. This should not be a new tax, but instead funded via their current tax contribution.
records.further_details: In our view, by funding such a buffer, when a person loses their job, they will not immediately fall into uncertainty of how to secure an income. Instead, they will be able to first draw upon their own Employment Security Buffer—a fund built gradually through their working life—before accessing wider state support if needed. We think this system could be administered via an Employment Security Buffer account set up for each individual eligible, administered through existing tax infrastructure.

records.title: Review Food Security and Self Reliance Strategy. Pause not-yet-started NSIPs
records.description: We believe more must be done to protect our food security, national security and farmland. Stop large-land-take solar schemes, review lower-land-take alternatives. Prioritise UK industry, home-grown energy, and self-reliance. Safeguard our domestic food production.
records.further_details: In our view, at a time of geopolitical uncertainty, losing countryside to large industrial energy schemes is strategically unsound. This petition calls for Government to pause all not yet started Nationally Significant Infrastructure Projects — whether already approved but not yet broken ground, or still awaiting examination — so that we can review our ability to build and maintain its own lower-land-take energy systems and safeguard domestic food production

records.title: Issue a formal apology for the UK’s role in the 1943 Bengal Famine
records.description: We call on the UK Government to issue a formal apology to India, Bangladesh and Pakistan for policies enacted by the British War Cabinet, which we feel caused or severely worsened the 1943 Bengal Famine and was estimated to have led to 3 million deaths.
records.further_details:
During WWII, the UK Government enacted a “Denial Policy” in Bengal, confiscating or destroying food stocks and destroying transport boats which crippled the economy. As starvation spread, requests for emergency food imports were repeatedly denied by London.
 
While the UK Government has expressed regret for some events like Jallianwala Bagh, it has never formally apologised for the UK Government’s administrative choices that allowed millions of colonial subjects to perish from preventable hunger.

records.title: Create a UK fuel security and price strategy
records.description: Create a national strategy to reduce UK petrol and diesel prices by securing competitive long-term fuel supplies, strengthening UK refining and supply resilience, and improving competition. Where these measures cannot prevent exceptional price rises, use temporary tax cuts to protect consumers.
records.further_details: UK households and businesses are heavily affected by volatile fuel prices. We believe the Government should use the UK's scale and purchasing power to secure better long-term supply arrangements, while strengthening domestic refining, supply security, and competition. The priority should be reducing the underlying cost of fuel before it reaches the pump, rather than relying solely on tax cuts. Where exceptional prices remain, temporary tax relief should act as a backstop.

records.title: Legally mandate premium holiday pay for all hospitality workers
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce legislation that legally entitles all hospitality workers to a mandatory premium pay rate (minimum time-and-a-half) or guaranteed paid time off in lieu for working on official UK Bank Holidays.
records.further_details: Unlike many sectors, the hospitality industry experiences its highest demand during bank holidays. Workers are routinely required to sacrifice time with their families, friends & communities to keep the economy running, yet the current law does not guarantee them a penny of extra pay for doing so. Under current employment law, there is no statutory right to extra pay on bank holidays; it is entirely at the employer's discretion. This can leave low-paid workers vulnerable to burnout & unfair compensation. As part of the Government's commitment to "Make Work Pay" and the introduction of the Employment Rights Act, a mandatory premium rate for holiday shifts should be codified into law. We believe hospitality workers deserve fair compensation for giving up their holidays to serve others.

records.title: Amend the Video Recordings Act 1984 to allow the sale of unclassified DVDs
records.description: I want the Video Recordings Act of 1984 to be either amended or significantly altered, to allow the sale of unclassified DVDs. As well as UK distributors being able to sell their products easier, it would also allow products from other countries, like the United States, to be sold in shops.
records.further_details: Adults should be trusted to decide what is appropriate for their homes. High BBFC classification costs can burden small indie labels, often making niche releases unviable. Allowing unclassified sales would support small labels and increase choice. Since unrated content is easily found on the internet and streaming sites, we think current rules for physical DVDs are outdated. For adult films, sellers could perform due diligence by checking online databases before selling to minors.

records.title: Introduce a legal minimum standard of provision for NHS clinical staff uniforms
records.description: We are calling on the Government to set a legal minimum for the number of uniforms provided to all NHS clinical staff. Currently, thousands of frontline clinicians are provided with an insufficient number of uniforms—often as few as two or three sets—despite working full-time rotations.
records.further_details: We believe the current situation is not just a matter of staff comfort; it is a significant issue of patient safety and personal dignity. In a cost-of-living crisis, some staff are forced to run expensive, high-temperature wash cycles every single night just to ensure they have a clean kit for the next day’s shift and are frequently expected to provide their own clinical footwear at their own expense. Every clinician deserves a kit that is fit for purpose, safe, and fully funded.

records.title: Give tax breaks to racing bodies that stop horses being put down
records.description: Introduce tax incentives for racecourses, owners and trainers who take real action to stop horses being euthanised after injuries. This must include strict welfare standards, better veterinary care, and investment in research to save horses that would otherwise be lost.
records.further_details: Every year, horses suffer fatal injuries on UK racecourses and are euthanised in front of the public. These deaths are not just statistics—they are preventable losses that are turning people away from the sport. Without urgent change, racing will continue to lose support and decline. Rewarding those who protect horses will save lives, rebuild public trust and bring people back. A safer sport means stronger attendance, protected jobs and greater long-term economic benefit for the UK.

records.title: Change how employees on mat leave are compensated for redundancy consultation
records.description:
Build on reforms:
-Require redundancy consultation during mat leave be treated as paid engagement (via KIT days/equivalent, with a paid process beyond 10 days)
-Ensure employees aren’t disadvantaged in redundancy processes due to mat leave
records.further_details:
Women on maternity leave and at risk of redundancy are still expected to take part in consultations with no clear requirement for that time to be paid. At best 10 KIT days and then working for free, while using precious time.

The Protection from Redundancy (Pregnancy and Family Leave) Act 2023 strengthened protections, but not the reality of engaging in the process during leave.

No clear pay, no limits, no structure.
Maternity leave shouldn’t mean being disadvantaged at your most vulnerable.

records.title: Mandate 24/7 real-time emergency monitoring on all social media platforms
records.description: Legislate to require social media companies to implement 24/7 proactive emergency monitoring. This should include AI-driven detection of immediate threats—such as severe cyber-bullying, self-harm, or illegal activity—and a requirement to alert emergency services instantly when lives are at risk.

records.title: Ensure protected wellbeing days for employees in addition to annual & sick leave
records.description: We want the Government to introduce a legal right for employees to take occasional wellbeing days, in addition to sick leave and annual leave, to support positive mental health, prevent burnout, and improve work-life balance.
records.further_details: Employees can call in sick when physically or mentally unwell, but there is no equivalent option for people experiencing exceptionally positive wellbeing. We ask the Government to introduce limited protected “wellbeing days” or “call well” leave, allowing employees to take occasional time off to maintain positive mental health, prevent burnout, and support long-term wellbeing and work-life balance.

records.title: Ban media coverage of coroner's court hearings
records.description: We call for a ban on media coverage of coroner’s court hearings, with an allowance only for verified summaries provided by trained court officials, not sensationalised accounts. Losing a loved one is shattering, marked by overwhelming grief, a desire for privacy during the most vulnerable times.
records.further_details: In our view, such a situation can be made significantly worse for families when the details of the dearly departed is spread across newspapers, and sometimes distorted & sensationalised, without due regard for family privacy. We believe that stopping media coverage of coroner’s court hearings will ensure the dignity of those who have passed and their grieving relatives can be maintained. Preserving the dignity of deceased individuals & protecting the mental well-being of their families.

records.title: Scrap the £2,000 NI cap on salary sacrifice pensions for Disabled people
records.description: Reverse the £2,000 National Insurance cap on salary-sacrificed pension contributions due in 2029, and keep National Insurance relief on these contributions in full for disabled people.
records.further_details: Salary sacrifice builds a pension automatically, with no repeated decision once set up. For disabled and neurodivergent people whose conditions affect impulse control, that structure is a reasonable adjustment, not a perk. From 2029, contributions above £2,000 attract National Insurance, likely cutting pension saving. Disability is protected under the Equality Act 2010. Under the Public Sector Equality Duty, we ask the Government to reconsider this cap or first assess its equality impact.

records.title: Require probate caveat applicants to sign legal declaration & notify next of kin
records.description: Require applicants of probate caveats sign a legal declaration confirming they understand that a caveat freezes the whole estate and to notify all next of kin when a caveat is entered.
records.further_details:
Caveats can freeze an entire estate instantly, yet caveators are not required to confirm they understand the legal consequences or to notify next of kin. We believe this allows misuse of caveats, confusion about the process and financial harm. We think that a signed declaration and mandatory notification to protect next of kin and ensure accountability should be required.

In our view caveats give individuals major legal power with no checks or safeguards. We therefore believe that a declaration notification rule would prevent misuse, protect families to ensure estates are handled fairly.

records.title: Ban Video Games and online games for under 18s
records.description: We think video games are creating a massive influence and impact on under 18s and that it is causing a massive decrease on their social life with friends and family and that is negatively impacting their eyesight and their school grades.
records.further_details: We think that if video games are banned then people will get better grades spend more time with their family and friends just like social media this is another massive problem for the younger generation after social media

records.title: Fund regular welfare checks for children and require parental co-operation
records.description: We think that we have to do a much better job protecting children from abuse and call for funding for a system where trained healthcare workers visit every family on a regular short or non-notice basis to examine the children for signs of physical, sexual or emotional abuse, or neglect.
records.further_details: We believe that we need a funded system where healthcare professional visit every home in the on a regular (for example monthly) basis to be able to examine children for specific signs but also see how the children live/ judge potential abuse. These visits should be unannounced or conducted after short notice, and the family should be legally obliged to grant the healthcare worker access to their home and to examine their children.

records.title: Require RTC helmets for frontline officers
records.description: Require all police forces to provide approved Road Traffic Collision (RTC) helmets to frontline officers. Police are often first on scene at collisions, managing hazards and creating safe working areas, but are not routinely issued specialist head protection.
records.further_details: Police officers are frequently the first emergency service to arrive at road traffic collisions. They manage traffic, preserve life and create a safe working environment for fire and ambulance crews. Despite facing risks from moving vehicles, debris and secondary collisions, officers are not routinely issued RTC helmets. We believe all frontline officers who may attend road-related incidents should be provided with suitable, approved RTC head protection.

records.title: Amend the Children Act to make parental responsibility enforceable
records.description: Amend section 3 of the Children Act 1989 to define enforceable financial and practical duties attached to parental responsibility, with proportionate consequences where a parent who has the ability to contribute persistently and deliberately fails to meet them.
records.further_details: Parental responsibility should mean enforceable duties to the child, not just legal rights. Some parents retain rights, seek court orders or claim shared care while providing little reliable practical or financial support. The law should require fair financial contribution, accurate income information and dependable agreed care, with consequences for deliberate non-payment, repeated cancellations, hidden income and abusive court applications. The child’s welfare must always come first.

records.title: Prohibit "filtering" (lane-splitting) in traffic by 2- or 3-wheeled vehicles
records.description: The Government must introduce regulations to prohibit filtering or lane-splitting by 2- or 3-wheeled vehicles, along with clear liability rules, to deal with such vehicles that often navigate aggressively between lanes of moving or stationary traffic.
records.further_details: Weaving between traffic can create safety hazards and financial burdens, sometimes causing real property damage. Riders squeezing through narrow gaps can regularly clip mirrors and scratch or dent bodywork. Because they can easily flee, riders can often leave the scene immediately, leaving motorists with expensive repair bills and insurance deductibles. Sudden overtaking from blind spots also leads to drivers constantly reacting to unpredictable hazards.

records.title: Require EBSA to be priority listed for EHCNA Educational Psychologist assessment
records.description: We want the Government to require local authorities to prioritise Educational Psychologist appointments for children with Emotionally Based School Avoidance (EBSA) during the Education, Health and Care Needs Assessment (EHCNA) process, so they can access timely assessments and the support needed.
records.further_details: EBSA can severely affect a child’s mental health, education and wellbeing, while placing emotional and financial strain on families. Delays in Educational Psychologist assessments during the EHCNA process leave many children without support. As a result, they can fall behind academically, become isolated, and experience worsening mental health. We believe children with EBSA should be prioritised.

records.title: Review timing of NHS Anatomy Scans for pregnancies at 15-16 rather than 20 weeks
records.description: We call on the NHS to review the merits of offering the anatomy scan to pregnant women at 15–16 weeks, where medically appropriate, instead of waiting until 20 weeks.
records.further_details: We believe earlier scans could detect serious conditions sooner, giving families more time to seek specialist advice, understand their options & access the care and support they need. Routine anatomy scans should take place at 15–16 weeks, where medically appropriate, to detect serious conditions earlier. Earlier diagnosis gives families more time to access specialist care, arrange further testing, prepare for treatment, or make informed decisions about their pregnancy. It can reduce the emotional impact of waiting for answers & improve access to timely support, helping parents & healthcare teams plan the best possible care for both mother & baby.

records.title: Require dogs to undergo mandatory sociability tests & introduce mitigations
records.description: We call on the Government to amend the Dangerous Dogs Act and require dogs to undergo mandatory sociability tests in order to test if dogs are likely to attack other dogs or people. Dogs failing the test, should be given compulsory retraining, muzzles, or put down if found a threat to safety.
records.further_details:
We believe there are too many unruly and dangerous dogs in public, and we cannot have threatening animals on our streets. My placid little dog has been attacked on four occasions this year, and I have been attacked once. An Alsatian went for my throat. The police were sympathetic, but unable to assist.

If people are aggressive in public, action is taken. However, we allow aggressive dogs to prowl our streets, seemingly with no consequences. Rather than being reactive, we believe we should be pre-emptive, and test dogs for sociability every two years. My dog would pass any test with flying colours.

records.title: Allow all legal residents paying tax in England & Northern Ireland to vote
records.description: We call on the UK Government to amend electoral law and extend voting rights in all general and local elections in England and Northern Ireland to anyone who is legally residing there and paying tax.
records.further_details: We believe “taxation without representation” is wrong in principle: people who pay taxes and are affected by decisions should be able to vote to shape national decisions. “Lawful residents” means people who are legally entitled to reside in the UK and who can obtain government-issued identification (e.g., a NI number, a driving licence, or similar).

records.title: Suspend UC work requirements while claimants with fit notes await a WCA
records.description: We want the Government to suspend work-related requirements, including Restart Scheme referrals, for Universal Credit claimants certified by their GP as not fit for work while awaiting a Work Capability Assessment, rather than leaving these requirements to the discretion of individual work coaches.
records.further_details: People awaiting a Work Capability Assessment can face lengthy delays. During this period, despite being medically deemed not fit for work by a GP, work coaches can impose work-related requirements and Restart Scheme referrals. We believe medical evidence should take precedence until the WCA decision is made. Claimants should not bear the health consequences of delays outside their control or risk sanctions for being unable to meet requirements that conflict with their medical needs.

records.title: Require employers to show a clear salary in job adverts
records.description: Legally require employers to include a clear salary in all job adverts and end the inclusion of vague phrases such as “competitive salary” and “salary dependent on experience”. We believe jobseekers deserve to know the expected pay before investing time in an application or interview.
records.further_details: Phrases such as “competitive salary” should no longer be accepted as a substitute for actual pay information. Salary transparency could save jobseekers time, reduce wasted applications and interviews, improve pay fairness and give people the information they need to make informed career decisions before applying.

records.title: Require by law landlords to pass solar panel benefits to tenants
records.description: Require by law that landlords, councils and housing associations pass the financial benefits of solar panels to tenants of properties fixed with those panels, including the benefit of electricity generated and payments for surplus electricity exported to the grid.
records.further_details: Many rented homes have solar panels, but tenants may not receive the full financial benefit. Landlords can receive payments for surplus energy exported to the grid. We believe these payments should benefit the household. Giving tenants the export income, or an equivalent energy bill credit, could help reduce household costs. This could particularly help people in social and affordable housing, ensuring renewable energy reduces bills for those who need the savings most.

records.title: Fund free public transport for under 16’s
records.description: Fund the provision of free public transport for under 16s across the country.

records.title: Require a prominence and relevance standard for nationality in crime reporting
records.description: We call on the Government to require a clear standard requiring news organisations to avoid highlighting nationality, national origin or immigration status in crime reporting unless materially relevant to the offence or public interest. The same standard should apply equally to everyone.
records.further_details: Criminal responsibility is individual. When nationality, national origin or immigration status is irrelevant to an offence, highlighting it can unfairly associate one person’s crime with an entire community and contribute to stigma against law-abiding people. Section 9 of the Equality Act 2010 includes nationality and ethnic or national origins within race. We seek a fair and consistent standard, not censorship. Press freedom, expression and open justice must be protected. Where nationality or immigration status is materially relevant or justified in the public interest, it should remain reportable. If it is relevant, report it; if not, it should not define the crime. Hold individuals accountable, not entire communities.

records.title: Have a referendum for Cornish residents on granting Cornwall nation status
records.description: We want the Government to hold a referendum for Cornish residents only to vote and establish if Cornwall Devolution is wanted by the majority of the county’s residents.

records.title: Review current laws on rabbit control
records.description: Review laws that impose obligations on occupiers of land to control wild rabbits in rabbit clearance areas. Rabbit numbers have fallen dramatically, yet rabbits support predators, plants, invertebrates and help maintain diverse habitats. Require evidence of significant damage before lethal control
records.further_details: The European rabbit is near threatened globally and UK rabbit numbers have declined by around 72–73%. Yet rabbits support predators and biodiversity through grazing and burrowing. Lethal control should require demonstrable significant damage, with non-lethal alternatives prioritised.

records.title: Ban schools from confiscating students' phones overnight
records.description: We ask the Government to introduce national safeguarding rules preventing schools from confiscating a child's phone overnight. This could protect children travelling to and from school, including ensuring they can contact a parent or responsible adult if they face an emergency.
records.further_details: We ask the Government to introduce national safeguarding rules requiring schools to protect children travelling to and from school. If a child is allowed to travel home independently, they should have a safe way to contact a parent or responsible adult, especially when their phone has been confiscated or retained. Children’s safety outside school must be treated as part of safeguarding.

records.title: Ban Plastic Tags on Children’s Clothing
records.description: This petition calls for the Government to ban plastic tags on children’s clothing, which we believe create avoidable waste, pose choking risks, and contribute to pollution.
records.further_details: We want the Government to urge retailers to use alternatives such as cotton loops, paper tags or stitched in labels to protect children and reduce environmental harm.

records.title: Require a standard disclaimer on all official legal documents and interfaces
records.description: Require all legal instruments, court communications, and official legal interfaces to include a prominent disclaimer stating that the text is written in legal terminology ("legalese"), where words hold precise, technical meanings distinct from everyday language.
records.further_details:
Legal language often uses ordinary English words in ways that carry specific legal definitions, creating confusion for the public. Without formal training, members of the public may interpret terms according to common usage, leading to misunderstandings during legal processes.
​Requiring a standardised disclaimer on legal communications and digital interfaces would explicitly notify individuals that the document operates under specialised legal language. This simple measure would improve clarity

records.title: Allow childcare vouchers & tax-free childcare for school activities & expenses
records.description: Allow childcare vouchers and tax-free childcare to be used for all in-school activities, to ease burden of the 'extra-curricular' and 'essential' needs of schools, and for expenses - such as uniforms, lunches, and activities— to ease the growing financial strain on families.
records.further_details: Parents work hard to earn, so their children have every opportunity to learn, explore, and build confidence—in school and beyond. Expanding what they can be used for could not only give parents peace of mind but could also benefit the country by supporting working families, boosting participation in the workforce, and reducing the need for additional financial aid.

records.title: Review laws on parental support & financial responsibility during pregnancy
records.description: Launch a review into UK family law to examine financial responsibility for a child during pregnancy and to consider whether courts should formally recognise a lack of emotional, physical, and practical support from a parent during pregnancy as a relevant factor in decision-making.
records.further_details:
Pregnancy can be a vulnerable time, and many mothers experience a lack of support that goes beyond financial absence. Financial responsibility for a child typically begins after birth and we feel there is limited recognition of a parent’s conduct during pregnancy. Decisions around birth registration may often be made when mothers are vulnerable.
 
We believe the law should be reviewed to consider whether a parent’s absence, lack of support, or abandonment during pregnancy should be formally recognised and taken into account by courts where relevant.

records.title: Fund annual cancer screening at 40 for adults with Down syndrome & LD
records.description: Fund an annual cancer screening programme for adults aged 40 and over who have Down syndrome or severe learning difficulties. This should include appropriate tests based on clinical risk, proactive NHS recall, and reasonable adjustments to ensure full accessibility.
records.further_details: Adults with Down syndrome and severe learning difficulties face major barriers to early cancer detection. Higher pain thresholds, atypical symptoms, and communication challenges mean signs are often missed. Diagnostic overshadowing and inconsistent health checks delay diagnosis. Annual screening from age 40 could support earlier detection, fair access, and better outcomes.

records.title: Make insurance optional for every driver in the UK
records.description:
Insurance is something that can be very expensive for first time drivers, especially for those who are young and can't afford it. 

Most people spend years paying for insurance and don't even claim it because they want to protect their accidents history. Therefore, insurance should be optional.

records.title: Combat adolescent substance abuse through increased funding
records.description: Fund targeted adolescent substance abuse awareness programmes and preventative educational resources in all secondary schools. Increase government funding for youth-specific rehabilitation centres and mental health support resources for adolescents.
records.further_details: Substance abuse among adolescents is still too prevalent, damaging young lives, mental health, and local communities. In our view, to tackle this effectively, we must address both prevention and recovery. We think current school education programs and youth rehabilitation services lack the necessary resources to manage this crisis.
