We call on the Government to increase funding for both targeted drug awareness initiatives in secondary schools and specialised youth support systems.

records.title: Mandatory ID Cards and Purchase Limits for Scratch Cards
records.description: We call on the UK Government to introduce mandatory ID verification and a daily limit of 5 scratch cards per individual to reduce gambling-related harm and promote responsible play.
records.further_details:
Every year, thousands of people struggle with gambling addiction, and scratch cards are often seen as a harmless entry point.
We want to:
- reduce excessive gambling and protect vulnerable adults and young people
- make it harder for people to buy unlimited quantities
- encourage responsible gambling while allowing adults to purchase scratch cards in moderation.

Just as ID is required for many age-restricted products, a properly age-monitored system could we believe promote safer gambling and reduce financial harm, while maintaining access for those who gamble responsibly.

records.title: Strengthen laws to protect lodgers from discrimination and short-notice eviction
records.description: Even though there have been more protections for tenants applied in law, these do not all apply to lodgers. Unlike tenants, they have no statutory minimum notice period. We want a 1-month minimum notice period for lodgers.
records.further_details:
Under the Equality Act 2010, discrimination in housing based on protected characteristics is generally unlawful. However, the Act contains a “small premises exemption” that allows resident landlords who share living accommodation with a lodger to discriminate when choosing who to live with. 
 
Whilst this petition respects that conflicts are more likely in a lodging situation that may need the housing relationship to end, it believes there should be a reasonable notice period (a minimum of 1 month) and you should not be allowed to discriminate against protected characteristics (say "no transgender people" or "white people only"). Right now, we are concerned that lodging is impossible for some people due to discrimination.

records.title: UK Government must raise human rights concerns in Balochistan
records.description: We call on the UK Government to raise the issue of enforced disappearances in Balochistan with the Government of Pakistan, to press for the release of detained activists, and to call for an independent investigation into human rights abuses in the region.
records.further_details: Balochistan has seen a rise in reports of enforced disappearances, where individuals can be detained without due legal process and their whereabouts often remain unknown to their families. Human rights activists have faced arrest and restrictions for peacefully raising these concerns. We ask the UK Government to raise the human rights situation in Balochistan with the Government of Pakistan, support calls for transparent investigations, and advocate for the safety and release of those detained without a fair trial.

records.title: Ban online comments on news stories about anyone under 25
records.description: We ask the Government to ban online comments on social media platforms and online news outlets on news stories relating to anyone under 25, including news stories relating to the death, accident, or assault of anyone who is under 25.
records.further_details: Following prominent news stories relating to the deaths of individuals under 25 years old, we would like the Government to ban social media platforms and news outlets from having open comment sections or functions on news stories relating to anyone under 25. We feel comments may incite hate, harm, distress & are wholly inappropriate and unhelpful, and that news outlets have a duty of care to all.

records.title: Uprate the Section 75 credit card protection limit in line with inflation
records.description: Raise the upper limit for Section 75 protection under the Consumer Credit Act 1974 from £30,000 to at least £96,000, so it reflects the same real-terms value it had when last set in 1985, and index it to inflation going forward so it never falls behind again.
records.further_details:
S75 makes your credit card company jointly liable with a retailer if goods or services you paid for go wrong, are never delivered, or are misrepresented. It's one of the strongest consumer protections in UK law, and it costs the taxpayer nothing.

The upper limit was set at £30k in 1985 and has not been increased since. That should be £96k today. Many big purchases have risen past the old ceiling leaving consumers exposed on exactly the kind of large purchases this law was designed to protect.

records.title: Ban the sale, import, & distribution of nasal energy powders ("energy sniffs")
records.description: Ban the sale, import, and distribution of non-medicinal, tobacco-free nasal powders marketed as energy boosters or "energy sniffs." Caffeine & herbal powders designed for nasal inhalation should not be exempt from food, beverage, & age-restriction regulations.
records.further_details: “Energy sniffs” are powders containing high levels of caffeine, taurine and guarana designed to be snorted. We believe they normalise drug-taking behaviour by mimicking Class A drug use, risk serious nasal and respiratory damage, and exploit regulatory loopholes by avoiding food safety rules and proposed under-16 energy drink restrictions. The UK must act now to protect public health and young people.

records.title: Publish clearer criteria for UK Emergency Alert System usage
records.description: Following the 14 August 2026 nationwide wildfire alert, which we believe was used for general information rather than a specific life-threatening emergency, we call on the UK Government to publish clearer criteria for when the Emergency Alerts system may be deployed.
records.further_details: We think this would maintain trust for genuine emergencies. The Emergency Alerts system was designed to warn the public about imminent, life-threatening emergencies requiring urgent action, such as wildfires, severe flooding, and extreme storms. In our view, on 14 August 2026, an alert was sent nationwide as a general wildfire awareness reminder rather than for a specific, actionable emergency. We believe this risks undermining public trust, encouraging users to disable alerts on their phones. Without published clear criteria, future misuse may render this vital mechanism ineffective.

records.title: Fund universal emotional and practical postpartum support for mothers
records.description: We want the Government to fund guaranteed, universal access to post-partum support for every mother during the first year of their baby’s life, including practical and emotional support for appropriately trained professionals such as Postnatal Doulas regardless of their ability to pay.
records.further_details:
The transition into motherhood does not end a few weeks after birth. The first year can bring physical recovery, sleep deprivation, feeding difficulties, isolation and emotional overwhelm, yet ongoing practical support can be limited.

Postnatal doulas are trained to support families during this period but are usually privately funded. We believe post-partum support should be funded and offered to every mother without means testing. The mother and her postnatal doula or appropriately trained professional should jointly determine the type, frequency and length of continued support required, based on her individual circumstances. This support should complement existing NHS maternity and health visiting services.

records.title: Launch a review into adult social care costs & tax reliefs
records.description: Review VAT treatment across social care and implement VAT relief on essential PPE. Introduce National Insurance relief for regulated social care employers. We also want the review to investigate Local Authority adult care fees to ensure they reflect the actual cost of care.
records.further_details: We believe social care is crumbling, despite its vital role in supporting vulnerable people at home. Providers have faced a rise in NI costs, inadequate local authority fees, VAT on essential supplies, and soaring operational expenses. Without urgent government action—such as targeted NI relief, VAT exemptions, fair fees, business rates relief, and sustainable funding—we are concerned that many providers will fail, squeezing families, councils, and the NHS. Social care is essential and we believe it deserves parity with the NHS.

records.title: Require free parking for all electric vehicles
records.description: Follow Poland’s lead by making parking free for all electric vehicles in parking spaces owned or managed by local authorities.
records.further_details:
By incentivising electric vehicles, we could boost our chances of meeting our climate goals. Free parking could make electric vehicles more financially viable for those considering the switch.

Electric cars are not just for the wealthy: many modest earners are saving-up and switching to help tackle climate change. Let’s reward them for doing the right thing.

records.title: Review NHS guidance for intimate examinations by healthcare professionals
records.description: Review NHS guidance for intimate examinations, including procedures, to ensure patients are provided with detailed information on the intimate physical exam, including what it will include, who will do it, how it will be done and why it is necessary, via a note sent with an appointment letter.
records.further_details:
When visiting gynaecologists, many women take part in physical exams and may not be aware of what it involves beforehand. For many, these exams can be stressful, overwhelming and painful.
 
By mandating that intimate physical exams must be clearly explained before an appointment, the patient, whether they are female or male, can know what to expect and what to prepare for, particularly when genital examinations are involved.

records.title: Adherents to the Churches of England & Scotland to advise on Church appointments
records.description: We believe appointments in the Churches of England & Scotland should each be advised on exclusively by adherents to those faiths. Amend the Church Appointments (Repeal of Discriminatory Provision) Bill to further limit who is able to advise on appointments rather than removing existing prohibitions.
records.further_details:
The Churches of England and Scotland are Protestant churches. Irrespective of whether they are, or remain, established churches, we believe the appointment of Church leaders should not be influenced by those who do not adhere to the faith. Currently, appointments in both churches cannot be advised on by Roman Catholics or Jews.
 
These provisions are indeed discriminatory, but the solution should be to limit this power to adhering Protestants of the two Churches concerned rather than extend it to individuals of any, or no, religion.

records.title: Limit compulsory homework in England to a maximum of 3 hours per week
records.description: Introduce a limit of 3 hours per week spent on compulsory homework for pupils in schools in England, with schools required to coordinate homework across subjects so that pupils do not receive more than this amount.
records.further_details: This petition calls for a maximum of 3 hours of compulsory homework per pupil per week in schools in England. The limit would apply to homework across all subjects combined, with schools coordinating deadlines and workloads. The aim is not to abolish homework, but to prevent excessive workloads while allowing pupils enough time for sleep, family, hobbies, exercise and other activities outside school.

records.title: The Government must review & update medical restrictions on joining the Military
records.description: We believe the UK Government is turning away too many people from their life-long dream of serving their country due to minor faults, even from a young age.
records.further_details: We want the Government to review current medical prohibitions. We feel that conditions like mild asthma, some food allergies and conditions that occurred at a young age should not deny entry, especially if the GP says they are able.

records.title: Seek to rejoin the Single Market and EFTA
records.description: We call upon the Government to seek to rejoin the Single Market (European Economic Area) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA). We think this would be a substantial boost to the UK economy & provide reassurance and safeguards to UK citizens living & working in Europe.
records.further_details: Under this arrangement the UK could keep the pound sterling and maintain sovereignty. We believe this option would respect the 2016 Brexit vote but foster UK-EU trade and friendship.

records.title: Ban authoritarian state ownership of football clubs
records.description: Ban authoritarian regimes, and the companies and funds they control, from owning or taking stakes in football clubs. Make this part of the Independent Football Regulator's owners' and directors' test, to prevent regimes seeking to 'sportswash' their image.
records.further_details: Football clubs belong to their fans and communities, not to authoritarian regimes using them to 'sportswash' human rights abuses. Ban these regimes, and the companies, sovereign funds and individuals acting for them, from owning or taking stakes in English clubs. Make this part of the Independent Football Regulator's owners' and directors' test, using an independent measure of authoritarian rule, so no club can be brought. Keep authoritarianism out of our game.

records.title: Increase funding for military catering
records.description: Provide higher quality food and produce for the British Army as they are currently defending and keeping us citizens safe.
records.further_details: I feel that currently, the quality of food provided to the British Army is poor. I believe that they deserve more than the average citizen but currently this is not provided which is unfair. I believe they deserve better quality meals for their work and dedication for putting their lives on the line for Britain.

records.title: Require employers to give reasons for unsuccessful job applications
records.description: Require employers to provide applicants with a clear reason when their job application is unsuccessful, particularly where the applicant has completed an interview or assessment.
records.further_details: Job applications can be stressful and time-consuming. After putting time and effort into an application, waiting anxiously for a response can be difficult, only to receive a rejection with no explanation. When this happens repeatedly, applicants can become frustrated and unsure where they are going wrong. Requiring employers to give a reason would male recruitment more transparent and help applicants understand what they could improve, particularly after interviews or assessments.

records.title: Ban horns in automobiles that only sound when the cars ignition is switched on.
records.description: If you are a driver or a passenger in a parked car and there is an emergency or you have an accident you cannot always use the horn to alert a possible danger if you don't have the cars ignition switched on. This isn't safe.
records.further_details: I would like to see the law changed so all car manufacturers are required to make cars that have horns that work at all times, with or without the ignition turned.

records.title: Freeze all student loan repayment thresholds for overseas borrowers until 2030.
records.description: The Government must freeze repayment thresholds for overseas borrowers, as it has done for UK-based borrowers. Currently, UK thresholds are frozen until 2030, yet overseas thresholds change yearly, which could increase the financial burden on those living abroad.
records.further_details: The Government committed to freezing student loan thresholds until 2030. However, this is not the case for overseas borrowers. We believe this creates a two-tier system where some people living abroad might pay a higher percentage of their income than UK peers. Parliament should mandate that all overseas thresholds are frozen at current levels until 2030.

records.title: International graduates to get 5-year post-study work visa for relevant job
records.description: International graduates who secure roles aligned with their field of study should receive a five-year post-study work visa to support skills retention and the economy. Those not in relevant roles would remain on the current two-year Graduate Route.
records.further_details: This proposal links post-study visas to relevant employment, encouraging graduates to use their skills in the UK economy. We believe it helps address labour shortages, supports SMEs without sponsorship costs, and boosts UK education appeal. A five-year visa promotes stability, economic contribution, and career growth, while motivating students to align studies with workforce needs. We believe that the UK Government consider this proposal as part of ongoing reviews of the Graduate Route.

records.title: Introduce mandatory rest time between calls for call centre workers
records.description: Require employers in call centres and high-volume customer service roles to provide a minimum rest period between customer interactions to protect workers’ mental health and wellbeing.
records.further_details: Many call centre and customer service workers are required to handle continuous back-to-back calls with little or no time to recover between interactions. This can lead to high levels of stress, anxiety and burnout, seriously affecting mental health and wellbeing. We believe the Government should introduce legislation to require a minimum rest period between calls to protect workers and promote healthier, more sustainable working conditions.

records.title: Require social media to add timed pauses during extended short-video use.
records.description:
Introduce timed pauses between each individual short-form video content.

- No delay for first 10 mins
- 2s delay after 10 mins
- 5s delay after 20 mins
- User confirmation after 30 mins

Applies only to short-form video feeds. Delays must be neutral, with no ads or added content.
records.further_details: Social media platforms are often designed for continuous, frictionless scrolling, which can encourage compulsive use and reduce attention span, potentially harming productivity, mental wellbeing, and public health. Introducing increasing pauses during extended use would prompt conscious choice without restricting access. Government action is needed to ensure proportionate safeguards against addictive design, similar to harm-reduction in other sectors.

records.title: Non means tested Legal Aid for foster carers challenging Council's care plans
records.description: Provide non-means-tested Legal Aid for foster carers challenging Local Authority care plans through court orders (Adoption/SGO). Carers shouldn't face financial ruin to protect a child's welfare. We need a level playing field to ensure the child’s best interests are always the priority in court.
records.further_details: Authorities have substantial funds for care plans, but foster carers must self-fund challenges, costing tens of thousands. Foster carers have successfully challenged local authority care plans in court because they were not in the best interests of the child, but this can cost tens of thousands of pounds. We believe the current system silences carers via legal costs. We must remove means-testing to ensure justice isn't dependent on a carer's bank balance.

records.title: Call for an international investigation into missing Alawite women in Syria
records.description: We ask the UK Government to call for a independent international investigation into reports of disappearances, alleged abductions, coercion, and forced sectarian conversion of Alawite women and girls in Syria, to press for the protection of minorities, and for accountability.
records.further_details: Many families have raised concerns about missing girls in Syria. Some families dispute videos and statements claiming relatives left voluntarily, alleging coercion and intimidation. Reports from media and human rights groups have increased fear among minorities. We believe the UK should support human rights, the protection of minorities, transparent investigations, and accountability for any abuses.

records.title: Encourage the ESA to study Sedna as a potential mission target
records.description: We are asking the UK Government to encourage the European Space Agency to study Sedna as a potential target for a future deep space mission. Sedna is one of the most distant known objects in our Solar System, and studying it during its perihelion (2076) could provide valuable information.
records.further_details: Sedna’s extreme distance means it has been only briefly observable from Earth, making this perihelion window scientifically valuable. A mission study could assess trajectory options, power systems, and long-duration communication for deep space exploration beyond the Kuiper Belt. Early planning now would ensure any feasible mission design is not missed during this rare orbital opportunity, which is a once in 11,000 years event.

records.title: Ban the publication of a criminal’s religion, nationality or immigration status
records.description: We believe publishing a criminal’s religion, nationality, or immigration status unfairly associates entire communities with the actions of one individual, and can fuel prejudice, division, and violence.
records.further_details:
We feel reporting should focus on an offender's actions and the facts, not characteristics shared by innocent people.

We call on the Government to ban public authorities, politicians and media outlets from publishing and highlighting a suspect or criminal’s religion, nationality, ethnicity, or immigration status unless it is directly relevant to the crime or public safety. Unnecessary disclosure could encourage collective blame, inflame tensions, and expose innocent people to hostility or violence. We believe public communication should focus on the individual and promote accountability without fuelling division in society.

records.title: Fund more special needs support in primary and secondary schools
records.description: I would like the government to fund more special needs support in schools. Increase the amount of one to one and small group support for students and find more specialists in this department.
records.further_details: The government could increase their budget given to the schools for the resources required for them to support these students.

records.title: Grant citizenship to legal foreign nationals living in the UK for 20+ years
records.description: Automatically grant legal citizenship to foreign nationals who have lived and paid taxes in the UK for over 20 years or were born to parents who have done this. We believe they should have the right to be considered British, and should receive citizenship without any hassle or fees.
records.further_details:
We do not believe someone should be charged over £2000 to become a British citizen if they have lived and paid taxes here for over 20 years, and that living here for over 20 years demonstrates that they are here to stay and happy to be part of your society.
We also believe the children of foreign nationals, who have not all been given British citizenship, should also be granted citizenship and should not be charged any fees either.

records.title: Set statutory maximum temperatures for schools and care homes
records.description: We call on the UK Government and Parliament to introduce a mandatory maximum temperature for schools and care homes to protect children, elderly people, and vulnerable individuals during extreme heatwaves.
records.further_details: Extreme heat is becoming more frequent and intense, creating unsafe conditions in schools and care homes. Children, elderly people, and vulnerable individuals are at greater risk from high temperatures, which can affect health, concentration, and wellbeing. We are calling for clear statutory standards requiring indoor temperatures in care homes and schools to be kept below a specified safe level.

records.title: Allow Child Benefit to be backdated to the start of a child’s eligibility
records.description: Amend the Social Security Administration Act 1992 to remove the strict three-month backdating limit for Child Benefit claims.
records.further_details: Families shouldn’t lose essential Child Benefit due to lack of awareness, illness, or complex rules. Misleading media reporting about a “2 child cap” caused confusion and delayed claims even where children were legally eligible. It’s unjust that statutory support is paid from the application date, not the true eligibility date.

records.title: Apply to adopt the Euro currency
records.description: We are regular everyday citizens who see that the UK is working towards refreshing the relationship with our closest trading partner which is the EU. We might be British but we feel aligned with Europe and would like to see the Euro being adopted here.
records.further_details: This is possible to do without being a member of the EU. Kosovo and Montenegro have already done it.

records.title: Do not introduce a new property tax without protecting recent stamp duty payers
records.description: Require any new annual property tax to include a full credit for Stamp Duty paid within the previous five years, with transitional relief for homeowners facing substantial increases.
records.further_details:
Homeowners who recently paid substantial Stamp Duty could be unfairly disadvantaged. They would have paid a large upfront tax under the existing system, only to face a new annual property tax shortly afterwards, while future purchasers benefit from the abolition of Stamp Duty.

Any reform should provide a full credit for Stamp Duty paid within five years of implementation, applied against future property-tax liabilities, plus a phased transition and protection from excessive increases.

records.title: Increase the Parliamentary Candidate Deposit to Reduce Ballot Paper Length
records.description: The Government should set up a review with a view to increasing the candidate deposit to reflect modern values and inflation. A higher deposit would continue to allow genuine candidates to stand while discouraging frivolous or publicity-driven candidacies that unnecessarily complicate elections.
records.further_details: The current £500 deposit required to stand for election to the House of Commons has remained unchanged since 1985. In real terms, inflation has significantly reduced its value.  At recent General Elections, many constituencies have seen unprecedented numbers of candidates. This has resulted in excessively long ballot papers that are more expensive to print, more difficult for voters to navigate, and which can place additional administrative burdens on Returning Officers and polling staff.

records.title: Make political motivation an aggravating factor in sentencing for offences
records.description: Introduce legislation to make political motivation an aggravating factor in sentencing when determining the seriousness of an offence, including a violent crime or an incitement to violence. We are concerned inflammatory political labels are being increasingly used to incite hatred and violence.
records.further_details: When people are called inflammatory political labels without evidence, it can incite hatred and violence against them. We are concerned political witch-hunting is escalating. We ask that political motivation be treated as an aggravating factor in sentencing for violent crimes and inciting violence, so those who use such labels to stir up violence face stronger penalties.

records.title: Legally require restaurants and fast food chains to cater for diabetics
records.description: Introduce mandatory laws requiring restaurants and fast-food chains to offer diabetic-friendly meal options certified by health and nutrition professionals, utilizing low-glycemic ingredients and healthy alternatives for diabetic people rather than just standard carbohydrates.
records.further_details: The UK faces a major diabetes epidemic, with 6M people estimated to be living with diabetes, and 1.3M of those undiagnosed. Diabetics are often excluded from dining out due to high-glycemic commercial menus. It is unacceptable for anyone to tell them to "just eat a salad"; plain salad lacks vital protein and amino acids needed for basic health. We want restaurants to be legally required to provide core menu alternatives for diabetics rather than just standard carbs, such as chip shops offering low-glycemic sweet potato options alongside white potatoes.

records.title: Fund more transport police
records.description: I want the UK government to increase funding for transport police to add more on-board police on train / bus services. I think this would help to stop any violence toward women and girls. They deserve a journey home or somewhere without a male coming up to them and abusing them.
records.further_details: I have made this petition to help women feel safe about using public transport.

records.title: Legal duty on local authorities to ensure sufficient road crossings near schools
records.description: The Government must place a legal duty on local councils to make sure roads have sufficient crossings, such as traffic lights or zebra crossings, within a reasonable distance to the schools.
records.further_details: We believe those going to and from school should have good safety when needing to cross the road.

records.title: Add Idiopathic intercranial hypertension to NHS medical exemption certificate
records.description: We want the Government to include Idiopathic intercranial hypertension (IIH) in the list for NHS medical exemption certificates. The nature of the conditions leads individuals to take additional medications for migraines, nausea, CSF production, fatigue, weight loss and increased ICP.
records.further_details: IIH is a condition where cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) builds up inside the skull around the brain for no known reason; causing debilitating daily headaches, pulsatile tinnitus, cognitive dysfunction, blurred or permanent vision loss. As a result, variety of medications are utilised to prevent this and manage effects of headache and migraines. these impacts for most individuals IIH is considered a disability, so we believe it should be added to the medical exemption certificate to help support individuals with many medications.

records.title: Require replacement of swimming pools and gyms lost via major development
records.description: We call on the Government to strengthen national planning policy so that where major development results in the loss of an existing swimming pool, gym or comparable indoor leisure facility, planning permission should require equivalent replacement leisure capacity.
records.further_details: Swimming pools and indoor gyms are vital community leisure facilities. We want the Government to strengthen planning policy so that when major development removes an existing swimming pool or gym, genuinely equivalent replacement capacity is required. Recent redevelopments show why this is needed: gyms and swimming pools are being lost, while proposed green space, outdoor exercise facilities and compensation do not provide equivalent indoor leisure provision.

records.title: Require education settings provide anti-loneliness & social isolation education
records.description: Require all education settings to provide education which tackles loneliness and social isolation among young people, which includes providing teaching on communication, relationship building and social connection skills to help reduce loneliness and social isolation.
records.further_details: Loneliness and social isolation are growing issues, particularly among young people. We believe education should play a greater role in helping students develop the confidence, communication and relationship building skills needed to form meaningful social connections. By teaching these skills in schools, colleges and universities, we can help reduce social isolation, improve wellbeing and better equip young people to participate in their communities and build supportive networks throughout life.

records.title: Conduct a review into school hours to support guidance for later start & finish
records.description: We call on the Government to conduct a review into school hours and to help introduce guidance encouraging schools to start at 9:30am and finish at 3:50pm or later, while maintaining the required amount of teaching time.
records.further_details:
We want the Government to look to encourage schools in England to move to a later school day, starting at 9:30am and finishing at 3:50pm or later, while maintaining teaching time.

Later starts could give children more sleep, reduce stressful mornings and better fit modern working patterns, including shifts and commuting. We also want the Government review to assess the impact on children’s wellbeing, attendance and traffic congestion. This aim would be to move the school day later, not reduce education.

records.title: Government to disclose legal advice on axing local authority reorganisation
records.description: The government recently announced the withdrawal or pausing of plans to reorganise several counties, following legal advice that it will not disclose. But plans to divide Surrey will not be reviewed. We want to see the legal grounds for this policy shift now before the new councils in Surrey start.
records.further_details: Government is accountable to Parliament for policy decisions. This decision follows new legal advice. The policy area is not sensitive so we think there is no reason why it cannot be disclosed. In our view secrecy would also set a terrible constitutional precedent: a government that changes policy on the back of legal advice need not disclose that advice. Surrey residents & councillors want to see this advice now to understand why Surrey is an exception.

records.title: Review exam and assessment pressures in the KS4 and KS5 curriculums
records.description: We are concerned that high exam pressure in Key Stage 4 and 5 is fuelling a severe youth mental health crisis. The Government must conduct an urgent review to look at how to reduce assessment pressure and inject vital new funding into school mental health awareness and professional support.
records.further_details: I am starting this petition to raise vital awareness about the unseen toll of our education system. Overwhelmed by testing, students face unprecedented anxiety.  Having witnessed the impact of relentless academic stress, I believe that the current setup breaks student well-being long before exam day. High-stakes testing can trigger severe anxiety and depression. We believe we urgently need a balanced system that protects youth health, backed by dedicated government funding for early mental health intervention.

records.title: Require people to give a minimum of £50 pa to charity
records.description: Studies suggest that 50% of people do not donate to charity, therefore some charities do not receive enough funds to achieve their desired aim. All charities have important goals, so we feel this problem is not OK. If my idea becomes a law, people have to give a minimum of £50 annually to charity.
records.further_details:
The following would be exempt from this law: minors, elderly, pensioners, people who are unable to work (due to mental and/or physical illness and/or disability), people who are unemployed for other reasons, homeless people, people living in poverty, and people with a low income.
 
UK charities have important goals in mind and they need help from us, the citizens.

records.title: Review the use of weight in CAMHS Eating Disorder service criteria
records.description: Review the use of BMI and weight when assessing people for treatment for eating disorders in CAMHS.
records.further_details: We believe using weight as a way to determine whether or not someone receives treatment for an eating disorder can be very damaging as it can lead people to think they have to lose weight in order to access help and reaching medical and mental crisis.

records.title: Review life-saving care for vulnerable patients, including with addiction issues
records.description: We believe that many vulnerable patients, including those with addiction issues, are systematically denied life-saving treatments. We call for a review to be conducted, as this medical neglect must end. Every patient deserves a fighting chance, regardless of their background or health challenges.
records.further_details: In our view, there is a disturbing pattern of doctors withholding treatment from vulnerable groups and those with addictions. My son Jamie passed away. Despite being in urgent need, he was denied surgical intervention and left to pass away in pain. We are calling for an immediate review to ensure all patients are given every possible chance to live.

records.title: Allow Any Motorcycle to Be Safely Restricted to 35kW for A2 Riders
records.description: We want the Government to allow motorcycles of any original power to be safely restricted to 35 kW for A2 riders, removing the “double power” rule. All restrictions should be verifiable and meet safety standards, giving riders more choice, freedom, and safer progression.
records.further_details: Current A2 rules limit riders to fewer motorcycles – those up to 35kW or, with a fitted restrictor, up to 70kW – reducing choice and sometimes forcing illegal riding, which increases risk. Modern restriction systems can safely limit any bike to 35 kW, giving riders access to more motorcycles and safer technology like ABS and traction control. Updating the law will expand legal options and could help encourage responsible riding, support skill progression, and protect all road users.

records.title: Create & grant a 5-year visa for students who worked in the UK for a year
records.description: We call on the Government to grant a 5-year work visa to international students who have worked legally in the UK for at least 1 year. This should be a direct pathway to residency based on BACS-verified tax contributions, independent of a single employer's sponsorship.
records.further_details: Many international students contribute to the UK economy for years via PAYE but may face deportation or employer exploitation due to the restrictive sponsorship system. By granting a visa based on verified HMRC/BACS history, the UK could retain vetted talent and increase tax revenue. This could reward legal migrants, many of whom are the backbone of the economy, and eliminate what we believe are exploitary conditions created when a visa is tied to a single employer, which may lead to financial extortion.

records.title: Safeguard registered charities from disruptive protests including buffer zones
records.description: We ask the UK Government to introduce proportionate safeguards to protect premises operated by charities registered with the Charity Commission from disruptive and abusive protests.
records.further_details:
Many registered charities are attended by vulnerable individuals and are often located in residential and commercial areas, where loud noise can disrupt local residents and businesses.
 
There have been instances of protestors using loudspeakers, shouting, and offensive or sexually explicit language, causing distress and disturbance.
We call on the Government to introduce targeted measures, such as buffer zones, to prevent protests in the vicinity of these registered charity premises.

records.title: Expand Windrush Compensation to Descendants and Remove Unfair Proof Requirement
records.description: The UK Government should expand the Windrush Compensation Scheme to provide automatic, standardised compensation to members of the Windrush generation who worked in the UK and to their children and grandchildren.
records.further_details:
The UK Gov should expand the WC Scheme to provide automatic payments to documented claimants and their children and grandchildren. Many were underpaid, denied pensions, and lost opportunities, causing lasting harm.
The current scheme requires extensive proof, many records are missing, claimants are elderly or deceased, creating a barrier to justice. Automatic payments recognise intergenerational impact and restore fairness. This is not new spending—it is an “outstanding inv” for wage and pension

records.title: Review impact of scrapping LISA for disabled savers, retain equivalent option
records.description: Carry out and publish an equality impact assessment and review the impact on disabled savers, before removing retirement saving option from the Lifetime ISA in 2028. We also call for an equivalent, tax-advantaged retirement saving option with Government bonus to be retained for those who rely on it.
records.further_details: Disability is protected under the Equality Act 2010. In our view, for people whose conditions affect impulse control or deferring reward, an automatic, structured account is a reasonable adjustment, not a preference. The Lifetime ISA's bonused retirement route is being scrapped for first-time buyers only. Disabled people, who may be less likely to have a workplace pension, can lose it disproportionately. Under the Public Sector Equality Duty, we ask the Government to assess this impact and keep an equivalent option.

records.title: Create new legal protections for child sexual abuse victims in criminal cases
records.description: Enact legal protections for child sexual abuse victims in criminal investigations & court proceedings to prevent re-traumatisation, including a limit on their exposure to recorded interviews of themselves giving evidence & a statutory time limit for the defence to submit cross-examination questions.
records.further_details: We support legislation which aims to protect child survivors of sexual abuse from unnecessary re-traumatisation during the criminal justice process. Children can be asked to revisit evidence years after disclosure, which could cause further harm and repeated trauma. We call for legal safeguards including limits on a victim’s exposure to recorded interviews of themselves and a clear, legally mandated timeframe for submitting defence questions.

records.title: Fund cash payments to students for school attendance
records.description: We believe the Government should pay children to attend school; they shouldn’t be able to use the money until they are 18. This could help give them a jumpstart in the real world. We feel this is necessary as school attendance is very important for a child’s future.
records.further_details: This could help future generations with housing, employment, life milestones, etc. We believe the cost of living is becoming higher every day and leaving many children with an uncertain future. Giving them money could have a significant impact by encouraging children to feel learning is truly worth it and could result in them having better job opportunities in the future.

records.title: Government must secure more funding for councils
records.description: The Government needs to do more so that councils receive additional funding to help them fully serve their communities. We think there are many ways to do this, including: implement council surcharges on existing taxes, expand second home premiums or stop the super-rich from dodging their taxes.
records.further_details: We believe the state of England's councils is perhaps the most appalling political horror story our nation has to offer. We feel that our councils are drowning in absurd debt for merely providing their people with basic necessities - this is unacceptable, and we must fight for change and justice. We can debate the means by which we achieve this extra funding, but what cannot debate the absolute urgency of the need for more funding. We believe our councils deserve more money.

records.title: Deliver long-awaited legislation for safer cosmetic injectable procedures
records.description: We call on the Government to publish and implement legislation for cosmetic injectable procedures without any further delay, ensuring clear national standards for patient safety, informed consent, transparency, competency, accountability and patient education.
records.further_details: The Government has acknowledged the need to regulate cosmetic injectable procedures, but patients are still waiting for legislation. We ask the Government to deliver legislation without further delay that protects patients while supporting ethical practitioners through clear national standards for competency, informed consent, transparency, accountability, product traceability and patient education, helping reduce unsafe practice and counterfeit products.

records.title: Create an annual UK Mental Health and Wellbeing Bank Holiday.
records.description: Create an annual UK Mental Health and Wellbeing Bank Holiday to encourage rest, reduce stigma, promote community support and raise awareness.
records.further_details: We want the UK Government to introduce an annual Mental Health and Wellbeing Bank Holiday. The day should encourage rest, improve work-life balance, reduce stigma around mental health and promote community support. The Government should work with employers, charities and local authorities to organise awareness campaigns and wellbeing initiatives across the UK. This would recognise the importance of mental health, encourage people to recharge, and help create a healthier, more connected society.

records.title: Allow trainee teachers in Initial Teacher Training to claim Universal Credit
records.description: We want the UK Government to exempt Initial Teacher Training from the advanced education group for Universal Credit claim purposes. We think eligibility for Universal Credit for Initial Teacher Trainees should remain subject to the usual means-testing and earnings rules.
records.further_details: England faces ongoing teacher shortages, yet we believe many people cannot afford to complete full-time Initial Teacher Training (ITT). Trainees spend much of their training on compulsory school placements, which can leave little opportunity for paid work. While some receive student finance or bursaries, this is not available to everyone and may not cover essential living costs. We believe trainee teachers should be able to claim Universal Credit if they meet the regular eligibility rules.

records.title: Review Funeral Expenses Payment rules for people in full-time work
records.description: I want the Government to review Funeral Expenses Payment eligibility so that people like me, who work full-time but cannot afford an unexpected funeral, can receive support based on their actual financial circumstances rather than being excluded because they do not receive a qualifying benefit.
records.further_details: I was refused Funeral Expenses Payment because I work full-time and do not receive a qualifying benefit, despite being unable to afford my father’s unexpected funeral due to limited savings, a mortgage and bills. I believe the rules unfairly assume that being employed means people can afford these costs and should consider income and financial circumstances rather than receipt of benefits.

records.title: Make verbal abuse of call centre workers a specific criminal offence
records.description: We are looking for Government to create a specific criminal offence to verbally abuse or threaten call centre workers whilst on duty working on the phone lines.
records.further_details:
Most experienced call centre workers understand that things do go wrong. System errors, human error, postal delays can all contribute to a customer's dissatisfaction.

While we have all handled complaints and dissatisfaction, abuse or threats of violence should never be tolerated.

We have been customers ourselves, what we wish to see is a law that seeks to criminalise verbal abuse towards us and threats of physical violence towards us.

records.title: Mandate online vehicle service history & maintenance schedule access for owners
records.description: Require vehicle manufacturers to give owners free online access to their vehicle’s complete service history and a vehicle-specific maintenance schedule showing completed, current and future maintenance requirements.
records.further_details: Digital service records vary between manufacturers, and owners can struggle to see what maintenance their own vehicle has received or what is due next. Government should require manufacturers to provide free, online, transferable and printable records, plus a vehicle-specific schedule based on mileage, age, engine, transmission and specification, clearly showing completed and upcoming maintenance.

records.title: Protect Good Landlords and Good Tenants: Establish a Tenant Registry
records.description: The Government should create a tenants registry to help improve screening, cut rent arrears disputes, and reduce pressure on courts by preventing avoidable non payment cases. This helps tenants prove good history and thereby rewarding good behaviour by faster and fairer vetting process.
records.further_details: We are asking the Government to introduce a compulsory National Tenants register, similar to the recently introduced compulsory Landlord's register. We believe a nationwide tenants registry would make renting fairer and more transparent. It would let landlords check reliable rental history and help good tenants prove their track record. By reducing avoidable rent arrears disputes and easing pressure on the courts, it supports a more stable, accountable housing system for everyone.

records.title: Require lighter coloured roofing and paving material to combat climate change
records.description: We call on the Government to introduce guidance on Minimum Solar Reflectance Index expectations for new residential walls and roofing. Including advice such as encouraging parking lots use high-albedo paving materials (like light-coloured concrete, pale pavers, or surfaces with reflective topcoats).
records.further_details: Building materials come in a range of colours and the fraction of light energy absorbed by them can make a real difference to the climate in our cities, but in our view most builders and architects give this little thought. In the public interest, we think that something closer to the colour pallet of a Cotswold village should be encouraged as a consideration when judging the adequacy of a planning application.

records.title: Keep 10-year Long Residence Route for people already living in the UK
records.description: Retain the 10-year Long Residence settlement route at least for those on the route living in the UK since 2021. Many came following the representation that they would qualify for ILR after 10 years. We believe replacing the Long Residence route and its existing rules would be a breach of contract.
records.further_details: Retain the 10-Year Long Residence Route and stop any retrospective application of the government’s proposed changes to ILR to those already living on the UK who are on the Long Residence route.

records.title: Fund free prescriptions and home heating for sickle cell patients
records.description: We want the UK Government to fund free NHS prescriptions and financial support for heating costs during winter for people with sickle cell disease.
records.further_details: People with sickle cell disease often face lifelong costs associated with medication, managing their condition and staying warm during winter. This petition calls for practical financial support to reduce these burdens and recognise the additional costs faced by people living with sickle cell disease.

records.title: Remove the 4-week overseas travel limit for Pension Credit recipients
records.description: Amend Regulation 3 of The State Pension Credit Regulations 2002 to remove all limits on how long a person can receive Pension Credit payments whilst they’re overseas and not in Great Britain.
records.further_details:
We believe people on Pension Credit should not be treated as prisoners or limited to travel. Regulation 3 of the State Pension Credit Regulations 2002 restricts absence to 4 weeks. 
 
We call on the Government to abolish the 4-week restriction so there is no restriction at all. Once entitled, we believe people should be free to travel, visit family, or spend time abroad for as long as they wish. Their support should not stop simply because they leave the country. We believe freedom to travel should not depend on financial support and we call on the complete removal of the limit.

records.title: Enact Statutory Oversight and Mandatory Safeguards for Frontier AI Development
records.description: Call on the Government to introduce binding regulation, mandatory third-party safety audits, and strict statutory oversight for private corporations developing frontier and superintelligent AI systems.
records.further_details: We think the rapid pace of frontier AI development poses severe risks to national security, public safety, and democratic stability. Industry whistleblowers warn that corporate competition drives firms to prioritise speed over safety. We believe leaving superintelligent AI in private hands without statutory oversight is as dangerous as privatising control of a nuclear arsenal. Voluntary commitments are insufficient; binding legal frameworks are urgently required.

records.title: Grant devolved powers to England & create an elected First Minister of England
records.description: Grant devolved powers to England, so that a devolved English Government operates within a framework comparable to the relationship between the US Federal Government and state governors.
records.further_details:
The UK Government should retain defence, foreign affairs and national policing, while an elected English First Minister governs England in partnership with regional mayors.
 
The UK Government has left England without a devolved government, while decisions affecting English communities remain heavily centralised at Westminster. We believe England deserves greater democratic accountability and a stronger voice over its own domestic affairs. An elected English First Minister would work with regional mayors, while the UK Government in Westminster would focus on UK-wide responsibilities such as defence and foreign affairs.

records.title: Require nurseries to have individual SEND support plans before a child starts
records.description: Parents can be told that a nursery can meet their additional needs without being told exactly what support will be provided. Children who are non-verbal or have significant developmental and communication difficulties may be unable to tell their parents when they are distressed, who cared for them.
records.further_details:
We believe parents should know, before their child starts, who is responsible for their support, what staffing arrangements are in place, what relevant training staff have and how distress or dysregulation will be managed.

This would give families greater clarity and accountability and help ensure children with significant SEND receive appropriate support from the beginning of their nursery placement.

records.title: Commission independent review of Child Maintenance Service rules and practices
records.description: Commission an independent review of Child Maintenance Service, including how it verifies eligibility, investigates information provided by both parents, handles shared-care arrangements, and whether its systems and rules remain fair, transparent and fit for modern families.
records.further_details: The Child Maintenance Service needs a fundamental review to ensure its systems reflect modern family life. Concerns include how CMS verifies whether children remain in qualifying education, how it investigates information supplied by either parent, and its reliance on other systems such as Child Benefit. The rules around shared care also warrant review, particularly where parents provide substantially equal care but one may still be liable for maintenance.

records.title: Create a bespoke Ofsted inspection toolkit aligned with the childminder EYFS
records.description: Childminders have their own EYFS framework and deserve a bespoke Ofsted inspection toolkit. We call for clear, proportionate criteria that recognise their unique provision, uphold high standards and provide a fair route to every grade, including exceptional.
records.further_details: Childminders often combine leadership, safeguarding, curriculum planning and direct care in one role or a small team. A bespoke toolkit should explain how these responsibilities, learning through everyday routines and meaningful progress within small cohorts are assessed. Developed with practising childminders, we believe it would strengthen consistency and recognise impact on each child, without allowing setting size or cohort composition to become a barrier to recognition.

records.title: Require free allergy badges and bracelets for children with food allergies
records.description: Provide children with diagnosed food allergies with a free, standardised allergy identification bracelet and badge. These should clearly display allergens and a recognised warning such as “FOOD ALLERGY ” helping adults quickly identify children who may be at risk of a serious allergic reaction.
records.further_details: I see first-hand how difficult it can be to identify and protect children at risk of anaphylaxis. I want the Government to introduce a clear, nationally recognised allergy identification scheme, such as standard wristbands or visible ID, for children with diagnosed food allergies. This could help staff recognise allergies quickly, reduce accidental exposure and improve safety in schools and public settings.

records.title: Introduce a Remembrance Day for all children under 18 who have lost their lives
records.description: Create a Remembrance Day for all families and parents who have lost a child or children under the age of 18, including a moment of silence. This could help families grieve better as there would be a special day for their beloved young angels.
records.further_details: There are so many families around the World suffering from the harsh effects and troubles around the globe. I believe losing a child has to be at the top of things to suffer through, and I think this day could bring families together and give every parent a better grieving process, as there would be a day to remember their children and all children who have lost their lives. It could ensure that they are still remembered for years to come, even when we do move on in life.

records.title: Make medical professionals mandatory in DLA award decisions
records.description: DLA decisions are made by non-medical staff (unless at the tribunal stage) and we believe this can lead to unfair outcomes. We are concerned that some children's complex needs can be underestimated.
records.further_details:
Including medical professionals at the initial stage could ensure fairer, accurate decisions and reduce stressful appeals for families.

We believe the DLA system is unfair, with decisions made by those lacking medical understanding, leading to inaccurate assessments. We think the system adds emotional strain to already overwhelmed carers and more medical involvement is essential to ensure fair, accurate decisions from the start.

records.title: Create a Charter of Stewardship for farming, food & heritage sports sectors
records.description: Create a Charter of Stewardship for farmers, butchers, fishmongers & those in heritage sports. The Charter should repeal 2026 digital reporting mandates, protect the Section 2 license distinction, halt bird shooting bans & bring forward a Farmer-Led Land Use Framework over industrial rewilding.
records.further_details:
We feel this is needed to secure our food and heritage. We believe current 2026 policies like the March 18 Land Use Framework and mandatory digital reporting create a “digital noose” that many disagree with.

We reject the merging of Section 1 & 2 licenses and the January 2026 "Processing Statement" requirement on local trade. We believe stewardship should remain in the hands of those who work the land and sea, not desktop modellers. Policy should be evidence-led to protect our ability to harvest and manage our countryside.

records.title: Introduce mandatory independent pre-appeal review of asylum refusal decisions
records.description: Introduce an independent pre-appeal review stage for asylum refusal decisions, allowing factual errors, misunderstandings, translation issues, and credibility concerns to be identified and corrected before cases proceed to tribunal appeal.
records.further_details: In our view, decisions with potentially irreversible consequences should not rely on a single subjective assessment without meaningful independent scrutiny. We think errors in factual understanding or translation should be addressed before appeal, as we believe the appeal process should not be the primary mechanism for correcting administrative errors. An independent pre-appeal review stage could improve accuracy, strengthen procedural safeguards, and reduce unnecessary appeals based on flawed initial decisions.

records.title: Review how DWP corrects RTI system errors for SME directors
records.description: We want a review of how DWP corrects incorrect HMRC Real Time Information (RTI) data in calculating universal credit. We think DWP often fails to use universal credit regulation to prevent year-end annual company profits from being treated as one month's personal income for company directors.
records.further_details: In our view, Universal Credit often misinterprets annual HMRC tax filings from small-company directors as a one-month personal income payment, thereby triggering the Surplus Earnings rules. Although Regulation 61 allows DWP Decision Makers to correct RTI errors, in our view, this is often not applied, which we believe can cause hardship, debt and business closures.

records.title: Fund AI training for all teachers
records.description: Fund dedicated CPD training to teachers in AI, to allow them to use AI in the classroom and explain to their students best practice and use of AI.
records.further_details: AI can be a useful tool in education from Early Years to University. However, we believe that unless there is a unified standardised approach to AI usage, there could be misuse or a disparity in education delivery. In our view each student has a right to have access to AI and that can only be provided in the classroom.

records.title: Allow all registered CICs and Not for Profits to benefit from Gift Aid
records.description: Allow all registered CICs and Not for Profits to claim gift aid from donors and the added benefits to corporate donations for tax purposes. We think this could help fund more vital services and encourage businesses to engage with the rapidly growing number of alternative not for profit structures.
records.further_details: We think this change could help create equality across all organisations supporting others by allowing the same incentives for al, and that it would demonstrate the support the government has for all not for profits who save the tax payer money in delivering critical services. In our view it appears at odds with the governments intention when they introduced CICs to encourage more charitable activity to simply curtail the support available to them, knowing the social return on investment and savings these CICs create.

records.title: Review UK naturalisation requirements & fees for settled residents
records.description: Review naturalisation fees and requirements, such as the Life in the UK test, for settled residents who may have arrived in the UK as children and have lived, worked, and paid tax in the UK.
records.further_details: Many long-term residents arrived in the UK as children, were educated here, have worked, paid taxes and contributed to society for decades. Despite this, many must pay substantial naturalisation fees and pass the Life in the UK test to become British citizens. We call on the Government to launch a review into this, including looking into reducing fees, creating exemptions or a streamlined route to citizenship for those who have spent most of their lives in the UK.

records.title: Require jury trials for all civil litigation claims exceeding £1 billion
records.description: Mandate the use of jury trials for all civil litigation claims exceeding £1 billion.
records.further_details:
Prior to 1933, civil jury trials were common in England. Recently multi-billion pound mass-tort litigations have been put to a single judge to make the final court decision. We believe such massive public-interest decisions should not rest on one individual. 
 
Restoring juries for civil claims could help ensure democratic transparency, and community alignment in the UK's highest-stakes corporate legal battles.

records.title: Hold a referendum on making Hampshire an independent, sovereign state
records.description: I call upon the UK Parliament to allow Hampshire to hold a binding independence referendum on whether Hampshire should leave the UK and become independent. I want Winchester to become the capital, and I want peace, fairness and safety for all of Hampshire.
records.further_details:
I believe Hampshire has a strong economy, history, identity and communities, and that Hampshire’s industries, farms, ports, tourism and public services are working well for it to become independent. I believe an independent Hampshire should have a fully written constitution agreed by its residents.
 
I ask for Parliament to let the people of Hampshire to choose their own future and give the people of Hampshire their democratic say on what they feel is best for them.

records.title: Commission a business case for UK sovereign data-centre network
records.description:
Commission and publish an independent feasibility study and business case for building standardised modular data centres on suitable public land.

It should identify all potential sites and compare ten-year public ownership costs with continued reliance on commercial cloud and hosting providers.
records.further_details: Public services need secure computing, storage & AI capacity. The Government should assess if public ownership could cut long-term costs, improve resilience, protect data and reduce reliance on technology companies. The business case should examine capital & operating costs, power & fibre availability, job creation, apprenticeship opportunities, cybersecurity, workloads, savings & income from leasing spare capacity. It should publish assumptions, shortlisted sites & recommendations.

records.title: Unlimited funding for police for any resources they need
records.description: I ask that police have unlimited funding in order to be able to act when needed on public safety; also for anything they should need in their line of work.
records.further_details:
As we rely on the police for safety and security, we believe it is only fit that they should have unlimited funding when needed.
 
In order for the public to feel safer and securer during day and night, we think our police forces should have unlimited funding.
 
Criminals and victimisers are none stop; and it is difficult for police to see everything or be more active if they haven’t got the resources of funding we think they should be entitled to in order to prevent anything from happening or take action when needed.

records.title: Align the UK tax year with the calendar year
records.description: Legislate to align the UK tax year with the calendar year by changing it to run from 1 January to 31 December, with a suitable transition period.
records.further_details: The UK's tax year runs from 6 April to 5 April for historical reasons dating back centuries. Aligning it with the calendar year could simplify the tax system, making it easier for taxpayers, employers, accountants and businesses to understand and administer. It could also better align the UK with international practice. We ask the Government to introduce this change following a suitable transition period to allow systems and legislation to be updated.

records.title: Require floor material restrictions in leases be based on acoustic performance
records.description: Some lease clauses still force carpet-only flooring in flats, despite modern wood/laminate floors with acoustic underlays matching or exceeding noise standards. This can harm allergy sufferers and limit choice. Leases should only be able to set acoustic performance standards, not mandate carpet.
records.further_details: Some leases contain absolute “carpet and underfelt” covenants. Courts interpret these strictly, so even high-performance floating floors can be treated as a breach. Modern acoustic underlays and isolated systems can even exceed Building Regulations Part E impact sound targets, yet many freeholders still refuse consent on principle. Leaseholders face costly licence applications or risk formal action. A mandatory performance-based standard would give clarity and fairness while still protecting neighbours.

records.title: Ban the sale of domestic gas hobs and ovens
records.description: We support a ban on the sale of domestic gas hobs and ovens to help the environment and public health. Ohio’s publicly owned MetroHealth study in July 2026 found that replacing gas hobs and ovens with electric ones improved asthma symptoms in a way that was as good as some asthma medications.
records.further_details: This proposed ban would not include industrial gas hobs and ovens, nor emergency equipment.

records.title: Ban anonymous reports to children’s social services
records.description: Require people making referrals to children’s social services to provide their identity confidentially, and introduce penalties for anyone who knowingly makes a false or malicious report intended to harass, intimidate or cause harm.
records.further_details: I want the Government to change the law so that anyone making a referral to children’s social services must provide their identity confidentially to the local authority. Their identity should not be automatically shared with the family. I also want penalties introduced for anyone who is found to have knowingly made a false or malicious report intended to harass, intimidate or cause harm. This could help prevent abuse of the system while protecting genuine safeguarding referrals.

records.title: Create a taskforce to review laws containing the term “reasonable”
records.description: The Government should create a taskforce which reviews all laws containing the term "reasonable”, identifies vague or unnecessary uses, and recommends clearer wording. Courts and public bodies should be mandated to explain how people’s circumstances are considered in their decisions.
records.further_details:
The taskforce’s review should cover “reasonable”, “objectively reasonable”, “reasonably”, “reasonable excuse” and “reasonable grounds”. These terms can leave important questions in the hands of judges or officials. 
 
Judges may be highly skilled, but we feel their role may not reflect the circumstances of people being judged. We believe laws containing the terms “reasonable” should clearly say whose perspective counts when judging what is “reasonable”, which factors are considered, and why an outcome is fair in each legal case.

records.title: Give families legal right to an independent investigation after a neonatal death
records.description: Create a law, "Rosie's Right", giving families automatic legal rights to an independent investigation into a neonatal death where concerns about care are raised. We believe it will help ensure a baby's prognosis or expected chance of survival can't be used to deny families answers or accountability.
records.further_details: We are concerned that families can face significant barriers to accountability when a baby dies following neonatal care, particularly where survival was uncertain. We think the inability to prove a baby would have survived should never prevent concerns about their care from being fully and independently investigated. In our view our proposed law, Rosie’s Right, would help ensure every family has equal access to an independent investigation, regardless of prognosis, so lessons are learned and future babies are better protected.

records.title: Separate water supply & infrastructure maintenance into separate entities
records.description: We believe the Government should require separate entities for managing the supply of water and maintaining water pipe infrastructure. This could ensure healthy market competition and prevent current providers from using funds earmarked for maintenance being used for other things.
records.further_details: BT Openreach was recently fined and forced to separate into supplier (BT) and infrastructure maintainer (Openreach) for failing to maintain their cables. Gas and electric suppliers and maintenance providers are already split like this. Water should be split along the same lines so that the sole focus of the water network owner is on infrastructure repair and renewal. Unlike other utilities, water is essential for all life, not just for humans, and we believe efficient water management should be the minimum requirement for any government.

records.title: Ban publication of unproven allegations and make news orgs moderate social media
records.description: Ban the press from publishing unproven allegations about victims and their families and require news organisations to disable or actively moderate comments on social-media posts about victims, the victim’s children or bereaved families.
records.further_details: We want the law to distinguish between reporting that on the outcome of a court case and on allegations relating to the victim or their family which may be made before that outcome. The former should be permissible and the latter should be prohibited.  We also want stronger protections for victim’s children, victims and bereaved families by requiring news organisations to disable or actively moderate comments on social-media posts about deaths and traumatic cases, preventing hateful abuse and further speculation.

records.title: Require free earplugs at live music and night club venues
records.description: Make night clubs and pubs legally have to give out free ear plugs and advertise this in their venues. This is to help reduce the risks of tinnitus and spread awareness about hearing damage.
records.further_details: According to the Royal National Institute of Deaf People (RNID), 83% of Gen Z adults have reported they have signs of hearing damage such as buzzing, ringing or muffled hearing, after attending night clubs or live events. This petition is to make these venues legally have to give out and advertise free ear plugs, in order to reduce the risk of hearing damage in young people and help spread awareness of the severity of this issue.

records.title: Replace Residential Stamp Duty with a Progressive Annual Property Tax
records.description: Replace residential Stamp Duty with an annual property tax: 0% on the first 250k, then modest rates of 0.10%, 0.20%, 0.30% and 0.40%. Do not tax people because they move house. Tax the underlying value of residential property, collect more tax over time, and improve housing-market mobility.
records.further_details: The proposal would make housing taxation more predictable, reduce financial barriers that leave families in unsuitable homes, encourage job-related relocation and increase properties available for sale. Taxing annually would spread contributions over time, rather than concentrating them at purchase. Regular valuations and calculations would support accuracy. As property values rise and ownership continues, the Government would collect more tax over time than through one-off transaction charges.

records.title: Consider funding and supporting colleges to offer resits in GCSE science
records.description: Colleges may offer GCSE maths and English part-time courses and resits. But adults wishing to enter primary teaching, health, social nursing etc that may need science, may not have passed at GCSE. Some colleges offer GCSE science. Consider funding and supporting more colleges to do so.
records.further_details: We believe more colleges offering GCSE resit science courses for adults would help as being able to travel to a local college will be more convenient rather than travelling further afield. Also, we think having a choice of what science, whether that's biology, chemistry or physics, and resitting it just like maths and English would help more people to get into the job they wish to. Many colleges have labs that could be used for resit courses when not being used for normal courses during the day or in the evening when maths and English lessons are on. Those without labs could explore working with local secondary schools that do to host practicals in the evening, and all the theory work in the college classroom.

records.title: Make alternative provision mandatory to register and independently inspect
records.description: Require all alternative provision settings in England to be registered and independently inspected, with mandatory safeguarding, SEND training and minimum staff competency standards to ensure vulnerable children are safe.
records.further_details:
I want the Government to introduce mandatory registration, regulation and independent inspection for all alternative provision settings in England.

Children who attend alternative provision are often among the most vulnerable children in education, including children with autism, ADHD, SEND, anxiety, trauma and complex needs. Parents should be able to have confidence that these settings are safe, properly monitored and staffed by people with appropriate training and experience.

records.title: Regulate ride-hailing fares for drivers and riders
records.description: We petition Government to regulate ride-hailing fares. Set a fair base fare, transparent per-mile or per-kilometre rates, and clear surge-pricing limits to protect passengers and drivers, promote fair competition, ensure predictable earnings, and provide reasonable, transparent prices.
records.further_details: This petition calls on Government to create clear, fair rules for ride-hailing prices. It asks for a regulated base fare, transparent rates per mile or kilometre, and reasonable limits on surge pricing. These measures would protect passengers from unexpected costs, help drivers receive more predictable and sustainable earnings, promote fair competition between platforms, and ensure that ride-hailing prices are transparent, understandable, and reasonable for everyone.

records.title: Offer UK Armed Forces for the International Stabilisation Force for Gaza
records.description: We ask the Government to offer UK Armed Forces personnel in formed armed units, with support to sustain them, to the Gaza International Stabilisation Force intended to protect Palestinian civilians, and seek an international mandate for a similar civilian-protection force in the occupied West Bank.
records.further_details: UN Resolution 2803 authorised a Gaza force and expressly includes protection of civilians in its mandate, but on 26 August 2026 the UN described its deployment and Israeli withdrawal as requiring implementation.
