On 4 September UN Human Rights said nobody in Gaza was safe and reported continued fatal attacks. Resolution 2803 provides no equivalent West Bank force. The UK should offer a contribution suitable for real civilian-protection duties, not limited to liaison, advisory or planning staff.

records.title: Introduce statutory minimum standards for fair and transparent recruitment
records.description: We want the Government to introduce statutory minimum standards for direct employer recruitment, including requirements for genuine recruitment, accurate material information about vacancies and proportionate accountability for serious or misleading recruitment practices.
records.further_details: Jobseekers can spend significant time completing applications, assessments and interviews. We believe people should be able to expect that advertised opportunities are genuine and material information is accurate. Employers should remain free to choose whom to hire, change legitimate business requirements or withdraw vacancies, but recruitment should meet basic standards of honesty and transparency.

records.title: Change the law so donors cannot withdraw consent after embryos are created
records.description: Change the law so that, once donated sperm or eggs have been used with consent to create embryos for a recipient, the donor cannot later withdraw consent to the use of those existing embryos. Donors should remain free to withdraw consent to any unused gametes.
records.further_details: For same-sex couples, every step towards having a child is intentional: the clinic, treatment and donor. By the time embryos exist, families may have spent months or years trying, endured weeks of injections and invested thousands of pounds. To then have a donor withdraw consent means starting again and watching embryos you have seen develop be destroyed, along with the hope attached to them. We believe that no donor should be able to take that away once embryos have been created with their consent.

records.title: Legalise Marijuana: Socialisation, Research and prevent waste in Cultivation
records.description:
To allow a revolutional process in the legalisation of Marijuana. Have clear narratives with Medicinal and Recreational Marijuana. Opening Medicinal and Recreational social cafes to allow research to reach its full potential. 
Educate/regulate responsible use.
Charity oppertunity to reduce tax.
records.further_details:
To boost Economics.
Break the social stigmatisation of Marijuana smoking.
Create 2 types of cafes: Medicinal and Recreational. 
Allow Hollistic, Sprititual and Cultured areas. 
Bring justice and create a 2 way relationship between ciminality and law.
Consented, anonymous, structured sampling oppertunities to heighten Marijuana research.
Use already cultivated Marijuana to meet the supply and demand of Medicinal and Recreational use in a strategic, healthy, guided way. 
Allow people to smoke sensibly.

records.title: Exempt people detained under Mental Health Act from energy standing charges
records.description: Require energy suppliers to suspend standing charges on unoccupied homes when the occupier is detained under the Mental Health Act 1983, preventing vulnerable people from building up energy debt while they are unable to live at their property.
records.further_details: People detained under the Mental Health Act 1983 may be unable to return home for weeks or months. Although their homes are unoccupied and little or no energy is used, standing charges continue to accumulate. This can leave vulnerable people facing unnecessary debt on discharge. We believe energy suppliers should be required to suspend standing charges during detention, helping to prevent financial hardship and support recovery.

records.title: Appoint a Minister to reduce violence amongst men and boys
records.description: Appoint a Minister for the Reduction of Violence among Men & Boys with the aim of de-normalising violence amongst men & boys. Males suffer c70% of all homicides in the UK. We believe these male victims deserve a voice in the same way as there is a minister to reduce violence against women & girls
records.further_details:
The UK has a Minister for Safeguarding and Violence against Women and Girls, in recognition of the disproportionate impact of sexual violence on females.

However, males actually suffer most from violent crime and suffer 70% of all robberies. The majority of these crimes are committed by males. Male victims deserve a voice, help, support, and a country that will stand up for them, regardless of the fact that they may share the gender of their attacker.

We believe that by denormalising violence against males, females would be less likely to suffer from it too.

records.title: Reintroduce dog licences for dog owners
records.description: Reintroduce mandatory dog licences for all owners. Licence conditions should include mandatory behaviour training. The licence fee could cover the administration costs of the scheme and fund additional resources for dog wardens and dog fouling clean-up.

records.title: Allow clubs and organisations to purchase & hold spare adrenaline auto-injectors
records.description: Extend the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Act to activity clubs and organisations, allowing them to purchase and keep emergency adrenaline auto-injectors (AAIs) on site, with staff training, so children or adults can receive potentially life saving treatment during anaphylaxis emergencies.
records.further_details: Schools can legally purchase and hold space adrenaline auto-injectors (AAIs) without a prescription to use in emergencies. However, this provision does not currently extend to activity clubs or organisations outside of school settings where snack breaks are present. We want to extend the law to these settings, so students can receive emergency treatment when needed.

records.title: Legislate to require MPs who leave their party mid-tenure to face a by-election
records.description: We believe if an MP defects from their party they were originally democratically elected in, they need to face a by election in their constituency to uphold the principles of democracy in the UK.
records.further_details: For example, over the past Parliamentary terms, there have been several defections from one party to another or an MP leaving a party to create their own. We believe that the principles of democracy in the UK mean that the constituents voted for that party through the First-Past-the-Post electoral system, not the individual and if the individual of the party they voted for defects or leaves, it is no longer a democratically elected constituency.

records.title: Require house buyers to be liable for solicitor fees once a mortgage is approved
records.description: I want the government to introduce a new law, mandating that a contract should be introduced once a mortgage has been approved, If after this point a buyer does not proceed with the sale, they should be held liable to pay for all solicitors fee’s in the chain.
records.further_details:
There is no law or repercussions for anyone who can make an offer on your house and can pull out at anytime of the process and then the people selling are left with solicitors fee’s to pay. We think this change will cut out utter time wasters and allow for a quick and easy process.
 
Your mortgage is valid for 6 months and you pay a mortgage fee on top, this law should allow for all processes to be completed within 4 months of getting into contract
If you are happy to accept that suggestion, let me know and I will publish your petition. If you would like something different, let me know and we can discuss the wording.

records.title: End distance learning classification for full time face-to-face weekend students
records.description: We want the Government to amend the weekend delivery policy so that weekend, face to face full time students are not classed as distance learners. We believe weekend attendance should be recognised as full time in person study with equal financial and regulatory treatment.
records.further_details: We believe the current policy is outdated and unjust, penalising mature and working students who study at weekends. We feel it contradicts fairness and widening participation by treating identical in person learning differently based solely on attendance days, creating unnecessary financial and social barriers. Study and work dynamics have changed. People have to balance their studies alongside their work due to the cost of living going high, and previously students did not need to work more hours but now they do.

records.title: Fund MEK inhibitors for NF1
records.description: As a person living with neurofibromatosis, a genetic condition caused by a mutated gene resulting in the growth of plexiform fibromas around the body, I am fighting for the government to grant access to MEK inhibitors, a drug that could greatly reduce pain/immobility caused by inoperable tumours.
records.further_details: MEK inhibitors are cancer targeting drug that block a step in the cell growth pathway. When this pathway is overactive it can result in the rapid growth of tumours, both cancerous and non-cancerous. By interrupting this, the growth of the tumour can be slowed or reduced in size. Access to this drug could change so many lives, especially those living with an NF1 but much like the condition, we believe it is incredibly underfunded essentially putting a price tag on the quality of somebody’s life.

records.title: Financial support for court-ordered drug & alcohol testing in family court cases
records.description:
Government to provide financial assistance for court-ordered drug and alcohol testing in family court cases by:
* Introduce means-tested financial assistance for testing
* Cap the maximum cost of tests
records.further_details: The Government should ensure low-income parents are not excluded from child contact due to inability to pay for tests. We believe this issue affects many families, and in our view no parent should lose contact with their child because they cannot afford the paying for court-ordered alcohol and drug testing as part of the court process.

records.title: Abolish the Multiplication Check due to concerns about children’s mental health
records.description: We think the multiplication check in Year 4 is having a negative impact on children’s already fragile mental health. We feel it serves no purpose for schools and is just another measure used by the government to put schools and children under pressure. It should be abolished.

records.title: Allocate an additional £3b to the Defence Housing Strategy
records.description: I believe that an additional £3 billion investment into the Defence Housing Strategy 2025 would effectively cover the cost of many maintenance issues and tackle problems such as damp, mould and asbestos, vacancy backlog in defence housing, HVAC malfunction, and improper contractor performance.
records.further_details: The government could tackle these issues by allocating £1.05 billion to Contamination issues and using the money to conduct permanent repairs with Amey and VIVO and upgrade insulation. The Vacancy Backlog Issue with £900m could prioritise longest-empty military properties for emergency restoration and modernising amenities. HVAC appliances could be improved with £600m with green energy upgrades, and Contractor Performance with £450m to introduce financial penalties and regular inspections.

records.title: Fund a statutory pay premium for frontline educational & healthcare staff
records.description: We call on the Government to fund a statutory pay premium above the National Living Wage for all frontline educational, childcare and healthcare support workers to reflect their essential role in emotional co-regulation and pastoral care.
records.further_details:
We feel the roles of teaching assistants, early years practitioners, residential care workers, & psychiatric healthcare assistants require intensive emotional labour. However, many of these vital workers are some of the lowest paid professionals in the country. This can lead to widespread burnout, long hours, & recruitment crises.
 
We believe we cannot expect workers to co-regulate & support others when their own financial security & well-being are under threat. The government should value and properly fund this essential workforce.

records.title: Add Yoga and Comparative Spiritual Education to the curriculum
records.description: Introduce yoga and inclusive spiritual education in schools to improve physical and mental wellbeing, teach respect, compassion and self-discipline, and help students learn the shared values of different faiths and beliefs while respecting freedom of religion and choice.
records.further_details:
Children face growing mental health challenges, stress and social division. Introducing yoga and inclusive spiritual education in schools could improve wellbeing, self-discipline, respect and kindness. Lessons could explore the shared ethical values of major faiths and beliefs without promoting any religion.

Alongside academic learning, schools play an important role in building character, respect, responsibility and community spirit. Promoting yoga and comparative spiritual education may help encourage healthier lifestyles, mutual understanding and positive behaviour among young people, contributing to stronger and safer communities

records.title: Remove clause decriminalising abortions from the Crime and Policing Act
records.description: This clause means it would not be a crime for women to perform their own abortions for any reason including sex-selective purposes at any point up to & during birth. We think this will increase infant death, leave women open to harm and coercion & results from a process with no public consultation.
records.further_details: This clause signals a huge change by our legislature and therefore on the country itself, and its success appears bureaucratic rather than democratic. I cannot find an explicit manifesto pledge from any major party to enact such change upon getting into power. No public consultation has taken place on this clause. It was debated for only 46 minutes in the Commons, which in my view, to quote Baroness Monckton does not allow time for "any evidence, scrutiny, public consultation or impact assessment".

records.title: Review law relating to inheritance to protect adult survivors of childhood abuse
records.description: Review laws relating to inheritance to consider what could be done to better protect adult survivors of childhood abuse. Survivors may feel forced to maintain contact with abusive parents to avoid losing an inheritance, which we believe may lead to wealth to be used as coercion.
records.further_details: A review should assess impact on survivors of such abuse, current protections, consult experts and survivors and explore possible reforms to prevent inheritance being used to coerce someone set to inherit. We think possible changes to be considered could include greater court discretion where disinheritance is linked to abuse. In our view survivors should not have to choose between wellbeing and financial security.

records.title: Make dedicated OCD education mandatory in the secondary school curriculum
records.description: All secondary schools to teach about OCD within the PSHE curriculum. It should include avoiding stereotypes and discussing different variants and types of OCD.
records.further_details: OCD is highly misunderstood with the average person making assumptions of it just being neat and tidy. Some even believe false rumours such as people enjoying the Compulsions of OCD, etc.

records.title: Fund free access to public pools for over-65s
records.description: We call on the Government to fund free access for senior citizens over 65 to public pools and baths during off-peak hours.

records.title: Define 'reasonable' in Equality Act adjustments to help end legal disputes
records.description: The Equality Act 2010 requires 'reasonable adjustments' but never defines reasonableness, meaning this must often be proven via costly tribunal or court claims. We ask the Government to publish a presumptive list of default-reasonable adjustments and strengthen enforcement for non-compliance.
records.further_details: Just 0.5% of discrimination cases receive funding for legal representation in court, and the EHRC estimates the average cost of funding an individual case at £28,000. There is no clear picture of how many Equality Act claims are brought in county courts, as those judgments are not published (Women and Equalities Committee, 2019). We ask Government to publish a presumptive list of default-reasonable adjustments, shifting the burden onto providers to justify refusal.

records.title: Income tax to apply only from £50,000pa with a Maximum Income Level of £300,000
records.description: We would like the current tax band system in this country to be replaced by a system where tax is calculated from a starting income of £50,000, rising to a maximum income figure of around £300,000 per annum - any income above this amount being taxed at 100% in order to set a 'maximum income'.
records.further_details: We feel that there have been years of gross inequity in Britain, which have promoted a tax system that seems designed to make the divide between rich and poor increase exponentially.

records.title: Review restrictions on regulated rodeo and western sports in England
records.description: We call on the Government to review restrictions on rodeo and western sports in England and assess whether properly regulated events could be permitted under strict animal-welfare rules, veterinary supervision, independent monitoring and clear penalties for breaches.
records.further_details: Rodeo and western sports are established in countries including France, Belgium, Italy, Germany, Portugal, Brazil and the USA. England has a growing western community but limited opportunities for regulated competition. This petition does not seek to weaken animal welfare laws. It asks the Government to review current restrictions and assess whether suitable events could be licensed under strict welfare rules, veterinary supervision, independent monitoring and penalties for breaches.

records.title: Review use of seat belts on trains & mandate installation and use on new trains
records.description: Mandate the installation and use of passenger seatbelts on all trains and examine the possible benefits of possible installation and use of seatbelts on trains currently in use.
records.further_details: High-speed rail travel involves risks from sudden emergency braking and derailments. Unrestrained passengers can be violently thrown, causing preventable fatalities, severe trauma and injuries – especially to children, the elderly and disabled. Coaches and planes mandate restraints; we believe trains should too. We want the Government to fund a feasibility study into retrofitting fleets and mandate seatbelts on all new trains bringing our transit safety into the 21st century as a matter of urgency.

records.title: Update rules to ban all bulls and cows with calves, in fields with public access
records.description: Update rules on farmland crossed by public rights of way to include a complete year-round ban on farmers placing any bulls, cows with calves, or any other dangerous animal on farmland or in a field where they're not separated from a public footpath. Some bulls are already banned but with exceptions.
records.further_details: We are concerned that lots of people feel unable to walk through a field where there are cows with calves, or a bull grazing. We think that most farmers know this but we are concerned that some may be trying to prevent access across their land.

records.title: Mandate the term "Care Experienced" in all public sector communications
records.description: We call on the government to mandate the term "Care Experienced" across all professional and legal terminology in public sector communications. We feel that "Care Leaver" has a negative connotation to it which for many reinforces the feelings that no one cares.
records.further_details:
We feel the term "care leaver" implies care has left us, creating a cliff-edge where support ends. As recent reports on deaths of those leaving care tragically show, it truly feels like care abandons us. We believe there needs to be a language shift that doesn't apply a negative narrative to the Care Experienced Young Person.

Language shapes reality. Shifting to "Care Experienced" restores dignity, recognises resilience, and tackles the systemic neglect that leaves vulnerable people isolated.”

records.title: Increase long-term funding for mental health services
records.description: We call on the Government to make mental health a national priority by increasing long-term funding for mental health services, including expanding crisis & community support, improving access to assessment and treatment, and increasing investment in early intervention and mental health education.
records.further_details: Mental health services are under huge pressure, while people wait for help, assessment and treatment. In England, the mental health service population grew by around 45.8% from 2016 to 2023–24. In 2024, 6,190 suicides were registered in England and Wales. Wales received 7,538 mental health referrals from April to June 2026. Behind these figures are real people and families.

records.title: Allow courts to waive victim surcharges where no identifiable victim exists
records.description: Make victim surcharges discretionary when an offence causes no direct loss, injury or trauma to an identifiable victim. Victim services need proper funding, but automatically charging people in victimless cases is misleading and unfair. Courts should decide when the surcharge is justified.
records.further_details: The surcharge is calculated from the sentence imposed, not from harm caused to an identifiable victim. This means people can be ordered to pay a “victim surcharge” when nobody suffered direct loss, injury or trauma. Victim services are important, but they should receive secure and transparent public funding. Giving courts discretion to waive or reduce the charge in genuinely victimless cases would make sentencing fairer without withdrawing support from real victims.

records.title: Require an option for whole foods and non processed foods at schools
records.description: Children should be able to have an option for whole and non processed foods as young children and young adults as it is extremely beneficial for brain development and hormones

records.title: Introduce a temporary 10p fuel duty cut when petrol prices exceed £1.65 a litre
records.description: Introduce a temporary 10p-per-litre reduction in fuel duty whenever the average UK petrol price exceeds £1.65 per litre, with the full duty rate restored once prices fall below this level for a sustained period.
records.further_details:
We want the Government to introduce temporary fuel-duty relief when fuel prices are exceptionally high.

When the average UK petrol price exceeds £1.65 per litre, fuel duty should be reduced by 10p per litre. The reduction should remain until average prices stay below £1.65 per litre for four consecutive weeks.

This would give motorists targeted support without permanently reducing fuel-duty revenue.

records.title: Review housing policies & prioritise constructing affordable housing
records.description: We want the Government to prioritise the construction of affordable housing to improve housing affordability. High housing costs, including rent and mortgages, are making it hard for many people and families to secure stable, safe, affordable homes.
records.further_details:
We also call on the Government to launch a review into affordable housing policies, which includes looking into policy options to incentivise the development of diverse housing options at prices accessible to those with moderate and low incomes, and exploring initiatives like rent control, more inclusionary zoning in new housing developments and increasing funding for building more social housing.
 
We believe that access to affordable housing is a fundamental human right, crucial for the wellbeing of our community and that it is time for action to ensure that everyone has a place to call home.

records.title: Fund free tram travel for youth aged 11-18
records.description: We believe the Government should make tram travel entirely free for youth aged 11-18. Many can't work, because they are in full time education or are too young.
records.further_details: We feel that the price of trams today is extortionate and isn't realistic for those who get it everyday to get to and from places of education to afford. It isn't right for students and young people, and their parents, who can't afford continuous tram tickets to have to pay.

records.title: Extend menopause action plan duties to Employers with fewer than 250 Employees
records.description: From April 2026, employers with 250 or more employees are encouraged to publish menopause action plans, becoming mandatory in 2027. We call on the Government to extend this duty to smaller employers, with practical support and guidance so that it is achievable for them.
records.further_details:
Women working for smaller organisations will have no menopause action plan, no published support, leaving a void of structured support to turn to.
Women have left jobs because of a lack of support at work. That loss of skills and experience happens in small businesses too, and small businesses can least afford to lose experienced staff.
We ask that the duty be extended proportionately, with a simple template and guidance so that smaller employers can comply without disproportionate cost.

records.title: Require restaurants to offer calorie-free menus on request
records.description: We want the Government to require food businesses that display calories on menus to also provide, on request, a version without calorie information. This would give customers the choice of whether they wish to see calorie information.
records.further_details: Calorie information can be useful for some people, but for others, particularly those with eating disorders or in recovery, seeing calories displayed on menus can be distressing or triggering. People should still be able to access calorie information if they want it, while those who do not should have the option of a menu without it. Requiring businesses to provide a calorie-free menu on request would preserve access to nutritional information while giving customers greater choice.

records.title: DEFRA to introduce licensing & minimum welfare standards for horse livery yards
records.description: Require DEFRA to introduce mandatory licensing for yards providing livery or horse-care services, under animal welfare law. Minimum standards for horse welfare should include facilities, biosecurity, emergency care, record keeping, insurance and staff competency.
records.further_details: Horse owners place their animals in the care of livery yards and expect appropriate standards of welfare, care and safety. We call on DEFRA to introduce a proportionate licensing system for yards providing livery or horse-care services, minimum standards covering welfare, facilities, biosecurity, emergency procedures, records, insurance and staff competency. Standards should be enforceable and regularly inspected, allowing proportionate arrangements for genuine informal or private agreements.

records.title: Require CCTV coverage around all parks & playgrounds to help protect children
records.description: We believe that tragedies involving children highlight the need for better safety measures. Require CCTV in and around parks, playgrounds and nearby areas. This could help protect children, trace their movements and assist police in emergencies.
records.further_details: Cameras could help protect children, establish their movements if they go missing, provide vital evidence to police and potentially help prevent further tragedies. Children deserve to feel safe in the places where they play.

records.title: Create a regulated UK cannabis market and national cannabis and hemp strategy
records.description: We call on the Government to establish a regulated adult-use cannabis market and a national cannabis and hemp strategy covering licensed production and retail, public-health safeguards, improved medical access, UK cultivation and development of a sustainable industrial hemp sector.
records.further_details: Prohibition has not eliminated cannabis use. We believe regulation could enable age controls, product testing, clear labelling and public-health safeguards while reducing reliance on illicit markets. Medical cannabis has been legal on prescription since 2018, but access remains limited. A national strategy could also support UK cultivation, industrial hemp, research, jobs and rural economies, with tax revenue helping fund health, education, treatment and independent research.

records.title: Move the start of UK British summertime from a Sunday to 1500 on the Monday
records.description: The weekends are short enough as they are without having to deal with an hour stolen from them. We believe a fairer system would be to have the hour brought forward at 1500 on a Monday afternoon, making the first day back at work almost bearable.

records.title: Review the Bank of England's remit to separate supply and demand inflation
records.description: We call on the Government to update the Bank of England's monetary policy remit to require the MPC to distinguish between demand-pull and supply-push inflation, and permit base rate cuts even when headline inflation exceeds target, if the cause is primarily supply-side.
records.further_details: The Bank of England's current remit requires it to target a CPI inflation rate of 2%, with interest rate policy used as the primary tool to achieve this. This framework was designed for an era of predominantly stable, demand-driven inflation. It does not adequately account for inflation driven by supply-side shocks — such as energy price spikes, global supply chain disruption, or geopolitical events — which cannot be meaningfully resolved by raising the cost of borrowing.

records.title: Create independent body for Special Allocation Scheme complaints & safeguarding
records.description: Create an independent body to handle all complaints and safeguarding concerns involving patients on the NHS Special Allocation Scheme.
records.further_details: We believe that having to complain to your SAS service provider in the first instance can create a conflict of interest, delay action, reduce accountability, and can leave patients at risk. We think that independent review would improve safety, fairness, transparency.

records.title: Ban textual based large audience social media platforms
records.description: Textual based social media platforms need to be banned immediately until content regulation is voted in. A digital health and safety board must be setup to pass these apps.
records.further_details:
These platforms allow unlimited followers and following and do not require a verified photo of the user to use the application.
We think that they allow hate speech and defamatory content to spread virally.
They are the free to use platforms. We think they allow the spread of hate speech, and allow the incitement of violence and anti social behaviour, giving victims life long horrific memories.

records.title: Allow social media for under 16s but with a time limit of 2 hours per day.
records.description: I believe that the UK government should enforce a limit on social media instead of a ban, although social media can have an affect on young people's mind, the fact that few abuse the use of social media can ruin it for all.Many young people use social media as a way to connect socially with friends.
records.further_details: Set a limit of 2 hours for each mobile device on all social media platforms.This way young people can still have a social life within the boundaries of the government - allowing them to express themselves whilst being safer and protecting their minds.

records.title: Review options for reform for Northern Ireland's devolved government
records.description: We believe Northern Ireland's devolved government is too divided. It has repeatedly collapsed, delaying decisions on healthcare and public services.  Review whether reforms or even direct rule from Westminster would provide more stable government, while fully respecting the Good Friday Agreement.
records.further_details: Northern Ireland's devolved government has repeatedly collapsed, which has delayed decisions on healthcare, education and other vital services. We believe its politics is too often dominated by constitutional divisions instead of improving people's lives. The UK Government should review whether Stormont needs reform or, if necessary, whether direct rule from Westminster would provide more stable and effective government, while fully respecting the Good Friday Agreement.

records.title: Require businesses to advertise the mandatory arrival time, not their start time
records.description: Introduce legislation that requires all ticketed attractions, events, and experience providers to prominently display the mandatory arrival time at the primary point of sale, rather than disclosing early arrival requirements in post-purchase confirmation emails.
records.further_details:
Currently, many companies advertise tickets for a specific time, only to inform consumers after purchase that they must arrive 30 to 45 minutes prior for check-in or briefings, often under threat of losing their slot without a refund.
 
We believe this practice is misleading and disrupts consumers' ability to accurately plan. We want the government to update consumer protection regulations to ensure that the time displayed before buying is the exact time the consumer is expected to be on the premises.

records.title: Create a Government Credit Card Service
records.description: Government should create a credit service and issue credit cards at reduced rates for UK citizens
records.further_details: Credit Cards charge a high rate of APR on average. Many people clear their card monthly, while others pay high interest payments each month amount to billions. The Government could sell UK Bonds to raise funds to clear existing citizen debt and issue their card at a rate of 12% (or a 1/3 of the current rate). The Bonds should be sold at 4%, making the Government profit, and the remaining money saved would be spent into the economy

records.title: Review and increase post-Brexit funding to regions to replace EU funding
records.description: Commission an independent review comparing EU funding before Brexit to UK regions such as Cornwall, with Government funding since. If the review finds these regions have received less long-term investment, publish the findings and ensure future funding reflects the economic needs of each.
records.further_details: Before Brexit, Cornwall received substantial EU funding to support businesses, skills, infrastructure, regeneration and local communities. Many people believe the replacement funding has not matched the level or long-term certainty previously available. We believe an independent review should compare funding before and after Brexit, publish the findings and ensure that each region receives investment that reflects its economic needs.

records.title: Mandate Bold Labeling for SLS (Sodium Lauryl Sulfate) on Toothpaste Packaging
records.description: Require manufacturers of toothpaste and oral care products to highlight Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (SLS), a common allergen, in bold text in ingredient lists.
records.further_details: For many people, Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (SLS) in toothpaste causes painful allergic reactions, including severe mouth ulcers and gum peeling. Yet it stays hidden in fine print. We want SLS clearly highlighted on toothpaste packaging and printed in bold on the ingredients list. Food labels highlight key irritants—toothpaste should too, preventing accidental, painful exposure.

records.title: Legislate to revoke Parental Responsibility after long absence
records.description: We want the Government to automatically review or revoke Parental Responsibility when a parent has been absent for a specified long-term period. Resident parents should not have to face costly, stressful court battles to make basic decisions for a child left by an absent parent.
records.further_details: Resident parents who raise children without support should not be held back by the legal rights of an absent parent. Right now, a parent with no contact or involvement for years can still block simple, necessary life choices for a child, forcing the primary parent into unnecessary court battles. We believe the law must evolve to protect resident families: if a parent abandons their duties for a specified prolonged period, their legal control over that child should automatically end.

records.title: Restrict low-level helicopter and airship flights over residential zones
records.description: We call on the government and the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) to tighten regulations regarding flight paths, minimum altitudes, and noise limits for helicopters, airships, and all sightseeing flights operating over residential areas in Greater London and across the country
records.further_details:
Residents living in urban residential areas are reporting an increasingly intrusive volume of low-flying aircraft over their homes and gardens. 
We urge the Department for Transport and the CAA to:
1. Increase the statutory minimum altitude for flights over residential areas.
2. Establish restricted flight corridors that redirect low-altitude traffic away from residential neighbourhoods.
3. Introduce enforceable noise limits and stricter penalties for operators who breach altitude guidelines.

records.title: Create UK-Wide Member-Owned Agriculture, Farming & Fisheries Cooperatives
records.description: Work with the devolved administrations to design, legally enable and provide start-up support for three independent UK-wide member-owned cooperatives for Agriculture, Farming and Fisheries, governed on a one-member-one-vote basis and focused on sustainability, welfare and small enterprises.
records.further_details:
Agriculture refers to the strategic, foundational infrastructure required for food production e.g. land access and stewardship, machinery pools, storage and processing facilities, seed and input supply, and shared logistics.
 
Farming refers to the operational production activities carried out by members — crop cultivation, livestock rearing, horticulture, mixed farming, and related on farm work.
 
A Fisheries Cooperative would manage fishing rights, vessels, landing sites, and sustainable stock governance.
 
The cooperatives would support shared machinery, training, purchasing, storage and marketing, while promoting sustainable practices, soil health, biodiversity, wildlife protection, stock preservation, and high standards of welfare.

records.title: Fund a museum dedicated to the Victoria Cross recipients
records.description: Fund a dedicated National Victoria Cross Museum to preserve and share the stories of those awarded Britain’s highest decoration for valour. It would honour their courage and sacrifice, educate future generations and provide these remarkable stories with a permanent national home.
records.further_details: The stories of Victoria Cross recipients are currently spread across regimental museums, memorials, cemeteries, private collections and locations around the world. There is no single dedicated place where we can remember these heroes and learn their stories. A National Victoria Cross Museum would provide a permanent home to commemorate every recipient, bringing their stories together and ensuring their extraordinary courage and sacrifice are preserved for future generations.

records.title: Establish a Chagossian home ownership grant up to £200,000 for eligible families
records.description: Establish a non-repayable Chagossian Home Ownership Grant of up to £200,000 for every eligible Chagossian family with an adult applicant, towards purchasing an adequate permanent family home in the UK, without requiring the family to take on a mortgage or other debt.
records.further_details:
Chagossians were forcibly displaced from their homeland in the Chagos Archipelago in the late 1960s and early 1970s, losing homes, livelihoods and communities. The housing consequences continue across generations.
The Government should provide long-term housing support to help Chagossian families establish secure homes in the UK, recognising multigenerational households including parents and adult children over 18.

records.title: Make it a requirement for all websites to accept the apostrophe in surnames
records.description: This petition calls for websites and online services to be required to accept apostrophes in surnames, ensuring people with names such as O’Rourke can enter their legal surname accurately and consistently across digital services.
records.further_details: This petition calls for websites and online services to be required to accept apostrophes in surnames. Many people have legally recognised surnames containing an apostrophe, yet some websites prevent them from entering their name correctly or remove the apostrophe automatically. This can cause inconsistencies with official documents, identification, banking, travel and other important services. People should be able to use their full legal name accurately and without unnecessary restrictions.

records.title: Make AI education a standalone subject in the national curriculum from KS1
records.description: We want the Government to make artificial intelligence a distinct subject in the national curriculum, taught from KS1, rather than teaching AI primarily through Computing. Children could learn how AI behaves, its capabilities and limitations, and how to think critically about it.
records.further_details: AI is a new technology and we think it must be taught as a standalone subject from KS1. AI agents already perform human jobs and children still need to learn things that AI can do. It can answer questions about identity, feelings and belonging. As a child psychotherapist, I see what children carry and how they can lose a sense of self, connection and trust in their own thinking. Other countries are already teaching AI from early years.

records.title: Allow people aged 14-15 to be able to get a motorcycle permit license
records.description: Allow 14–15-year-olds to obtain a restricted 50cc motorcycle permit after approved training and testing. They must attend their test with a parent/guardian who has held a motorcycle licence for 5+ years. No passengers or night riding; certified gear required, with parent/guardian approval to buy.
records.further_details: This petition asks the Government to introduce a restricted 50cc motorcycle permit for 14–15-year-olds. Applicants would need approved training and testing, with a parent or guardian who has held a motorcycle licence for at least 5 years attending the test and approving the motorcycle purchase. Permit holders would ride without supervision but have no passengers, no night riding, and must wear certified protective gear.

records.title: Launch mandatory, annual civic and media literacy training for UK adults
records.description: We think democratic participation requires citizens to be able to recognise manipulation tactics, not just to vote. The Government should introduce annual civic & media literacy training covering human rights, propaganda recognition, historical anti-democratic tactics & detection of misinformation.
records.further_details: Adults who left education years ago receive no ongoing training in democratic resilience, despite voting and facing exposure to propaganda, disinformation, and manipulation tactics online and offline. We ask the Government to introduce annual training covering rights, propaganda recognition, anti-democratic tactics (taught not partisanly), and misinformation. Sessions should run briefly and regularly, by employers or via online App, with extra sessions before elections.

records.title: Introduce a 50% levy on new fossil fuel revenue for health & social care fund
records.description: Introduce a levy on revenue from future fossil fuel exports to establish a UK social care investment fund (UKSCIF), modelled on the principles of sovereign wealth funds, which directly provides stable, long term funding support for health and social care across the UK.
records.further_details:
The levy should ensure that half of all future UK oil and gas revenues are put into a protected investment fund that will then grow over time. The revenue from the fund, not the savings, should go towards funding high-quality, affordable social and health care for everyone who needs it.
 
This could mean better care for older people and those with disabilities and better funded health care for all, a system that’s fair, sustainable, and in place for future generations, and which ensures investment in the people of our country, rather than just spending whilst in the moment.

records.title: Ban individuals from camping outside of retail stores before special events
records.description: I would like individuals to be banned from camping outside retail stores. This includes camping within store car parks for hours before normal opening times. This could discourage scalpers and huge profit making on reselling platforms.
records.further_details: We feel like this behaviour means others are at a huge disadvantage. Less fortunate households sometimes simply cannot camp outside for special events.

records.title: Allow classic car owners to reclaim registration marks from scrapped vehicles
records.description: Change regulations so the DVLA can reissue and transfer registration marks from scrapped classic cars to running chassis of the same era. This will let automotive enthusiasts legally reclaim and preserve family heritage vehicle identities across the UK.
records.further_details: Once a car is scrapped, the DVLA permanently locks its plate. This stops enthusiasts from preserving family car history. We propose a system where owners pay a £5 online fee to reclaim these frozen marks. Applicants must provide an official change of ownership document or logbook linking to a current or previous address issued within the last 25 years to prevent fraud. This lets the next generation legally rescue family history and protect UK classic car heritage.

records.title: Fund free period products in public spaces
records.description: We believe we must try our best to tackle period poverty and a great approach to this is to fund free period products in public spaces such as libraries and public toilets. Scotland has already implemented this law so why can’t it extend to England?
records.further_details: Women deserve to have a free period. Toilet paper is free to use inside toilets but free period products are too much to ask for? In the UK period products are quite expensive with the average price for a packet of pads ranging from £1.50-£3.50. Period poverty is a very real thing impacting many women across the country.

records.title: Create a legal right & formal process to renounce ILR & Settled Status
records.description: We want Parliament to pass a law which gives ILR / Settled Status holders the legal right to renounce their status.
records.further_details: We believe that ILR / Settled Status holders should have the legal right to decide whether they want to keep or renounce their ILR / Settled Status and to create a formal process for renunciation.

records.title: Set out that UK entry for & diplomatic ties to any who use nuclear arms be ended
records.description: Set out that any leader and their government who deploys a nuclear weapon as an offensive measure or disproportionate response - anything other than retaliation under the principle of mutually assured destruction - should be refused UK entry, and diplomatic ties with them be severed. Retroactively.
records.further_details: Being the user or target of nuclear weapons represents a critically low point in our development as an (ostensibly) intelligent and ethical species. No matter where someone lives, they would be our neighbour if that bomb dropped on them; we would feel the moral/spiritual and scientific consequences. I believe anybody with that power and who acts recklessly with it, should not step foot on British soil or treat with us in a diplomatic capacity.

records.title: Review and clarify guidance on 3-year residency and 5-year ILR rules for spouses
records.description: Review and clarify the guidance on the relationship between ILR and naturalisation for spouses of British citizens, making more explicit the distinct requirements for a 3-year residency period and 5-year ILR qualifying period so it clearly reflects the citizenship route for many spouse visa holders.
records.further_details: Most spouse visa holders need around five years before they can obtain ILR. However, official guidance for citizenship refers to a three-year residence requirement for spouses of British citizens while also requiring ILR or settled status. We are concerned this can cause confusion because, in practice, most applicants cannot benefit from the three-year rule until they first complete the five-year settlement route. The guidance should clearly explain that, for most spouse visa holders, eligibility for naturalisation normally follows completion of the five-year route to ILR, despite the separate three-year residence requirement.

records.title: Require schools to teach about the Roma Community
records.description: We ask the Government to require schools to teach about the Roma Community. Many in the Roma Community have experienced a lot, yet there are some who do not know who they are and mistake them for other communities. This proposal could stop racism that Roma pupils experience in school.
records.further_details: If we specifically teach pupils about the Roma Community, Roma children may not feel left out or receive racial abuse. We are taught in school to respect all races, and we therefore believe that schools should teach about the Roma Community including what they have experienced and how they were impacted by Nazism in World War II, as well as what members of the Roma Community experience during their day-to-day lives.

records.title: Equalise visa, settlement & benefit access rules for EU & non-EU nationals
records.description: We believe non-EU nationals and EU nationals in the UK under the EU Settlement Scheme should be governed under the same immigration, visa, settlement, benefits and social housing rules and requirements.
records.further_details:
This could create a fairer and more transparent system post-Brexit, reduce differences in the current system, and may help reduce pressure on public services and public finances. It could also reduce the number of dependants coming to the UK after being sponsored by EU nationals with EU Settled Status.
 
We ask the UK Government to reform the current legal arrangements so that non-EU nationals and EU nationals residing in the UK under the EU Settlement Scheme are governed by the same rules and requirements.

records.title: Exempt homeowners from disclosing neighbour disputes when selling homes
records.description: Amend Consumer Protection regulations to exempt homeowners who are victims of criminal or persistent anti-social behaviour (ASB) from being legally required to disclose their neighbour’s behaviour & neighbour-related disputes when selling their home.
records.further_details:
Homeowners should not be required to disclose this information on TA6 Property Information Forms.
 
Home sellers are currently required to declare neighbour disputes. We feel this unfairly punishes innocent victims of ASB, as it can trap homeowners facing noise, drug activity, or intimidation. This may force them to either stay in an unsafe area or slash their property price due to forced disclosure. Perpetrators face no financial penalty, while victims suffer financial loss. The government should create an "Innocent Seller" exemption. ASB should be treated as an external crime matter, not a defect of the property asset.

records.title: Fund a free-to-use AI powered satellite crop & soil intelligence for farmers
records.description: We want the Government to establish a free-to-use Crop & Soil Intelligence Service, using satellite data and AI to give every farmer and grower clear, field level info on nutrients, soil health, water stress and crop risks.
records.further_details: This would be a public digital information service for agriculture, analogous to weather forecasts and weather broadcasts to the shipping and fishing industries. Individually, this would provide farmers with actionable information to help improve yields and crop quality, whilst reducing costs by better targeting interventions. Collectively, it would be in the national interest to improve food security, nature recovery (esp. soil condition), and to understand and mitigate the impact of weather changes.

records.title: Require security employers to provide seating at fixed security stations
records.description: Require all retail stores employing security guards to provide a suitable chair or seating at fixed security/CCTV stations, where duties can safely be performed while seated. Allow guards to alternate between sitting and standing to reduce the health risks associated with prolonged standing.
records.further_details: Security guards in retail stores can be required to stand for many hours, even when stationed at a fixed podium or CCTV desk where their duties can be safely performed while seated. Prolonged standing can cause fatigue, discomfort and musculoskeletal problems. This petition calls for retail stores to provide suitable seating and allow security guards to alternate between sitting and standing when operationally safe, without compromising security.

records.title: Streamline driving theory test syllabus and reduce retake fees
records.description: Cut the question count, drop non-essential numeric trivia, reduce retake fees, and update the syllabus to focus on practical safety instead of academic memorisation.
records.further_details: We believe that theory pass rates sit below 45% because the exam tests trivia over real safety. Safe drivers regularly fail it, which we think proves it measures memory over skill. 50 text-heavy questions can cause severe fatigue, penalising neurodivergent learners (ADHD, dyslexia). At £23 per attempt, repeated failures accumulate into hundreds of pounds in wasted fees. In rural areas with poor public transport, this financial and cognitive barrier restricts young people from getting the licence they need to work.

records.title: Expel all US military personnel from UK bases & request for the UK to join BRICS
records.description: We call on the UK Government to expel all US military personnel from all military bases in the UK and submit a formal application requesting that the UK join BRICS – an intergovernmental organisation containing Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa.
records.further_details:
BRICS countries make up around 55% of the global population, over 40% of the World’s GDP, and possess abundant natural resources, making them one of the main driving forces of global economic development.
 
We believe that the UK has been in the economic grip of the United States of America for too long.

records.title: Start funded childcare when an eligible child turns 9 months old
records.description: We want the Government to change the Free Childcare for Working Parents scheme in England so that eligible children can access their funded hours from the date they turn nine months old, rather than having to wait until the next termly funding period.
records.further_details: Termly cut-offs create an arbitrary childcare funding cliff edge. A child who turns 9 months on 31st March can receive 30 funded hours a week from 1st April, while a child turning 9 months one day later must wait until September. At £60 per 10-hour day, this can leave a family paying about £2,340 for the same childcare over an estimated 13-week summer term. Two children one day apart can therefore receive the same support almost five months apart.

records.title: Introduce mandatory multi-agency infant checks and increase abuse sentences
records.description: Mandate multi-agency safeguarding checks during pregnancy and up to age four, and introduce mandatory Whole Life Orders for child homicide and severe abuse of infants under five.
records.further_details: Abusers (including parents) can conceal warning signs in children being abused, and in our view, agencies frequently miss critical risks due to poor communication. We call on the Government to introduce statutory multi-agency screening across police, NHS, and social care during pregnancy for domestic abuse and drug misuse, followed by mandatory in-person health checks until a child turns four. We also think sentencing of child abuse and homicide must be overhauled: anyone convicted of severe abuse, fatal neglect, or murder of a child under five must face mandatory whole-life sentences.

records.title: Mandate 2:1 female-to-male ratio for public toilets and require unisex provision
records.description: We call on the Government to legislate for “potty parity” by requiring public toilet providers to ensure a 2:1 ratio of female to male toilets when building public toilets. We also call for a requirement to provide unisex toilets in order to take into account the needs of transgender individuals.
records.further_details:
We believe this is necessary to ensure the fair provision of toilets in all areas. The Royal Society for Public Health’s report, “Taking the P***: Decline of the Great British Public Toilet” from 2019 says equality of access to toilets is an important factor, particularly for women. We believe a fair toilet ratio would be at least 2:1 in favour of women. The British has historically relied on a 1:1 building standard.
Calls to address the unfairness have led to ‘potty parity’ legislation in parts of the US and Canada. 
 
We also call on the Government to require public toilet providers to provide unisex toilets in order to take into account the needs of transgender individuals.

records.title: Create a public awareness campaign about fibromyalgia
records.description: The Government should develop and fund a national fibromyalgia awareness campaign, providing accurate information about fibromyalgia, its symptoms and its impact on daily life, and promote this information across NHS services, schools, workplaces and public services.

records.title: Fund & mandate the installation of defibrillators in every household
records.description: We call on the Government to fund and mandate the installation of defibrillators in every household across the country. Every year, people lose loved ones from cardiac-related attacks.
records.further_details: To prevent them from going through the same horror, we call for the defibrillators in every household to save people’s lives.

records.title: Review Public Transport Equivalent Costs in Disabled Students' Allowance
records.description: We urge the Government to review the regulations and establish a system that reflects the real costs faced by students today so that disabled students are not financially disadvantaged when accessing education due to inaccurate transport cost calculations.
records.further_details: We call on the Government to reform how the Student Loans Company calculates Public Transport Equivalent Costs (PTEC) for Disabled Students' Allowance. We feel current calculations often ignore real-world situations, forcing disabled students to pay more than their non-disabled peers to access education. We think the rules should be reviewed so PTEC reflects actual travel costs and does not create a financial penalty for disability.

records.title: Require foreign travel agencies to pay a visitor’s levy to all local authorities
records.description: We call on the UK Government to require agencies that arrange holiday lets based overseas to pay a visitor's levy directly out of their profits made in our country to all local authorities, in order to enhance the areas their clients visit.
records.further_details: Currently, many of these companies pass charges onto the client (either host or visitor), at a time of rising travel costs. To make these companies more responsible, we ask that they pay out of the profit they make here to help keep areas better for visitors and locals alike.

records.title: Allow time on Skilled Worker Visas and Family Visas to be combined toward ILR
records.description: Individuals who work and contribute to the UK on a Skilled Worker Visa and subsequently marry a British Citizen before moving to a Family Visa should be eligible to combine the time spent on these two visas together when counting ‘time’ toward ILR.
records.further_details: In our view individuals travel to the UK with the view of joining the community and integrating into the British way of life, whilst working and paying for a Skilled Worker Visa. In the circumstances where a person then marries a British Citizen and moves to a Family visa, we think these two visas should count together toward Indefinite Leave to Remain. We think spouses of British Citizens should be granted additional rights, like using time spent on previous visas to count towards ILR.

records.title: Formally join & intervene as a party in the DRC’s ICJ case against Rwanda
records.description: The DRC has sought justice through legal means. We believe if the UK stands for human rights, it cannot remain silent, and that history will remember who stood with the victims and who turned away. We urge the UK Government to join the DRC’s ICJ case as a party to obtain justice and defend lives.
records.further_details:
For thirty years, we believe a silent catastrophe has unfolded on Congolese soil. It is estimated that nearly 6 million men, women and children have been killed in wars and conflicts in the DRC since 1996. Survivors have faced face mass rape, ethnic cleansing, child abduction, and the theft of their land and wealth. We believe these acts meet the legal definition of genocide and crimes against humanity.
 
On 26 June 2026, the DRC turned to the International Court of Justice to file a case against Rwanda for its role in this tragedy. We believe this is not a political dispute, but a plea for justice after decades of suffering.

records.title: Stop Requiring NI Contributions and Pay The Full State Pension to All.
records.description: We call on government to stop requiring NI contributions in order to pay state pensions. We feel this is a degrading humiliating practice. We suggest the Full State Pension is paid to all of pension age. We believe that for too long, our elderly have been portrayed by media as 'burdens on state'.
records.further_details: We think all of the elderly should be entitled to a decent pension, comfortable lifestyle, as most will have already paid into the system for longer than anyone else. We believe any Government should have a responsibility toward our nation's elderly people. In the Victorian era, retirement was often only an option for the wealthy. Are we regressing back to those Dickensian times? We believe any need for previous NI contributions seems deliberately demeaning and intrusive.

records.title: Require minimum heat safety and ventilation standards in live music venues
records.description: Introduce minimum ventilation and heat safety standards for indoor live music venues to protect audiences, performers, staff and photographers during extreme heat. Provide grants to help smaller independent venues improve ventilation and cooling where needed.
records.further_details: Overcrowded venues can become dangerously hot, increasing the risk of dehydration, heat exhaustion and medical emergencies. Better ventilation and cooling would make live events safer without placing an unfair financial burden on independent venues. As a live music photographer, I recently worked at a sold-out indoor gig where the heat became overwhelming. Audience members, staff and the band all commented on how extreme the conditions were.

records.title: Mandate the teaching of Anglo-Indian history in the curriculum
records.description: We believe Anglo-Indians, the mixed-race community formed as a result of the British Raj, have made a monumental contribution to the UK. Yet, we feel they are almost invisible today. We are calling for the Government to make it compulsory for schools to teach about Anglo-Indian history.
records.further_details:
Anglo-Indians are the mixed-race community formed during the British Raj and earlier. Tens of thousands of Anglo-Indians arrived in the UK after 1947. Many of the women becoming nurses around the inception of the NHS.
 
Yet for many, all they met in the UK was racism and prejudice which lead many, including my Grandad, to hide their heritage. We feel they are almost invisible today. We believe Anglo-Indians should be recognised as an important part of the UK's post-war Asian migration and their history should be taught.

records.title: Mandate candidates in elections to attend the returning officer's announcement
records.description: Candidates for elections to Parliament should attend the Returning Officer's declaration of the result or forfeit their right to represent the seat.
records.further_details: People who wish to represent a constituency in Parliament should account for themselves and be present at the Returning Officer's announcement of the result of an election. We believe it's a basic courtesy to voters and fellow candidates.

records.title: Amend the Firearms Act 1968 to allow security training for PAVA/Pepper Spray
records.description: Amend the Firearms Act 1968 to allow appropriately licensed, vetted and trained security professionals to carry approved PAVA or incapacitant spray while on duty, subject to strict training, competency, accountability and lawful-use requirements.
records.further_details: Security professionals regularly work face-to-face with the public at events, venues, buildings and other busy locations, where they can face aggression or violence. Verbal de-escalation should always be the first approach, but words are not always enough. We believe properly trained and licensed security professionals should have access to PAVA as a regulated defensive option, subject to strict training, vetting, medical guidance, accountability and lawful-use requirements.

records.title: Require disputed court orders to be checked against the hearing recording.
records.description: Written court orders can sometimes differ from what the judge said in court. People can be arrested and prosecuted on the written version. HMCTS keeps audio recordings of hearings. We want a right to have a disputed order verified against the recording before it is enforced.
records.further_details: Breaching some court orders, including non-molestation orders, is a criminal offence carrying up to 5 years’ imprisonment. Yet where the accuracy of an order is disputed, we are concerned there is no clear procedure requiring it to be checked against the official hearing recording. We ask the Government to introduce prompt, free verification, pause enforcement where material discrepancies arise, require notice and reasons for substantive amendments, and strengthen accountability for inaccurate court records.

records.title: Legalise riding gas-powered bicycles & pit bikes under 100cc on public roads
records.description: Fully legalise the right to ride gas-powered bicycles and pit bikes under 100cc on public roads and paths. We feel current laws demand costly motorcycle licenses, tax, and insurance—impeding cheap travel.
records.further_details:
We want the Government to stop punishing low-income commuters and young people, and to give us affordable transport! We feel travel costs are too high. E-bikes provide free travel but can cost thousands to buy. Gas-powered bicycles and pit bikes under 100cc can cost a fraction of the price and match e-bike top speeds, yet current legislation restricts their use.

Legalising the use of gas-powered bicycles and pit bikes could create transport equality for low-income workers and youth, and unlock affordable, independent travel!

records.title: Increase UK support for climate adaptation to disaster vulnerable  country Nepal
records.description:
Increase UK funding for climate adaptation, disaster resilience, infrastructure, essential services and emergency response.
Invest in early warning systems,glacier,river monitoring, data sharing, community alerts, evacuation plans and training.
Ensure Nepal does not take on more debt.
records.further_details:
Nepal contributes only around 0.05% of today's global CO₂ emissions and just 0.01% of historical cumulative CO₂ emissions,yet suffers such catastrophic climate change consequences.What Nepal needs from UK are 
1.	Increase and protect UK funding for climate adaptation and disaster resilience for NEPAL.
2.	Expand investment in early warning systems
3.	Ensure climate-vulnerable countries can access timely and adequate adaptation.

records.title: Seek a reciprocal deal with India to extend GHIC coverage to Indian healthcare
records.description: We ask the UK Government to negotiate and seek a reciprocal healthcare agreement with the Indian Government that extends GHIC coverage to India and allows UK nationals to use their GHIC to access state-provided healthcare in India.
records.further_details:
Many UK residents travel to India to visit family, for tourism, work and other purposes. Unexpected illness or injury can result in significant medical costs. 
 
A reciprocal agreement could give UK nationals access to medically necessary state healthcare in India on agreed terms, while offering corresponding arrangements for Indian nationals in the UK. We ask the UK Government to begin negotiations with the Government of India, look into the feasibility, costs and benefits, and publish the final draft of the agreement.

records.title: Require level 4 teaching diploma & DBS checks for all music instrument teachers
records.description: Reform the Music Education Framework to protect children and vulnerable adults from this existing unregulated sector of education by requiring every music instrument teacher to be qualified in teaching to a minimum level 4 diploma and have a DBS check.
records.further_details: We believe requiring an Ofqual Level 4 diploma as the benchmark for instrumental music teaching professionalises the sector by embedding evidence-based pedagogy, technical rigor, and standard accountability. Crucially, coupling this with mandatory safeguarding training helps protect children and vulnerable adults within vulnerable 1-to-1 learning environments. Tutors learn to enforce professional boundaries, and prevent physical or auditory injuries. Mandatory standards can elevate teaching quality.

records.title: Legislate for a "50+1" football club ownership model to protect clubs and fans
records.description: Legislate a mandatory "50+1" rule in professional football, requiring fans to hold 50% plus one share of club voting rights. This could give fans a democratic veto, stop reckless financial management, and ensure ticket prices remain affordable.
records.further_details:
We believe reckless ownership threatens clubs. A German-style 50+1 model puts fans in the boardroom. A fan voting majority could help:
 
- Stop financial ruin
- Prioritise long-term survival over high-risk debt
- Lower ticket prices.
 
Fans could cap matchday & season ticket costs. Clubs are vital community assets. We believe we need a true fan democracy.

records.title: When parents are separated, Child Benefit to be awarded to the non-HICBC parent
records.description: Change the Child Benefit rules so that, where separated parents have competing/rival claims and one parent is liable to repay Child Benefit through the High Income Child Benefit Charge (HICBC), the award is given to the other parent who is not liable for HICBC.
records.further_details: Under current rules, where separated parents have equal care of a child, Child Benefit (CB) may be awarded to a parent who is liable to repay it through the High Income Child Benefit Charge (HICBC). The rules should require HMRC to consider whether the parent claiming CB is liable for HICBC. If they are, and the other parent is not, CB should be awarded to the parent who is not liable for HICBC. We believe this would ensure the benefit is retained for the benefit of the child and not repaid in tax.

records.title: Statutory code of practice for police when issuing Community Protection Notices
records.description: Introduce a statutory Code of Practice which outlines specific evidential and procedural safeguards that all police forces must follow when issuing Community Protection Warnings (CPWs) and Community Protection Notices (CPNs) and investigating CPN and CPW breaches.
records.further_details:
Breaching a CPN is a criminal offence, yet we feel safeguards are limited. The safeguards should include requiring the police to record all evidence that ensures any statutory tests are met, consider evidence for and against allegations, give the accused a right to respond, and consider whether people issued CPNs and CPWs may be a victim of harassment or malicious reporting.
 
We believe alleged breaches should be properly investigated and that a right of appeal is no substitute for fairness before a CPN is imposed. A statutory Code could ensure national consistency, transparency and accountability.

records.title: Raise tax threshold for the public sector to £17,500 basic & £62,000 higher rate
records.description: We call on the UK Government to implement structural tax reforms for public sector workers by raising the basic rate threshold to £17,500, expanding the higher rate threshold to £62,000, and establishing a flat 15% Income Tax and 5% National Insurance cap on all overtime hours.
records.further_details: Public sector employees—including NHS staff, teachers, police & Fire officers, prison staff, and civil servants are public servants who dedicate our lives to service, frequently working under immense pressure in some of the most testing and challenging environments. Despite this unwavering dedication, the current UK Income Tax Framework seems to rely on a prolonged freeze of allowances. We believe this has triggered severe fiscal drag, pulling dedicated workers into higher tax bands due to nominal inflation.

records.title: Make bullying in the workplace a criminal offence
records.description: Make it a crime for employees to bully other colleagues. We feel this is commonplace and some good co-workers end up leaving because of bullying. Making workplace bullying an offence could act as a deterrent and support mental health at work. This could also support a rise in employment.

records.title: Fund access to the state pension for people who are terminally ill
records.description: We want the government to allow any person who has been diagnosed with a terminal illness immediate access to the state pension.

records.title: Fund expanded access to bleed kits in public venues & outdoor spaces
records.description: We call for the Government to fund the placement of bleed kits in public venues and outside spaces, including outside of shops, to ensure they are easily accessible if someone is injured.
records.further_details: This could result in less people being killed due to excessive blood loss.

records.title: Launch a youth equine voucher scheme and support self-fund community stables
records.description: Government to support to lower horse care costs for working-class families by cutting horse feed/bedding VAT to 10%, fund livery vouchers and subsidise equine insurance. We think the Government should make vacant public land available to build community stables funded by shows/charity betting.
records.further_details: We demand the Government fund local pilot stables on vacant public land. To keep costs low, we suggest that builders could construct safe outer structures, while volunteers could build their internal stalls. Paid staff could be school-leavers earning legal minimum wage, alongside free rehabilitation/Community Payback volunteers. We believe this could ensure a safe, self-funded community network with minimal cost to the British taxpayer.

records.title: Fund clinical research into wellness and longevity peptides
records.description: We urge the UK Government to fund clinical research into wellness and longevity peptides. Increased funding could support proactive preventative health, improve public safety by curbing unregulated markets, and help reduce the long-term burden on the NHS.
records.further_details: While funding seems to be focused on treating late-stage diseases, we think that proactive biological optimization is largely ignored. Formal government grants could allow independent institutions to map out long-term biological outcomes, establish standardized dosing parameters, and protect citizens through evidence-based guidelines rather than internet speculation.

records.title: Make care experience a protected characteristic under the Equality Act 2010
records.description: Make care experience a protected characteristic under the Equality Act 2010 to protect care-experienced people from discrimination and ensure they have equal rights, opportunities, and recognition across society.
records.further_details: Care-experienced people can face lifelong barriers in education, employment, housing and services. Care experience is not currently protected under the Equality Act 2010. Recognising it as a protected characteristic would protect people from discrimination, improve equality, and ensure care-experienced people have the same opportunities as everyone else.

records.title: Require local authorities to prioritise HMO demand in new developments
records.description: I ask the Government to consider changing planning policy so that demand for Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) is met through new developments rather than converting existing family homes. Where there is a demonstrated local need, planning authorities could work with developers
records.further_details: With more homes required HMOs can play a role in this but should not significantly affect established residential communities where family houses are increasingly converted into HMOs. This can cause pressure on parking, waste management, noise, crime, drug misuse, and effect local infrastructure and community stability. We believe a better approach would be new housing developments providing purpose-built HMO or shared-living rather than allowing established family neighbourhoods to become affected by this.

records.title: Calculation of child maintenance payments to exclude overtime and extra earnings
records.description: Change the child maintenance calculation rules so payments are based on regular net income and do not include overtime, bonuses or other irregular additional earnings.
records.further_details: We want child maintenance to be calculated using the paying parent's regular net income only.
