Overtime, bonuses and other irregular additional earnings should be excluded from the calculation.  Additional earnings are often voluntary and unpredictable and should not be treated as regular income when determining a fixed child maintenance payment. We believe this would create a fairer and more predictable system while ensuring children continue to receive reliable financial support.

records.title: Require an evidence-based review of health programmes before public broadcast
records.description: We want the Government to amend media law so that factual TV and on-demand programmes, that make significant health or medical claims, undergo documented review by suitably qualified, independent experts before they are released to the public.
records.further_details: Ofcom doesn't approve shows before broadcast and the rules do not require independent review before release. We want prevention and post-release enforcement to improve public information. Misleading health claims can affect stigma, help-seeking and treatment decisions.

records.title: Lower the legal age for getting a tattoo to 16
records.description: We believe that, as the Government considers 16 to be mature enough an age at which to vote, a person of that age should also be able to get a tattoo as it shows no direct harm. For people aged between 16 & 18 years they must however have parental consent.

records.title: Mandate guidance on prioritising search areas with water for missing children
records.description: Mandate guidance on prioritising search areas with water for missing children. Water can pose a particular risk for autistic children. According to the National Autism Association, accidental drowning accounts for roughly 71% of all lethal wandering incidents among individuals with autism.
records.further_details:
We believe the risk is too high to not do something about this. 

Drowning is the number one cause of injury-related death for autistic children in the US. We believe the risk is too high to not do something about this. 
Why the Risk is so High
Drawn to Water: Autistic children often find water soothing or fascinating, leading them to seek it out without realizing the danger.
Lack of Awareness: Many children lack the skills to recognize hazards, swim safely, or understand deep water.
Elopement Triggers: Sensory overload, anxiety, or curiosity can cause a child to bolt suddenly from safe areas.
 
Some families have lost their children as the risk is so high around water. This needs to be recognised in guidance.

records.title: Fund & implement risk assessment systems in schools for vulnerable youth
records.description: We believe all schools should have mandatory risk assessments to identify children who are at risk of gang recruitment. These could be targeted at students aged 9-16.
records.further_details: In the past year, a survey estimated that around 90,000 young people aged 13 to 17 in England and Wales had been involved in a gang. Home Office estimates also suggest that around 15,500 children were identified as at risk of or involved in child criminal exploitation in the year ending March 2025. As a result, we believe the government should employ risk assessment systems in all schools to prevent the exploitation of young vulnerable children by gang activity.

records.title: Equality in Employment Law for Employees Undergoing Fertility Treatment
records.description: Individuals and couples undergoing fertility treatment should receive the same employment protections as pregnant employees. Equal protections would help prevent discrimination and support those building a family.
records.further_details: Individuals and couples undergoing fertility treatment should receive the same employment protections as pregnant employees. Fertility treatment can involve medical procedures, appointments, and significant physical and emotional challenges. Like pregnant employees, those undergoing treatment should be protected from discrimination, allowed paid time off for medical appointments, and have access to reasonable workplace adjustments to support their family-building journey.

records.title: Legalise right to work & pay taxes for asylum seekers during asylum process
records.description: We call on the Government to legalise the right for asylum seekers to work and pay tax whilst they’re awaiting a decision on their asylum application. Many asylum seekers come to the UK as they believe life is in better in a democracy; they may wait up to 5 years for a decision and cannot work.
records.further_details:
Many are already able and willing to work, so we call on the Government to legalise their right to work and pay taxes in the UK. We have met many asylum seekers who are desperate to work and make their own money, instead of sitting around all day and doing nothing.
 
Many are prepared to do low-paid jobs which are difficult to fill, such as working in agriculture and the hospitality sector. By allowing them to work, the financial burden as a result of providing asylum seekers with state benefits to survive could be reduced.

records.title: Increase the maximum cc for motorbike use by a 16 year old to 125cc
records.description: We believe the law about 16 year olds only being allowed to ride a 50cc motorcycle has to be changed. We are concerned being restricted to a 50cc means these riders can hold up traffic on national speed limit roads which can be dangerous and terrifying when being overtaken at speed.
records.further_details: Allow 16 year olds to ride a 125cc motorbike. This will allow 16 year old riders to keep up with the flow of traffic instead of holding everyone up. They are just trying to get to work or college

records.title: Allow all medium-skilled Health & Care Worker visa holders to bring dependents
records.description: Allow all medium-skilled NHS workers to bring their families to the UK. Let's remove this barrier and allow healthcare workers to perform to their fullest potential while enjoying the support of their families.
records.further_details: For three years, I dedicated my life to the NHS, contributing to the wellbeing of countless families across the UK. When I was granted sponsorship, I was filled with hope for a new chapter in my career, but this opportunity came with an unexpected and painful sacrifice—my family's presence. Like many Healthcare Assistants nurses, and auxiliary workers, I am not permitted to have my dependents join me here in the UK. This restriction has profoundly affected both my professional and personal life.

records.title: Recognise Electric Vehicles with 'Camp Mode' as leisure accommodation
records.description: Update the 1960 Caravan Sites Act to let EV drivers sleep in cars with "Camp Mode." Current site licensing bans this due to outdated rules on engines. EVs run silently with zero emissions. We want councils to grant an EV exemption so we can use green tech for sustainable UK eco-tourism.
records.further_details: Current legislation prevents zero-emission electric vehicles (EVs) with dedicated "Camp Mode" software from being legally recognised as overnight leisure accommodation. Update the legal definitions within the Caravan Sites Act 1960 to officially recognise stationary, zero-emission vehicles with active climate-control software as permitted overnight.

records.title: Introduce nationally recognised Funeral Cortege identification sign for vehicles
records.description: We want the government to introduce a nationally recognised, removable vehicle identification sign for funeral corteges, which may be displayed on a max of 3 immediate-family vehicles travelling directly behind the funeral vehicles.
records.further_details: The purpose would be to clearly identify these vehicles as part of the funeral cortege, so that other road users can recognise the procession and, where it is safe and lawful/legal to do so, avoid unnecessarily separating the immediate family from the funeral vehicles during the final journey of their loved one.

records.title: Require cameras in vehicles used to transport children with EHCPs
records.description: Require cameras in vehicles used to transport children with Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs). Children with EHCPs are some of the most vulnerable children in society and deserve the necessary and adequate protections to transport them to and from school on a daily basis.
records.further_details:
This could enhance children's welfare and offer an extra layer of protection for safeguarding children.
 
We have cameras on trains, trams, buses and at bus stations, train stations and tram stations. Yet, we have not caught up with adding cameras to transport vehicles both private and council-led for the most vulnerable children in society.

records.title: Upgrade to 100/125cc the type of motorbike pre-Feb 2001 full car drivers can use
records.description: I would like the Government to change the law that allows people who passed the full car license before 1 February 2001 to ride a moped up to 50cc without a CBT or learner plates. I believe this law is a waste of time & still very dangerous on today's roads & should be increased to at least 100cc.
records.further_details: This petition is seeking to allow people of my age and older who have ridden bikes up to 125cc many years ago to ride such bikes without a CBT or leaner lates. We want the law to increase it to at least a 100 or 125cc, as we believe this would make the roads safer. On 50cc bikes you can inadvertently create a rolling road block at 28mph, which can be dangerous if you ride on a dual carriageway, or a dangerous road.

records.title: Do not ban social media for Year 11 students
records.description: Due to exam season being in May/June, many Year 11s do not turn 16 until during or after this. Some social media apps can help students with revision. We feel this is important because some students require different ways to revise.

records.title: Keep the 5p fuel duty cut for another year and reduce amount for small firms
records.description: Keep the 5p fuel cut after December 2026 and do not put fuel duty up. The Government should also cut fuel duty now for small firms that rely on vans and lorries.
records.further_details: We are concerned that small firms with vans and lorries are struggling. We believe when fuel goes up, only two people pay: the business owner or the customer. Either we earn less, or you pay more to move home, get a delivery or shop locally. Lorries got a road tax break in May. Vans got nothing. Fuel duty is 52.95p a litre, with VAT on top, in all four nations. The 5p cut ends in December and rises could start in January. Many small firms are close to closing. We need help now.

records.title: Urgent review of the Disability Living Allowance (DLA) appeals system
records.description: We want an urgent review into what we believe is the administrative collapse of the Disability Living Allowance (DLA) appeals system. We are specifically concerned about the time taken for the Department for Work and Pensions to provide response bundles required by the Courts service to hear cases.
records.further_details: We believe the DLA appeals system has collapsed into severe judicial gridlock, denying access to justice for vulnerable children. Backlogs of DWP appeal cases have accelerated to 129,000, with DLA appeals surging by 187% and forcing families to wait an average of 37 weeks. We feel this is a breach of our human rights.

records.title: Legalise pavement cycling where roads are unsafe
records.description: On roads where the conditions present a considerable danger, we think cyclists should be allowed to use public pavements, especially on those with higher speed limits, sharp bends, or heavy traffic; this could offer a safer option even though cyclists would have to give way to pedestrians.
records.further_details: Cyclists are currently obliged to use roads that can pose considerable danger from motor vehicles. We believe the law should allow them to use suitable pavements where this offers a safer alternative, provided they travel slowly, give pedestrians priority, give sufficient warning when approaching from behind, and slow down or stop when necessary. This could protect cyclists without undermining pedestrians’ right to use pavements.

records.title: Mandate a standardised national NHS aftercare pathway for spine surgery patients
records.description: We call on the UK Government to create a mandatory standardised NHS postoperative rehab pathway for spinal cord surgery patients to end the postcode lottery of post operative care.
records.further_details:
We are concerned that post-operative rehab pathways for patients undergoing major spinal cord procedures are severely lacking across the NHS. Many patients are discharged with no clear aftercare plan, guidance on post-surgical medication or emergency protocols for critical complications.
Patients require: Guaranteed neuro-physio, psychological support, holistic planning, rapid re-referral safeguards, a cross trust electronic record system, early social care assessments and a named clinical coordinator.

records.title: Reintroduce the "Peace Day" Bank Holiday on the 19th of July
records.description: The people of England & Wales have the fewest Bank Holidays in the UK. We think this is unfair. To redress the inequality, we want the government to formally approve the 19th of July as the new annual public holiday. This date was formally an official "Peace Day" Bank Holiday.
records.further_details: We think bank holidays significantly boost national morale, while tourism, retail and hospitality benefit from increased consumer spending. The 1919 "Peace Day" observed a national celebration of the feats and legacy of our ancestors' toil for the benefit of future generations. Promoting peace and prosperity are key roles of democratic governments acting for the people.

records.title: Review Gynaecology, Fertility, Early Pregnancy, Maternity & Menopause Care
records.description: We call for an urgent review to improve women's healthcare, including shorter gynaecology waiting lists, fairer fertility treatment, improved early pregnancy and maternity care, better menopause support, and earlier identification and treatment of reproductive health conditions throughout life.
records.further_details: The Government must make women's healthcare a national priority. Urgent action is needed to tackle gynaecology waiting lists, remove unfair fertility treatment restrictions, improve early pregnancy, miscarriage, pregnancy loss and maternity care, and ensure timely menopause support. We believe routine gynaecological assessments should begin from the first menstrual cycle to enable earlier diagnosis, faster treatment and better outcomes throughout women's lives, with fair and timely access to care.

records.title: Create a Clear National Early‑Stage Charity Pathway
records.description: Create a clear, nationally consistent early‑stage charity pathway so community groups can begin lawful, safe public‑benefit activity without long delays.
records.further_details: Businesses can register in minutes, but community groups often wait months before they can begin lawful, safe public‑benefit activity. We ask the Government to introduce a national early‑stage charity pathway that provides clear guidance, consistent processes, and timely support for new community groups. A clear pathway would maintain safeguards while reducing unnecessary delays, helping volunteers support vulnerable people, strengthening communities, improving early intervention, and increasing homelessness‑prevention capacity.

records.title: End the Loss of Rights During Immigration Judicial Review
records.description: Judicial review may expose an unlawful Home Office decision, yet claimants can lose the right to work, rent and support their families while the case is pending. Access to justice is hollow if pursuing it destroys the stability needed to see the challenge through.
records.further_details: A person may lawfully challenge a Home Office decision by judicial review yet lose the right to work, rent and support their family while the case is pending. This can happen before a court has decided whether the Home Office acted lawfully. We ask the Government to introduce temporary statutory protection preserving previous immigration rights for genuine judicial review claimants until the challenge is finally determined.

records.title: Reduce Article 3 medical leave route from 10 years to 5 years
records.description: We call on the Government to reduce the 10-year route to settlement for those granted leave under Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights medical grounds to 5 years, as we believe this will ensure stability and humane treatment.
records.further_details: We call on the Government to amend Immigration Rules so people granted leave on Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights medical grounds can settle after 5 years instead of 10. In our view, the current system forces seriously ill individuals into repeated applications, high fees, and prolonged uncertainty, harming their health and wellbeing. A 5-year route could provide stability, reduce stress, and better reflect the UK’s human rights obligations.

records.title: Align Armed Forces officer-entry age limits with equivalent for Other Ranks
records.description: Require the Ministry of Defence to review and align direct-entry Regular Officer upper-age limits with equivalent Regular Other Rank age limits, unless it can provide clear operational, medical, or workforce-planning reasons for maintaining lower officer-specific caps.
records.further_details: The Ministry of Defence should review direct-entry Regular Officer upper-age limits across the Armed Forces and explain whether lower officer-specific age caps remain justified. This should include a review of Army Regular Officer and Royal Marines Officer age limits.  Where a service allows candidates to begin equivalent regular service as soldiers, commandos, ratings, or airmen at an older age, we believe officer candidates should not face a lower age bar unless there is a clear evidence-based reason.

records.title: Create route for student visa holding spouses of Graduate visas to switch visa
records.description: We call on the Government to create a route for student visa holding spouses of Graduate visas to switch visa to Graduate Dependent Visas. Spouses who are both legally in the UK on separate Student Visas can face disruption as they switch onto the primary applicant's Graduate Visa.
records.further_details: In our experience current rules can force international student couples to separate upon graduation if they held separate Student Visas, even if they have children born in the UK. We believe this loophole breaks families apart by forcing one parent to leave or apply for a completely different visa route. This can cause massive emotional and financial distress for families who already legally reside here. We urge the government to fix this loophole and allow existing student families to remain united on the Graduate Route.

records.title: Require all beachgoers to have a life jacket with them
records.description: Legislate to require anyone going to the beach to have a life jacket with them. We believe that it would be much safer to put on a life jacket when in the sea or when you see someone in trouble at sea.
records.further_details: If people have a life jacket with them at the beach and saw someone in trouble whilst in the sea, it could be safer if they quickly put on their life jacket to help them. We believe that if it was the law to have a life jacket with you when at the beach, it would be easier and less dangerous to rescue someone at sea.

records.title: Require guarantor agreements to be tied directly to fixed-term tenancy contracts
records.description: We call on the Government to amend consumer and housing legislation to require that rental property guarantors must be direct signatories on the primary tenancy agreement, rather than signing standalone Deeds of Guarantee.
records.further_details:
Letting agents and landlords can use standalone Deeds containing "blanket indemnity" clauses to claim that a guarantor's liability continues indefinitely even after a tenancy is surrendered, renewed, or  altered without the guarantor's ongoing knowledge or consent.
Tying the guarantor's legal liability directly to the primary tenancy contract will, we believe, ensure that when a specific tenancy agreement ends or is replaced by a new contract, the guarantor's financial liability automatically terminates.

records.title: Require trade unions to ballot members within 2 weeks of public sector pay offer
records.description: Legislate to require trade unions to ballot their members on whether to accept or reject a formal public pay offer within 2 weeks of receipt. If rejected, any subsequent industrial action ballots must also be initiated, conducted, and concluded within a strict 2-week timeframe.
records.further_details:
Prolonged delays in union balloting leave workers waiting months for back pay settlements and create unnecessary operational uncertainty. For example, following the April 2026 NJC pay offer, some unions over 3 months to run strike ballots.
 
Enforcing a mandatory two-week window for consultative pay ballots and strike ballots could modernise dispute resolution, empower members, and prevent drawn-out pay freezes.

records.title: Replace the Tourist Tax with redirection of VAT on hotel revenue to local areas
records.description: Replace the Tourist Tax with a provision directing some of the existing 20% VAT revenue from hotels to benefit local areas. The hotel VAT rate of 20% is currently higher than in some other countries.
records.further_details: We believe that levying the Tourist Tax would only increase costs to hard working families on holiday in this country.

records.title: Review legal costs of landlords breaching tenancy deposit law
records.description: Following breaches of tenancy deposit laws, prohibit courts from ordering landlords to pay legal costs or court fees. We believe landlords should only be made to protect or return deposits if there are inadvertent breaches.
records.further_details: Tenants deserve secure deposits and effective remedies. Landlords deserve equal treatment and a fair chance to correct an honest mistake. Missing the 30-day deadline can lead to a court penalty of one to three times the deposit even after it is repaid. The landlord may then face substantial legal costs, creating pressure to settle for much more. A balanced law should protect the tenant, sanction the breach once and prevent additional costs after a deposit penalty is imposed.

records.title: Put diplomatic pressure on China to stop repatriating North Korean refugees
records.description: We call on the UK Government to apply diplomatic pressure on the Chinese Government to stop the forced repatriation of North Korean refugees, to end any injustice faced by North Koreans fleeing their country and to ensure their safety.
records.further_details:
If the UK Government successfully pressures the Chinese Government to stop the forced repatriation of North Korean refugees back to North Korea, it could allow North Koreans to have a better chance in life as the border with China is the most common route for North Koreans to cross into and who are trying to escape their country.
 
It could also help protect North Korean women, men and children from being exploited or harmed by Chinese brokers, who may try to take advantage of them by using laws on deporting North Korean refugees against them.

records.title: Scrap VAT and Insurance Premium Tax on Motability vehicle Advance Payments
records.description: Exempt all Motability scheme vehicle Advance Payments from Value Added Tax (VAT) and Insurance Premium Tax (IPT), and conduct an urgent review into commercial pricing pressures currently locking disabled people out of suitable vehicles.
records.further_details: Advance Payments for Motability cars have surged across quarterly lists, even on identical specs with VAT already applied. Combining 20% VAT on deposits with 12% Insurance Premium Tax and commercial leasing pressures is pricing disabled people on fixed benefits out of essential, accessible family vehicles. Motability is a vital lifeline for independent living, not a luxury. We call on HM Treasury and the DWP to scrap these taxes and protect affordable mobility.

records.title: Allow E-Bike Throttles Up to 15 MPH
records.description: Allow e-bike throttles up to 15.5 mph. A throttle limited to 15.5 mph is no faster than a pedal-assist e-bike limited to 15.5 mph. The only difference is how the motor is activated. Throttles like this could make starting, hills and junctions easier while keeping the same speed limit.
records.further_details: We are asking the UK Government to allow e-bike throttles up to 15.5 mph. A throttle limited to 15.5 mph is no different in maximum speed from an e-bike providing pedal assistance up to 15.5 mph. The difference is simply how the motor is activated. Throttles like this could make starting at junctions, traffic lights and hills easier, while helping riders who struggle to pedal continuously. The same speed and power limits could remain, keeping throttles properly regulated.

records.title: Let 17 Year Olds be able to ride a 300cc motorbike
records.description: We believe 17-year-olds should be allowed to ride motorbikes up to 300cc, with proper training and licensing. A higher engine limit would give young riders more practical options while ensuring safety through training, testing, and responsible riding.
records.further_details:
The proposal could require appropriate training and testing, meaning riders would still have to demonstrate they can ride safely before using a 300cc bike.
    A 300cc motorcycle can provide better acceleration and cruising ability, which can be useful when joining faster-moving traffic.

records.title: Dedicate one day a year where lights are turned off to see a clear night sky
records.description: Have one day a year, when weather is clear, where all lights in non-essential buildings are switched off past a certain time across the country to allow people to enjoy a clear night sky.
records.further_details: Imagine how nice it would be to have a day in winter where everyone can get outside on a clear night and gaze at the sky together.

records.title: Override leasehold clauses that block London's 90-day short-term letting right
records.description: Legislate to override leasehold clauses that prevent leaseholders from using London's statutory 90-night short-term letting allowance, helping to protect first-time buyers and other leaseholders facing financial hardship.
records.further_details: Londoners can let homes for 90 nights a year to offset high mortgages, service charges, and utility bills. However, restrictive lease covenants banning lets under six months exclude leaseholders from this planning flexibility. Long-term letting is no longer a practical alternative for temporary relief due to costly borough licensing fees and the Renters' Rights Act 2025, which replaced fixed-term tenancies with periodic arrangements. The Government should make lease clauses blocking short-term lets within the 90-night limit legally unenforceable, aligning leasehold law with planning policy.

records.title: Exempt smokeless tobacco (snuff) from the generational tobacco ban
records.description: For smokeless tobacco to be exempted from the generational tobacco ban. We believe smokeless tobacco (snuff) could help push some people away from consuming vape and all illegal drugs and that this could be a step to help create a socially, mentally healthier and more mature society.
records.further_details: We believe that with government support we could have a society that has a more mature relationship with both tobacco and substance use, using a product with an existing and historically important industry here in Britain. The aim is not to have everyone use it, just to allow those who want to.

records.title: Make the Battle of Cable Street a mandatory topic during KS3
records.description: We would like the Department of Education to make the Battle of Cable Street mandatory in Key Stage 3 as we believe it is an incredibly defining moment of British history that shows unity despite differences
records.further_details: The Battle of Cable Street took place in October 4th of 1936 where a crowd of anti-fascists blocked a planned march by Oswald Mosley of the British Union of Fascists (BUF), police failed to clear a path through the barricades and so the commissioner was forced to cancel the BUF's march, ultimately it is remembered as a major victory against the rise of fascism even to this day

records.title: Ensure access to private pension at any age
records.description: We have been encouraged to invest in a private pension by the government, but we are concerned that the state pension will not exist in the future. We think the government should have NO say in when we can access our own private pension. They should be accessible without tax charges at ANY age.
records.further_details: In our view, we do not see why the government, or anyone for that matter, should have any say in when we can access the money we have been saving for the majority of our lives. They shouldn’t. It should be our choice when we access our private pensions, no one else’s. We should have the opportunity to access our pensions at any age without tax charges, no matter the risk to our personal circumstances.

records.title: Incorporate mandatory neuro-inclusive risk criteria during pre-birth assessments
records.description: We ask the Government to amend the Children Act 1989 and/or Working Together to Safeguard Children guidelines, ensuring that all pre-birth assessment frameworks incorporate mandatory neuro-inclusive risk criteria.
records.further_details: We are concerned that the strict pre-birth assessment criteria currently which is a standardised checklist does not sufficiently take into account neurodiverse differences. e.g. Autistic masking can be misconstrued as lack of parental insight. We feel many neurodivergent parents (especially ones that have been put into the system in the vulnerable adult criteria) have wrongly been put on child protection plans which are inappropriate due to the criteria not understanding neurodivergent presentations.

records.title: Amend law to allow minimum-term reviews for child offenders sentenced at 18+
records.description: We want the Government to change the law so people who committed murder while under 18, but were sentenced after turning 18, can have their minimum term independently reviewed, taking into account their maturity, rehabilitation, development and current risk.
records.further_details: We want the Government to amend the law so people who committed murder while under 18 but were sentenced after turning 18 can have their minimum term independently reviewed. Following the Supreme Court’s 2026 Quaye judgment, this group remains excluded from the statutory review available to those sentenced before 18. Reviews should consider maturity, rehabilitation, development and current risk. This would not mean automatic release but more a review into each personal case.

records.title: Revoke the 2021 and 2025 heather burning regulations to allow controlled burns
records.description: We call on the Government to revoke the Heather and Grass etc. Burning (England) Regulations 2021, as amended in 2025, so land managers can carry out controlled burns to reduce fuel loads and protect peat soils, habitats, wildlife, people and infrastructure from increasingly devastating wildfires.
records.further_details: Since 2021, burning on peat deeper than 40cm on some protected sites has needed a Defra licence. From September 2025 this was extended to peat over 30cm in any Less Favoured Area, covering three times more land, while the UK suffered record wildfires. Controlled burning in season safely removes fuel, creating firebreaks and reducing wildfire intensity. We ask the Government to revoke these regulations in full and ensure Natural England amends management plans to allow burning on protected sites.

records.title: Require equal access for licensed private hire vehicles and hackney carriages.
records.description: We want the UK Government to review and standardise the rules so licensed private hire vehicles can have equal access to road and parking facilities where hackney carriages (black cabs) are permitted, subject to appropriate safety and traffic-management requirements.
records.further_details: Licensed private hire vehicles and hackney carriages (black cabs) both provide licensed passenger transport, but face different rules for bus lanes, taxi ranks and designated parking. We believe these restrictions can cause longer journeys and added congestion. We want the UK Government to review these differences and create a clear, consistent framework allowing appropriate access for private hire vehicles where hackney carriages are permitted, subject to safety and traffic-management requirements.

records.title: Review how military considers mental health of potential recruits
records.description: I would like the government to review how the military considers medical fitness and previous mental health conditions of potential recruits. I would like this review to consider how references could be used to support applications.
records.further_details: Many people with previous mental health issues are turned away from the army, we feel without proper consideration. Many of these people would be capable and willing, and would expand our army and contribute to our society as capable soldiers and as people leaving the army with a trade to make use of within society. As we face shrinking forces numbers, we think this is a viable solution with positive consequences.

records.title: Create a 'Light Electric Trail Vehicle' licence category for off-road trail use
records.description: Introduce a new licence category for lightweight electric trail bikes. We feel current categories are outdated, and may classify these as full motorbikes which many, in our view, clearly are not. They're new technology which we feel needs a new classification, not just thrown into an existing one.
records.further_details: Technology has evolved, and we feel light electric trail bikes do not fit existing vehicle categories. We call on the government to introduce a new legal category for lightweight electric trail bikes. Creating a distinct 'Light Electric Trail Vehicle' class with specific weight, power, and trail speed limits would allow responsible riders to legally and courteously enjoy public bridleways and byways. These bikes can give people freedom.
